I bought this game on steam sale, came with the DLC "Scorched Earth" for $15, the base game was $5.  This game is not even worth those prices.
This is the single most frustrating 14 hours I've spent gaming (and I've played Dark Souls and Bloodborne).  My gameplay experience went like this:
First spawn start punching trees to make the first items.  Get a pick, axe, and club, kill a dilo.  Think "Hey, this isn't so bad" run about 20 feet off the beach and get killed by a level 320 dilo.  Respawn, am immediately jumped by a raptor and die.  Respawn again, jumped by raptor again.  Choose different spawn location...Trex gets me there.  Get teleported to a tribe base.  That's session 1.
Session 2 borrow tribe's beaver to help farm trees to build a house.  Get attacked by a scorpion beaver runs off the cliff of the floating island I'm on.  I go and try and retreive it. Spend 2 hours trying to navigate shark infested water and a swamp, can see the bridge back to the tribe's base and get killed by a giant snake, beaver runs off into the swamp.  I go to try and retreive it, 20 feet outside the walls of the base am jumped by 5 sabertooth tigers.  Try again, jumped by raptors that time.  Try again, back to sabertooths. One more time...make it to the bridge and cross to be killed immediately by a giant snake.  That was session 2.
Session 3, I'll give it one more shot.  I group up with my tribe to go farm some materials for an elevator.  This should be better because I'll be with people who are more familiar with the game.  Shortly after leaving the base, I die.  The group keeps going.  I die 2 more times trying to get back to my body to retreive my gear so I can at least try to catch back up to the group.  After getting my gear back I continue on toward the meeting place...giant snake kills me again.  I say forget this. This isn't fun at all nor is it the least bit enjoyable.   I spend rest of the night playing Fallout 4.

(I do very harsh and very detailed critiques to hit every aspect of the game. Nothing I say in this review points towards the game being bad or pose a negative impression about the game in any way. I simply point out the game's flaws and talk about them and explain how the developers can improve and remove these flaws.)
The game itself has a lot of diverse content to see and is very well layed out. But I find the developers are working on content updates (like the new DLC that came out recently.) rather than trying to fix the game's multiplayer system. Numerous people have reported connection issues when trying to either join or host a server for the game due to the game's global servers being unstable and require the person joining to have the same mods as the host which then takes up more time. I undertstand the game is still early access but the game itself should not have these basic issues and should have had them resolved by now.
The game developers somewhat copy other developers in a sense that they may have a suggestion and bug report thread open in their discussions, the developers pay no attention to those threads and are more concerned with adding more content updates rather than trying to fix the issues addressed by the community who bought the game in the first place. When I first got the game, I was excited to see what the game had to offer, I was a bit dissapointed in the lack of developer support with their community and neglect to further improve their game.
The game was built on an engine that wasn't made to support the game on different computers. The developers neglected to realize that this game would be installed on computers that don't have a graphics card that can handle the game like mine (I used an AMD which can only support 40-59 bit games). I cannot stress this enough, if you're going to be building a game, make sure to take in account for weaker PCs that don't have a strong graphics card. Not everyone is going to have or even afford a GTX 780 or GFORCE to be able to run the game at the quality it's meant to be played at.
The image below shows the quality of this game running on a machine that can't handle ark entirely. This is the quality I run ark at, I am dissapointed that I can't enjoy playing the game using the best graphics but my computer simply can't handle it.
The image above shows the quality of the game I have to run and the image below shows the quality I want to run
The game has anti-alias built in but it doesn't quite help with the lag experienced in-game. I do hope the developers fix this issue as well as the other issues of the game that the community has addressed several times.
The game I find feels real gameplay wise and makes me feel immersed. The way you tame animals in game feels real because you actually have to know what the animal eats and what it's diet is. The animal harvesting mechanic feels real in the sense that each animal doesn't harvest the same thing but harvests a different material for the player(s).
The game in single-player I find is a bit too challenging due to the fact that grinding for resources takes up a lot of time on your own since the resources aren't relatively close together. Another thing I'd like to point out is the fact that once you die, you're forced to start from square-one but do like the fact that you have time to recover your lost gear if you can remember where you died. When I first tried playing this game on my own without the help of my friend, I found it too difficult to obtain resources quickly and also found it difficult to tame high leveled and bigger animals on my own. I think there should be more ways to be able to knock out or immobilize animals than bolas and tranq arrows/darts.
The engram points given to the player by defualt is too low and makes grinding and advancing to the next tier of equipment longer, making me waste more time trying to save up points for better engrams than trying to survive and be able to sustain myself.
The game needs a tutorial for new players, new players are pretty much thrown into the frey with no clue of what's going on. I think a tutorial shouldn't be forced, the tutorial should just give you tips along the way or time to time to help the player understand the mechanics of the game.
Overall, very great game and I would recommend it to someone else. I just think the developers need to pay more attention to improving the game client rather than content as their prioritization is not great. But I do think the updates for the game are a bit rushed in the sense of there being a single update every day, the developers need to relax and take it easy, it's best not to rush updates. Take your time with updates but still get them released, but the developers need to focus on listening to their community, because the people who purchase the game want good content, and the best way to get good feedback is to listen to what people are saying about your game rather than just ignoring the game, because then the game will become increase in popularity.
So to close, I would like to wish the developers the best of luck and hope they'll try and improve the quality of the game for the community and see things from the player's viewpoint.
One more thing, the game is mod supported but should allow mods from the Nexus.

This is a very grindy and self-motivated game about loot for loot's sake; that said, you are a backflipping space ninja with unreasonable superpowers and overpowered weaponry. Basically the core gameplay revolves around running a few basic game types like defense and capture to gear up, level equipment, and collect resources for more equipment to do it all better. Though it is a grind, it's one about setting entire armies on fire or clawing them apart with your bare hands with your buddies.
I didn't think much of it at first, and it certainly looks like a standard pay-to-win time waster, but after a few hours I found myself having some honest-to-goodness fun and a fair environment to have it in. The movement is exciting and the community is refreshingly polite and helpful. It's fairly easy and efficient to grind out valuable items that other players will buy for premium currency, so even the most luxurious MTX cosmetics are within reach.
I do feel a small monetary investment (I've paid $5 so far) is necessary to feel comfortable, but that is a necessary evil of funding a game like this.  The decisions of the dev team can be questionable, but the core gameplay is solid. Just expect the usual "devs plz" ordeal and trust that the overall direction is stable and positive.
Overall I give it an 8/10. It's far from perfect, but for a free (or very cheap) game, it's a heck of a time.
I still enjoy logging in and killing 4 grineer with one arrow while spreading toxic spores over entire maps, and that's enough reason for me to keep playing.

The problem with ARK now is that you literally cannot play on official servers. They have NEETS running the show and calling the shots because of the time investment that's required. So one may think, "Should I play on a private server then?" Answer to that is a hot "hell no" too as the resource rates are so quick entire wipes are more or less just a common sport. Eventually, almost always at least, a primary tribe dominates and then they server hop using the character upload system into a new server and try to take over that way.
I wish it was like how the streamers show where there's silly shenanigans. I wish there was more incentive to "specialize" into a water tribe, a mountin tribe, a swamp tribe, or a plains tribe. But there is absolutely none. A hyper-active group will take a small bit into all four slots. Without this area of specialiization, inter-tribe trade and diplomacy is never going to happen and THAT'S where all the emergent gameplay should lie.
The devs should focus on making tribes specialize above all else, forcing them into certain routes and havce opportunity costs that matter as that's the only reason a hyper-tribe is going to let that beach-side small tribe live. Even then there will still be issues but at least the intra-player communication will be necessary.
The game's a hot mess as it is, new blueprints are literally slapped on with no concept of a talent tree or requirements besides the basic buildings and 'essential' tech route. Smaller groups literally stand no chance without protection and there's no real way to even the odds as Guerrilla tactics just don't seem to work in this game. Damage for hit-and-run is either not substantial enough, or the cost of doing such (in time that is) is underwhelming for the rewards. Mix this with a lack of creativity in the buildings and you can see why most people just get tired of the game after a few months.
There are so many beasts with various perks and utilities on their own that they honestly deserve more than what they have. Conceptually, it is an amazing venue to even odds but the execution is flawed in a sense that the "biggest critter" almost always wins. The game needs to have a sort of "Mechwarrior" approach to size, where larger things take more hits and can dish more damage but the lack of agility and mobility means they might have problems against certain smaller things. But, due to the time investment it takes to actually tame on of these monsters, the forums would be ablaze in a series of rants that their Trex was taken down by a large pack of dilophs.
Maybe I'm just jaded, but this game doesn't need more beasts and the like. It needs:
1) A need and incentive to specialize PER TRIBE
2) Ingram Tech Trees
3) Beast balance overhaul
4) Weapon/building damage and hp overhaul
Those four things if fixed properly will make this a very, very fun game. Sadly I don't see this happening.

I started playing warframe when I've been wandering through steam to find something new and worthy. Didnt even consider free2play at that time, but decided: well, what I loose?
Here is what I found after 3.5K+ hours: forget about grind, you won't find it very soon, just try playing. It will worth it! :)
Some features of game:
At start, don't use you 50 platinum given to new players (later you'll decide what you want to use it on, I recommend warframe slots). And don't pay anything until you're sure you like the game. I didn't pay until reached mastery rank 18 (at which point I've been sure I'm fine with grind and will continue playing).
Other than initial platinum misuses, game is not punishing any way. Do whatever you want, explore any way with group of randoms (like you) or friends. Out of 3 starting frames, all are fine (choose any you like, you can get others later, even if you don't pay a cent or sell anything for plat). Also, to get mastery, you'll have to get them anyway at some point.
At first, it's exploration game. Until 3rd or 4th planet, it's not getting boring in any way or tiny part unless you intentionally repeating some mission for some weird reason. New player missions (up to archwing & kubrow) alone worth more than many steam games. Probably you'll get overwhelmed at some point (too much stuff). But don't worry, game not gonna punish you if you do something wrong. Just try it. Try anything! (hint: if you don't want explore, you can read everything at
After initial phase, grind starts creeping in. But first, until then you'll be already amused for some time, and second, it's not prevalent unless you get too deep (like prime stuff or something).
Endgame is mostly grindfest, but if you get there, you probably like the game enough to keep it going ;)

Respawn, am immediately jumped by a raptor and die.  Respawn again, jumped by raptor again.  Choose different spawn location...Trex gets me there.  Get teleported to a tribe base.  That's session 1.

(I do very harsh and very detailed critiques to hit every aspect of the game. Nothing I say in this review points towards the game being bad or pose a negative impression about the game in any way. I simply point out the game's flaws and talk about them and explain how the developers can improve and remove these flaws.)
The game itself has a lot of diverse content to see and is very well layed out. But I find the developers are working on content updates (like the new DLC that came out recently.) rather than trying to fix the game's multiplayer system. Numerous people have reported connection issues when trying to either join or host a server for the game due to the game's global servers being unstable and require the person joining to have the same mods as the host which then takes up more time. I undertstand the game is still early access but the game itself should not have these basic issues and should have had them resolved by now.
The game developers somewhat copy other developers in a sense that they may have a suggestion and bug report thread open in their discussions, the developers pay no attention to those threads and are more concerned with adding more content updates rather than trying to fix the issues addressed by the community who bought the game in the first place. When I first got the game, I was excited to see what the game had to offer, I was a bit dissapointed in the lack of developer support with their community and neglect to further improve their game.
The game was built on an engine that wasn't made to support the game on different computers. The developers neglected to realize that this game would be installed on computers that don't have a graphics card that can handle the game like mine (I used an AMD which can only support 40-59 bit games). I cannot stress this enough, if you're going to be building a game, make sure to take in account for weaker PCs that don't have a strong graphics card. Not everyone is going to have or even afford a GTX 780 or GFORCE to be able to run the game at the quality it's meant to be played at.
The image below shows the quality of this game running on a machine that can't handle ark entirely. This is the quality I run ark at, I am dissapointed that I can't enjoy playing the game using the best graphics but my computer simply can't handle it.
The image above shows the quality of the game I have to run and the image below shows the quality I want to run
The game has anti-alias built in but it doesn't quite help with the lag experienced in-game. I do hope the developers fix this issue as well as the other issues of the game that the community has addressed several times.
The game I find feels real gameplay wise and makes me feel immersed. The way you tame animals in game feels real because you actually have to know what the animal eats and what it's diet is. The animal harvesting mechanic feels real in the sense that each animal doesn't harvest the same thing but harvests a different material for the player(s).
The game in single-player I find is a bit too challenging due to the fact that grinding for resources takes up a lot of time on your own since the resources aren't relatively close together. Another thing I'd like to point out is the fact that once you die, you're forced to start from square-one but do like the fact that you have time to recover your lost gear if you can remember where you died. When I first tried playing this game on my own without the help of my friend, I found it too difficult to obtain resources quickly and also found it difficult to tame high leveled and bigger animals on my own. I think there should be more ways to be able to knock out or immobilize animals than bolas and tranq arrows/darts.
The engram points given to the player by defualt is too low and makes grinding and advancing to the next tier of equipment longer, making me waste more time trying to save up points for better engrams than trying to survive and be able to sustain myself.
The game needs a tutorial for new players, new players are pretty much thrown into the frey with no clue of what's going on. I think a tutorial shouldn't be forced, the tutorial should just give you tips along the way or time to time to help the player understand the mechanics of the game.
Overall, very great game and I would recommend it to someone else. I just think the developers need to pay more attention to improving the game client rather than content as their prioritization is not great. But I do think the updates for the game are a bit rushed in the sense of there being a single update every day, the developers need to relax and take it easy, it's best not to rush updates. Take your time with updates but still get them released, but the developers need to focus on listening to their community, because the people who purchase the game want good content, and the best way to get good feedback is to listen to what people are saying about your game rather than just ignoring the game, because then the game will become increase in popularity.
So to close, I would like to wish the developers the best of luck and hope they'll try and improve the quality of the game for the community and see things from the player's viewpoint.
One more thing, the game is mod supported but should allow mods from the Nexus.

Please note: my "Hours on Record" is inflated as I leave the game running on my PC.  I'm closer to 1,000 hours as of this review.
First up: tl;dr: I like the game, and would recommend it.  Anyone who says it's Pay-to-Win has a definition of that I don't understand.
Warframe is a free-to-play third person shooter game, where you play "future space ninjas" seeking to free the solar system from various factions.  However, "space ninjas" is a bit of a loose term: each Warframe is more or less a character, each with four abilities.  Frost is snow-themed (creating a bubble of snow that protects allies within it, summoning an avalance), Ash is the stereotypical Ninja warframe, Titania is the warframe that can turn into a little butterfly of death by flying around the map, Inaros is a Egyptian God themed warframe that throws blinding sand and can turn into a sandstorm, etc.  Each warframe is generally overpowered in their own rediculous way, which is kind of needed: sometimes you'll be trying to take on level 100 (or higher) enemies, and it's due to your overpoweredness that your team can accomplish its' goals.
Each Warframe is powerful in what they do, and each one can be augmented using Mods which drop in-game, which can be leveled up against a modification capacity, so even two of the same warframe, through modding, can play differently.  As well, you can swap out your mods between missions, so there is no problem with experimenting with different builds.
The game is primarily PvE, though there is a PvP mode, which includes full-on PvP deathmatch/team-deathmatch, as well as a gametype that is somewhat reminiscent of Lacross-meets-Aztec football.  However, as the abilities of each Warframe can be absurdly overpowered, most abilities in the game work differently in Conclave (the PvP mode) vs the general game.  To be honest, to me the PvP seems tacked on, and I never play it.
Currently, the game has a good methodology of guiding the players through the solar system, unlocking story quests.
The good:  really good-engaging gameplay, multiple "characters" that allow people to experiement and rewards modding and strategy, however can be played in a solo queue.  Later story missions (Natah, Second Dream, Sands of Inaros, The Sacred Grove) have become really good.
The bad: many systems, such as modding, relics, etc. could be explained better, and typically most players end up watching youtube videos to figure out some of the in-game systems, if they don't end up groking them.  The good part is that you can generally get a pretty good ways into the game without understanding the systems before you hit a knowledge wall and need to read the wiki..
The funny: As a Free-To-Play game, most every resource, warframe, or weapon can be bought with Platinum, the currency you can buy from the developers in-game.  Some people (usually people who don't like the game) claim that this allows people to Pay To Win... but it's a mostly PVE game.  And, to be frank, most of the time people use Platinum in-game, is to pay other PLAYERS for items that they have, such as Primed Weapon or Warframe parts (Primed items are in-game "upgrades" to in-game weapons, basically super-prototypes, which can only be obtained in-game by farming), or for specific mods that are difficult to obtain.  The only items that can only be obtained via Platinum, and not by farming, are purely cosmetic items, like different skins for particular Warframes or weapons.
Even if you buy a Warframe or Weapon directly with Platinum, it still starts at level 0, and you need to spend the time to level it up/mod it properly.  And even then, certain weapons are only "good" with specific modifications/build playstyles, so buying the "best" weapon in the game is subjective to the most part.  Yes, there are weapons that are the best Crit-weapons or best Status weapons, but lots of people just play with what is the most fun for them, and can do end-game content just as well as people who only use the L33T OPT1M4L build.
I would NOT recommend spending any Platinum as a starting player beyond the starting Platinum that you get to buy a Sentinel; however, I would recommend buying Platinum if you get a 50% or 75% off Platinum coupon, which you have a chance of getting every day, especially if you've ended up enjoying the game.
The devs are constantly updating the game, usually with new weapons and the like once per week, usually a monthly "special event", bi-weekly reward events, and adding new Warframes and Quests (a major expansion, the War Within, is supposed to come in November).

Okay, so people give this game a lot of crap, but after having put a modest sum of hours into it myself (and expecting that I will continue to do so) I must admit that I think it is a great game.  Hell, it is better than the 'AAA' games that have been coming out over the past year or two.  I have a 1070 GTX and I play the game on EPIC settings with little to no trouble.  There remains plenty of opportunity to optimize the game, but overall the game runs quite well (particularly on single player).
My biggest complaints about this game are that when playing on an official server, I get 'lag' spikes that occassionally last 3 - 15 seconds; I suspect the issue may be due to a memory leak because the problem becomes more pronounced the longer a play session lasts (computer diagnostics don't indicate any issues with heat dissipation for those that may be wondering).  The other complaint I have against this game is that some people / tribes on the servers just POLLUTE the maps with pillars that prevent you from building (much less placing down a damn fire and/or sleeping bag) in a large multitude of spaces.  They do this to 'claim' their territory and just prevent other people from building in certain areas, but people really just overdo it... big time.  People will complain that your small base with spike walls ruins their FPS but say nothing of the scourge that is the abundance of pillars all over the place--bit of a double standard imho.
Anywho, I can confidently recommend this game.  I've certainly gotten my money's worth out of it compared to the assortment of AAA games I've bought in recent times that have just rotted in my library with less than 60 hours play time.
TLDR:  8.75 / 10  [Opportunities for improvement in engine/performance optimisation, server performance, and general gameplay elements (the UI has really improved in recent months!)]

This is a very grindy and self-motivated game about loot for loot's sake; that said, you are a backflipping space ninja with unreasonable superpowers and overpowered weaponry. Basically the core gameplay revolves around running a few basic game types like defense and capture to gear up, level equipment, and collect resources for more equipment to do it all better. Though it is a grind, it's one about setting entire armies on fire or clawing them apart with your bare hands with your buddies.
I didn't think much of it at first, and it certainly looks like a standard pay-to-win time waster, but after a few hours I found myself having some honest-to-goodness fun and a fair environment to have it in. The movement is exciting and the community is refreshingly polite and helpful. It's fairly easy and efficient to grind out valuable items that other players will buy for premium currency, so even the most luxurious MTX cosmetics are within reach.
I do feel a small monetary investment (I've paid $5 so far) is necessary to feel comfortable, but that is a necessary evil of funding a game like this.  The decisions of the dev team can be questionable, but the core gameplay is solid. Just expect the usual "devs plz" ordeal and trust that the overall direction is stable and positive.
Overall I give it an 8/10. It's far from perfect, but for a free (or very cheap) game, it's a heck of a time.
I still enjoy logging in and killing 4 grineer with one arrow while spreading toxic spores over entire maps, and that's enough reason for me to keep playing.
Hard to start at begin but in end game it's easy peasy recommend

I was disappointed more than I have in a long time when I tried this game for the first time. Maybe I've been lucky or frugal in my purchases on Steam, or because I don't have a lot of free time, I don't get to try all the games in my library, because most of the games I play I can find something positive to say and give it a recommendation to some kind of individual taste. Perhaps this game was over-hyped in my mind, much like other big games that invariably flopped on launched due to the pressure that was placed on their shoulders to be this perfect, flawless game.
Whatever the case, this game comes as a hard pass for me. I will likely never install it again. The idea of what is essentially Minecraft meats dinosaur hunting seemed to good to fail. I will also concede that perhaps the true flaw in this game is that the early game is awful, but one you get past the hump, this game turns into a masterpiece of some kind.
Regardless, I cannot give a pass to a game that makes the start of the game (the most important part) the hardest to get through.
Ark, I heard you have grappling hooks? How could you break my heart so?
The honest reason why I find this game fails for me is because the tutorial is horrible, in the sense that there is truly no guidance. I don't think a game should be considered successful if you are required to go to a Wiki in order to get started. Everything that you need in a game should be in the game; Wikis should only supplement what is already available, to help you master a game. I found myself dead more often than not, and all the promises of cool gadgets and gizmos that the game makes are hollow and meaningless if I can't get to them.
If you like "hard" survival games, then maybe this is a game for you. It wasn't for me. Still, the game is pretty, and from what I hear of other people who DO have a good time, this game is pretty good. So maybe if you can get over the hump, then more power to you. I hope the game is a fun experience. All I know is that I am glad I got this out of a Humble Monthly; spending money on this would have made me feel really bad about my decision.
Numerical review: 2/10 (potential, and I know there are things to like, but none of them hooked me, mostly just disappointed that I wasn't able to get past the hour mark)

I picked this game up back in 2014 on the PS4, and I thought it was pretty good.
I ended up in a tight spot and had to give up the console, so I stopped playing for a good, long while.
Got a PC specifically for Fallout, since there's no way I'm shilling out $400 for another console that will be 100% obsolete in a few years anyway. I took my sweet time getting back to Warframe because I knew exactly how much time I would sink into it. Let me tell you, the game is an amazing time killer. With the right gear and even one other competent player, you can spend easily 30m in a single round of Survival, racking up affinity(experience), credits(money), and components.
They updated the map, and I'll admit that I didn't like either of the versions that they tried at first, but I've really come to love the new model of the solar system that DE has cooked up. Aside from them taking out the neat-o little sidebar that showed the possible drops for each planet/moon, I think it's perfect.
At first, you have only one real option. Mercury, then Venus, Earth, and once you hit Mars, the path of progression becomes your choice. Each of the planets/moons is controlled by a main faction, either the Corpus or the Grineer. Occasionally, the Infested will invade, presenting the *option* of doing Invasion missions, where you get to fight alongside the two aforementioned factions. They will also occasionally have Invasion events against each other.
Players have a choice in the opening sequence to select one of(I think) three suits, known as Warframes. As the sequence progresses, you get to choose a melee, primary weapon, and secondary weapon. The "mission" is quick and fairly easy, with toturials to help you learn the action keys. Once you get out, you have free reign of how you want to play. Tank? Sure. Stealth? Sure. DPS? Go nuts. There are even a few healers, if you want to be a real team player.
There have been many weapons added since I gave up the console version, and I'm very happy with them. It feels like there are more weapons than any one player could really have a use for, which is perfect for supporting a variety of playstyles. Automatic rifles, semi auto rifles, snipers, bows, semi auto pistols, automatic pistols, dual pistols, throwing knives, shurikens, the list goes on. And those are just the weapon classes. Outside of a few "unique" weapons, there are three, four or five options in each class. Melee weapons have just as much, if not more, variety.
All of the weapons are highly customizable with a selection of 8-10 of the many, MANY mods that you can get as enemy drops, mission rewards, you can even buy some with in-game money from vendors, Mods are what really make weapons and Warframes effective.
There are a variety of mission types, the classic Exterminate, Spy, Rescue, Survival, Defense, Interception, and they even added a new Archwing mission type, which can be played in space, underwater, or a hybrid of one of the two with standard mission tiles.
The one con that I have regarding the game is the very rare glitch. DE has done a fantastic job of making a well-rounded game that allows many different types of players to come together and save the solar system.
If you're on the fence, do yourself a favor and just try it. The download is free, and you don't have to spend a single cent to get over a hundred hours of playtime. The microtransactions are 100% optional, and only grant access to items that you can get for free if you only put in the time to get them the hard, rewarding way.
Also, who in their right mind doesn't even want to TRY being a space ninja?!

At the time of writing this review it is my most played game with 375+ hours. That should give you some indication as to my opinion of this game...
The game has fast gameplay, nice graphics and some of the story is incredible. The game has a lot to offer people, even if they have played for years, as new content is constantly being added. The community is (generally) nice which helps as the game emphasises heavily on team work to do a lot of the game. There is a nice variety of weapons that can suit your play style however, a lot of them are underpowered and are not viably for use on harder missions. This does mean that the player has to keep upgrading their weapons and mods, use to improve certain aspects of the weapon, which gives them something to work towards. There are many different 'warframes', characters that the player can use, that all have advantages and disadvantages which helps keep the game interesting and makes people think about team compositions.
This all being said, there are a few things that I dislike about the overall experience. I actually hate the new navigation system that got added a few patches ago and considering I have to use it to get to every mission it does take away from the overall fun (this is probably me but I felt I should add it). Grinding for materials can become tedious and boring but is required for the improvement of your weapons and warframes. After 375+ hours the gameplay has begun to become stale and repetitive, although I know people with over 1000 hours and still enjoy it. If you wish to fully experience the game you need to buy the ingame currency, which allows for the purchasing of cosmetics, weapons and warframes (all of which are horribly overpriced). There are also 'prime warframes' which are better versions of other frames which game be obtained through void missions but not purchased through the ingame store. This leaves two options: farm it or buy it from another player in the trade tab. As a new player the trade section is confusing and takes time to learn but sadly the game doesn't explain how to properly use it (or at all from my memory).
I would recommend the game as it is enjoyable and has fun combat but like most games it has its flaws. But it is free which is nice.

This is an overall beautiful game with multiple massive maps to explore. There is a good balance for spending countless hours playing. If you are intrested in a short story game, this is not for you. Even with a powerful trib it could take weeks of playing to accomplish all of the taming, leveling, and caves needed to fight the multiple bosses. I spent almost 1200 hours playing and I knew others that had around 3000 hours of play time and still enjoy it.
That being said, it has alot of bugs and like others have said, the patches dont always fix them or sometimes make them worse. Like when a patch caused dinos to starve very quickly and everyone lost their Gigas, which support did not help  get back. For the amount of money this game has brought in, you would think the development would go faster. Many added dinos dont add to the game and sometims break it. For example when allosaurus was added and packs of 20-30 allos would run around tearing down bases, and they arn't even any good compared to existing dinos. At this point the game is basically a zoo filled with dozens of animals but you only want to use 5 or 6 of them.
There is also a well known memory leak, and the resource drain on a system is quite large. Even my $1500 alienware  couldnt run it on any of the higher settings and I had to restart my system every few hours to stop the memory usage from increasing. I ended up having to disable most of the graphics features and force dx10.
Unrealistic physics and gameplay also give many players a headach. Water that magically clears with goggles, birds that sometimes clip through objects and sometimes don't, and dinos that magically become less powerful after you tame them are all part of the games "balancing". PVP balancing also affected PVE, so attacking boss dinos with machine guns was often a good way to waste resources and not do alot of damage.
Overall I really enjoyed it, but really wish it was more polished. Seriously its been out for this long and made millions of dollars and it's still conisdered Early Access. If the team can fix the glitches, resource managment, remove balancing in PVE, and stop adding useless dinos, I think it would be a great game. adding VR would also be a plus.

I have played the game for around two years by now.
I have mostly played on our own Unofficial Server as I realized quite soon the Developers incapability of hosting proper servers themself - stability- and gameplay-wise.
This review ist heavily funded on my experience as an Unofficial Server Hoster and an player with over 700 play hours put into this game and also the opinions and expierences made by players of said Unofficial Servers. I also have limited knowledge of the utilized Unreal Engine 4.
The game is in a horrible state in absolutely every aspect except creature variety.
The utilization of the famous and excellent Unreal Engine 4 is simply devastating. At release the game ran at a horrible performance even on the newest graphics cards and that has not changed mentionable since then.
The amount of video memory (VRAM) needed to run the game with high or epic textures is absurd.
No (known) game released around the same time and with that engine requires that much memory and every graphics card with >= 4 GB of VRAM should have been sufficient.
With other comparable games using the same engine and a graphics card comparable to a Geforce GTX 980, a player can expect to reach around 60 or even more FPS in certainly most cases on high settings while in Ark you will almost never reach even 40 to 45 FPS in High or even Epic.
I do not know what the Developer did to this excellent Engine to bloat it up to make it run in such a devastating performance.
Instead of concentrating their manpower into fixing issues in the game from day 1, they instead regularly come up with another - in my very personal opinion - completely useless game mode or event. I never played Survival of the Fittest myself but watched live streams regarding it. It is nothing that is supposed to exist in this game nor is it wanted by the players who actually bought this game for the "Real Experience".
Another example of their horrible decision is their way to communicate with their players.
Back when the main map "The Island" did not have any biomes yet like the snow biome, they felt it would be a good decision to "announce" the implementation to their change log as all upcoming updates go there. What they did not mention there was a very essential detail, that player structures and tamed dinos will get eliminated at every place on the whole map, that will be changed. They wrote that very important info somewhere in a wall of text in some unimportant upcomming dino dossier, which only got read by a handful of players (aka the "really big dino nerd forum lurkers").
There was no mention of this in the change logs and not even in the game's main menu, where they regularly spam the players screen with their uninteresting news regarding boring Official Server nonsense.
This lack of communication has led some (many?) players with wet eyes in the past by getting their most beloved dinos (aka "friends") rolled over by lawines of ice. My own tribe has lost a good number of them and that would be okay, if they would have had the chance of dying in a proper game-wise fight instead of being killed by the Developers enormous incompetence. (RIP Maggy, Blue, Keko, Ichty, Janina, 4 not named stego's, Taka, Tara, Leyra and Nightwish!)
(That was also the Day I swore the Developers to be Kill-On-Sight and a lifetime ban on all our servers - not that I expect them to ever put a step on our Unofficial Servers anyway. Just know we got incredible hatred for you (game-wise).)
Another example of their evil incompetence is their decision to have many players buy this game and then suddenly getting the idea to implement EasyAntiCheat into it. EasyAntiCheat is a well known Spyware, which will spy on your computer for processes while the game is running, sending
private informations to their Servers.
Also I feel to mention that EasyAntiCheats privacy policy is void, invalid and even illegal for at least some countries the Developers of this game sell it to - like in my case Germany.
The Developers are - of course - allowed to implement such changes to their game, but such a change of their software requires their customers to accept this change (again: in many countries with strict customer protecting laws, especially Germany) or to refund the whole game to those who do not accept it. By not doing so in such countries, the Developer acts clearly in an illegal and even criminal way. Too bad for the customers that steam does not care as steam is a US-Corporation and the USA does not care for user proective laws at all.
For further informations regarding this, please read EasyAntiCheats (most probably void!) Privacy Policy at their website:

At the time of writing this review it is my most played game with 375+ hours. That should give you some indication as to my opinion of this game...
The game has fast gameplay, nice graphics and some of the story is incredible. The game has a lot to offer people, even if they have played for years, as new content is constantly being added. The community is (generally) nice which helps as the game emphasises heavily on team work to do a lot of the game. There is a nice variety of weapons that can suit your play style however, a lot of them are underpowered and are not viably for use on harder missions. This does mean that the player has to keep upgrading their weapons and mods, use to improve certain aspects of the weapon, which gives them something to work towards. There are many different 'warframes', characters that the player can use, that all have advantages and disadvantages which helps keep the game interesting and makes people think about team compositions.
This all being said, there are a few things that I dislike about the overall experience. I actually hate the new navigation system that got added a few patches ago and considering I have to use it to get to every mission it does take away from the overall fun (this is probably me but I felt I should add it). Grinding for materials can become tedious and boring but is required for the improvement of your weapons and warframes. After 375+ hours the gameplay has begun to become stale and repetitive, although I know people with over 1000 hours and still enjoy it. If you wish to fully experience the game you need to buy the ingame currency, which allows for the purchasing of cosmetics, weapons and warframes (all of which are horribly overpriced). There are also 'prime warframes' which are better versions of other frames which game be obtained through void missions but not purchased through the ingame store. This leaves two options: farm it or buy it from another player in the trade tab. As a new player the trade section is confusing and takes time to learn but sadly the game doesn't explain how to properly use it (or at all from my memory).
I would recommend the game as it is enjoyable and has fun combat but like most games it has its flaws. But it is free which is nice.

Warframe's motto should be "entry is free, but donations are required".
Like spending hours upon hours grinding through the same 6 or 7 missions and maps?
Like having no story or overall goal to accomplish while you kill the same 4 enemy types over and over?
Like being punished for playing the game with cooldowns lasting 72 hours and grossly limited slots you need to shell out real cash for (or get someone else to pay you cash for something you grinded out hours for)aka pay walls?
Like spaghetti code that will constantly be causing fixable glitches (collision errors), bugs (Same z-depth flicker issues [two textures flickering because they share the same space, but it could also be engine issues with backface culling or any number of things but it CAN be fixed], and just lazy design issues that break immersion (like containers and non-interactable objects being placed in walls or the floor; actors are understandable but non-moving objects? come on.)
(another example: your actor, when on a conveyor belt, moves slightly faster than conveyor belt. these are not game-breaking issues but they bug me because you can avoid/fix them if your code is organized properly and you're not lazy and just figure most people won't notice it. but I noticed because I'm anal like that)
Bugs aside, the gameplay is just not riveting enough to justify spending more than 50 hours in the game; it gets old and stale after a while. In most successful MMOs players have something to do besides just grinding; there are minigames, actual quest lines (not the vague mystical mission-reskin ones in warframe), PVP, puzzles, etc. Warframe doesn't have ANY of that.
If you like those things or have no issue with them, You'll probably enjoy it.

As far as free games go, this is a fantastic game. This game has a fantastic environment, great gameplay and beautiful look. I like how you're not really 'forced' into buying any cash items at all, almost everything is available in-game through farming. There is fantastic customisations on virtually everything you obtain. The dojo (guild hall) is great, and very fun to decorate (although the interface needs to be improved for that).
I do have some "pet-peaves" with this game though...
Firstly, I hate how gear-oriented this game is! The mob armor scaling at higher levels is rediculous! I found that even when doing basic map completion (star chart nodes/quests) that my character was extremely squishy against mobs that took little damage from me while 1-shotting me! This mean taking time away to grind out some better weapons and mods just to continue.
Secondly, the reward to effort ratio is completely unfair! I'm doing missions where I'm barely able to survive, struggle for a while, often dying a few times just to come away with 2000 credits and I need like 100k for something. Come on!
Thirdly, dead squads. The game has been out a while, so nobody is doing star chart any more. Unless there's an alart or something, you can forget anyone grouping with you. And no thanks, I don't want to try solo an Interception mission.
Fourth, pressing 'X' and ending up sky high somewhere because there was a trip-wire NOWHERE near you! Everyone who's played Warframe, will know exactly what I'm talking about here lol.
Fifth, having to stand with you shoulders perfectly squared to a locker to open it. OMG this one really bugs me!! I run through maps as fast as I can, and I see lockers, I walk up to them spamming 'X' to open then quickly. Nothing happens, you have to stand 100% perfectly in front of the darn thing JUST to open it, come on!
Lastly, you should rename this game to "Farmframe" or "Grindframe". Sure, every game has RnG etc, but this one takes grinding to a whole other level. I hate grinding in games, it's not fun at all. Who wants to spend hours upon hours just to get a single item, then have to repeat that task another 10 times for the other items you need?! We're not all no-life 100% game time people without a social life or job. I think loots should be more attainable. Not through cash shop, but through improved squads/grouping.
To conclude, despite these so-called "pet peaves" of mine, this game is fantastic fun! Please don't let me personal opinions put you off this great game! I would still highly recommend it to you.

In short - Great Game, absolutely money well spent. I've spent more time in this game than all my other steam games combined. ~500 hrs of entertainement for $30? Best deal ever. I know some people complain about all the things the Developer has or hasn't done, how they've ruined the game, and how they're just out to steal your money and not deliver... blah blah blah. I think a lot of this stems from the fact that you get very invested in Ark. Which is a great quality in a game! However, with the ups (and there are tons) also come the downs (and they can be very down). You will laugh and cry. You will rejoice and then want to punch your monitor and scream. IMO, it's all part of the Ark experience, and it truly is a gaming experience I will never forget.
I'm sure I'll get flak for this but a lot of the negative reviews are done by people who have spent hundreds or thousands of hours in game and then got♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥(maybe♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥multiple times). Then they go and give the game a thumbs down and write a scathing review in a hot headed state. If it really was a terrible game those thousands of hours would have been spent elsewhere. I don't mean this as disrespect to the people who left the game frustrated- I can testify that that frustration is very real. I'm more saying it so people new to Ark will have some context. Did I end up leaving disappointed/frustrated? Yes, but that was only momentary. It had been preceeded by countless hours of enjoyment. With respect to entertainment bang for your buck, Ark will get a Thumbs Up from me all day long.
Last point, I don't really care if Wild Card ever does end up releasing the "Finished" game. This game already had enough content and played well enough to keep me playing longer than I've ever played any other game, regardless of price. I definitely got my money's worth, and then some. Not to mention, most AAA titles release with plenty of bugs now anyway, so "Finished Game" is really just a matter of perspective. As far as early access games go, Ark is definitely among the gems, even if it's not perfect.
In conclusion, buy Ark, have your fun, and then when it's not fun anymore, move on with life.

I rather like this game and find myself dumbfounded at why some people will speng 100+ hours playing it, and say they are unhappy. Repeated play seems to indicate that an individual was getting some kind of enjoyment out of it. I think it might be because people are playing wrong. While combat is a mechanic, combat is difficult. It requires resources and manpower. And if you're into FPS games and like to blow stuff up and shoot things full of holes, this game kind of makes you pay for it because you can't magically be dropped into a battlefield with high tech equipment and run in, guns blazing, like an hormonally crazed super soldier. War is hell, war is costly, and war is difficult. If you're the FPS kind of player, then you might want to consider somethign else because obviously, you will be frustrated by the inevitable failure you will experience when someone's brontos tailwhip you halfway across the island.
With that said, open world games based upon crafting and taming are something I enjoy. I waited until this game was on sale to get it. Graphics and gameplay justify it's cost. It's visually appealing and it takes time to develop systems that are as wide and complex as what is presented here.
I enjoy online play, but I am not especially fond of the occasional griefer who decides to visit a server and kill all the tamed creatures just because they can. This is easily remedied because server backup is done seemlessly and and unwanted damage can be rolled back. But in ununofficia non-dedicatedl servers, survivors are teathered to the host. An increasingly frustrating mechanic when the host is in-game, but you want to explore other areas, or find that a beacon is just out of reach.
I'm also puzzled by aggression of creatures. Thsi isn't to say that creatures shouldn't attack threats on site, especially if they are carnivores, but when you just witnessed a Rex take down three Trikes, it strikes me as odd that if you're in the vicinity, you're the next meal. Having just eaten three main courses, going back to the appertif seems odd, and when Rex does this, I wonder why aggression is not tied to a carnivore's hunger. Perhaps that might be a bit to complex, but I have learned to pretty much avoid such carnivores seeing how I'm a more peaceful player.
Construction can be a tad difficult as some pieces won't fit together properly. Having made a three story building, where each floor has a height of 6 meters or so, many of the wall joins don't match. For those prefectionists, it's maddening to see a crack of light coming in though a wall. Or worse yet, when a doorway happens to be lower than what it should be. I'm a little disappointed that objects places by a player, can't be moved by that player. Placing an inward facing wall, when you wanted outward facing infuriates me, but even moreso that I can't pick it back up to replace. It has to be torn down and you get some salvage.
There is a subtile story, at least on the Island, that is in the form of notes. In the past, it seems people form different times and cultures had been brought to the island, each one left journals about thier time there, but those journal pages are scattered thought the landscape, easily located by the presence of ruins.These pages tell about the events of several different people, a scientist, a naturalist, a general, a bandit. Some are dossiers of the animals on the island, others are records of geologic observations, and some are about the conflicts between previous tribes. Acquiring these pages also grants an experience boost for an allotted time, 500, seconds if I recall. So finding them is in your best interest.
The animals are tameable, these range from avians to dinosaurs, to amphibians and reptiles, to mammals. Each has a different preference as to how to be tamed. Some are fine with berries and vegetables, others need meat or even fish. And each have their own benefits. Some make excellent shock troops, when you need to go ito battle, others are awesome mounts, and some are great hunter/gatherers. And many can be used as mounts, but sometimes, you might not want to do that as you can possibly walk faster than some might run.
Crafting is done with engrams. Every level, you unlock engrams and can purchase them with accrued  points. From a humble stone pick and axe, you can go on to cannons, GPS, and private communication radios.
There are a few bug and glitches. Constantly the game need updating because improvements are made frequently. There's a shield glitch, that if you log out with a shield equiped, a fantom shield will be stuck to you, and to remove it, you need to fast travel to another bed (this is less painless if you have two next to each other). Occasionally you just might drop dead for no reason at all, or rather, the reason is a sudden disconnect. This can be quiet frustrating to someone with lost of items because locating corpses is not an easy task, and corpses and items have decay timers.
There's also a survival mechanic. It's important for you to keep your survivor not only fed and hydrated, but cooled or warmed as each biome has their own climate.
So really, if you were/are a Minecraft fan, you may enjoy this. It's pretty much like Minecraft, but grown-up. But lets not forget dinosaurs, a fantasy that nearly every child had.

Running up a snowy mountain firing a machine gun at a woolly mammoth from the back of a tyrannosaurus is a fantastic example of the reason many video games exist: living out ridiculous childhood fantasies. ARK has plenty of that to go around across its multiple sprawling maps which it calls ARKs  which can be explored solo or crowded with up to 100 players. Some lingering technical issues, bad dino AI, and an extreme amount of grinding to reach endgame are the main factors keeping it from being as sharp in the tooth as it could be.
Like many of the survival/crafting games of the genre it partially helped popularize, ARK dumps you on the beaches of a massive, foreboding island with just enough clothing to stay modest and your own two fists. From there, the challenge is to stay fed and hydrated while avoiding a huge variety of terrifyingly detailed dinosaurs and other beasts long enough to progress up the tech tree. Early in the life of a character, you might be taking out dilophosaurs with throwing spears and hoping a triceratops doesn’t come and knock your thatch hut over in the middle of the night.
From there, there’s a really nice flow of technological progression that makes advancement feel like more than just an increase in stats. Thirty hours later, you may preside from a sturdy stone castle from atop which you snipe pterasaurs out of the air with a rifle. By the endgame, it’s possible to have a massive steel fortress full of blast furnaces, complete with electric lighting and gas generators, churning out components for building rocket launchers and SCUBA gear.
On public PvP servers, other players are both your greatest opportunity and greatest danger. As I learned the hard way more than once, making sure your shelters are hidden from potential looters is far more important than making sure they are strong, and I often returned from less than 12 hours offline to find my barricades wrecked and hours worth of resource harvesting hauled off. Things get much better if you can work your way into a strong tribe of players that can protect your stuff 24/7.
Well let me come to the point. When I’m having a good time in ARK, I’m having a really good time. The problem is that those moments are usually one part to every nine parts menial grinding and crafting - especially at the later tech tiers. Having to repeat so much work after failing an attempt at a boss feels far too punishing, and some really dumb dinosaurs can take a lot of the challenge and sense of danger out of the many primal locations. Even with all of those quirks, however, I’m still hungry to play more after nearly the 1.5k hours I’ve spent so far. There aren’t a lot of survival games that have legitimately held my attention that long.

This game and I have a complicated relationship. Ark is a beautiful, mechanically okay survival experience with an extrodinary difficulty curve, and an incredibly unusal deficit. However, I strongly reccomend this title, despite it's failings.
Foremost, dinosaurs are a split pea soup type mix. Boas and Rexes will **** you to death in just a couple hits, while dodos run in terror as you beat them to death with your mildly deformed flailing appendages. Your character will look like a strangly colored dino human with hips as wide as his chest is bird. You'll feel like a mutant out of the oblongs and you'll giggle like you inhaled laughing gas for an hour. You will be the walking pole and the dinosaurs will fear you and hail you as the decimator. All the while, terrorbirds will two shot your turtle stallion and leave you dieing in a pool of your own blood and excriment. Truly a time to be alive.
Now to the deficits.
Multiplayer is an absolute mess! Protip: unofficial servers are your friend. The official ones are like Day Z's abusive alcoholic cousin and make you feel like a two foot tall mildly obese man in a maximum security prison filled with giant lizards. That is, dead or soon to be.
Dino strength is um.. Highly variable. You can take down a trike or a dodo with your basic filthy-peasant tier wood and stone "weapons," but just you wait until you see that "walking mountain" and fail to understand how physics works as you accidently plink it with a rock and watch as it ****s you, ****s your pets, ****s your homes, neighbors homes, and the city council and leaves you crying under a rock as it screams with a fury from your worst nightmares and maybe beyond that. If "nuke" had a corporeal form, that would be it.
It's as my friend once said, with his max tier gear and army of like 20 upper tier dino mak daddies, "You see everything we have?" Yeah, I said. "If you attack that thing, these don't exist anymore." Truly terrifying.
Then, we come to region locking. You see, ark is a forced multiplayer game. Unlike 7 days to die *cough*, they don't kick down your sand castle after they're done seeing you play. Ark is different. They want you to have friends and recruit them, but it isn't specifically necessary. Like if you want to encounter anything beside the beaches, you'll need a tour guide, but that doesn't leave you totally bohemian. Oil is your sand castle crasher, but it's not "required" to play.
Overall, is it worth playing?
Yes.
Is it easy.
Absolutely not.
Does it deserve a better review than "7 days to cry"?
Yes. Wherein 7 days enjoys curb stomping your manhood and leaving you shamefully crying to your mommy after the neighborhood kids stole your softball, Ark gracefully believes in you, bringing you up with wonder and excitement before beating you senseless the second you secret the exit to your resort beach. Lovingly, and with compassion.
Remember kids, survival games are not your friends. You survive them, you don't win.
Until next time!

To tell you the truth, this game does get on my nerves sometimes. Since its release, I've developed a habit of putting 20-50 hours on it, then uninstalling it for a year or so. When I get the itch to play it again, I reinstall it, and then spend a considerable amount of time glued to wikis and walkthrough videos, trying to make heads or tails of the changes that have happened since I was gone. It's easy to get lost in the ever-changing landscape of this game, and you best not get too attached to any one aspect of it, as it could be gone with the next update.
Now, at the time of my yearly rage quits, I might be inclined to not recommend this game, but that is ultimately unfair. Despite the long hours of grinding, or constantly having to rely on the internet to tell me how to complete certain tasks, or the sudden jumps in difficulty without warning, this still remains the best free-to-play game I've encountered, hands down. For me, the enjoyment outweighs the frustration. (And of all the games that require a lot of grinding, I definitely have the most fun doing it in this one.)
What you get in the end is a third-person action game with extremely satisfying controls (most of the time), gorgeous (if repetitive) environments, and a lot of fun crafting and management elements, all with a price tag of zero. My advice to you is to heed the warnings of the negative reviews, and then give it a shot anyway.

This is the story of a man, a regular man, one of you, one of us.
He goes to his computer, like every other human being in the 21st century.
He goes on Steam.
"Oh! What's this Warframe?"
He looks at the reviews.
"Huh. Most of them are good."
He downloads Warframe.
The computer finished downloading Warframe.
He opens up Warframe.
And spends 5 minutes making an account.
After he has finished making his account, he chooses his Warframe.
He has three options.
Excalibur
Volt
and Mag.
He chooses Excalibur, because the game told him it was good for a beginning player.
Everything goes dark.
He wakes up in a pod.
He sees 3 figures. Two identical, and one with a key shaped badge on him.
He doesn't know what's going on.
He hears something, but isn't sure if it is English.
The three figures walk away.
Four figures guard his pod.
"Are they friendly?" he thinks to himself.
Suddenly, a voice.
A beautiful voice.
Who is singing in his head.
She calls herself,
Lotus.
She releases him from the pod.
The four figures aim guns at him.
Then, a sword of light comes out of his right hand.
He swings it, and it strikes one of the four figures.
He swings it again, defeating the other 3.
He puts the sword of light away.
The Lotus tells him to pick his weapons.
He has two options:
A gun or a bow.
He picks the gun.
She tells him how to manuver.
And he does.
She gives him two other options.
A pistol or kunai.
He picks the pistol.
They both rush to the final weapon, a melee.
Sword, or a staff.
He picks the sword.
He then meets the figure unlike the others.
She calls her, Captain Vor.
She says we aren't ready.
She says we need our ship.
Another voice pops up in my head.
His name is Ordis.
We wait.
We find our ship.
We go into outer space.

It is unfortunate, as ARK had SO much potential when it began.  The freedom to explore and build was fulfilling.  Interaction with neighboring tribes was a social experiment.  It was really fun to have long term goals, to achieve difficult tasks through planning and to work as a team.
Unfortunately Wildcard SUCKS with customer support.  Any software requires a corrective actions process to fix bugs, administer servers, interact with the user group, etc...  Wildcard has poured all of their effort and resources into new models, new skins, new features and NOTHING into fixing glitches or exploits.  They release game changing new models (tek) that WRECK the game... and provide almost no apologies or fixes.  Every release seems to be in favor of the griefers and the exploiters who destroy the economic balance by duping, glitching under the map, using server lag to their advantage, denial of service attacks, etc...  The ability to move resources across servers without first providing human referees and administrators MONITORING GAME PLAY was a STUPID idea.  Providing tek transmitters that can be placed UNDER THE MAP with no server admins on duty 24/7 is completely irresponsible.
Unlike other massively multiplayer online games (UO, WOW, EVE, LOTR, TF, CS...), Wildcard slapped a beta label on a two year old game in order to bybass any responsibility of maintaining their servers.  When you play the game, you WILL be greifed by a cheater.  There is NO recourse.  Months of effort will vanish at 4 AM by a handful of cockroach-players who spent a few hours grinding weapons that, when combined with any of a hundred exploits, will bypass your defenses.  Your five generations of dino breeding will be wiped in minutes.  200 auto-turrets on redundant power generators, will be completely impotant as griefers slide into a map glitch and attack your base from underneath the map.  They will bring a T-rex from an unofficial server to an official server (dup exploit) during a major patch deployment, with health 50x what is allowed... and wipe the dinos you took MONTHS to raise.  You will watch your favorite dino fall through the map, never to be seen again.  Your best bird will die as your client lags out and fall to earth.  There as SO MANY THING WRONG WITH THIS GAME.
IF there was a full time admin present on each server that would respond to these problems and restore your hard work, it would be an awesome game.  BUT, when you fill out a ticket with WildCard, they will tell you that it is a beta and you are screwed.  They have only rolled back servers when evidence of MASSIVE exploits are so painfully obvious, they have to step in.  Think about that: their only recourse is to restore to a snapshot.  That's it.  They apparently have no parallel database tracking individual objects IN A TESTING ENVIRONMENT.
Seriously, don't waste your time.  If ARK gets bought out by a larger, more professional company (Blizzard, EA)... then they will spend money on the support layer.  But WildCard has proven to be completely incompetent in this area.  Don't give them any more funding EVER.

I love me a good 3rd-person action game, and Warframe certainly delivers the goods. It combines satisfying shooter + melee combat gameplay with fantastic parkour-style movement in beautifully detailed alien environments. There are tons of upgrades to unlock and the 4-person team system works well to keep things fun and challenging at the same time.
My one major gripe is that the game doesn't do a great job of taking you through everything that you can earn or do in it. There are tutorials and places to find information, but you'll have to resort to looking up the wiki every so often to figure out certain things.
That being said, Warframe is still home to a great community of friendly players, and you can always ask for help in the in-game chat.
If you're looking for a fun f2p game with a fair pricing model, this is certainly worth a few hours - or several hundred.

I wrote a review almost a year ago and I feel like I need to revise it just because I sunk so much of my time into this game.
Like the synopsis says, this is a fast-paced run and gun game with plenty of variety(I will get to this later).
Pros:
The gameplay is great. Running around fast and jumping on walls is fun. The movement may feel a bit floaty at first but you'll get used to this over time and it's easy to learn, thanks to the tutorial at the beginning.
Shooting dudes while gliding down from the air, blasting them with a quad-barreled shotgun then seeing their gibs fly off is immensely satisfying. There is so much variety with the guns here, although as fun as this sounds, it does have its flaws. A lot of flaws. But if you don't care about numbers and only care about shooting dudes, then have fun!
The melee system is okay. It's satisfying to chop enemies in half with a greatsword or electrocute them with a stun baton. Fast and brutal or slow and devastating, that's pretty much how I would describe it. A lot of Warframes actively reward you for melee combat. However it can get repetitive if you choose to restrict yourself to just a single playstyle.
Finally we have the Warframes. If you like scifi supersuits, this will make your dreams come true. Warframes have powers and stats, which dictate their playstyle, and often times your designated role. Some would argue there are "useless" Warframes in the game, which isn't completely false, but whatever they say, pick the one you think looks the coolest and explore from there. From raining lightning to your foes to summoning dead enemies to fight for you, there's a bit of everything for everyone here.
Graphics are fantastic for a free-to-play game. Definitely better from when I initially started playing this game back in 2014. That doesn't mean this game will destroy your PC, it won't. It runs buttery smooth on both my low and high end machines. Tweak the settings that better suit your preference.
Sound design is great. Most guns feel so satisfying to use, but some are kind of underwhelming. Shotguns have this delightful bang to every shot. Heavy melee weapons have a nice gut-slice sound and clang to every swing. Warframe powers vary greatly, but Excalibur's powers have the most satisfying sounds, very fun. Ambient sounds are somewhat eerie on the Infested missions.
Music is mostly great. There's the heavy percussion style for the cloned army Grineer. A bit of electric and techno for the space corporation Corpus. Void soundtrack is the best as it has this orchestral theme to it. Thank Keith Powers for the OST.
Art style is mostly subjective, but I personally love it. If the look and feel of Warframe alone attracts you, go for it. There's not a lot of games out there with similar aesthetic.
The community has been generally good based from my experience. Nothing too radical to say about it. Just make sure you set your server region to the correct one, so you don't go wandering off to unknown territory that don't speak English.
Cons (these are big ones):
Contrary to what a lot of people say, this game IS NOT pay-to-win. It's just pay-to-get-things-faster. That's what it is. That's why everything feels so crushingly slow. You need to gather resources in order to gather resources faster, which pretty much describes most endgame stuff (if this game had endgame).
That's right, NO ENDGAME. Raids just aren't engaging enough, everything feels dull when you have everything. On the plus side, if you think looking good is true endgame, then that shouldn't be too far ahead. There's just no area for endgame players, if I had a suggestion to the developers, create a new star system. Write a new story on that, it will greatly increase the longevity of this game.
As mentioned above, it's not a pay2win game. However, you only start with 2 Warframe slots. You CAN'T increase this by ranking up. You have to spend the premium currency Platinum in order to increase slots. The only way to acquire that without spending money is to grind for valuable items ingame.
You read that correctly, GRIND. To the game's benefit, you'll never really feel like you're grinding, as the game itself is fun, unless you bang your head repeatedly on a single mission or mission type, that's your fault. You will grind for items to trade for Platinum, so you can grind for more resources to wait 72 hours to craft your shiny new Warframe.
72 HOURS!? Yes, most items require to be crafted in the Foundry, this game's backbone. Every weapon takes 12 or 24 hours to craft. Warframes? I'll say that again, 72 HOURS. Excited about your new Warframe? Too bad, 72 hours. You can rush it for 50 Platinum though, but who's going to do that? Certainly not you, I trust you wouldn't do that to your precious Platinum. Not that it matters, every weapon and Warframe possess only half of what you can put inside in its upgrade capacity.
You need to find random alerts for those upgrade items, catalysts and reactors. I mean your fellow players would tell you it's not necessary. Of course not, but you can only put 2-3 max ranked mods on your Warframe, mainly the ones that increase your shield and health capacity. But good luck actually finding those mods that you saw on a YouTube build.
Mods drive this game's meta. They are upgrade cards you can insert into weapons and Warframes. They vary greatly in rarity and value. Variety comes from the weapons and Warframes, however, melee weapons require stances. Swords and Staves are among the first you encounter in the game, their stances are extremely rare you might as well just trade them from other players.
By the way, the trading system is atrocious. There could have been a billion ways in the past to improve it but it seems they really want to slow down the exchange of Platinum between players. From a business standpoint I can understand that, but that doesn't mean it's good.
Praise the RNG because this game is full of it. In fact, if you want to grind for a particular item you want, you'll have to go through several layers of randomness. Nothing is ever certain here. You have RNG for what reward type you'll get, RNG for what's inside an item that holds other items, RNG for what stats inside your special mod will have. If you despise RNG, I highly discourage you from playing this game.
Lastly, enemy scaling is ridiculous. You either one-shot them or they one-shot you. I'm leaning towards the latter. They get crazy armor values and become invincible nukes. They're not impossible to kill, but certain setups become a requirement rather than a compliment.
Then there's PVP... I personally don't know because I don't play PVP.
Conclusion:
I sunk 950 hours into this game. You think I'd give it a thumbs down? What am I, stupid? If I put 950 hours into something it means it was worth 950 hours of my time. Don't be discouraged by people giving this a thumbs down because "it's not what it used to be", while having 2000 hours on their playtime. Above all else, use your better judgment.
It's a great free-to-play title, one that you should definitely give a shot. Unless you hate RNG of course, then don't.

I started playing this game when early access was first available two years ago.  The game had many major bugs, but it was ridiculously fun to play.  The sense of adventure and exploration is what made the game amazingly enjoyable for me.  There were no guides or in depth instructions, and a big part of the fun was discovering how to best tame dinos, or coming up with good base designs.
The reason I cannot recommend this game anymore is in part due to the fact that the sense of adventure and discovery is completly gone since so many guides and databases are available.  In addition, the game has become very punishing for new players as the addition of more and more advanced technology has been introduced.  Wooden and stone bases simply don't do anything to keep robots and lazer guns out.
This is just my opinion, but I feel like the game is not worth playing anymore because it is so easy for one tribe who plays more than anyone else to utterly dominate a server.  The only two options to avoid this is to play on a PvE server (which is boring imo) or play on a server that wipes periodically (this makes any progress you make pointless).
If you don't mind dealing with any of the problems I have mentioned, you will probably like this game.  However, I don't recommend it.

Warframe's motto should be "entry is free, but donations are required".
Like spending hours upon hours grinding through the same 6 or 7 missions and maps?
Like having no story or overall goal to accomplish while you kill the same 4 enemy types over and over?
Like being punished for playing the game with cooldowns lasting 72 hours and grossly limited slots you need to shell out real cash for (or get someone else to pay you cash for something you grinded out hours for)aka pay walls?
Like spaghetti code that will constantly be causing fixable glitches (collision errors), bugs (Same z-depth flicker issues [two textures flickering because they share the same space, but it could also be engine issues with backface culling or any number of things but it CAN be fixed], and just lazy design issues that break immersion (like containers and non-interactable objects being placed in walls or the floor; actors are understandable but non-moving objects? come on.)
(another example: your actor, when on a conveyor belt, moves slightly faster than conveyor belt. these are not game-breaking issues but they bug me because you can avoid/fix them if your code is organized properly and you're not lazy and just figure most people won't notice it. but I noticed because I'm anal like that)
Bugs aside, the gameplay is just not riveting enough to justify spending more than 50 hours in the game; it gets old and stale after a while. In most successful MMOs players have something to do besides just grinding; there are minigames, actual quest lines (not the vague mystical mission-reskin ones in warframe), PVP, puzzles, etc. Warframe doesn't have ANY of that.
If you like those things or have no issue with them, You'll probably enjoy it.
