As far as free games go, this is a fantastic game. This game has a fantastic environment, great gameplay and beautiful look. I like how you're not really 'forced' into buying any cash items at all, almost everything is available in-game through farming. There is fantastic customisations on virtually everything you obtain. The dojo (guild hall) is great, and very fun to decorate (although the interface needs to be improved for that).
I do have some "pet-peaves" with this game though...
Firstly, I hate how gear-oriented this game is! The mob armor scaling at higher levels is rediculous! I found that even when doing basic map completion (star chart nodes/quests) that my character was extremely squishy against mobs that took little damage from me while 1-shotting me! This mean taking time away to grind out some better weapons and mods just to continue.
Secondly, the reward to effort ratio is completely unfair! I'm doing missions where I'm barely able to survive, struggle for a while, often dying a few times just to come away with 2000 credits and I need like 100k for something. Come on!
Thirdly, dead squads. The game has been out a while, so nobody is doing star chart any more. Unless there's an alart or something, you can forget anyone grouping with you. And no thanks, I don't want to try solo an Interception mission.
Fourth, pressing 'X' and ending up sky high somewhere because there was a trip-wire NOWHERE near you! Everyone who's played Warframe, will know exactly what I'm talking about here lol.
Fifth, having to stand with you shoulders perfectly squared to a locker to open it. OMG this one really bugs me!! I run through maps as fast as I can, and I see lockers, I walk up to them spamming 'X' to open then quickly. Nothing happens, you have to stand 100% perfectly in front of the darn thing JUST to open it, come on!
Lastly, you should rename this game to "Farmframe" or "Grindframe". Sure, every game has RnG etc, but this one takes grinding to a whole other level. I hate grinding in games, it's not fun at all. Who wants to spend hours upon hours just to get a single item, then have to repeat that task another 10 times for the other items you need?! We're not all no-life 100% game time people without a social life or job. I think loots should be more attainable. Not through cash shop, but through improved squads/grouping.
To conclude, despite these so-called "pet peaves" of mine, this game is fantastic fun! Please don't let me personal opinions put you off this great game! I would still highly recommend it to you.

To tell you the truth, this game does get on my nerves sometimes. Since its release, I've developed a habit of putting 20-50 hours on it, then uninstalling it for a year or so. When I get the itch to play it again, I reinstall it, and then spend a considerable amount of time glued to wikis and walkthrough videos, trying to make heads or tails of the changes that have happened since I was gone. It's easy to get lost in the ever-changing landscape of this game, and you best not get too attached to any one aspect of it, as it could be gone with the next update.
Now, at the time of my yearly rage quits, I might be inclined to not recommend this game, but that is ultimately unfair. Despite the long hours of grinding, or constantly having to rely on the internet to tell me how to complete certain tasks, or the sudden jumps in difficulty without warning, this still remains the best free-to-play game I've encountered, hands down. For me, the enjoyment outweighs the frustration. (And of all the games that require a lot of grinding, I definitely have the most fun doing it in this one.)
What you get in the end is a third-person action game with extremely satisfying controls (most of the time), gorgeous (if repetitive) environments, and a lot of fun crafting and management elements, all with a price tag of zero. My advice to you is to heed the warnings of the negative reviews, and then give it a shot anyway.

This is the story of a man, a regular man, one of you, one of us.
He goes to his computer, like every other human being in the 21st century.
He goes on Steam.
"Oh! What's this Warframe?"
He looks at the reviews.
"Huh. Most of them are good."
He downloads Warframe.
The computer finished downloading Warframe.
He opens up Warframe.
And spends 5 minutes making an account.
After he has finished making his account, he chooses his Warframe.
He has three options.
Excalibur
Volt
and Mag.
He chooses Excalibur, because the game told him it was good for a beginning player.
Everything goes dark.
He wakes up in a pod.
He sees 3 figures. Two identical, and one with a key shaped badge on him.
He doesn't know what's going on.
He hears something, but isn't sure if it is English.
The three figures walk away.
Four figures guard his pod.
"Are they friendly?" he thinks to himself.
Suddenly, a voice.
A beautiful voice.
Who is singing in his head.
She calls herself,
Lotus.
She releases him from the pod.
The four figures aim guns at him.
Then, a sword of light comes out of his right hand.
He swings it, and it strikes one of the four figures.
He swings it again, defeating the other 3.
He puts the sword of light away.
The Lotus tells him to pick his weapons.
He has two options:
A gun or a bow.
He picks the gun.
She tells him how to manuver.
And he does.
She gives him two other options.
A pistol or kunai.
He picks the pistol.
They both rush to the final weapon, a melee.
Sword, or a staff.
He picks the sword.
He then meets the figure unlike the others.
She calls her, Captain Vor.
She says we aren't ready.
She says we need our ship.
Another voice pops up in my head.
His name is Ordis.
We wait.
We find our ship.
We go into outer space.

I love this game, but it certainly has it's downsides, namely the early game. The game is incredibly complex to a new player, to an almost rediculous degree. There are a few things you should know about for when you get started.
1: Either find an experienced player to help you learn the ropes early on, or look up a guide. Bookmark the wiki while you're at it. If you can't find a player to help you out, my username is RagingGator.
2: The microtransactions are almost entirely not worth it, unless you receive a discount as a daily reward. There are only two things you cannot get without platinum, and they are slots for your warframes or weapons, and many of the cosmetics. EVERYTHING ELSE you can get through simply playing the game.
3: Farming. This game has quite a lot of it, and if you don't like repeating missions, you might have some problems with the game in general. You can get by without farming somewhat, but to thrive, it's a necessity.
4: Starter mods. When you start the game, it will start giving you 'damaged' mods. DO NOT UPGRADE THEM. They have only half of the available capacity, and are alltogether worse than an undamaged mod. To progress smoothly, you will need undamaged versions of the following mods: Serration, hornet strike, pressure point, (Straight damage mods,) Vitality, redirection, (Health and shields,) flow, streamline, and intensify. (power max, efficiency, and strength.) After you get these, you will be more or less prepared for what the early to mid game has to throw at you, and prepared to progress.
Good luck, Tenno

I played over 500 hours of ARK shortly after it's release on Steam. It's the only survival games I've ever gotten really into. It's loads of fun, if you have the time to sink into it. I don't recommend playing on official servers, as it's a huge time sink. This is arguably part of the experience, so it's not recommended for casual players.
If you are anything less than an extremely hardcore player (and don't have a full time job or other real life obligations), I would recommend playing on a private server where the taming rates are increased (3-5x feels about right), unless you want to spend multiple hours taming a single dinosaur and gathering resources.
The developers are some of the best I've ever known when it comes to creating new content. New dinos and updates are released very often and the ARK world quickly evolved a diverse ecosystem. Sadly, the same can't be said about Wildcard's commitment to other aspects of development, most notably opimization and performance issues. It takes a lot to run a game as beautiful as ARK in a seemless world capable of hosting dozens of concurrent players, and all the glorious structures they can build. In that sense, perhaps the blame can't all be attributed to the developers. Maybe current technology just isn't quite ready for a game of this magnitude. Regardless, even if you have a top tier gaming PC, if you play on any semi-populated server you will soon learn all you need to know about rubberbanding.
In the end this game became quite a lot of work, and putting it behind me tremendously reduced the stress in my life. It can be difficult to find the right community of players if you are going into it alone or with a small group, especially on PvP servers where larger tribes will dominate all (which I imagine is true with any survival game). Although I did have some of my best experiences playing alone and encountering other players (even being "hazed" into larger tribes with strangers was incredibly of fun).
A lot of people were upset by the paid DLC for an early access game, understandably. I was never able to play it, but I'm sure I would have enjoyed it as it looked just as beautiful as ARK but was different enough in it's own way.
In fact, the reason I stopped playing this game is because I was VAC banned (probably on account of some glitch or due to a mod I was using to increase visibility at night). I was actually surprised Valve issues bans for early access games. Anyways, perhaps I will return someday after the official release to give this game another chance, but unfortunately it won't be on this account.

Alright, lets be real: The haters for this game is HUGE! But that's ok, every game has it's haters. But I found this game is really fun, especially with Play as Dino. Even with my computer that rus the game at 15 fps, its great. Now, if you want to get the game, the only problem with that is IT TAKES SO LONG TO DOWNLOAD!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!1

Basically Ark is Mount and Blade with Dino's. Which means you can't do a lot without a mount and you will need to lvl them and get better ones. The maps look nice and the community is flushing out more of em + you can use a world gen.
But these maps have issues like the whole game. Bugs & glitches are more or less on every map. So sometimes you fall below the map after death and cant recover the backpack or you or your Dino get stuck and have to suicide/carve your way out.
The worst thing is the performance. I can look pretty but even with a 1070 and decent rig it plays like vomit. Fortunately ini tweaks might help a bit for single player in multiplayer it seems worse. You can play it fluent but then it looks nowhere near all the advertised vids and pictures.
If you like open world games and you have fun building stuff and riding around a nice island - the game still has to offer a lot. Do your self a favour and wait for a sale - the technical state of it is nowhere near justifying the asking price.
Since its in EA for a long time now its shocking that these issues havent been solved. I mean you're forced to have 16gb of ram and its still not running well. Mantra is: We put everything in then we fix. Other teams like Empyrion devs tell a different story: We fix as soon as we can because it gets harder to find the troublemaker with every new version. Strange thing is they sold a DLC (wich also needs to be updated...) in early acess. *caugh caugh* While they already have hughe sales...
You can't dig like in 7d2d but you can cut trees and plants and rocks for resources. Different tools give different materials. Fortunately you can mod the game via sliders or ini tweaks. That would be like longer or slower day cycles, more regen, faster exp and taming etc. The basic game is very slow because of slow progression. Nice but if you wanna have a life or job its difficult to play ark. If you check the official site you see art design/marketing which is more appealing to teenagers who might not have those time issues. I guess i'm a bit to old for the official communication.
While you can mod the single player it makes life harder to find PvP/PvE servers with the settings you like. In pvp players can move from server to server which is a cool thing but it just brought male hordes whose imagination is so big hughe that the only thing they can do is to destroy other bases - preferably those in different time zones. Some admins do try to contain these things but a lot pvp servers are full of social darwinists. So a lot players moved to PvE which results in lack of space there and your best bet might be a private server where you contact the admins and you hope for an invite. Sometimes you find nice active admins but thats rare - and depending on your definition of nice. Some servers also look like a garage because most ppl just come on to feed dinos and go off again for the week.
To solve this... well it seams the devs made an arena fight version for "competition". Unfortunately in fps shooters we never needed arenas we were into great gameplay and we just needed a propper match making. Nowaday everythings need an extra piece of i don't know what... which takes time for fixing away. I also wonder why dinos need laser weapons etc. Nice as gag/mod but as officially crafable stuff? I didnt buy Ark just because of these laser vids untill this sale... Thats a lot pew pew but indepth gameplay would be more interesting or at least more bug hunting because the community is creative enough to develope these things. Unfortunately it happens a lot that updates breaks stuff even in vanilla game. That might always happen but its smth different if it happens while you try to take care of it or not.
Since Ark is also played MMO style it takes ages for high tier Dinos and equippment to get and you loose it very fast. Sometimes just because a map breaks. With admin tools in single player less of a problem but overall this game feels like the precarious world we live in seems to manifest in software development. Its a constant work in progress without even trying to fix and finish something. Also Valve - usually having high standards - seem to have given up on steam. Of course ark is still decent compared to the pile of s... out there but still. Its one of the most played games and still the bad reviews tell a different story.
You also have tedious stuff ingame like soundeffects. Dinos do different noises but when you press the attack button or you harvest smth its always a repetitive noise. Like a doll for a kid and everytime you shake it it makes the same dull noise. You find a lot of these repetitive things in Ark which is a shame. Pattern variation would do a lot for immersion. Dinos have different skills and single/group behaviour. Thats great but needs to be "evolved" into other areas. Also taming - nice idea but basically you just use a Dino as container for his favorite dish and narcotics. Unless its tweaked it takes ages. For the 1st few animals its fun waiting close to the sleeping giant but it gets boring. There should be really different ways to do it to keep interested. You also take fall damage way to easy and specially in low levels it kills you a lot. Untill you learn the basics and you start with propper mounts and techtree its more or less a dying simulator. Which is fine for a survival game but i miss the feeling i can turn the tide by being smart - i have to turn it by running fast. But even dying can be fun like a boa grabs you out of the saddle and the dinio trie to rescue you while the damn snake drags you into the swamps. There are of course fun parts and well made ideas, no doubt about it!
You also need to love the wiki just because some dinos are obsolete in doing certain tasks like collecting berries. There are a lot of animals in game but the balance could be better. It would also be interesting to be able to teach them different things - imagine dinos with at least a bit of the possibilities the path of exile skilltree gives you. Would be 10 times better than laser rifles.
Another good thing is you can literally build where you want as much as you want (and your pc is able to...). The only downside is the building system is a bit ♥♥♥♥♥y, like sometimes it jumpes to another position when you place a wall or it wont build when the ground is not plane enough. With almost no tool to flatten the ground.
So in the end of the day its what EA became: You get super nice ideas which are not fully developed ingame and may never will be while the game stays for years and years in EA to squeeze out the advanteges there.  So thumb down doesnt mean bad game but the overall package is disappointing especially the performance issues which should be a top priority since ppl complain for years now.

This game is one of the most well-optimized games I've played. I've had a blast with it, and I normally hate grinding as much as you need to to go anywhere in this game. For a quick rundown:
PROS:
-Not a lot of glitches, and a couple are kinda fun actually (kubrow/kavat hybrid monstrosities were fun)
-Lots of variations to base your playstyle on, the Warframes are all fairly unique and accomplish their roles in varyng ways, and the weapons list is a long one, with some hidden gems.
-Most of the bosses are pretty fun, with mechanical know-how required to fight them at-level
-Some fun gore to it (optional), splitting people in half lengthwise with a battleaxe never gets old
-It's parkouring, sometimes run-n-gun, sometimes stealth-based, hack 'n' slash or ranged as you see fit. Space ninja's, as the ads say.
-Some decent story, actually, if you take the time to delve into it.
-Not P2W, the "cash currency" is actually quite easy to earn ingame.
CONS:
-Grind. ♥♥♥♥loads of grind, as far as the eye can see
-The few glitches that do exist tend to be somewhat dealbreaking, robbing you of your time and loot, which, in a grind based game that's all about the loot-for-time ratio, REALLY sucks.
-The community. Now, it isn't League of Legends or World of Tanks bad by any means, but just be wary of the advice you take. people will tell you their own personal meta like it's the new gospel written by Jesus himself right in front of them. Most of them are full of♥♥♥♥♥♥ Nearly everything (not all, but damn close) is viable if you take the time to build it right. Just...god help you if you run into one of them in a match or in chat hile discussing your favorite weapons, because they will abuse in chat with no end.
-Power creep
-The developers. Oh my god the developers. I'll save a separate section for more details.
This game is at the same time ridiculously fun and ridiculously rage-inducing. Yopu can spend hours upon hours jsut farming all the weapons, the mods, the frames, getting rare♥♥♥♥♥♥ then upgrading all those things to be a true badass. Building a clan dojo from scratch with your friends, and getting some of the unique weapons and stuff from there as well. It is a HUGE timesink, and it can be a blast, and it IS free, and no, it is not pay to win. Platinum is easily earnable ingame, simply farm up some stuff and sell it to other players for platinum, it's that simple. The game is optimized very well, and the special effects are so fun to watch as you and 3 other random Warframers just set about obliterating things with an array of colorfully deadly moves and ammo.
That all being said, you must be prepared to grind your♥♥♥♥♥off, and to be patient with the crafting system (crafting a new frame takes 3 days, for instance). There is a learning curve that is quite frankly not apparent at first, and there is no tutorial for tricks beyond the very basics of run-jump-attack (I didn't know how to gain the most airtime until I was Rank 9). You level your account by leveling gear, so if you are a slow grinder, you will not rank up fast, and some weapons are locked behind an experience wall. There is a test to pass for every rank-up you get, and if you don't pass, you have to wait 24 hours, which I think is a great system...if your personal rank meant anything to anyone but yourself in this game, and if some of the tests weren't so stupidly pointless (most of the "skills" tested have very little in-mission value).
Above all else though...the devs are slow, and they are vicious. Do NOT, under any circumstance, criticize them ingame or on their forums, you get banned quite easily for that, it has happened to me (criticized a rather annoying glitch that screwed me during a special event mission run, got chat banned the next day). The saga of RevXDev is an interesting one, not to say he didn't deserve a ban for some reasons, but he got one for all the wrong reasons (check it out on youtube, it's ridiculous, he is kind of a♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥but he makes some pretty good points). Skoliak got banned for being too good, and they still never have told him what "proof" they supposedly have for his "cheating" to top the boards on "Best Interception Run" (over 10 hours in-mission, then the boards got whiped and he got a permaban on his account, a 2000 hour veteran gone like that). If you plan on playing this game, do NOT put money into it, it gains you no leeway if you ever say they have mae a mistake. They have an attitude of "we have the money already, so it doesn't matter now", and quite frankly need to be removed from steam for hostility towards players. They even have a clause where they say they do not have to have a reason to ban you, your time and money gone forever, no explanation necessary.
Think hard before you download this, it can be a blast, but there are some serious underlying flaws, especially with the company. I enjoy the gameplay, but cannot in good conscience recommend it to anyone.

Pretty awesome game. There's almost a dino for every need that simplifies life. Of course, some are not needed when having a big tribe, but those same exact ones are valuable for solo players, and those just starting out. Needless to say, this is a survival game, and the people that play are doing just that.
Ark's mimicks real life ((albeit, I use that phrase  -very- loosely; I mean, we're talking about riding rexes into battle while shooting machine guns, only to jet pack away while the monkey sitting on your shoulder flings poo to blind the enemy. )), in the sense we moved from nomads, and villages, to creating larger and larger communities to survive and thrive in,like cities, as in case of the alpha tribes. At first, there was chaos as some would wipe out all the other tribes, however it would only lead to same tribes rallying together to take down said alphas.
However, the devs have taken it a step further with the server transfers, creating an even larger community. Servers either unite or divide, which leads to large warfare from one server to the next. People get wiped, and people rebuild; in some cases, they quit because they thought their home would last forever on a pvp server.
This is a fallacy, folks: Don't go into the game thinking your "empire" will last forever ((especially if looking to aimlessly grief, which is your perogative to do, but don't go thinking tribes are going to just bend over, and put up with that lol)). If you're looking to last forever, try a pve server.

To say Warframe has changed over the years would be a major understatement. The game presented to players today barely ressembles the game I played 3 years ago.
That's great! Over the years, Warframe has been lovingly polished by its' developers into a free-to-play game that puts many premium priced games to shame. It's clear to anyone that Digital Extremes truly loves the game they have created - from the intriguing art style to the gameplay mechanics, Warframe is a labor of love.
Warframe is a third-person, co-op, looter, mission-based shooter in which players take control of powerful Warframes (basically space-ninjas). The game focuses almost exclusively on PVE elements, although PVP elements are also provided.
The core of the game sees players partaking in various missions to gather resources in order to build new equipment such as new Warframes, weapons, etc. In this aspect, the game can be quite a grind at times, but never unfair. As you may be aware, Warframe is free-to-play. It is
pay-to-win. More on that later.
The gameplay is fantastic! Each Warframe and weapon offers players wildly different play styles that best suit them. Players have incredible control over their mobility and experienced players can often look like performers on a stage. After playing countless games, I have yet to find one that offers the same freedom of movement and exilerating power that Warframe provides. It's pure power fantasy and I'm loving every second of it!
Ah, the topic we all love to talk about nowadays. It's true that many free-to-play (and even premium priced games) like to shake us for every penny we have on hand. Warframe is not one of those games.
Sure, you can buy the premium currency - Platinum - for real world money and aquire new equipment. However, everything that is able to be purchased in this manner can also be obtained completely free by just playing the game. Furthermore, you cannot purchase advantages over others and Platinum itself can be earned by trading for it with other items in-game.
Overall, the existence of Platinum in Warframe is non-intrusive and does not negatively affect one's experience.
Warframe is a game that might just suprise you with the level of depth that can be found. Take it from me, it can't hurt to just give it a try.

The satisfaction of running into a crowd of enemies and meleeing them all to death, or shooting a singular enemy from 100 meters away with a bow, or even sprinting through a corridor with a shotgun is enough to make me recommend this game. Each of the gamemodes are unique and different from one another, and make it a lot of fun to progress through planets.
I have played very few games that give me the same level of satisfaction through progression. At first, the game is incredibly grindy, and will put off a lot of gamers, but if you stick through it, it's worth it. In the game, you have to collect resources for different primary weapons, secondary weapons, melee weapons, warframes, etc. These resources can be a pain to collect, especially since things like plasmids, rubedo, and orokin cells are only present on certain missions, which are generally on the later planets. So collecting them will take time, but once you start to progress further and further, you'll find it gets easier, and a ton more fun.
There is one MASSIVE drawback to this game though, one that, sadly, plagues most F2P games: Microtransactions. The epitome of anger. This game doesn't force you to buy anything, however, you'll be forced to climb a brickwall so massive that you'll give up and quit playing this game if you don't buy some platinum. Platinum is essentially the secondary currency, and the main commodity in this game. Thankfully, you can also collect blueprints and sell them on the market place to other players for platinum, and with the recent introduction of relics, getting these blueprints are much easier. With platinum, you can purchase minor things like colour palettes (since the starting colours are all disgusting), aesthetics for your frames, and resources. However, platinum is also the only way, besides relics, to obtain most blueprints for Prime frames (enhanced versions of the normal frames). And of course, my biggest problem with this game is a limit on weapons and frames. You can only have a certain number of anything at one time, unless you purchase an extra slot for platinum (I think its 20p for 1 extra frame slot, which is a lot of platinum). This forces you to give up the frames that you worked so damn hard for, and to sell them for a tiny amount of credits. It is somewhat infuriating, but not enough to make me stop playing.
Overall, I love this game, and it's 100% worth playing. 9/10

I love this game, but it certainly has it's downsides, namely the early game. The game is incredibly complex to a new player, to an almost rediculous degree. There are a few things you should know about for when you get started.
1: Either find an experienced player to help you learn the ropes early on, or look up a guide. Bookmark the wiki while you're at it. If you can't find a player to help you out, my username is RagingGator.
2: The microtransactions are almost entirely not worth it, unless you receive a discount as a daily reward. There are only two things you cannot get without platinum, and they are slots for your warframes or weapons, and many of the cosmetics. EVERYTHING ELSE you can get through simply playing the game.
3: Farming. This game has quite a lot of it, and if you don't like repeating missions, you might have some problems with the game in general. You can get by without farming somewhat, but to thrive, it's a necessity.
4: Starter mods. When you start the game, it will start giving you 'damaged' mods. DO NOT UPGRADE THEM. They have only half of the available capacity, and are alltogether worse than an undamaged mod. To progress smoothly, you will need undamaged versions of the following mods: Serration, hornet strike, pressure point, (Straight damage mods,) Vitality, redirection, (Health and shields,) flow, streamline, and intensify. (power max, efficiency, and strength.) After you get these, you will be more or less prepared for what the early to mid game has to throw at you, and prepared to progress.
Good luck, Tenno

As you can see i have about 450 hours as of this reviews but that isnt enough to finish this MMOTSP (Only about halfway done).
I would definatly recommend this to gamers who are into games for the experience you gain from teamwork and also those who enjoy games due to the lore aspect of games. With all the optional quest's like Stolen dreams and The Second dream you get to know a lot about not only the tenno but also the lotus, General lore is sprinkled throughout the game in the form of cephalon fragments that give you details about the grineer, corpus and orokin races.
Talking actual gameplay there is definatly a learning and level curve (About MR 5 but changes from person to person) and once you complete the first few planets the actual grind of the game for componants and exp really sets in as you should prepare for the task of completing the starchart (Usually done by MR9-10). So whats next? you have to complete the major lore quests to complete the starchart but what do you after? The final level of the star chart is lvl45 (Ignoring Sedna's arena) and you realise that the enemys are just way to easy to beat. You will tire of the grind for better gear and look for something that is actually a challange to beat. look to the direlict and sorties then finally going on the trial missions to really complete every mission that is achievable ingame.
For those of you who arent looking for a pure PvE game dont worry there is conclave where you can use your gear to test your skill agaisnt other players or for those who arent into the whole fighting with weapons thing there is lunaro. pretty much bordenball but actually lets you bash people to gain posession of the ball.
-PvE and PvP elements that appeal to all gamer-types
-Many different weapons and warframes to choose from leave play-style up to the player
-Interesting lore for the player to search for
-Great community you can look towards if you need a little boost to get that mission done
-Good development team wo look towards the community for input on updates (most of the time- Looking at you vacuum within)
-Its a true Free Too Play (all weapons and frames are achievable without spending a penny, cosmetics not so much)
-Difficult learning curbe that makes the starchart difficult for new players
-Difficult warframes to master (Looking at limbo for this one)
-Boring grind to gain more exp
TL,DR - Warframe is an engaging game for all playstyle's that lets you chose how you go about doing things, putting the player before the devs. Letting everyone have their own choice of what they want to use to complete the game with a friendly community to help new players learn the basics and forgiving gameplay early on that gets harder and mercyless as you complete more of the game.

I played this game for almost six months on PS4 before getting my new PC.
Let's make this clear up front: This game is not Pay to Win. It is Pay to Skip.
Warframe is a co-op shooter where the primary goal is simply expanding your arsenal. Weapons, armors, and mods.
There are tons of weapons and plenty of armors to be had. While they are all available for purchase with real money, everything significant is available in-game with a bit of work to craft. The only things that are premium currency only are cosmetic only, things like cloaks and such.
The basic game cycle is to select a mission, clear the objective while gathering crafting resources, collect your reward, and repeat. This might be repetetive, if this weren't the best shooter I've ever played.
The gameplay is butter-smooth, with no noticable frame drops, even in missions where the entire screen is just filled with utter chaos of enemy swarms, explosions, and blood. Guns have plenty of punch and feel good to use, and there's a full melee combat system as well utilizing all kinds of weapons like swords, axes, scythes, and staffs. And just to make you feel awesome, you can deflect incoming enemy fire with your melee weapon while you move toward them.
The game also has a way of making you feel like an unstoppable juggernaut as you rip through enemy swarms with little to no effort, but it's not without challenge, and has plenty of moments where a mistake will result in you going down  surprisingly quickly.
I feel the real key to enjoying the game is to set attainable goals for yourself, since the game tends to let you go how you want once past the intro. The main thing to cause the game to feel too grindy would be setting your eyes on end-game kind of equipment too soon.
And while I do feel the game is not suitable for marathon sessions, due to becoming repetetive, but an hour or two at a time is absolutely perfect.

I would have loved to be able to recommend this game but I can't. I wouldn't bring my worst enemy on the emotional roller coaster I have experienced during my time with Warframe.
A few things you as a new player need to know.
#As a PC player you are literally Digital Extremes beta tester/QA team. They push out updates that are untested and often there are patches within hours of updates with hot fixes. This is working great for them since they save money not needing a proper QA team/policy to test their updates. And when the update is stable they push it to the consoles.
#Almost every update/rework of Warframe's mechanics, frames, weapons or whatever contains a nerf. Especially things highly wanted by the community. And your playstyle will get hit, sooner rather than later. The only update I remember in the last year that was good is the new endo system. It was not a nerf but an actual buff.
#It's almost impossible to discuss things you dislike on the official forum, the mods get butthurt of any criticism or negativity. Only happy thoughts are allowed on
#It seems like DE have problems with project planning and project management. Every big update with an announced release date gets delayed. The latest update U19 was schedule to release in June if I remember correctly. It was pushed back and split into multiple smaller updates. We just got U19 part 4 and the biggest part of U19, the quest The War Within is delayed to November or even December.
*My Steam time counter is not correct. According to stats ingame I have 1300 hours of gameplay and I don't think I have spent 1000 hours in the Liset.
There are many good and even extremely good things in this game. Just too bad DE is treating their customers as crap. If a company in another line of business treated their customers the way DE manage to do, there would be hell to pay. But DE gets away with it since Warframe is a "Free to Play" game. So many people rush to DEs defence just because it's "Free to Play", "be grateful and not an entitled *insert condescending name*" is often seen. So someone like me that likes to pay to support developers of games I enjoy have no "product warranty". The "Free to Play" business model is extremely flawed. And this complaint is not because I regret paying € for platinum. At that time I wanted to support DE. But the "you can't complain because it's Free to play" argument drives me mad.
I think the biggest problem with Warframe is that Digital Extremes didn't think the game would become popular and didn't have a plan for that scenario. And I'm not sure they even have a plan after 3 years of development. For example the focus system introduced in U18. It was presented as a beta system that could/would change in the future. It's now more than 9 months since that mechanic got introduced and the only big change we got was a huge nerf to the focus gain and an increased daily cap. It's like DE thinks they need to shove as much crap into the game so the player base have something to do instead of trying to "perfect" the game mechanic before they abandon it for x month/years. "Just launch it, we can always rework it in the future = new content" said by someone at a meting in DE HQ, at least that is how I think of it.
But what was the thing that broke the camel's back you may ask? It was two things that is so "Warframeish", nerf and bug. Yesterday after the The Vacuum Within update with the vacuum nerf, I run a syndicate exterminate mission and collected all 8 medallions, found 2 Cyan Ayatan Star, 1 Amber Ayatan Star and an Orta Ayatan Sculpture. And 2 Kubrow eggs which I couldn't pick up so why mention it. When I had 2 Grineer left to kill the map showed one red dot outside the map and after various attempts to finish the mission I had to abort. That sculpture fully upgraded was worth 2700 endo=$12,5 according to market rate. If a bug happens once or during a short period of time, it's ok. But spawn bugs have been in the game since 2013 and the bugs just keeps on showing up. The Dev team might squash 2 bugs but in the next big patch they introduces 3 new once. I think Warframe is the most unpolished game I have played... Ok Just Cause 3 might be worse but that isn't saying much.

This game is one of the most well-optimized games I've played. I've had a blast with it, and I normally hate grinding as much as you need to to go anywhere in this game. For a quick rundown:
PROS:
-Not a lot of glitches, and a couple are kinda fun actually (kubrow/kavat hybrid monstrosities were fun)
-Lots of variations to base your playstyle on, the Warframes are all fairly unique and accomplish their roles in varyng ways, and the weapons list is a long one, with some hidden gems.
-Most of the bosses are pretty fun, with mechanical know-how required to fight them at-level
-Some fun gore to it (optional), splitting people in half lengthwise with a battleaxe never gets old
-It's parkouring, sometimes run-n-gun, sometimes stealth-based, hack 'n' slash or ranged as you see fit. Space ninja's, as the ads say.
-Some decent story, actually, if you take the time to delve into it.
-Not P2W, the "cash currency" is actually quite easy to earn ingame.
CONS:
-Grind. ♥♥♥♥loads of grind, as far as the eye can see
-The few glitches that do exist tend to be somewhat dealbreaking, robbing you of your time and loot, which, in a grind based game that's all about the loot-for-time ratio, REALLY sucks.
-The community. Now, it isn't League of Legends or World of Tanks bad by any means, but just be wary of the advice you take. people will tell you their own personal meta like it's the new gospel written by Jesus himself right in front of them. Most of them are full of♥♥♥♥♥♥ Nearly everything (not all, but damn close) is viable if you take the time to build it right. Just...god help you if you run into one of them in a match or in chat hile discussing your favorite weapons, because they will abuse in chat with no end.
-Power creep
-The developers. Oh my god the developers. I'll save a separate section for more details.
This game is at the same time ridiculously fun and ridiculously rage-inducing. Yopu can spend hours upon hours jsut farming all the weapons, the mods, the frames, getting rare♥♥♥♥♥♥ then upgrading all those things to be a true badass. Building a clan dojo from scratch with your friends, and getting some of the unique weapons and stuff from there as well. It is a HUGE timesink, and it can be a blast, and it IS free, and no, it is not pay to win. Platinum is easily earnable ingame, simply farm up some stuff and sell it to other players for platinum, it's that simple. The game is optimized very well, and the special effects are so fun to watch as you and 3 other random Warframers just set about obliterating things with an array of colorfully deadly moves and ammo.
That all being said, you must be prepared to grind your♥♥♥♥♥off, and to be patient with the crafting system (crafting a new frame takes 3 days, for instance). There is a learning curve that is quite frankly not apparent at first, and there is no tutorial for tricks beyond the very basics of run-jump-attack (I didn't know how to gain the most airtime until I was Rank 9). You level your account by leveling gear, so if you are a slow grinder, you will not rank up fast, and some weapons are locked behind an experience wall. There is a test to pass for every rank-up you get, and if you don't pass, you have to wait 24 hours, which I think is a great system...if your personal rank meant anything to anyone but yourself in this game, and if some of the tests weren't so stupidly pointless (most of the "skills" tested have very little in-mission value).
Above all else though...the devs are slow, and they are vicious. Do NOT, under any circumstance, criticize them ingame or on their forums, you get banned quite easily for that, it has happened to me (criticized a rather annoying glitch that screwed me during a special event mission run, got chat banned the next day). The saga of RevXDev is an interesting one, not to say he didn't deserve a ban for some reasons, but he got one for all the wrong reasons (check it out on youtube, it's ridiculous, he is kind of a♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥but he makes some pretty good points). Skoliak got banned for being too good, and they still never have told him what "proof" they supposedly have for his "cheating" to top the boards on "Best Interception Run" (over 10 hours in-mission, then the boards got whiped and he got a permaban on his account, a 2000 hour veteran gone like that). If you plan on playing this game, do NOT put money into it, it gains you no leeway if you ever say they have mae a mistake. They have an attitude of "we have the money already, so it doesn't matter now", and quite frankly need to be removed from steam for hostility towards players. They even have a clause where they say they do not have to have a reason to ban you, your time and money gone forever, no explanation necessary.
Think hard before you download this, it can be a blast, but there are some serious underlying flaws, especially with the company. I enjoy the gameplay, but cannot in good conscience recommend it to anyone.

Warframe is iffy to me. I hated it when I started some four years ago, I thought "What is this P2W trash?". But about a year later, a friend of mine convinced me to give it another try, and showed me that I was doing it all wrong. Fast forward a few years and I have two prime Warframes with a third on the way, a decked out dojo, and my friend has to leave, putting me in charge of the (empty) clan. I went right back to where I started, a lonely farmer.
To address the elephant in the room, micro-transactions, or platinum in Warframe... Eh. Platinum is used for a lot of things, buying rare materials, rushing buildtimes, buying cosmetics, or trading with other players. There are two ways to get it, as I said, trading with players, or buying it. Buying it is definately easier, but I'd only recomend it if you're impatient (like me) and don't want to farm forma for your dojo. Anything you buy with forma on the market place with platinum will be drastically more expensive than anything you trade for, so either option is viable. (You also get pretty decent discounts every once in a while. I like to buy $50 of platinum for $20 when I can.)
But hey, it's free. Get some friends, and give it a go.

If there ever was a game with smooth and enjoyable enough mechanics to make a grinding game worth it, it would be Warframe.
The graphics are absolutely phenomenal. The movement and overall combat can only be described by smooth and clean. Everything feels very good, especially melee weapons.
But, as I'm sure everyone else has said, this is one of the grindiest games in existence. BUT, you can acquire every single item with enough grinding and trading for platinum. For a free to play to have player-tradeable IRL currency, just, yes. It doesn't feel futile to just keep playing if you don't want to spend money.
Why is a grind bad normally? Because it gets super repetitive and unfun. The mechanics are the fun part of the game, so it doesn't get repetitive that quickly. Also the clan features are great.
9/10.

I played this game for almost six months on PS4 before getting my new PC.
Let's make this clear up front: This game is not Pay to Win. It is Pay to Skip.
Warframe is a co-op shooter where the primary goal is simply expanding your arsenal. Weapons, armors, and mods.
There are tons of weapons and plenty of armors to be had. While they are all available for purchase with real money, everything significant is available in-game with a bit of work to craft. The only things that are premium currency only are cosmetic only, things like cloaks and such.
The basic game cycle is to select a mission, clear the objective while gathering crafting resources, collect your reward, and repeat. This might be repetetive, if this weren't the best shooter I've ever played.
The gameplay is butter-smooth, with no noticable frame drops, even in missions where the entire screen is just filled with utter chaos of enemy swarms, explosions, and blood. Guns have plenty of punch and feel good to use, and there's a full melee combat system as well utilizing all kinds of weapons like swords, axes, scythes, and staffs. And just to make you feel awesome, you can deflect incoming enemy fire with your melee weapon while you move toward them.
The game also has a way of making you feel like an unstoppable juggernaut as you rip through enemy swarms with little to no effort, but it's not without challenge, and has plenty of moments where a mistake will result in you going down  surprisingly quickly.
I feel the real key to enjoying the game is to set attainable goals for yourself, since the game tends to let you go how you want once past the intro. The main thing to cause the game to feel too grindy would be setting your eyes on end-game kind of equipment too soon.
And while I do feel the game is not suitable for marathon sessions, due to becoming repetetive, but an hour or two at a time is absolutely perfect.

I've mostly been playing this game single player because, if the oppurtunity arises where I don't have to play with other members of my species then I will gladly take that option over having to deal with other people.
Regardless I definately reccomend the single player option for this game, despite it being a lot harder to grab together points that allow you to craft things.
Overall, this game is a time killer, and I think that's the best I can describe it as. It's a game you can play if you want to indulge yourself in a bit of time consumption for the most medial of tasks, and personally I'm fine with that. This is coming from someone who initially plays games where you start with nothing and work your way up, and what this game is is probably a glorified, glossy refined version of minecraft with dinosaurs, which is probably it's most prominant aspect: the dinosaurs. This game would probably immediately lose my interests if it weren't for them.
But I'm not going to go off and praise this game for it's "cutting-edge design" and "one-of-a-kind gameplay", I haven't gotten too terribly far in the realm of fully immersing myself into the deeper story or elements within this game, but here's a good idea of what you'll get starting out.
The most memorable moments I have are usually harvesting for fibers and grabbing narcoberries with the intent of taming dinosaurs, so far I haven't really encountered anything that's grabbed me on the edge of my seat (except for the times where I've overestimated my abilities and have gotten killed a few times which had my heart racing). This game's most prominant aspect is it's graphics, which is glaringly obvious. I'm not going to pretend like this is the best game of its brand, because I am well aware there are better survival based games out there with plenty of elements that are worth praise, but for what this is, it isn't as bad as most may make it out to be.
If you're looking for a game like Skyrim, I don't really think this game is for you. The truth is, this game is the core definition of survival: It's time consuming, it's frustrating, but it's worth it slowly building yourself to the top and allowing you to feel some form of accomplishment as opposed to a simple "Well, I did it, NOW what?" So, if you're looking for a game that gives you a taste of surviving out in the open with nothing but your bare rear end and a couple azulberries to get you through the day, this is probably the game for you.

I would have loved to be able to recommend this game but I can't. I wouldn't bring my worst enemy on the emotional roller coaster I have experienced during my time with Warframe.
A few things you as a new player need to know.
#As a PC player you are literally Digital Extremes beta tester/QA team. They push out updates that are untested and often there are patches within hours of updates with hot fixes. This is working great for them since they save money not needing a proper QA team/policy to test their updates. And when the update is stable they push it to the consoles.
#Almost every update/rework of Warframe's mechanics, frames, weapons or whatever contains a nerf. Especially things highly wanted by the community. And your playstyle will get hit, sooner rather than later. The only update I remember in the last year that was good is the new endo system. It was not a nerf but an actual buff.
#It's almost impossible to discuss things you dislike on the official forum, the mods get butthurt of any criticism or negativity. Only happy thoughts are allowed on
#It seems like DE have problems with project planning and project management. Every big update with an announced release date gets delayed. The latest update U19 was schedule to release in June if I remember correctly. It was pushed back and split into multiple smaller updates. We just got U19 part 4 and the biggest part of U19, the quest The War Within is delayed to November or even December.
*My Steam time counter is not correct. According to stats ingame I have 1300 hours of gameplay and I don't think I have spent 1000 hours in the Liset.
There are many good and even extremely good things in this game. Just too bad DE is treating their customers as crap. If a company in another line of business treated their customers the way DE manage to do, there would be hell to pay. But DE gets away with it since Warframe is a "Free to Play" game. So many people rush to DEs defence just because it's "Free to Play", "be grateful and not an entitled *insert condescending name*" is often seen. So someone like me that likes to pay to support developers of games I enjoy have no "product warranty". The "Free to Play" business model is extremely flawed. And this complaint is not because I regret paying € for platinum. At that time I wanted to support DE. But the "you can't complain because it's Free to play" argument drives me mad.
I think the biggest problem with Warframe is that Digital Extremes didn't think the game would become popular and didn't have a plan for that scenario. And I'm not sure they even have a plan after 3 years of development. For example the focus system introduced in U18. It was presented as a beta system that could/would change in the future. It's now more than 9 months since that mechanic got introduced and the only big change we got was a huge nerf to the focus gain and an increased daily cap. It's like DE thinks they need to shove as much crap into the game so the player base have something to do instead of trying to "perfect" the game mechanic before they abandon it for x month/years. "Just launch it, we can always rework it in the future = new content" said by someone at a meting in DE HQ, at least that is how I think of it.
But what was the thing that broke the camel's back you may ask? It was two things that is so "Warframeish", nerf and bug. Yesterday after the The Vacuum Within update with the vacuum nerf, I run a syndicate exterminate mission and collected all 8 medallions, found 2 Cyan Ayatan Star, 1 Amber Ayatan Star and an Orta Ayatan Sculpture. And 2 Kubrow eggs which I couldn't pick up so why mention it. When I had 2 Grineer left to kill the map showed one red dot outside the map and after various attempts to finish the mission I had to abort. That sculpture fully upgraded was worth 2700 endo=$12,5 according to market rate. If a bug happens once or during a short period of time, it's ok. But spawn bugs have been in the game since 2013 and the bugs just keeps on showing up. The Dev team might squash 2 bugs but in the next big patch they introduces 3 new once. I think Warframe is the most unpolished game I have played... Ok Just Cause 3 might be worse but that isn't saying much.
My dislike of Warframe started after U18. Before that I accepted all the bugs and nerfs that happened. But

#Mag pull nerf (the nerf of Greedy Pull wasn't enough), her whole rework sucked. She was a fun corpus killer, it is ok with frames specially designed for specific parts of the game. All 40+ frames doesn't have to be designed for the whole game!
#Hydroid's Tentacle Swarm-Pilfering Swarm nerf, another loot nerf.
#Deception mission nerf to stealth/spawning to prevent people getting focus in a way where they don't have to play 5 hours every day.
#Tonkor, Kulstar aoe headshot nerf, yes one could say that nerf was needed. But the Kulstar went from usable on specific missions to crapiola. I have a 7 forma Kulstar with maxed mods and 16k+ damage. It one-shotted Infested up to L60-70+, after nerf? Haha total garbage and that is on Akkad where you are protected from self damage. Bringing the Kulstar to an "ordinary" mission is suicide in two ways. And now the Tonkor is also kind of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ at L80+ like most weapons.
*Nekros Desecrate nerf, it's almost useless now. Another loot nerf. Do you see the pattern...
*Kubrow Egg nerf. One can only hold one egg that you find as loot.
*Nullifier buffs, where the bubble squashing Frost Snow Globe was the worst.
*Sortie Eximus missions, who the hell came up with the idea that every third enemy should be parasitic or a better question, who came up with the parasitic mod? In a game where the usage of your warframe's abilities is more than half the battle... The idiocy of that game mechanic is mind boggling.
*Vacuum nerf, from 12 m in diameter to 6 m. That is a huge nerf and yet another nerf to the loot mechanic. DE must think that making the game annoying to play is something that will make us want to play more, play longer and spend more € for platinum.
*Dying resets your focus ability "countdown"
*Dying resets your energy
*The endless spam of alarms that mobs activate. I'm mostly a solo player and after 4-6k console hacks, I'm really tired of being forced to hack 3-10 consoles every mission where I'm not running from start-objective-end. Especially in syndicate missions. Or as in Void Fissure mission, why the hell would corrupted enemies run to sound the alarm in a level they are "invading"?
*Having the Juggernaut spawn in almost every mission or the ♥♥♥♥ing Bursas. Both are easy in mp but can easily one-shot you in sp and no one is revive you.
*Corpus ship missions, who the hell designed their ships? Reinforced GLASS! At least in Star Trek they used transparent aluminium.

Let me write a bit of a comprehensive review of this game. Also, my play time is only slightly deceptive simply because some of my friends have used my rig to check in and play on Warframe.
I have 1,000 hours by myself on this game. I have been playing since the day before Update 10.
Let me tell you, the changes I have seen.
I am rather unsure as to where to begin with this review, but here goes.
The quests are rather well done and do let you in on some of the lore in the game itself. As much as the quests can be slightly grindy themselves, they are still worth doing.
Customization of weapons, warframes, colors and accessories never ends. Millions of colors to choose from, tons of attachments to make yourself look more pretty. Please for the love of whatever god you believe in, do NOT be that guy in the game who has no stance and basic colors on all of your crap. You look like a chump.
Companion Mechanics aren't so bad, you can have Dog [Kubrow] Cat [Kavat] or a sentinel. They all give benefits, bonuses, and can fight alongside you. (Insert inert vacuum update appreciation here.)
There are plenty of alerts, challenges, invasions, syndicate missions and relic runs that you can do to get better mods, rewards, weapons, and customizations.
Syndicates and their rewards are great and extremely useful.
The player ships was a great addition to the game and helped organize the arsenal, mods, foundry, relics, etc, in a much cleaner fashion.
The enemies come in all shapes and sizes and difficulties, and trust me-I might be mastery level 19 but I still get the crap beat out of me in some missions. The challenge is always there and that's a great thing.
Recruiting chat is useful-USE IT.
Clan system
It's great, although it is hard to start one and run it efficiently, I started one with the help of a few and it grew to over 250 at one point. The more people to help contribute to research and builds, the better. Plus, there are clan based weapons and warframes that only come from clan research so joining one is beneficial to you.
The Mastery Rank up missions.
They start easy but holy crap, you play long enough, the devs are gonna make sure you're good at what you do. Don't even get me started on the MR19 test. It was fun, but a true challenge.
The tilesets of missions have changed over time and many of them are quite pretty.
The factions all have their units, and even they change over time. I remember when there weren't mutalist moas...those were the days.
The bosses are always fun to go and fight, just remember to let someone else get the kill shot. You know what I'm talking about.
Scanning and getting things put into your codex is actually fun, you can go to easy missions by yourself and just relax and scan, and get out.
The Simalcrum is a wonderful addition as well, allowing you to test your weapons and frames on multiple enemies at different levels to see how much damage you can do. Or, to test whether or not a certain frame build is good.
Passive abilities being added to warframes was another great addition to the game, and helps give you a little bit of an edge sometimes if things go south.
The Void Trader was an awesome addition, as well as primed mods. This also gave you some pretty weapons too, at the expense of your credits and ducats. Which unfortunately you have to sell prime parts for but hey, everyone has extra bronco prime parts.
The relays are an extremely useful place, as well as a cool place to go see and talk to other players (occasionally even the server will bestow it's great wisdom upon us).
ENDO.
This was a massive change especially to those of us with over a few thousand fusion cores. Okay, so endo is what you use to power up your mods that you put on frames, weapons, companions, and the like. Used to be that you had fusion cores to do so, and there was a fusion core market. With the change to endo, the market was all but vaporized. As extremely unfortuante as this was-the endo is still a nice change, to me at least. I still sorta miss my cores though...
The Trading system is much better than it used to be, I recall when it first came into the game.
NO. YOU CANNOT TRADE BASIC WEAPONS/WARFRAMES/BLUEPRINTS OR MATERIALS. Carry on.
Dark Sectors
Now I know that the invasions are off for now, but let me remind you that these missions give LOTS of credits and TONS of materials and XP, so please, if you need XP, go for one of these. They all have their benefits.
I believe that's as many pros as I have for now, and if I think of any more, I will add them.
Now here's what we all need to talk about.
ARCHWING.
This is quite literally, to me, the MOST HATED mode in this game. I will say that when it came around, it was pretty cool. I would sometimes run an archwing mission because, hey, space ninjas...IN SPACE. Am I right?
But here is where it went to literal♥♥♥♥♥♥to me.
The second it was shoved down our throats.
When the relays came to be, there was one orbiting every planet. Then this boss character by the name of VAY HEK decided it was time to 'destroy' them. Which forced many of us to begrudgingly get out our half-leveled archwings, level them up, mod them, and go spend our time protecting these relays. Mind you, there are only three left at this point. Four if you count Maroo's Bazaar. These relays orbit Mercury, Saturn, and Pluto. But the only way to defend these were with our archwings. Yes, we got nice and dandy rewards from it and all, but this game mode is total CRAP. Plus they added in the stupid♥♥♥♥♥submersible missions on Uranus. There are already so many things wrong with that statement right there.
I could spend all day trashing the abortion that archwing is, but I have other things to cover.
The Grind
IT SUCKS. But what sucks the most to me are the relic missions. Yeah it makes things a little more organized and changes up the void rewards, but holy crap guys and gals. It is one horrific thing to go through. It made this game more grindy than it was, which I did NOT think was possible. Yes, you have to wait 24 hours for weapons to build and 72 hours for warframes. It's a wait, it's true. It sucks. But the wait is well worth it. (So what I rushed Inaros, leave me alone. I was excited)
PLATNIUM
I ONLY put this as a con because well, you pay for it with real money.
Oh and trading it, the tax rate on it is INSANE.
Plus the discounts you get on it aren't always that great. I've passed up so many 20% offs, it's bordering on crazy.
The Introduction and Starting Out
Now this is much more lengthy and grindy than I remember it being. I even played through the beginning and tutorial to see what it was like when it was changed. So, what. Everyone starts on Earth now, rather than Mercury? I guess that's part of improving the game though, showing off your new tileset and such. I understand. I guess the tutorial needed a change at some point. But SERIOUSLY. DAMAGED MODS. It's not all that hard to get INTO the game, but the damaged mods make you feel like a peashooting crapwad. It's embarassing to say the least, and honestly I feel like it's slightly discouraging to any new player. But that's what a new player is being all about, right?
Side note-
Maroo's Bazaar.
Okay New players and anyone looking for something in particular.
Do NOT. Bother those of us there that have set up shop with UNSOLICITED BEGGING.
I WILL NOT GIVE YOU MY ONLY BERSERKER MOD. I came to see if anyone was up for trading what I had set up shop for, not what you came there to beg me for. I know the Bazaar leaves you open for unsolicited trades, but that is ♥♥♥♥ing annoying. Try trade chat and the warframe markets first, or even your buddies, before you go looking to trade with people who don't want to just hand you their hard earned things.
That's all for now folks, postive review from a 3 year veteran.

Disclaimer: This review is from the perspective of someone who has spent a great deal of money on items ingame.
Warframe is a game where you get to live out wild fantasies of being a techno space ninja. Its fun, its addicting, and it touches that little part of your soul that enjoys making badguys dead.
What got me hooked on Warframe was how much it reminded me of Mass Effect 3's multiplayer. The whole "fight off badguys while doing X objective with your really cool super powers and/or guns" thing. Mass Effect 3 did it really well and Warframe does it better.
The mission types are fairly varied and, for a newcomer, can be really exciting. I say "for a newcomer" because the game shifts after playing for a few hundred hours. When you're new there is much less a desire to complete levels as fast as possible and more emphasis on exploring and being stealthy. My first weapon was a bow and for the first week or so I played every mission stealthily. It was a lot of fun but you really can't play like this with other people. 99% of the time when you play with other people they rush through the mission really fast and don't give a crap about stealth (this is my biggest problem with the game. Steal and sniping gameplay is not very useful outside of a few maps and mission types. This is something that needs revision as the game moves forward).
But where Warframe shines is in its creativity. There are a ton of weapons with various qualities that make them unique, pets, alternative gameplay modes (lunaro and archwing) and totally unique characters (warframes) for the player to use. The warframes really steal the show here. There is, quite honestly, something to appeal to almost every personality type. You want to be a stealth ninja? Use Loki. You want to be an archer? Use Ivara. You want to be an invincible monkey-god with the power to dissipate into a cloud so as to easily traverse large maps? Use Wukong.
Warframe has a LOT of content.
The cost of admission is free. You don't have to pay money to enjoy it, but if you do enjoy it consider supporting these developers. They're very creative and have made a really great product.

I like this game, in terms of content it can't really be beat. There are two real problems: the community and the developer's lack of optimization. I can't really fault the developers for a bad community so I don't see why people give negative reviews for that, but the optimization is awful. Now, this game is massive so it makes sense that it's hard to run, and I'd be willing to put up with that, if it weren't for the fact that this game is ONE HUNDRED GIGABYTES without mods. 100 GB. That's a crazy amount of hard drive space that personally I can't give up for one unoptimized game, so I have it uninstalled as of the time I'm typing this. If they can fix the worst bugs and optimization problems, I'll probably edit this review, but in it's current state, this game should have had another year to bake in the early access oven.
Worth a buy? On sale for 30$ or less, if you're willing to give up the hard drive space.
Runs well? No, you can lower the settings to fix it but it's still pretty buggy. Given time I'd hope this can become the game it had (and still has) potential for, but we'll have to see.
Multiplayer? Probably better off playing solo or with friends from what I've heard, but I don't have too much experience.
Modding? Amazing and easy with the workshop, but can slow down the game or glitch it more.
I wish I could give a neutral review, but this is a positive because, while the game has it's flaws, I don't really believe it deserves as many negative reviews as it's getting.

One of the most amazing concepts for a game I've ever played that has been completely destroyed by the devs. Before I start digging into the bad, which there's a ton of, I want to say what an amazing one of a kind design this game has.
I played PvE with my boyfriend and his brothers on a private server for about a week and it was such an amazing experience. After my boyfriend took a couple hours to set up the server we all started playing together, and it was wonderful. Starting out on the beach with nothing and just gradually working your way up was such a fun experience. At first we were constantly in danger, always having to watch our backs, but once we created our huts we finally found some safety. But there was always that element of danger when we played and it made the game exciting. Every time I ventured inland in search of resources or dinos I felt on edge. I would be terrified of losing the dinos I had or the gear I took and I loved every second of it. The first time I went to the center I couldn't leave my boat because I was so terrified of all of the caros and raptors I saw lurking around the beach. And the first time I lost my raft to a leed was amazing because it was just a reminder of the constant danger of the world.
But all of that goes away once you advance high enough up the tech tree. Eventually you get to a point where you don't have to worry about any of the dinos you run into. By taming Argents you're able to fly all across the map without ever being challenged, and the large carry weight means you can just bring a couple and mine all the material you want and head back to your base. The challenge goes away. Guns one shot a ton of creatures and flak armor makes it so you can fight most wild dinos in a melee fight. My boyfriend was able to kill an alpha raptor on foot with a pike and flak armor by just running around it and hitting it in its blind spot. Eventually it just gets to the point where you're grinding and taming dinos for no real reason since flak armor and longnecks are all you basically need to become immortal in this game.
So after about a week we got bored of PvE, but there was still so much to explore and do. So we decided to play PvP to try and get the challenge back. The only problem is that there is no challenge in PvP, it's impossible to play and you'll just frustrate yourself if you try. Basically every server has a massive alpha tribe who owns a server, and they go on wipes to make sure that no one else rises up and challenges them. Imagine spending an entire day scouting out a hidden base location and grinding out resources in order to build it and than just having some hacker come along and esp it in the bushes. Hackers aside, the way the game is set up is designed to keep alphas on top and new players on the bottom. All the new stuff that is being added doesn't benefit new players because alpha tribes will never let you obtain them. They block off caves and put auto turrets there so that no one can go down there and get good gear, they place metal foundations in areas that have easy access to metal and crystal so that they don't respawn and other players can't use them. And even if you are somehow able to build a base, it's impossible for you to protect it. I had built a huge fortress with a ton of tames in it that me and my small tribe got that day. When we all logged of that night the alphas on the server  came and destroyed it all. By using the website Battlemetrics, they're able to get alerts sent to their phones when a specific player logs off or onto the server, meaning that they always know if you're online or offline. And because of this they will never attack you when you're online because it makes it a little bit harder for them (even though all their dinos and gear are 3x better than anything a new player can get). And the game is designed so that literally anyone with enough explosives and time can destroy your base (unless you're an alpha in which case you have an indestructible fortress with hundreds of auto turrets and thousands of plant x). There's no defense against this which means you're always vulnerable, even if you have a metal base with a ton of guard dinos.
The devs just seem content to let their game die, every update they put out makes the game a little bit worse. Server transfers were the start of this game dying off. Anyone can transfer onto any server and bring any items they want, which means that alpha tribes can just raid on another server and than leave. Processes like breeding are impossible for a single player to do, if you don't log on for one day during the two week process than your breed dies. If you're not constantly watching over it and making sure it's feed, it will die. This means if you're a normal person and have work or school, than this is something that isn't possible for you to do. Large tribes have giant breeding rooms full of air conditioners and tribe members to feed them so this isn't a problem for them. And the biggest issue with this is that breed dinos can reach a much higher level than wild tames. So anytime you face up against an alpha tribes dinos its always going to be better. And now the devs have added a tek cloning chamber, which is also impossible for small tribes to get because the only way to beat bosses in this game is to tame multiple high level rexes and attack it at the same time. It takes 0 skill to do, all it takes is someone who has a ton of tribe members who do whatever he says. So people saying you need to get better at PvP haven't realized that it takes literally 0 skill to be an alpha. All it takes it tribe members and resources and you can overthrow anyone if you have the time.
My last point is that the game literally punishes you for not playing 24/7. Dinos have to be fed often or they'll die. I had a high level argent that I tamed and it died the next day because I forgot to put food in it's inventory.  That wouldn't be a huge issue but food spoils, so if you go on vacation for a week and you're not playing ark the whole time then all of your tames will die. And if you're not online around the clock than someone will come along and destroy your base. And not to mention all the grinding this game makes you do. This game might as well be called Farming Simulator 2017 because that's what you spend the majority of your time doing. And than when you log off that night someone comes along and steals everything you farmed. If you want to try and go raiding you have to spend the whole day farming materials and at the end of the day you get 40 C4. Meanwhile alpha tribes can get hundreds of C4 within an hour due to all their members, tames, and the exploits they use.
Anyways I'm done with this review. It's sad to see such an amazing and unique idea turned into such a♥♥♥♥♥♥show. To sum it up PvE is cool at first but gets really boring quickly and PvP is a broken mess that you shouldn't even think about trying to participate in.
