I would have loved to be able to recommend this game but I can't. I wouldn't bring my worst enemy on the emotional roller coaster I have experienced during my time with Warframe.
A few things you as a new player need to know.
#As a PC player you are literally Digital Extremes beta tester/QA team. They push out updates that are untested and often there are patches within hours of updates with hot fixes. This is working great for them since they save money not needing a proper QA team/policy to test their updates. And when the update is stable they push it to the consoles.
#Almost every update/rework of Warframe's mechanics, frames, weapons or whatever contains a nerf. Especially things highly wanted by the community. And your playstyle will get hit, sooner rather than later. The only update I remember in the last year that was good is the new endo system. It was not a nerf but an actual buff.
#It's almost impossible to discuss things you dislike on the official forum, the mods get butthurt of any criticism or negativity. Only happy thoughts are allowed on
#It seems like DE have problems with project planning and project management. Every big update with an announced release date gets delayed. The latest update U19 was schedule to release in June if I remember correctly. It was pushed back and split into multiple smaller updates. We just got U19 part 4 and the biggest part of U19, the quest The War Within is delayed to November or even December.
*My Steam time counter is not correct. According to stats ingame I have 1300 hours of gameplay and I don't think I have spent 1000 hours in the Liset.
There are many good and even extremely good things in this game. Just too bad DE is treating their customers as crap. If a company in another line of business treated their customers the way DE manage to do, there would be hell to pay. But DE gets away with it since Warframe is a "Free to Play" game. So many people rush to DEs defence just because it's "Free to Play", "be grateful and not an entitled *insert condescending name*" is often seen. So someone like me that likes to pay to support developers of games I enjoy have no "product warranty". The "Free to Play" business model is extremely flawed. And this complaint is not because I regret paying € for platinum. At that time I wanted to support DE. But the "you can't complain because it's Free to play" argument drives me mad.
I think the biggest problem with Warframe is that Digital Extremes didn't think the game would become popular and didn't have a plan for that scenario. And I'm not sure they even have a plan after 3 years of development. For example the focus system introduced in U18. It was presented as a beta system that could/would change in the future. It's now more than 9 months since that mechanic got introduced and the only big change we got was a huge nerf to the focus gain and an increased daily cap. It's like DE thinks they need to shove as much crap into the game so the player base have something to do instead of trying to "perfect" the game mechanic before they abandon it for x month/years. "Just launch it, we can always rework it in the future = new content" said by someone at a meting in DE HQ, at least that is how I think of it.
But what was the thing that broke the camel's back you may ask? It was two things that is so "Warframeish", nerf and bug. Yesterday after the The Vacuum Within update with the vacuum nerf, I run a syndicate exterminate mission and collected all 8 medallions, found 2 Cyan Ayatan Star, 1 Amber Ayatan Star and an Orta Ayatan Sculpture. And 2 Kubrow eggs which I couldn't pick up so why mention it. When I had 2 Grineer left to kill the map showed one red dot outside the map and after various attempts to finish the mission I had to abort. That sculpture fully upgraded was worth 2700 endo=$12,5 according to market rate. If a bug happens once or during a short period of time, it's ok. But spawn bugs have been in the game since 2013 and the bugs just keeps on showing up. The Dev team might squash 2 bugs but in the next big patch they introduces 3 new once. I think Warframe is the most unpolished game I have played... Ok Just Cause 3 might be worse but that isn't saying much.
My dislike of Warframe started after U18. Before that I accepted all the bugs and nerfs that happened. But

#Mag pull nerf (the nerf of Greedy Pull wasn't enough), her whole rework sucked. She was a fun corpus killer, it is ok with frames specially designed for specific parts of the game. All 40+ frames doesn't have to be designed for the whole game!
#Hydroid's Tentacle Swarm-Pilfering Swarm nerf, another loot nerf.
#Deception mission nerf to stealth/spawning to prevent people getting focus in a way where they don't have to play 5 hours every day.
#Tonkor, Kulstar aoe headshot nerf, yes one could say that nerf was needed. But the Kulstar went from usable on specific missions to crapiola. I have a 7 forma Kulstar with maxed mods and 16k+ damage. It one-shotted Infested up to L60-70+, after nerf? Haha total garbage and that is on Akkad where you are protected from self damage. Bringing the Kulstar to an "ordinary" mission is suicide in two ways. And now the Tonkor is also kind of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ at L80+ like most weapons.

How awesome is it to be a space ninja who can leap from wall to wall, killing hordes of enemies without ever touching the floor? Warframe has kept me entertained for hours; there's just so much the developer got right to create a fluid experience. It's SORT OF an MMO so of course you'll have people complaining that a patch broke this or that and then threatening to stop playing (threatening to stop playing a free game, way to stick it to the man).
In a game like this movement and control of your character is essential and the developer clearly knew this. It has evolved over the years to be pretty freaking easy to master. Combat is well executed; you can cut down a wall of enemies with your rifle and then move in with melee attacks instantly; no having to switch weapons (although you can choose to weild your melee weapon in your main hand for the added bonus of being able to block and "channel" energy into your weapon for added damage).
The modding system for your weapons gives you dozens of possibilities PER weapon (and there are probably at least a hundred weapons in the game with more being released constantly). You don't "level up" the same way you do in other MMO's; each weapon and warframe has its own level which determines how many mods you can equip and the strength of your abilities. Your character also has an overall mastery rank which is like character level but doesn't really effect your stats, it's more for added bonuses like how many player trades you can make in a day and unlocks some weapons.
It isn't perfect (what is) but I've rarely encountered a bug or glitch except for the expected ones immediately after a patch (which are usually fixed within the day, 2 days max). The main reason I don't play as much as I used to is that at a certain point, even though there's always something new to get, there isn't enough new content to keep me interested. Late-game content is pretty thin and the PvP system has never been, and probably will never be, any good. I usually play for a month or two and then take a few months off as by the time I come back there is usually a ton of new things to do.
As it is free to play there are of course in-game transactions but unlike a lot of free to play games you don't really gain anything by buying them other than getting weapons and warframes faster or having a community designed piece of armor. I've bought a few things that I really liked but overall I prefer to just farm the parts I need which doesn't take as long as you'd think. If you play for a few hours in a day you can get a lot of the basic warframes in one or two days. Pretty fair. Some weapons are a bit more difficult to get but still totally possible to get without spending a dime. If you play long enough and get a lot of the rarer prime parts you can trade them to other players for in-game currency and never have to worry about spending your own money.
I typically don't like multiplayer games but this one is executed so well that you always feel like you're part of a team (of course there are the occasional trolls). I highly recommend checking Warframe out; it's free, bro.

Warframe is a game where you get to live out wild fantasies of being a techno space ninja. Its fun, its addicting, and it touches that little part of your soul that enjoys making badguys dead.
What got me hooked on Warframe was how much it reminded me of Mass Effect 3's multiplayer. The whole "fight off badguys while doing X objective with your really cool super powers and/or guns" thing. Mass Effect 3 did it really well and Warframe does it better.
The mission types are fairly varied and, for a newcomer, can be really exciting. I say "for a newcomer" because the game shifts after playing for a few hundred hours. When you're new there is much less a desire to complete levels as fast as possible and more emphasis on exploring and being stealthy. My first weapon was a bow and for the first week or so I played every mission stealthily. It was a lot of fun but you really can't play like this with other people. 99% of the time when you play with other people they rush through the mission really fast and don't give a crap about stealth (this is my biggest problem with the game. Steal and sniping gameplay is not very useful outside of a few maps and mission types. This is something that needs revision as the game moves forward).
But where Warframe shines is in its creativity. There are a ton of weapons with various qualities that make them unique, pets, alternative gameplay modes (lunaro and archwing) and totally unique characters (warframes) for the player to use. The warframes really steal the show here. There is, quite honestly, something to appeal to almost every personality type. You want to be a stealth ninja? Use Loki. You want to be an archer? Use Ivara. You want to be an invincible monkey-god with the power to dissipate into a cloud so as to easily traverse large maps? Use Wukong.
Warframe has a LOT of content.
The cost of admission is free. You don't have to pay money to enjoy it, but if you do enjoy it consider supporting these developers. They're very creative and have made a really great product.

It's quite a shame to see Ark's review section turn into a sea of "Not Recommended". It's even sadder to see these reviews consisting of terribly petty things.
Let me say this to you: If you're thinking about buying Ark: Get it. It's a beautiful game and all these negative reviews, well, they're just opinions. Not fact-based opinions though. What everyone seems to be doing is taking the true beauty of Ark - gorgeous graphics, the immersion and atmosphere, the smooth game mechanics and recent endgame progression, the amount of great content and overall just a wonderful concept for a game - for granted.
Sure, I get that servers are unbalanced. I get that every official server is dominated by an alpha tribe, and no other tribe will ever have a chance against that tribe. Is that the game's fault? No. Nothing the devs could do would stop that. After all, one large group being in power is the path humanity has historically taken and still takes in the modern world. Before complaining about how difficult it is to make progress on an official server, how about playing on your own or on a private server with a friend. Maybe then you'll focus more on the aesthetics of the game, which are unparalleled.
The thing that irritates me the most - people are leaving negative reviews for one of the most recent updates - the flyer nerf. BOO ****ing HOO. Your bird can't move as fast anymore. Maybe this will encourage you to once again re-enter the true exploration atmosphere of Ark and utilise land dinos and convoys of dinos and tribe members to travel. Ark isn't made to be a game where the end-game travel is lightspeed. It's meant to be atmospheric; immersive. Exploration with your friends. Riding through the snowy forest on a pack of howling wolves; transporting mass amounts of metal on a convoy of Anky's from the volcano. Not see how many glitches you can utilise to cram as much of the stuff as you can onto a Quetz's platform saddle. The flyer nerf was bloody needed if you ask me.
The game does have a crippling flaw though - it's optimization isn't great. The game is quickly becoming more bearable and will get a significant boost to performance in the near future with the predicted update to DX12. But I use a GTX 1060 and it runs just fine on max settings. Games like this aren't meant to be run on your GTX 280 HP Laptop, kids.
In conclusion: What I see in the review section is a lot of people complaining about a lot of tiny, petty things - that are the community's fault rather than the devs' anyway. People leaving negative reviews after playing 1000 hours. 2000 hours. If a game hooks you in for that long enough, you are just incorrect if you don't think it is good.
So how about we stop taking all the beauty of Ark for granted. How about we try to play it in it's original purpose; an exploration and survival game to be played with a small group of friends, fighting off wild dinos as you move through the woods on your affectionately named and raised Trikes. How about we stop blaming the devs - the amazing people who put their life's work into developing everything we passionate players love about this game and adding new content at an unrivalled rate - for what the online community has done.
Because this game is a masterpiece. In every aspect of the word.

I have played well over 600 hours, on public, privite and hosted single player/multiplayer servers. After years of game play, I decided to write a short review.
Many of the complaints are just complaining childish self-importance crying overshadowing the real complaints and problems, but after so many hours of play and meeting many new friends I have learned the biggest problem with the game isn't the game, its the community that plays it. Many of the same cry bagging people are mad because they can't bully others due to balances, control public servers with a thousand pillars or they get raided and lose a base or dino's on public pvp servers. So take notice closely the actually complaints as many are just butthurt children.

Now, yes the game has some REAL problems with the optization for some lower end computers, I have no problems but I do know some who can barely even play on decent computers that should be able to at least run on med and yet they can't even get more than 5 FPS on low across the board being one of the biggest problems I have seen over the last few years.
But all in all the game is great, it has a very deep grind of survuval that really pushes you to survive or you will find yourself 30 times dead in the first few hours naked on some beach or forest. Its very unforgiving, it punishes harshly for making stupid mistakes ( takeing low level dino's into areas they should not be is one example). But that is part of surviving is being pushed to the limits and finding a way to make it though the night. Being able to tame, ride, and work dino's is very fun and also rewarding early and late in the game. My complaint on this is later in the game you become so over powered that very few things can touch you and  most of your dino's and the ones that do are so overly powerful that you are lucky if you walk away with anything left and even luckier if your dino survives. After a while PvE get boring without new maps, PvP can be fun but if its not controled on a privite server it can quickly become unbalanced and drives people off servers.
SoTF (Suirvival of the fittest) pvp is actually great! So it can give you that PvP excitement and doesn't interfear with any PvE enjoying some want.
I highly recommend this game if you love dinosaurs, survival games that are very tough from the start with a easy UI and skill system and a very detailed landscape with so many great places to build bases, homes, dino farms, and even cites. Be ready for a lot of grind ( depending on server settings as many privite servers increase harvesting speed and taming times) but when your favorite dino from your childhood it makes it that much more rewarding to toss a saddle on it and ride it into battle or to gather materials.

It's quite a shame to see Ark's review section turn into a sea of "Not Recommended". It's even sadder to see these reviews consisting of terribly petty things.
Let me say this to you: If you're thinking about buying Ark: Get it. It's a beautiful game and all these negative reviews, well, they're just opinions. Not fact-based opinions though. What everyone seems to be doing is taking the true beauty of Ark - gorgeous graphics, the immersion and atmosphere, the smooth game mechanics and recent endgame progression, the amount of great content and overall just a wonderful concept for a game - for granted.
Sure, I get that servers are unbalanced. I get that every official server is dominated by an alpha tribe, and no other tribe will ever have a chance against that tribe. Is that the game's fault? No. Nothing the devs could do would stop that. After all, one large group being in power is the path humanity has historically taken and still takes in the modern world. Before complaining about how difficult it is to make progress on an official server, how about playing on your own or on a private server with a friend. Maybe then you'll focus more on the aesthetics of the game, which are unparalleled.
The thing that irritates me the most - people are leaving negative reviews for one of the most recent updates - the flyer nerf. BOO ****ing HOO. Your bird can't move as fast anymore. Maybe this will encourage you to once again re-enter the true exploration atmosphere of Ark and utilise land dinos and convoys of dinos and tribe members to travel. Ark isn't made to be a game where the end-game travel is lightspeed. It's meant to be atmospheric; immersive. Exploration with your friends. Riding through the snowy forest on a pack of howling wolves; transporting mass amounts of metal on a convoy of Anky's from the volcano. Not see how many glitches you can utilise to cram as much of the stuff as you can onto a Quetz's platform saddle. The flyer nerf was bloody needed if you ask me.
The game does have a crippling flaw though - it's optimization isn't great. The game is quickly becoming more bearable and will get a significant boost to performance in the near future with the predicted update to DX12. But I use a GTX 1060 and it runs just fine on max settings. Games like this aren't meant to be run on your GTX 280 HP Laptop, kids.
In conclusion: What I see in the review section is a lot of people complaining about a lot of tiny, petty things - that are the community's fault rather than the devs' anyway. People leaving negative reviews after playing 1000 hours. 2000 hours. If a game hooks you in for that long enough, you are just incorrect if you don't think it is good.
So how about we stop taking all the beauty of Ark for granted. How about we try to play it in it's original purpose; an exploration and survival game to be played with a small group of friends, fighting off wild dinos as you move through the woods on your affectionately named and raised Trikes. How about we stop blaming the devs - the amazing people who put their life's work into developing everything we passionate players love about this game and adding new content at an unrivalled rate - for what the online community has done.
Because this game is a masterpiece. In every aspect of the word.

Disclaimer: I have never played PVP in this game, that's not for me. I have also played on official servers just briefly.
I'll be honest, the game has its flaws, mainly some bugs and optimization problems (the latter one being the only real issue I have with this game). There was a drama with devs releasing a paid DLC while the game is still in EA state. And there is a new Sci-Fi tek tier, not a good addition to a dino game. That is also a game that made me forget about other games for months - but I guess that speaks in its favor.
However, I can recommend the game with clear conscience. It's given me a hell lot of entertainment, well worth the money put into it. I even bought the DLC mainly to appreciate the devs' work, because I felt like ripping them off for 600 hours of gameplay for 28 euro, so that drama didn't really concern me.
I recommend trying this game at first without checking online solutions and guides, unless you have some serious problems with some specific issue.
At first I ran the game in single player mode, just to check it out. I kept checking it out in that mode for good 200 hours. And I haven't even moved close to understanding or discovering that game properly. It was a hell lot of fun from the very beginning. Unlike quite a few survival games I've played, PVE (and even SP) has enough in it that it doesn't require enemy players to be engaging and challenging. The reason for this are dinos. In time you learn how they react and how to outwit them, but at the beginning even a single raptor can be a challenge.
Then I moved on to PVE official server for just a few hours. However, that mode is very grindy (and not exactly my jib), so I tried unofficial servers. And I stayed there ever since.
You understand how important metal is, how to use rafts effectively (for those I actually do recommend online guides, especially for "embedding" foundations into rafts), how and when to use narcotics or narcoberries... That's just the top of the tip of the iceberg regarding this game. Finally, you learn how to properly tame dinos, how to use each one of them... how to breed them properly (and damn, that's actually way more compley than cross Mr X with Miss Y and make a baby, unless a crappy baby is all you're aiming for).
Then there is an issue - why bother to play PVE, why breed those even better dinos? Well, because of bosses. And that's both a pro and a con. Like in many MMORPGs, killing bosses is there to tell the world that you did it, to test your preparations and dedication. And skills, to some extent. However, killing bosses also gives you some access to TEK tier, which, as I said, I'm not really fond of. There is also a semi-boss dino, that can be tamed (but not used in fights against the actual bosses).
To be honest, there is too much to write about this game. Over those 2 years it's grown to be really complex.

This game is fun, and I'm giving it a positive review, however, if you're not willing to do a few quick tweaks to make it run smoother, then you shouldn't get the game. It takes only five minutes to go from 5 fps to 60 fps. I've never used steam in my life and I was able to do it, with the help of the internet's guidelines. I recommend it to those who are willing to actually try to make it better. EDIT: Now that the price has jumped, I would recommend buying it in the summer or winter months for the cheapest prices. If you're thinking about getting it, check the price every day. I got it for ten dollars. Like I said earlier, you will need to make a few tweaks to allow your computer to survive if it's not one of the better PCs or computers. Most of these tweaks are really simple, like using d3d10 in the launch options. Some of them involve lowering the graphics.
The game itself:
Good:
Ark has a very challenging setup if you're going to play it without changing the settings. It would be impossible to survive, resources seemingly extreme for a simple saddle. But, changing some of the settings, like harvesting settings for example, can make this kind of thing really quick. Baby hatch time and taming time can be sped up too, as well as a day/night cycle control. These all make it more enjoyable for people like me, who just wander about and tame Megalosaurus and nothing else because they're pretty and cute.
Bad (Also how to deal with):
Even with the change in settings, some of these things (like taming) can take up to twelve hours. It's a little annoying, so once I knock a dinosaur out, (Or set down an egg) I tend to it in my free time on ark and until it's tamed, usually spend my time typing (Do whatever you want) and set an alarm for every five or so minutes after building around it with thatch to keep the unwanted ones out. This can get taxing though, and it's hard for me to organize my resources. For example, storage just simply isn't big enough for me to do what I want to. I end up having to drop lots of items that lag the game so that I can collect the loot crates I run into. The loot usually is worth it though, except for when I think that it's going to be fantastic and it ends up as thatch and wood.
Anyways, overall I'd give this game a 9/10, although the price now is quite steep.
Further edit: DEVELOPERS FIX BIOME TRANSITIONS! I don't want to sit for so long watching as I can't do anything to help my Megalosaurus when I leave the cave for a hunt at night, or when I jump in the water and end up being knocked unconscious by Titanoboa. (Cause I get stuck, screen freezes, and then when my game starts to respond again somethings happened to me, like being unconscious underwater with a titanoboa attacking me and leaving the cave where I live to hunt, only to end up with my megalosaurus seriously injured because it couldn't move. This has also happened with transitions to the Frozen plains areas and the swamp biomes. The two most frequent and strongest lag spikes though are entering the water and leaving or entering caves, but mainly leaving caves.)

At first I was very hesitant to play the game, but after weeks of pushing from my friends I finally caved and decided to play it; and I don't regret a second of it. The game has a fantastic community, and a very large amount of content that is regularly updated by Digital Extremes; though it can get grindy at times with its Mastery Rank system, it still offers a very large variety of playstyles that you will eventually be forced to try out in order to move on to the next Mastery Rank.
Despite the Prime Access and Platinum, this game is definitely not play to win. Aside from various cosmetics and paid access to Prime items and Warframes, everything else is very much obtainable in game. Even the Prime Weapons and Warframes are obtainable, albeit with a lot of grinding for them. They will occasionally place Prime Warframes and Weapons in the Prime Vault, but are known to even open up the Vault on occasion to allow players who missed the opportunity to obtain them another shot at getting them. The only items permanently unobtainable, are the Founders Exclusive items including Excalibur Prime.
Now, you CAN play the game strictly solo if you want; but the cooperative play is where it shines, and it will definitely alleviate the difficulty of certain missions. Though, don't expect to do end game things such as sorties or raids solo; everything else, however, is fair game for anyone willing to take on the challenge.
Out of all of the MMOs I have ever played, Warframe is the only one that has managed to keep me coming back. Its high paced, action gameplay which combines class-based combat; gunplay; and melee gameplay is extremely smooth. However, I will admit it can get repetitive occasionally. Every Warframe, and every Weapon is viable endgame; so do not worry about your favourites being scrapped. Just throw a Catalyst/Reactor, and change the weapon/warframe Polarities with Forma and you can continue to make them more powerful.
I would say Warframe is friendly to both casual and hardcore gamers alike, including having its own PvP mode; Conclave. Though, I don't participate in Conclave myself, I can definitely see the allure to competitive players. Only certain mods are permitted in Conclave, to help maintain balance. So, a new player will be on roughly the same playing field as even a veteran player provided you are not using your starter equipment.
Overall, I would highly recommend the game to anyone looking for an MMO that is both unique and diverse in terms of gameplay; or to anyone preferring a more action-based experience over the typical point and click MMO experience.
Later Review:
Plains of Eidolon has only sweetened the game's pot, adding a very large; open world space to the game. The only caveat, is it can get repetitive after some time. But, due to changes with the Operator system, and intriguing story, and the ability to get things once locked behind raids (Arcanes specifically,) the game is only showing more promise for the future.

So many people with hundreds, if not thousands, of hours complain and hate on the game. Truth be told, that's a very extensive amount of time to play something you "dislike", isn't it? So there has to be more than that.
And there is. Ark is a wonderful game with very big ambitions and a lot of content. It's a sandbox, so whatever you make it is yours to play. You can go alpha, stay solo, go PvE and have fun, etc. Most of the hate reviews on the game are from hardcore gamers that don't understand that this game is still in development. There will be bugs, there will be Chinese players hacking and doing crap, but these things get ironed out with time.
Wildcard is one of the best devs in the regard that player feedback is taken into account nearly always, as permissible by their goals. If people want something and they decide it's good, it gets put in. Player feedback is acknowledged, player content is made official (maps, etc.) and they aim to have the players involved in the development and growth of the game. They did release a DLC pre-release, but that's their choice, and that DLC is god damn amazing in terms of content, I have they release more.
I haven't said much about the game so far. Long story short - You tame dinos, build stuff, breed, gather, can go underwater and do the same there. There's some end-game progression in at the moment that isn't as tweeked as people want it to be. You have tribes that on PvP servers fight each other and wreck everything in the process. You have peaceful PvE servers that can be pillar'd all over sometimes. It has its pros and cons, but I would say that the pros outweigh the cons significantly and the game is getting better and better each month.
I'm waiting for official release myself, having put nearly 1100 into the game and want to do more, but decided to stop as not to burn out on content. 4-5 months after I stopped, there's so much new stuff that I feel like I'd have to discover the game again.
Just, buy the game, give it some time and you'll enjoy it. It grows on you, and you're making an investment that will pay itself off in time.

The game can be great however to be able to enjoy this game here's a few things/tips your gonna wanna do.
step 1. Stay the ♥♥♥♥ away from offical servers, otherwise your gonna have a really bad ♥♥♥♥ing time. Your not gonna become the next alpha tribe there pretty much set in stone at this point. I can't stress this point enough at all, just stay away from them....
step 2. Download and make sure the unoffical server has some mods trusts me without S+ a stacking mod and a few other quality of life mods. Your only worsening and making your gameplay experience terrible S+ allows you to actually build decent structures pretty much all unoffical servers have S+ at this point, it's in my opinion required at this point. Step 3. Make sure the server you are playing on is not standard ark rates, only if you hate grindy games or have a job this is important otherwise your not gonna enjoy the game or get anything done.
step 4. If your not a pvp person avoid pvp servers this should go without saying, but just don't do it man so not worth it...

Step 6. You may wanna read a guide or two now the game is massive and there's a lot to learn starting out and you will be completely clueless otherwise. Step 7. Build a simple bed as early as you can this allows you to respawn back there when you die, ark is a pretty big map so trying to find your base again when starting out can be annoyingly hard. Not to mention you only have limited time to get back to your body or bag before it's gone.
After you do those steps you will enjoy the game so much more. I find the first few steps are a must and i can't stress that enough. At any rate i wish you all good luck. I hope i helped a few people out in the process.

After almost 400 hours of gameplay in Ark: Survival Evolved, I can say it is a brilliant game with huge potential. The key to enjoying yourself here is having friends to enjoy the game with. The game is fairly pointless without a tribe as all of the challenges will be too great to tackle solo and have it be enjoyable. Something as simple as building your first house is made immensely easier and more rewarding if you are doing so with a tribe. Taming something like a high level T-Rex will take you several hours on your own... maybe half an hour to knock the thing out, then 5 hours of sitting and defending the unconcious dino from wandering predators. For this reason it's nice to be in a tribe so you can take shifts and not have to spend 5 hours of your life sitting and waiting.
Taming takes wayyyyyy too long on official servers. Friends and I did have fun taming powerful dinos for the first time, but after that, it's just a chore and makes losing dinosaurs terribly frustrating. Sometimes this happens randomly when they fall through the level or glitch through a wall into a cave. A common theme in the game is working incredibly hard to achieve something, only to lose it shortly thereafter due to circumstances out of your control. I lost my first T-Rex because I was sprinting through the jungle and ran out of stamina right before hitting a river which was full of Megapirhanas. My T-Rex got stuck in a river deep enough only to cover its feet and was mauled to death by low level fish. This is a perfect example of stuff that WILL happen every time you play, making you wonder if the time spent is really worth it.
It boggles my mind that this game is still in Early Access because it has been in roughly the same state for 2 years now. The devs keep adding dinosaurs and maps but core features still aren't working right, there are weird map bugs, and a ton of polishing that needs to be done. How a game can be in early access but have paid DLC out just doesn't sit right with me, especially when so much other technical aspects need work. I was excited about Primitive Plus DLC until I learned that it'll take 15-20 mins to load the world every time you want to play (with a solid state drive).
I have a hard time not recommending games that gave me hundreds of hours of enjoyment, but this is one that the devs are screwing up. Cross-server transfers ruined the game for many people, alpha tribes dominating PvP servers ruins the game for many people, and at this point we need less new content and more existing content to function correctly. The game is a huge time sink with no payoff, because the minute you stop playing your work begins to be undone. If you don't log on for a week, you will log in to find yourself dead, your dinosaurs gone, and your base completely destroyed. That's not a game, that's a job -- one that can sometimes be fun, but a job nonetheless.

As far as F2p, online, rpg-like shooter games go, this is the best thing on the market.
Graphics/Sound/Immersion:
The game looks and feel unique and awesome.  You really do feel like a Space Ninja/Power ranger/Terminator/Space badass while playing the game.  The abilities, weapons, warframes... etc, it's all awesome.  On top of it, this game is one of the best optimized games that I've played.  I ran it really well on my old potato back in the day, and it still managed to look decent.
Gameplay:
The actual gameplay is really fun though not extremely complex.  The different warframes all play differently and feel very different.  The weapons also feel different from each other, and there are a lot of cusomization available as well through modding.  Though the game is sort of the "grind for better things to be better at grinding", the gameplay is fantastic so it is easy to sink a lot of hours into it.
Content:
The game is F2P, and it is pretty fair.  You are able to get everything in the game just by playing, and most things are not hard to get.  Yeah, there are a few things that are extremely grindy to get, but there are a lot of shortcuts you can find if you know what you're doing.  A good 50%+ of the content are easy to unlock, so you really shouldn't feel the grind that much.
Overall, I would recommend this game to anyone, especially since it's free to try.  If you like shooters, pve online, or futuristic RPGs, you should definitely give this a go.

I got into this game late - 3 years or so after release. I waited so long because I hate freemium games and did not think it worth my time. A recent "Top 100 Games" site had Warframe in it, so I decided to give it a try.
Overall, I like the game. Graphics are great, sound is great, voice acting is very good, etc. It has a basic plot that is interesting, and there are dozens/scores of other missions to play, once you open things up.
It is a grinding game. You grind for everything, and that is where they tempt you for cash. Don't want to grind for days/weeks/months? Buy some platinum. Want more warframe slots or weapon slots? Yeah, that takes platinum. And you only get platinum early on by buying it. Later, when you are established, you can sell rare items to other players for platinum, but it takes a while to get to that level, and you will need platinum well before that to truly enjoy the game.
Yes, you can play the game without spending a dime. However, that process will be frustrating at times when you cannot hold more weapons/warframes due to a lack of slots and are forced to sell off (for in-game credits, not platinum) items in order to open up inventory space. I am at the point where it makes sense to buy some platinum, and the suggestion from seasoned players is to wait until you get a 50% or 75% off daily bonus.
The game is much more fun if you play with others. You can play solo all the way through it, but it is so much better if you play with a team. Clan communities are very friendly and helpful. You will find random high level people who are interested in helping you out. Often they will ask in chat if you need help with any missions, grinding for some element/item, etc.
The game is unreasonably complex. There are so many weapons, so many warframes, so many items, and so many mods for all those items, that it is overwhelmingly complex at the beginning. There really is no good tutorial, and your best bet is to read the wiki, watch some YouTube videos, and join a clan so people can explain things to you. Even then, some of the high level missions your clan-mates bring you on are so fast and complex that you will be lost. This game takes time to learn.
Given that most AAA games cost $40 - $70, and that $50 with a 75% coupon gets you a reasonable amount of platinum, it is a reasonably price to pay for the benefits of platinum.
Missions are anywhere from 10 - 20 minutes in length, so you can spend as little or as much time in the game as time allows.
I could never get in-game chat to work, no matter what I tried. I tried using Steam's voice controls - no dice. I tried in-game voice controls - no dice. In-game voice testing proved my mic was working fine, but it just does not work in-game. I finally ended up joining a clan and using TeamSpeak.
The folks in the ArsTenno clan are very helpful and friendly, although they always deny it.
I give it a 4/5 if you put the time into it to learn, join a clan, play online, and get some platinum. If you insist on doing solo and free, I give it a 3/5.

Warframe has the smartest business model of all Free-To-Play games on the market. It is a business model that invites you to spend money to accelerate progress or acquire cosmetic stuff, but does not force you to.
The entire game is truly free to play. The entire game works very well and is in active development for years now, receiving mechanics reworks and balance tweaks throughout its entire lifespan. And the game's economy is very much tied into the business model and the game's mechanics. A smart trader in-game can save real world money and still get everything he wants. Those who don't want to, get a great return on their investment because of the many metric tons of gameplay content the game has to offer.
Onto the game itself:
Warframe is a third person action game, with a surprising amount of depth and serious amount of progression to be had. It contains a good dose of pretty deep RPG elements and character/loadout building, mixed in with fast paced and highly mobile action. It runs on a toaster, and it runs well.
Each different Warframe in the game presents a small subset of very specific playstyles, with a large variety of roles available. Warframes are built from blueprints, of which the components are available as drops in the game. Every single Warframe and almost every weapon in the game can be built without spending a single dime - or you can buy/trade yourself a shortcut. Timed events offer some of these drops, while the vast majority of them is readily available in regular missions. Farming and grinding for new stuff, both Warframes and weapons, is the meat of this game. The farm never ends, and the game is built around that principle. As a consequence, the farm is as fun as you make it, and can be approached in any way you like.
Constructing a Warframe or a weapon takes days, up to a week, of building time. This game wants you to return often and play a bit, and allows you to come online whenever and however much you like, while still offering meaningful and entertaining time spent regardless of how dedicated you really are. You won't be missing out on too much - just keep an eye on special events that offer truly unique pieces of kit!
In conclusion, Warframe has my upvote, but only as long as you approach it for what it really is: a fun and fast-paced space-ninja action game. If you approach this as an MMO and play it as such, you are doing it wrong and will eventually, sooner or later, become disappointed. Warframe offers no persistence, no real end game, just more content to explore - always and forever.
NOTE: This review aims to globally describe the game, regardless of content patches and updates / changes to the game. It therefore goes into less detail, but will always be accurate!

It was on special, I had some spare cash floating around, thought I'd finally give this thing a look.
And right off the bat, no I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone.  Not even tempted to try multiplayer given the stories that fill most reviews.
The singleplayer experience is a mess.  A lethal mess.  Going with everything on default I was shanked by a Raptor just far enough in that regathering everything was going to be a pain.  Said Raptor never moved far enough away from my corpses to manage a recovery.  After adding two more to the pile at his feet I decided heading up the beach next respawn would be a better option.
Troodon turned out to be the bane of my existence.  Zippy little buggers with poison and a nasty bite.  My next attempt at exploration ended abruptly in a valley full of them.  Hanging round near my starting area just resulted in more deaths, taming anything just resulted in it dying along with me shortly afterward.
I checked, yes I was on singleplayer, not some multiplayer mode where the other players are dinosaurs.  It was... unsettling...  just how closely my first playthrough was mirroring the gankfest horror stories from other reviews.
Next respawn I tried a different area, somewhere down south, and found a spot that was just getting occasionally visited by Dilophosaurs.  Things were a bit calmer, but any attempts at moving up the valley or north along the beach were met with the usual gruesome deaths.  Water was full of piranha things, and at one point a fast moving Baryonyx scared the everloving jibblies out of me by bursting up out of the water.

Gate the bigger stuff out, have a CLEAR progression for that first hour. A half destroyed base somewhere near the starting point to give a sense of what can be done?

Overall Warframe is a great game. Good graphics, runs well on most PCs, very smooth controls and movement is fluid, the mission types are engaging and keep you wanting to progress further into the game.
People who complain that it's too "grindy" are missing the point and purpose of what the game is. Warframe is not an open world RPG where you can simply roleplay without putting in any work, the entire point of the game is about fighting and doing missions. It also isn't supposed to be a game where you can get your gear and characters up to max tier within a week. You're meant to spend a lot of time on it to rank up and get the gear that you'd like. While you can straight up buy your stuff with platinum (the currency that you purchase with real life cash), you are not obligated to and you don't have to as almost everything outside of cosmetic items can be built with in game only materials, albeit taking more time to craft.
The devs made a good in game trading interface for players where you can get platinum for items that you acquire with only in-game materials, such as prime gear parts and mods. If you are dedicated and seriously want something that is only obtainable with platinum, you can get it through effort and trading worthy items to other players that would want what you have. It takes time, but if you don't want to spend any cash, you can still work for what you want.
I do recommend playing the game with at least one or more friends though if possible, as it's a lot easier to learn and figure things out with a friend to help you, especially if it's someone who has already played the game before and can help get you a headstart into learning the core game mechanics. Playing solo is still viable though, since there's a huge amount of player-to-player interaction, and you can figure out almost anything you need by just searching through the warframe forums or steam community page.
Onto the actual gameplay and bread 'n butter of the game, everything really flows together really nicely in this game. I'm a huge fan of the movement system, since you can be really agile and parkour around maps, and it's all extremely fluid feeling. All of the warframes are pretty balanced and you can do a decent amount of work with any warframe you choose to use, given that you equip and upgrade proper mods to your gear. Mods are basically just 'boosters' to your weapons and your warframe (Your warframe is basically like your class, btw. Your warframe is what gives you all your abilities and sort of defines what your role is in the game.) and they apply various different perks and bonuses, and you can further ugprade to get even more out of them. The weapons are decently balanced as well, of course the harder you have to work for a weapon and the higher rank it is, the better it'll be, just like any other game, but with proper mods you can turn even low quality weapons into pretty good ones.
Some people say the game gets repetitive, which I could see why people would think that, but it really depends on what kind of person you are and what kind of games you find personally fun. I for one haven't gotten bored of Warframe yet in the 2 or so weeks I've been playing it. Warframe definitely isn't an open world game, but it still has a good community with loads of content to explore and learn about. There are hundreds of different weapons to choose from, so you can always switch up your playstyle and try new things to keep the game fresh. If you go into the game with an open mind and not expecting it to be a f2p version of WoW, you'll have a lot of fun.
If you like to be a perfectionist in games and always want to seek out the best possible outcomes and the strongest gear in a game, Warframe will be awesome for you because you can spend days upon days hunting down the rarest and most powerful weapons and mods to gear up with. With the alert mission system, there's a bit of luck involved with getting the best gear as well, since you may or may not be online while something super good pops up on the alerts, so you may end up having to wait for it to pop up again if you aren't on in time to get it.
All in all, Warframe is a good game, especially since it's totally free to play. It's hard for me to find a real complaint when I'm not in anyway obligated to play the game if I don't want to. The only negative thing I'd have to say is that corpus missions suck. Corpus enemies have a bunch of shields, plus they have flying drones that give even more shields as well as certain enemies who nullify your abilities. They also deal pretty good damage, especially as you go later in the game. If the enemy spots you and triggers the alarm and you don't clear it fast enough, a tank-like enemy called a Bursa will come rushing in and wreck your day, while being pretty hard to kill in most circumstances.
This paragraph is probably going to sound stupid but I just need to comment on it. The single worst part for me is these enemies in corpus missions that I like to call "turkey legs" (or MOA, which is their actual name.) They are literally just a pair of green mechanical legs with a gun on top. They seriously look like some sort of oversized robotic bird legs running around the place. Their design is so absurdly silly that I can't help but get angry whenever they kill me or when a swarm of them come to attack me with their never ending laser gun attacks. There's also the infested MOA, but at least their design kind of makes sense to some degree since they're actually a living thing and it looks like they got hit with some sort of plague. With the corpus MOAs, I can't help but imagine this stupid picture in my mind of some mad scientist in a lab creating the corpus turkey legs with them flooding off of a conveyor belt thinking the design is super wicked and unstoppable, when in reality it's no joke, just a pair of green legs that shoot at you while looking hilarious running around the map.
Also, the boss fights can get a bit ridiculous at times, since some of them are literally invincible unless you hit them in super specific spots, make them use an ability so that they become vulnerable, or use a specific type of damage against them. The game usually gives very little indication of what to do, aside from Lotus perhaps making a small comment here and there about the boss's general weakness, for the most part you have to either figure it out on your own, or search up how to beat the boss. While not unbeatable, I'd recommend finding someone to bring along with you if you need to do boss fights until you get stronger gear at least. It's usually easy to find someone in the recruitment public chat, so I'd try that if you don't know anyone personally who plays warframe. A lot of people are usually willing to give a helping hand, especially if you're somewhat new.
Anyways, this game is overall very enjoyable, and for being free to play it would never hurt to at least try it for an hour and then just uninstall it if you don't like it.

The Devs promised optimization, optimization, optimization throughout the one year developement cycle. Two years later, still in EA and waitng for an optimized game.
- The Devs continue to build and update this game regularly.
- After two years of EA, it is still doing well with Steamcharts reporting that the average player base has been consistent at 42,000 with an all time high peak of 100,723.

- You can host your own server.
- The game can be very fun.
- The problem with the game is it can cripple high end gaming systems. The game seriously lacks any optimization on both PC and console.
- The gameplay is unbalanced making it very difficult for new players to play and enjoy the game.
- There are still a lot of bugs and they seem to multiply with patches.
- An expansion pass (costs 67% of base game) for an EA game is ridiculous, even if it was to resolve funding due to a contractual/legal settlement.

This is an EA title and as such the bugs, balance issues, and optimization should be remedied prior to the full launch. The game has a lot of content and multiple modes for those that can play it without issues and those that choose to dredge thru with low settings and frame rates. As an EA game, I do recommend it but keep in mind it does have issues.

This game has and will entertain me for some time to come, but I can not recommend you to get into this game as a new player.
Let’s start with the ninja theme. Its cool and all hopping up and down walls and throwing ninja stars and what not. But that's about as far as the Ninjaing goes. And you'd think that with mission types labeled as "Assassination" and "Spy" THere would be a good amount of stealth, right? WRONG! There is nothing in this game that can’t be brute forced with a little bit of speed and a good gun. The assassination missions are just kill/run past the dudes to fight a big dude, who is sometimes not a hard as the dudes who preceded them, and run to the exit. And the spy missions are more of the same. Kill/run past some guys, bruteforce a short stealth segment, and run to the end for loot.
As for the other mission types you have Extermination, Defence, Mobile Defence and interception. Extermination should be self explanatory, kill all the things. Defence is a gamemode where you defend a thing from the guys for 5 rounds and you repeat this 4 times for the best loot and bail. The mobile defence game mode is where you defend X points from the dudes all over the map and run to the exit when you’re done. And finally there’s Interception which is King of The Hill but with 4 points instead of 1.
Now luckily for us this game is early access beta and all of this will be fixed upon releasing their finished product.
Pfft, yeah right.
This game has so much potential, or had. But somewhere DE started caring more about the money and less about their fans and product. They pay people to play their games and make their game look good, when there are blaring, obvious problems. Like recently they said they were trying to minimize grind so players didn’t get burned out. Now we are several updates past that and the grind is so much harder than before. It used to be you’d do a mission for a key that unlocked a special mission and you’d play that mission hoping for the reward you wanted. And you’d repeat that until you got the thing you wanted. Now you do a mission for a rock which unlocks a special mission and hope you get the reward you want. BUt now you can run more of these special rock missions to get another resource to alter the drop tables of these rocks and STILL not get the reward you wanted. Effectively not changing anything at best and at worst adding in more steps and more grind time.
Now how about we go on to the weapons. The weapons in this game are pretty fun. There’s a wide variety and something for almost anyone. Now there used to be a huge problem with weapon tiers, but with recent changes to the game almost any weapons with a few forma thrown into it can take on the entire universe and then some. But this has left people who grind out all this stuff without challenge. What’s the point of us having grinded out all these top tier weapons that can take a chunk out of the planet with the single squeeze of a trigger when Mr.Joeblow and his pump-action shotgun can do the same thing? Is it the gold bits on my gun? It’s gotta be the gold bits. It’s always been for the gold bits.

Ark...Just saying the title makes me cringe. The default settings for this game are borderline impossible, and even with settings lowered it's still unforgiving, oh, and WHY THE HELL IS IT STILL EARLY ACCESS AFTER 3 YEARS WHEN IT WAS SUPPOSED TO LAUNCH IN 2016?! That being said, DO NOT PAY FULL PRICE! I think I bought the game for $12 and only just bought the JOKE that is Scorched Earth for $7.
Overall Game:
It's a fun game...when you have friends, taming significantly lowered, faster level up, and a lot of patience and tolerance. This isn't a game you can just sit down and play for a few hours; in our first playthrough with my friends, we didn't have a base and good dinos (dinos that can fly or help you quickly gather resources) until I was about 100 hours in. And that was with lowered taming, fast level up etc. Like I said before, even with everything lowered he game is pretty unforgiving; feels like the Dark Souls of survivial games. Mods help make the game a little easier; oh and screw PVP. The players aren't friendly at all and will attack/kill you the second you join if a dino doesn't kill you first -_- so I only play PVE with friends so I at least get killed by a dino when I spawn, and respawn, and respawn....this fricking game
The game is low-key broken with glitches and OP dinos just cause. It's like everythime players find a way to survive better, the Devs add some ridiculous new dino to punish you. For Example: Devs: Oh! Players are using the rafts to build mega boats to easily and safely traverse waterways and tame dinos from afar and safely bring them home! That's Great! LET'S ADD A BOAT EATING WHALE IN THE NEXT PATCH THAT YOU CAN'T ESCAPE FROM AND DEVOURS EVERYTHING ON THE BOAT; I low-key HATE this game
I do have to say Ark has taught me how to better cope with signifcant losses in life...Now when my lvl 140 beast of a dino dies, I just sigh and look for a new one...to start all over again...*sighs*
Scorched Earth:
How does ark in the wastelands of hell sound to you??
FIRST OF ALL: You have no business releasing PAID DLC for an Early Access game, wtf?? This game has had Mixed reviews ever since...
SE is Ark, but like in the wastelands of hell. We joined a server with such high level up speeds we were level 107 in FIVE MINUTES. In 3 hours we built a base in an oasis, tamed a few dinos, made some metal armor, and explored the area around us a little. Then we quit for the night only to come back in the morning to no base (it was literally ALL GONE) and a Wyvern killing the inactive bodies of my three friends and the last of our dinos....Inspight of that traumatic loss, we'll be playing SE again. I do have to say the added challenge was something short of fun...At least you can transfer your character back and forth so you can use the SE exlusive items in any other Ark map.
Final Thoughts:
Devs need to sop dragging this on as an Early Access game. Ark is fine as is just STOP UPDATING FOR A DAMN MINUTE, launch the game as a "Full Title", take some time to read some player feedback, fix the♥♥♥♥♥♥from when the game first started -_- , repeat the last two things at least one more time, THEN AND ONLY THEN should you add more new content to this game.

Lets keep this as short as possible.
I have been playing ARK for about 240 hours now, and I can only recommend it.
I have to mention though, that I have ONLY PLAYED ON A PRIVATE SERVER.
This is important, because on official servers, people can just erase you from the
island in minutes. If you want to have a good experience, either try to stick to a big
tribe, or do it as I recommend and find a privatly hosted server, or even host your own with friends.
This game has an incredible amount of content and doesnt get boring easily.
It takes a lot of time though, so I would also recommend turning up the harvest and taming multipliers.
Without those, you may have to wait 3 hours to tame one t-rex, having to defend it and yourself for the whole time.
Its not fun and kind of a waste of time, so turn up the multiplier settings to at least 3x.
About the Performance: I have a medium tier gaming pc that can handle GTA V on medium settings.
For ARK this is barely enough to play it. I play it on pretty low settings, only changing small things so it doesnt look completly crappy. It is very performance heavy, and there are some performance tweaks to be made for sure.
BUT since this game is STILL EARLY ACCESS dont go nuts about it and just wait for what they will add later on.
This game is not finished yet, allthough contentwise its very close, so give them some more time.
So far -- they kept adding features regulary and of high quality --- , so i have no doubt they will fix most of the performance problems aswell. This may take quite a while though.
Still, this is a good game and I can see past its flaws easily. Dont expect a fully polished experience yet.
Its Early Access after all.´
EDIT: It's out now, i have upgradet from 6GB RAM to 10GB RAM, and it runs on medium settings at 30+FPS.  Now that this game is properly playable for me performance wise, I can only recommend it. Maybe wait for a special offer, because its price change to 60€ is a bit harsh indeed, but on the other hand you had all this time to get it for 30€ so why are you just now thinking about buying it? I have played enough of this game to say that its absolutely worth it if you play with friends, and I havent even seen half of the content yet. Yes, its that much stuff.

Warframe is exactly what you think it is. It's like Dead Space. Well the Space and sometimes Dead part.
Pros:
- Quite welcoming to new players
- Plethora of weapons, gears and Warframe for new players
- Smooth movement and parkour (my reccomendation is to play this game with full FOV)
- It's a serious free to play even when it doesn't seeem like it sometimes
- Music and game sounds are amazing and wonderful
- Lots of quests, two cinematics quests
- Plenty of lore that you can find and speculate about
- You can earn premium money by selling common to rare items to other players or trading for other parts you require to build your weapon or Warframe
- Updates, there are good update in every game
- Microtransactions are there but aren't shoved down your throat.
- Gore! Lots of it!!
Procs
- I have a laptop and a gaming rig, Warframe runs beautifully on my rig however doesn't run on my laptop so I cannot tell you what you need for a middle rig
Cons:
- There is a prescence of premium money. It is a FTP, but like any other FTP. There are players that become greedy and want to advance before everyone else and hence the P2W feeling
- You need patience to farm resources, blueprints and blueprint parts to build things in this game. This point ties in well with the first one.
- As you advance, the plethora of weapons start to decrease and can cause the game to become boring
- Updates, there are bad updates in every game
-> The game is updated regulary (through major or hotfixes) which is good however it can break the game and it may take the devs 1-14 days to fix it.
- You can turn off the gore
As you can see, there are more pros than cons for Warframe. I highly reccomend it, it's my favourite FTP game and the only FTP game I play a lot. One last note, this is my opinion about the game so some of the things I have mentioned may not be of your liking and that's totally okay.
Final verdict:
10/10 for a free to play
9.65/10 compared to other games I enjoy

I got into this game late - 3 years or so after release. I waited so long because I hate freemium games and did not think it worth my time. A recent "Top 100 Games" site had Warframe in it, so I decided to give it a try.
Overall, I like the game. Graphics are great, sound is great, voice acting is very good, etc. It has a basic plot that is interesting, and there are dozens/scores of other missions to play, once you open things up.
It is a grinding game. You grind for everything, and that is where they tempt you for cash. Don't want to grind for days/weeks/months? Buy some platinum. Want more warframe slots or weapon slots? Yeah, that takes platinum. And you only get platinum early on by buying it. Later, when you are established, you can sell rare items to other players for platinum, but it takes a while to get to that level, and you will need platinum well before that to truly enjoy the game.
Yes, you can play the game without spending a dime. However, that process will be frustrating at times when you cannot hold more weapons/warframes due to a lack of slots and are forced to sell off (for in-game credits, not platinum) items in order to open up inventory space. I am at the point where it makes sense to buy some platinum, and the suggestion from seasoned players is to wait until you get a 50% or 75% off daily bonus.
The game is much more fun if you play with others. You can play solo all the way through it, but it is so much better if you play with a team. Clan communities are very friendly and helpful. You will find random high level people who are interested in helping you out. Often they will ask in chat if you need help with any missions, grinding for some element/item, etc.
The game is unreasonably complex. There are so many weapons, so many warframes, so many items, and so many mods for all those items, that it is overwhelmingly complex at the beginning. There really is no good tutorial, and your best bet is to read the wiki, watch some YouTube videos, and join a clan so people can explain things to you. Even then, some of the high level missions your clan-mates bring you on are so fast and complex that you will be lost. This game takes time to learn.
Given that most AAA games cost $40 - $70, and that $50 with a 75% coupon gets you a reasonable amount of platinum, it is a reasonably price to pay for the benefits of platinum.
Missions are anywhere from 10 - 20 minutes in length, so you can spend as little or as much time in the game as time allows.
I could never get in-game chat to work, no matter what I tried. I tried using Steam's voice controls - no dice. I tried in-game voice controls - no dice. In-game voice testing proved my mic was working fine, but it just does not work in-game. I finally ended up joining a clan and using TeamSpeak.
The folks in the ArsTenno clan are very helpful and friendly, although they always deny it.
I give it a 4/5 if you put the time into it to learn, join a clan, play online, and get some platinum. If you insist on doing solo and free, I give it a 3/5.

Warframe has the smartest business model of all Free-To-Play games on the market. It is a business model that invites you to spend money to accelerate progress or acquire cosmetic stuff, but does not force you to.
The entire game is truly free to play. The entire game works very well and is in active development for years now, receiving mechanics reworks and balance tweaks throughout its entire lifespan. And the game's economy is very much tied into the business model and the game's mechanics. A smart trader in-game can save real world money and still get everything he wants. Those who don't want to, get a great return on their investment because of the many metric tons of gameplay content the game has to offer.
Onto the game itself:
Warframe is a third person action game, with a surprising amount of depth and serious amount of progression to be had. It contains a good dose of pretty deep RPG elements and character/loadout building, mixed in with fast paced and highly mobile action. It runs on a toaster, and it runs well.
Each different Warframe in the game presents a small subset of very specific playstyles, with a large variety of roles available. Warframes are built from blueprints, of which the components are available as drops in the game. Every single Warframe and almost every weapon in the game can be built without spending a single dime - or you can buy/trade yourself a shortcut. Timed events offer some of these drops, while the vast majority of them is readily available in regular missions. Farming and grinding for new stuff, both Warframes and weapons, is the meat of this game. The farm never ends, and the game is built around that principle. As a consequence, the farm is as fun as you make it, and can be approached in any way you like.
Constructing a Warframe or a weapon takes days, up to a week, of building time. This game wants you to return often and play a bit, and allows you to come online whenever and however much you like, while still offering meaningful and entertaining time spent regardless of how dedicated you really are. You won't be missing out on too much - just keep an eye on special events that offer truly unique pieces of kit!
In conclusion, Warframe has my upvote, but only as long as you approach it for what it really is: a fun and fast-paced space-ninja action game. If you approach this as an MMO and play it as such, you are doing it wrong and will eventually, sooner or later, become disappointed. Warframe offers no persistence, no real end game, just more content to explore - always and forever.
NOTE: This review aims to globally describe the game, regardless of content patches and updates / changes to the game. It therefore goes into less detail, but will always be accurate!

Pros:
Dinosaurs are cool, and riding them is satisfying.  Many game elements that feels good to master.  Cool mods help as well.  Servers are also able to greatly modify values for most aspects of gameplay to make it easier or harder.  Frequent updates come all the time too, adding bug fixes and new dinos.
Final Thoughts:
If you do want to try the game, then 100% start on an unofficial server with difficulty turned down till you get the hang of it.  A must-buy if you catch it on sale.

Having being pulled into the game from a friend back in 2014 I thought I should write a review of the game based on my experiences.
When I first started to play the game I was pulled in by the speed and the style of the game play. It was definitely fast based and quite alot of fun up to a point mowing down whole hoads of enemies at a time. I must admit when I first playing the game I spent alot of hours grinding over the same missions on earth before the recent star chart changes in order to obtain credits. Also at the time, because I was a noob and didn't have access to a clan I didn't get the help most people seek when they first start playing the game. I'd have loved to have a taxi to the dark sectors and go on some credit runs to help me rank my mods a little quicker.
The basic concept of the game is pretty much the same as when I first started playing. In order to progress you must  do the following: Obtain credits to rank mods and buy blueprints. Rank up your gear to level 30 and if you like a weapon/frame/sentinal/companion you can add forma allowing you to squeeze out as much as possible from your gear.
Soon after you do this for quite some time it starts to hit you, You feel as though you're just a hamster running around in your little wheel doing the same thing over and over. You've invested alot of time and effort in your gear and then bang. You get the big fat NERF Hammer. I understand nerfs are required in games for one reason or another but that needs to be based on some kind of structure or formulae in getting to that conclusion.  Now this is my biggest issue in the game including alot of the dumb players in the community who agree with the nerfs all the time or petition so strongly for a nerf.
For example. Alot of the players that advocate a nerf only play the star chart or do not know that certain other factors can greatly help your gear despite it not having much invested. A party of 4 players that all have the aura mod Corrosive Projection against a party of something else will kill things easier with the same weapons. This is not a fair assessment of what is over powered and requires a nerf.
So if for example a player like myself turns round and says its not really a fair assessment because of the example given above or the fact that you are playing low level enemies, you receive idiotic replies like the following. "You're not supposed to play higher or at those levels you are talking about"
There are 2 problems with this statement. Firstly why do DE even have these levels in the game? And secondly, when there is a clan event of some sort. You are actively encouraged by the DE to run as long as you possibly can in order to compete with other clans for the top spot in the event boards.  I recall not long ago there was a mission where the enemy level was level 9999. Yes thats right 9999 and there was 1 post on the forums who said "DE are you♥♥♥♥♥♥♥taking the P1ss" as the player never played past the star chart and didn't understand the mechanics of how to deal with that level enemy. Hence the solution in my next paragraph or cheese tactic as so many like to use.
Now after a certain level you resort to what the community call cheese tactics. You go stealth using frames like loki or ivara, equip the deadly covert leathality mod to 1 hit kill almost all units with a dagger. But if you do not play this way, you are instantly killed from 1 bullet. Thats right a single bullet will kill you and anyone else that tries to revive you. Where's the nerf to the enemies if the warframes are constantly being rebalanced/nerfed all the time?
The enemy scalling is completely and utterly broken. Far to much time is spent re doing weapons and frames but these cannot EVER be balanced correctly when the base of the game is broken with regards to enemy scalling.
Since the recent update to the star chart which effectively killed the void, a large number of older or high geared players have minimised their game time or stopped playing the game altogether. The is no incentive to forma any new gear or do endless void runs as you do not get any rewards except for endo and some resources. Right now you play more of the star chart now in order to obtain the prime parts you are seeking although all people in a party are required to use a key and farm new keys when new prime parts are released.
I could write alot more but I will leave the following for you to decide if this game is for you at the current time/state of the game:
If you are into the following then this game will be right up your street:
Fast paced plowing dumb hoards of enemies
Love fashion frame ( Want to look pretty hanging out at relays with other tenno)
Build you're own clan ( Clans dont really do much apart from serve as trading posts and obtain blueprints etc)
Casual game play
Join a clan and alliance to play with other people.
Play sorties (DE current high level missions with terrible rewards)
A completionist (do all scans, forma everything in game etc)
Lacross sport (Its called Lunaro but not many play it anyway)
However, If you are looking for the following in this game then this is DEFINITELY NOT the game for you:
Balanced enemy scailing:
Meaningful Clans (They are more than just trade posts and where people grab the research)
Deep mission types
Good enemy AI.
Rewarding and fun/challenging missions for what ever level you may be.
Huge clan battles or alliance battles (Dark Sectors would most likely be the cloest thing but this is currently disabled due to the mechanics being poorly thought out and were exploited by players/clans)
Content and missions for hardcore players.
There is barely any rarity in the game in terms of gear/mods. It kills the economy for alot of items because all can easily buy and sell. Only a few items and Prime chamber are currently not available.
No rewards for vet players or those that seek endless missions.
Dedicated Servers to play on.
