Overall Warframe is a great game. Good graphics, runs well on most PCs, very smooth controls and movement is fluid, the mission types are engaging and keep you wanting to progress further into the game.
People who complain that it's too "grindy" are missing the point and purpose of what the game is. Warframe is not an open world RPG where you can simply roleplay without putting in any work, the entire point of the game is about fighting and doing missions. It also isn't supposed to be a game where you can get your gear and characters up to max tier within a week. You're meant to spend a lot of time on it to rank up and get the gear that you'd like. While you can straight up buy your stuff with platinum (the currency that you purchase with real life cash), you are not obligated to and you don't have to as almost everything outside of cosmetic items can be built with in game only materials, albeit taking more time to craft.
The devs made a good in game trading interface for players where you can get platinum for items that you acquire with only in-game materials, such as prime gear parts and mods. If you are dedicated and seriously want something that is only obtainable with platinum, you can get it through effort and trading worthy items to other players that would want what you have. It takes time, but if you don't want to spend any cash, you can still work for what you want.
I do recommend playing the game with at least one or more friends though if possible, as it's a lot easier to learn and figure things out with a friend to help you, especially if it's someone who has already played the game before and can help get you a headstart into learning the core game mechanics. Playing solo is still viable though, since there's a huge amount of player-to-player interaction, and you can figure out almost anything you need by just searching through the warframe forums or steam community page.
Onto the actual gameplay and bread 'n butter of the game, everything really flows together really nicely in this game. I'm a huge fan of the movement system, since you can be really agile and parkour around maps, and it's all extremely fluid feeling. All of the warframes are pretty balanced and you can do a decent amount of work with any warframe you choose to use, given that you equip and upgrade proper mods to your gear. Mods are basically just 'boosters' to your weapons and your warframe (Your warframe is basically like your class, btw. Your warframe is what gives you all your abilities and sort of defines what your role is in the game.) and they apply various different perks and bonuses, and you can further ugprade to get even more out of them. The weapons are decently balanced as well, of course the harder you have to work for a weapon and the higher rank it is, the better it'll be, just like any other game, but with proper mods you can turn even low quality weapons into pretty good ones.
Some people say the game gets repetitive, which I could see why people would think that, but it really depends on what kind of person you are and what kind of games you find personally fun. I for one haven't gotten bored of Warframe yet in the 2 or so weeks I've been playing it. Warframe definitely isn't an open world game, but it still has a good community with loads of content to explore and learn about. There are hundreds of different weapons to choose from, so you can always switch up your playstyle and try new things to keep the game fresh. If you go into the game with an open mind and not expecting it to be a f2p version of WoW, you'll have a lot of fun.
If you like to be a perfectionist in games and always want to seek out the best possible outcomes and the strongest gear in a game, Warframe will be awesome for you because you can spend days upon days hunting down the rarest and most powerful weapons and mods to gear up with. With the alert mission system, there's a bit of luck involved with getting the best gear as well, since you may or may not be online while something super good pops up on the alerts, so you may end up having to wait for it to pop up again if you aren't on in time to get it.
All in all, Warframe is a good game, especially since it's totally free to play. It's hard for me to find a real complaint when I'm not in anyway obligated to play the game if I don't want to. The only negative thing I'd have to say is that corpus missions suck. Corpus enemies have a bunch of shields, plus they have flying drones that give even more shields as well as certain enemies who nullify your abilities. They also deal pretty good damage, especially as you go later in the game. If the enemy spots you and triggers the alarm and you don't clear it fast enough, a tank-like enemy called a Bursa will come rushing in and wreck your day, while being pretty hard to kill in most circumstances.
This paragraph is probably going to sound stupid but I just need to comment on it. The single worst part for me is these enemies in corpus missions that I like to call "turkey legs" (or MOA, which is their actual name.) They are literally just a pair of green mechanical legs with a gun on top. They seriously look like some sort of oversized robotic bird legs running around the place. Their design is so absurdly silly that I can't help but get angry whenever they kill me or when a swarm of them come to attack me with their never ending laser gun attacks. There's also the infested MOA, but at least their design kind of makes sense to some degree since they're actually a living thing and it looks like they got hit with some sort of plague. With the corpus MOAs, I can't help but imagine this stupid picture in my mind of some mad scientist in a lab creating the corpus turkey legs with them flooding off of a conveyor belt thinking the design is super wicked and unstoppable, when in reality it's no joke, just a pair of green legs that shoot at you while looking hilarious running around the map.
Also, the boss fights can get a bit ridiculous at times, since some of them are literally invincible unless you hit them in super specific spots, make them use an ability so that they become vulnerable, or use a specific type of damage against them. The game usually gives very little indication of what to do, aside from Lotus perhaps making a small comment here and there about the boss's general weakness, for the most part you have to either figure it out on your own, or search up how to beat the boss. While not unbeatable, I'd recommend finding someone to bring along with you if you need to do boss fights until you get stronger gear at least. It's usually easy to find someone in the recruitment public chat, so I'd try that if you don't know anyone personally who plays warframe. A lot of people are usually willing to give a helping hand, especially if you're somewhat new.
Anyways, this game is overall very enjoyable, and for being free to play it would never hurt to at least try it for an hour and then just uninstall it if you don't like it.

Pros:
>Addicting as hell, i won't lie it's much like Cocaine. You quit for a little but come back to it and regret leaving.
>Has a enjoyable level of difficulty (Scorched Earth map is my favorite thus far because of the weather changes)
>It's something to be running or riding with a pack of tamed Dinos, even just hunting other wild Dinos.
Meh:
>Building mechanics could use some improvement. They aren't the worst but i've seen far better in other games. The snapping is awkward at times and there is little tips showing which way things will be facing (Fence Foundations are the worst for this) [A good suggestion is to be able to raise or lower things like foundations, have text or an arrow to show which way things will be facing instead of just a glowing transparent outline. also the idea of things refusing to go along a hill is quite annoying, everything generally has to be straight and box like... corner triangles or even curves would make building way more enjoyable as well]
>Pathway AI, Yep i know still in Early Access bla bla... But Wild and Tamed dinos move with the grace of a cripple old man who's had his wheelchair stolen by some punk kids and his cane broke while going down four flights of stairs. Sometimes they move, other times they get stuck on the smallest objects and just keep trying to walk forward, other times they go barreling past you like a freight train.
Cons:
>If on a dedicated server, you have to care for everything and it takes a lot time to play/enjoy...Reminds me of Eve in some Degree when it comes to this.
>Wildlife imbalance, what i mean by this is that The wild Dino's don't act as i think they personally should. Yup personal in this but it makes sense to me. To me Predators should fight each other as well as hunting for food, There is a territorial instinct when it comes to some wildlife, i would assume that started way before our time. Having Predators fight one another would also help with the balance of things, instead of having tons of predators who just eat and kill all the more passive dinos. Or would help prevent spots where you see a pack of mix matched Predators [Example: three Sabertooth's with two Carno's and a pack of Direwolves all hanging around together and working like the A-Team]
All-in-all I do enjoy the game [900+ hours played, so i can't really say otherwise] and can't wait for it to leave the "Early Access" phase that it's been in for a while even though it dropped an Expansion and for the most part seems to be fully developed in a lot of regards.

I'd been warned that optimisation was appalling and the designers didn't care, but was horrified to discover that it was **even worse** than 'Conan', even when my RAM was 2-3 times greater than minimum specified requirements (though other reviewers have already pointed out these are total fiction). Even consulting online guides, I found it impossible to get FPS up to that I enjoyed in 'Assassin's Creed: Unity' - and this for some rather bodgy MMO.
I'd been warned that official ARK servers were populated by the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s that dominate 'Conan' PVP and developers didn't care about this either, but planned to play singleplayer, focusing on base-building and exploring the lavish-looking environment. Not much chance of that, given the magic lantern show I was subjected to!
Life is waaaay too short for ARK and its technical fails. I may reload it again when we've got a working game here for non-Cray-3 owners--Scorched Earth looked particularly atmospheric in Let's Plays--but it's been so long in Early Access and so many players dissatisfied to date, I'd be surprised if it's ever officially released.

I've been playing this game for more than 100 hours now and I have to say that it is great.  It's brutally frustrating at times and really rewarding at others.  I play PvE exclusively at this point and I have no complaints about the game nor how it runs on my system (I have a 5+ year old system and I run the game with "No sky Effect" and it's plays just great - although I did change to a SSD HD in order to cut the loading times down).  I've noticed several reviews with people complaining about being dominated by higher level players/tribes in PvP mode and that is exactly what I would expect to happen.  Once a group has dominance on a server, it will be nigh impossible to defeat them unless they allow others to build up the necessary experience and equipment to do so.  Don't think many are going to do that!  This isn't a game about balance, like a typical online competitive shooter.  It's a survival game and it's meant to be impossibly hard and this is why I see Ark as a game to be played with and against, friends, even in PvP mode.

Begin test. At this point I want to like this game.
The game comes with a launcher and requires you to create an account with them to log in. Okay, fine, I can put up with that.
Then it decides to launch in windowed mode. Not ideal, but easy enough to fix. Alt+F4, open the launcher, set it to fullscreen.
Launch the game again. Now we have a fullscreen game, but it looks hideous -- it decided to default to 720p. Again, no big deal, we'll just go to the options menu and correct the settings.
But the game wants to show me a cutscene. Press Esc to skip cutscene. Another cutscene comes up. Rinse and repeat for half a dozen of these cutscenes. At this point I'm feeling less charitable towards the game.
Finally the movies are over and we can go through the menus to begin to make this thing playable. Nope! Now you have to select a character to play, there is no main menu to be seen. Surely I've missed something.
Pick a character. More cutscene. Eventually we get control, and hammering Esc brings up a menu! Change the resolution to something sane. Crawl through the various screen and see controler support -- aha, I have one of those. And this game does look quite consoley, the sort of thing that would benefit from a controller.
Plug in my Xbone controller and make sure it's enabled in the menu. But none of the in-game prompts change, so we're left guessing which button does what. But hey, it's gameplay -- let's finish the tutorial and see where it takes us.
---
The tutorial does not inspire great loyalty. Because of the lack of menu, I don't care about your world -- you forced me to chose between skipping the intro movies or watching them in the wrong resolution, and both of these are losing options. The gameplay isn't bad, but nor does it turn lead into gold. For putting up with that initial experience, the gameplay needs to blow me away in order to redeem it.
It did not.

I have done it all... Literally.
I have played this game since mid 2013, and I've seen its high and low points. I have farmed every piece, leveled every weapon and frame. I have seen new and exciting content and hilariously bad mess-ups from the developers. At this point it has become a love hate relationship.
This game is suited for someone who is really into grinding. There is no way to avoid it, and if you dont like collecting gear piece by piece then you wont like this game. The new player expirience has gotten alot better, but as soon as you are out of the tutorial you will have to be self sufficient. Want to build this new gun? Youre gonna have to go farm for it. Want this cool warframe? Go farm one boss fight over and over again for 3 different pieces, then wait 84 hours before you can use it. The grinding for new gear will punish you ruthlessly.
However, once its over you feel a sense of accomplishment. You farmed this cool weapon and this cool warframe, and now you get to take it and customize it and make it powerful. Customization is incredible in this game, whether it is coloring your stuff or unique cosmetics customization. "Fasionframe" will eat up much more time than you think.
In the end, I am glad that I have played Warframe for so long, and I will continue to play it. DE has messed up alot, but in general they are headed in the right direction and are improving the game and keeping it in the right direction.

I purchased ARK almost as soon as it came up on Early Access back in June of 2015. I've seen ARK evolve from its earliest days to where it stands now. I also own the dubious Scorched Earth expansion. I've taken part in pretty much every kind of activity to be found in ARK: solo building, working with small public tribes, all the way up to large scale alpha tribe vs alpha tribe PVP. Granted, there are -plenty- of people who have more time in ARK than me, but I've pretty much seen it all. Now with all that said, and considering everything I've seen and played, I cannot recommend ARK. Here's why.
If you really, really wanted to boil it down into the most basic explaination possible, it's because ARKs combat is simply not fun. All the other issues in the game all relate back to this point in one way or the other. Allow me to explain.
Look at ARKs promotional videos and ask yourself what you see. You'll see armies of players alongside T-Rexes fighting across open fields. You'll see epic assaults on heavily defended bases by seige platforms mounted on mighty dinosaurs. Look at the promotional pictures here on Steam. You'll see trader caravans escorted by raptor cavalry making long treks across the island. You are probably thinking of buying the game so you too can take part in these epic struggles for survival.
I'll tell you right now that you will NEVER experience ANY of that. Wanna know how ARK combat REALLY goes down? You farm up C4 for a week and then wait for your target to go offline. Then you and your tribe go to their base, which is in fact not an epic castle but a metal cube slathered in auto-turrets, and you drop friggin turtles on their base until their turrets run out of ammo. Then you take your C4 and blow your way in. If their dinosaurs are all on passive stance, just shoot them in the face until they die. If they are on nuetral, lure them out of the base and have your own dinos kill them at your leisure. Once all their dinos are dead, just keep blowing stuff up and stealing everything until you run out of explosives. If your REALLY lucky, one of their guys might get on and you MIGHT have a firefight. Then the next morning you can get on and hear them crying that they lost 6 months of work in one night. Eventually, one day you will suffer the same fate. Of course, all of this is assuming that you and your tribe reach the point where you can raid bases, and that you and your tribe weren't effortlessly curbstomped by an already established tribe the moment you set down your first foundation.
The entire game, and I do mean the ENTIRE GAME, consists of nothing but months of grinding resources to do that exact thing. ARK demands that you invest so much time in it that it might as well be a part time job, and when the chips are down and all is said and done, the end result of all your labor is going to be blowing up a metal cube. Every other activity in the game is nothing but grinding up to get to that point.
In summery, all the neat gear, all the cool dinosaurs, and all the other features of ARK become a zero sum game when the end experience is something as uninspiring as offline raiding.
--------------------------------------------------------
Addendum: It has come to my attention that many people are expressing their opinion that options such as PvE mode, private servers, mods, etc invalidate my points and redeem the game.
Firstly, if the community of players have to start enforcing their own personal rules (ie. private servers) or adding their own content (ie. mods) in order to make the game palpable, then that is a telling sign that the games core, fundemental mechanics are intrinsically flawed. I do not believe it is the responsibility of the community to fix a games flaws. Things like mods and private servers should be tools to enchance an already well built game, not used as crutches to sidestep a games core issues. I am writing my review concerning the game as the developers intended it to be played; which I believe has serious shortcomings that show no signs of getting fixed. I don't think its fair to potential customers to review a game any other way.
Secondly, PVE servers suffer from a myriad of problems. First and foremost, by eliminating direct player competition, you remove about 50% of the games entire premise. I found that some of the most fun aspects of ARK involved server politics such as alliances, betrayals, territorial skirmishes, rescues, ambushes, etc etc. By taking out any form of player vs player engagments, you can forget about all that. Which leaves you with... what exactly? You will collect dinosaurs to sit in your corral, you go spulunking through a few caves, and MAYBE if your REALLY lucky, you'll fight a boss with some other players, although good luck getting enough people to help you with that last one. The fact of the matter is that the PVE elements to this game, while much deeper than other survival games out there, are simply not compelling enough to stand on their own two feet. That's not even touching on the fact that PVE servers STILL have ways where other players can screw you over (for example, surrounding your base with foundations to prevent you from building, and preventing resources from spawning nearby) and since it's a PVE server you have absolutely no methods of retaliating.
ARK has great potential and can frankly be a lot of fun. People wouldn't spend 500+ hours in this game if it wasn't at least kinda fun. However, the fact of the matter is that it's potential is horribly squandered by boring combat, tedious grinding, balance issues, and several downright stupid mechanics (bringing back server transfers? After what happened last time? Really?). Paying customers should not have to put up with this considering how long ARK has been in development. At this point, it's obvious the game is only going downhill, so I can't recommend it to new players.

The currency system uses platinums and is pretty fair, there are 3 kind of things:
-ones you can buy only with platinum: these are mostly visual stuff, like skins armor pieces, robes, paints etc, basicly the blings
-the ones you can buy for platinum or farm and craft: these are the basic weapons and warframes and drones and devicces and stuff, the things you use the most of the time
-the ones you can only craft: the fanciest of weapons and warframes and stuff, the things that matter the most (tho you can buy relics, that are needed to farm the fancy stuff for platinum, otherwise you have to farm the relics to farm the items)
Platinum can be gained in 2 ways, either by buying it from the devs (it can be pretty cheap with a 75% coupon that you might get on daily login so I recommend you wait until then(and you will get it soon))
or you can trade rare tuff with other players for it, obviously for that you need plenty of freetime to farm rare stuff and to find a trading partner as there is no actionhouse you have to spam a trading chat if you want to sell soemthing. but the option is there to get platinum for free.

This is an excellent free to play game.
This one reminds me alot of Destiny with its differing mission locations on planets.  Though each mission even if you do the same one is always different.  The maps in this game use specifc locations but put them together differently each time.
In addition this game has alot of parkor moments and alot of hidden places to find and go to.  If you can get there chances are there is something hidden there.
This game uses a cash shop although using it is easy its not always the best thing to do...as you still have to play.  Alot of the game is unlocked by completing specifc missions and leveling up your items and you own character.  The cash shop also allows you to use in game cash to get certain items like scanners and blueprints....but also lets you spend real cash to do the same thing.
Your character has what is called a mastery rank this is raised by completing tests.  To unlock the ability to complete a test you again have to play the game.
Your items, warframe, weapons, sentinels, etc, all have levels as they go up levels you gain more experience thus can eventualy do a test you unlock another mastery rank.
In a way this game can be very grindy, but with each frame offering 5 differing powers and a differing look and considering you can choose whatever weapons you want it makes this game have alot of replay ability.
My only gripe is a few things....the tutorial and help stuff isnt very good....at times i didnt see what i was supposed to do next and didnt see the small text explaining my powers or how i could open certain lockers etc.  In addition I literally had to look some things up on a warframe wiki or just found out after readiong some of the in game players chatting about differing things.
Also many missions seam to just all together give up on stealth....there you are sneaking around taking your time....and suddenly everything comes after you.
I tend to do things slowly....i like to ninja the missions in games...kill them all so to speak at times.....but this game sometimes forces me to run out.
Fissure missions, bounty missions and infested missions all have this global they come right at you thing.....no matter where you are.....its very annoying.
This in turn makes me miss items and hidden stuff....which is annoying and disapointing.
All in all i recommend this game.
They are continualy updating and fixing things....the newest frame called the titania is alot of fun to play.
All i need now is a cat one(cat ears and a tail on a female frame) i can already think of what it would have on it.
Sooo in conclusion....play this game....its free after all.

More than 600 hours and counting...I feel like I'm ready for a review.
I've been playing this game since 2013, despite my seemingly low amount of hours for a Free-to-Play cooperative third-person hack-and-slash/shooter game that's been out for now 3 years on Steam. Watching this game grow and become what it is now has been a treat and I will continue to track and follow this game for the foreseeable future, but there are some issues I'll warn against with this game.
For new players, this game seems like a godsend. The graphics are beautiful and worthy of any AAA studio, despite many believing this game would fail during its humble beginnings. The gameplay is solid and damn near the best I've ever enjoyed in a video game thanks to its solid and almost freeform flow between gunplay and melee combat coupled with its ever satisfying and enjoyable "parkour" system. The number of weapons, cosmetics, and playable characters rival even the heaviest hitters of the RPG genre, such as Borderlands. Best of all, damn near everything in the game can be obtained for absolutely free. The greatest part of this game is certainly the fact that this game is still constantly being updated, cared for, and nurtured by its developers and now its own community thanks to the Tennogen system. However, for veterans, this may be the game's greatest flaw.
For veteran players like me and plenty others, its difficult to muster up the passion to play this game after farming for every single thing we want in this game, and then some. For a lot of older players with all the weapons, Warframes, resources, mods, cosmetics, clans, solar rails, and completed quests we could ever want, we don't pick the game back up for sometimes months at a time as we wait for the next big update to add in the new story quest or new Warframe/weapons or new event which interest us enough to hop back on. Then, once we, for the umpteenth time, grind the new piece of equipments' resources then grind for its levels to later slap a "potato" on to and then play maybe one more survival with it, we just put the game back down and wait again. I find it a bit sad that even I beg the devs for new content I'll acquire and max out within a month or so just to put the game back down for another few months in anticipation of the next new chunks of content.
In short, new players are sure to love this should you be able to push through the grindfest that is Warframe, as you'll soon be grinding without even realizing what you're grinding for. As for veterans of Warframe, try convincing friends to join so you can enjoy helping the Lotus teach them the ways of the Tenno. If all else fails, the game's creative community has some of the best fan art and cosplay I've seen in a while.

The cash shop also allows you to use in game cash to get certain items like scanners and blueprints....but also lets you spend real cash to do the same thing.
Your character has what is called a mastery rank this is raised by completing tests.  To unlock the ability to complete a test you again have to play the game.
Your items, warframe, weapons, sentinels, etc, all have levels as they go up levels you gain more experience thus can eventualy do a test you unlock another mastery rank.
In a way this game can be very grindy, but with each frame offering 5 differing powers and a differing look and considering you can choose whatever weapons you want it makes this game have alot of replay ability.

All in all i recommend this game.
They are continualy updating and fixing things....the newest frame called the titania is alot of fun to play.

I have done it all... Literally.
I have played this game since mid 2013, and I've seen its high and low points. I have farmed every piece, leveled every weapon and frame. I have seen new and exciting content and hilariously bad mess-ups from the developers. At this point it has become a love hate relationship.
This game is suited for someone who is really into grinding. There is no way to avoid it, and if you dont like collecting gear piece by piece then you wont like this game. The new player expirience has gotten alot better, but as soon as you are out of the tutorial you will have to be self sufficient. Want to build this new gun? Youre gonna have to go farm for it. Want this cool warframe? Go farm one boss fight over and over again for 3 different pieces, then wait 84 hours before you can use it. The grinding for new gear will punish you ruthlessly.
However, once its over you feel a sense of accomplishment. You farmed this cool weapon and this cool warframe, and now you get to take it and customize it and make it powerful. Customization is incredible in this game, whether it is coloring your stuff or unique cosmetics customization. "Fasionframe" will eat up much more time than you think.
In the end, I am glad that I have played Warframe for so long, and I will continue to play it. DE has messed up alot, but in general they are headed in the right direction and are improving the game and keeping it in the right direction.

Warframe is a large, multiplayer game in which the player, known as the Tenno, control their warframes to complete missions and tasks, with an overarching goal of restoring order to the system, Taking place over all the planets in the solar system, plus some extra terrestrial bodies such as Ceres and Europa.
The basics of gameplay are fairly easy to understand, where in a very basic level could be played out similar to other shooters. However the Warframe has much greater capabilities, with alot of mobility at their disposal and frame-exclusive abilities which can turn the tide of battle, offering a more skilled level of play in working for synergy between weapons, abilities and mobility options available. This can provide even greater strength with others, as each mission can be completed in a squad of up to four players, which extends to eight for the Trials of the systems, the end-game content so to speak.
The initial arsenal which the Tenno has access to is limited, but different weapons are made ready for construction as you experience the game, with the increase of the Tenno's Mastery Rank (MR). MR is essentially a measurement for how much of the game a certain Tenno has experienced, in which a Tenno of rank 3 has not experienced nearly as much of the game of a Tenno of rank 12, for example. Increasing your MR also unlocks the avaliability of some sections of the game's content, such as weapons, quests and certain areas.
Missions are easy to get into and intially can have significant variance, such as defense, interception and capture missions, and after a short while of gameplay the Tenno can also complete a quest to obtain an Archwing, which can provide a fresh task to undertake.
Community is also rather nice, with many members willing to aid others and there is the ability to join a clan within the game to interact with a smaller community within.
However, the Single biggest flaw for the game is repetition and grinding. Many parts of the game can require grinding for specific materials and blueprints, which often results in returning to missions multiple times, and weapons and warframes require useage in order to gain levels, which adds to this grind. For a player who doesnt mind a grind, this isnt much of a big issue, but many players, myself included, do not enjoy the huge amount of grinding required.
Warframe IS a fun game, and also holds lore which at times can play a significant impact into the game, But the grind which it holds is a significant deterrent for many players in the long run. despite this, I find myself returning time and time again to play, with the updates adding more content to indulge in. It is not a game for everyone in the long run, but by heck it at the very least can provide at least 10 hours of fun for most people.

This is a great game from a PvE point of view, I play vanilla settings except gathering rates, you will need alot of time invested into this game whichever server you play on or solo play, and im not exaggerating, on Vanilla settings taming can hours if you dont have the correct food the dino prefers and the high end dinos such as Rexes, Spino's etc etc, still take hours of time and preparation even with the correct food and equipment.
However this does make the tames in my eyes all that more precious when you've spent such a long time taming a dino that will help you greatly reduce the time it takes you to stock on materials and essentials to expand your base or even protect it and you while your still getting set up.
The biomes are very varied from Snow to Jungle to Swamp to Scorched volcano islands, so it caters to players who want to build in a particular biome but that doesnt always mean it will be easy, you really do have to progress as a player starting with thatch building working your way up all the way to metal and even further into TEK, but it all takes time and dedication to progress that far.
You also have the "Caves" which harbour artifacts hidden all over the map which tend to need to work with other players or to conquer it as a tribe, and upon gathering these artifacts you can challenge the world bosses that exsist in ARK, and even if you get comfortable playing a certain way there are always re-balancing updates or new dinos that can change how you play and approach the game completely.
You can also breed dino's to try and improve its base level on the baby, breed hordes of dinos for attacks, or even try for the rare "Mutations" which as you might of guess means the dinosaur has changed in someway, this can be a stat that is improved more than standard or even a colour mutation, so yes the possibility exsists for you to run around on purple and blue Rexes, that is a thing.
But, the problem with all this content is it can be overwhelming for new players to get into the swing of things, trying to understand how the building system works, making weapons, surviving in general, there isnt really a tutorial as such its more of a play by learning method, which works for some but not others, but overcoming that initial start is when the game can start to become addictive.
Now "Bugs" there are a ton of bugs, and with each update more bugs arise but the devs tent to tackle new content bugs pretty fast but exsisting bugs seem to take a while to fix, I mean ive experienced a bug where I jumped inside a cave and teleported to the land outside above, i've seen offline players floating in mid-air, dinosaurs "inside" stone walls and metal nodes, I mean just yesterday one of my tribe members logged into the game and was in the air and fell to her death even though she logged out inside her house, so yeah it can be buggy but it is "Early Access" and given the amount of time i've put into the game I dont seem to come across bugs all that often.
Now ill point why i've put DLC in both "+" and "-", the main one that seems to peev people off is its early access and yet already has DLC, yeah I see where they are coming from but the dev's explained that they intially hadnt planned this feature and decided to release it as a DLC which gives people the ability to travel between servers if they allow it and different maps, even dinos aswell so if the servers allow it you are able to raise a Wyvern on the DLC map "Scorched Earth" and bring it home to your normal base, but the other factor was the different survival elements, since in SE you encounter a harsh enviroment that disables your weapons, machines, hinders you personally so alot of different elements were introduced to make it harder for the player that have no place at all in the base game, so its better to decide yourself if its a + or a -.
Anyway to wrap up, you will need a decent machine to be-able to play this well since once a server starts to get popular the lag will start to kick in when your loading up bases you encounter or even just returning to your empire that you spent the laast 3 months building, it is a fun game to play and even more so with other people but you need to invest a ton of time into it.

This is a great game from a PvE point of view, I play vanilla settings except gathering rates, you will need alot of time invested into this game whichever server you play on or solo play, and im not exaggerating, on Vanilla settings taming can hours if you dont have the correct food the dino prefers and the high end dinos such as Rexes, Spino's etc etc, still take hours of time and preparation even with the correct food and equipment.
However this does make the tames in my eyes all that more precious when you've spent such a long time taming a dino that will help you greatly reduce the time it takes you to stock on materials and essentials to expand your base or even protect it and you while your still getting set up.
The biomes are very varied from Snow to Jungle to Swamp to Scorched volcano islands, so it caters to players who want to build in a particular biome but that doesnt always mean it will be easy, you really do have to progress as a player starting with thatch building working your way up all the way to metal and even further into TEK, but it all takes time and dedication to progress that far.
You also have the "Caves" which harbour artifacts hidden all over the map which tend to need to work with other players or to conquer it as a tribe, and upon gathering these artifacts you can challenge the world bosses that exsist in ARK, and even if you get comfortable playing a certain way there are always re-balancing updates or new dinos that can change how you play and approach the game completely.
You can also breed dino's to try and improve its base level on the baby, breed hordes of dinos for attacks, or even try for the rare "Mutations" which as you might of guess means the dinosaur has changed in someway, this can be a stat that is improved more than standard or even a colour mutation, so yes the possibility exsists for you to run around on purple and blue Rexes, that is a thing.
But, the problem with all this content is it can be overwhelming for new players to get into the swing of things, trying to understand how the building system works, making weapons, surviving in general, there isnt really a tutorial as such its more of a play by learning method, which works for some but not others, but overcoming that initial start is when the game can start to become addictive.
Now "Bugs" there are a ton of bugs, and with each update more bugs arise but the devs tent to tackle new content bugs pretty fast but exsisting bugs seem to take a while to fix, I mean ive experienced a bug where I jumped inside a cave and teleported to the land outside above, i've seen offline players floating in mid-air, dinosaurs "inside" stone walls and metal nodes, I mean just yesterday one of my tribe members logged into the game and was in the air and fell to her death even though she logged out inside her house, so yeah it can be buggy but it is "Early Access" and given the amount of time i've put into the game I dont seem to come across bugs all that often.
Now ill point why i've put DLC in both "+" and "-", the main one that seems to peev people off is its early access and yet already has DLC, yeah I see where they are coming from but the dev's explained that they intially hadnt planned this feature and decided to release it as a DLC which gives people the ability to travel between servers if they allow it and different maps, even dinos aswell so if the servers allow it you are able to raise a Wyvern on the DLC map "Scorched Earth" and bring it home to your normal base, but the other factor was the different survival elements, since in SE you encounter a harsh enviroment that disables your weapons, machines, hinders you personally so alot of different elements were introduced to make it harder for the player that have no place at all in the base game, so its better to decide yourself if its a + or a -.
Anyway to wrap up, you will need a decent machine to be-able to play this well since once a server starts to get popular the lag will start to kick in when your loading up bases you encounter or even just returning to your empire that you spent the laast 3 months building, it is a fun game to play and even more so with other people but you need to invest a ton of time into it.
Ark is a great game but takes alot time, best played with other players or friends, and it can be buggy but it is highly fun and addictive as my playtime kinda shows!

IMO the three goals of Warframe:
,
,
. And that's what I'm going to be explaining with this review and also add why I love the game in the later part.
Warframe is a co-op 3rd person shooter version of an action RPG like Diablo and Path of Exile. The game has procuderally generated levels and all of it are instances. All of this is set in the far future of our Solar System, so there's an interesting SciFi setting going on. There various co-op missions ranging from kill everything in the level to stealth your way to a computer terminal and even endless point defence missions where newly spawned enemies scale in stats to insane levels. There's also large group content that plays out like an MMO raid. There's even PVP that plays like an arena shooter and one mode that's basically space lacrosse.
In the game you're the Tenno/Operator which is a player faction that's the only one that can use Warframes. And Warframes are essentially powered suits/mindless beings where you channel void energy in various flashy powers. So imagine a frost mage, a fire mage, and a sound mage. Things go crazy with the powers, okay. There are warframes for any playstyle. And not just warframes but also weapons like guns, bows, swords, gunblades, an biological glaive, and so much more. And all of those weapons and warframes give you a strong power fantasy since you can literally kill an entire army with your friends. Also, there's a lot of customization of stats and loadouts with the warframes and weapons with the use of their respective stat modifiers called
. Mods are like collectible cards which give stat differences to weapons and warframes. Some are straight up damage boost while others give off elemental damage or increase crit chance. You know RPG stats. And all of this play into the first goal:
. When you get the right gear and the right group, carnage ensues. And the game engine can support so much carnage and particle effects to the point where JJ Abrams lens flares are put to shame.
Going back to the customization, I have to emphasize that it's a lot. From colour schemes to different armour sets for your warframe and even capes made of fire. Also, the game now allows for user made content so expect more skins and what not. Thus,
. Always look good when destroying an entire space military force.
Goal 3
: But how do you get these items since it is loot game, isn't it? Well, that's the cool thing about the game is since it's free you can craft everything in the game or you can buy them with real money. The loot you get isn't a straight up complete weapon but the parts of it. And so that's how the game plays: you do missions to get parts to then build cool stuff. Although, I have to admit it's pretty grindy. For a single weapon, it could take a day or two to gather materials. Then a 12 hr to 3 day wait for it actually build. They had to put some mechanics for you to sink real money into.
Which nicely brings up the business model, it is a free-to-play game. And in my opinion, it's pretty fair and not actually to pay-to-win. Sure, you can straight up buy a weapon with real cash. But it's a co-op game. How can you get an unfair advantage against other players when your in a co-op game? You basically just skip the grind. Also, there's not really a clear best when it comes to warframe and weapon setup. Oh sure, the forums and reddit will say there is. But again it's a co-op game. And any all gear setup in place in the game is just there to provide a very different playstyle. Now, I did say PVP is in the game. But it's tricky since they balance the weapons there differently for PVP and PVE. And you don't get to use the PVE mods in PVP which is where the real power comes from in the game. Those mods you can't buy with cash. You can trade for them from someone who has it. But that someone had to put hours in the game to get said mods. So all-in-all, it's a tricky balancing game the devs did with the business model. And so far it's not really pay-to-win.
But in my opinion. The best thing about Warframe is the devs commitment for the game. They always update the game. They add in meaningful and new mechanics to just better the game. And they often do bring in new mechanics in a lore friendly way. The last update changed up how reward tables are done in missions. Instead rolling the dice in a huge reward table. They now have it so you bring an item with you on mission which is a more focused reward table to roll the RNG dice with. And you can affect the chance you get the item you want with item boost. If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

More than 600 hours and counting...I feel like I'm ready for a review.
I've been playing this game since 2013, despite my seemingly low amount of hours for a Free-to-Play cooperative third-person hack-and-slash/shooter game that's been out for now 3 years on Steam. Watching this game grow and become what it is now has been a treat and I will continue to track and follow this game for the foreseeable future, but there are some issues I'll warn against with this game.
For new players, this game seems like a godsend. The graphics are beautiful and worthy of any AAA studio, despite many believing this game would fail during its humble beginnings. The gameplay is solid and damn near the best I've ever enjoyed in a video game thanks to its solid and almost freeform flow between gunplay and melee combat coupled with its ever satisfying and enjoyable "parkour" system. The number of weapons, cosmetics, and playable characters rival even the heaviest hitters of the RPG genre, such as Borderlands. Best of all, damn near everything in the game can be obtained for absolutely free. The greatest part of this game is certainly the fact that this game is still constantly being updated, cared for, and nurtured by its developers and now its own community thanks to the Tennogen system. However, for veterans, this may be the game's greatest flaw.
For veteran players like me and plenty others, its difficult to muster up the passion to play this game after farming for every single thing we want in this game, and then some. For a lot of older players with all the weapons, Warframes, resources, mods, cosmetics, clans, solar rails, and completed quests we could ever want, we don't pick the game back up for sometimes months at a time as we wait for the next big update to add in the new story quest or new Warframe/weapons or new event which interest us enough to hop back on. Then, once we, for the umpteenth time, grind the new piece of equipments' resources then grind for its levels to later slap a "potato" on to and then play maybe one more survival with it, we just put the game back down and wait again. I find it a bit sad that even I beg the devs for new content I'll acquire and max out within a month or so just to put the game back down for another few months in anticipation of the next new chunks of content.
In short, new players are sure to love this should you be able to push through the grindfest that is Warframe, as you'll soon be grinding without even realizing what you're grinding for. As for veterans of Warframe, try convincing friends to join so you can enjoy helping the Lotus teach them the ways of the Tenno. If all else fails, the game's creative community has some of the best fan art and cosplay I've seen in a while.
P.S. You can buy everything instead of farming for it, but not every single person has the liquidity to drop hundreds of dollars on a free-to-play game. For those who farm by choice, you guys and gals are the true MVPs.

A LOT of GLITCHES....

I've even fallen victim to this myself many times. I've taken note to be sure NOT to be standing on a resourse while harvesting because I would be left simply dangling in the air unable to move once the resourse disappears untill I restart the game ( which takes several attempts at times ). And then there is the lack of collision with the walls I build and dinos. seems dino collision is only applied to thier feet. the rest of their body can easily go through any wall I build. Which again at times leads to a tamed dino being killed. Again.... NOT COOL ( Dinos even up getting entwined with each other due to the lack of collision )
Secondly I end up going back and forth gathering tamed dinos that have somehow forgoten how to move AROUND the lanscape as the are following me. The wild dinos have the same problem at times however not while in persuit of me. They always seem to know to go AROUND some ores or trees or whatever to get to me. Not my tamed dinos though. An EASY fix might be to have the tames follow MY PATH instead of ME. I'm just saying... With all the weaving to get through some places. The AI needs to be more " Intelligent "
There are many other flaws or glitches that I'm not going to go into at this time as I'm truely not trying to simply bash the game.
As far as the Graphics, Crafting, and overall mechanics of the game goes.... I LOVE it !!!  HOWEVER.... All those things could be 10 out of 10 but if the PLAYABILITY is lacking to the point that ARK is at currently I could not recomend the game. It seems to me to be a game that is in TESTING and should NOT be charged for at this time.  I WILL however continue playing in hopes that these issues are soon resolved. As I said... I do like the game. Just was expecting more for my money. Frustrated that I spent over $40 on a game that I don't even consider playable to the degree that I KNOW it could be.
So with that said.. I truely hope to see some of these issues fixed in the upcoming updates. ARK has the POSSIBILITY to be worthy of being labeled one of the BEST games of its day....

good:
-cool looking space ninjas
cool looking environments
-controls well
-satifying ragdoll/death physics
-wide range of weapons and powers
-sufficiently challenging
-free
bad:
-the game is designed in such a way that you naturally lean towards rushing through everything as fast as you can which makes it feel samey and repetitive
-the menu/inventory/crafting menu are all counter-intuitive and difficult to navigate
-it takes 100,000+ credits, one orikin cell (really rare), two nurodes (also really rare), at least 3 boss fights, and 84 hours to craft a single warframe.  You can then sell this (regardless of level) for a whopping 25,000 credits.  That is stupid!  I should get at least a million for all the effort it takes!
-buying/selling/trading with players and npcs is inconvenient and not flexible enough
-everyone can design their ninja as they like so teams of 4 generally end up looking like a crazy troop of clowns
-bosses are extremely unsatisfying to fight
-you can own no more than two warframes and a handful of weapons at a time unless you spend money on the game
You will enjoy this game if you just like insane explosions of raw power and then collecting millions of little treasures that fall in your wake.  It's very much about the journey and not so much about the destination

As much as I enjoy the positive aspects of this game, the negative just weigh it down too much to recommend it to anybody.. After leveling my character to level 67 through hard work and about 100 hours of gameplay, I had nothing to show for it.. All my bases I've built on Pvp have been destroyed. I could have joined a tribe but the system of building and rules of joining a tribe are confusing and atrocious.
I joined a tribe with a level 2 player when I first started playing and he eventually became innactive and left the tribe to me, and after multiple hours trying to construct a small base, I decided to leave the tribe and what do you know... I was now locked out of my own base because it belonged to the tribe I quit, which now had nobody in it.. Bye bye all my hard work. From then on, I never joined someone elses tribe..
Which was fine by me since I've always been sort of a loner and find friends a little bothersome at times.. But this game is clearly designed to be played with a tribe. So any time I had an altercation with someone on a dino, even lower level players, I lost. There's no way a single player can tame enough dinos to defend himself from any type of tribe of people. I spent hours and hours taming but the only thing I could tame effectively were dilo's which are absolutely useless.
They are just pretty to look at, meat fridgerators but can't fight their way out of a wet paper bag. I did manage to tame a parasaur but it was gone the next day with the gate I built also knocked down... Everything I managed to tame was killed pretty fast. I once got into it with some very low level players who used bola's to tie me up and take all my stuff and they someone made their way into my base multiple times and my raft which I swear I had closed.
I always closed the door behind me when I walk out of my bases. But anyway I got to be trolled by a level 8 and a couple of his level 5 buddies. I told them it wasn't fair of them to use such cheap tactics, but they insisted it was fair because it gave low level players a chance to fight against bigger players. Even though I worked my butt off to get to level 60 (I was around this level at the time) and all they had to do was find a had a some thatch and they could take everything I had. In every other mmo game, you have to actually work your way up and have something to show for it, but nope not in this game.
You get punked by anyone. And eventually the low level newbies got someone to raid my base with one of his flyers and I just had to sail away in my raft to the far north and say bye bye because those things can't be killed and now everyone knew where my base was. I was absolutely devastated by anyone with flying dinos. They picked me up constantly and dropped me into the ocean where I would eventually tire and drown from hitting their dino as many times as I could with my at least 300% melee damage working it's charm like a feather duster and tickling the dino to drop me...
They are tanks with wings and to add insult to injury, it was guys about half my level flying them and terrorizing me.... And so back to the other part of the story, I sailed to the far north and made a base there, and I also made a base far in the mountains on the west coast where I thought nobody would find them. I upgraded my fortitude and spent forever on the north base but came up short handed and died at least 100 times from cold and starvation. So I spent most of the rest of the time trying to build my mountain base where it was at least warm enough not to die. I built traps to trap large dinos to tame but never once got enough supplies or power to do so. I trapped many, but tamed none...
I only managed to tame a raptor which died quickly. I tried to tame sabortooths, a therizinosaurus, and a trike and flyers to at least fight back against other players but to no avail. It was just too risky, too time consuming, and with a very small percent of it even working. 100 stacks of meat do crap to tame a sabortooth because you end up killing it for it to stay unconscious and trying to make narco arrows is a pain and shooting it at the right time, and by that tame your trapped sabor could mysteriously disappear which has happened before. This just got me too frustrated to play anymore so I stopped playing for about a month and came back and every single dang thing I built was gone.

I've been holding off on writing a serious review on this game for a few reasons
- I'm 700 hours in and only MR9 (Although I've just been joking around with a few friends for most of that)
- I've not play the game consistantly enough
- I'm not late-game
- I've been waiting for more lore quests to come out
But, despite all of that: here's my opinion on this game
Warframe is a game where you're an agile-space-ninja-mercenary-thing, and you're goal is to


, well there is no real goal, you just play it. There are quests, but they're all optional. Some give you some pretty neat stuff, and others are just very lore heavy(Which i found very interesting), and give you the parts of differnt warframes. There is a premium currency, like many other F2P games, which can be obtained by buying it from the website, or trading with other players that probably paid for it. This game is more fun, and enjoyable with friends, because solo makes some missions harder, and you'll just have people to interact with, so that you dont go insane while doing these repetitive missions, and the game rewards you for playnig with others, you get an Affinity(Warframe's form of Experience) boost from being in range of other players. With a new player base probably going to arrive, since DE(Digital Extremes) paid Rooster Teeth to play their game on Acheivement Hunter. As much as i enjoyed this game, I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone who has a life, and or friends/family outside of the internet. If you don't have any of those, then you're good, play this game to your heart's content.

Warframe is a large, multiplayer game in which the player, known as the Tenno, control their warframes to complete missions and tasks, with an overarching goal of restoring order to the system, Taking place over all the planets in the solar system, plus some extra terrestrial bodies such as Ceres and Europa.
The basics of gameplay are fairly easy to understand, where in a very basic level could be played out similar to other shooters. However the Warframe has much greater capabilities, with alot of mobility at their disposal and frame-exclusive abilities which can turn the tide of battle, offering a more skilled level of play in working for synergy between weapons, abilities and mobility options available. This can provide even greater strength with others, as each mission can be completed in a squad of up to four players, which extends to eight for the Trials of the systems, the end-game content so to speak.
The initial arsenal which the Tenno has access to is limited, but different weapons are made ready for construction as you experience the game, with the increase of the Tenno's Mastery Rank (MR). MR is essentially a measurement for how much of the game a certain Tenno has experienced, in which a Tenno of rank 3 has not experienced nearly as much of the game of a Tenno of rank 12, for example. Increasing your MR also unlocks the avaliability of some sections of the game's content, such as weapons, quests and certain areas.
Missions are easy to get into and intially can have significant variance, such as defense, interception and capture missions, and after a short while of gameplay the Tenno can also complete a quest to obtain an Archwing, which can provide a fresh task to undertake.
Community is also rather nice, with many members willing to aid others and there is the ability to join a clan within the game to interact with a smaller community within.
However, the Single biggest flaw for the game is repetition and grinding. Many parts of the game can require grinding for specific materials and blueprints, which often results in returning to missions multiple times, and weapons and warframes require useage in order to gain levels, which adds to this grind. For a player who doesnt mind a grind, this isnt much of a big issue, but many players, myself included, do not enjoy the huge amount of grinding required.
Warframe IS a fun game, and also holds lore which at times can play a significant impact into the game, But the grind which it holds is a significant deterrent for many players in the long run. despite this, I find myself returning time and time again to play, with the updates adding more content to indulge in. It is not a game for everyone in the long run, but by heck it at the very least can provide at least 10 hours of fun for most people.
Plus the game is free. Because it helps bring in players :3

On a dark winter night, a ghost walks the ramparts of Elsinore Castle in Denmark. Discovered first by a pair of watchmen, then by the scholar Horatio, the ghost resembles the recently deceased King Hamlet, whose brother Claudius has inherited the throne and married the king’s widow, Queen Gertrude. When Horatio and the watchmen bring Prince Hamlet, the son of Gertrude and the dead king, to see the ghost, it speaks to him, declaring ominously that it is indeed his father’s spirit, and that he was murdered by none other than Claudius. Ordering Hamlet to seek revenge on the man who usurped his throne and married his wife, the ghost disappears with the dawn.
Prince Hamlet devotes himself to avenging his father’s death, but, because he is contemplative and thoughtful by nature, he delays, entering into a deep melancholy and even apparent madness. Claudius and Gertrude worry about the prince’s erratic behavior and attempt to discover its cause. They employ a pair of Hamlet’s friends, Rosencrantz and Guildenstern, to watch him. When Polonius, the pompous Lord Chamberlain, suggests that Hamlet may be mad with love for his daughter, Ophelia, Claudius agrees to spy on Hamlet in conversation with the girl. But though Hamlet certainly seems mad, he does not seem to love Ophelia: he orders her to enter a nunnery and declares that he wishes to ban marriages.
A group of traveling actors comes to Elsinore, and Hamlet seizes upon an idea to test his uncle’s guilt. He will have the players perform a scene closely resembling the sequence by which Hamlet imagines his uncle to have murdered his father, so that if Claudius is guilty, he will surely react. When the moment of the murder arrives in the theater, Claudius leaps up and leaves the room. Hamlet and Horatio agree that this proves his guilt. Hamlet goes to kill Claudius but finds him praying. Since he believes that killing Claudius while in prayer would send Claudius’s soul to heaven, Hamlet considers that it would be an inadequate revenge and decides to wait. Claudius, now frightened of Hamlet’s madness and fearing for his own safety, orders that Hamlet be sent to England at once.
Hamlet goes to confront his mother, in whose bedchamber Polonius has hidden behind a tapestry. Hearing a noise from behind the tapestry, Hamlet believes the king is hiding there. He draws his sword and stabs through the fabric, killing Polonius. For this crime, he is immediately dispatched to England with Rosencrantz and Guildenstern. However, Claudius’s plan for Hamlet includes more than banishment, as he has given Rosencrantz and Guildenstern sealed orders for the King of England demanding that Hamlet be put to death.
In the aftermath of her father’s death, Ophelia goes mad with grief and drowns in the river. Polonius’s son, Laertes, who has been staying in France, returns to Denmark in a rage. Claudius convinces him that Hamlet is to blame for his father’s and sister’s deaths. When Horatio and the king receive letters from Hamlet indicating that the prince has returned to Denmark after pirates attacked his ship en route to England, Claudius concocts a plan to use Laertes’ desire for revenge to secure Hamlet’s death. Laertes will fence with Hamlet in innocent sport, but Claudius will poison Laertes’ blade so that if he draws blood, Hamlet will die. As a backup plan, the king decides to poison a goblet, which he will give Hamlet to drink should Hamlet score the first or second hits of the match. Hamlet returns to the vicinity of Elsinore just as Ophelia’s funeral is taking place. Stricken with grief, he attacks Laertes and declares that he had in fact always loved Ophelia. Back at the castle, he tells Horatio that he believes one must be prepared to die, since death can come at any moment. A foolish courtier named Osric arrives on Claudius’s orders to arrange the fencing match between Hamlet and Laertes.
The sword-fighting begins. Hamlet scores the first hit, but declines to drink from the king’s proffered goblet. Instead, Gertrude takes a drink from it and is swiftly killed by the poison. Laertes succeeds in wounding Hamlet, though Hamlet does not die of the poison immediately. First, Laertes is cut by his own sword’s blade, and, after revealing to Hamlet that Claudius is responsible for the queen’s death, he dies from the blade’s poison. Hamlet then stabs Claudius through with the poisoned sword and forces him to drink down the rest of the poisoned wine. Claudius dies, and Hamlet dies immediately after achieving his revenge.
At this moment, a Norwegian prince named Fortinbras, who has led an army to Denmark and attacked Poland earlier in the play, enters with ambassadors from England, who report that Rosencrantz and Guildenstern are dead. Fortinbras is stunned by the gruesome sight of the entire royal family lying sprawled on the floor dead. He moves to take power of the kingdom. Horatio, fulfilling Hamlet’s last request, tells him Hamlet’s tragic story. Fortinbras orders that Hamlet be carried away in a manner befitting a fallen soldier.

Right off the bat I want to say that I've gotten a lot of enjoyment out of this game. I like this game, it can be great fun and there's a lot of potential here. I've been playing it off and on since the earliest launch. But I CAN'T RECOMMEND IT, for a variety of reasons.
First of all, it's been almost two years, at the time of writing this review, since ARK's early access began. I can't think of a worse example of abusing the early access system. They developers are constantly pushing new content, which would be great, except the game has MASSIVE optimization issues, an ever growing list of bugs and glitches, and a lot of core gameplay issues. In my opinion, the devs should be focusing on polishing the core game before trying to add a bunch of extra content. After this much time, it's clear that the devs are not managing time effectively and have misplaced priorities.
Secondly, and this is a big thing for me out of principle, ARK released a premium purchaseable DLC pack while STILL IN EARLY ACCESS. If you are still in the developing stages of a game, and have asked people for money to help finish the project, you should NOT be cashing in on popularity and trying to sell an additional DLC pack. In my opinion, that's agregious and ethically wrong. You owe it to early backers to finish the BASE GAME before you try selling off additional content. Scorched Earth should have either been free to early access players, and then made a paid DLC after full launch, or better yet the devs should have just waited until the base game was finished to spend valuable time working on DLC.
Finish the bloody game before you try cutting it into pieces to sell me. It still runs like garbage, even on incredibly powerful high end gaming PCs, and the core game is still hugely flawed. I've now quit playing the game indefinitely. I'll reconsider once they fully launch, if the game is actually a polished product. Otherwise I will no longer be wasting any time or money on this disappointment.
EDIT: The fact that they've now forcibly rolled the lazy hunger games spinoff in with the original STILL UNFINISHED game for an exorbitant price is absoulutely despicable. Prime example of a potentially great game ruined by overly greedy developers. Don't give them your hard-earned money, they've repeatedly slapped their customers in the face, they don't deserve a penny.

IMO the three goals of Warframe:
,
,
. And that's what I'm going to be explaining with this review and also add why I love the game in the later part.
Warframe is a co-op 3rd person shooter version of an action RPG like Diablo and Path of Exile. The game has procuderally generated levels and all of it are instances. All of this is set in the far future of our Solar System, so there's an interesting SciFi setting going on. There various co-op missions ranging from kill everything in the level to stealth your way to a computer terminal and even endless point defence missions where newly spawned enemies scale in stats to insane levels. There's also large group content that plays out like an MMO raid. There's even PVP that plays like an arena shooter and one mode that's basically space lacrosse.
In the game you're the Tenno/Operator which is a player faction that's the only one that can use Warframes. And Warframes are essentially powered suits/mindless beings where you channel void energy in various flashy powers. So imagine a frost mage, a fire mage, and a sound mage. Things go crazy with the powers, okay. There are warframes for any playstyle. And not just warframes but also weapons like guns, bows, swords, gunblades, an biological glaive, and so much more. And all of those weapons and warframes give you a strong power fantasy since you can literally kill an entire army with your friends. Also, there's a lot of customization of stats and loadouts with the warframes and weapons with the use of their respective stat modifiers called
. Mods are like collectible cards which give stat differences to weapons and warframes. Some are straight up damage boost while others give off elemental damage or increase crit chance. You know RPG stats. And all of this play into the first goal:
. When you get the right gear and the right group, carnage ensues. And the game engine can support so much carnage and particle effects to the point where JJ Abrams lens flares are put to shame.
Going back to the customization, I have to emphasize that it's a lot. From colour schemes to different armour sets for your warframe and even capes made of fire. Also, the game now allows for user made content so expect more skins and what not. Thus,
. Always look good when destroying an entire space military force.
Goal 3
: But how do you get these items since it is loot game, isn't it? Well, that's the cool thing about the game is since it's free you can craft everything in the game or you can buy them with real money. The loot you get isn't a straight up complete weapon but the parts of it. And so that's how the game plays: you do missions to get parts to then build cool stuff. Although, I have to admit it's pretty grindy. For a single weapon, it could take a day or two to gather materials. Then a 12 hr to 3 day wait for it actually build. They had to put some mechanics for you to sink real money into.
Which nicely brings up the business model, it is a free-to-play game. And in my opinion, it's pretty fair and not actually to pay-to-win. Sure, you can straight up buy a weapon with real cash. But it's a co-op game. How can you get an unfair advantage against other players when your in a co-op game? You basically just skip the grind. Also, there's not really a clear best when it comes to warframe and weapon setup. Oh sure, the forums and reddit will say there is. But again it's a co-op game. And any all gear setup in place in the game is just there to provide a very different playstyle. Now, I did say PVP is in the game. But it's tricky since they balance the weapons there differently for PVP and PVE. And you don't get to use the PVE mods in PVP which is where the real power comes from in the game. Those mods you can't buy with cash. You can trade for them from someone who has it. But that someone had to put hours in the game to get said mods. So all-in-all, it's a tricky balancing game the devs did with the business model. And so far it's not really pay-to-win.
But in my opinion. The best thing about Warframe is the devs commitment for the game. They always update the game. They add in meaningful and new mechanics to just better the game. And they often do bring in new mechanics in a lore friendly way. The last update changed up how reward tables are done in missions. Instead rolling the dice in a huge reward table. They now have it so you bring an item with you on mission which is a more focused reward table to roll the RNG dice with. And you can affect the chance you get the item you want with item boost. So, yeah, there's always something to look forward to and come back to with Warframe.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

The game in of itself is massive, and the amount of content is absurd considering the lifespan of the game, and is a tribute to the developers ability to keep the game fresh. A truly outstanding survival game that stands head and shoulders above the rest in it's genre. Most negative reviews complain about the lack of optimisation and PvP (shortcomings which do exist), however they fail to mention that the actual game itself is brilliant. Occasionally it is a bit of a slog to grind for resources to build and tame dinosaurs, but FOR CHRIST'S SAKE YOU CAN TAME DINOSAURS! Who doesn't want to ride to battle on a T-Rex? To be honest if you try and play PvP on an official server though your more likely to ride to battle on a dodo, die instantly then rage quit. Yes, it can be frustrating occasionally, especially when you have poured alot of time into building or taming something, but half the fun is starting over. The actual gameplay is solid, with all the key survival elements, and the dev's add new content monthly, keeping it fresh. People seem to forget this game is early access, and that's because it plays like a finished game (most of the time), so unless you try and play it on a potato, it should offer hours of fun, heartbreak, frustration, satisfaction and acceptance that you never will get that T-Rex, as well as infinite re-playability.

You can build your domain from a thatch shanty to an island spanning fortress with Rexes walking the grounds, you know sort of guard dog like.
In classic sandbox mod there isn’t currency as such.  It ends up being more barter than even exchange because what’s trash to you might be treasure to someone else.  Its very nature is unknown and that’s the best part.
There is pain, logging in to find your Rex died of a leach that you didn’t see before you logged off, and pleasure, finding that 145 plesiosaur literally trapped in your unfinished water fort.  There is fun and friendship.  There is annoyance and antagonism.  It is what you make it.
I find the game enjoyable and on occasion frustrating, but I think it has some good legs and should be running for a while.
