After more than 1000hs of play i can wholeheartedly recommend this game fully. I have mainly played solo or in small groups so i will review as such.
I can understand a lot of people feel turned down by the ruthless concepts that make up the core of this game, especially after they had invested 100hs of play hours into animal representations that were erased in a matter of seconds. for me, the high stakes are making this game a chalenge worth to play, over and over again.
The game is meant to be played pvp and all deviations of this primary condition will make the game less. But depending on your expectations it would be the wiser choice to go at it alone or purely with friends on a private server.
Expectation management is what this is all about. As you will invest many days to building up your base, your dinosaur breeds, your relations, it can be confronting to watch it all go because of a bad decision or a stroke of bad luck. All starts with the choice of your server. You must spend some time figuring out the way you want to play the game.
I played a stretch of four months mainly solo on online unofficial server after stocking up 400hs on various other places first. To be brief, look for high difficulty settings with tame/breeding rates between *5 and *10, this will get you the best experience for your buck. The 'official' tame rates are defined by people with their heads up their asses, who think their game is flawless, which it is obviously not. These flaws, bugs, whatever, just make the official tame rates not worthed. As simple as that. mechanics are erratic at times and its sad to see fly your 3hr tamed argentavis fly off due to a pathfinding bug, and nothing you can do about it. Same goes for breeding and imprinting. so if you play at higher rates, you can have more animals with more ease, and you can enjoy breeding and the endgame content, still very challenging, which make it a better game overall,imho.
The game will keep you on top of your toes so be prepared to invest some real time. don't pick this game up right before exams or major career change or you will regret it.

Roughly one or two years ago, I tried to run this game on an ambitious budget build. The pentium G3258 was a pretty good CPU, but no match for poor code it seemed, while other Triple A titles worked just fine. Later on, I upgraded my GPU to a GTX570. The game played a bit better, but still crashed. Today, I downloaded Ark to try it one more time. I'm running a 6-core, 12 thread Xeon X5670 with a GTX 1050 ftw. I had a hard time getting past the opening menu and into the game, and it's STILL sluggish. Seriously, how much hardware does one need to play this game?
Edit:: had a bit of time to test it out. I ran it on medium with some settings dialed back. Gameplay was decent albeit some frames dropping occasionally. Turns out I can't play in full screen because once enabled, the menus don't respond to the mouse (Had to delete the config file several times during testing just to be able to play.) So I played in windowed mode. I know it's harder to optimize games for Linux, but come on. Those minimum requrements are a complete lie. My RAM usage shot up from 1 GB to 8GB when I started the game.
I know this build isn't super impressive, but I'm currently running two simultaneous Android emulators side-by-side, and they work just fine. The fact that I can run three operating systems at the same time, but still have to run ARK below medium settings with frame drops and jerry rigging is both disgusting and hilarious at the same time.

The only game I'm aware of with no gap between those who wallet-warrior through the game and those who don't. Good in-game community. (I can't say anything for the warframe forums, never used it.) Good controls, lore, etc-- with lots of satisfying moments depending on your loadout. One notable downside is the rather obvious power creep, but honestly in comparison to everything else this game has to offer, that's easily overlooked. If you like being, looking like, and talking to badasses, you'll probably enjoy Warframe.
Then again, you might want to run while you still can. :^)

When the biome update came out our server was shut down and when we joined a new server it took over a week to even be considered a tribe in the server. This game was the best of the survival game series until they tried being too fancy and now there are bionic rexes and abilities to run through bases and animals so OP they have a cap on their spawn and time in the game. Personally I feel if the developers took their time and stopped pumping out updates at super sonic speeds, this game would still be in the running for the best survival game.

I have played 172 hours in this game: 142 on official servers and 30 single player. The public MP servers are a toxic wasteland of griefers. If you ever wondered what anarchy would be like, just hop onto a public server. Yeah, there are some decent people out there, but all it takes is one griefer to transfer in from the other side of the world and all your work will be undone.
On the other hand, playing on a single player / private server has been blissful. Taming no longer requires half a day of babysitting. If you can't login for a week, your dinos won't starve and your base won't be wrecked. For anyone who says that's no fun or is too easy, you can just turn up the game difficulty so that you're dying every 10 minutes. I do miss coming across the random good person on pub servers. It's just that the system is so flawed, that it's simply not worth it.
As a single player game: highly recommend.
As a public mulltiplayer game: stay far away.

I'll start with what's wrong with the game.
-The Mastery Rank can be really grindy, and it's basically what determines how much of the game you      have access to.
-There can be some really big difficulty spikes from time to time. Looking at you, Trinity Specter. You know what you did.
-Rush missions. If you've played them then I don't need to say more.
-There are microtransactions. I’ll talk more about them below but they still earn a spot here
On a more positive note, what the game does right:
-Maneuvering around is fun and easy and melds really well with the fighting
-Switching combat styles on the fly is easy once you get the hang of the melee attack button being the   E key.
-Gunplay is rewarding
-The damage system is fairly simple to understand
-There is nothing in the game that you have to pay real money for
-The coop makes it easy to find backup on a harder mission
-The ragdoll physics + arrows/bolts = hilarious
-Stealth is well implemented and if you know what you’re doing can be done relatively easily.
-The new Relic system makes grinding for rare gear far easier, as the game has methods of adjusting the drop odds in your favor, and you can even take a copy of whatever your allies got instead of your own drop, meaning that your odds of getting what you want increases drastically.
-Alerts make getting cool drops and rare skins fairly easy
-The story and lore is pretty cool
-The developers give out the ‘freemium’ money during their weekly livestreams.
-if you have a playstyle or basic idea for a character, they probably have a Warframe for you.
-The wiki is almost always up to date, which means you can find out anything you don’t know
-It’s FUN.

At first I thought that this is nothing but your casual third person shooter. You're given the enemy and you gotta put that bullet through their heads, but after actually trying it out my view completely changed. Warframe is more complex than you could imagine. You get to actually choose your own frame, "character", who comes with it's own special set of abilites, and apart from that, you have 3 groups of weapons you get to choose from for a wide experience, and a unique way to build and augument them to make them all stronger. The multitude of tasks and missions will surely keep you busy and entertained, and if farming is your specialty (get dem argon crystals, boys), even better!
As much as the game may get repetitive, you have several quests to take care of, and soon you will discover the actual storyline going on behind that will end up getting you even more addicted; each one of these quests unlocking new features, such as having your own companions to aid you in battles.
As I am a sucker for high quality graphics and detailed landscapes, Warframe left me breathless. From smooth, ship surfaces to rough asteroid tilesets and robotic designs, you will never get bored of looking around and telling yourself "these graphics are totally slayin it".
Long story short, if you wanna be a space ninja alien thingy, shoot and slash things, be bombarded with a ton of game lore for you to piece it together, see pretty things or just brag that you have the prettiest frame (fashionframe ftw), this F2P is definitely for you!
And now, on to farming some more argon crystals for myself... :'I

I have played 172 hours in this game: 142 on official servers and 30 single player. The public MP servers are a toxic wasteland of griefers. If you ever wondered what anarchy would be like, just hop onto a public server. Yeah, there are some decent people out there, but all it takes is one griefer to transfer in from the other side of the world and all your work will be undone.
On the other hand, playing on a single player / private server has been blissful. Taming no longer requires half a day of babysitting. If you can't login for a week, your dinos won't starve and your base won't be wrecked. For anyone who says that's no fun or is too easy, you can just turn up the game difficulty so that you're dying every 10 minutes. I do miss coming across the random good person on pub servers. It's just that the system is so flawed, that it's simply not worth it.
As a single player game: highly recommend.
As a public mulltiplayer game: stay far away.

The premise of this game is amazing but the execution is absolutely embarrassing. Even for an early access game, ARK is far too broken to be recommended to anyone.
The balance issues are extremely prohibitive. Taming a dinosaur takes literal hours even for experienced players, and most species are useless while some are far too overpowered. Once you have a base and some dinosaurs, you can expect to have to log in at least every few days to keep your structures and animals from "timing out" and being deleted.
There are bugs and glitches within every single mechanic of this game. I've had 30 dinos disappear at once. I've had many dinosaurs starve to death next to troughs full of food. I've had dinosaurs get stuck hundreds of feet in the air or get pushed below the terrain, never to be seen again. I've had my character get stuck underground or in my own walls. The devs have claimed to fix all these bugs multiple times but they keep happening.
And not suprisingly, customer support is non-existant. Lost dinos or your whole base to a known bug? Too bad. When - not IF - ARK destroys hours of your work, don't expect anything more than a half-arsed copy/paste "sorry."
The developers of this game are far more interested in pushing unfinished and over-priced expansion packs than they are in actually fixing anything in the core game.
This is not worth your time or money now, or possibly ever.

This game is very good right, but as every game, it has it's issues. I will like try to share the expirience I had with the game so far so keep in mind that everything I say about the game is my personal opinion and it doesn't have to match with yours. First whats so good about the game?
1. It's free to play right? Even if you dont enjoy the game you didn't pay sh*t to play it
2. Multiplayer. Warframe is like 90% about playing with your friends/guild members. What a surprize since it is MMO, right?
3. Tons of content. There is like a 1000000 of different weapons, warframes and even events/alert missions.
4. Graphics. Warframe has such a beautiful graphics for a F2P game, it even competes with some of the greater non-F2P games (imo)
5. Character customization. OK, it's not like Blade&Soul level of character customization, but it's still really good. Every Warframe has it's own skins and you can recolor litteraly everything. Even the pets and ship etc etc.
6. Map/Missions. The map in Warframe is really big, right? It's like the whole solar system. On each planet you have like 15-20 missions and if you dont like doing that much stuff before moving to the next planet, dont worry. You only have to complete a couple of missions in order to unlock the next planet.
7. The game gets a lot of updates in which new weapons, warframes or enemies are added. Sometimes even new mission types, raids or boss remakes but none of these are actually that common.
8. If lore is something you like about games dont worry, because warframe got a lot of lore and more is yet to come. If you dont like it, well nobody is forcing you to watch the cinematics or read the lore. It's up to you.
9. It's not pay2win. The only thing you can buy with premium currency (platinum) and not with normal currency (credits) are some skins and resources from shop. Thats it. Everything else you can get simply by playing. Plus you can get platinum from trading with other players, so you dont even have to spend money to get these skins
Sounds pretty nice for an F2P games, right?
But it has it's cons. Not much, but pretty significant ones.
1. Grind. Everything you do in warframe is grinding resources, bosses and other suff. Over some time grinding the basic stuff gets boring. But there are many ways to speed up the farming.
2. End game. This is the reason I don't play much lately. Not so far ago, EG/endless EG missions (Void missions) you had to do in order to get EG stuff got removed from the game and instead Void Nodes got added, I won't explain what these are because it would be pretty long. In short, huuuuge part of EG was removed, but more EG weapons are being added and investing time in upgrading them is like completely useless right now because all you would get from that is overkilling the enemies even more.
OK, that's it. I would recommend warframe to you if you wanted to play it for some time AND to play it with friends. Rating: 5/10 before 100 hrs; 9/10 100-1000 hrs; 7,5/10 1000+ hrs
Hope this review helped :)

First of all Warframe is free to play. Does that mean its pay to win? No, but you could say its pay to win faster. You can achieve nearly everything in the game without investing any money. The only thing that you can't get by just playing are cosmetics for your Warframe and Weapons.

There are more then 300 different weapons for your disposal, divided into Primary, Secondary and Melee. You can get more then 20 Warframes with different skills and abilities.
In general Warframe is a nice coop game if you got time. And you will need time to dive into the great experience of Warframe. But after this time you find out that Warframe has got a great and helpful community. You can also join a clan.
And after all these hours of Warframe I still really like it and I can only recommend it for you. If you like science-fiction you should give it a try.

I started to play this game 3 years ago and much has changed since then. The developer team Digital Extremes has added new content over the whole time. You will be able to participate in events, which are been held regulary.
The Story of Warframe is part of this new content. It is told with multiple questlines that the player is able to play. These questlines will not only give you background about the space ninjas but also give you new gear.
There are more then 300 different weapons for your disposal, divided into Primary, Secondary and Melee. You can get more then 20 Warframes with different skills and abilities.
In general Warframe is a nice coop game if you got time. And you will need time to dive into the great experience of Warframe. But after this time you find out that Warframe has got a great and helpful community. You can also join a clan.
And after all these hours of Warframe I still really like it and I can only recommend it for you. If you like science-fiction you should give it a try.

Back when games used to be good, developers were never afraid to treat their players as intelligent human beings capable of rational thought and problem solving. They would add all sorts of complicated systems to their games in order to create depth and enrich the learning experience, design long term goals requiring patience, and experiment with a lot of clever if risky ideas that no longer fly in today's homogenised market, some of which worked well and some of which didn't, but were still very interesting anyway.
Warframe is one of 'those' games. It's like a pineapple. If you just try and bite into it at surface level, you're getting nothing. You need to sink your teeth into it and tear the armored skin away to get to all that juicy goodness inside, or stop being a scrub and actually go get a knife and cut it into slices.
A ragtag band of passionate gamer devs holds this piece of work together. They've weathered through ♥♥♥♥♥♥ investors trying to dictate what kind of games they should make in the past, and critics telling them that their ideas won't sell, and yet they went and did it anyway. This game is a labor of love. It's ambitious, weird, and confusing but also has that delightfully raw edge that gives it all sorts of charm. It's like walking into a one of those really fancy old style kitchens where the chef has garlic cloves all neatly bound and hanging up on the walls.
What is the premise of Warframe? It takes part in the far far future. High society got too high and the Orokin space nerds created a dangerous mutational zombie virus that ran out of control. Over time, remnants of humans started fighting for territory. Grineer space nazis fighting with Corpus space jews threatened to tear the universe apart, and still nobody was doing anything about the Infestation space zombies clawing their way through the starchart one planet at a time. Some lady named Lotus decided something had to be done, and activated a signal or something to awaken Tenno Space ninjas from their cryo sleep in order to solve the problem. The Tenno pilot their remote controlled ninja space suits and kill everybody who's causing trouble using their super space ninja powers, retrieve sick loot while doing so, and craft a variety of bizarre space weapons for use in honorable (??!?) combat. The intricacies of this lore are presented to the player through a series of quests, scans, and hidden documentation, needing to be sniffed out bit by bit.
As a Tenno, you are basically a God on the battlefield. You are insanely mobile, able to leap across large distances, climb walls, defy gravity and slide across the ground as if your knees were made of soap. Unlike many other 3rd person shooters, the player is gifted an expansive list of character commands, some of which you'll find yourself using way more often than others (Did you know you could even do a backflip?) but all of which fill some sort of purpose. A less experiencd player can easily get by with minimal use of their mobility, using cover tactics and careful application of their powers, but a player who's put time into masteirng the game's systems will be everywhere at once, dancing back and forth between large waves of enemies, mixing melee attacks with bursts of gunfire, and utilizing status effects and the environment to their advantage. This game is very much about learning, the kind of game where you learn a specific set of rules through repetition and experimentation, and then slowly build up a mastery of the game while unlocking new toys to play with as a reward for your hard work.
The sheer amount of content that has been shoveled into the game over time is positively staggering. Warframe is choc full of little experimental systems that the developers thought would be a good idea at the time, but now serve hardly any purpose. Why can you still scan plants on Earth and brew them into antitoxins? They allow you to get higher tier rewards specificaly on sabotage missions but ONLY on the earth tileset. They were once part of a temporary event, but remain in the game anyway as a small, but cute little system that might be fun to exploit when the player is bored. Game developers Digital Extremes are not shy about adding content to the game, while also batting their noodle arms haplessly at the unending tide of bugs and balance issues, somehow managing to outdo their list of fixes with every patch. I'm still waiting for my favorite gun, the Embolist, to get a buff, it's been rubbish for years now, and yet I can't complain about these nifty toxic gas throwing knives they just released. (knives? More like miniature octopi)
The game's major systems have been re-designed at least once each through the game's development cycle. There are not many developers out there who are prepared to make mistakes of that magnitude, then try to fix them while still making an enjoyable fanfare out of the process. Good guys DE run weekly dev streams, conversing with their players and showing tidbits of what they're working on for everyone to get hot and bothered about. They are a bunch of loveable goofballs and it's hard to dislike them (even though we may all scream at them for not fixing infinate scaling enemies and not cutting down on RNG)
There is a lot of RNG in this game. There is a lot of grinding, but there's also a lot of consistency where it counts. There are damage number explosions from various overlapping damage sources, filling your screen with clouds of coloured numbers, enough to make the hardcore nerd inside you froth with sensory delight. If you're the kind of player who absolutely cannot abide grinding in any form, or doesn't like videogame systems that might break immersion, then Warframe is not for you. I'm in the boat that thrives off grinding as long as the game's core systems are fun, so in essence, Warframe is the perfect kind of game for me, and I LOVE damage number explosions.
And the art...Warframe is really pretty. It has this pulpy sci-fantasy aesthetic, like H.R. Gieger somehow got over a mental illness and stopped making creepy imagery, trying to go for something beautiful instead but not quite getting it. The character designs are a twisted mess of organic shapes and mechanical excess that somehow comes together anyway in a passably cohesive manner. You learn to love the bulky potato armor of the Grineer, the boxy Fifth-Element fashion sense of the Corpus, and the lovecraftian body horror of the Infested while piloting faceless space gimp ninja suits who somehow manage to convey plenty of character, even without any discernable facial features. Your missions will take you through a wide variety of scifi tilesets, each with little nuances and shortcuts to spice up the status quo.
Do I recommend Warframe? Absolutely. Do I recommend it for everyone? Hell no. If anything I've talked about sounds fascinating to you, then definately give it a shot. The game is free to play, and DE makes most of their money off cosmetic items, convenience sales like exp boosters, and inventory slots (which are pretty cheap, and you're going to need a lot of them). However, you can also trade rare items in-game with other players who are prepared to pay real money for them, allowing you to relieve some other poor sap's frustration while they support the developers in your stead, you miserly sod.
If you're the kind of gamer who believes that less equals more, or only wants in for the story, then you're not going to have a good time. Warframe demands a lot of time and energy commitment. The new player experience is pretty bad, even though the developers are working on it slowly but surely. This title appeals to a very specific kind of gamer and personality, the kind that big developers are trying to phase out, and it does it's job very well. It has issues. Tons of them, but the pros heavily outweigh the cons.

Okay, here's my review. I'm gonna talk about whats bad with this game, but hey, I'm still recommending it to everyone !
- Warframes basic gameplay is similar. no matter which one you choose. And for your first choice of the Warframe (you suit / model / character ) make it a good one, because you will be stuck with it for a long time till you can buy a new one.
- This game is a grind ! Sooner you accept it, the better it will be for you.
- You get to play co op. But it's up to you. It's true that this game is best enjoyed by at least 2 players fighting side by side, but it's equally enjoyble in solo missions as well.
- Speaking of co op, you might get some players who would just rush on ahead witout thinking twice about objectives or plans or just stray far behind. Best played with a buddy who knows your play style, has a decent grasp of objectives and tend not to mess around much. Many times I have had random players who rushed ahead and tiped off the NPC I was supposed to capture, made it to the NPC before me and engaged every other enemy except the target to watch it run away right before my eyes, failing the mission, because they were showing off how awesome they were at fighting and parkouring.
- The game kinda has a drop-in-drop-out but with very limited support. So, it's better to have pre-made squad before you attempt a difficult or key or critical mission and make sure that squad actually sees it through.
- I haven't spent any money on the game yet, so I can't comment how rewarding it is to spend money on it.
Okay, that's it !
EDIT :
With the latest Plains of Eidolon update, so much in Warframe has changed now. It's got a solid mix of old and new gameplay styles, a new Warframe that's super-cool and tons of new content. But still, this game was always a grind and will forever be one.
DE (Developers) have done a monumental job in making the Plains of Eidolon, filling up with objectives and enemies, and level that is freakishly large yet feels so natural and hand-crafted. Plus Warframe's fast paced, ninja-parkour themed gameplay suits perfectly well in it. Any other developers or publishers would have made it a DLC pack or something, but DE being the most repectable devs of them all, have allowed this huge content for free, and even accessibe to the new players. Obviously, new players won't have access to Archwing Launcher or things necessary to fight the bosses that emerge in the night time, but they can very well explore during the day-time and complete a bounty or two before moving on.
Plain of Eidolon continue the stale World-State of Warframe in a meaningful way. Seems like the efforts of Lotus and Tenno have paid off and Humans (Orokin, or whatever is left of them) are returning to inhabit the earth once again. You start off with a town of Cetus, which is a reclamation colony. Even the steel meridian setup their base of operations on earth - called as the Iron Wake. Cetus is a town full of life and activity. Here's where you'll find quests, bounties and other useful things...
New players and Veterans alike, Warframe's new update is absolute must play !

I liked this game, but I can slowly see where this game is going. The rest of the updates seem to add only nerfs. Not just nerfs, though. We also have to worry about new dinosaurs that ruin the game, like the Leedsichthys or the Ichthyornis. Another thing is that these game-breaking dinosaurs can't be tamed or don't really have a good use when tamed. Also, about that BIG flyer nerf, it should have at least the speed-upgrading mechanic added back again. They're so nerfed already, but why remove the option to upgrade their speed? And the new sounds the Quetzal makes are alarming to me, since it is like the old sound it used to make when it was provoked. And actually, I'm pretty sure it alarms other people, too. And if you're thinking of something to nerf, can you PLEASE leave us humans alone? We really don't need nerfs, I promise you. We don't have high health like dinos do. And we don't run the fastest.
As for that Classic Flyers mod, it isn't really a good solution. For unofficial servers, they could add it, but not without us begging for it. They have the power to add or remove the mod. I want the flyer nerf to be minimized in an update or something, at least. As for official servers, people are stuck with the flyer nerf, because the owner can't add mods their official servers, even if they wanted to. Also, something that bothers me are the trailers for this game. They are outdated! Why does it matter to me? Well, I see people riding on flying dinos...AT THE TIME where the flyer nerf WASN'T there. And it doesn't show the "new stuff" like tek, the hair growth system, new caves, and new dinosaurs.
And something I kind of care about is the new inventory style. What if people never found out that 'E' was to use an item? I'm still used to clicking the item and showing the options "consume" and "drop". And I don't see anything wrong with spam-eating meat. I don't know why it's there, but it's kind of annoying, with that 0.2 second cooldown added. And please, PLEASE leave the breeding alone. It's fine the way it is. No need for nerfs, okay? Another thing is that the Scorched Earth DLC is as pricy as buying another game. It's $20, but why can't it just be for free? And I can see that humans have been nerfed. It's very hard for some people to see. But what's the nerf? Well, I saw that everyone who logged on had all of their emgrams and stats reset. Okay, we have to apply them again, but what else? Well, I see that some engrams like the Quetzal platform saddle has been PUSHED BACK to level 97. Seriously? First, you nerf the Queztal and other flyers. THEN, you push the platform saddle over to 97. Was that really necessary? The Quetzal is already not as good as it was before! There's no need for nerfs like THAT one.
Also, I have a question...for the developers. And that question is, do you care about your reviews anymore? I don't know if developers read them or not, but even if they do, it looks to me like THEY DON'T CARE. The game just keeps on going without taking any feedback into suggestion. I don't want to imagine how ARK would be like in the future when it's complete. Just PLEASE listen to the reviews, and stop nerfing everything!

In short - Great Game, absolutely money well spent. I've spent more time in this game than all my other steam games combined. ~500 hrs of entertainement for $30? Best deal ever. I know some people complain about all the things the Developer has or hasn't done, how they've ruined the game, and how they're just out to steal your money and not deliver... blah blah blah. I think a lot of this stems from the fact that you get very invested in Ark. Which is a great quality in a game! However, with the ups (and there are tons) also come the downs (and they can be very down). You will laugh and cry. You will rejoice and then want to punch your monitor and scream. IMO, it's all part of the Ark experience, and it truly is a gaming experience I will never forget.
I'm sure I'll get flak for this but a lot of the negative reviews are done by people who have spent hundreds or thousands of hours in game and then got♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥(maybe♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥multiple times). Then they go and give the game a thumbs down and write a scathing review in a hot headed state. If it really was a terrible game those thousands of hours would have been spent elsewhere. I don't mean this as disrespect to the people who left the game frustrated- I can testify that that frustration is very real. I'm more saying it so people new to Ark will have some context. Did I end up leaving disappointed/frustrated? Yes, but that was only momentary. It had been preceeded by countless hours of enjoyment. With respect to entertainment bang for your buck, Ark will get a Thumbs Up from me all day long.
Last point, I don't really care if Wild Card ever does end up releasing the "Finished" game. This game already had enough content and played well enough to keep me playing longer than I've ever played any other game, regardless of price. I definitely got my money's worth, and then some. Not to mention, most AAA titles release with plenty of bugs now anyway, so "Finished Game" is really just a matter of perspective. As far as early access games go, Ark is definitely among the gems, even if it's not perfect.
In conclusion, buy Ark, have your fun, and then when it's not fun anymore, move on with life.

I liked this game, but I can slowly see where this game is going. The rest of the updates seem to add only nerfs. Not just nerfs, though. We also have to worry about new dinosaurs that ruin the game, like the Leedsichthys or the Ichthyornis. Another thing is that these game-breaking dinosaurs can't be tamed or don't really have a good use when tamed. Also, about that BIG flyer nerf, it should have at least the speed-upgrading mechanic added back again. They're so nerfed already, but why remove the option to upgrade their speed? And the new sounds the Quetzal makes are alarming to me, since it is like the old sound it used to make when it was provoked. And actually, I'm pretty sure it alarms other people, too. And if you're thinking of something to nerf, can you PLEASE leave us humans alone? We really don't need nerfs, I promise you. We don't have high health like dinos do. And we don't run the fastest.
As for that Classic Flyers mod, it isn't really a good solution. For unofficial servers, they could add it, but not without us begging for it. They have the power to add or remove the mod. I want the flyer nerf to be minimized in an update or something, at least. As for official servers, people are stuck with the flyer nerf, because the owner can't add mods their official servers, even if they wanted to. Also, something that bothers me are the trailers for this game. They are outdated! Why does it matter to me? Well, I see people riding on flying dinos...AT THE TIME where the flyer nerf WASN'T there. And it doesn't show the "new stuff" like tek, the hair growth system, new caves, and new dinosaurs.
And something I kind of care about is the new inventory style. What if people never found out that 'E' was to use an item? I'm still used to clicking the item and showing the options "consume" and "drop". And I don't see anything wrong with spam-eating meat. I don't know why it's there, but it's kind of annoying, with that 0.2 second cooldown added. And please, PLEASE leave the breeding alone. It's fine the way it is. No need for nerfs, okay? Another thing is that the Scorched Earth DLC is as pricy as buying another game. It's $20, but why can't it just be for free? And I can see that humans have been nerfed. It's very hard for some people to see. But what's the nerf? Well, I saw that everyone who logged on had all of their emgrams and stats reset. Okay, we have to apply them again, but what else? Well, I see that some engrams like the Quetzal platform saddle has been PUSHED BACK to level 97. Seriously? First, you nerf the Queztal and other flyers. THEN, you push the platform saddle over to 97. Was that really necessary? The Quetzal is already not as good as it was before! There's no need for nerfs like THAT one.
Also, I have a question...for the developers. And that question is, do you care about your reviews anymore? I don't know if developers read them or not, but even if they do, it looks to me like THEY DON'T CARE. The game just keeps on going without taking any feedback into suggestion. I don't want to imagine how ARK would be like in the future when it's complete. Just PLEASE listen to the reviews, and stop nerfing everything!

I'll start with what's wrong with the game.
-The Mastery Rank can be really grindy, and it's basically what determines how much of the game you      have access to.
-There can be some really big difficulty spikes from time to time. Looking at you, Trinity Specter. You know what you did.
-Rush missions. If you've played them then I don't need to say more.
-There are microtransactions. I’ll talk more about them below but they still earn a spot here
On a more positive note, what the game does right:
-Maneuvering around is fun and easy and melds really well with the fighting
-Switching combat styles on the fly is easy once you get the hang of the melee attack button being the   E key.
-Gunplay is rewarding
-The damage system is fairly simple to understand
-There is nothing in the game that you have to pay real money for
-The coop makes it easy to find backup on a harder mission
-The ragdoll physics + arrows/bolts = hilarious
-Stealth is well implemented and if you know what you’re doing can be done relatively easily.
-The new Relic system makes grinding for rare gear far easier, as the game has methods of adjusting the drop odds in your favor, and you can even take a copy of whatever your allies got instead of your own drop, meaning that your odds of getting what you want increases drastically.
-Alerts make getting cool drops and rare skins fairly easy
-The story and lore is pretty cool
-The developers give out the ‘freemium’ money during their weekly livestreams.
-if you have a playstyle or basic idea for a character, they probably have a Warframe for you.
-The wiki is almost always up to date, which means you can find out anything you don’t know
-It’s FUN.

Right, first of all, this game is NOT P2W/P2P, most certainly not, you can obtain everything apart from cosmetic type items by just playing the game. However, this game, like all games, is not necessarily for everyone of course.
So: The game itself:
Well, the game is a grindfest, it requires a lot of time to get anywhere, but don't let this put you off, it can be rather rewarding most of the time. First of all, with some friends, the grind isn't that bad, it can be pretty fun sometimes, if you have no friends, well, it's still not bad, just takes a bit longer.
Visuals are rather pleasent to look at, considering it's F2P, they are rather nice, apart from the fact that my PC is a potato plugged into a wall, so I have to run everything on low and turn most of the fancy settings off, but the game still looks decent, kinda like looking through a window on a rainy day, you can still see things, just a little less so.
Gameplay is relatively simple, the starmap which has seen some changes is rather simple and has improved since it's first version, the game now rewards you more for completing these "Junctions" to get to new planets, but these rewards are for those who are new and genuinly need to traverse the starmap to get resources ect.
Combat is smooth and much like most other shooters, but with parkour thrown into the mix, this spices things up a notch just to make it a little more creative, y'know, Assassin's Creed style jump off a 500ft ledge to land on someones head with an Axe or Hammer that's the same size as your entire body, I mean, why not?
Weapons and Warframes are relatively varied amongst each other, primarily Warframes, you won't really find a Warframe similar to the next which is nice, as well as there being a fair few to choose from. Weapons are easily accessbile, those being great starter weapons to prat about and smack some Corpus melons in the face or blow them up and laugh at them, to others which are unbelieveable strong and a must have for any true Space Ninja Tenno.
All-in-all, I would recommend this game, from personal experience, I have enjoyed it more than most of the games I have purchased, hell, it's my most played game on Steam, although that's the grindfest for you.
This game does have bugs, as to be expected due to it's somewhat frequent updates, the team really do care for this game, which shows with how quickly they hotfix new bugs and what not. Put money into the game if you want but don't let anyone tell you that you can't get far without paying, that is not true, although I think that stigma has dispearsed from this game.

The devs of this game don't know how to properly balance game. They listen to the wrong complaints when they make a player-decision patch (like the flyers nurf), and change it to a completely useless point. My hours on this may be low but thats only cause i mainly play this on Xbox one (where its still not optimized but runs better for me then on my PC), where i have clocked maybe almost 1000 hours.
Although their is a huge amount of different prehistoric species to interact with in this game that have their own capabilities that set them apart for different uses, their potential for player use is not high due to their potential being lowered. And instead of making these creatures more useful to players, Dev's decide its better to make them more useless to force players to use other dinos more. This goes back to the flyers nerf, which the main complaint was towards PvP servers involving automated turrets not being able to catch insanely fast tamed flyers. So the devs responded to the childish naggings of players who couldn't use the already implamented resources at hand (the previous updates that added new species specifically made to dismount players from flyers). This game is very good right, but as every game, it has it's issues. I will like try to share the expirience I had with the game so far so keep in mind that everything I say about the game is my personal opinion and it doesn't have to match with yours. First whats so good about the game?
1. It's free to play right? Even if you dont enjoy the game you didn't pay sh*t to play it
2. Multiplayer. Warframe is like 90% about playing with your friends/guild members. What a surprize since it is MMO, right?
3. Tons of content. There is like a 1000000 of different weapons, warframes and even events/alert missions.
4. Graphics. Warframe has such a beautiful graphics for a F2P game, it even competes with some of the greater non-F2P games (imo)
5. Character customization. OK, it's not like Blade&Soul level of character customization, but it's still really good. Every Warframe has it's own skins and you can recolor litteraly everything. Even the pets and ship etc etc.
6. Map/Missions. The map in Warframe is really big, right? It's like the whole solar system. On each planet you have like 15-20 missions and if you dont like doing that much stuff before moving to the next planet, dont worry. You only have to complete a couple of missions in order to unlock the next planet.
7. The game gets a lot of updates in which new weapons, warframes or enemies are added. Sometimes even new mission types, raids or boss remakes but none of these are actually that common.
8. If lore is something you like about games dont worry, because warframe got a lot of lore and more is yet to come. If you dont like it, well nobody is forcing you to watch the cinematics or read the lore. It's up to you.
9. It's not pay2win. The only thing you can buy with premium currency (platinum) and not with normal currency (credits) are some skins and resources from shop. Thats it. Everything else you can get simply by playing. Plus you can get platinum from trading with other players, so you dont even have to spend money to get these skins
Sounds pretty nice for an F2P games, right?
But it has it's cons. Not much, but pretty significant ones.
1. Grind. Everything you do in warframe is grinding resources, bosses and other suff. Over some time grinding the basic stuff gets boring. But there are many ways to speed up the farming.
2. End game. This is the reason I don't play much lately. Not so far ago, EG/endless EG missions (Void missions) you had to do in order to get EG stuff got removed from the game and instead Void Nodes got added, I won't explain what these are because it would be pretty long. In short, huuuuge part of EG was removed, but more EG weapons are being added and investing time in upgrading them is like completely useless right now because all you would get from that is overkilling the enemies even more.
OK, that's it. I would recommend warframe to you if you wanted to play it for some time AND to play it with friends. Rating: 5/10 before 100 hrs; 9/10 100-1000 hrs; 7,5/10 1000+ hrs
Hope this review helped :)

They are so wholly focused on making new and exciting content they havent stopped to check if the content they already have works! You can command dinos at range with a series of whistles, but half it just doesnt register even if you spam the command! Dinos new and old have absolutely zero balancing. Troodons, Theriznos, Jellyfish, Alphas, Pegos, Seagulls, These and more are the bane of every player. There is a temp system which can kill you and literally no one understands how it works. I have died from heat exhaustion in the middle of a foggy night! And every time the devs post another update, these problems are ignored in favor of new, flashy content. They have put the cart so far in front of the horse that they had to release a DLC horse just so they could put the cart infront of that one too!
Development team, stop it! just stop it! This premise has too much promise to be treated this way! Minecraft with dinos! how are you screwing that up? Right, first of all, this game is NOT P2W/P2P, most certainly not, you can obtain everything apart from cosmetic type items by just playing the game. However, this game, like all games, is not necessarily for everyone of course.
So: The game itself:
Well, the game is a grindfest, it requires a lot of time to get anywhere, but don't let this put you off, it can be rather rewarding most of the time. First of all, with some friends, the grind isn't that bad, it can be pretty fun sometimes, if you have no friends, well, it's still not bad, just takes a bit longer.
Visuals are rather pleasent to look at, considering it's F2P, they are rather nice, apart from the fact that my PC is a potato plugged into a wall, so I have to run everything on low and turn most of the fancy settings off, but the game still looks decent, kinda like looking through a window on a rainy day, you can still see things, just a little less so.
Gameplay is relatively simple, the starmap which has seen some changes is rather simple and has improved since it's first version, the game now rewards you more for completing these "Junctions" to get to new planets, but these rewards are for those who are new and genuinly need to traverse the starmap to get resources ect.
Combat is smooth and much like most other shooters, but with parkour thrown into the mix, this spices things up a notch just to make it a little more creative, y'know, Assassin's Creed style jump off a 500ft ledge to land on someones head with an Axe or Hammer that's the same size as your entire body, I mean, why not?
Weapons and Warframes are relatively varied amongst each other, primarily Warframes, you won't really find a Warframe similar to the next which is nice, as well as there being a fair few to choose from. Weapons are easily accessbile, those being great starter weapons to prat about and smack some Corpus melons in the face or blow them up and laugh at them, to others which are unbelieveable strong and a must have for any true Space Ninja Tenno.
All-in-all, I would recommend this game, from personal experience, I have enjoyed it more than most of the games I have purchased, hell, it's my most played game on Steam, although that's the grindfest for you.
This game does have bugs, as to be expected due to it's somewhat frequent updates, the team really do care for this game, which shows with how quickly they hotfix new bugs and what not. Put money into the game if you want but don't let anyone tell you that you can't get far without paying, that is not true, although I think that stigma has dispearsed from this game.

I've been playining since 10/2015 and have almost 2900 hours in ARK.  Minecraft meets Call of Duty, meets Jurassic Park.  The game is fun, addictive and ever changing.  Ever changing....yeah, that happens a lot and sometimes not in ways you like.  Occasionally, the dev's will make a fundamental change that "breaks" the game.  But patches are often and new content added all the time.  Collecting dinos, breeding them, building bases and conquering the PvE aspects is thrilling enough, but then there's PvP on top of that.  If you don't like having everything you built destroyed while you're at work, don't do PvP.  Alternatively, get on a server that has a PvP schedule and that activity is only allowed during certain hours.  You'll likely start on an official server and that's fine to get the basics.  However, most people will end up on a unofficial server and there are several times more of those than official.  The mods are nuts and add legs to this "alpha" game.  Get it on sale and buy the xpac Scorched Earth as well.  I used to play WoW eight hours (or more) a day for six years and ARK stopped that cold.  If you like a triple-A title experience, ARK is not for you.  If you like a sandbox where you can tweak and mod to your heart's content, buy ARK asap.

Warning: This many get a bit ranty and preachy.
I think a lot of these reviews were left without taking into account that this game is an early access title. That and a lot of trial and error goes into making a game so ambitious. I feel like Wildcard has done a pretty damn good job all things considered. This game is a huge time sink and I think everyone fully understands that. If you expect anything less then you should not have even started playing this game in the first place.
To all those who have played a vast amount of this game and the flyer nerf is what was the "final nail in the coffin," I question your integrity. I too did not understand at first but when hearing from a friend and reading the reasoning behind the patch it makes perfect sense. They saw flyers as an extremely overpowered force in the game, making many other dinos obsolete. What makes it even worse is how easy early flyers were to tame then make ridiculously powerful. They were nerfed and now they are slowly being brought up to a balanced level. Community feedback is really needed in that situation. Leaving a negative review with hundreds or thousands of hours in this game plainly saying that the developers suck is not only not beneficial, but it is untrue. You found some enjoyment to play this game for as long as you did and I would hope that you would want to see it at least somewhat succeed. Having a negative community makes developing an already difficult game even more difficult. A lot of these reviews were left with a very narrow point of view.
I urge new players to give this game a chance and for old players to understand the full scope of developing a game like this. I am not asking you to return. Many of you feel insulted by these patches but that is a mistake on your part. Stick with the game and let these patches sit at least for a little while. Give them your feedback. I guarantee you are not the only ones that feel that way. I understand this game is not flawless. We all do. If you leave a negative review at least go into detail into why you feel that way or how it can be improved. Then maybe you may see a beneficial change in a game you clearly loved at some point.
It sucks that all the people who still enjoy this game are still playing and not leaving any reviews. Too many people use these reviews as a last ditch effort to spite the developers once they are done playing.

I feel like Wildcard has done a pretty damn good job all things considered. This game is a huge time sink and I think everyone fully understands that. If you expect anything less then you should not have even started playing this game in the first place.
To all those who have played a vast amount of this game and the flyer nerf is what was the "final nail in the coffin," I question your integrity. I too did not understand at first but when hearing from a friend and reading the reasoning behind the patch it makes perfect sense. They saw flyers as an extremely overpowered force in the game, making many other dinos obsolete. What makes it even worse is how easy early flyers were to tame then make ridiculously powerful. They were nerfed and now they are slowly being brought up to a balanced level. Community feedback is really needed in that situation. Leaving a negative review with hundreds or thousands of hours in this game plainly saying that the developers suck is not only not beneficial, but it is untrue. You found some enjoyment to play this game for as long as you did and I would hope that you would want to see it at least somewhat succeed. Having a negative community makes developing an already difficult game even more difficult. A lot of these reviews were left with a very narrow point of view.
I urge new players to give this game a chance and for old players to understand the full scope of developing a game like this. I am not asking you to return. Many of you feel insulted by these patches but that is a mistake on your part. Stick with the game and let these patches sit at least for a little while. Give them your feedback. I guarantee you are not the only ones that feel that way. I understand this game is not flawless. We all do. If you leave a negative review at least go into detail into why you feel that way or how it can be improved. Then maybe you may see a beneficial change in a game you clearly loved at some point.
It sucks that all the people who still enjoy this game are still playing and not leaving any reviews. Too many people use these reviews as a last ditch effort to spite the developers once they are done playing.

Warframe is a really good game. When you start to play, you're given a cool start to choose your 'character' which is refered to as a Warframe. -Seemingly Fast fixes
-Lots of new updates happen quick
-A ton to do
-You can play without buying everything with real money!
-Runs smoothly and looks good
-Great community
-Not everything is easy to get
The Cons of this game:
-There are some annoying glitches such as
--Possibly bugs with connecting online, if failing can 'break you' but rejoining fixes
--Some unknown things can happen to waste your long period of time spent on a mission(or quick)
-Some stuff takes a long time to get without paying w/ money
-Building can take 1min, 1hour, 12hours, 24hours, or 3 days!
-Not everything is easy to get

This review is based purely on Singleplayer and some, maybe 50 hours, multiplayer with friends on a private server.
I bought this game a while back because it looked enjoyable and I wanted a different type of survival experience other than the usual zombiefest and/or walking simulators. So far, it is extremely enjoyable. As a purely casual player, singleplayer is basically an enormous sandbox for you to play, kill, tame and generally do whatever you want with zero consequences. When you get bored, just delete your ARK and start fresh.
My multiplayer experience was a lot of fun, but I learned quick how boring it can get when the Admin likes to play in god mode with the survival aspect turned off. If you have friends who play or want to play, I definitely suggest setting up your own private server and have someone trustworthy being the Admin.
As with all Early Access titles, this game is bugged and glitched. There are still problems in-game that were present when I first purchased it a year+ ago. They will be fixed, hopefully, but you will have to learn to put with them if you play for an extended period of time. Currently they are almost finished adding content, and have started balancing and optimizing the game more, so it's getting better but still not ready for full release.
The learning curve is harsh. Very harsh. But once you get a handle on the game world it becomes extremely easy, and I say this from a casual aspect. You have unlimited options to customize your world's mechanics and setup the type of game you want. Whether it's a construction sandbox where you can OHKO the mightiest beasts, or a vicious, survival oriented land where you are hunted by everything and even a dodo can slay you. Finding the right balance to suit your desires might take a while, but it's well worth it in the end.
Personally, I won't touch the Official Servers until release. Right now they are a toxic mess or whining and griefing, and that's even on the PvE servers. Just following discussions on the Steam Forums shows the foolishness of not having regular server wipes on an Early Access title. Until they balance PvP, get rid of the duping, and figure out a way to get rid of the usual bots, glitch abusers, and griefers that are prevalent on MP games, there's not much use even playing on them. You'll save yourself a huge amount of stress and pain by playing on the Unofficial Servers only, and that's if you can find a good community.
As far as the world itself, it's fantastic. Multiple biomes, each with their own set of native creatures, multiple tiers of building types, a small assortment of weaponry to arm yourself setup in tiers, resources in the places they are supposed to be (you won't harvest pearls on land), and absolutely beautiful scenery. This doesn't even touch the multiple "new island" mods that are in the Workshop.
I definitely recommend buying this game as long as you understand it's still EA and are willing to put up with the bugs and glitches associated with such a product. I have high hopes for the finished product, and the dev team puts out regular updates (just don't go by their official release date/time), but we'll see what happens when it happens. This is a game where patience and personal experience will serve you better than watching YouTube videos.

If you keep finding a goal to reach, working towards it will make this game a blast for a long time.
I started this game by beating Earth and discobering Rhino (Tank warframe). I went on to work for Rhino prime and boltor prime.
Then my buddy and I started clan Hotline Bling and we made it our duty to make a dank dojo.
Then our friends joined us so I worked with them to get them suited up.
Then I saw that the nikana prime was locked behind player rank, so I gradually leveled gear until I finally got it. It went on to be my most used weapon.
Then I discovered Trinity prime, Queen bubble butt and focused on getting her.
Then I saw Frost prime was back from eternal slumber so I farmed him up.
Then My clan wanted to do the first raid so we all helped each other gather mods and level up gear.
Then I saw the Destreza (rapier) and went on to find it's stance mod
Then I met a banshee player that inspired me to do find banshee, and make her kill things with sound.
Then I saw the war and spent 20+ stalker beacons to find him, only to give up and buy the pack.
Then Lunaro came around and reminded me of my griffball days and I went ham into it.
Then the void disappeared and relics came along so I went on to understand the system.
Now I am on a Quest to capture the elusive BOOBAN PRIME for my pokeframe collection.
I've had many more objectives during my time playing but in all honesty, my fun was in the grind the game has to offer. It seems odd, although you will subconsciously enjoy this "WarFarm" or "GrindFrame" other people may call it. Kill. Get better loot. Repeat. There is no real goal to the game besides what you set for yourself.
Warframe is a fun game. I'd say for the money you can't go wrong.

To start off with: I have over 1300 hours in-game and 600 hours in-mission. By the way this is not a P2W game by any means, spending money on it is totally optional and up to you, you can get basically everything in the game by just playing it.
I have a lot of experience with this game, and I love it, however I do want to say that it is not a game for everyone.
There's a lot of grinding and levelling up to do, but you can get friends or clanmates to help you with that. Theres over 330 different characters/weapons/companions at the time of writing this and there's plenty of stuff to do for 2+ years worth of normal playing. I've played this game since the very first few weeks and a few months ago got back to it.
The developers always update the game with new quests, weapons, warframes and more cool stuff, it's a easy game for just casual play but you can take it a few steps further by going to endless missions which can have enemies far stronger than anything you will usually find. There's sorties: a set of special missions that appear everyday with special rewards, some of which only obtainable through this missions. There's a mod system for weapons which is very easy to understand and use. Finding people is automatic however you can find a specific set of players through recruit chat. There's trading, daily events, invasions which are a type of special mission where you help a faction defeat the other, alert missions that reward you with credits, the normal currency of the game, and sometimes alternative helmets for the different characters, there's a Archwing mode where players use Archwings, a type of technology used to fight in space.
So now that I gave you some info on the game, I'll tell you how much I like it: And thats's a hell of a lot. I spent 90% of the time I play games playing this one and have done so much and still have more to do, and even though this is a free game where it's completely up to you to spend money... I have spent over 100£ or ~125€ on this game and it was all worth it, while you can choose to trade things with other players toget the currency which i spent money on, I don't have the patience for it but some websites such as warframe.market will definitely help with that.
Overall here are my scores:
Gameplay 9.5/10 , sometimes it's a bit hard to understand where you are because the spaces are too small and this is a 3rd person shooter.
Graphics 10/10 ,  for a free game, even for a 60€/60$ game, this is incredible and they look amazing.
Lore/Storyline 10/10 , it's super interesting and fun, there's many quests to teach you about this, a codex which lets you read about the different characters stories and a lot of interesting dialogue.
This game is amazing and I absolutely recommend you try it out for a few hours, while the first few 2-3 hours are very boring, after that it's just fun after fun after fun and a bit of lore in every hour you play.

This is, one of the best and worst games I've ever played. The idea behind it is phenomenal. Unfortunately, the execution left a lot to be desired for me personally.
Pros:
- Loads of awesome dinosaurs that you can fight, tame, ride, fly, and gather supplies with.
- Modular base building mechanics, which for the most part works pretty well.
Cons:
- Probably the worst developers I've experienced in quite a while. Every patch that they released seemingly made the game worse, at least in my opinion. Patch after patch would only affect the largest tribes, completely ignoring the balancing issues faced by players who wanted to start their own tribes, or just play casually. I don't believe in my entire time of playing that I ever saw any significant bugs, abusive gameplay, or glitches fixed really. I was just expected to accept each patch because it would come with a handful of new dinosaurs that I couldn't have cared less about.
- Literally no concern for balance regarding small tribes or casual players. Servers set up and enforce their own rules. They even go as far as to completely block off areas which allow players to leave the server with their characters, which can ultimately destroy hundreds, if not thousands of hours of work for a player. The developers will do nothing for you on this either. I attempted to contact them serveral times myself, and either got no answer, or a generic one which ignored my problem followed by no response.
- Horrible optimization. I have a relatively good PC, and I was lucky to pull 30 FPS most of the time.
- Random and frequent server disruptions leading to dinos which take several hours, or even days, to tame failing,
- Server wars, in which a tribe which had a monopoly on another server would build up a massive force, and then bring over all of their dinosaurs and resources to a new server, completely destroying the tribes there if they were too weak, and setting up another monopoly there if possible.
- The game has a prisoner system in which you can knock another player unconcious, and then handcuff them and keep them in a cage. They cannot fight, run, or even die without interaction from another player. Their only hope is to spam global chat and hope that someone powerful enough to fight the captor might care enough to come and rescure them.
I'm probably missing a lot of cons as well, but honestly I think that whatever good you might have to say about this game, it's overwhelming outweighed by the amount of garbage you have to put up with in this game. I really don't advise putting your time into this game, tempting as it might be, unless it is on some sort of private server.
(Edit)
Disclaimer: This is only my experience and opinion on the game. I had a lot of fun with it in the beginning, but that quickly started to sour for the reasons posted above. I had several friends that played the game that quit before I did, and several that stayed long after, eventually becoming the server alphas. None of them ended up staying ultimately, and all of them have said they have no intent of going back any time soon.
If you can stomach PVE, have hundreds and hundreds of hours to invest, or want to play on a private server or something, this may still be the game for you. In its current state, it just isn't for me, and the developers have shown no signs of improving it to that end, which is fine. This is their game, and they may have a large audience of players who disagree with me. This is just my opinion and warning to like-minded individuals.

So I played this game now nearly 1000 hours now:
Pros:
- Alot of weapons

- it's up to you how hard it will be to get into the game ( there are alot of things you will have to learn and understand)

- the lore of the game is interesting but also complicated and not completed so you will have to wait till there comes more of it

- it's annoying to play with randoms in a lagging lobby ( host has bad connection)
- it get's sometimes really repetitive (farm->craft->leveling to 30->formating->leveling to 30->...)
- some weapons are useless, no matter how many formas you're using for them
- the prices for some rare stuff are ridiculous high (like 100€ ingame currency for one mod)
- the new recources like nitain extract (you can't farm them. you have to wait till a mission comes with it as reward)
So if you can accept the weak points of this game, you will have a good time with it. the devs are still working on it and there will be some cool new stuff in the future ( "plains of eidolon")

The progression gating on this game is atrocious. The combat is fun, but each planet is locked behind a set of requirements that are buggy, poorly explained, and often frustrating.
I have been stuck on Mars (1/4 into the game) because I need to find 5 fragments that randomly spawn during missions. I have been trying to do so for 3 days now. I almost found one, but then the other person on the team got to the "end" of the level first, and forced it to end before I could get to it. Needless to say, this alone is enough to reccomend passing on this game.
If that weren't enough, a majority of the mechanics are designed specifically to get you to spend money. While I undestand free to play games need to make money, the "good" ones do it through selling cosmetics, convenience items, or speeding up access to high teir items. Warframe intentionally forces you to wait an eternity to get new armors and items, giving even the simplest items a 12hour crafting time. That's right 12 HOURS; if you want a new weapon, you better be ready to grind the materials, buy the crafting blueprint, and then wait 12 hours before you can use it. And this is for a weapon that is different, but no better then your starting weapon.
This is really a shame, because the shooting and melee mechanics in this game are pretty solid, and it looks great to boot. Too bad it that the designers decided that RNG is the best way to add longevity and replay value, and don't mind forcing you to grind less than 1/4 into the game.

I am thumbing this up only because I have gotten my money's worth from this game. (read the entire review or my conclusion to see why I and who I do not recommend this for)
At the time of writing this I have just under 150 hours in this game. I have had it for a very long time. I have played it here and there throughout its development, and here is what I have to say about it..
This is a very hard game at default settings, very, very hard. When you wake up on the beach for the first time, you think of how nice it is and you punch some trees, pick some berries, and pick up some rocks. Out of the blue a raptor comes and kills you. You would think the spawn area would be safe, it's not. no matter where you spawn it is dangerous. I will say there are different parts of different maps that you can sapwn at that are less harsh than others, but none of them are "safe".
The optimization in this game is not the worst I have seen but it is not good. To run on ultra at 1920x1080 they reccoment you have a GTX Titan card. I have a GTX 970 SSC  paired with an i7 4770k and I can not sustain 60 fps on the high preset, and even then they have it set to automatically render only a percentage of the resolution so it looks like someone smeared pixelated poo on your screen if you look more than 10 meters ahead of you. Oh and the high preset recommends a 970 so... yeah.
All they do is add dinos, and minor bug fixes. You would think wild card would have made enough money to invest something in better optimization, PLEASE wildcard if you read this optimize your game!
Speaking of the dinos, most of them are just everywhere there are certain ones that you will find in certain regions but really it feels like a clusterf*ck of dinosours everywhere, and when I say everywhere I mean EVERYWHERE, Dinos are all over the place, there are so many of them, no wounder it is so poorly optimized there are hundreds if not thousands of AI dinosours roaming the map. It makes it feel very cluttered and it lacks attention to detail. I guess the best way to say it would be it feels like a survival game and someone had the idea to add dinos after the fact and just made a bunch and threw them onto the map everywhere.
Last complaint, it takes FOREVER to get anything done. Especially if you are alone. So if you want a game to replace your life, this is it. If you are a casual gamer who has other responsibilities that take a majority of your time, this game will suck for you.
Now I will say, if you are able to sell your soul and just play this game it is really fun after a week or more, you get weapons and can actually kill dinos that annoy you (don't worry they will respawn and annoy you more, forever). The game looks great if you have a god PC or are able to withstand the eye-killing low fps.
My conclusion is that this review is all over the place but the game is good. If you have the spare money and you have been interested in it, get it. If you are somewhat apprehensive, unless you have a group of friends who regularly play, don't bother. If you are tight on money, don't bother. It is a frustrating and time consuming game that will make your PC cry. I will continue to periodically play the game but it is nowhere near my favorite game, not even an honorable mention.

TL;DR  DE broke a good game in an attempt to milk us for cash, the game is no longer good, don't commit to the large download time.
This was fun before all the newest major changes as of writing this review. First off to anyone who is told you can get everything that cost premium currency (Platinum) just by doing a little work, that is no longer true, DE has made it so if you want a lot of things you either have to fork over $100's or spend every waking hour farming, also if you are someone without friends to play with it is impossible to get anywhere anymore. Prime parts still sell for small amounts of ducats unless you get a really rare drop then they are 100 at best, even then most of the time to get everything you want from the void trader you will need somewhere around 2,000 - 3,000 ducats unless he has trash stuff but that rarely happens, that amount is do-able but takes a VERY long time if you have bad luck and have to run everything solo like me. The new startchart takes away almost all the freedom to "choose your path" like you could in 2.0, for example if you don't like Mobile Defense like most people in this game with 2.0 you could usually go around that mission but now the path is set and if there's missions you don't want to do or can't do (High level interceptions while playing alone) you know what the only answer is? Quit the game or swim through that cancer pool. The new "Endo" system makes it so if you have duplicate mods such as Redirection, you no longer get a little extra boost because they are the same mod, now it all just takes endo, and a TON of credits. I could rant so much more about how this *Was* good and now it *is* a pile of♥♥♥♥♥♥ but odds are not much people will see this review. I may only have 900 hours here on steam but I had well over 2k on ps4 if that matters to anyone. If anyone hasn't played this game before and is thinking of getting it because of the good reviews, Don't, DE's most recent updates have driven this game so far down the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that I doubt it will ever come back, I have yet to see them try to fix these monumental mistakes to bring this game back to the fun times when you could hop on for a few hours, farm alone, make a bunch of plat by selling that stuff and still have prime things left over to craft or sell for ducats, thank you for reading and I hope this helped you make the choice on downloading Warframe or not.

I got over 700 hours on record and will stop playing this game which I cannot recommend at this point anymore.
The is called early access and you do have to accept bugs and glitches. This game though started as a normal early access game with a few bugs and glitches here and there. At this point though the number of bugs and glitches keep increasing and content that used to be bug-free now is inplayable.
If you do start the game you might only encounter few bugs in the first 50 hours of gameplay. Like falling through the world (your character will die and you probably cannot recover the gear you had with you), your dinos falling through the world (thus losing them), dinos spawning inside your buildings (your character will die) etc etc...
The moment you start exploring breeding, caving, bosses etc... be prepared that this content does not come without major bugs that makes it unplayable. This wasn't always the case. Breeding and boss fights had few minor bugs and glitches but the mechanics more or less worked. They do not anymore.
You will lose babies because they simply will stop eating, they will despawn etc etc The caves have wild dinos spawning within the walls that will jump you, dinos will fall from the ceiling. In the underwater caves your Mosasaur will be grabbed by a squid and pushed beneath the texture where it will starve as it won't be able to get out. Loot crates will spawn within the textures but be aware: not only in the core game. Even on SE, the dlc Wildcard was not able to code loot crates that do properly spawn. So you might explore a cave, waste tons of materials to find out that there is no loot. And this in a dlc - not only in the core game.
My advice: if you do plan to play more then 100h in this game, do not buy it at this point, way too many bugs that will probably be fixed in a year or two.

So I bought this game to play with a friend.
It's kind of a Turok-meets-Minecraft style MMO with Turok 64 style graphics and official servers from the same time period. The game can't seem to go for more than 30 minutes or so without lagging so badly that you get two solid minutes of work done for every five minutes of standing there wishing the game would register your actions. Literally, ANY of your actions.
There's no real introduction to the mechanics or "Oh, good, you're awake!" icebreaker to get you started down the path of dino tamer extraordinaire. Sure, I've seen the counter argument of "how hard is it to figure out to run up and punch a tree for wood?" To which I tend to counter with: "When was the last time I punched a tree to get wood in real life?"
This is basically a death-simulator until you spend any real amount of time or find friends to give you things and then, circling back to the official turd-shaped monstrosities they're calling servers, even at higher levels you can still get wiped out when you're out trying to farm for materials because the server knows you're there. And it wants to kill you. Always.
There's massive memory leaks that make the game stutter and freeze after you play for more than an hour or so(actually, that seems to have been touched up because the last few days have been fairly alright on that front). The graphics and hitboxes are terrible enough that sometimes I would log in and dinosaurs would be randomly frolicking outside our enclosed compound. I also can't even remember how many times I logged in with no gear because I had fallen through the floor while I was logged out. How does that happen, you ask? Let me tell you: When you log out, you just fall asleep and you're always online, even after you log out. ALWAYS. That means you can fall through the floor into open space, just waiting for dinos to turn you into a snack or for someone to find you who then can do whatever they want to your sleeping body. Including putting handcuffs on you that can only be removed by that person so that you can do nothing but wave your hands around.
The only consistent redeeming quality I found was the companionship of my real life friends while we played together because it's much better with a community but unfortunately, this game and its seemingly dial-up based servers screwed me, like it was a♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥on the coma floor of a hospital, one too many times. I'd much rather go play a game made by developers who do more than take your money while they laugh and crank out new content instead of fixing the inumerable standing issues.

This is basically a death-simulator until you spend any real amount of time or find friends to give you things and then, circling back to the official turd-shaped monstrosities they're calling servers, even at higher levels you can still get wiped out when you're out trying to farm for materials because the server knows you're there. I also can't even remember how many times I logged in with no gear because I had fallen through the floor while I was logged out. How does that happen, you ask? Let me tell you: When you log out, you just fall asleep and you're always online, even after you log out. ALWAYS. That means you can fall through the floor into open space, just waiting for dinos to turn you into a snack or for someone to find you who then can do whatever they want to your sleeping body. Including putting handcuffs on you that can only be removed by that person so that you can do nothing but wave your hands around.
The only consistent redeeming quality I found was the companionship of my real life friends while we played together because it's much better with a community but unfortunately, this game and its seemingly dial-up based servers screwed me, like it was a♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥on the coma floor of a hospital, one too many times. I'd much rather go play a game made by developers who do more than take your money while they laugh and crank out new content instead of fixing the inumerable standing issues.
