Ark, oh where do I start. Probably best to start with the pros and cons.
Pros:
1.Huge Variety of animals. Seriously, there are 137 of them in-game right now, with more on the way!
2.Lots of different ways to play. Thanks to the steam workshop, you can spend a life time in this game and never have the same experience twice.
3.Large, frequent updates. While the content in the updates can be unapperciated, the game does still recieve a major game update about once a month. Not many games that I know of can claim that.
Cons:
1.Community. The community is not always behind the steps taken in the devlopment process. Major outbursts of disgust include the release of a well made, paid DLC in early access, and the recent crippling of the flying creatures.
2.Optimization. While the game is in alpha, (despite what some reviews might say), optimization is lacking. However, it was worse, alot worse.
3.Size. The game is huge, almost taking up a whopping 80 gigs of space. Hopefully this will be helped in the upcoming optimization update. (Edit: The game now takes up 100 gigabytes of space with all DLC installed.)
4.Lack of scientific accuracy. No creature in the game is scientificaly accurate, most being far over or undersized. This is a minor con, and does not significantly affect my opinon of the game.
Overall Opinon: ARK is still evolving. At the time of writing, a final release seems only a few months away. My advice to potential early access buyers is to get the game and dlc bundle when on sale. As for starting off, play single player for a while.Use single player to get accoustomed to the game and the mechanics, then start looking into finding a server, preferably one that you think you would have fun on. Un-officals can have great communitys, while officals are reliable, with some even offering offline raid protection. Single player is where the majority of my hours in-game were spent, only recently did I move to a low population un-offical server.
I recommend this game for any one who loves dinosaurs, and is willing to tolerate a little bit of fantasy. I hope this was helpful to any future buyer.

If you are new to Ark you may be wondering what's up with the recent mixed reviews? I mean, isn't this game super-popular and one of the most played currently on Steam?
You would be right to wonder. Ark is an Early Access game currently so a lot of the main content is still being developed or tweaked, and much more is yet to be polished and perfected as is to be expected. Many players recently have become frustrated (to put it lightly) by recent nerfs to flying mounts. It was game breaking/traumatizing for a lot of people who've sunk time into this game breeding/capturing good flyers. Now, the good news is, if you're a new player you won't be able to tell the difference having never experienced flight prior to the change. For most players, the nerf was just something we had to adapt to. The flyer nerf has brought some balance to the game that wasn't their previously, and overall the game's balancing is still being tweaked over time.

There is a lot that can be said about Ark. One of the main reasons for my own, personal thousand-plus-hours I've put into this game is that Ark can still do what most online games no longer do: bring people together. You've got to rely on others to get anywhere in this game with any relative ease so people do play together. A lot. The community isn't perfect since it's online, but it's a great game to enjoy with friends and make new friends whilst playing. You'll find a lot of people willing to cooperate and mingle, and that is a great thing IMO.
Of course, this game is still quite grindy and still quite glitchy, but if you can look past some glitches and imperfections you'll find an addictive survival game with a nice resource gathering system, and plenty of dinos to tame, breed, and battle.
If you do not like grinding to achieve victory in a game, Ark is not for you. If you do not like changes being made to a game, Ark is not for you. You will die. Repeatedly.  However! If you enjoy meeting other players, and you enjoy a challenge and can grit your teeth and bear through a rough start this game does have a lot to offer and will keep you coming back to collect more dinos and more resources with your friends.
That being said, Ark is a timesink. It's not for everyone. If you want to play online you do need to have access to log on occasionally or all you have worked for will slowly deteriorate or be destroyed. If you don't have the time to dedicate to the online world try single player or look into private servers.

To start off with: I have over 1300 hours in-game and 600 hours in-mission. By the way this is not a P2W game by any means, spending money on it is totally optional and up to you, you can get basically everything in the game by just playing it.
I have a lot of experience with this game, and I love it, however I do want to say that it is not a game for everyone.
There's a lot of grinding and levelling up to do, but you can get friends or clanmates to help you with that. Theres over 330 different characters/weapons/companions at the time of writing this and there's plenty of stuff to do for 2+ years worth of normal playing. I've played this game since the very first few weeks and a few months ago got back to it.
The developers always update the game with new quests, weapons, warframes and more cool stuff, it's a easy game for just casual play but you can take it a few steps further by going to endless missions which can have enemies far stronger than anything you will usually find. There's sorties: a set of special missions that appear everyday with special rewards, some of which only obtainable through this missions. There's a mod system for weapons which is very easy to understand and use. Finding people is automatic however you can find a specific set of players through recruit chat. There's trading, daily events, invasions which are a type of special mission where you help a faction defeat the other, alert missions that reward you with credits, the normal currency of the game, and sometimes alternative helmets for the different characters, there's a Archwing mode where players use Archwings, a type of technology used to fight in space.
So now that I gave you some info on the game, I'll tell you how much I like it: And thats's a hell of a lot. I spent 90% of the time I play games playing this one and have done so much and still have more to do, and even though this is a free game where it's completely up to you to spend money... I have spent over 100£ or ~125€ on this game and it was all worth it, while you can choose to trade things with other players toget the currency which i spent money on, I don't have the patience for it but some websites such as warframe.market will definitely help with that.
Overall here are my scores:
Gameplay 9.5/10 , sometimes it's a bit hard to understand where you are because the spaces are too small and this is a 3rd person shooter.
Graphics 10/10 ,  for a free game, even for a 60€/60$ game, this is incredible and they look amazing.
Lore/Storyline 10/10 , it's super interesting and fun, there's many quests to teach you about this, a codex which lets you read about the different characters stories and a lot of interesting dialogue.
This game is amazing and I absolutely recommend you try it out for a few hours, while the first few 2-3 hours are very boring, after that it's just fun after fun after fun and a bit of lore in every hour you play.

If you are new to Ark you may be wondering what's up with the recent mixed reviews? I mean, isn't this game super-popular and one of the most played currently on Steam?
You would be right to wonder. Ark is an Early Access game currently so a lot of the main content is still being developed or tweaked, and much more is yet to be polished and perfected as is to be expected. Many players recently have become frustrated (to put it lightly) by recent nerfs to flying mounts. It was game breaking/traumatizing for a lot of people who've sunk time into this game breeding/capturing good flyers. Now, the good news is, if you're a new player you won't be able to tell the difference having never experienced flight prior to the change. For most players, the nerf was just something we had to adapt to. The flyer nerf has brought some balance to the game that wasn't their previously, and overall the game's balancing is still being tweaked over time.

There is a lot that can be said about Ark. One of the main reasons for my own, personal thousand-plus-hours I've put into this game is that Ark can still do what most online games no longer do: bring people together. You've got to rely on others to get anywhere in this game with any relative ease so people do play together. A lot. The community isn't perfect since it's online, but it's a great game to enjoy with friends and make new friends whilst playing. You'll find a lot of people willing to cooperate and mingle, and that is a great thing IMO.
Of course, this game is still quite grindy and still quite glitchy, but if you can look past some glitches and imperfections you'll find an addictive survival game with a nice resource gathering system, and plenty of dinos to tame, breed, and battle.
If you do not like grinding to achieve victory in a game, Ark is not for you. If you do not like changes being made to a game, Ark is not for you. You will die. Repeatedly.  However! If you enjoy meeting other players, and you enjoy a challenge and can grit your teeth and bear through a rough start this game does have a lot to offer and will keep you coming back to collect more dinos and more resources with your friends.
That being said, Ark is a timesink. It's not for everyone. If you want to play online you do need to have access to log on occasionally or all you have worked for will slowly deteriorate or be destroyed. If you don't have the time to dedicate to the online world try single player or look into private servers.

On my third night in Ark, when the sun had finally set and I was left alone in the seething blackness of the jungle, I saw a glimpse of my possible future. I was chopping trees in the dark, too scared to even light a fire for fear of what the warmth might draw toward me, but as another tree toppled with a groan I spied lights in the valley below. I crept closer. Silhouetted in flickering torchlight towered a tyrannosaurus rex, around which a group of hunters darted back and forth, attacking with spears and arrows. Eventually, they hunters prevailed, and, as they set upon the fallen dinosaur with tools to harvest its meat and hides, I faded back into the jungle and began chopping with renewed purpose.
Ark: Survival Evolved is an early access survival game full of these moments – the kind that fill you with trepidation and excitement in equal measure. But for every moment that adds to the enchantment of surviving on an island teeming with prehistoric life, there are just as many capable of frustrating you. Building on a firm foundation well tread by online survival games, Ark certainly has potential, much of it unrealized, but I can’t help but wonder if the claim of Survival Evolved is just too hyperbolic of a statement to make.
When I spawned on a beach, squinting up at the tropical sun, I felt almost disappointed with how by-the-books Ark initially seemed. If you’ve played Rust or DayZ, you’ll be intimately familiar with the song and dance that Ark would have you perform. Naked, without so much as two sticks to rub together, I was thrust onto a hostile island. Unlike many of the barren wastelands that form the survival genre though, Ark’s setting was infused with a sense of alien mystery that quickly washed away how unimpressed I felt.
Even though I felt strongly familiar with what was expected of me, like maintaining my levels of hunger, dehydration, and temperature, Ark quickly surprised me. As I completed my crucial “press every key to see what it does” routine, I couldn’t decide if I was more alarmed or amused when a line of text informed me that I had defecated. When I turned around to see the little dollop laying on the beach, I was even more surprised that I could pick it up. But by the time I swallowed it whole and was promptly overcome by a sudden, crippling illness, I only felt bemused; of course I can eat my own poo.
While there are many aspects to Ark that are worthy, like the freedom to consume your own waste, few of them elicit the wonder inspired by the dinosaurs roaming the vast expanse of the island. These beasts are everywhere, and my first hours in the game were spent largely learning where I fit in this strange environment. While other players always posed an ever-present threat, it was within the jaws of a dinosaur that I often met my demise.
Over 40 species exist on the island, and the number seems to grow with each passing week. Ranging from hapless dodos (a willing supplier of meat at an early stage) to the threatening predators that hunt and savagely kill anyone without a keen sense of their surroundings. I truly felt like a small cog in a much larger machine.
Originally, the dinosaurs instilled a sense of awe as I watched them lumber around, but it wasn’t long until the spell was broken by the half-baked behaviors that guided them. I know dinosaurs were dumb, but this is something else. In just a short time, any threat they posed was quickly disarmed by the one dimensional artificial intelligence. I came to view them not as deadly creatures to be treated with care but rather as resources in the environment to be controlled and exploited; an image reinforced by the bizarre and clumsy way in which they moved and engaged with one another.
Of all the interactions you can have with dinosaurs, taming is easily the most important. With careful use of sedatives (or the less surgical application of blunt force trauma) every creature can be rendered unconscious and eventually tamed. Doing so requires an overly steep investment of time and some understanding of what the creature prefers to eat. By keeping the beast sedated and fed, a meter gradually fills until the monster awakens ready to dutifully serve. Some monsters can be tamed within 15 minutes, but others require upwards of a handful of hours. Most of the large creatures can also be fitted with a saddle and used as transportation, a prospect that had me drooling with anticipation as I mothered my first unconscious turtle who, after successful taming, I promptly named Ori and to whom I became too emotionally attached.
Like many survival games, Ark prides itself on teaching through repetition and trial and error. In the savage wilds of the island, my demise often greeted me suddenly. But each time I respawned naked on a beach, the process to recovering from my death became more and more precise.
Where Ark begins to veer into uncharted territory is with the implementation of stat-based character progression. Earning experience by crafting, killing, and even walking eventually netted me a level, which allowed me to increase a stat like health or stamina, and afforded me a few points to spend unlocking crafting recipes. Called engrams, these recipes can be used alongside the required resources to create everything from armor, weapons, and structures that I could place in the environment. But while this interesting blend of RPG inspiration created a sense of progression even in the face of death, it did little to dampen the severe sting.
The prospect of tangible loss is a valuable component to creating meaningful encounters with other players. While some servers cater to the non-aggressive crowd, player versus player combat was the catalyst for so many of the rich moments I’d experienced. Not every encounter had to end in blood, but one of the biggest issues I discovered was how severely the scales were tipped in favor of the aggressor.
Crafting and building is a core component of Ark, but feasibly creating the highest tier of recipes requires a monumental group effort. Even furnishing my humble wood cabin took me the better part of an hour when I accounted for the trips to the beach to replenish my stocks of water and meat. But creating a proper fortress requires a staggering number of resources that can only feasibly be gathered by a group.
Ark features a built-in tribe system, which grants access to a rudimentary suite of tools for managing allies and sharing various benefits like spawn points and control of tamed dinosaurs. Playing as a team is a crucial aspect of Ark – not just to survive but to experience the deeper aspects of base building and crafting. But the way I felt strong-armed into cooperating with others – by disproportionately increasing the requirements for gathering higher quality materials – felt constrictive and demoralizing rather than inviting. It also paved the way for one of my greatest issues: the effort to build something up far surpasses what is required for someone else to tear it down.
When I woke up one morning, eager to log in and feed Ori, I was confused to find that I wasn’t within the cozy confines of my secret base but rather naked on a beach. After hurriedly checking the forums to see if there had been a server wipe, I discovered the true cause for my death. When you log off in Ark, your character doesn’t magically vanish without a trace. Like Rust, your unconscious body is left behind, totally vulnerable to anyone with an appetite for the catatonic.
In theory I like this concept because it loans a sense of permanence and responsibility to the world I inhabit. I’m no longer free to quit the game whenever it might please me, so I have to alter my behaviour. The problem stems from the fact that, for a fraction of the effort, anyone can break into my fort and, without much consequence or effort, destroy everything I worked so hard to achieve. An exceptional game! Yes it's brutal when starting and yes the AI leaves a lot to be desired, but the overall feeling of depth is intensely addictive.
Gameplay experiences can vary hugely, depending on how you decide to play. Singleplayer is enjoyable, but lonely. Official servers offer multiplay diversity, but that also introduces the increasingly common element of personality clashing and toxicity, should you find the wrong crowd. It also means you can't tweak the game difficulty to your playstyle, as administration is done on your behalf. If you like big crowds and working in a large team, it seems to offer some interesting PvP and guild level gameplay.
The sweet spot for me and my wife has been to rent our own dedicated server from Nitrado (the people that host the official servers) and tailor the game settings to our requirements, which include cross travelling to different maps (such as Scorched Earth). It costs about the same as a subscription to an MMO and gives plenty of options for friends and family to tinker with.
Dinosaurs are beautifully imagined, with incredible animations, textures and overall design. Some real love has gone into this! There's nothing else quite like this out there...
The engram (level based recipe unlock) system is fairly well designed, with a huge amount of stuff to craft and build.
Large sandbox maps to explore that have been lovingly designed, with plenty of biome diversity.
A massive library of dinosaurs and other creatures that keep the world alive. Different biomes bring different creatures, many (if not most) of which can be tamed as pets, for use as armies and mounts (or both).
Private multiplayer server (and single player) settings are numerous and with some careful thought can rebalance the game for a smaller playerbase, as long as administrators don't make things too easy.
The Unreal Engine is absolutely beautiful, although it has some optimization issues that will likely be ironed out by release. Sound is atmospheric to say the least and the music suits the game extremely well.
Simply hours of playability...
Poor dinosaur pathfinding and an environment that seems to lock creatures in place from time to time (most often mid-sized beasts glued to trees and rocks) can make for some frustrating moments. Careful planning is required when traversing large distances with your beast armies.
The graphics engine is beautiful but comes with its own pitfalls. Simply put you; can't expect this game to run on an older system without having problems with framerate or bottlenecking. I use a 4Gb GTX980 and can max most things out as long as I don't run my native 2K resolution. 1080p seems to be what the developers have optimized the game to, for now.
It's early access, so expect plenty of patches, server restarts and gameplay balance tweeking from the developers. It's something that can cause quite a stir of negativity from the current audience and has left the Steam scoring system in disarray, giving the impression the game is far worse than it actually is.
Don't let anyone convince you this game is good or bad; try it for yourself. It's definitely worth the asking price and offers plenty of choice to the player when it comes to how you want to play.

Ark: Survival Evolved is such an interesting game in a lot of ways from my perspective. First off, I play PvE so the review is from that perspective.
Before I get started, This thing's verbose,  Sorry.
In tons of ways I very much like it. The problem is, in those same ways it doesn't particularly do anything I find exceptional, or warrant of purchase, especially for the game it is. What it is, is a survival game. A building simulator with mechanics that will kill you if you don't address them. And while that seems good, in vanilla form, there's not much here to really praise.
So let's hop in and focus on what the game is:
Survival.
Survival focuses on a decent amount of stats. Most of which aren't useful, or are situationally useful,and don't massively boost you character's survivability.
Le Pointless: Crafting Speed, Food and Water, no real benefit to boosting these stats. Water less so than food, as becomign thirsty at inopportune times will kill you or interrupt you. But You can carry food, and you can carry water. Crafting speed is the only stat is geniunely do not understand why it exists. Yes you could build stuff faster, but aside from the practical thing being that you can level quicker doing so, it doesn't help. Maybe you could repair faster in a pinch? Don't see the point.
Health, oxygen, melee damage, Movement speed, and fortitude really share the same segment, they're all pretty much pointless to invest heavily in But you may need some. Health is made pointless due to torpor based enemies, Oxygen is pointless once you're high enough level for Scuba Gear, Melee Damage is pointless because dinisaurs will always be better at attacking or harvesting, and Fortitude is amazing at not making a lick of difference, Movement speed falls off usefulness quickly.
Weight, and stamina- needed, and probably worth a couple of points. In fact, high stamina and high weight will probably keep you alive better, since being able to carry more means you can do more which means you level up quicker earlier, and being able to sprint even with very minor investment in speed for an eon will keep you alive. No matter what way you slice it, if you want to live you need solid investment in these stats.
But there are hidden stats. Torpor being the most important. You can't directly buff it. But Fortitude does increase resistance to torpor as does heavy armor. This stat is precisely the reason Health is useless. Gathering 50 torpor makes you fall unconscious, which leaves you prone and open to any sort of attack. Any animal that inflicts torpor will keep you unconscious until you die. With tons of health, this will take forever, and you're more or less powerless to stop it.
So what else is there to survival? Well, there's cold, which if you begin freezing will slowly kill you. Overheating which will drain your water like a seive so you die of thirst.
To survive, you do stuff you gain levels, and you learn recipes (engrams) to make stuff so you can do stufto gain levelsf to get more engrams so you can make more stuff to do more stuff to gain more levels to make more stuff so you can do more stuff.
There's no direct point, even with the mega bosses, they respawn and have drops. So end game you farm the boss to get stuff to farm the boss more efficiently so you can get more stuff instead of levelling up more.
Ganeplay
The physics in this game hate you especially if you're fast, the building mechanics hate you because nothing snaps properly or as expected, and even if it somehow does the number of time's the game has downright lied to me on a placement ghost mapping which doesn't turn out anything like depicted is inexcusable. Not only that but larger objects are difficult to view for placement, and the foundation system is just frustrating beyond compare.
I'd say it plays like minecraft in premise, but minecraft controls better, has amuch more intuitive building system, and a far less limiting set of mechanics in place to prevent players from actually building anything.
Materials in vanilla are rare, in fact to enjoy the game even somewhat I'd say times them by four in drop rate. To build a metal foundation, you need:
50 metal ingots (100 metal + cook time + fuel source)
15 cementing paste ((60 Keratin/Chitin + 120 Stone) That's about, maybe 2 -3 large stones, and like 4 or 5 trilobytes
So you need a good 30 mins a piece about for 1 foundation made of metal. If you're using less than optimal methods. Which you will be doing because you need to use unoptimized methods to unlock or get access to optimized ones, or at least not run a risk of dying horribly trying.
Aside from gathering, eating, and avoiding certain doom around every corner, there's death.
Death involves you dying and then engaging in immense frustration. if you have a bed you may respawn there as long as you haven't used that bed in the last 5 minutes. Otherwise you respawn randomly in a zone of your choice. Then you have 15 minutes to find your corpse, on an enormous island where you liekly weren't paying attention to your exact coordinates when you were mutilated by a pack of Allosaurs running and screaming like the Dodo you truly are. So you'll wander aimlessly looking for all of your stuff. Finding all of your stuff in the underbrush with no player cues while a pack of allosaurs tries to get a second lunch because your stuff stays on your corpse is only slightly difficult. Wait it gets better, you will have to find a BROWN bag. Not neon, not yellow, not biege or thatch colored. BROWN. BUT WAIT THERE'S MORE. You can be eaten or not, which means your items might be a corpse or a bag. BUT HERE'S THE SHOWSTOPPER LADIES AND GENTLEMEN. Nightime is a thing, and you can't see crap, even with a torch. So, there's no identifier for your body if you're close, if you don't routinely look at the map, you won't know whereabouts you died, If you somehow do know, it's a royal pain to find yourself, And if you died at night, well let's just say I hope you have ice cream handy, because you need something to cheer you up for this crap dang-it.
Then there's just the GRIND. Ark Grinding Evolved makes you grind at everything to advance, make petty items or narcotics, literally farm and harvest dook to make items to allow you to get access to stuff so you really don't have to do that anymore, but still have to because stuff gets killed all of the time.
Did I mention all fo your mounts and companions are dead dead once killed? Oh yeah, permadeaths kind of a thing.
And finally, dino's themselves as well as you can level, you can tame them, the higher level the tame, the stronger the dino is, then you can level it and up its stats more. BUT the tiem it takes to tame a lv 1 dino vs a 150 variant is vastly different. And grindy, ever wanted to sit next to a dinosaur that could be eaten at any time because it's unconscious requiring your presence for hours at a time while it makes god awful noises at you? If so, Ark's your freakin' game.
Aside from the dinosaurs which are always being added, nerfed and added, and rebalanced, and did I mentioned nerfed? There's very little reason I'd say Ark manages to Survival better than other Survival games. It doesn't do much different than add dinos to the mix. And honestly, it's cool. It's just really too bad the game is like JuicyFruit Gum. You chew it for a tiny bit, and go back when you want more sweet, but it never lasts very long, and if you chew too long it starts being bad.
I've never had a session when I left Ark feeling good or accomplished, there's always more to do, more busywork to plan, or things to rebuild because you died and ragequit or some random thing aggroed your base and dismantled it halfway because you can't build crap out of metal yet.
Maybe the view from the top's great, but after 160 hours, I'm done trying to like it. Cheap deaths due to poor balance, and grind has burned me out, I just don't think it's fun.

15 cementing paste ((60 Keratin/Chitin + 120 Stone) That's about, maybe 2 -3 large stones, and like 4 or 5 trilobytes
So you need a good 30 mins a piece about for 1 foundation made of metal. If you're using less than optimal methods. Which you will be doing because you need to use unoptimized methods to unlock or get access to optimized ones, or at least not run a risk of dying horribly trying.
Aside from gathering, eating, and avoiding certain doom around every corner, there's death.
Death involves you dying and then engaging in immense frustration. if you have a bed you may respawn there as long as you haven't used that bed in the last 5 minutes. Otherwise you respawn randomly in a zone of your choice. Then you have 15 minutes to find your corpse, on an enormous island where you liekly weren't paying attention to your exact coordinates when you were mutilated by a pack of Allosaurs running and screaming like the Dodo you truly are. So you'll wander aimlessly looking for all of your stuff. Finding all of your stuff in the underbrush with no player cues while a pack of allosaurs tries to get a second lunch because your stuff stays on your corpse is only slightly difficult. Wait it gets better, you will have to find a BROWN bag. Not neon, not yellow, not biege or thatch colored. BROWN. BUT WAIT THERE'S MORE. You can be eaten or not, which means your items might be a corpse or a bag. BUT HERE'S THE SHOWSTOPPER LADIES AND GENTLEMEN. Nightime is a thing, and you can't see crap, even with a torch. So, there's no identifier for your body if you're close, if you don't routinely look at the map, you won't know whereabouts you died, If you somehow do know, it's a royal pain to find yourself, And if you died at night, well let's just say I hope you have ice cream handy, because you need something to cheer you up for this crap dang-it.
Then there's just the GRIND. Ark Grinding Evolved makes you grind at everything to advance, make petty items or narcotics, literally farm and harvest dook to make items to allow you to get access to stuff so you really don't have to do that anymore, but still have to because stuff gets killed all of the time.
Did I mention all fo your mounts and companions are dead dead once killed? Oh yeah, permadeaths kind of a thing.
And finally, dino's themselves as well as you can level, you can tame them, the higher level the tame, the stronger the dino is, then you can level it and up its stats more. BUT the tiem it takes to tame a lv 1 dino vs a 150 variant is vastly different. And grindy, ever wanted to sit next to a dinosaur that could be eaten at any time because it's unconscious requiring your presence for hours at a time while it makes god awful noises at you? If so, Ark's your freakin' game.
Aside from the dinosaurs which are always being added, nerfed and added, and rebalanced, and did I mentioned nerfed? There's very little reason I'd say Ark manages to Survival better than other Survival games. It doesn't do much different than add dinos to the mix. And honestly, it's cool. It's just really too bad the game is like JuicyFruit Gum. You chew it for a tiny bit, and go back when you want more sweet, but it never lasts very long, and if you chew too long it starts being bad.
I've never had a session when I left Ark feeling good or accomplished, there's always more to do, more busywork to plan, or things to rebuild because you died and ragequit or some random thing aggroed your base and dismantled it halfway because you can't build crap out of metal yet.
Maybe the view from the top's great, but after 160 hours, I'm done trying to like it. Cheap deaths due to poor balance, and grind has burned me out, I just don't think it's fun.

Hello Everyone. I have never written a review on Steam, but I decided to share my experience with playing this trainwreck of a game.
I bought the game after seeing videos on Youtube, and I convinced a friend to get it too so we could play together. We ended up playing online and settling on a server. We expected to level up, build all kinds of cool stuff, tame dinosaurs, and so on. Boy were we in for a suprise. We died about 10+ times per hour as a result getting drugged, robbed, and killed by ridiculously higher level players. Then, I would spawn hundreds of miles aways in a swamp right next to a 25ft long level 100 snake and, ultimatley, get killed again. The animals that we encountered in the game are relentless. They will see you a mile away and chase you until you are forced to fight them face to face. But being only armed with sticks and stones, we are no match for any kind of predator that we encounter. Even if you are fortunate enought to make it to a shelter, the animals are not only able to glitch through the walls, but they can eventually destroy your shelter and kill you. In some cases, they will keep destroying everything even after you die or escape your shelter, and will smash your hopes into the ground.
After a grueling month and a half of leveling up from killing dodo birds and crafting fiber clothing, we were finally able to set up a tiny little stone shack. We actually had a thatch shack at first, but thatch shacks are pointless because they can be destroyed so easliy. Our hopes got high and we were excited to keep progressing on in the game, but then a plague was introduced into our lives. That plague was a level 75 griefer who would constantly kill us for no reason and take all of our things. Not to mention he was about 4 feet tall and his speed stats were maxed out, so it was impossible to hit him. And to top it off, he could still take both of us down in a single blow with a wooden club. After confronting him, he stated that he didn't need any of the stolen items, he was just doing it to be a♥♥♥♥♥♥
So, we were forced to move our whole operation onto a completley isolated island, where we established a large base with multi-layerd walls and many guard towers. Keep in mind that it is near impossible to level up when you are constantly being killed by every living thing in sight, so were were still about level 20's and basically have no way of defending ourselves. The only practical things you can make being below a level 40 are houses, furniture, and basic weapons such as spears and bows. So we had to constantly grind in order to gather materials and level up. Probably 60-70% of my logged time was spent chopping down trees, gathering fiber, and mining rocks, due to the fact that it took a ridiculously amount of materials to build anything and everything we built would get stolen or destroyed. Fun right?
Once we were able to craft items like guns, metal tools, and armor, we thought we were well-enough equipped to defend ourselves, and we started collecting valuable materials such as metal and oil. We were progressing quite well at first; we had just gotten a fabricator and we were preparing to install electricity into our base. After we accepted the harsh reality of griefers like the level 75 super midget, a new threat arose: the Chinese. No matter what console you play on, and no matter what game you play, the Chinese will always be there to completley ruin the experience for not only you, but for everyone that has the misfortune of playing with them. Sadly, we were those people. We had gangs of Chinese players constantly bombing our base, stealing our valuable items, and destroying our crafting devices. So, we would have to continue to grind and grind just to get back to where we were started, and then we'd just get ♥♥♥♥ed again.
You may think that the Chinese wouldn't be a big deal, right? Just gather a few players together and tell them off, maybe kill them a few times to send them a message? Wrong. The entire server ganged up on the Chinese in hopes of running them off, but they were ALL absolutley destroyed by these cheating, glitching, no-life China-men. There was no point in even trying anymore, as we would constantly be raided and set back to square one. And don't even bother trying to tell them off, because they don't speak a lick of english. And if you thought that was bad enough, our super midged plauge came back and constantly harassed us when we tried to do anything. So when we were online, we were being beaten, drugged, fed to dinosaurs, and killed, and when we were offline our base would be destroyed and all of our things would be gone. One day we logged on and our entire base was gone, our boats were destroyed, some random people had taken over our island, and we literally had nothing. I have not opened that game since, and I do not plan to ever play this game again.
Trust me, this game seems good in the pictures, but this game is such a nightmare and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone. I didn't even mention how poorly optimized this game is, which resulted in a constand lag that never goes away. I have noticed that this game puts out a ton of updates, yet absolutley nothing changes. The only update that has changed anything was the DLC, which was just a new map and a few new dinosaurs that made the game even more like hell. The developers don't worry about fixing things like building glitches, player enhancement exploits, their riduculous ranking system, or their truly garbage AI, and they'd rather just keep piling trash into this dumpster that they call Ark Survival.
I would recommend a game called Conan Exiles for anyone who wants a game with the same premise as Ark, but with a much better executed plan. This game has only been out for four months and, in my opinion, is already much better than Ark.
However, if you like spending all of your time grinding for materials, getting killed by everything in sight, being constantly harrassed by higher level players and/or cheaters, and not being able to progress at all, then Ark Survival is the game for you.

To be completely honest, this is a great game if you play on unofficial servers ONLY. However I can't recommend this to anyone given the state this game is in. I've put in close to 1,000 hours into this game and I can tell you that it can be incredibly addicting to play if you choose the right server and play with friends.
The negatives I experienced:
The PvP feels VERY Broken and can be easily one sided
Takes incredibly long periods of time (weeks) to progress and can easily be destroyed and wiped in what feels like minutes
The bigger tribes basically own more the the servers than Wildcard does it feels like. (Which is why I tell people stay away from official servers)
Being able to transfer your stuff from server to server was the last nail in the coffin for me. This allows people to migrate and wipe other servers
Official PvE servers are impossible to build anywhere useful due to people building a few structures and never returning.
Taming/Breeding is a very slow and tedious process that can cause people to sit in a single spot for over half a day to tame bigger dinos and demand several days of tedious micro-management to make sure babies don't starve.
Can be stuck in an endless cycle of this mindset that says "we need to keep building up our defenses!" and it all is basically useless.
Dinos are very imbalanced. Some Feel useless while others are too game breaking
Dino AI needs HUGE improvements
Flying dinos were nerfed incredibly hard. Just not worth the trouble to tame them most of the time now.
What I liked about this game:
Almost everything I said negative above is (or can be) accommodated by playing on unofficial servers; where a lot of time is put into the game is greatly reduced by multipliers that most of the community likes and allowing mods makes the game feel like a much more unique and enjoyable experience
This is super fun and enjoyable playing with a group of friends and making your own tribe. But honestly most games become way more fun by adding friends to it.
Can provide crazy amounts of play time when the right server is chozen and will feel very rewarding
Mods are a real highlight of this game as they can change how the core of the objective can work, adding even more hours of gameplay
If you still really want to buy this game Id strongly recommend to only play on unofficial servers and with friends. Otherwise you might find yourself hating this game and feeling like you wasted your money. Everyone is already so built up on official servers that it feels pointless to even try going there. Plus all the negatives I listed earlier about them.

Honestly I think this game is getting a lot of flack for no reason. They just released a  huge update with a lot of new endgame content to do. Also FINALLY SOMETHING TO USE TEK EQUIPMENT FOR! Final review:
Welcome to Warframe where variety of weapons and frames to use will surely take a lot of time of your life. What can I say? If you don't like to grind to earn stuff for yourself - don't play it.
Now that we're finished with the intro we can talk about the game itself seriously. WF is a completely free to play game, due to premium currency being main currency in the game. And that's probably the biggest pro - you can litetally get everything without spending a penny(except for steam exclusive items).
There are quite a few game modes, including my favourite defence and survival, which get progressively harder and about 200 nodes to unlock on the starchart. The thing about this game I really like is the story and epic cutscenes. DE surely did a great job presenting the lore in their game.
Game sure is famous for it's unique "parkour-like" move mechanics. It definitely makes the combat feel faster and overall more interesting, unless you just like to run with grenade launcher and blow everything up.
Graphics are an eye candy, and most of the screenshots can be easily used as a wallpaper. The thing that is annoying as hell though are all the skill effects in a 4 player party. You can get seizures sometimes, but thankfuly they do not interfere or prevent you from playing the game as effectively as you would without them.
Soundtrack is not the strongest side of the game, but sound effects definitely are. Also addition to ingame voice chat is a big plus, regardless of wether you want to use it for communication or playing Charlie the Unicorn for other people(you have been warned).
Overall this game is a strong 7 or 8 out of 10. If I could include Tonkor in the score it would probably  be like 15. The reason why this game loses few points is developers. They sure give us a lot of hotfixes, but sometimes serious bugs are fixed week or two weeks after being discovered, and usually upon fixing one thing they break two.

A friend of mine introduced me to this game 2 years ago when it first released on Xbox One. I decided to get this on PC because it honestly did'nt feel like a game fit for a console - but I'm not complaining. When I started Warframe I felt it was boring and did'nt make much sense. I thought it's fiction was unclear & meaningless, I was always getting lost in the interface. But once I got a feel for the controls, it all snapped into place and became a VERY fun experiance that I have yet to find in any other game.
This game could be VERY compared to Destiny (you know, that game from ps4 and xbox one?) because it is mainly a shooter that relies on player progression and endlessly unique fighting styles in combat, and the only thing that really makes it an "MMO" is that there can be many players at once.
With 3rd person shooting paired with crazy super-power-like abilities, along with a VERY well made parkour system, plus weapons & armor that make you feel SO AWESOME, it's kinda hard to ever get tired of this game's action once your familiar with it. Co-op on this game is very fun. While playing single player you have no allies except for your own abilities, making you feel like a one man army of awesomeness.
This game has outstanding soundtrack, but is also A BLAST to rock out to your favorite tunes with! (simply by muting the in-game music and playing your own from an extrnal device like a speaker or aux cable).
I eventually learned that the game's story, lore, and fiction is (while you still get a good enough narrative through short videos and transmissions on-screen), most of it is a lot like Destiny or Fnaf - there is SO MUCH OF A STORY that you simply can't fit it into direct cutscenes. IF you want the FULL experiance of ALL the story behind EVERYTHING, you will need to do a lot of reading and A LOT of careful in-game observation. And that's not a bad thing, because if you want the standard narrative, just watch the transmissions on your screen when they happen. Point is, it does not force everything in your face at once.
This game's progression is VERY grindy and not friendly to beginners, but with every hour of gameplay and every unlock you make, the game becomes so much more fun! As you progress you unlock new forms of gameplay (I.e, archwing missions) and new forms of combat, so even if you have put more hours into this game then the earth has existed, you'd probably still be descovering new things.
9/10! This game took a LONG time for me to get into, but now it's one of the best games that has EVER been installed on my PC.

I have over 200 hours into the game, compared to a lot of ARK players i'm still a noob so if you aren't ready to turn this into a full time job, don't even bother thinking about getting this game. I'll explain why this game is a full time job later on, but basically it punishes any player that can't or won't play it 24/7.
First I'll talk about the PvE. I started playing PvE on a private server with friends and had tons of fun discovering everything there is to enjoy. We started on The Center, the biggest and in my opinion the coolest of the three maps. The beginning is the hardest part for new players. Every dino you meet can easily kill a noob, even the spitter dinos. It can be annoying running around naked and getting killed by raptors, but stick with it and find your friends and build a safe place. Once you get the base built, the game gets so much more fun. Every new dino you find is cool, and it so fun the first time you get all your friends together and explore a cave. The most dangerous foes we encountered in PvE were the alpha predators. Our base got killed multiple times by alpha raptors, but it was fun because it showed us that even though we had a big base with spike walls and gaurd towers, there was still a threat out there that had to be beaten. Ofcourse once you build a metal base nothing can break it anymore and once you tame flying mounts you don't have to worry about dangerous expeditions so late game it got boring. We basically got to the point that nothing PvE had to throw at us outside of boss battles was a challenge, and even fighting bosses had no point because what would we use the tek gear to kill? Harder versions of that boss? That's why we decided to turn to PvP to see if that was better late game.

I never expected my review to actually be popular, but now that it is I feel like I should address all the kids telling me I suck and that I'm still a noob who doesn't know what he's talking about.

Some key points on why I gave this game a positive review.
Pros
- Free to play, 100 hours into gameplay never spent a dime, after 100 hours I have spent $25.
- Currently No subscription option available that gives players advantage over non subscribers.

- Most items on the in-game currency market can be earned via in-game.
- A lot of Cosmetic Customization.
- Enormous variety of weapons, warframes, and melee weapons.
- In-depth combat
- Graphics
- Story missions with cinematics
- plenty of planets.
- Multiplayer coop and pvp.
- Stable servers.
Cons
- Repetitive maps.
- Repetitive Enemies.
- Repetitive Mission types.
- Dumb AI.
- Becomes a difficult grind for F2P players (after 100 hours).
- Difficult interface to navigate for beginners.
- Huge learning curve.
A little more In-Depth on the F2P Model:
The game truly is one of the best free to play titles on the market. After putting in over 100 hours of gameplay I decided to finally make a purchase for in-game currency only because one of my daily login rewards was a one time 75% off coupon. (Please note these are very rare, so don't wait on it)
If you ever get this daily reward I highly recommend using it in combination with the $100 platinum purchase, you will receive over $100 worth of platinum for $25.
Again, it is unnecessary but would be extremely helpful for long term players.
In-game currency market items can all be obtained via missions and daily mission rewards as well as random loot. With a little patience you can earn everything you possibly will ever need when building your weapons and warframes without spending ANY money.
The key here is to focus only on one warframe and weapon set in the beginning, use the free 50 platinum that is given to you only on the first sets of gear you decide on.
Otherwise you are gonna have a bad time unless you purchase more platinum.
The first 50 platinum that is given to you lasted me 100 hours of gameplay!
The best warframes are not buyable through the in-game marketplace but must be earned through the game.
This is why warframe is not pay to win nor pay to play.

Warframe is a third person shooter developed by Digital Extremes and released in 2013. There are frequent changes and updates being made to the game, being that this game is Free To play, the only reasons people wouldn't download and play it for themselves is "game memory size" and/or download bandwidth limitations
.
Full disclosure, I've barely scratched the surface of the game (Yes, at the time I'm writing this review, I've only played for 20 minutes... and that's barely scratching the surface!), but I've been getting caught up in other review projects and other games, so I don't know how long it'll take until I return to Warframe to continue my progress. That detail will either qualify or disqualify my review in many people's eyes, so I want to be open and upfront with it right now.
You are Tenno. The story starts out Tenno being awakened from Cryostasis by a mysterious figure known as "Lotus", you fight back the wave of enemies and secure a ship called the Orbiter where there's a slightly unstable AI known as Ordis. Get used too these two voices because you're going to hear them A LOT! From being on my ship and Ordis constantly asking whom I plan to kill and destroy next, to Lotus always scolding me whenever I get caught or an alarm has been raised on a mission. She could pretty much say "So I guess you aren't as good at stealth as you thought you were, huh Atratzu".
There are many different "Warframes", but they're all connected to the same "Tenno". Each warframe looks slightly different, is highly customizable, Warframes have different powers, and some warframes appear male or female. Which inspired me to google "Is Tenno Male or female" and veteran players on forums seem to hate being asked that question so hopefully I've prevented some heated exchanges without butchering the explanation too much. Again: there really isn't a gender for the Tenno, just different looking Warframes.
As you go through the game there are a number of story progression and developments. You need to restore your ship, build crafting stations, active other stations. And then brace yourself for a huge time sink because after you unlock crafting you're in for the farming spree of your life
. The game can be completely Free To Play and farm and grind your way to earn whatever you want to get.
Or you can use Platinum to speed up cool downs, or purchase upgrades or other Warframes.
As far as the story is concerned, there's a great deal of information and lore in the game, you can dig up even more by checking out codex entree's on your ship on the various NPC's, warframes, and much more. I've always found that the longer you work on a story the more satisfaction you get out of it.
The controls for Warframe are quite straightforward, "easy to learn, hard to master", as people like to say about games like these. You can jump, double jump, sprint, roll, crouch, melee, shoot, change weapon, and use special abilities. There are also combo techniques for example, I frequently find myself sliding because I crouch and sprint all the time, so I often times find myself skidding on the ground off a ledge, and double jumping just in time to avoid falling off a ledge.
You have many different weapon times, I found myself wielding a bow and Bo... HA, just realized I double Bo'd. But I also used Spira (kunai / throwing knives) side arms, and my most recently crafted weapon was the Grakata (machine gun). I typically try to play stealthy throughout a mission; thus my choice of weapons. But some missions you really can't be stealthy on, and for those missions I wanted something with a higher rate of fire.
Warframe starts out very easily, so easy I completed missions without ever being detected.
However, the game gets complicated after you get closer to level 20-30 area's the game starts to pick up in difficulty and I could no longer easily sneak through the game pinning my foes against the wall with my epic green arrows. The advent of moving out of "early level / total noob status", it became quite clear I had/have absolutely no idea what's going on, and it's going to take a great deal of research, reading, and explaining from friends who have played a lot of warframe, before I'm any good at it.
Take that as you will, the best suggestion I have is to watch some tutorial videos, or read up on some guides, there's a lot that goes into this game and and the stats, gear, weapons, strategies, and tricks people use to get through the game. Sometimes the best strategy is to sneak through a level and pick people off with headshots, other-times you're better off grabbing a noisy weapon, and gunning down a specific target you're tasked to take down.
There are many ways you can gauge your progression throughout Warframe. Your warframe and weapons have levels and upgrades that you can use on them. You also have "Mastery Ranks", and probably much more that I haven't discovered yet. You can also take care of a pet, but you need to play actively to be able to get the resources to take care of your pet. Sadly I had to put my pet into stasis because I don't play enough regularly.
I feel like I've only scratched the surface in this review, and I've already written a lot about game mechanics, the story, and controls. Ultimately the thing to take away from this review is "Are you interested in this game? Has anything I mentioned in this review piqued your interest? If yes, download it and try it out for yourself, you've got almost nothing to lose."
I will add that I streamed some of the gameplay on my twitch channel and the warframe players I met over stream were quite friendly and didn't insult me for not knowing anything about the game... and that's pretty cool! Hopefully the majority of the community is like that, because that makes learning the game easier and less stressful.
If I've missed anything really important in this review, or got something terribly wrong, feel free to comment with a correction! Thank you for reading!

Final review:
Welcome to Warframe where variety of weapons and frames to use will surely take a lot of time of your life. What can I say? If you don't like to grind to earn stuff for yourself - don't play it.
Now that we're finished with the intro we can talk about the game itself seriously. WF is a completely free to play game, due to premium currency being main currency in the game. And that's probably the biggest pro - you can litetally get everything without spending a penny(except for steam exclusive items).
There are quite a few game modes, including my favourite defence and survival, which get progressively harder and about 200 nodes to unlock on the starchart. The thing about this game I really like is the story and epic cutscenes. DE surely did a great job presenting the lore in their game.
Game sure is famous for it's unique "parkour-like" move mechanics. It definitely makes the combat feel faster and overall more interesting, unless you just like to run with grenade launcher and blow everything up.
Graphics are an eye candy, and most of the screenshots can be easily used as a wallpaper. The thing that is annoying as hell though are all the skill effects in a 4 player party. You can get seizures sometimes, but thankfuly they do not interfere or prevent you from playing the game as effectively as you would without them.
Soundtrack is not the strongest side of the game, but sound effects definitely are. Also addition to ingame voice chat is a big plus, regardless of wether you want to use it for communication or playing Charlie the Unicorn for other people(you have been warned).
Overall this game is a strong 7 or 8 out of 10. If I could include Tonkor in the score it would probably  be like 15. The reason why this game loses few points is developers. They sure give us a lot of hotfixes, but sometimes serious bugs are fixed week or two weeks after being discovered, and usually upon fixing one thing they break two.

After close to 1,000 hours worth of game play I feel as though it is time I review a game. First I must say that the negative reviews about the recent nerfs are actually unfair. Yes they handed out the nerfs with very little warning, but for any private server owner/player there were options. We did not stop until we found a mod that reverted the flyers back to their original glory. They did what they did because of feedback from a large portion of the community, most of that portion being PvP. The server that I help run is a PvE server but we still have alot of fun, etc. I am not using this review for advertising though so I will not be posting a link, if interested just add me as a friend. Now to the actual review.
There are still small annoying bugs/glitches that I hope will get ironed out eventually. It has definitely come a long way since it's initial release. The recent nerf, as stated above, was due to the Ark community complaining about the things that were nerfed. To leave a bad review based off of one update alone is unfair. As far as the update and playing on an Official server, I am sure that leaves alot to be desired. I stopped playing on Official servers quite a while ago after playing on a modded unofficial server. Gameplay in my opinion is still fun, although rather "grindy" at times, as long as you have friends to play with then it's still a hell of a time.
One thing this game is not lacking in is content. There have been a pretty steady flow of updates with new content since initial release. Most all of the new content has helped the game in one way or another, even SOME of the Tek stuff. Me personally I would rather play on a primitive server but since the "official" Primitive + DLC is a joke at best then the only way to accomplish this is on unofficial servers that are modded. Some dinosaurs make sense and some do not but everyone has their opinion about what works best.

Don't get me wrong it has improved a lot since it was first released but it still lacks in certain areas. There are times when the game runs smooth as silk and then out of no where frame rates drop drastically for an intermittent amount of time then back to smooth. In a past update, the way mods were loaded on unoffical servers was changed which makes it take quite a while longer to load into a game. This by itself is not a problem but when you get disconnected during something important and need to load back into a game as quickly as possible, well that just isn't happening.

With all of the content added to the game there is just too much constant gathering you would have to do in order to have any of the new stuff. At least with an unofficial the server owners can adjust the rates to help out their playerbase. The game in itself is rather fun especially with friends, but fun can also be had alone. A friend of mine introduced me to this game 2 years ago when it first released on Xbox One. I decided to get this on PC because it honestly did'nt feel like a game fit for a console - but I'm not complaining. When I started Warframe I felt it was boring and did'nt make much sense. I thought it's fiction was unclear & meaningless, I was always getting lost in the interface. But once I got a feel for the controls, it all snapped into place and became a VERY fun experiance that I have yet to find in any other game.
This game could be VERY compared to Destiny (you know, that game from ps4 and xbox one?) because it is mainly a shooter that relies on player progression and endlessly unique fighting styles in combat, and the only thing that really makes it an "MMO" is that there can be many players at once.
With 3rd person shooting paired with crazy super-power-like abilities, along with a VERY well made parkour system, plus weapons & armor that make you feel SO AWESOME, it's kinda hard to ever get tired of this game's action once your familiar with it. Co-op on this game is very fun. While playing single player you have no allies except for your own abilities, making you feel like a one man army of awesomeness.
This game has outstanding soundtrack, but is also A BLAST to rock out to your favorite tunes with! (simply by muting the in-game music and playing your own from an extrnal device like a speaker or aux cable).
I eventually learned that the game's story, lore, and fiction is (while you still get a good enough narrative through short videos and transmissions on-screen), most of it is a lot like Destiny or Fnaf - there is SO MUCH OF A STORY that you simply can't fit it into direct cutscenes. IF you want the FULL experiance of ALL the story behind EVERYTHING, you will need to do a lot of reading and A LOT of careful in-game observation. And that's not a bad thing, because if you want the standard narrative, just watch the transmissions on your screen when they happen. Point is, it does not force everything in your face at once.
This game's progression is VERY grindy and not friendly to beginners, but with every hour of gameplay and every unlock you make, the game becomes so much more fun! As you progress you unlock new forms of gameplay (I.e, archwing missions) and new forms of combat, so even if you have put more hours into this game then the earth has existed, you'd probably still be descovering new things.
9/10! This game took a LONG time for me to get into, but now it's one of the best games that has EVER been installed on my PC.

Do you like ninjas?
How about robots?
Pirates? Zombies? Farming?
Well, Warframe manages to give you Robo-Ninja Pirates, that fight against Robots/cyborgs, genetically mutated clones, and endless hordes of Hive-minded zombies.
The graphics are amazeballs (for you visual junkies), the gameplay (fighting, movement, etc) is varied and feels fresh the majority of the time, it's both team-based and soloable (after a bit, obviously you cant solo high-tier stuff right out the gate).
There is a bit of a learning curve, but just ask a squadmate in a mission, or read up on the forums. The playerbase is overall friendly (you do have your bad apples, but that's a given).
It can get a bit...boring between major updates, but there are regular updates (every wednesday to be exact).
There is a 'premium' currency, but you don't have to pay for it if you don't want to, due to the trading system via other players. Find a Prime part or fancy mod (mods are an in-game item, aka 'Modules' that are used to power up weapons and 'Frames), and see if other players want to buy it for 'Platinum'.
Overall, a great game. Highly recommend.
2017 Edit - My views stay the same, even after all this time.

Full disclosure: I don't play on public servers.
Ark is a great survival game. It had me at dinosaurs, it kept me with farming, breeding and building.
There are plenty of bugs, but I'm pretty tolerant and they don't seem to bother me as much as they do other people.
Server settings can be tweaked well enough to accommodate those who don't have the time or patience to grind or wait for baby dinos to take their sweet time maturing.
With technological tiers ranging from primitive to alien you can choose how you want to experience life in Ark.
With a passionate and talented community of moders, you can customize the game to be exactly what you want it to be, and play the way you want to play.
Updates and new content are fairly regular, though like most things players seem to wish the devs would work more on optimizations and bug fixes more than new content.
Textures, animations, sound and general graphics are beautiful but you'll need a very good machine to run it well.
My main complaint now is that the basic maps are too small in my opinion, but moders have created many large and beautiful maps to explore (their main problems are incompleteness and bugs of their own of course).
I would highly recommend Ark to anyone who likes survival sandbox games.
Hours of fun for me, And still a lot more joy to come. Keep up the work DE.

---- Short Review ----
This was my entry into the whole survival genre; and it got me hooked. The building/crafting system and the interface itself is hands down the best I've seen in any surivial game. It's a massive game with a massive world and there's quite a bit to do.  As I'm sure you've noticed it's also a beautiful looking game. I've been around as far as survivial games go and none of them quite resonate with me like ARK does.
So why am I giving this a negative review you ask? Two reasons. One, it's really not enjoyable for casual/solo players (this is forgivable, more of an opinion really) and two, the community is one of the most toxic I've encountered (this is a HUGE negative for me).
---- Long, Ranty, Whiney Review ----
I have spent more times hopping servers trying to find a good one than actually playing the game. I've gotten above level 40 maybe twice. Even on PvE servers people will go out of their way to find some means to sabotage you and steal your stuff. There are people who level your entire base just for ♥♥♥♥♥ and giggles and then there are people who will kill you and steal everything you own out of greed/laziness. If you're not willing to be on every day then you're not going to do very well in ARK. Hell, even if you are on everyday you'll still get creamed by some alpha tribe.
The devs implemented this setting a way back that allows structures and the like in PvE to be dismantled by other players after a certain time of inactivity. This was originally designed so that the PvE servers wouldn't get cluttered in ungodly amounts of structures and pillars. This is all well and good on paper, the problem is that the people building the ungodly amount of structures usually tend to be the people on all day every day. SO what happens when I decide to take a break from ARK to go play another game? Well buh-bye all those hours of work.
Honeslty I would recommend this game if we could get a setup like this:
People go come onto a server merely for the social, cooperative aspects of it. You could build up your base, join a tribe, go solo, and everyone would just leave your things alone. People could help one another out and if both parties agreed to it there could be some competivite play. (Like the current tribe warfare system that is implemented) You could play as casually as you like, not having to worry about your base being gone just because you left the game for a month or two. Perhaps if there was a way a bunch of like-minded individuals could all join a server together and just do our own thing. Not having to worry about griefing tribes/players and losing all you've worked for just because you decided to take a break.
I feel people should be working together to surivive and thrive, not constantly competing against one another. Of course ARK is a perfect example of why in reality, mankind can never get a perfect utopia world. We're greedy, selfish, and just straight up ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s. We're only in it for ourselves and will watch someone else suffer if it means some sort of personal gain or benefit.
---- TL;DR ----
If you have time ( or money ) to kill, friends to play with, and some serious perseverance, I recommend ARK. Otherwise, give it some more time and let's see what it turns into.

Yes and No.
I'll start with the downsides, mostly because there's less of them and it's pretty simple. In the current state of ARK, Optimization is always some sort of issue. I do not blame the developers or demand, scream, shout, cry etc etc, simply because the constant updates or new things can't always be immediately addressed until it's a fair portion of the way in, by which time, another update will probably have dropped. However, once the game actually 100% releases, maybe by then most of the issues can be fixed.
Another downside is the constant "Early Access" feel. Once again, I don't blame the Devs completely, but I do feel that by now, the game really shouldn't be labeled as Early Access anymore and focus on finishing everything up, making the regular updates seem more fair and kind to players who can finally enjoy the "full build". On top of this, you have DLC that is being charged at quite a price, despite players simply using mods to bypass that. The DLC is really neat (I don't own it, but have seen it in play) and I feel the price should either be a little lower, or become free with exceptions (such as free for Early Access, but pay for on full release)
Now, onto the good stuff.
Contradictory to my "need optimization" statement, the game is still quite beautiful even in low everything. TheIsland (Main Map) could use some touches here and there, but is still fairly beautiful and grand. I absolutely LOVE "TheCenter" because it feels like it has more to offer, although I hope an update can roll out to change how Boss Fights are run on that map to help those who don't have access to the full TEK Tree. I'm currently playing a SteamWorkshop map called "Shigo Islands" and it shows how well people can work with the game to produce beautiful landscapes with extreme functionality.
The regular updates are also really nifty, bringing in some more content here and there to keep people busy, aswell as further pushing ARK to its' limits to see how well it can cope in several different terms.
I, personally, prefer to play on higher rate servers (50x+ everything at least) mainly because I can't always provide the time to spend on farming and taming constantly whilst hopping in and out of my workplace. I like things fast, clean and consistent. For those who have played official or default servers, I would suggested giving a slightly faster server a quick view, for example, 5x or even 10x servers.
Conclusion: A visually sweet game with good timing updates and replayability, but requires more optimization, review of systems and a look back on its' DLC and Defaulting Standards.

My feelings are mixed but I've gotten my $20 worth out of the game. There are public and private servers. I play on a private pve server because it's less punishing timewise and you don't have to worry about raiders destroying weeks of work.
Pros:
+Different game modes (pve, pvp, private, official, solo private)
+Strong sense of progression
+Nice dino models
+mods
+Thrill of tracking down and knocking a dino unconscious
+Flexibility in base building
+Each dino has a specific utility that can be somewhat customized (attacker, efficient resource gatherer, pack mule, and more)
+The need for resources forces you to venture outside of your base no matter how self-sufficient you are
Cons:
-Taming times
-Breeding times
-Griefers on pvp servers
-Lack of endgame content
-Base building can be tedious
-After knocking a dino unconscious, taming is a boring waiting game
The initial playthrough is great. When you're building yourself up and taming new dinos for the first time, it's a lot of fun. However, after taming everything, there is not much to the end game and it gets stale. On pvp there are raids, on pve there are boss battles and improving your base. The breeding system is pokemon X1000 aggravation because of sheer wait time.
I can't imagine playing on official where some tames take 5+ hours and servers can't be shut down to allow people to sleep while breeding something. Baby dinos want care every 3-4 hours for a special bonus at the end. Depending on the dino, this can be a horrifically lengthy process over several days.
I came in after the flyer nerf so I don't have strong feelings about it. For the most part I don't have a problem with how flying currently works. I think flyers could use more stamina to compensate for their lack of speed.

Do you like ninjas?
How about robots?
Pirates? Zombies? Farming?
Well, Warframe manages to give you Robo-Ninja Pirates, that fight against Robots/cyborgs, genetically mutated clones, and endless hordes of Hive-minded zombies.
The graphics are amazeballs (for you visual junkies), the gameplay (fighting, movement, etc) is varied and feels fresh the majority of the time, it's both team-based and soloable (after a bit, obviously you cant solo high-tier stuff right out the gate).
There is a bit of a learning curve, but just ask a squadmate in a mission, or read up on the forums. The playerbase is overall friendly (you do have your bad apples, but that's a given).
It can get a bit...boring between major updates, but there are regular updates (every wednesday to be exact).
There is a 'premium' currency, but you don't have to pay for it if you don't want to, due to the trading system via other players. Find a Prime part or fancy mod (mods are an in-game item, aka 'Modules' that are used to power up weapons and 'Frames), and see if other players want to buy it for 'Platinum'.
Overall, a great game. Highly recommend.
2017 Edit - My views stay the same, even after all this time.

Skimming over the complaints/reviews of the game I see a lot of people listing problems, but there is one colossal problem that I don't see. The bloody HDD spaces.
This game is bloody HUGE on a HDD. I performed a clean install [complete with unsubbing my mods] just to make sure I wasn't wrong.
An entirely clean install measures out to 75.9 GB of space.
That's almost twice the reccomended HDD space in the System Requirements, and contrary to what some people will argue, there is NO excuse for it. The textures aren't outstandingly impressive and the audio, compared to other large, open-world games (Witcher 3 is 40 GB or so) of near or equal size. It's just development being lazy and not cleaning up after all of their patches.
Make no mistake, this is a great game (was? I haven't played for awhile despite having it installed.) and I definitely feel I got my money's worth, but so long as the system requirements are misleading I cannot advocate purchasing this game.
tl;dr
The game takes WAY more HDD space than is remotely justifiable and requires twice as much HDD space as the System Requirements indicates. Make damn sure you have a significant portion of spare HDD if you plan to buy/play this game.

Back in 2013 me and my friends played this new game called "Warframe".
It was a shining example in free to play games and what seemed like the offspring of Mass Effect and GunZ.
Featuring a vast array of Warframe (which are the 'classes', basically), weapons and companions, this game was jaw droppingly good, and, it actually still is.
Revisiting this game in the recent past months I was amazed. Not only did it remain enjoyable, it added
.
Aside from the obvious need to add microtransactions (Which, I can't judge, they do need to make money) there were tons of new features - Ships being added, Focus Lenses, Odonata (Which is basically Gundam), PvP, Syndicates, Formas... So many things to do!
And the best thing? Even when grinding:
If you like fast paced, third person shooters, co-op games, you're in for a treat.
Make sure you bring a friend!

Anoter pro point: Although the game is out for quite some time already, it is still getting updated by the devs even with bigger story updates! These guys don't make a game that is "finished" they develop it further and further, making it better with every update.

Single player review:
Concept and ideas behind this game are such that it could have been one of the greatest games of all time.  Sadly, the UI is cumbersome and non-intuitive.  The resource gathering is repetetive and frustrating.  THERE IS NO SAVE GAME FOR SINGLE PLAYER.  You will find information to the contrary, but that has to do with experience, levels, and ingrams (blueprints).  Those things do get saved, but when you die, you lose everything. All inventory. Meaning you have to gather sticks and rocks off the beach to rebuild a stone hatchet all over again when you die.  Every time.  Yes, you can find your body and retrieve your items, but there is no marker indicating where your body is, so if you weren't paying attention or were just trying to have fun enjoying the game and the awesome scenery, you will have a hard time finding your body.  And you'll want at least a hatchet to go looking for it anyways, because the world, while gorgeous, is dangerous.  This discourages exploration of what is a beautiful environment.  Boo.  Dino taming is incredibly slow, and the system in place is unintuitive and a chore.  So there goes that potential out the window.  In short, it's a game that is incredibly NOT fun.  Which obviously defeats the whole purpose.  This is terribly sad when you look at what it could have been.  Early access is no excuse at this point, 2+ years down the road.
To the Devs:  Lighten up.  Focus on fun, not punishing the players.  Adjust the pace by keeping some tools and resources in inventory after death, and make building a permanent respawn area easier, mark the body, and encourage exploration and advancement.  Add a save game function.  (Also: Why the hell do I have to grind for hours to reach 15th level before I can learn a simple bow and arrow?)  It's not supposed to feel like work, its a game.
