It's an overall average game, Some parts shine, but those parts are brought down by just as much of a turd splattered mess.  Let's start with the positive:
-The controls are solid, even on a gamepad.
-Movement feels smooth and the more you master things like chaining bullet jumps and rolls you'll be able to move quickly across any environment.
-The weapon variety is good, though there's a downside I'll get to later.
-Visuals are nice, although none of the environments really made me stop and admire them.
-There are new regular events and such that offer new and good rewards mostly along with them.
Basically, the core mechanics are polished.  Shooting and melee are both fluid and I never really had any trip-ups involving these and the movement.  Because of where I stand on visuals preferring stylized over realistic I can't be the one to judge the graphics, but I like the warframe and weapon designs.
Where the game fails, however, is much more broad.
-There is a reason this game is commonly called bugframe.  you will constantly run into glitches putting you out of the map, making some objectives bug out, as well as affect other aspects of gameplay, progression, and just annoy you.
-This game is heavily based on timers unless you have platinum, which is premium currency.  You can trade for parts, but good luck getting anyone to buy common prime parts even for a pittance.
-The gun and weapon power is incredibly underwhelming save for a few.  You'll either end up with a  Vaykor Hek, Soma Prime, Dread, or Synoid Simulor for primaries, Marelok, Lex Prime, or Talons for Secondaries, and the melee weapons fare a little better with a choice between any dagger, Fragor Prime, Galatine, Nikana Prime, Redeemer, Estreza, or Orthos Prime.  This is because these are the only weapons that reliably do damage to higher enemies that you'll inevitably be roadblocked by.
-This game is a grind fest. It literally trumps Monster Hunter in having to farm for anything and everything from mods to prime parts to credits and even beyond that.  Everything in this game requires it.
-The entry bar is steep. You'll be hitting walls really early on unless you have a friend to help you along and a wiki open just to learn where crap drops and what to look for.
-The enemy balancing is nonexistant.  The game doesn't care whether it's one person or four people, meaning if you're a poor sap like me that prefers going alone to missions you'll be using at least half a clip of the aforementioned weapons just to bring down higher enemies, because while you max out at level 30, the enemies only go higher, meaning while your weapons have a damage cap, the enemies don't.  This can especially be seen in the Sortie missions, good luck killing heavy gunners or any other heavy enemy on the level 80-100 missions unless you have a dagger and have somehow built your warframe to take enough bullets to the chin.
-The customization is limited unless you shell out platinum for more color pallettes because the starting ten colors you get are lackluster and muted at best.
This reason this game balances out to average for me is because I value mechanics, then gameplay, then visuals. and as I stated, movement, shooting, and melee all feel nice and smooth and working. The core of this game though is timers and grinding, and nothing but. In my opinion this game has the potential to shed that common yoke of extending the game through padding, but instead they embrace padding, and built a village around it like canals through Venice, letting it become the veins of their game in the worst aspect possible.  Game length, does not attribute to game quality.  If they took out the timers, and maybe grinding for resources and parts not as much of a hassle, then you'd a 7/10 instead of the 5 it's getting from me.  If they made every weapon feel useful instead of crappy fluff and mastery fodder on top of that, then it would be an 8.  If they made more of an attempt at balancing enemies relative to the maximum capable power of the weapons as well, then it would be a 9.
But no, none of that happened or probably will happen, looking at progress in the past till now, so it gets a 5/10.  It's average, it doesn't matter whether it's considered in beta or not, it's been out for years at this point, well beyond when other games when have already been fully patched. I wouldn't reccommend this game unless you already have a friend that plays and would be willing to help you over some of the hurdles.

This review is for those who are only now checking out ARK.
Do not let these reviews mislead you. Most of the negativity comes from the official servers, which makes sense, considering these servers have a history of duping and downright negative behavior. Unofficial is arguably the best way to enjoy the game if you are playing PvE in particular, though PvP can be much better on unofficial, as well.
This is a fantastic and addictive game. There is so much to do, from taming hundreds of creatures to crafting hundreds of items. The building system is in-depth with many mods available for better builds and other quality of life changes that make the game more fun - more reasons why unofficial is preferred.
The bulk of the negativity comes from the typical official PvP server, where the alpha tribe races to the top and then proceed to continuously wipe out any competition, strong or weak.
One has to question why ARK even provides these servers to begin with. Sure it's helpful, but I believe ARK would be stronger if we were required to look into an unofficial server.

Its about time I wrote a review for this game.
Warframe has absrobed my life. In a month I got over 130 hours and thats with a job, school, and family. Its a great F2P game that is 100% free. Paying allows you to look cool (which is probably the end goal) and you can also pay to get things faster. This game does have a lot of farming in it, but its a fun farm unlike The Divsion or Destiny. The people in this game are extremely helpful and finding a group to play with is super easy.
The combat and art is so great. It blew me away when I first saw my space ninja fly through the air, slow time and shoot an arrow at a bad guys head, inst-killing him. I would recommend giving this game a try!
Do note that the new player experience can be kind of rough, but the game has a great wiki and forums, so anything you want to know google it.

Issues: It is to be noted that game crashes from time to time (like once in a day or two) and experiences lags and frame drops as expected from a incomplete game.  It may happen due to a ram being overflown so I suggest to reload game from time to time and sometimes it is just an error.  If you have a short temper and not ready to take a loss from a game crash - maybe this game is still too early for you.
Dinos: Spectre of dinosaurs range from little Compis size of your feet to 10 stores high T Rexes on steroids called Gigas.  There are also other creatures like monkeys which throw poop at your enemies, pegos which will steal your underwear (or a rare shotgun), troodons... F*ck them.  Oh yes - stay away from swamps or you will get the most annoying disease which can blind your character with a green overlay, can make your friend abandon you and is only healed when you get some rare resources.
Building: It is similar to Rust although a bit inferior at the moment (no triangular foundations) and can trigger OCD when you build a fence.  However it doesn't have much realism and has few exploitation points.
Loot:  At times you will get loot crates.  Sometimes you get blueprints you can use to craft items, sometimes you get an accursed medium crop plot.  Devs, I beg you to fix it.  I am tired of getting these blueprints for n hudreds time.  Have a mercy.
Taming:  Different dinos need different food.  Either master a witchcraft of kibble or spend 5 to 10 hours taming a decent Rex.  It is a well refined mechanic and will be useful for you to survive.
Bosses:  I heard of them.  Never encountered them.  Plan to kill one in a month or two.
Addiction Level:  If WoW or MMO can suck you in for years - there is an another option for you right there.  Don't play it if you can't control your gaming habit.
Poop:  There is poop you can eat or use in farming. Coprophilia all the way!
Host:  If you want, you can host a game for you and few more players (read about local servers, there are some important parameters) or play on bigger servers.  If you play in Europe, try UK Evolved.
P.S.
You maybe have read about the flyer nerf and other stuff, with people getting angry and upset.  My opinion - flyers were overpowered before the patch and now they are not game breaking creatures.  Developers do optimise game (compare it from Sep 2016 to April 2017) but it is still to be done more (I hate the crashes due to memory leaking).

At this point when I'm writing this review, I am already way past 100 hours into the game. This game is every bit amazing and I will list why below:
Pros:
1. BEAUTIFUL world. Amazing graphics and details, be it for the landscape, or for the beasts.
2. CAPTIVATING. Keeps you engaged as you work to your own personal goals because you have to overcome the natural obstacles of the world.
3. MANUEVERABILITY: You can engage the world in various means of transports on land, sea and sky.
4. BUILD: Build your own 'base' or lodgings in however you see fit. You can even see in my screenshots that I have made an ark-style boat "The Enterprise" featuring its own lookout on the official server.
5. EVOLVING world as the devs brings up patches now and then to improve the world or even do something disastrous like making a volcano active (in a way it's challenging. Imagine you were really building a shelter in that era and a natural disaster erupted out of the blue. IT DOES HAPPEN!)
Cons:
1. Limited space: on official servers anyway. Most people or tribes have been enlarging their own boundaries in various servers, inhibiting new and other players to build in many spaces. I was lucky to be able to secure a sufficient spot and the tribe nearby are very friendly to me. I have also known them to help other newcomers, while I decided that I would take up the challenge and do things on my own first.
2. Toxic players? I mean, this is quite common in any mmo where you encounter selfish failures. Thankfully, I haven't decided to label anyone this so far, although I did find a particular jerk rather obnoxious.
3. Goals. You can't just wait for someone or the game to give you a goal. You have to make your own goals to survive! Technically this should be a pro, but some people are just ignorant and expect someone to help them survive in the game. If you are such a person, you won't last long anyway.
OVERALL:
Lots of fun for building up your home, pets and more!

When Destiny came out, I unloaded on it, I played that game till I hit max level with the first expansion, and the second. It was great. I had always wiffed off warframe because I simply believed that free to play could not be better than a full on $100 or so game. I was dead wrong. When I was finally bored of Destiny as everyone should be by this point, I installed warframe on ps4 just to check out what I was potentially missing out on. I could not believe how cool this game was, it was literally allowing me to become a space ninja. Destiny was cool for what it was, but warframe excelled at keeping me interested. Warframes environment is a lot smaller (in space, not size) than destiny's, however it's procedrially genorated making the game so much more interesting than grinding the same mission over and over again in Destiny. Also the first thing you notice when you compare Destiny to Warframe is how many more classes their are. There are 3 in Destiny, and like 30 in warframe (probably more).
Enough comparing Destiny to warframe however, how does Warframe stand up on its own? Amazingly. If you're play for free, there's a multitude of things you can do. Daily log in rewards, modifiable suits, heck even just hanging around in your clans tower is interesting enough to just break boredom.
Buy this game if you have no life.

Warframe has changed alot since its release.
It went from being a small game with a small community, to a big game with a big community. But after all of my time with this game, through it's various updates, I feel like something is changing slowly, for the worse.
It may just be me, but I feel like the Devs are slowly getting too comfortable with their jobs, no worries, no pressure, no determination to get things done. It feels like they are getting used to saying, "well, we wanted to get this update out this month, but perhaps it's best if we delay it for just a bit longer." In a twist of irony, recently the devs were talking about just how hard they had worked on the game to make sure it would stay interesting, and kept building on it as best they could to make this game possible, in spite of what all the "pros" said.
These "pros" said, "It will never work, people are losing interest in sci-fi games." To which I say, "maybe if you made one with a soul that's interesting and not P2W, we can talk." (of course, I havent bothered with most recent games anyway, so where do I have room to talk?)
I believe this game will fail, but NOT because people don't want good sci-fi games. But rather, because the devs seem to be getting more and more lazy about producing updates, and more and more focused on hyping them instead.
By all means.

After around 1,060 hours of in-game mission time and 1,517 hours in Steam, I stand in a good position to make some judgments about this game. I am terribly, intimiately familiar with it.
At its surface, Warframe is an eclectic mission-based science-fantasy shooter with a huge variety of weapons and the eponymous Warframe suits, giving unparalleled player choice and customization. Add in a unique PvP system resembling nothing quite so much as Unreal with aerial mobility and a secondary game mode with free-space flight missions, and it seems as though the game offers something to appeal to everyone. To sweeten the deal, it even comes wrapped in a tidy and beautiful package of gorgeous and well-optimized visual assets, with beautiful effects and atmospheric lighting lending every mission a dramatic and empowering cast.
This is where the good parts of Warframe stop. Now for a little bit of criticism. Or, well, a lot.
Warframe's core gameplay is no deeper than a glass of water, if that, with the extent of player success in the main PvE content of the game determined by only the smallest amount of player skill and strategy and the seemingly endless customization being suffocated under poor balance of a truly bloated supply of player armaments, only 10-15% of which end up actually being useful and worthwhile in "endgame" content. Rather than requiring the player to be careful and assiduous in their play, the game instead leans on the crutch of horde-mode game scaling mechanics to arbitrarily overwhelm the player and force them into a tight, efficient, very un-fun metagame structure.
The supposedly diverse set of mission types - assassinations, infiltrations, wholesale slaughters - is extremely homogeneous, and is buuilt in such a way that every single moment of gameplay in PvE is fungible, with only the most minute details of what specific MacGuffin or forgettable procedurally-generated starship being relevant in estsablishing that the player is not, in fact, just engaged in the longest MMO fetch quest ever built.
The sound design of the game is at best mediocre, with the background music fading into the background in a way that only the least cerebral or euphonic sounds can - it is, in the overwhelming majority of circumstances, simply the Muzak of the interminable elevator ride with a fat mant that the game feels like from roughly ten hours in onward. Sound effects associated with weapons, Warframe powers, and most other elements of gameplay are cheap, hollow, and rough, and the development team seems to continually grapple with releasing poorly-implemented, ear-splitting sound effects in new content every few months, as though just to remind long-term players that the game even has sound at all.
While the visual design of the game is very pleasing on the whole, the level of detail put into Warframes and weapons is much higher than that put into most environments, with the visual presentation of the game relying overly much on the recently revamped lighting engine. While the lighting engine lends a great deal of life to even the most drab of environments, the age of much of the game's original level design and art is jarringly apparent. This is something the developer team seems to actively be working on, but the progress is very slow.
Perhaps most disheartening for me personally is the way that so much of the game's incredibly broad content base - third-person shooter, discount Rocket League, space flight simulator, and Unreal-on-crack PvP - is not well developed, or is often subjected to unnecessary modifications that are regularly unsolicited and unsupported by the player base. Recent developments, such as the vacuous Lunaro "sport" or the entirety of the Archwing free-space combat platform - tends to feel shoehorned in and plays as though left partway through development.
Last on the note of the gameplay: Warframe has no cohesive motivating goal or well-crafted plot. The player is given a vague sense of their role in the game's universe, but past this all story exposition is done through overwrought "minimalist" lore snippets and the occasionally plot-significant quest. Frankly, though, past the first few hours of gameplay when novelty illumines the game, there is simply no reason to play. The entire thesis of Warframe is "play unremarkable missions for materials to craft weapons and Warframes to play more unremarkable missions," without significant content existing past Mastery Rank (account level) 12 despite a rank of 22 currently being possible. This says nothing of the gaping void that is the Warframe endgame - relevant content barely exists past the unchallenging enemy level range of 90-110, and most of the "endgame" as it might be thought to exist comes in the form of players compelling themselves to play marathon instances of infinitely scaling horde survival missions.
Game aside, my final concern is the developers themselves. While the regular panel of Digital Extremes staff that handles official livestream content is amusing and affable, the great majority of DE's less-visible staff or associates - forum moderators/administrators, customer support, and minimally-present developers - is a mass of incommunicative, adversarial, and relationally opaque individuals who seem to act off apathy toward or sometimes even contempt for the player base.
I really enjoyed Warframe when I began playing, but as I grew in account level and time spent on the game, my attitude sank slowly into the morass of a good concept handled by the wrong people with malformed goals, and I became disillusioned with the truly Sisyphean task of playing the game... in order to play the game more.
That's all Warframe really is, in the end: a smattering of random content smeared across the vague idea of a unifying premise that turns out to be no more than the circular reasoning one would expect to find in a freshman philosophy class or a US Republican Party debate.
I do not recommend that you play this game, no matter how much it sounds like "Destiny that doesn't suck."

Don't listen to the negative reviews about the game being "Pay To Win". Warframe is a game where you don't have to spend a single dollar to unlock all of the content. Yes, there are items only purchasable with Platinum (the premium currency) but so far all of these Platinum only items are purely customization items (Syandanas, colour swaps). Yes, you can buy weapons and Warframes for Platinum, but you can also craft them using resources and credits. Crafting takes some time but it's an infinitely better idea than spending Platinum.
Well what if you want access to more customization options? And what about needing more weapon and Warframe slots? If you've already spent the 50 Platinum that you get when you start the game (SPEND IT ON WEAPON/WARFRAME SLOTS). you can easily earn Platinum over time by farming for Prime items and trading them away. After my first week of play I sat down for a few hours, cracked some relics, went to warframe.market (a third party website that helps buyers and sellers find each other) and looked for people buying what I had. Another day later I had made enough Platinum to buy a Syandana.
Yes, earning Platinum takes time but it isn't hard. If you are hurting for Platinum and are too lazy to work for it, you have a  chance to earn up to 75% off of all Platinum purchases for one purchase through the daily login rewards. I've played for 220 hours and I'm still enjoying it. Try it for yourself, it's free after all.

Warframe is a fun, free to play MMO sci-fi RPG where you play as a race known as the Tenno.
You control these suits known as warframes and you travel around the solar system to fight one (or two) of any of the major factions such as the grineer or infested. After you have leveled your mastery rank a little, you can join a conclave which is essentially another faction to gain access to marks, mods, sydanas, weapons and spectres.
Since its initial launch, Warframe has gone through major game changing updates which have made the game 1000% better than when it was released as a beta.
The game has a fun movement system which makes everyone who runs around seem like a badass, jumping off walls, sliding and bullet jumping, even slowing down time to glide through the air whilst you aim your weapon.
Some of the games cons do include though; paywalls for platinum (though you can trade for platinum), a lot of grinding, real time waiting for crafted items/weapons/Warframe, occasional glitches, sometimes little to no indication on where you should possibly go next which can be frustrating if you are a new player.
All in all, I find Warframe to be a game I would recommend to anyone who likes shooters, and don't mind grinding.

I have a few hours into this game now, and I have to admit... it is quite addictive.  It is designed to allow players to "grow" with the game, meaning that as you learn all the basics from the beginning, all the way through completing end-game content and even sortie missions, that the player is gradually introduced to each faction, the various mission types, weapons, their capabilities and of course the endless combinations of modifications for everything.  It is furthermore designed to allow the players to "rank" their chosen weapons, warframes, and the mods for them.  Players can also decide to work their way through the levels and missions, or can speed the process with affinity, credit and drop-rate boosters if they choose to.  This is NOT a pay-to-play game, nor is it a pay-to-win game.  Although you can acquire everything in-game simply by playing the game itself, players can also purchase certain items from the market to quickly get you more involved with the game if you choose to.

As a rule, I am not a fan of Free to Play games with microtransactions (or, in the case of this game, you could call it macrotransactions... you will see why if you look at them), but Warframe is an extreme exception. I have, according to Steam, played 240 hours of Warframe, and it still holds my attention.
Firstly, my favorite aspect of it: co-op. This is a game that puts cooperative mode in the forefront of all other aspects, and it is one of very few that do so. Mainstream games nowadays are either single player, or PVP multiplayer, or a bit of both. One of my favorite things about this game is that I have heard PVP mentioned only a few times--it's entirely possible to pretend the game doesn't even have PVP if you're not interested in it.
The down side is the cost of microtransactions in the game. Platinum, the in-game premium currency, is cheap enough when you get a 75% off coupon from your daily reward (happens on average every 10-15 days in my experience, but that is higher than most others) but the Prime Access and Prime Vaults are quite expensive. Still, as the game can be played 100% for free if desired, it's not a huge deal.

Ark: Survival Evolved is an open world action-adventure survival video game in development by Studio Wildcard in cooperation with Instinct Games, Efecto Studios, and Virtual Basement. It is scheduled for release on PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Microsoft Windows, OS X, and Linux in 2017. The game's early access began for Windows in June 2015, for OS X and Linux in July 2015, for Xbox One in December 2015, and for PlayStation 4 in December 2016. In the game, players must survive being stranded on an island filled with roaming dinosaurs and other prehistoric animals, natural hazards, and potentially hostile human players.
The game is played from either a third-person or first-person view and its world is navigated on foot or by riding a prehistoric animal. Players use firearms and improvised weapons to defend against hostile humans and creatures, with the ability to build bases as defense. The game has both single-player and multiplayer options.
Development began in October 2014. The development team conducted research into the physical appearance of the animals, but took creative license for gameplay purposes. One of the game modes, Survival of the Fittest, was released as a free standalone game in March 2016. Egypt-based developer Instinct Games was hired to facilitate the game's development. Three DLCs (The Center, Primitive Plus, and Scorched Earth) were also released.
Ark: Survival Evolved is an action-adventure survival game set in an open world environment that uses a first-person perspective, with the ability to use a third-person perspective in some instances. To survive, players must establish a base, with a fire and weapons; additional activities, such as taming and feeding dinosaurs, require more resources. The game's world, known as the "Ark", is approximately 48 km2 (19 sq mi) in size: there is approximately 36 km2 (14 sq mi) of land with 12 km2 (4.6 sq mi) of ocean.
To build a base, players must gain structure components—such as floors, doors and windows built with the resources littered throughout the world—which are earned as they progress and gain levels. These components can be crafted and placed in the world. Players can create any structure, as long as they have the logistics and resources; the structural integrity of the building is compromised when the pillars and foundations are destroyed. Creating structures out of metal make them the most durable; only titanosaurs and explosives can damage metal structures. Players can also craft items in the game, such as weapons, by collecting the resources and technology required for crafting. In addition, players can craft and attach accessories to their weapons, such as a scope or flashlight for a pistol or machine gun. Should players take damage, their health meter will gradually regenerate if they have consumed the necessary food, or if they craft items that regenerate the health meter at a faster pace.
There are sixty species of dinosaurs in the game. Dinosaurs in the game can be tamed by feeding them food after they have been rendered unconscious, or by using kibble designed especially for each species. Once a dinosaur is tamed, players can utilize the dinosaur's abilities, such as flight or fast underwater movement, as well as its statistics, such as speed, health and damage. When riding atop certain creatures, players can use their weapons. With the larger dinosaurs, other players can ride on the side with full control of their own weapons. They can also be used to carry items, and players can issue offensive and defensive commands to them; for example, a pack of Utahraptors can be assigned to defend the base, or a group of Triceratops can be ordered to attack an enemy's base. The game also features various other animals, such as the dodo, saber-toothed cat, woolly mammoth, Meganeura, Titanomyrma, and Doedicurus. Every creature in the game has living ecosystems and predator hierarchies.
Like DayZ and H1Z1, ARK: Survival Evolved is another Early-Access survival game that has received an explosive amount of attention. But does it provide something different enough to warrant all the publicity? In short, no. You can collect materials, craft items, and tame dinosaurs, but many of those features are not exclusive to ARK, nor are they any better here. Serious functionality problems and lag exist, sapping enjoyment and crippling immersion. Still, it’s not completely awful. Given the chance, you can have a lot of fun, even if there are not many fresh ideas at this stage of development. The game can be entertaining at times and frustrating on occasion, but the evolution of survival it is not--at least not yet.

I wanted to like this game. The developers clearly have a passion for dinosaurs and other prehistoric life, and it shows. Unfortunately, there is no game here. What we have is an aimless grindathon that struggles to serve as a dinosaur toy box. Dinosaurs are rarely fun to fight, there's an absurd amount of waiting or doing tedious tasks, and progression is miserably slow.
This game is built around taming and riding dinosaurs. So why is it that when I tame a dinosaur, I can't ride it until I build a saddle that I can't unlock for another 30 levels?!
I'd suggest that saddles should be optional. You can ride any creature you tame without a saddle, but you can't sprint with them, you can't control their attacks, you lose control during combat, and you fall off if they take too much damage. Boom! Now the game doesn't punish you for taming that theriziniosaur at an early level while offering incentives for the saddle to gain more control and stability.
The engram system needs to either be removed altogether or drastically altered.
My idea would be to condense most engrams together. Instead of having an engram for every piece of the house, have a single engram for each building material type; a thatch housing engram, a stone housing engram, etc. Have an engram for all pieces of an armor set, rather than one for each piece separately. Have one for primitive tools which includes the stone pick, axe, spear, torch, campfire, club, slingshot, bow, and arrow. Have an engram for saddles that grants you access to multiple saddles all at once, preferable at earlier levels. Having hundreds of engrams means nothing when each one grants you exactly ONE item. Leveling up becomes tedious when you have to unlock each item separately.
Remove inventory weight. Your carry weight should only apply to your clothing, tools, and weapons. All having a carry weight does is slows down the game. You're required to gather hundreds of materials, yet have to stop every 10 or 20 minutes to drop off everything you have because your carry weight has maxed out. You're clearly not carrying the hundreds of stones and pieces of wood on your back. They seem to be stored in this magical nexus rock on your wrist. So why have a carry weight at all. At least if it applies to the tools and weapons on your main selection bar, that makes sense. If you're trying to say it's because of "realism" or "immersion," I'd ask what's immersive about carrying around 4 stone foundations at once?
Speaking of building, give me the ability to pick back up a building item I've placed WITHOUT destroying it. This is especially annoying for small things like the mortar and pestal or a chair; things I know I can pick up without obliterating.
Give players the option to not drop their items when they die. It becomes tedious having to go half way across the island to find that one tiny backpack at the bottom of a piranah-infested pond. Similarly, have the option so that all or selected creatures you've tamed respawn near you. Maybe have a place set for them to respawn when you do, or make sure it's outside of your house. I've spent countless hours desparately trying to find lost dinos, only for them to have died off screen to the endless threats.
Reduce the number of predators on the island. Bugs and tiny things like compies or piranahs are fine as is. But I shouldn't be able to spot a pair of mated T-Rexes barreling down the beach at first level. Nor should I find 3-6 Therizinios in frame all at once despite them being defined as rare and solitary. Predators are WAY too abundant, and become a tiresome chore. There's nothing special about fighting off your 18th Carnotaur and 30th Utahraptor today.
There should be likee 3-4 T-Rexes spawned on the island at any given time. Maybe have a total of 15-20 raptors in packs of 4-6 each instead of countless lone raptors running about. Fighting a predator should feel like a rare threat/treat; not an every minute occurence. I dread going into swamps because I know I'm going to constantly be up to my eyes in pythons and super crocs before I'm snatched up by a jumping croc.
A lot of the new creatures being released are great, but the old ones desperately need an update. No one is going to tame a Parasaur or Phiomia. Utahraptors are just a massive pain meant to sucker punch you, and pale next to troodons which are truly terrifying and fun to run from. The sabertooth cat and mammoth are pitiful next to the thylaco and wooly rhino respectively. The Pachyrhino is just as effective as the Triceratops and comes with a pheramone attack. The list goes on.
Stop making spears break after one use. It's annoying and should never have been implemented.
Reduce the crafting cost for a lot of the tools and saddles. It only serves to add hours of tedious grinding for resources rather than having fun.
Make caves easier to find. As it stands, I can only find them with a guide.
And make the game fun to play in single player. Without cheats and major multipliers, this game is miserable to play on your own.
I can't recommend this game in its current state because there's virtually no game. You are buying a dinosaur toy box that constantly stops you from playing with the dinosaurs.
People call this "the next Minecraft." Minecraft had a lot you could do. The interface was simple, you weren't arbitrarily barred from crafting things, building was quick and simple, you could get creative with how you place blocks, and you could shape the entire world around you. With Ark, you have none of that. Your character feels weightless, combat is barebones, and it takes far too long to have fun.

Warframe is a fun, free to play MMO sci-fi RPG where you play as a race known as the Tenno.
You control these suits known as warframes and you travel around the solar system to fight one (or two) of any of the major factions such as the grineer or infested. After you have leveled your mastery rank a little, you can join a conclave which is essentially another faction to gain access to marks, mods, sydanas, weapons and spectres.
Since its initial launch, Warframe has gone through major game changing updates which have made the game 1000% better than when it was released as a beta.
The game has a fun movement system which makes everyone who runs around seem like a badass, jumping off walls, sliding and bullet jumping, even slowing down time to glide through the air whilst you aim your weapon.
Some of the games cons do include though; paywalls for platinum (though you can trade for platinum), a lot of grinding, real time waiting for crafted items/weapons/Warframe, occasional glitches, sometimes little to no indication on where you should possibly go next which can be frustrating if you are a new player.
All in all, I find Warframe to be a game I would recommend to anyone who likes shooters, and don't mind grinding.

I wanted to like this game. The developers clearly have a passion for dinosaurs and other prehistoric life, and it shows. Unfortunately, there is no game here. What we have is an aimless grindathon that struggles to serve as a dinosaur toy box. Dinosaurs are rarely fun to fight, there's an absurd amount of waiting or doing tedious tasks, and progression is miserably slow.
This game is built around taming and riding dinosaurs. So why is it that when I tame a dinosaur, I can't ride it until I build a saddle that I can't unlock for another 30 levels?!
I'd suggest that saddles should be optional. You can ride any creature you tame without a saddle, but you can't sprint with them, you can't control their attacks, you lose control during combat, and you fall off if they take too much damage. Boom! Now the game doesn't punish you for taming that theriziniosaur at an early level while offering incentives for the saddle to gain more control and stability.
The engram system needs to either be removed altogether or drastically altered.
My idea would be to condense most engrams together. Instead of having an engram for every piece of the house, have a single engram for each building material type; a thatch housing engram, a stone housing engram, etc. Have an engram for all pieces of an armor set, rather than one for each piece separately. Have one for primitive tools which includes the stone pick, axe, spear, torch, campfire, club, slingshot, bow, and arrow. Have an engram for saddles that grants you access to multiple saddles all at once, preferable at earlier levels. Having hundreds of engrams means nothing when each one grants you exactly ONE item. Leveling up becomes tedious when you have to unlock each item separately.
Remove inventory weight. Your carry weight should only apply to your clothing, tools, and weapons. All having a carry weight does is slows down the game. You're required to gather hundreds of materials, yet have to stop every 10 or 20 minutes to drop off everything you have because your carry weight has maxed out. You're clearly not carrying the hundreds of stones and pieces of wood on your back. They seem to be stored in this magical nexus rock on your wrist. So why have a carry weight at all. At least if it applies to the tools and weapons on your main selection bar, that makes sense. If you're trying to say it's because of "realism" or "immersion," I'd ask what's immersive about carrying around 4 stone foundations at once?
Speaking of building, give me the ability to pick back up a building item I've placed WITHOUT destroying it. This is especially annoying for small things like the mortar and pestal or a chair; things I know I can pick up without obliterating.
Give players the option to not drop their items when they die. It becomes tedious having to go half way across the island to find that one tiny backpack at the bottom of a piranah-infested pond. Similarly, have the option so that all or selected creatures you've tamed respawn near you. Maybe have a place set for them to respawn when you do, or make sure it's outside of your house. I've spent countless hours desparately trying to find lost dinos, only for them to have died off screen to the endless threats.
Reduce the number of predators on the island. Bugs and tiny things like compies or piranahs are fine as is. But I shouldn't be able to spot a pair of mated T-Rexes barreling down the beach at first level. Nor should I find 3-6 Therizinios in frame all at once despite them being defined as rare and solitary. Predators are WAY too abundant, and become a tiresome chore. There's nothing special about fighting off your 18th Carnotaur and 30th Utahraptor today.
There should be likee 3-4 T-Rexes spawned on the island at any given time. Maybe have a total of 15-20 raptors in packs of 4-6 each instead of countless lone raptors running about. Fighting a predator should feel like a rare threat/treat; not an every minute occurence. I dread going into swamps because I know I'm going to constantly be up to my eyes in pythons and super crocs before I'm snatched up by a jumping croc.
A lot of the new creatures being released are great, but the old ones desperately need an update. No one is going to tame a Parasaur or Phiomia. Utahraptors are just a massive pain meant to sucker punch you, and pale next to troodons which are truly terrifying and fun to run from. The sabertooth cat and mammoth are pitiful next to the thylaco and wooly rhino respectively. The Pachyrhino is just as effective as the Triceratops and comes with a pheramone attack. The list goes on.
Stop making spears break after one use. It's annoying and should never have been implemented.
Reduce the crafting cost for a lot of the tools and saddles. It only serves to add hours of tedious grinding for resources rather than having fun.
Make caves easier to find. As it stands, I can only find them with a guide.
And make the game fun to play in single player. Without cheats and major multipliers, this game is miserable to play on your own.
I can't recommend this game in its current state because there's virtually no game. You are buying a dinosaur toy box that constantly stops you from playing with the dinosaurs.
People call this "the next Minecraft." Minecraft had a lot you could do. The interface was simple, you weren't arbitrarily barred from crafting things, building was quick and simple, you could get creative with how you place blocks, and you could shape the entire world around you. With Ark, you have none of that. Your character feels weightless, combat is barebones, and it takes far too long to have fun.

NOTE: If you're looking for a shorter review, scroll down past the line.
I know a lot of people are whining and absolutely freaking out over the recent updates, but they're really not that bad.
A lot of people are complaining that removing the option to up flyer speed just to make ground dinos more effective didn't do its job, but I personally think it did. I personally hate pteranodons, and since those are now among the fastest flyers on non-SE servers (because of wyverns), I find it easier and more entertaining to just hop on a wolf or a saber or raptor to get where I need to go.
I also view it from the point of view that flyers with an insane amount of movement speed were often crashing unofficial servers (I can't speak for Official ones. I don't play on Official servers). If you have a flyer that can literally zip across the map in 5 seconds flat, it's easy to crash a server with all the loading and unloading it has to do, and some servers have their backups very spread out, which would make hours worth of work void.
I remember when I first noticed the flyer change I was like 'aww, what?' and was admittedly a little upset about it for a bit, but after playing for a while with the new change I realized I actually like it. It made me want to give more TLC to my other dinos too!
I know it can suck to have days and months worth of work with breeding (for example) to be rendered useless, but you do have to remember that this is an EARLY ACCESS game. Whether it was supposed to be out of Early Access forever ago or not, it's still in Early Access right now, which means ANY feature is subject to change at ANY time. You knew this when you bought the game, and you knew this when you put hundreds of hours of work into it, so you have no right to turn around and complain about how it's 'unfair' or 'complete BS' because you lost so much progress.
There have been and still will be a LOT of new features and changes, some of which not everyone will like. That's just how it is. If ARK was completed and released out of Early Access like most other games before anyone got a chance to play it, there would still be things you didn't like. Truth of the matter is literally no game is perfect and every game appeals more to some people than it does to others.
The devs might not be that great at communication, and I agree that's something they do need to work on, but I can't speak too much of that because I haven't had any issues with it myself. I've never had to approach a dev, I've never had any troubles, so I can't give my own two cents on the matter. Though I think maybe they should look to the community a bit more before pushing major changes. At least giving players a heads up would make them less furious about it.
-------------------------------------------------------
That aside, on to an actual review.
I do highly recommend this game IF you're able to stand the fact that things can and will change. If you're a serious PvP player, you might have trouble liking the way things change a lot, but if you're a more casual player who, for the most part, only plays on private self-hosted servers, it's easy to get absorbed.
Here's a list of some of the game's features:
- Open-World / Sandbox Survival / Animal Husbandry. I've personally always been a lover of open world/sandbox games, survival games, and taming/animal husbandry games. ARK is literally all of those things in one, and I couldn't be happier with it!
- Fairly Frequent Content Updates. The content is great and I think the rate of updates is fair. It's not too quick, giving people time to fully explore the current new features before adding something new, and it's not too slow to the point where you're practically dying for an update.
- Mods. The community has many great and fun mods to work with too, and I use a handful of them on my own servers! I check the workshop every few days, since there always seems to be something new.
- Extensive Maps. The maps are huge and there's always something new to explore. Even years later I'm still finding new and fun things about The Island (the first map).
- Dinos! There's an incredible amount of dinos to tame and play with, and there's always new ones being added.
- Important and well-made core mechanics to a survival game like base-building and material processing (i.e. turning metal into ingots).
- Lots of fun and interesting features, like random mutations in breeding, hair/beard growth, and beer!
***IMPORTANT NOTE: It's a good idea to have a pretty beefy computer if super realistic and great graphics is something that matters to you.
In the end, ARK is a game I have thoroughly enjoyed over the years. It's been a long, wild ride so far but I've made many friends and had a ton of fun, and I know there's more of that to come.
Keep on going, devs! Maybe work on your communication a bit, but keep on keeping on!
And anyone thinking of buying this game, just remember that it will require A LOT of patience while the game gets updated and things change. If you can do that, then I think this is a game you'll enjoy.

Having played for about two years, I can say that this is one of the most enjoyable games I have played.  Of course the lore of the game is limited as it is a F2P and muliplayer game.  However, the game was not meant to be lore heavy and is all about making your "personal world" via the grinding and playing of the game.  The frames are very numerous and quite diverse and DE is constantly bringing out new frames and equipment.  The stories continue to be upgraded and the community is overall very friendly.
This is a game of grinding to build your own ecosystem of sorts.  If you are not into such games, Warframe will not interest you.  However, if you do like leveling up your equipment, interacting with other players and creating a place for yourself, Warframe is a wonderful place to do so.
Oh and one final word.  I have never "Had to" pay for anything in the game.  The only time I did was to give something back to DE by buying Pt during a 75% off deal (I already had thousands of Pt but did so anyway), or to buy Tennogen products.  This is definitely a F2P game if you are willing to play it as such.

I have a few hours into this game now, and I have to admit... it is quite addictive.  It is designed to allow players to "grow" with the game, meaning that as you learn all the basics from the beginning, all the way through completing end-game content and even sortie missions, that the player is gradually introduced to each faction, the various mission types, weapons, their capabilities and of course the endless combinations of modifications for everything.  It is furthermore designed to allow the players to "rank" their chosen weapons, warframes, and the mods for them.  Players can also decide to work their way through the levels and missions, or can speed the process with affinity, credit and drop-rate boosters if they choose to.  This is NOT a pay-to-play game, nor is it a pay-to-win game.  Although you can acquire everything in-game simply by playing the game itself, players can also purchase certain items from the market to quickly get you more involved with the game if you choose to.

i have a total of about 1k hours on this game and i cannot reccommend it to anyone. This game is riddled with bugs, glitches and exploits some of which can result in you losing days of work and grind with no way for you to help or sometimes avoid it. Because of the way that the developers have decided that PVP should be played being a defender in raid is usually a disadvantage as the attacker can most often that not win the war of attrition. And because of how long it takes to do absolutely anything within the game and how quickly and easily it is to be destroyed the larger tribes are forced to destroy anyone they meet, often completely locking down entire servers so no one else can join. This problem has now been amplified since the developers allowed for cross server item/player/dinosaur transefers allowing large tribes and alliances to fill a server to capacity, preventing you from coming online to even defend. The end game tier of items and dinosaurs are reserved only for those within the largest of tribes as on official servers the grind required is mind blowing. To stay competetive and to not be overrun by those that abuse the game by exploiting known bugs or outright cheating the larger tribes are forced to partake in those activities too or face losing months of progress. The developers themselves are unable to cope with the number of complaints and as such have now given up on banning the cheaters and exploiters and have gone completely silent on the matter. They release patches everyone couple of weeks but all they contain are more items and dinosaurs, which usually have bugs but are never fixed. The same bugs and balance issues that existed over a year ago still exist today. (some are starting to believe that they don't know how to fix the bugs/exploits.) and they refuse to hire more staff to help moderate their servers or help develop the game.
PVE is in no better state with people being able to glitch and exploit the game to allow them to grief and destroy all your hard work with no repurcussions.
The game cannot be allowed to hide behind the excuse of still being an early access game as they have released the game to consoles and have also released a £15 DLC that adds a new map and new dinosaurs and items that are all locked behind the DLC paywall.
TLDR: Game has huge potential but unfortunetly the developers continue to run the game into the ground allowing cheater to continue to ruin months of hard work and fixing none of the problems that the game has in terms of exploits and bugs, it takes far to long to do anything considering how quickly it is all destroyed. unless you have 50 friends with no life there is no point in  buying this game in its current state. At first, I was quite stunned by this game. It has so many dinos and other prehistoric creatures that I stopped counting. I've spent over 350 hours on this account and over 250 on my friend's account. But this game does come with it's pros and cons.
Pros:
-Endless hours of playtime

-All the DLC are great

Cons:
-Poorly optimized (Low FPS on even a pretty High-end PC)
-One paid DLC while still in early access
-The developers focus more on quantity (amount of dinos) over quality (Fixing the lag)
Overall, I think that the pros outweigh the cons but not by very much. If there was a "Maybe" button then I would've clicked that. This game isn't bad but it still lacks a lot. But I'm still recommending this game for whoever is interested in an open world survival game.

I have 300+ minutes on this game and I can tell you one thing for certain: KEEP UP. This is probably one of the most rapidly changing games probably ever, and with this are some pros and cons.
Pro's:
#1: If you don't like something in game and/or theres a bug about the game, exepect around 2-4 Hotfixes (which are mini updates) to fix them/change them.
#2: This game is LITERALLY 100% NO ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ FREE2PLAY. Cosmetics and looking cool might cost you a tad bit, but its no bank-breaker. Everything in-game (besides vaulted aka not accessable primed things) can be acheived free. Mostly. I probably might be forgetting a few things, and even if those are very significant and will NOT change the gameplay or experience.
#3 The game is very unique with its parkour mechanic. Parkour 1.0 used to have a tribes ascend parkour type feel to it and it was kind of meh, but now with parkour 2.0 you can literally reach any point of the map ever.
#4 Um, space ninjas?
#5 Does NOT require a huge PC to run this game.
Cons:
#1 The community is either super chill or just filled with ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s.
#2 MASTERY RANK DOES NOT EQUAL HOW GOOD YOU ARE AT THE GAME AJKDHGAKMHALKH
#3 Though this game, like listed previously, changes alot, sometimes it changes to a point where it just sucks. For me, the SotR update was abysmal. Like I actually hate the new void system WITH A PATION. Newer players might not get it, and even veteran players prefer it, but I hateeee it.
#4 This game throws you in with NO introduction to ANYTHING. Okay that was a bit exaggerated, but without watching a well-made begginers guide (ID SUGGEST iFlynn's 3.5 BEGGINERS GUIDE) you are basically stranded.
#5 The economic system in this game (The Trade chat) was very nice. You could stack up Trinity P systems, Ash P blueprints, and get hella cash, but now the new void system makes farming SO much more easier so the Trade chat is super messed up (In MY opinion at least) Now you might be thinking this is no issue, but it IS an issue if you try to buy a vaulted Warframe such as Frost or Rhino for example. Their prices might go down because of economic reasons and such but from what i've seen they wont. Because leading to....
#6 A LOT of people who play Warframe are greedy with platinum. I've been scammed multiple times and frankly it sucks. Not a huge issue for veterans or more experienced players, but if you are a new player and just so happened to get Vauban blueprints, some asshat will say its only worth 5 platinum, when its probably worth WAY more.
Another thing about WF too is that alot of people have different opinions and philosophies about how this game is supposed to be played or looked at, and this is my own philosophy. I'd suggest watching gameplay on youtube, reading other comments, and hell just ask people about this game.

I used to play around 6 different games every day. Then I found Warframe. For my first 1,200 hours of playtime I played almost excusively Warframe. Out of the ~250 games I've played, There've only ever been 3 games which have occupied my interest to the point that I play it for hundreds of hours on end without playing anything else. I think after reaching 2,000h of playtime it's about time I wrote a review. Warframe's a fast-paced, horde-based third person shooter. Whether you play this game casually or play like a badass, you'll probably enjoy this game if you enjoy a fast paced movement and combat system supported by great art, UI and an enjoyable non-linear progression system.
Before I played Warframe, I thought calling a game grindy almost objectively made it bad. Turns out I was quite wrong. A grindy game is♥♥♥♥♥♥if you get unsatisfactory rewards for excessive or boring grinding. (that's what she said) Warframe is neither of these, but if you choose to play like that, you absolutely have that option available!  Whether you want to run, jump, and parkour everywhere killing everything that stands in your path, or lie down on your bed for 5 hours with a toggle ability to do everything for you, both work. I've done both plenty of times... I wouldn't say this game is very P2W, but you do get things easier if you just pay. I know plenty of people who've never bought anything in-game who have more or just as much things as I do, however. Making a build for your frames (basically your character; there's 29 right now, all for different situations and stuff) is pretty straight-forward, but you can get fairly in-depth with things if you want to. Platinum (in-game currency) is tradeable, and there is nothing you can buy only with platinum except for cosmetics and some minor things which are supposed to encourage you to trade with other players. The progression in Warframe is definitely not very linear, except for the star-chart. The performance you get with the graphics quality is also very well optimized. Particle effects can be pretty fantastic in Warframe. I'm running this on a GT240 which doesn't even support DX11 on low/medium happily enough. There's plenty of people who run it on worse rigs.  If you enjoy shooters and/or fast-paced games based around acquiring resources and such for progression, I'd absolutely recommend this game.

Warframe,
In 4 months, I dumped 730 hours into this game, playing it every single day, with my Xbox controller. I went over my hourly highest, which was made over a year of gameplay.
Anyways, right off the bat, this game is worth playing.
Its fun with friends, by yourself, and its mostly coop.
There is a lot of content to play with. A lot of weapons to get, warframes to get, different planets to play on, missions.
There is just a lot of things to do in this game before you get bord with it.
I did everything, quests, and missions in, maybe 200 hours.
Now, I will rate this game up, but I'm going to list a few things that bug me. It may seem like I would want to thumbs down this game, but, really, most/all of this is from playing for so long. Any game, even the ones I love most, I find flaws in.
1. Repeating Maps. Even on different planets, the maps were re-used and the same. It gets VERY old with a lot of hours.
2. Devs Nerfing Weapons and Warframes. Early last month, they nerfed Excalibur, and few other things. It really hits players that use those weapons and frames, becuase it takes a long time to get those weps and frames built to be very good.
3. Devs changing the Leveling map. The old leveling mission was Draco. That isn't the same anymore, they also added a distance on the team XP share, which makes it so much harder to level things now, the map to replace Draco is much bigger so that distance come into play. You might not think this is a big deal, but there are over 300 items in the game to level. At least 150 hours of my time was leveling, and that was with double xp. I only did 200 as well.
4. OP Weapons and Warframes. Want to know the best in the game right now? For killing, Ember/Prime and the Synoid Simulor. Use that with Carrier/Prime, and you will easily kill everything in the game, up to level 100s. Nothing will stand in your way. Ash is awesome for higher levels, but Ember is better for lower. The Tonkor/Gernade launcher was the king, it might still be but it took a nerf hit a few weeks ago. I believe there are over 40 warframes in the game. After all my time, I will only use 3 out of all of them. Ember, Ash, Mirage.
5. The sense of balance between you and the AI. From what I've seen, its very lopsided. With what I used to kill with, I would kill everything below level 80, mostly 1 hit them. After 80, everything starts severely turning against you. If your frame isn't built to take hard hits from level 120s, you won't stand a chance, cause you'll get 1 hit. The AI's accuracy is WAYYY too high. They don't miss very often. In the higher levels, the AI's damage is increased, and their health/armor is increasded. When in the higher level range, you have to be using the best weapons and frames in the game to survive. Now, when they start nerfing the best in the game, thats a problem. A very big problem.
6. Grinding. Don't get me started on grinding. Ugh. For some frames and weapons, there are primed versions. Only way to get them, is to grind away, and hope the game gives you a part for a mission reward. That or buy it with platinum, which can be bought with $$$. Each primed version mostly has 3 or 4 parts.
I stopped playing for a while cause of when they changed to this new map. Its really cool, but they changed how you get Primed items in the game. I just didn't want to relearn all of that stuff.
Bottom line, this game is worth putting a few hours in. You can just beat game and move on if you want. This game has its flaws, but not that many. You don't have to unlock everything and grind until you can't anymore.
There are lots of sites out there to help you with every aspect of this game.

Warframe,
In 4 months, I dumped 730 hours into this game, playing it every single day, with my Xbox controller. I went over my hourly highest, which was made over a year of gameplay.
Anyways, right off the bat, this game is worth playing.
Its fun with friends, by yourself, and its mostly coop.
There is a lot of content to play with. A lot of weapons to get, warframes to get, different planets to play on, missions.
There is just a lot of things to do in this game before you get bord with it.
I did everything, quests, and missions in, maybe 200 hours.
Now, I will rate this game up, but I'm going to list a few things that bug me. It may seem like I would want to thumbs down this game, but, really, most/all of this is from playing for so long. Any game, even the ones I love most, I find flaws in.
1. Repeating Maps. Even on different planets, the maps were re-used and the same. It gets VERY old with a lot of hours.
2. Devs Nerfing Weapons and Warframes. Early last month, they nerfed Excalibur, and few other things. It really hits players that use those weapons and frames, becuase it takes a long time to get those weps and frames built to be very good.
3. Devs changing the Leveling map. The old leveling mission was Draco. That isn't the same anymore, they also added a distance on the team XP share, which makes it so much harder to level things now, the map to replace Draco is much bigger so that distance come into play. You might not think this is a big deal, but there are over 300 items in the game to level. At least 150 hours of my time was leveling, and that was with double xp. I only did 200 as well.
4. OP Weapons and Warframes. Want to know the best in the game right now? For killing, Ember/Prime and the Synoid Simulor. Use that with Carrier/Prime, and you will easily kill everything in the game, up to level 100s. Nothing will stand in your way. Ash is awesome for higher levels, but Ember is better for lower. The Tonkor/Gernade launcher was the king, it might still be but it took a nerf hit a few weeks ago. I believe there are over 40 warframes in the game. After all my time, I will only use 3 out of all of them. Ember, Ash, Mirage.
5. The sense of balance between you and the AI. From what I've seen, its very lopsided. With what I used to kill with, I would kill everything below level 80, mostly 1 hit them. After 80, everything starts severely turning against you. If your frame isn't built to take hard hits from level 120s, you won't stand a chance, cause you'll get 1 hit. The AI's accuracy is WAYYY too high. They don't miss very often. In the higher levels, the AI's damage is increased, and their health/armor is increasded. When in the higher level range, you have to be using the best weapons and frames in the game to survive. Now, when they start nerfing the best in the game, thats a problem. A very big problem.
6. Grinding. Don't get me started on grinding. Ugh. For some frames and weapons, there are primed versions. Only way to get them, is to grind away, and hope the game gives you a part for a mission reward. That or buy it with platinum, which can be bought with $$$. Each primed version mostly has 3 or 4 parts.
I stopped playing for a while cause of when they changed to this new map. Its really cool, but they changed how you get Primed items in the game. I just didn't want to relearn all of that stuff.
Bottom line, this game is worth putting a few hours in. You can just beat game and move on if you want. This game has its flaws, but not that many. You don't have to unlock everything and grind until you can't anymore.

First things first I play with intel onboard graphics so my playing experience will differ from others.
I started playing Warframe in 2015 after a friend showed me the game, i can say after almost 700 hours that this is the best free to play game currently on the market, DE have really done well, especially in making this game non pay to win which many other games promote and actively encourage *cough* Call of Duty *cough*.
Regarding my gpu the game often crashes on mission end and i can only load the missions if im not in the warframe window, but by no means does that ruin the fun of this game, the replaybility is endless no matter how many times you have to grind for a certain prime item, no two missions are the same, even boss fights.
Every Frame is unique and offers alternative playstyles for every player, even if they are not that good (hydroid), most frames are available by simply farming bosses, others can be get from quests, alerts and sorties, might aswell mention that my favourite frame is Nova Prime, but as i was saying every frame offers unique gameplay, unlike me though i reccomend playing every frame before you choose a favourite.
As for missions there are a huge variety of missions and map nodes to play (love the new starchart btw, also RIP Draco) there are lots of unique tilesets and due to the level being proceduly generated on every load up hardly any two levels are the same, the quests are also really fun and have interesting stories (War within hype).
Sorry for this generally short and unstructured review, but to write about all the positves and negatives  of this game for me would take a while, but in short I would reccomnd this game to absolutely anyone that games, if you want a fun triple A quality game for free then this is the right game for you!

Feel like playing casually?  Here you go, and you get to blow up everything in the process.  Feel like playing competitively?  There's an entire network of clans and alliances  that are always looking for people.

Do not spend your 50 starter platinum until you know what you are doing. Never rush anything building. And if the game gets boring, back away, take a breather for a while, and try again. If a level seems impossible, you're doing it wrong or too early.

Warframe... Where do I even begin...
The basic concept is a bit cobbled together, as you are essentially a space ninja with guns, swords, and all manners of weapons in-between in a sci-fi world, with mobility and control that I've never seen in other 3rd person shooters. At it's peak, it can be a fight for survival against an invader, or a power fantasy, and you will
be on the move, and looking for ways to navigate the environment faster or more efficiently.
I have had the pleasure of following this game for 3 years now, and I can tell you that if you looked at this game now, and came back 6 months later, some drastic change will have been made, likely for the better. This game is constantly evolving, with new weapons or Warframes to use or master or mechanics being changed or added. There is an update of some kind almost every week, be it for new weapons/Warframes, Cosmetics, Events, or just bugfixes.
Another shining spot on this game is it's community. This is not a community like your Dota's or your CSes, as (With maybe the exception of region chat) the community is more than willing to help you out in missions, and give info if needed. Some of the devs or mods often stop by the relay and chat, as well. You can also build or join a clan and have a massive dojo that can be customised!
I could go on for hours talking about this game, but the main thing you should come away with is that you really should play this game. For veterans, it's still got challenges like Sorties, and for new players, there's many options that you can take, be it collecting parts to powerful Warframes and weapons, taking part in quests, or just clearing the starchart. Find the suit that fits you best in Warframe (In my case, Rhino), and enjoy!

First off, this game IS good! It is fun under the right conditions of play!! I Love ARK and want it to succeed. The price tag is a bit high though, but if your really that tight on money, wait for a sale and get it then. I defeintely got $60 worth out of it.
Pros:
-Ark is a visually beautiful game, provided you have the PC powerful enough to run it. But as of late, it seems even lower spec computers can run it decently well with decent FPS. I only own a 960 graphics card with some slightly high end specs elsewhere (good motherboard, good processor, etc.) and I can get at LEAST 60fps, with the game still looking beautiful.
-The game has so many was to 'customize' your gameplay. THIS is what saves ARK for me really. You wanna play a hard mode with PVP on an official server where other players can reset your progress back to 1? Go ahead, you masocist you. Wanna play solo? There's singleplayer for that! Wanna play on a server that has different rates with mods that can add so much variety? Ark can do that on so many awesome levels! So even if you find the state of offficial servers terrible (and you most likely will, you've been warned...), at least you can avoid it if you are willing to look around for some well maintained, well-admined unofficial servers that can make playing so much more fun. And if looking becomes too tedious, you can always rent your own server for the dream experience.
-The mod community for ARK is one of the best I've seen. If playing vanilla is too rough for you (and it is given how time-demanding it is), then there are hundreds of servers out there that have boosted rates and mods that make things easier for people with jobs or you know...lives. Official servers are VERY time-sink demanding right now, with taming, breeding, and imprinting taking hours to DAYS to complete. So if you have a job or family to care for, I'd say go straight to your own server or another unofficial server and avoid officials.
-It's a game where you tame a bunch of dinos that all have a unique quirk about them. DINOSAURS! And ancient mammals. With the right rates (not-official, you'll hear me say that a lot), you can look forward to having tons of fun using over 100 different kinds of well animated and fun mounts.
-The music is beautiful. Nuff said.
Cons:
-Yes there are bugs. But none extremely game-breaking. If anything you might run into a random small bug. But at the moment, the biggest issue is duping on officials and raiding from under the map. If you avoid officials, your fine, but Wildcard is slowly adding ways to counter duping, so even this isn't a huge deal, and the problem is non-existant on unofficials.
-The game is heavily catering to PVP official, aka the developers vision of the game. PVE takes a bit of a hit with patches that 'balance' things for the PVPers of Ark official, which sucks hard for those PVE official players. Again you can work around them as long as you play unofficial and use mods to 'restore' what you didn't like changed, but the fact that their Official vision of the game is so unbalanced, unfun, and catered to so much that they have ignored other possibilities is very disappointing. And it's even more dissappointing that you need to play unofficial to even enjoy the game.
Even with the unpleasant nerfs and the fact that I had ot avoid their own vision to enjoy the game fully, this game is STILL one of, if not THE most favorite game I own in the library. The developers have put so much time and effort into this game, and it shows how attentive they are with their updates and content additions. They are a talented bunch of content makers yes, though their optimizations and sense of 'balance' for PVP has a lot to be desired. If you have been eyeing this game for a while and still find the concept of taming dino's to kill other things with, and you don't mind taking some time to find a good server for yourself and your friends, then you will probably get $60 worth of fun out of this game! But you will probably ONLY get $60 of fun out of it if you play singpleplayer, or an unofficial server with rates catered to your playstyle, unless you are a masocist...in which case, go play somethign else cause you are not welcomed here. The official servers to this game are cancer, are barely ever tended to by the devs,the early game on officials for new players on PVP servers is TERRIBLE due to alpha tribes jsut curb stomping any new player they find, and if this is what WC is baking on in hopes their game will succeed, they are sadly mistaken. They will see eventually that Ark's playbase isn't hiding in the bushes of it's PVP servers.
I can recommend this game, even at $60, but a wise person will still wait for a sale. If you hold interest in a survival game, where you enjoy the challenge of risking losing everything from other players (PVP), or you enjoy taming, breeding, raising, and being social with your dinos and other players (PVE), then this game is for you.

The optimization of the game is absolutely awful. All servers I've tested lag to no end, and rubberbanding is a constant nuisance. Picking up a lot of items at once can cause a disconnect, so good luck recovering your items from a dangerous place. You're likely dead again when you log in.
The devs seem to be busy adding new stuff into the game before fixing stuff that already is broken. And Implement patches that break stuff that previously was working. The QA team is either not doing their job or is absolutely incompetent. Or doesn't even exist.
Building is a big part of the game, and contributes to the god-awful performance. Tribes can and will build massive square boxes that should by any real physics collapse on themselves and form a sphere due to their insane mass. Not to mention these square trashcans are on the beaches where people spawn, and woe unto you if you happen to spawn inside one. There is often no way out, other than waiting to die out of starvation. There is no unstuck command, on PVE servers you can't even damage yourself by hitting the walls, and if there is no pet dinos around, you can't even poison yourself by eating their feces. Yes, that really is a thing in this game. Oh, there was a suicide command, but devs removed it since it didn't "feel realistic" in a game where humans armed with rocket launchers ride dinosaurs armed with laser cannons.
The building system itself is finicky, wasteful and frustrating. But that won't be fixed because there is no real wow factor in it. They need to get more dinos in the game.
And the excuse of game being in early access doesn't really work, since they already have released paid DLC for the game, and that DLC required them making even more creatures and other assets, instead of fixing the broken stuff.

Instead of trying to make this review a complicated 3 paragraph review, I'll just stick with Pros and Cons.
Pros:
-Good Story
-Each of the three different starter armor types make the game feel much different gameplay wise, and are different from the default types most games go with (Balenced, speedy, strong)
-Looks awesome. Lighting, muzzle flashes and the animations feel mostly on point.
-Like to have lots of weapons and armor types to choose from? *BOOM* There ya go.
-Many mods with different effects to choose from. Will change the expreince in ways that are noticable.
Cons:
-Takes quite alot of Platinum to get the really good goods, which means lots of real money, which means lots of sad.
-A few of the different frames can make certain missions or underwhelming or totally overwhelming.
-PvP? Nothing all that exciting. Lots of weapons become instagibs. I would prefer some change here.
And that's all I got. Should you play it? Sure, if you like to run on walls and jump around while shooting at stuff, go right ahead. Even though Platinum can be a pain in the wallet, some of the frames you can get look AWESOME and can definetly be fun to play with.

I used to play around 6 different games every day. Then I found Warframe. For my first 1,200 hours of playtime I played almost excusively Warframe. Out of the ~250 games I've played, There've only ever been 3 games which have occupied my interest to the point that I play it for hundreds of hours on end without playing anything else. I think after reaching 2,000h of playtime it's about time I wrote a review. Warframe's a fast-paced, horde-based third person shooter. Whether you play this game casually or play like a badass, you'll probably enjoy this game if you enjoy a fast paced movement and combat system supported by great art, UI and an enjoyable non-linear progression system.
Before I played Warframe, I thought calling a game grindy almost objectively made it bad. Turns out I was quite wrong. A grindy game is♥♥♥♥♥♥if you get unsatisfactory rewards for excessive or boring grinding. (that's what she said) Warframe is neither of these, but if you choose to play like that, you absolutely have that option available!  Whether you want to run, jump, and parkour everywhere killing everything that stands in your path, or lie down on your bed for 5 hours with a toggle ability to do everything for you, both work. I've done both plenty of times... I wouldn't say this game is very P2W, but you do get things easier if you just pay. I know plenty of people who've never bought anything in-game who have more or just as much things as I do, however. Making a build for your frames (basically your character; there's 29 right now, all for different situations and stuff) is pretty straight-forward, but you can get fairly in-depth with things if you want to. Platinum (in-game currency) is tradeable, and there is nothing you can buy only with platinum except for cosmetics and some minor things which are supposed to encourage you to trade with other players. The progression in Warframe is definitely not very linear, except for the star-chart. The performance you get with the graphics quality is also very well optimized. Particle effects can be pretty fantastic in Warframe. I'm running this on a GT240 which doesn't even support DX11 on low/medium happily enough. There's plenty of people who run it on worse rigs.  If you enjoy shooters and/or fast-paced games based around acquiring resources and such for progression, I'd absolutely recommend this game.
