Don't buy into this early access nonsense. There is no reason why they can't label this games as a full game. Just becuase you update the game with a new dinosaur everyonce in awhile doesn't mean its early access. All games get updates and patches that does not mean you are still "develoeping." Simply holding on to EA so there is not commitment to finishing the game or quality content. Terrible patch/update? "It's EA we are still working things out"
As for the game itself:
PVP: If you were ever curious what the most cancerous community of server overlords and chinese warmongerers this side of the milky way looked like, search no further than ark official pvp servers.
PVE: So pvp wasn't for you? Trying an official PVE server? Enjoy trying to find the singular inch on the map you can place a campfire, because you bet everyone else on the server needs to spam pillars across the map to insure their city sized dominion for their tribe of two players is protected because they plan on "expanding, and building things."
Before you criticize, I have hundreds of hours of ARK on Xbox. And I wasn't some struggling "thatch hut peasant" either. I was in a tribe only second to the alpha tribe (who were are allies) on the server with around 10-12 members, plenty of allies, and so many dinosaurs that it probably lowered everyone on the servers FPS by 5. With plenty of allies around the map we were doing well and prospering. But when you get established the game just becomes boring, logging on every day or so to do the chores (get metal, feed dinos, hunt meat, fertilize turrets and crops, and other the other "thrilling" things that make up ARK) Then one day we log on naked on the beach, where our fortress of steel, gun turrets, and teeth once stood was the smoldering remains of months of work, all that was left some building tiles laying around. Not a single dino was spared. Why did this happen? Who could have done this? Guess what, the alpha tribe (again, they were "allies") got bored  because there wasn't really a lot of fighting going on around the server. So they got a couple of guys and while we were all offline "raided" us. In one night months of spending time grinding away on ARK were wiped away. That's what your time and money investment gets you in ARK. A big F*** you from WildCard and ARK. After that, we all quit ark and no one has played since.
So TLDR: Don't waste your time, it's absolutelty not worth it.

-Game is far too repetitive and doesnt have much going for it other than the weapons.
-This game revolves around the "grind for hours on end to make 1 to 2 things" formula
-Having to wait 8 to 78 hours (real time) to make just 1 item is absurd and to think they wanted me to pay real money for in-game currency to shorten that time is terrible. Acts like a phone game.
-Melee is completely thoughtless it is just mash E until the enemy is dead and there is no form of strategy
-The guns are cool but take hours and some might take days to make. Also there could have been many more creative weapons especially more creative silent weapons other than the generic throwing knives and bows (which are actually the only silent weapons in the game. There are no silent guns or silent lasers that I know of.)
-The mods are cool although i wish there was a larger variety of mods instead of getting the same duplicates over and over
-Grinding was a pain because you would be doing different mission types but on the same map for each planet
-Stealth is only sub-par since the ai is blind and crouching is %100 pointless
-Stealth is not very rewarding due to no sneak dmg bonus or anything exciting
-Game is EXTREMLY glitchy and I exited the map multiple times within the first hour of playing.
-Dead bodies constanly glitch around from weapons with a large amount of impact
-The AI moves in such a poor pattern it is the equivalent of fighting mindless zombies. (there is no thought to them) I went against the AI they would take cover in plain sight. Some would run into walls. Some would be turned around starting at a wall while I was sneaking around. Some would slowly walk straight towards me or even avoid the "strength in numbers" tactic. In games like this I want AI that is difficult because they are naturally difficult and not be difficult just because they are leveled up above the player.
-The game controls feel completely off with the keyboard but they dont feel much better with a controller either. I constantly found myself adjusting the controls and sensitivity just to get the right feeling but even then it felt like my mouse was on a slip and slide.
-The Warframes seemed to be really cool being able to cusomize the colors and all but note that ALL (but about 16 colors) were behind some form of pay wall. Even simple colors like black and white needed real money to be obtained.
-The three factions were pretty different from each other but the infested seemed a bit too easy.
-The small amount of pvp that I did felt completly meaningless although it was functional all I obtained were credits and no crafting materials. Not only that but there seemed to be nobody playing it unless it was because of my low ranking but even then I should have been able to find more than 1 game.
-There are limited inventory slots for weapons and warframes (armor) but the free inventory is super small and wants real money to be expanded to a thoughtful size.
-The community seemed to be mostly clean although I did not see many people typing in the regional and recruiting chat but I don't really think that can be judged or anything especially since I do not know the games playerbase. The only issue with the community is 1 guy that wanted to power level me from level 1 to whatever when I was still in my first hour of gameplay. Then he wouldn't leave me alone until I blocked him.

This game is rather diffifult to get into. Seriously difficult to get into. While the entire game is free there isn't much of a hook to guide you like most triple A games. While I do hope that they refine the experience for new players and at least have a lure to keep you interested and curious. (lure as in something for you to chase or keep your attention.)
after the first quest your kind of left hung up to dry and thrown into the vast world of warframe. granted there are wiki's but Digital Extreme should seriously put a little more effort in helping you see more of their world at a steady pace. I don't expect a full fledged amazing story but something that would introduce the guilds you can join, more info on corpus and the infested along with the orokin and also who the heck you are as a "Tenno". Granted there is an introduction quest but it's so hyperfocused, streamlined and goes by way too fast. granted there is a bit of a hurry up element in the quest but for real.
People say that the game starts to get seriously good when you hit Uranus and I think it's because of the quest called the Second Dream. I haven't realy gotten to that point but I have been grinding away for quite some time as getting powerful is kind of a chore.
The main leveling system in this game is Mods and the way you use them determins how strong you are. Area's that say enemy lvl 20 or something only pertains to their difficulty. not how strong you should be. You won't know if your strong enough till you try. seriously, either you are seriously powerfull or you will die really fast it's one or the other. There isn't a challenge in difficulty, the challenge is the grind and thats about it. It sounds like I'm doking the game points for this but honestly it's more of a frustration. My only challenge is grinding and it only gets me so far especially when you mow through thousands of units making the gameplay feels dull after a while or you get mowed yourself feeling utterly weak and rage. It doesn't feel like theres a true gameplay challenge :(
Microtransactions. Of course these people need to have some sort of income. Granted I'm not really all that about the crazy grind this game has but the grind does respect you and your time. I've already invested 150$ in the span of 3 years which would have been 300$ if it weren't for the discounts they give you from time to time. The things I purchased immediatly was color pallets and got 2 weapons if I remember properly. granted I got me a warframe, as well as a bunch of mods packs. (aka lootboxes, be careful those are easily addicted)
There isn't an item you can't reach and granted you can purchase them with premium currency (platinum) you'll probably get to your goal in respectable time. overall the time dedication isn't really egregious. Especially considering that you will have multiple things you'll chase after within the game. The one thing your most likely going to chase is warframes. it's what changes the gameplay up but minorly. you get new powers and your stats change which requires you to play the game in different style. I bought Nezha with Platinum and I found out that he is good when constantly moving and can be pretty lethal. Also I had to change my mods to accompany the frame, aka make my powers stronger and last longer. the same applies to weapons as well. it's best to figure out the best way to optimize weapons of your choice. Though what sucks is that you can't keep a weapon that you really like, as it's very likely to be too weak to use further into the game.
Lore is gotten by scanning enemies and there is plenty of that but I'd just recommend equipping your sentinal with the scan mod so you don't have to spend an absured amount of time scanning. Hopefully they make some missions so that you can get some lore through that instead of just scans.
Overall the game is worth a try. I know free to play puts people off but this game does have a lot to offer and is probably known to be the best free to play game in the entire business of free to play. I expect most of you to fall off but I would suggest giving this game a DEEP dive (checking guilds, make a list of stuff to go after, figure out enemy weaknesses, how to best optomize your warframe and weapons, etc). not just dipping your toes in (doing missions and not much else). otherwise your going to find the game rather dull really quick.

Caution: Overly detailed, so I am very sorry
So I've been playing this game for about 3 years now, and this has easily become one of my most played games that I own. Not even exclusive to steam. Warframe is a game that takes place in space, where you take control of a 'Tenno', which is the faction/race of everyone else that plays. What is a Tenno? Well... play for yourself, and you'll find out with time. -wink-
"What is a Warframe?"
Warframes are the battle-suits that you control. You walk as them, you fight as them, you hang out as them...you pretty much ARE the Warframe. (Yes, I told you that you are a Tenno as well. Like I said, it's just a suit. It's complicated.) There are currently 29 different Warframes to collect/build and use, each with their own unique set of flashy abilities. I say 'currently' because the development team behind this game are constantly working on it and sending out updates (also, one of the most enjoyable development teams I've ever seen, tbh), and the community helps shape the game greatly.
Anyhow, the Warframes are battle-suits for a reason. In this game, you are a freaking ninja, in probably the most ninja way possible. From wall jumps, slides, air-kicks, backflips, gliding, rolling, super jumps, throwing stars, dual daggers, etc.. You name it, it's probably possible. There is so much movement and control, you can fly through areas like a breeze if you get the hang of the movement system. There is also so much customization in this game. Assault rifles, rocket launchers, bows, crossbows, sniper rifles, shotguns, laser-beams, sawblade launchers, wormhole creators, grenade launchers, laser cannons, lightning shooters, gas cloud launchers, laser-rifles, infested growth that shoots bullets and grappling hooks, freeze-rays, and much more. Also, most of what I just listed are primary weapons, meaning you ALSO have secondary weapons, which are your sidearms, and melee weapons. There are an equal amount of interesting categories for sidearms, but if you are an in-your-face type of player, then enjoy your collection of melee weapons, including single swords, dual swords, katanas, daggers, glaives, bo staffs, polearms, hammers, axes, whips, whip/blade combos, energy-blades--well, you get the point by now. There are many skins for your weapons and your warframes as well. Another thing that heavily affects customization is the fact that you can color anything that you own, from warframes, weapons, companions (little robotic fellows that float behind you with their own supportive abilities..or, you know, a cat or a dog.), armor pieces and scarfs (this game is called Fashionframe by the community for a reason), and even your own ship.
Your ship serves as your personal hub, where you can access the star chart for missions, your arsenal, your foundry (for building weapons, warframes, gear, and everything else), your mods, and more. What are mods? Mods are these little cards that drop from enemies in the game, some mods being specific to certain enemies. They also have tiers of rarity. Anyway, mods are a very important feature, and are used for upgrading your warframes and weapons. There are hundreds of different mods, ranging from additional health percentages, additional damage, elemental damage (which you can mix different elements to form new elements, might I add), ability range, and just...pretty much anything you need to help you progress and spice up the gameplay a bit more. Want a silenced loadout for stealth? There are mods for that. Screw stealth, you want explosions? Mods.
"Who are the bad guys?"
There are a handful of different factions in the game, mostly all of them against the Tenno.
There are the Grineer, who are crude, ugly, bulky clones of other Grineer, made to produce a massive army. Usually found in their battleships, or their own settlements, destroying the planet's landscape with machinery. They look dumb, but can be pretty tough.
Another faction is the Corpus, who are driven by greed. They are more technologically advanced than the Grineer, using robotics, drones, and lasers in their favor.
The Infested is another faction. They are...a bit of a mess. Disgusting heaps and masses of flesh, screeching as they charge to attack. They are basically zombified, destroyed forms of Grineer and Corpus, but you really don't see them that way, considering how mutilated they become. They don't have much of a role other than to spread the virus, and, most importantly, kill you.
There are a couple of other factions, but they are a bit spoiler-y, so I'll avoid talking about them.
"Why are we doing any of this in the first place?"
Because Space-mom tells you to, and you must listen to Space-mom.
"....who tf is space-mom?"
Upon the Tenno's awakening, you are contacted by a mysterious woman by the name of Lotus, who first appears to be an AI of sorts, although taking a humanoid form. You have no memory of anything before this 'awakening', so you should probably listen to her.
She guides and cares for the entire Tenno faction, alerting them of dangers and important events happening throughout the solar system. She is your leader.
"So what is the main objective, overall?" +bonus info i dont know where to fit otherwise
Really, it's anything you want. A lot of players get lost because they don't know what they should be doing, but you are just supposed to make your own personal missions, which you can invite friends to. Also, this is a very heavy co-op based game, so have as much fun as you want with up to 4 players in a squad (or up to 8 in raid missions). You can play this game completely solo if you want, of course. It will be pretty challenging, though.
So let's start from a new players point-of-view. You have unlocked your first planet. You can continue to do the mission-nodes that it has to offer, all the way up to the planet boss. Each planet also has a newly-added feature, which are known as Junctions. Junctions are what players have to go through to get to the next planet, and will offer a variety of trials before passage. Upon completing a Junction, you are rewarded with a few things, such as blueprints for weapons, a few parts for building a few specific warframes, and they will unlock quests. Quests are side-things that you can do, which also give you some rewards. There are a handful of warframes that are quest-exclusive if you want to obtain them, as well as some helpful items to assist you along the way. Another recent addition (as in since December) are Cinematic Quests. These are main story-related quests that have cutscenes, and usually have a lot to reveal about the lore, and will unlock some other nice things (You still have to unlock these quests from Junctions, or even just through the market.) The in-game market shows mostly all of everything you can get in the game. The best part? You can get most of this for free! Of course you can add money to just BUY weapons, warframes, gear, companions, etc., and gain access to them immediately, but this is not a pay-to-win game. Not at all. It's more of a 'pay-to-progress-faster' game. However, building these things by yourself without paying any real currency can be a fun time-consuming process. The word Fun can be taken literally or sarcastically in this subject, depending on what the building requirements are, for what you are making. You gather resources to build and complete these things from different planets throughout the solar system, each having their own set of different resources. They drop from enemies, loot lockers, and storage containers (there is even a warframe that increases loot drops, while simutaneously punching souls and raising the dead!). Also, you can earn the real-money currency in this game by trading with other players. I'm out of space at this point, but all I have to say is I wish more of my friends could get into this.

Holy Heavens above! It's my first review! I woke up at 1:44 in the bloody morning waiting for my friend, (who wasn't going to be on till 3:00.) and decided that I was going to write a review on the game we would play.
Ok! Let's start with the cons:
1. As my friend always says, welcome to RNG worshipping town. Prepare to put weeks into that shiny new warframe.
2. All those FashionPrimes out there are flat broke. Cosmetics come at a price. Real money.
3. If you are trying to be a lone wolf with absolutely NO friends... you are going to have a bad time.
4. Despite the above statements, addicting as all Hades. IF you have a squad. Say goodbye to your jobs!
So that seems bad, right? Course it does! You haven't even seen the good stuff yet!
Pros:
1. Even a team of 2 people playing every-so-often makes this game a heckuva lot more fun to play. And the built in clan system makes it easy to turn that fireteam of 5 or so into a well of benefits.
2. Have 3 or more groups of friends who really don't feel like tearing down their clans to join yours? Make an alliance! More benefits!
3. I have seen many a review saying new players are doomed. My personal opinion ( and most likely that of my mates) says that is only true if you are alone. You seeing a trend yet?
4. Warframes and weapons are well varied, stated, and interesting. And the steam workshop gives the FashionPrimes a new style to blow money on every once in a while.
5. THE DEVS ARE STILL HERE!
6. Lore is nice and colorful. Storyline is linear, but only when you want it to be. Those planets aren't going anywhere...
7. Community is nice and very helpful. If the locals won't help right away, there is always the guides of the lotus. It's their job to help you.
I could go on. I really could. I am a mastery rank 5. I plan to continue. Please come join us.

Warframe is not only one of the greatest free-to-play games ever made, it's also probably one of the most under-appreciated games available today, period.
From its initial ease of use to the almost inexhaustible depth to which you can explore its myriad and increadibly detailed character development mechanics.
In addition to this extreme "value for money" one can also certainly consider it to be one of the best examples of delivering a fluid and powerful movement system into an FPS. You manage to feel both increadibly powerful and yet, if you are playing the harder parts of the game, also very, very fragile. This balance is delivered in such a polished way that one hopes all, so called, "triple-A" titles can spend some time learning from DE in this regard.
I would consider this a "Must Play" title for any serious Action Game fan. Particularly if you enjoy "unlocking" / "collecting" as, in that regard, Warframe offers you hundreds, if not thousands, of hours of fun!

In my time playing Fashionframe i've learned a great many things, and the single most important advice I could pass on is this; play to your liking. Unlike many classic MMO's who have a "best gear in game" Warframe is all situational, and there is no such thing as a "best in slot" in this game.
-This game is progression based, and has a wide variety of asthetic customization based on how you'd like to play.
-You choose the weapons you want to work with, and customize them with collectable Mods to fit your need.
-29 (soon to be 30 as of 7/24/16) different Warframes to choose from, not counting Prime variants separately. All greatly unique from each other and offering different gameplay styles.
-Color palettes for customization are locked behind a small pay-wall climbable with in-game effort; no money actually spent unless you choose to. (Look up Player Trading, and Void Rewards for more info on this.)
-Regular daily login bonuses can return resources, new Blueprints, and 25%+ discounts on Platinum currency packs if you do choose to buy into it, you can in fact wait for a better deal. (That mythical 75% is bae.)
-New forms of PVP recently added whether you are the competitive head to head fighter (Conclave) or the co-operative sportsy type (Lunaro) there is something for everyone.
The long and short of it is this; the game looks massive to newcomers, and that's because it is. DE strives to keep things moving and to keep it fresh for everyone involved. If you haven't tried the game before and you're curious to try it, it's a Free to Play for a reason. Come and join in, and ask around the Region chat for some help if you get lost. There will always be a few helpful souls waiting to help out.

This game is hands down my favorite game. The gameplay is exciting, fun, and rewarding. But it has its issues.
The game requires a large time commitment. People often give a full night's rest just to raise a new dino.
The game is still in alpha, so it has bugs and issues, none of which are currently being fixed because of the development cycle.
The official servers are terrible. Abandoned bases everywhere drives up your lag, griefers and raiders roam around constantly, and any tribe on official can server hop. So, all the servers are basically at war with each other. All of that can be fun, but there is a work around, in unofficial servers.
Let's get to the good stuff though.
The development team is hands down my favorite. They are highly involved in making the game better. adding new creatures, adding new features, recently they began reworking the original creatures to bring them in line with the newer ones. They even started a huge balance sweep. Nerfing the Flyers, a much needed change.
Recently, the development team has made some controversial changes to the game, that have upset a large portion of the community. These changes largely do not affect no players, but one does. Server transfers enabled aggressive tribes to roam about, and attack any tribe they want, big or small. So threats can come from unknown places now. Frankly, I'd suggest unofficial servers. They do have this issue.
Take the current reviews with a grain of salt, people are angry. It's the internet after all. I'd still recommend the game without hestitation

-Game is far too repetitive and doesnt have much going for it other than the weapons.
-This game revolves around the "grind for hours on end to make 1 to 2 things" formula
-Having to wait 8 to 78 hours (real time) to make just 1 item is absurd and to think they wanted me to pay real money for in-game currency to shorten that time is terrible. Acts like a phone game.
-Melee is completely thoughtless it is just mash E until the enemy is dead and there is no form of strategy
-The guns are cool but take hours and some might take days to make. Also there could have been many more creative weapons especially more creative silent weapons other than the generic throwing knives and bows (which are actually the only silent weapons in the game. There are no silent guns or silent lasers that I know of.)
-The mods are cool although i wish there was a larger variety of mods instead of getting the same duplicates over and over
-Grinding was a pain because you would be doing different mission types but on the same map for each planet
-Stealth is only sub-par since the ai is blind and crouching is %100 pointless
-Stealth is not very rewarding due to no sneak dmg bonus or anything exciting
-Game is EXTREMLY glitchy and I exited the map multiple times within the first hour of playing.
-Dead bodies constanly glitch around from weapons with a large amount of impact
-The AI moves in such a poor pattern it is the equivalent of fighting mindless zombies. (there is no thought to them) I went against the AI they would take cover in plain sight. Some would run into walls. Some would be turned around starting at a wall while I was sneaking around. Some would slowly walk straight towards me or even avoid the "strength in numbers" tactic. In games like this I want AI that is difficult because they are naturally difficult and not be difficult just because they are leveled up above the player.
-The game controls feel completely off with the keyboard but they dont feel much better with a controller either. I constantly found myself adjusting the controls and sensitivity just to get the right feeling but even then it felt like my mouse was on a slip and slide.
-The Warframes seemed to be really cool being able to cusomize the colors and all but note that ALL (but about 16 colors) were behind some form of pay wall. Even simple colors like black and white needed real money to be obtained.
-The three factions were pretty different from each other but the infested seemed a bit too easy.
-The small amount of pvp that I did felt completly meaningless although it was functional all I obtained were credits and no crafting materials. Not only that but there seemed to be nobody playing it unless it was because of my low ranking but even then I should have been able to find more than 1 game.
-There are limited inventory slots for weapons and warframes (armor) but the free inventory is super small and wants real money to be expanded to a thoughtful size.
-The community seemed to be mostly clean although I did not see many people typing in the regional and recruiting chat but I don't really think that can be judged or anything especially since I do not know the games playerbase. The only issue with the community is 1 guy that wanted to power level me from level 1 to whatever when I was still in my first hour of gameplay. Then he wouldn't leave me alone until I blocked him.
-Note that I only played for 24 hours and did not discover everything in the game.I also did not pay any real money.This review is just a hint on what you might encounter after your first few hours of gameplay.
---Overall

This game is hands down my favorite game. The gameplay is exciting, fun, and rewarding. But it has its issues.
The game requires a large time commitment. People often give a full night's rest just to raise a new dino.
The game is still in alpha, so it has bugs and issues, none of which are currently being fixed because of the development cycle.
The official servers are terrible. Abandoned bases everywhere drives up your lag, griefers and raiders roam around constantly, and any tribe on official can server hop. So, all the servers are basically at war with each other. All of that can be fun, but there is a work around, in unofficial servers.
Let's get to the good stuff though.
The development team is hands down my favorite. They are highly involved in making the game better. adding new creatures, adding new features, recently they began reworking the original creatures to bring them in line with the newer ones. They even started a huge balance sweep. Nerfing the Flyers, a much needed change.
Recently, the development team has made some controversial changes to the game, that have upset a large portion of the community. These changes largely do not affect no players, but one does. Server transfers enabled aggressive tribes to roam about, and attack any tribe they want, big or small. So threats can come from unknown places now. Frankly, I'd suggest unofficial servers. They do have this issue.
Take the current reviews with a grain of salt, people are angry. It's the internet after all. I'd still recommend the game without hestitation

so, where should i start?
i played the game for over 1600 hours according to steam. I come back from time to time to check for updates and new content.
to put things in a nutshell,you are a space ninja. (a warframe) and you have to kill the bad guys, basically. you can do crazy tricks like walljumping and bullet jumping. each warframe comes with their own unique abilities, looks and aesthatics. want to be a swamp monster?no problem. want to be a mummy? no problem. want to be a pink colored sassy pseudo body builder?no problem.
i love a LOT of things in this game. but that doesn't mean the game comes without it's flaws.
so here's a couple of pros and cons;
-Pro's-
-A lot of class diversity
-A huge variation of weapons
-A lot of customization on both frames and weapons
-The game offers interesting co-op gameplay
-The devs listen to their players
-Both great artistic and unique tilesets and npc's
-Companions :D (cats dogs and small flying robots)
-Devs do weekly platinum givaways (ingame currency)
-Red text <3
-One of the lesser toxic communites out there
-F2P!
-#Fashionframe
-Weekly (mostly interesting) devstreams
-Cons-
-Very Few and kind of repetetive mission types
-The community doesn't tend to take criticism too lightly
-Not a whole lot of content to go through
-There's no real endgame (especially after spectres of the rails launched)
-A LOT of RNG based farming (it's basically the main drive for the game)
-Unbalanced pvp
-It can take up to 3 days to craft new items
-The game wont pose a challenge at all after after you get some of the less basic stuff
-Leechers
-A lot of bugs...
-Clunky interfaces
-Today's strongest weapon is tomorrow's mastery fodder
Know that the game is still in beta and receives monthly updates.
The devs put a lot of work and effort in the game.
So obviously some of the pro's and con's might shift a little over time.
I dont think there's a whole lot more to say.
All in all, not a bad game.
The game is worth to give a try at the very least.

I enjoyed the game a lot at first. Now, not so much. Read below to see why
--- Original game---
The original game was by far the best design. Challenging but logical in approach. They really strived to bring realism to the game in everything including fatigue, thirst, hunger, building and crafting. This is what hooked me for as long as I've played. In fact I had a dedicated server running for my family and a few friends to play whenever we were up to it.
The down side with the original was the amount of time and energy required to do anything. Setting a 2x to 3x multiplier fixes a lot of the slowness and makes the game a more enjoyable experience.  Especially after you've leveled up enough that constant death is no longer a concern.
~~~ Scorched Earth ~~~
This to me is where the game began going down hill. They took away a lot of was was good with the original by just making things harder, because. For example, a canteen that I have used in real life, in extreme desert circumstances, is your life blood and can even remain cold for a number of hours without much help. Well, in SE, your canteen leaks out water, because its harder. That's it. They repeat the same "because its harder" approach in a number of other areas as well which personally is just obnoxious, not fun.
~~~~   Flier Changes ~~~~~  ~~~~ Final Remarks ~~~~~
So you've read a number of reviews here regarding this already. I see the reasoning behind them locking movement speed to 100%, (realism and PvP balancing), yet they lost the RPG aspect in flying units that made them not only fun, but key to single players and small 4 to 10 man private servers as my own. Instead of being able to fly to gather supplies to quickly bring them back to your main base, you now have to spend 2 to 3 times as much time traveling to accomplish the same thing.  The solution is to go into the workshop and download a 3rd party revert. But the biggest issue is that we have to use a 3rd party to begin with to fix something that should have been optional. There are a lot of customizable items in the game on the server end, this should have been a simple True / False command line to enable / disable the feature. That would have saved a lot of headaches and kept from♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off large amounts of the community.  Sadly I have to agree, the game has gotten worse with age, not better. My play time is quite limited now as I no longer find it an enjoyable experience. The only time I actually play is when my children ask me to join them. Then I only do it for them, not because its fun.
UPDATE: I've edited to give the base game a thumbs up and a not recommended for Scorched Earth expansion.

Neutral

Cons

Overall I find it to be a fun game, but it can get boring after a certain point.

)

Updated 2/6. Warframe now makes a third of my holy trinity of looter-shooter timesucks, alongside The Division and Destiny, but possibly the longest lasting passion of all three. I am experiencing an interesting quirk of engagement; now that the rush for gear and mastery ranks is done, I'm getting back to the point where I pick frames and gear because they're genuinely enjoyable to play, not because I'm trying to burn through mastery fodder or theroycraft another forma into a Tonkor. The core gameplay loop of Warframe remains fun after nearly 1000 hours, and that's a notable achievement in my book - tl;dr I highly reccomend this game.
Positives -
+ Fun. Period. The core gameplay is fast paced, exhilarating, and lets you feel like a friggin' space ninja. Total power-fantasy wish-fufuillment.
+ Variety in gameplay is astounding. Nearly every weapon handles uniquely, and every Warframe is a new experience that goes beyond tradtional RPG class archetypes.
+ Parkour system is what Mirror's Edge should aspire to. Though the learning curve is steep, the skill ceiling is astronomical, and after months of play I feel like I am only just getting a handle on the true power of in-game movement. It's thrilling to move this fast.
+ Incredible and unique art design. I don't know if I have any kind of easy comparison visually to Warframe - organic influences like insects and lotus petals are crossed with eastern-influenced modern design and minimalist geometry? This game also looks incredible from low-end to high-end machines. The PhysX particle effects make me feel warm & fuzzy on the inside.
+ Warframe is full of surprises. It is absolutely worth prioritizing getting to the quest known as The Second Dream. Do not spoil yourself in the process if at all possible.
+ Mastery Rank system level-up tests - not a big thing, but a great mechanic that reminds me of my old Taekwondo exams. The high stakes nature of every test (one try per day, and when you're power-levelling, a day feels like forever) makes them a consistent adrenal rush.
+ Contrary to popular opinion, I think the Archwing vehicle sections are incredibly fun, especially after the last patch (incomplete tho it may be). Again, power-fantasy wish-fufillment is why I'm here, and AW delivers.
+ F2P design is secretly brilliant. While the core is obvious and effective (buy premium currency, spend premium currency on item slots/cosmetics/skipping grinds for an item/skipping build times), the true power comes from the market trading system. Via out-of-game websites, and subtle checks, balances, and taxes, you are able to broker a sale for the vast majority of your somewhat-rare items, and recieve premium currency in return. This makes the value of farming for rare and powerful item components extremely valid, because at any given point you could get a blueprint on a mission that is worth dozens (if not hundreds) of platinum. All it takes is a little time, effort, and a google search for "warframe market".
(Please also remember that this coming from an EVE nerd, for better and for worse, so I find the economic model in Warframe usually non-problematic - as if you are really bothered by the grinding cost of any given item, you can just sell crap until you have enough plat, without paying a cent. The free market at work. Beautiful.)
Negatives -
- Confusing state of affairs to get going as a new player. The Warframe Wikia should honestly be embedded in-game if the complex/robust systems will not be explained otherwise. The lack of hand-holding was rewarding and entertaining for me personally, but there were a couple of moments where I almost felt "cheated" by investments of time and effort into mechanics that weren't well-explained (i.e. Kubrows, not knowing about methods of acquiring Prime weapons).
- Alternately, very easy to get into a hazardous feedback loop of min-maxing as a semi-new player. The game is a captial-G Grind, however it is only via awareness of said Grind via a desire to min-max stats and hunt for specific items, that the Grind becomes a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥
- A split in design philosophy. The irony is that min-maxing -is not necessary- to enjoy the game, and in fact most of the game's content can be beaten with weapons chosen for style and flavor than destructive functionality. As in, the devs say; play the game to have fun, go for it, you'll be OP and crush everything anyway. Cool, right? However, the game also contains certain types of playstyles and encounters that absolutely require modding/cheese/more-than-reasonable-replay-of-the-same-goddamn-mission/horrific-bloody-grinds-for-fusion-cores. DOUBLE however, this kind of high-level content is also tailored towards veteran players, and there is a sense that the developers aren't sure how to please a certain tier of player. AKA...
- An underlying sense that the developers keep biting off slightly more than they can chew. I.E. current patch is on Hotfix 12 with some major bugs unresolved, Lunaro gameplay mode at launch being basically non-functional, dated game mechanics poking out in weird and awkward ways (like the Relays/underwater AW/Conclave PvP), etc. I confess to being somewhat apprehensive about the next major Update based on the current run of bugs.
- A definite feeling that the goalposts are moving for the acquisition of gear & levelling up. Given that many veteran players are sitting on 2+ years of loot and experience, I understand that there's a hellish balance to achieve between noobs and nerds. Yet when I look at the crafting requirements for a frame like Vauban Prime (in that case, due to Oxium, a rare resource that was difficult to farm effectively when I started playing, and is currently impossible to focus-farm), I just write that frame/item off as unobtainable until an indeterminate point in the future when I just happen to passively have enough crap to spend it on. I personally wish that there was still an environment like Draco that would allow you to quickly level up weapons/Warframes for efficent forma, but imo this comes from my inherent desire to min-max, because I read the Wikia, and then I'm suffering from the negative feedback loop. Etc et al.
If you treat Warframe like a roller coaster of discovery and combat, and it will remain deleriously fun. Treat Warframe like a game that will give you anything resembling instant gratification, and you will be frustrated.

I had been following the progress on the development of Ark: Survival Evolved long before I'd ever bought the game. The concept of an open world survival game with dinosaurs and other prehistoric creatures was taken straight out of my dream bucket, so naturally I was immediately on board for it. I purchased my copy of Ark sometime nearly 2 years ago. Previously my only gaming PC was a crappy laptop with a low end NVIDIA card which was not recommended to run this game. I was aware of this before purchasing, and proceeded to play the game anyway. I spent 250 hours playing Ark with lowest settings and claylike graphics at around a consistent rate of 12 FPS, and even then for me personally it was absolutely worth it. After that I was out of the game for about 10 months while saving up for a new gaming rig. When I returned to ark many updates later, all of the quality and replay value were still there with even more to offer. I'm now going on 350 hours into the game with a steady rate of 150 FPS on my new GTX 1070, and the enhanced graphics and playability has greatly increased compared to my previous experience with ark (which I still consider to be a positive one.) The core gameplay for ark itself maintains a very high replay value even as the game is in its current state. I can see myself coming back to play Ark again and again, and enjoying every phase of the game from beach goer to tek tier for many years to come. However - the reviews for this game are true, and it is horribly unoptimised for low to mid tier systems. If you do not have a very powerful gaming PC, I would not suggest purchasing the game, or at least only purchasing it on sale until at some point in the future when the game is further optimised. Alternatively, if you do have a high end system, and you like dinosurs and survival games, or you want a totally customizable game to get addicted to and lose thousands of hours playing, I can highly suggest you invest in Ark. Because of the core dynamics of the game, I can see a very open and ambitious future for Ark as it is now, and as a franchise for future installments. Depending on the type of server you play, you really can customize your Ark experience to be whatever you want it to be. This has the potential to attract a greater diversity of players. Whether you favor single player, multiplayer, PVE or PVP or something in between, there will be a server type and a play type out there for you and your tastes. If you are intending to start playing the game for the first time, I wouldn't recommend anything other than doing your research first. Find out what play style suits you and become aware of the different server types, current game status, and game dynamics before you purchase. If you already love ark - play it now, but if you're unsure or unable, I would reccomend that you wait.

At the time I’m writing this review I have nearly 1000 hours played. In my opinion that is enough time to properly gauge the quality and atmosphere of this game. My review will be in two parts, a review of the development team/moderators, and then a review of the game itself.
Development Team Review
To begin my review of the development team I would just like to say that they are some of the most money hungry people I have ever seen. You may think I’m about to rant about the paid dlc in early access, or the release of Ark on consoles when it’s far from finished, but no, I am going to rant about the fact that the Ark devs are paying/influencing the forum moderators on steam to delete any threads that are anti-Ark. I had heard stories about this, but never believed it until it happened to me. It all started when Ark released a horrendous nerf on the flyers, rendering them useless. So I watched the community response and wrote the predecessor to this. -
The reason I wrote the original was to poke some fun at the community and devs for following such a strict cycle when nerfs come out. It was all fun and games until a moderator deleted the post with no good reason. At first I thought it was moved, but nope, it was deleted by a moderator. I was undoubtedly confused, so I wrote the following thread voicing my opinion at the time that mods where indeed paid to delete anti-Ark posts from the steam discussions page.-
After the post had been up for a while loads of people started to tell their story about being banned or blocked from the ark forum after they posted a complaint or grievance about Ark. But just as the stories were getting really interesting, boom. The discussion was locked by a moderator, stopping anyone else from telling their story. This only threw gas on the fire for me; it proved my point even more that the moderators are censoring all anti-ark posts. As a bit of retaliation and wanting to call them out on their wrong doings, I wrote this post.-
This was the smoking gun, proof that the moderators are trying to silence anyone who speaks out against Ark. But, the story is just getting interesting. Shortly after my second post was up a moderator (who is the community hub leader at Wildcard) locked up the second post. This was outrageous; there was no cussing, mean comments or mudslinging. He simply locked it up so that no one could come forward and call Wildcard out on their corrupt actions. As if that wasn’t bad enough, I logged in today to find that I have been banned from the ark discussion page.
For what? They claim it was for posting the same thing twice, I think not. I was banned because they do not want me calling them out for what they are. You may be asking yourself, “Well why would they delete anti-ark things in the first place? Don’t they want community feedback?” The short answer is money. They are deleting the anti-ark posts because they will scare away new customers, causing them to lose money. And they DO want community feedback, so long as it is only positive feedback, the type of thing that will attract customers. This is absolutely ridiculous. Companies that do this should be shut down for corruption. So before you buy this game think about what I’ve said. If you speak out against Ark you WILL be censored.
The Game Itself
I have far less grievances with the actual game than I do with the developers. Don’t get me wrong Ark used to be a very fun game. That was until the tek and nerf bombs went off. Even as much as the devs have shoved tek down your throat Ark still comes across as a fun caveman game where you slowly progress to a decent sized base with a few large dinos. This WAS the case up until a few months ago. Used to I had loads of fun raiding and defending my base from tribes my size. But then someone bigger than you gets tek and all bets are off. Tek is yet another feature added for the alpha tribes, or the largest people on your sever that never stop playing. Tek is basically an unbeatable force that only people who play for weeks on end can get. Ark needs to stop with this Tek nonsense and start adding things that mid-low range tribes can enjoy, such as more decorative items or primitive raiding gear. Not elite weapons that hardly anyone can get. My next grievance is the flyer nerf. This nerf makes it where you can no longer level your birds in movement speed, and their stamina has been drastically cut. The nerf renders birds absolutely useless. The only ones not greatly affected by this are the alpha tribes, who have dozens of high level birds and can most likely teleport anywhere they want to go. This is just my two cents. Nerfs are often needed but not as drastically as Wildcard dumps on its players.
Final Thoughts
Ark used to be a fun game that I could play all day, but unfortunately that time has passed. Thanks to the development team’s lust for money, community corruption, alpha boosting updates, and endless nerfs, I am done with Ark and am giving it a thumbs down. I have definitely gotten my money's worth, but anyone who buys it now is simply wasting theirs.

There's a huge battleground not only between you and the dinosaurs, but between you and players. There's numerous different tasks you need to complete before doing anything, and one of them is making friends. This game is extremely hard to play alone, it's do-able, but very hard. Alliances or joining tribes with other people, can and will ensure you have a more enjoyable play time.

so, where should i start?
i played the game for over 1600 hours according to steam. I come back from time to time to check for updates and new content.
to put things in a nutshell,you are a space ninja. (a warframe) and you have to kill the bad guys, basically. you can do crazy tricks like walljumping and bullet jumping. each warframe comes with their own unique abilities, looks and aesthatics. want to be a swamp monster?no problem. want to be a mummy? no problem. want to be a pink colored sassy pseudo body builder?no problem.
i love a LOT of things in this game. but that doesn't mean the game comes without it's flaws.
so here's a couple of pros and cons;
-Pro's-
-A lot of class diversity
-A huge variation of weapons
-A lot of customization on both frames and weapons
-The game offers interesting co-op gameplay
-The devs listen to their players
-Both great artistic and unique tilesets and npc's
-Companions :D (cats dogs and small flying robots)
-Devs do weekly platinum givaways (ingame currency)
-Red text <3
-One of the lesser toxic communites out there
-F2P!
-#Fashionframe
-Weekly (mostly interesting) devstreams
-Cons-
-Very Few and kind of repetetive mission types
-The community doesn't tend to take criticism too lightly
-Not a whole lot of content to go through
-There's no real endgame (especially after spectres of the rails launched)
-A LOT of RNG based farming (it's basically the main drive for the game)
-Unbalanced pvp
-It can take up to 3 days to craft new items
-The game wont pose a challenge at all after after you get some of the less basic stuff
-Leechers
-A lot of bugs...
-Clunky interfaces
-Today's strongest weapon is tomorrow's mastery fodder
Know that the game is still in beta and receives monthly updates.
The devs put a lot of work and effort in the game.
So obviously some of the pro's and con's might shift a little over time.
I dont think there's a whole lot more to say.
All in all, not a bad game.
The game is worth to give a try at the very least.

Pros:
#1: Very well optimized, the game runs fast and smooth.
#2: Heavily Co-Op based game, yet still contains competitive PVP gameplay in the "Conclave"
#3: The PVP is not manditory or forced on the player, neither does it effect PVE or PVE balance, as it exists in a microcosm of it's own, entirely seperated and balanced by itself.
#4: A suprisingly deep universe for a free to play game with no franchise or books to base all there backdrop on. Honeslty the quests of "Natah" "Stolen Dreams" and "Second Dream" "War Within" are huge for people who get lore boners. If you pay attention and obsorb this games history and lore by reading codex entries or playing minor quests (Codex found ingame), and THEN play those quests.... You will have no regrets!
#5: Cool Concept and great gameplay! I mean come on! Space katanas and laser cannons in the same game.
#6: Constant and passionate development by a team of 170+ dedicated people.
#7: Even the item shop currancy of this game, that you have to buy with real money, can be traded between players, got something someone else wants? Make a trade and buy that fancy whatever from the item shop.
#8: No weapon or warframe is out of reach, anything and i mean anything that effects gameplay is free to get, ONLY cosmetics are locked behind "Platinum" which as stated in #6 can be gotten for free by trading with other players who are willing to part with it for something you have!
#9: TennoGen a system where players or digital artists can create cosmetic items, skins, and retextures of various things ingame. Where Digital Extremes picks the most voted for items and puts them ingame, purchasing of these items does not effect gameply statistics and provides a source of funds to both the artist to made them and Digital Extremes while providing a method for the community to directly add to the game on a cosmetic level. (♥♥♥♥in briliant if you as me but everyone has their own opinion)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Cons:
#1: RNG will rule your life! (Pro? Con? im 50/50 on RNG)

The development team knows this, and is working at another rework of it, DE is the type of company that never gives up until they make it work, take that as you will, i think it's good.
#4: There are and will likely to continue to be long dry spells between real content updates, this is due to how much each content update usually contains, as Digital Extremes tends to think big and then do bigger, this is both a good thing and a bad thing, but for the sake of fairness lets put it in the cons.

Having over 1000 hours of this masterpiece of a game probably gives me the privellege to finally create a "proper" review of it.
The focus of this review is going to be on the developers of the game and their means to communicate with their playerbase, rather than focusing on anything in game like: Graphics, Story, Gameplay, etc. which are subjects that i could ramble over for literally days.
It definetly is an odd subject to talk about, but it's the main reason why i love this game with a passion as big as the rings of Saturn.
So why not just give you a background story of these developers ?
Digital Extremes, commonly referred to by it's community as DE, had never really been a company that stood in the spotlight, they were mostly assisting other companies in their projects of which most were genre-defining titles such as: The Unreal Tournament games as well as Bioshock and Bioshock 2. Founded in 1993, it was not until 2008 that DE was able to create their own IP that was not a Pinball game. A game by the name Dark Sector which is the game that completely defined Warframe's character design, art style and also has some tiny lore influences in the game itself.
Moving along to 2013, DE finally released the first versions of the game in question: Warframe. But just a month later DE  had to deal with the Iceberg of the company.
Star Trek
A game where Star Trek fans amongst the Studio had probably the most excitement for.
Sadly, the game had to cut down on content that DE wanted to add by members of Warner Bros. .
After that, not only were the Star Trek fans of the company saddened by these news but the release of the game made Digital Extremes fall into decline. Almost ending the career of all of it's employees.
But there was a shining star in the distance ..... the game that the studio always wanted to create....
Warframe
Thank's to Founder Pack's implemented and the community enjoying the early stages of the game, the company received amazing financial support which allowed them to continue development on their beloved game
Along it's way, Digital Extreme's had ... quite the reputation after their failed abomination of a game known as Star Trek. Causing them several issue's with finding Publishers. As well as several companies telling them that their game had amazing potential and an incredible art style, which was overshadowed by a phrase stated by one of them.
"You will Fail"
There were tons of arguments of the company not being able to supply content and probably ending up abondening their work which ultimately have been proven false.
DE has managed to bring major content updates to the game nearly every 3-4 months throughout the past years as well as supplying the community with other game changing updates such as the recent implementation of Warframe passives or other reworks of some kind, improving the game almost week by week.
But how come a company can make all these improvements in such short amounts of time with literally no end to their idea's of improving the game?
Because Digital Extremes isn't a company that wears suits.

The sole reason why Digital Extremes stands proud to this date, is because they aknowledge and treat the people that saved their company well, Warframe's Community.
DE has managed to create absolute transperence between them and their community, reading through feedback all day and aknowleding every 4th post of their Forum's they do not hesitate to inform their community on what they think are good ideas comming from the community as well as informing them and asking them about opinions on certain mechanics of the game.
There are alot of prominent faces of the studio amongst their community due to their apearance on their Twitch event's labelled:
Devstream and Prime Time.
Rebecca   - Community Producer
Megan      - Community Coordinator
Steve        - Creative Director
Scott        - Design Director
Goeff        - Animation Director
Sheldon    - Studio Manager
The way these people interact with their community and show their apreciation for their ideas is simply astonishing. Each one of them is not afraid to show their personality and their feelings towards things giving the community the feeling not talking to a corporate body all the time, instead they get to talk to people that understand their opinions, can reason with them. Simply put, DE could be described with only two words: They care.
A prime example for this occured on their PAX panel when the community present, were asking questions while Steve did not hesitate to not every single one of them of which all listed have since then either already been adjusted or are primairly worked on.
Something you might have stumbled upon is the fact that Warframe has a Workshop where players can make their own designs for custom skins for their favorite Frames or Weapons. Obviously this isn't too much of a special thing considered that there are Workshop's for CS:GO, TF2 etc. . Severe difference is that these skins actually get to be "elected" to be in the game at a frequent paste, since DE always loved the idea's that their community had and want's them to be part of the game as fast as possible.
But this isn't the only thing that the community created for this game.
As of recent DE has added the feature to create a gallery in your ship which serves as your HUB, allowing you to not only to put up pictures created by DE into your trusty Orbiter but also Fanart from the community. Some of which even defy's the lore of the game depicting that eventhough there is a set lore, everyone on Warframe is allowed to have their own interpretation their own way of seeing the characters, the frames and the world of the game.
There have been alot of community influences on games for sure, but one thing is certain:
The community did not only influence Warframe, it shaped it, made it it's own and only thanks to the developers that allowed them to do so.
With my 1000 hours of playtime I have only encountered around 4 people that i would consider ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s. But everyone else i ever talked to, everyone else that i have ever traded with, that i have partied up with to play together, have been proven to be amazing people.
There is a good chance that if you talk to this community, they answer gently, they understand, and they have no means to be absolute nobheads like other members of other communities.
For me
Warframe is not just a game, it is the product of how a team of developers can create an almost considered to be Utopia of a playerbase.
I enjoy every second of playing it, knowing that day by day I am part of a community that is a byproduct of a game that not only effort was put into, but true passion, true love.
And even if i get bored, if I don't feel like playing the game because i already achieved so much. I can always come back in a week or two and have fun with the new content they are adding.
If you managed to stick through this little ramble of a kid paying tribute to their favorite Developer Studio, than I am sorry that i didn't really give you any Information on what this game is actually about, this is just something i really felt like getting of my chest.
- Thanks for checking in

This game is phenomenal.  I absolutely love it and definitely recommend it for anyone who wants to play a survival game.  I've played this game since early access and I am always excited to see what the developers add.
PROS:
-Dinosaurs!  A large variety of dinosaurs you can tame, fight, hunt, or run from in fear
-Large amount of content allowing for hours of fun
-Huge and very well designed crafting system
-Total character creation, wtih a huge variety of customizations
-Not a dead-end survival sandbox game.  Most games of the sort just have the endgame goal of survival such that there really isn't anything to aim for.  The only to look forward to in such games is burning out.  With ARK, there are bosses to defeat when the player feels ready.
-Very edittable sandbox environment
-Multiplayer
-Large fanbase with many workshop mod-creators.  Mods created are taken into consideration by the developers and implemented into the game if the idea is liked enough.  Otherwise, there's a large variety of mods to spice up gameplay for when one finishes vanilla
-2 games in one! (Comes with ARK: Survuval of the Fittest)
CONS:
-NONE!
There's a lot to look forward to in ARK; so much that it's hard to ever get bored of it!  When you've grown tired of the original map, you can purchase the dlc map which allows for a new survival experience.  There's even ARK: Survival of the Fittest, a survival games take on ARK, where players partake against each other to see who is the most fit for surviving on a dinosaur infested island.  ARK is especially fun in multiplayer (whether in Survival Evolved or Survival of the Fittest)
Overall, ARK is extremely fun and addicting and I recommend it for anyone who likes the survival genre.  10/10.

I LOVE THIS GAME, but i didnt at first. There were a few things i wish i knew about prior to my purchase. some good some bad.
1. Yes ASE has a functioning single player, which is great for learning how to play. unlike rust and similar survival games, after you take out the player to player element, ASE has PLENTY of content and depth, that makes single player a challenging and rewarding experience.
2. the learning curve is STEEP and i mean STEEP. but i dont think thats nescessarily the devs fault. mentioned before; ASE has buku content and depth and i challenge anyone to streamline it without cutting content or adding a 6 hour long tutorial level. youtube is a must for new players.
3. CLUNKY UI. the UI is horrid, it isnt very well built, confusing, and often glitches. some of the poor design choices here make learning how to play extremely frustrating at times. since i bought this game the UI was updated but it still needs work.
4. Grind. ASE is SUPER GRINDY. i mean having dinos helps, but i feel like the building materials are waaay too expensive for single player, itd be nice to be able to scale down costs for building.
5. DINO AI. The AI for this game is really bad, pathing is bad; i cant tell you how many times ive had to destroy foundations to get my dilos out from under it.
6. DINO SPAWNS. the island you're on is overpopulated with dinos, this makes sense if your on multiplayer but in single player you see some odd things happening. starting off i had to respawn 15 to 20 times before i could walk without pulling aggro on a raptor or a group of dilos within the first literal 12 seconds. this is something else i hope they make adjustable.
7. DEPTH. ASE is extremely deep; building and crafting requires a lot of thought and planning. which is great. its a shame they dont advertise that because thats a huge plus for me.
8. Toxic community. the official servers are alright but ive com across a few toxic players/admins that just suck the fun out of it for me. i stick with single player, but i might just start hosting soon.
9. YOU CAN HOST YOUR OWN SERVER!!!!!
10. LVLS? the leveling system seems a bit wonky and out of place for what this game is, i could inderstand leveling for dinos and i could understand leveling in players as a sort of pseudo-tutorial, but once you know how to play its frustrating to have to start over, and depending on the server you join, leveling could take minutes-hours-days. for an experienced player, leveling is pointless. i hope they adopt a different system for upgrading health/stam/weight ect.
overall, i would highly recommend buying this game, even in its current state. but be warned, its a game you will have to learn to love. its difficult, exciting, frustrating, beautiful, glitchy, and the UI in dire need of a facelift, but its also well worth your time and money. add it to your wishlist and snag it next time its on sale.
At the end of the day remember that this game isnt finished yet and the DEVS ARE ACTIVE, EVERY aspect of this game is subject to change. have fun and watch where it goes

I LOVE THIS GAME, but i didnt at first. There were a few things i wish i knew about prior to my purchase. some good some bad.
1. Yes ASE has a functioning single player, which is great for learning how to play. unlike rust and similar survival games, after you take out the player to player element, ASE has PLENTY of content and depth, that makes single player a challenging and rewarding experience.
2. the learning curve is STEEP and i mean STEEP. but i dont think thats nescessarily the devs fault. mentioned before; ASE has buku content and depth and i challenge anyone to streamline it without cutting content or adding a 6 hour long tutorial level. youtube is a must for new players.
3. CLUNKY UI. the UI is horrid, it isnt very well built, confusing, and often glitches. some of the poor design choices here make learning how to play extremely frustrating at times. since i bought this game the UI was updated but it still needs work.
4. Grind. ASE is SUPER GRINDY. i mean having dinos helps, but i feel like the building materials are waaay too expensive for single player, itd be nice to be able to scale down costs for building.
5. DINO AI. The AI for this game is really bad, pathing is bad; i cant tell you how many times ive had to destroy foundations to get my dilos out from under it.
6. DINO SPAWNS. the island you're on is overpopulated with dinos, this makes sense if your on multiplayer but in single player you see some odd things happening. starting off i had to respawn 15 to 20 times before i could walk without pulling aggro on a raptor or a group of dilos within the first literal 12 seconds. this is something else i hope they make adjustable.
7. DEPTH. ASE is extremely deep; building and crafting requires a lot of thought and planning. which is great. its a shame they dont advertise that because thats a huge plus for me.
8. Toxic community. the official servers are alright but ive com across a few toxic players/admins that just suck the fun out of it for me. i stick with single player, but i might just start hosting soon.
9. YOU CAN HOST YOUR OWN SERVER!!!!!
10. LVLS? the leveling system seems a bit wonky and out of place for what this game is, i could inderstand leveling for dinos and i could understand leveling in players as a sort of pseudo-tutorial, but once you know how to play its frustrating to have to start over, and depending on the server you join, leveling could take minutes-hours-days. for an experienced player, leveling is pointless. i hope they adopt a different system for upgrading health/stam/weight ect.
overall, i would highly recommend buying this game, even in its current state. but be warned, its a game you will have to learn to love. its difficult, exciting, frustrating, beautiful, glitchy, and the UI in dire need of a facelift, but its also well worth your time and money. add it to your wishlist and snag it next time its on sale.
At the end of the day remember that this game isnt finished yet and the DEVS ARE ACTIVE, EVERY aspect of this game is subject to change. have fun and watch where it goes

As you can see, I have a lot of time in this game. I will say it now, you will either love this game or you will just feel kinda meh about it; those are the only two sentiments I've seen expressed by anybody who's played Warframe. The gameplay is fluid and solid; the graphics are superb even on low settings and on a low-end computer; the quests (the main story quests, anyway) are well-made, compelling, and have amazing depth; oh and the lore....people who love lore will probably love this game.
Be warned: you will spend a lot of time farming. You will spend virtually all of your time farming. There is no way around it other than spending way too much money. If you don't like time-demanding farming-oriented games, you'll probably enjoy Warframe's gameplay, but I doubt you'll advance far.
Also, there is no endgame right now. Content is added regularly, but at the level I've reached many (including myself) often have difficulty maintaining interest. But by the time you get to that point, you'll have enjoyed at least a few hundred hours of superb gameplay, so who cares if you end up moving on?

In short:
This is a great game for new players but recent update has alientated a large portion of older players.
The Long:
Specters of the Rail Update:
The good:
Added graphically impressive star chart.
Added mini-bosses to unlock Star charts.
The Bad:
Changed How to get prime parts.
What are prime parts?
There are many characters and weapons in the game given a prime version. The prime version is usually a little stronger and has a different look from its regular counterpart.
You use to have to get one time use keys to be able to access special mission in a region called the void. Every mission type, and level, had different rewards to be able to get. While this required some time to "grind" in order to get the piece you wanted this was considered generally an end game area and activity.
Wait. wait. Wouldn't that mean you'd get a bunch of extra stuff?
Yes. But there is a special character in the game where you can trade in the extra stuff for special currency to buy special items.
Now. They have integrated the Void with the rest of the game and have demoted it to a "Farm the only special resource this region has" area.
The new way to get prime parts? You must farm for these things called relics (instead of void keys). You take these relics to a special mission type called "Void Fissure" (If fissures are from void then how does the void region have fissures?) and you get a chance at getting one of the items that specific relic you bring has in it. Everyone must now bring his/her own relic (when there where keys people had the option to host 3 others for a mission) and at the end of the mission you get to select one of the items from any of the 4 relics. ... in other words everyone has to have a relic, so everyone has to farm for relics now to play a mission to have a chance at getting an item - maybe - but only one. (The old system there where missions that only had one reward but also missions that had potential for up to 8 rewards.)
Now you can "improve" your chance at getting the rare item in these relics but you have to farm things called "void traces." How to get these? Play the void fissure missions in the first place. Be careful because you only get to have up to 100 traces .... which is exactly how many it takes to do a full upgrade of a relic. Only get to upgrade a relic once so might as well max it out. But any extra void traces you get past 100 disappear.
Want to buy something from the special trader now? Sure.... maybe you'll have enough parts in 3 months for an item or two. (Unless you have absolutely no life.)
As a result of the change to the late game I cannot, in good conscience recommend the game at this time.

Having over 1000 hours of this masterpiece of a game probably gives me the privellege to finally create a "proper" review of it.
The focus of this review is going to be on the developers of the game and their means to communicate with their playerbase, rather than focusing on anything in game like: Graphics, Story, Gameplay, etc. which are subjects that i could ramble over for literally days.
It definetly is an odd subject to talk about, but it's the main reason why i love this game with a passion as big as the rings of Saturn.
So why not just give you a background story of these developers ?
Digital Extremes, commonly referred to by it's community as DE, had never really been a company that stood in the spotlight, they were mostly assisting other companies in their projects of which most were genre-defining titles such as: The Unreal Tournament games as well as Bioshock and Bioshock 2. Founded in 1993, it was not until 2008 that DE was able to create their own IP that was not a Pinball game. A game by the name Dark Sector which is the game that completely defined Warframe's character design, art style and also has some tiny lore influences in the game itself.
Moving along to 2013, DE finally released the first versions of the game in question: Warframe. But just a month later DE  had to deal with the Iceberg of the company.
Star Trek
A game where Star Trek fans amongst the Studio had probably the most excitement for.
Sadly, the game had to cut down on content that DE wanted to add by members of Warner Bros. .
After that, not only were the Star Trek fans of the company saddened by these news but the release of the game made Digital Extremes fall into decline. Almost ending the career of all of it's employees.
But there was a shining star in the distance ..... the game that the studio always wanted to create....
Warframe
Thank's to Founder Pack's implemented and the community enjoying the early stages of the game, the company received amazing financial support which allowed them to continue development on their beloved game
Along it's way, Digital Extreme's had ... quite the reputation after their failed abomination of a game known as Star Trek. Causing them several issue's with finding Publishers. As well as several companies telling them that their game had amazing potential and an incredible art style, which was overshadowed by a phrase stated by one of them.
"You will Fail"
There were tons of arguments of the company not being able to supply content and probably ending up abondening their work which ultimately have been proven false.
DE has managed to bring major content updates to the game nearly every 3-4 months throughout the past years as well as supplying the community with other game changing updates such as the recent implementation of Warframe passives or other reworks of some kind, improving the game almost week by week.
But how come a company can make all these improvements in such short amounts of time with literally no end to their idea's of improving the game?
Because Digital Extremes isn't a company that wears suits.

The sole reason why Digital Extremes stands proud to this date, is because they aknowledge and treat the people that saved their company well, Warframe's Community.
DE has managed to create absolute transperence between them and their community, reading through feedback all day and aknowleding every 4th post of their Forum's they do not hesitate to inform their community on what they think are good ideas comming from the community as well as informing them and asking them about opinions on certain mechanics of the game.
There are alot of prominent faces of the studio amongst their community due to their apearance on their Twitch event's labelled:
Devstream and Prime Time.
Rebecca   - Community Producer
Megan      - Community Coordinator
Steve        - Creative Director
Scott        - Design Director
Goeff        - Animation Director
Sheldon    - Studio Manager
The way these people interact with their community and show their apreciation for their ideas is simply astonishing. Each one of them is not afraid to show their personality and their feelings towards things giving the community the feeling not talking to a corporate body all the time, instead they get to talk to people that understand their opinions, can reason with them. Simply put, DE could be described with only two words: They care.
A prime example for this occured on their PAX panel when the community present, were asking questions while Steve did not hesitate to not every single one of them of which all listed have since then either already been adjusted or are primairly worked on.
Something you might have stumbled upon is the fact that Warframe has a Workshop where players can make their own designs for custom skins for their favorite Frames or Weapons. Obviously this isn't too much of a special thing considered that there are Workshop's for CS:GO, TF2 etc. . Severe difference is that these skins actually get to be "elected" to be in the game at a frequent paste, since DE always loved the idea's that their community had and want's them to be part of the game as fast as possible.
But this isn't the only thing that the community created for this game.
As of recent DE has added the feature to create a gallery in your ship which serves as your HUB, allowing you to not only to put up pictures created by DE into your trusty Orbiter but also Fanart from the community. Some of which even defy's the lore of the game depicting that eventhough there is a set lore, everyone on Warframe is allowed to have their own interpretation their own way of seeing the characters, the frames and the world of the game.
There have been alot of community influences on games for sure, but one thing is certain:
The community did not only influence Warframe, it shaped it, made it it's own and only thanks to the developers that allowed them to do so.
With my 1000 hours of playtime I have only encountered around 4 people that i would consider ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s. But everyone else i ever talked to, everyone else that i have ever traded with, that i have partied up with to play together, have been proven to be amazing people.
There is a good chance that if you talk to this community, they answer gently, they understand, and they have no means to be absolute nobheads like other members of other communities.
For me
Warframe is not just a game, it is the product of how a team of developers can create an almost considered to be Utopia of a playerbase.
I enjoy every second of playing it, knowing that day by day I am part of a community that is a byproduct of a game that not only effort was put into, but true passion, true love.
And even if i get bored, if I don't feel like playing the game because i already achieved so much. I can always come back in a week or two and have fun with the new content they are adding.
If you managed to stick through this little ramble of a kid paying tribute to their favorite Developer Studio, than I am sorry that i didn't really give you any Information on what this game is actually about, this is just something i really felt like getting of my chest.
