So first off, I only have 11.9 hours on this game. That is roughly 714 minutes worth of gameplay. I know that is nothing to brag about since people have over 3k hours on this game, but I want to give a little math lesson that will put in perspective how bad this game is. First, I have spent at least 7 hours worth of play time trying to fight the lag on a gaming PC. I could only play it at around 30 fps (or around the speed of games on the Nintendo Gamecube ran on average) and it was still jittery and completely absurd with the amount of 0 fps drops I received. When I got the game, I was well aware that it was better played on multiplayer, so some friends of mine also got the game and decided to play with me and had the same lag issues. Eventually we were able to get 0 fps drops downb to about only 7 per minute, and we decided to start playing on a server. We tried to find one that wasn't over run with trolls or groups with biased devs in them, but to no provail. About 2 hours of my time was spent on looking for a server alone. That leaves only about 1.9 hours left of my "Play Time". At this point, we've found a server and we actually managed to get a little bit of progress made, or about 10 minutes before we got off. The next day, Battleye is in♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ed. This made it completely impossible to play this game for me, and it made it worse for my friends.
Also, the updates to this game are trash, as the devs are too busy adding on to realise that the reason the game is still an Early Access Game is because they aren't fixing the flaws such as glitchy "Solid objects" as well as the lag I talked about. By doing this, they delay the game more and more, eventually making so much new content that they spend another so many years fixing bugs so the game actually can be released. Of course by that time the game may as well be unplayable and die out.
Luckily this game was free, so you risk nothing by getting it. Oh wait, it wasn't. This horrible excuse of a game that is even worse than Minecraft singleplayer cost $20, wasting your money and your time.
Just to wrap up the message I'm trying to get across hrough this whole mini-rant; don't get this game until it is out of Early Access, if it is even playable for new people at that point.

Ignore the negative reviews. If you have a friend that you like to play games with and want to try something new, try this game. It is an absolute blast. I don't regret the purchase at all and look forward to months of game time.

A good game marred by a lack of difficulty and the developers constant need to rework old parts of the game.
Co-op shooting through randomly generated levels is naturally fun, but the system the devs have created allows you to make some absurdly powerful setups. The game balance problems mean that a player running a powerful build can ruin the fun for everyone by running ahead and killing everything.  There is almost not content that is capable of challenging these powerful builds.
It is fun as a time waster, but be wary spending money on it - the game you spent money on may not exist after the next patch. This happened to me with the movement update that took stamina management, wall running, wall attacks, the skill involved in climbing difficult geometry, and replaced it with 'hold this button to ninja!.' It is happening to other players right now with the rail update. The game is in a constant state of change, and it is guaranteed to change things that you enjoy.
The game also has very poor quests.    The games story is told through a handful of quests, giving you background on the enemies, allies, and yourself.  Though I was pleasantly surprised when the devs finally managed to tie their seemingly unrecoverable lore together, the slow and annoying quests still are not worth the time it takes to complete them.  Unfortunately, you must complete several quests to progress.  They are not just easily ignored filler, but actively make the game worse.
My final major annoyance with the game is how buggy it is.  The devs have been labeling it "beta" for years now, which seems to somehow give them a free pass on bugs.  Though some bugs are minor, I frequently run into bugs that force me to abandon whatever mission I am on.
Even with these problems, the game probably has more good than bad.  There is a good sized playerbase, the game does a great job at quickly putting you into groups, there is a crazy amount of content, co-op is fun, the f2p system is fair, and the developer releases updates frequently.
I am reminded, though, of another f2p scifi class based third person shooter that reworked itself endlessly. It was called Firefall. Constant reworks of things players like alienated their playerbase and the game died.  I am surprised that has yet to happen to Warframe, but maybe it is just a matter of time.

Decided to give Specters of the Rail a try. A lot has changed. A lot needs to change. The best quality about Warframe is that, for better or worse, they actually bother to make the changes. That's more than what can be said for a lot of other games out there.
My biggest complaint about Warframe has always been the grind. The grind is ridiculous, something like 40-50 hours of grinding for a single piece of gear, which can be bypassed by spending somewhere between 2 and 7 dollars. Sometimes this gear isnt even good and you end up feeling like♥♥♥♥♥♥for bothering with it.
I have a lot of time in this game, so I can bypass most of these grinds by virtue of having enough rare stuff in game to either trade for it or have already farmed the rare stuff required. However, new ways to grind keep getting added. I've been playing since the start of open beta some 3 years ago. I've seen countless ways to farm nerfed to the ground and disappear from the community's knowledge. I've seen rare material drop rates globally nerfed, not once, but two times. I've seen new things added with sub-1% chances to acquire it, mandating dozens, if not over a hundred runs of the same mission. I've seen exploits exploited, and completely unfair and unjust changes made in the span of 8 hours, damning anyone who couldn't log in in time to prepare. I've seen all the worst Warframe has to offer and it's been pretty damn bad sometimes with the decisions Digital Extremes have made. But they live up to that name.
For all the full on disappointment I've felt for Warframe, there are also awesome moments. Moments where people really come together and just be players in a game, discovering all the cool combos, hidden places, or fancier ways to murder countless enemies, together. That feeling of being in a new world, ready to discover whatever's next. That feeling that I only get from great MMOs when they were in their prime.
That's where Warframe is right now, a great game, in its prime, ready to capture the imaginations of any player willing to give it a chance. If I ever get angry at the game, disappointed because whatever system was made too grindy, or some item made too hard to acquire, or a nerf hitting too close to home, I feel that because I care. I care about what happens in Warframe. I want it to be the best it can be, the game that I was meant to play and enjoy for years.
Its still that game that got me hooked. However, I cant enjoy it like I used to. Is it because the game didn't change enough for me to keep liking it as much? Or did I change, and now my interests don't align with the fun to be had in Warframe? Was there more I could have done, but didn't do?
I hope that its just me.
TL;DR: It's okay.

I know that is nothing to brag about since people have over 3k hours on this game, but I want to give a little math lesson that will put in perspective how bad this game is. First, I have spent at least 7 hours worth of play time trying to fight the lag on a gaming PC. I could only play it at around 30 fps (or around the speed of games on the Nintendo Gamecube ran on average) and it was still jittery and completely absurd with the amount of 0 fps drops I received. When I got the game, I was well aware that it was better played on multiplayer, so some friends of mine also got the game and decided to play with me and had the same lag issues. Eventually we were able to get 0 fps drops downb to about only 7 per minute, and we decided to start playing on a server. We tried to find one that wasn't over run with trolls or groups with biased devs in them, but to no provail. About 2 hours of my time was spent on looking for a server alone. That leaves only about 1.9 hours left of my "Play Time". At this point, we've found a server and we actually managed to get a little bit of progress made, or about 10 minutes before we got off. The next day, Battleye is in♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ed. This made it completely impossible to play this game for me, and it made it worse for my friends.
Also, the updates to this game are trash, as the devs are too busy adding on to realise that the reason the game is still an Early Access Game is because they aren't fixing the flaws such as glitchy "Solid objects" as well as the lag I talked about. Of course by that time the game may as well be unplayable and die out.
Luckily this game was free, so you risk nothing by getting it. Oh wait, it wasn't. This horrible excuse of a game that is even worse than Minecraft singleplayer cost $20, wasting your money and your time.
Just to wrap up the message I'm trying to get across hrough this whole mini-rant; don't get this game until it is out of Early Access, if it is even playable for new people at that point.

Understand that these are my opinions about the game, and remember, you are entitled to your own opinion.
What I like about this game:
-It isn't a pay-to-win game like most free to plays, and you can trade items you find in-game to other players for an alternative currency called Platinum. Platinum is basically the currency that is equivalent to real money, but if you actually play the game, you can earn a lot of Platinum by selling full sets of weapons and such.
-There are a variety of classes to choose from, making gameplay a lot more interesting
-Every class is OP in it's own way, and they can be very helpful during certain missions or useless in others, thus making players strategize what class they should use for missions and what mods to use to be as helpful as possible.
-The Warframe community is great
-IT'S FREE TO PLAY!!!
Now the Cons of the game:
-Crafting stuff TAKES FOREVER.
This doesn't bother me as much, but there are gamers out there who don't have the patience to wait for their gear to be built, thus why I put it in the cons section of the review. As a warning to those impatient gamers who want their stuff now, it usually takes about 11 hours to complete a weapon, and about 2-3 days to finish building a new class. HOWEVER, you can spend Platinum to speed up the process so it finishes instantly, but it's about 50 platinum to do so. Obviously, this price shrinks as it gets closer to completion, but honestly it's better to just wait for your items to finish.
-You have a limited inventory.
In the beginning of the game, you have a limited inventory space for your weapons and classes (warframes). Now the downside here is that you have to spend platinum to expand your inventory, and if you're a completionist who wants to have every single weapon in your inventory, it can get quite expensive. HOWEVER, you don't necessarily increase your inventory size until you reach late game, and so far, I only needed to increase the inventory size of my Warframes, cause a lot of my builds share the same weapons; the only difference is what warframe I'm using.
So basically, give this game a shot. It's really well developed for a free to play game, and I'm sure you'll enjoy it.
And a message to all those who got salty over the Specters of the Rail update:
I know you veterans miss a lot of stuff from the old Warframe, and honestly, I miss how the void was designed as much as you. But you know what? You guys should just deal with it. Change in gameplay is what keeps this game fresh, and I personally love the new way to get prime parts. Before the update, you had to grind through the void to get a chance for a prime item, and it's most likely a very common one too. Key word here is chance; players in the past had to grind through like, 40-50 void missions just to get ONE rare prime part. Some don't even get any at all. Now, there's a higher chance to get the prime part you want, and on top of that, you can use void traces to increase the chances of getting the desired part.
And all those who complain about the new way to get to new planets? Yeah, no offence, but I think you guys are just being lazy. For those who don't know, before the update, all you had to do was to defeat the "boss" of the planet, and you unlocked the next planet. With this new update, you not only have to defeat the boss, but you have a few other objectives as well. On top of that, you have to beat the junction specter, which is basically fighting another warframe, adding a considerable amount of gameplay into the game.
So in conclussion, new players should definitely try out this game if crafting and building your gear sounds attractive to you. Oh, and Veterans? Do keep your sentiment out from your reviews. You're supposed to show the pros and cons of the game, not get all negative and say, "Oh the game got more difficult, so I don't like it anymore".
If you're complaining that the community is getting smaller, then how about you fix it by NOT creating a negative review and creating a possitive one so you can attract more players to the game.
Hope this review helps!

Let me start this out with this: I don't play PVP on this, so I have no clue if that is fun or not for those that like PVP. I also play on a private, unmodded server. If you want a review that reflects the PVP aspect or that of official servers, this is not the review for you.
That said, ARK is not a bad game. It's just also not a good one. Graphically, it's really lovely to look at. The Islands and the animals all look beautiful.
But ARK lacks a good AI for said animals and progression/maintenence balance.
What I mean by this, is that the AI has animals get stuck on stones and cliffs as they try to get you. I had pack animals (wolves) die because they got stuck on each other as they were attacking an enemy. Animal death is usually due to something like that, where an animal gets stuck, or in case of sea creatures, they just can't keep up with you and get lost.
The entire taming mechanic is based around this, as you have to shoot about 100+ tranqs into high end creatures, but you can only do so if the animal stays in one spot for enough time. Taming in general, something that I bought this game for, is rather laughable too. Without certain mods, you will be beating most of the animals over the head, before sedating them further and feeding them. Only more recent animals mix this up a bit, but some just require special food instead of basic berries and meat, making it still just as frustrating. Also, on public servers, this entire process takes hours upon hours. On our private server, the taming time is set down dramatically and still takes a lot of time. In short: Taming should get an overhaul to be more fun, despite its length. But that is not really going to happen.
Also, progression along the way, as your work yourself up from stone tier to metal and so forth, will reach a point where nothing can be achieved anymore. This would be okay, if there was a sort of work for maintenence, but as soon as you reach the point of having apex animals, anything you might need for maintence gets far too easy. If you need food, take your Rex around the block. If you need metal, take your Anky up a hill. It stops feeling rewarding and it stops feeling like survival, where every piece of meat felt earned.
All of this is my own personal opinion on ARK, but I think there are better games out there and I also feel like it only delivers poorly on the dinosaur taming/keeping aspect. I know others will disagree.But if any of this would bother you too, you are best to stay away from it.

I've spent over 1,700 hours on this game.  It's been fun most of the time.  In my humble opinion, the developers/publisher of this game have made three very poor decisions for this "early access" game.
1.  Cross Server Transfers on official servers:  This was a terrible choice that affected every small tribe and casual player on a colossal scale and not in a good way.  This allowed all the MASSIVE alpha tribes, who had already dominated their servers and were twiddling their thumbs with boredom to decimate any other server they chose.
2.  Charge for a DLC:  This game is in "early access".  It was understood that all money earned from sales of this game went into developing and finishing the product all of us bought, not a DLC.  No matter the case, this makes Studio Wildcard look like they've spent time, money, and resources developing a DLC and not completing their base game.  This really reflects poorly on their company.
3.  Game updates and no communication:  I absolutely love the steady influx of game updates.  Afterall, the game is in "early access" right?  What I don't appreciate is no real communication on their plans or game philosophies.  What's the main focus here, PVP, PVE, or a survival title?  What philosophy can we expect their decisions to cater to?  The nerf to fliers, while I felt was necessary to some degree, was abrupt at best.  The game had gone on for so long the way it was, everyone felt like they were just kicked in the d*ck after the nerf to fliers.  Had the devs made it clear that fliers weren't where they wanted in the meta of the game, everyone could have been a bit better prepared to accept these changes, and perhaps hold off on investing literally hundreds of hours breed/taming said fliers.
Is the game worth $30?  It has been for me.
Would I recommend it to newcomers?  Based on my three points above, I cannot.  In fact, they only way I get any enjoyment from this game now, is on unofficial/private servers.

Pro's
-Tons of Content
-Constant additions to the game
-Dev's are literally paying people to make mods that they could use to improve the game

I haven't been able to spend enough time with the game recently to properly review gameplay.  The reason for this is the reason for my negative review:  horrible, unacceptably bad optimization.  Now, before the fanboys come out of the woodwork to remind me "This game is in early access you moron!" I'd like to remind them that I can find nearly every early access game in my gamelist that at some point during Alpha, the devs of those games patched their respective games with performance and optimization changes.  Conan Exiles just came out in EA, and it has already had several performance patches.  So, my question is, why is Ark unable to do this?  It's simple.  Ark has and continues to make lots of money despite its performance issues.  So the devs have no reason to focus on that.  If sales dipped and people stopped playing it while providing reviews and feedback on the poor state of its optimization, I guarantee they'd focus on performance.
"But, JR!  Get a better PC you peasant!"
Here are my system specs:
OS:  Win 10
GPU:  EVGA GTX 1080 FTW
CPU:  i7 6700k 4.6ghz
RAM:  16gb's corsair
With this rig, I cannot play for more than 5 minutes before the game crashes or freezes.  It has been this way for many, many months now.  I don't really need to list the games my rig can handle, because it can handle EVERY game out there on Ultra settings.
Any game that is in Alpha this long, releases Alpha DLC, and continues to say "screw it" to optimization should not be bought as it sends a bad message to future developers of alpha games.  If you have fun it with despite its bad optimization, then good on ya, but I won't settle for that.

In short:
This is a great game for new players but recent update has alientated a large portion of older players.
The Long:
Specters of the Rail Update:
The good:
Added graphically impressive star chart.
Added mini-bosses to unlock Star charts.
The Bad:
Changed How to get prime parts.
What are prime parts?
There are many characters and weapons in the game given a prime version. The prime version is usually a little stronger and has a different look from its regular counterpart.
You use to have to get one time use keys to be able to access special mission in a region called the void. Every mission type, and level, had different rewards to be able to get. While this required some time to "grind" in order to get the piece you wanted this was considered generally an end game area and activity.
Wait. wait. Wouldn't that mean you'd get a bunch of extra stuff?
Yes. But there is a special character in the game where you can trade in the extra stuff for special currency to buy special items.
Now. They have integrated the Void with the rest of the game and have demoted it to a "Farm the only special resource this region has" area.
The new way to get prime parts? You must farm for these things called relics (instead of void keys). You take these relics to a special mission type called "Void Fissure" (If fissures are from void then how does the void region have fissures?) and you get a chance at getting one of the items that specific relic you bring has in it. Everyone must now bring his/her own relic (when there where keys people had the option to host 3 others for a mission) and at the end of the mission you get to select one of the items from any of the 4 relics. ... in other words everyone has to have a relic, so everyone has to farm for relics now to play a mission to have a chance at getting an item - maybe - but only one. (The old system there where missions that only had one reward but also missions that had potential for up to 8 rewards.)
Now you can "improve" your chance at getting the rare item in these relics but you have to farm things called "void traces." How to get these? Play the void fissure missions in the first place. Be careful because you only get to have up to 100 traces .... which is exactly how many it takes to do a full upgrade of a relic. Only get to upgrade a relic once so might as well max it out. But any extra void traces you get past 100 disappear.
Want to buy something from the special trader now? Sure.... maybe you'll have enough parts in 3 months for an item or two. (Unless you have absolutely no life.)
As a result of the change to the late game I cannot, in good conscience recommend the game at this time.

First of all I do like this game. It has many great aspects and a chance to be a great open world building and do whatever you wish simulator (have fun with dinos for example). But one of the main reasons why I do not recommend this game is how much time it consumes to progress and how easy it is to lose everything.
Thanks to those players who have progressed through half content that this game has to offer right now. Other players are able to (with wyverns or other overpowered stuff/dinos) dominate whole server and you have to live by their rules or just perish and lose everything.
I think PvP is great when both sides have almost equal chances to win or survive but when other side is so overpowered than the other side, it is just like slaughtering pigs.
Problem with PvE is that there are not enough resources and space for everyone and it takes a week before you can demolish other players stuff. Let's say you would like to expand but you are not able to, thanks to your friendly neighbour who is just trying to learn play game.
Although this game is still in development. The Devs are not fixing bugs and developing gameplay in anyway that we players could see. Some could say that they just released a patch where they added a new dino. Wow.. A dino. How about the bugs and glitches and other gameplay (almost) breaking issues?
Also I do not like that you can so to say "server hop" your resources and dinos to other servers. That makes new servers unnecessary when huge tribes can just begin to dominate a new servers after it has been established.
Conclusion:
Ark: Survival Evolved could be a great game but it lacks balance in terms of progressing and how much time is needed to play it. Ark also needs dev time to get rid of bugs and glitches.

I haven't been able to spend enough time with the game recently to properly review gameplay.  The reason for this is the reason for my negative review:  horrible, unacceptably bad optimization.  Now, before the fanboys come out of the woodwork to remind me "This game is in early access you moron!" I'd like to remind them that I can find nearly every early access game in my gamelist that at some point during Alpha, the devs of those games patched their respective games with performance and optimization changes.  Conan Exiles just came out in EA, and it has already had several performance patches.  So, my question is, why is Ark unable to do this?  It's simple.  Ark has and continues to make lots of money despite its performance issues.  So the devs have no reason to focus on that.  If sales dipped and people stopped playing it while providing reviews and feedback on the poor state of its optimization, I guarantee they'd focus on performance.
"But, JR!  Get a better PC you peasant!"
Here are my system specs:
OS:  Win 10
GPU:  EVGA GTX 1080 FTW
CPU:  i7 6700k 4.6ghz
RAM:  16gb's corsair
With this rig, I cannot play for more than 5 minutes before the game crashes or freezes.  It has been this way for many, many months now.  I don't really need to list the games my rig can handle, because it can handle EVERY game out there on Ultra settings.
Any game that is in Alpha this long, releases Alpha DLC, and continues to say "screw it" to optimization should not be bought as it sends a bad message to future developers of alpha games.  If you have fun it with despite its bad optimization, then good on ya, but I won't settle for that.

Very little I can say about this game will really do it justice. The seemingly insurmountable content still leaves me bewildered even after all of the progress I've made. I've invested quite a lot of time into this game, however if you compare this number to veteren players I would still be considered more of an amateur than my peers. This is ultimately meaningless however as there are all manner of players ranging from hardcore to casual and anything in between.
I've seemingly managed to power through a lot of content that most have taken double the time to complete however I have had help most of the way. This is where the game shines through the most in my opinion. Playing with friends is a very rewarding experience as most of the time you'll find yourselves working towards the same objectives whether it's gaining that new and shiny gear or simply experiencing the latest update and all it has to bring. The sense of camaraderie with both friends and even random players as you work towards your goals is something I feel every time I venture in, despite how well versed with this game I've already become. That is of course not to say that the game doesn't hold up as a solo experience, but I'd highly recommend bringing a long a friend or two... or three. The community in this game is worth commending both for their general friendliness and tolerance as well as their contributions to the game. Many of the game's features are derived directly from the imagination of the playerbase such as the famous "Clem" figure.
The game however, is not without its flaws as minor as they may be. Currently the game is still technically in its beta phase despite its large size and you will no doubt come across a number of glitches and issues. Almost every time however, these have provided chuckles and good memories and some extreme examples will go down in Warframe history forever. Another problem I find is that although the game is free to play, if you in any way want to progress you will most likely have to fork over some cash in order to gain the game's virtual currency used to buy equipment space and other such things associated with "premium currencies". This is circumvented through the use of the trading system however not only is this a much more tedious way of gaining currency, it still doesn't make up for the fact that at some point someone would have had to have bought currency to trade with in the first place.
Despite its flaws, and I must reiterate that they are indeed minor, this game is absolutely incredible through both the scope of content available and the sheer enjoyment it provides. Never have I encountered a Free-To-Play title with such quality, comparable to a AAA title. This game has given more to me than most ever will and I'll never forget the experiences that I've gotten and will continue to gain. The developers are constantly working to add more and more to this game and I'm positive it will continue its success for a long time.

Played this game awhile back and I got to say, my first impression was a good one at that, but the more I played, hours upon hours of gameplay (and endless loading screens), the game started to downgrade VERY quickly.
I loved the idea of riding dinosaurs, taming them, exploring the different maps, gathering materials & ressoruces, building a base, collecting loots and crafting the strongest armor to survive longer. All of these aspects seem very promising, especially if you're playing with friends. Unfortunately, the players inside some of the servers and a few untrustworthy friends ruined the game for me. One of the biggest issue in terms of maintenance is that... there is none. The game is constantly bugging, making it hard to travel from one place to another without loosing a dinosaur on the way or glitching through the floor with no means of escaping. The more I played, I noticed the game was mostly built for hardcore PvPers who want to duke it out 1v1, tribe vs tribe and not for the overly left-out and under-developped PvE servers. Not everyone is going to enjoy PvP games (especially me), so it could've been nice if the developpers would've put more effort into balancing both types of gameplay. I hate the fact that I had to be "forced" to play PvP just to even be able to encounter one of the few final bosses (or you could just join modded servers with bosses roaming around the map). People who played a lot of ARK found ways to exploit the game like hell at this point, so sometimes I felt like it wasn't even worth playing because I had to follow the rules to become better at the game, especially when the rules kept changing from servers to servers. Did I mention it takes frickin' forever to load a server, especially the ones with loads of mods added to them? Yeah... that's an issue too! Also ARK is not meant for people with old / outdated computers. If you don't have the recommended settings for the game or an upgraded graphics card, you can forget it, because the game will run like molasses and the graphics will look like an unpolished PS1 game on the lowest settings. So you might as well stick to Minecraft in that case.
So yeah, with a game as broken as this, what's the point of adding a DLC if the game isn't even finished yet? When the 'Scorched Earth' DLC was released, I've given up on the game as quick as bowling ball thrown on the floor (except it keeps falling until it reaches the center of the Earth).
With all the bad memories I experienced with ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s stuck inside the serves I was in, claiming they were the "best ARK players ever" and the lack of polish and maintenance from the devs is a great reason for me to tell you to NEVER touch or even try that game out, even if you are the least bit curious. It's not worth it. Avoid it at all costs!

Ark is an emotional game.
You will spend hours taming dinos and farming materials just to see all of it die or get destroyed. Heartbreak is around every corner, and there is that mini panic attack when you get a random steam message from a tribe mate because you know it's bad news. This is the most recent game that made me feel such a vast range of emotions.
The scale and variety of Ark is Impressive, and I feel you could do almost anything with this game.
Ark has many problems though.
Since the day it released, Ark has had significant, periodic lag that seems to happen every 5 -10 minutes and lasts about 10 seconds. Imagine you land your argentavis and dismount, only to see the server was lagging and you dismounted over a gourge full of rexes, and both you and your argent die. This is nearly a daily occurance, so you have to be prepared. (preparing takes 20 minutes before you feel safe enough to wander outside)
Also animals will "clip" through walls making only the most heavily fortified camps safe from wild animals. Also if you put anything on wander (dung beetles) they will slip through walls and you will get the random death message days later.
But I saw through these GLARING problems because Ark is too damn fun!

This game was fun for me before I realized how very repetitive and boring this game is. You grind grind grind and grind until you die IRL, before getting just that one prime part.
The resources and the prime grinds: And after you get the part/bluperint, don't forget to skip work/school for that nitain alert, and to grind more oxiums or argon crystals.
And do you know how hard and frustating it is to farm the prime parts? Oh God, farming the prime parts is the reason I'm taking a break from Warframe. It's the worst part of this game. Even after changes on how to farm the prime parts (now WF uses relics, instead of void keys), which should fix the repetitive feeling of the game, but I feel it's a bit worse, because you can't just speedrun the mission or play a long endless mission while only using 1 key, and getting like what, 5+ prime junks to be sold as prime junks. Now, it's 1 relic for 1 reward what ever the type of the mission is. Of course, you can use void traces to upgrade the relics so the chances for getting the rarest part/blueprint is easier. At least, that's the theory. I was once trying to build the Nekros Prime, I used a lot of  relics and traces for that one rare blueprint (forgot which one), but I only got 1 blueprint, and the rest was trash and prime junks.
Mods (upgrades): Now after you wait 3 days and 12 hours (or just 12 hours if it's a weapon) for that prime warframe, you need the mods, yes? Now u grind more until the mods you need, and farm the endos and credits so you can max the mods.
Leveling and forma: Also, don't forget formas, and leveling up your frames/weapons, it became repetitive if you do the defense missions. Another option to leveling up is Bere, that is if you now how to do it and get a good squad. And a forma can take 24 hours to craft, and some rare resources (not as hard to get as nitain extracts/argon crystals though).
Riven Mods: Lul, I don't care. It's just like farming mods, but harder and worse.
Platinum (The premium currency): It's better than the other free 2 play games, because you can get the premium currency, for free! All you need to do is GRIND MOAAAAAAARRRRRRR, and also be lucky. You can sell your prime parts/blueprints that you don't need for platinums (usually, the not-rare ones only valued at 20 plats, max, which is like nothing, or the junk ones for 2p plats each). You can use this to buy prime parts/blueprints. Other ways to get this is from winning giveaways on the devstream (or smth I forgot), or buy it from WF's website. It's an alternate route on getting a mod, or prime part/blueprint (items) that you really need but can't get becase the RNG hates you.
Trading: This is another way on getting the mod, prime part/bluperint that you really need. This is just like buying and selling items with plats, but change the plats to other items that are valued the same.
High level stuff: It's fun, if you have the gear for it and a good squad for it. Or it's not fun if you don't have the part for it and/or a good squad for it, or until before you play the high level stuffs everyday on every weeks on every months.
Quests: IT'S ♥♥♥♥ING GOLD. Best part of the game. Most of the quests are fun, I can only name one that really frustates me, which is the Nidus' one. The main quests have some pretty good stories, and the game itself has a really interesting lore. The sidequests for warframes/archwing/kubrow are also good.
The community: People here are good, very helpful, unlike other games
. This game's community really restores your faith in humanity, unlike those that are found in other games
.
The PVP part: Nobody plays it, why even bother lol.
Cosmetics and the weapon/warframe models: Nicely done, looks beautiful as ♥♥♥♥. It's some of the best models i've ever seen in a video game.
The sound: Sounds good, strong weapons sounds really strong. When you walk on metal, it's sounds just like when you're running on a metal. Etc.
Combat/movement: Feels really good. I love the melee combos, and the shooting is also good, just like in other games, but the melee feels 100x better. The movement in the game really adds another level of fun to the game, even though it will hurt your pinky finger after trying to bullet jump accross the map.
Playability (in terms of fps): Even my laptop with the first gen AMD A6 CPU (which is really ♥♥♥♥ing bad) can play this game above 30 fps (except in surv after 40 min+).
The graphics: This game is ♥♥♥♥ing beautiful. Even if it's easilly run buy a potato, it still looks beautiful. No complaints.
Customization: Pretty good, there are 5 color channels on each weapons and warframe. A lot of skins for the weapons and warframe. The warframes even have different helmets. You can customize your operator and pets (including sentinels) too, which is pretty good. My only gripes is that, to buy more color you either need to wait for the holidays (DE usually sells the easter/halloween color palletes on their respective holidays), or you have to use platinums.
The early game: This game has a lot of contents, but you have to learn of these contents from other players/the wiki. The game doesn't really tell you about its contents, or how to get that content. Example, is the quest, some new players wouldn't even know how to start the Natah Quest (which is the main quest) if
doesn't exist. Play the early parts with your friends. Please.
Sort of tl;dr:
Do I recommend this game? -No, if you don't have the time to grind at all, and/or is poor.
-Yes, if you have a lot of time to grind, or is rich.

And even though this game is still in an open beta, but damn this game looks ♥♥♥♥ing beautiful. Also, the amount of contents in this free to play, open beta game is so much it took me away from grinding away 24/7 and forgetting to go to school.
Even after I talk♥♥♥♥♥♥about this game, I still recommend it, because enjoy the game before you can't. Enjoy it before you become bored of the game. I had a good time while still playing and enjoying this game.

This is definately one of my top games of all time, and I highly recommend you play it, but even though I'm giving it a good rating I don't really enjoy it anymore. Not because I lost interest, but because the official pvp servers have been overrun by griefers.
This game is one of the most beauiful, challenging, scare-the-crap-out-of-you games I have played. You're basically trying to survive in Jurassic Park with some sci fi mixed in. Just don't expect to play on the official servers and enjoy yourself.. They are fuxed now...
But it wasn't always bad.... In the beginning, official servers evolved their own little communities because player stats didn't transfer. Servers were a commitment and most had fairly reasonable/loosely established rules between the larger tribes. They were moderated in a way and it wasn't too difficult to solo/play in a smaller tribe, which is typically how most players start out. As long as you weren't a♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bases/dinos were respected and raiding was more... friendly?.. I don't know...Basically, you wouldn't have to worry about getting completely wiped and then have to start from scratch.
The griefer tribes that get off by wiping other players/tribes could only get so big b/c servers only held 70 players at a time, and if one of those tribes wanted to change servers, everyone would have to start back at level 1, and then they'd be left to battle for available slots, so most would remain on whatever server they started.
This all changed when an update was released that allowed players to transfer themselves and their dinos between servers. Not only that, but the Scorched Earth dinos could transfer to the Surival Evolved servers, which was a great sales tactic, but screws any player that doesn't own it.
So what ended up happening is the griefer tribes spread, and players that had established themselves and their tribe on a particular server were wiped over and over until the tribe fell apart and/or they abandoned the server. For most of the game since I started, I was able to solo b/c the server community was pretty chill and respectful of each other. Once the griefers came, playing became a painfully annoying groundhogs day-like experience. It seemed like every week one of the griefer tribes would transfer a bunch of OP dinos and wyverns over and destroy everything they possibly could.
Other than that, the game is great. Unfortunately, not being able to play and enjoy the official servers with the character that I spent so much time on has definitely been a deal breaker for me. So, if you made it this far into the review, just beware that the official servers aren't all their cracked up to be.

Balanced Review from a Warframe Veteran:
I have been playing this game for 3 years now. After the mountain of negative reviews and forumn posts after the most recent update, U19 Specters of the Rails, I feel i need to update my review to prevent new players being terrfied away, This is what i wrote a while back as my first review.
I have searched for a good combat  aside from the popular console Call of Duty/Halo etc. for a long time. And i have finally found one. Strategy, combat skills, construction, critical thinking, lore, all in one game. The devs are always coming up with ways to add to the game or expand the game's lore universe/gameplay, so the game is always evolving. The user base is for the most part supportive and friendly, and unlike most games i have tried, the elitist jerk few can set up roadblocks to the common player base and make their gameplay miserable and unfruitful.
A word of warning, because the game is always evolving it is natural that bugs come with that territory. Players affectionately call it Bug Frame or Crash Frame because of it, but in my opinion the rewarding gameplay is worth it.
A word on its Free 2 Play status as there is much criticism especially after 15.0 Update. Although there are some limitations at trying to running it F2P, it can be done. Game currency can be earned thru the player trading system, game currency only items can be earned in the game although takes more time/in less quantity, and certain items can be traded for things you want but cant get. If you do decide to put some money in the game, a little goes a long way, and there is discount coupons all the time.
Posted November 3, 2014.
I still stand by that review.
Now, to explain some things that u19 changed and a word to the negative rotten tomatoe throwers.
U19 was a big in your face change, but this update DE is trying very hard to move away from the zombie farmframe mentality that has plagued this game for a long time and make a more polished, progressive mission based game. Which is what the community has been demanding for 2 years. You can't have it both ways.
1) this was a double edged sword to the way  to obtain Prime Parts, the soul of P2P trading, and items that are basicalyl upgraded versions of some game weaponry. Before, you could spend hours apon hours of farming, Youd get a giant pile of loot but more then likely not what you wanted. Now You easily farm what you want, but you dont get that pile of loot that you dont need which goes to trading.
2) This nerfed the most popular and most effinct way of XP farming, a mission called Draco, where 2 players nuke the enemies standing in one place whiel the other 2 squad members afk nearby.
The game should not, does not and now cant revolve around a handful of nodes. (Draco, Hiercon, Void Survival.) This created a user base that had all the guns and mastery rank. Then 1) Draco players went into end game content or showed up for events and did zero damage, offered zero team support and/or died all over the place because they lacked the mods, understanding of game mechanics and battle experience that you gain from fighting in regular missions.
2) Void Farmers couldn't cope with events/ end game content that caused them to play cooperatively and think outside the box because they they were used to solo playing in a multiplayer game. They then acted liek elitist butholes that ticked off everyone around them, gave warframe's a bad name, and caused migrations and mission failures. (im looking at you RAID players that leave a RAID just because the EV does not have maxed power strength and you Shadow Debt junkies that left missions just because the mod you wanted didn't drop)
TRUE Trying to end zombie farming in the void was a double edged sword. Now you can run a handful of short missions and get exactly what you want. I've had to change my review on this game multiple times as time has gone by, many things have happened since I first bought this game.
I will first start off with the cons:
* Bugs

Though many of the bugs that used to be a problem earlier in the games life have been fixed, there are new bugs that keep appearing that are almost game breaking and it seems like the devs don't even care enough to fix them. Two recent examples are the light flickering bug which is really annoying, but is almost bad enough to seem that it could cause sezuires in those with epilespy. Another glitch that really dampers game play is this really bright blue night fog that goes on from 24:00 to 4:30. You can't see past 10 ft in front of you and you have to stay inside base because you can't do anything in this horrible condition. (Wildcard PLEASE fix these game breaking bugs!)
* Deadlines

Wildcard can't seem to meet any deadlines they make, be it for little 100 mb patches, 1.5 gb updates, or let's say, maybe, Aberration! Don't get your hopes up when they say that such and such is coming this week, IT WON'T.
* Not caring about their customers
I wrote a review about this on the season pass store page, but I'll give a summary of what I said here too. Wildcard released a season pass that includes Scorched Earth, Aberration (coming out soon) and a DLC coming out in Spring 2018. It was originally $44.99, but you got a dicount for about $10 to $15 if you already owned SE. Excited for Aberration, I bought the season pass, already owning SE I got the reduced price. I was happy until Aberration was said to be delayed until November, this was somewhat okay due to the fact that Wildcard never releases things on time anyways. Then the season pass went on sale, down to about $19. Basically, everyone who bought the season pass when it came out got a huge middle finger, both Aberration wasn't coming out in October and they pretty much got ripped off by Wildcard. You can't even return the season pass even though Aberration isn't even out so you never able to put over 2 hours on it.
Now the pros:
* Main Idea of the Game
Surviving with ancient creatures? Awesome! This is the type of game that I always wanted to play. I love this game, I have over 500 hours in it, it is the main game that I play, and I intend on playing it for many more hours to come.
* Playability
Most games I play for a couple hundred hours, maximum. They just don't have the replayability like ARK does, ARK catches my attention and keeps me glued to the screen with how fun it is to play, especially with friends.
* Customizability
Whatever your play style is, this game is pretty much for you. The game is so customizable it's crazy. Every mechanic in the game has a slider that you can adjust, making it so you can make the game what you see fit.
Do I recommend ARK? Yes, of course I do! This game is one of the best I have ever played, the idea is great it keeps my interest etc. Is the game perfect? No! There are bugs and not everything comes out on time and so on. Can Wildcard fix some of these things? Yes! They can make more realistic dates to release stuff, they can actually fix some game breaking bugs, etc. This game will be all the better once Wildcard does those things, and I look forward to when that time comes.
Anyways, keep on surviving ARK players, and if you are on the fence on deciding wether to get the game or not, wait unitl it's on sale, I agree, $60 is a bit much (coming from a guy who got it for $9.59). Thanks for reading and have a nice day fellas.

lets get straight to the point shall we:
Pros
-Excellent and enjoyable gameplay
-Servers are mostly stable
-Large variation in Dinosaurs with some requiring different taming methods than others and some having special abilities
-ability to customise the game to how you want to play it e.g increase XP rate and decrease Time needed for taming
-large open sandboxes with plenty to explore
-large player base
- interesting and largely well executed concept
Cons
-Options menu is a complete mess with no tabs what so ever
-UI is a tad overwhelming and ugly
-Frequent Glitches such as dinosaurs and players clipping into walls and scenery
-Developers seem to have a quantity over quality mindset,focusing on releasing more dinosaurs not fixing the bugs
-A lot of Grinding for bases and dinosaurs,some higher level dinosaurs require about 6-12 hours of taming
-DLC for an Early access game(Seriously WildCard?)
-2 years and 256 patches with Console releases and theres still Texture glitches such as hovering grass and creatures
-Potential loss of high lvl dinos on servers due to said clipping into walls with no way to get them out
-Troodons
-Anti-Cheat system doesnt stop cheaters like its supposed to
Conclusion
Overall Ark is a very good game with a unique concept and easy to learn gameplay, but its held back by its many glitches and lack of simple bug fixing patches that could save players so much frustration from losing equipment and creatures due to said equipment getting stuck in scenery.

I was reluctant to give this a "No" and really had to go through the pro's and con's of this game. Firstly the pro's:
This is a visually wonderful game 'if' you play this as a single player. There are just to many issues with rendering and uptime to take full advantage when playing off a server but as a single player this is really quite beautiful.
The general game mechanics make a lot of sense, yes it can be a bit tough but it 'is' a survival game and throwing a load of prehistoric creatures and a few fantasy creatures really sets interests high and desire to play on even when it is tough going to a fairly addictive level
There is a console command for single player and when hosting a server so it gives you a good chance to play around with the possibles and inpossibles without having to go through the painful hardship of 'playing' the game. Yes, this does kill a lot of the 'survival' aspect of the game but for the uninitiated it does help you understand the full mechanics of the game as well as give you a good road map for when you do decide to 'play it properly'
It is fun, taming dino's, riding dragons building tech that can be incorperated into every aspect of the game. It is a pretty original game (though the mechanics can be seen in other survival games) but again, this can really ever be experienced in single player or private hosting.
The map is pretty epic with a massive area to play in a full 3D eniviroment (don't fly to high, you'll likley freeze to death.) After 200 odd hours I have explored less than 10% of the entire map.
Now for the bad points!
As a MMO open world survival game (Playing with others on servers) it is really quite unplayable, even when the server is not lagging and the main reason are a small percentage of other players. I have yet to come accross a server either offical or unofficial that does not have a troll problem. To the point that the only enjoyment some of these players have is making sure no one else enjoys the game. There is no way to report the abuse, kick the players or anything to even attempt to stop this. It is a very small percent but enough to make enjoying the game very difficult.
Early access is being seriously abused by development team to excuse the multiple bugs in the game. Instead of fixing them they just seem to just keep developing new things, worlds and maps.... to the point they developed a whole new world as a stand alone game before addressing many of the issues with the first. Its great to see such eager developers but honestly the new things have problems of their own as well not to mention they are a little bit 'more of the same.' Examples of issues are:
-Rendering: I always have half a dino sticking into through my walls of buildings i have built
-Server Lag: At least once every 5 minutes
-Poor physics: I cannot dismount a large dino without killing myself (the fall from its back kills you)
-Coding: Lost count the number of times I have got 'stuck' in another object
-In game commands: nothing does what is told. Tamed creatures just disappear never to be seen again or follow you so close that you cannot build anything because they are always in the way. Predator dinos go on killing rampages for no real reason even when told to stay put.
I could go on but i think the rest of issues would be pulled apart by others as it may just be me that is bothered by them. However, I think what has already been mentioned is reason enough to stay away for the time being.

In short: the game developers are making it worst and worst with each new update.
In long:
I quite liked this game a few years ago (2013) when it came out of closed beta. It was a fresh breeze after the overload of fantasy themed online games that sadly seem to have been the way to go for developers.
The game is more and more unrecognizable with new each update.
For me has been a downhill since they remade the void into  literally a black hole and implemented the void relics.
Then the operator mode came in, which feels totally like a lackluster and very limited game mode compare to running around in your frame (basically you turn off your frame and run around with your operator, who is a teenage person of undetermined sex -judging by the portraits-.
Also raids and events that require us more and more to team up if we want to progress.
Its alright if its a coop game but right now is turning more and more into a Mandatory coop/multiplayer experience.
Not everyone has the social aptitudes or skills to be constantly in a party.
But nvm.
Now we got this hmm Plains of Eternal Grind (Eidolon for short).
Imagine a little portion of your favourite tundra themed open world game, fill it with water spots, ruins, ore, fish, enemies, npcs who speak like russian inmigrants who own that little shop near your place... you get the idea right?.
And on top of that another team play oriented enemy which requires more operator mode to be defeated.
Just try the game and decide yourself.
If you like a lot to team up and so on, to air your opinion on everything, talk about anime or japanese weirdo stuff, you might be fine.

Balanced Review from a Warframe Veteran:
I have been playing this game for 3 years now. After the mountain of negative reviews and forumn posts after the most recent update, U19 Specters of the Rails, I feel i need to update my review to prevent new players being terrfied away, This is what i wrote a while back as my first review.
I have searched for a good combat  aside from the popular console Call of Duty/Halo etc. for a long time. And i have finally found one. Strategy, combat skills, construction, critical thinking, lore, all in one game. The devs are always coming up with ways to add to the game or expand the game's lore universe/gameplay, so the game is always evolving. The user base is for the most part supportive and friendly, and unlike most games i have tried, the elitist jerk few can set up roadblocks to the common player base and make their gameplay miserable and unfruitful.
A word of warning, because the game is always evolving it is natural that bugs come with that territory. Players affectionately call it Bug Frame or Crash Frame because of it, but in my opinion the rewarding gameplay is worth it.
A word on its Free 2 Play status as there is much criticism especially after 15.0 Update. Although there are some limitations at trying to running it F2P, it can be done. Game currency can be earned thru the player trading system, game currency only items can be earned in the game although takes more time/in less quantity, and certain items can be traded for things you want but cant get. If you do decide to put some money in the game, a little goes a long way, and there is discount coupons all the time.
Posted November 3, 2014.
I still stand by that review.
Now, to explain some things that u19 changed and a word to the negative rotten tomatoe throwers.
U19 was a big in your face change, but this update DE is trying very hard to move away from the zombie farmframe mentality that has plagued this game for a long time and make a more polished, progressive mission based game. Which is what the community has been demanding for 2 years. You can't have it both ways.
1) this was a double edged sword to the way  to obtain Prime Parts, the soul of P2P trading, and items that are basicalyl upgraded versions of some game weaponry. Before, you could spend hours apon hours of farming, Youd get a giant pile of loot but more then likely not what you wanted. Now You easily farm what you want, but you dont get that pile of loot that you dont need which goes to trading.
2) This nerfed the most popular and most effinct way of XP farming, a mission called Draco, where 2 players nuke the enemies standing in one place whiel the other 2 squad members afk nearby.
The game should not, does not and now cant revolve around a handful of nodes. (Draco, Hiercon, Void Survival.) This created a user base that had all the guns and mastery rank. Then 1) Draco players went into end game content or showed up for events and did zero damage, offered zero team support and/or died all over the place because they lacked the mods, understanding of game mechanics and battle experience that you gain from fighting in regular missions.
2) Void Farmers couldn't cope with events/ end game content that caused them to play cooperatively and think outside the box because they they were used to solo playing in a multiplayer game. They then acted liek elitist butholes that ticked off everyone around them, gave warframe's a bad name, and caused migrations and mission failures. (im looking at you RAID players that leave a RAID just because the EV does not have maxed power strength and you Shadow Debt junkies that left missions just because the mod you wanted didn't drop)
TRUE Trying to end zombie farming in the void was a double edged sword. Now you can run a handful of short missions and get exactly what you want. But for those trying to get piles of junk primes, you're going to be SOL. To me, I would RATHER go into the void, get what i want, and get out. Then go do something else, whether it's farming for resources i need, helping a newb out, or even playing another game i've been really wanting to or actually getting some sleep for once instead of spending hours upon hours of void farming in the hopes i get that one part i want.
All in all, this game is a good game and even better to those that are just starting out in it.
So there it is, my counter rant to the "thsi is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ game club". Hope it helps you make a better informed decision to this game.

After having put hundreds of hours into this game, and enjoying most of them, I am unfortunately forced to stop playing. Yes, the recent need to flying dinos was a pain for PvE players. Yes, it's more frustrating to travel because of it. But the game is still rather playable given the new changes. What makes it literally unplayable are the caps on the servers.
For those of you unfamiliar, there is a server limit to the number of things built on platform saddles AND the total number of tamed dinos. This is in addition to the tribe limit of 500 dinos. So, you're HEAVILY penalized for being a new player. My tribe of 3 people has less than 100 dinos total, and no platform saddle items. And we can't build any or tame (or breed for that matter) more dinos. So, we're completely prevented from playing much of the game.
We can't go do the dungeons as easily, and there's no way we'll be able to even attempt any end game activities like bosses without stronger dinos. Meanwhile, the server (like nearly all servers) is filled to the brim with bases and dinos of players you NEVER see online. They pop on to keep all their things from timing out, and just take up space. The entire system is unfair and penalizes anyone who started playing more recently.
So I can't recommend this game to anyone until they change those systems. It's ashame too, because there is some good fun to be had.

Warframe, also known as Grinding Simulator. Let's face it, the game is mostly just an endless grind. You grind to get certain parts for a weapon/warframe, then you grind for the materials that you need in order to build said item. Once done, you essentially continue to grind in order to level it up. Grind for Mods, just to repeat the same process over and over again. Literally, that's Warframe right there (at least in my opinion). I noticed some people saying that there is a LOT of content in this game... where? I can't see it! Where is it hiding?!
Yes, there are plenty of weapons, cosmetic (Primed) items and such, but what's the point? You're going to be stuck repeating the same thing over and over again. The game is also stuck in a permanent Beta, apparently. it's just how it appears to me due to the occasional bugs and glitches I encounter. Yes, Warframe can be fun at times. No, it's not a BAD game. It's just extremely repetitive, lazy, and overrated to no end. If you don't have friends to play it with you're going to grow tired of it rather quickly. Yes, the Story is going to keep you entertained for a while... a short while, but once finished you're back to where you were before: Grind, grind again and grind some more. That's it, rinse and repeat. The game is using the same formula for literally -everything-. Go there, kill a billion of the same enemies until you get the ingredients that you need in order to make your item. Even for the story missions! (Oh, not to mention the RNG, which is essentially going to give you every single item in the game except the one you're actually grinding for), I asked a few friends about their opinions regarding Warframe before deciding to share this, and their responses were mostly along the lines of:
"You grind more than a cheap ♥♥♥♥♥."
"At the end of the day, with all the grinding I could have done elsewhere, I would have at least made some money.."
"Obtaining a Part of the Warframe you're farming for is as rare as getting a Girlfriend. I still don't know what level I unlock that at!"

I have come up from being a newbie with a few friends with nothing to taking down and becoming the alpha tribe on our server. - Many different Biodomes in each map with different creatures and unique enviromental hazards to deal with
Cons:
- Your base will get wiped by higher lvl tribes with more players due to below
- Jumping from server to server with everything you want is easy and quick aka (People build on 0 population servers and safely build up resources to jump to another server and raid bases when everyone is asleep and take all their stuff back to there server with no way to find out what server they are from)
- Hard to protect your dinos from raiders for more than a week or two without being in an alpha tribe

Take Note:
ARK is a evolving game as the early access tag applies, but since the game has a high level of polish and looks amazing people tend forget this and get in the mindset of its in a released state.
If you can't deal with sweeping changes you might not like, WAIT for the final release!
Review:
At this point I have about a 180 hours into the game, others have thousands. This review is from the prospective of someone that has enough playtime to form a good opinion of the game and its mechanics and convey a well rounded opinion.
Art & Graphical Quality:
The game is absolutely beautiful if you have the hardware to run it on at least medium settings bordering on high settings. The game is by no means optimized but still can run decently giving a tolerable experience. Please note that if you are going off there listed minimum req specs you will be disappointed.
They recommend a dual core 2.0 Ghz processor, you can get away with a dual core but you really need at least a dual core with hyper threading giving you two physical cores and two virtual cores providing what I would consider the minimum processing power needed for a tolerable experience. Even with top end hardware you will still get big lag spikes but that is due to poor optimization right now and not reflective of hardware in most cases. I get optimization issues with my I-7 6700K and GTX 1070 but this should change as the game becomes more optimized.
Speaking of the GPU, there minimum of 1 GB of Video ram can be done but again you will be disappointed. In my opinion you need at minimum a GPU with at least 2GB of Vram, even better if that Vram is GDDR5.
Here is a example, a PC with a 4th gen I-3 4150 @3.5GHZ with a GTX 1050 with 2 Gig of GDDR5, 8 Gig's of DDR3 ram runs good @ 1080p on the high preset. Its FPS at low are 31 and high @67fps and the average being 52fps. Once this title has been optimized this machine should run ARK around 60 FPS, yes you could run it with a non hyper threaded chip but it would be less than a desirable experience.
Sound:
The sound in this game as with the graphical quality is superb, sounds are crisp and well done pulling you into the environment making the game-play come to life in a meaningful and imposing way. Whether it being the beautiful ambient sounds or surrounding wildlife it draws you in to a highly immersive experience. (use headphones for a optimal experience)
Game-play:
Do yourself a favor and avoid the official servers, there more aggravating than fun with very few exceptions. PVE servers are littered with abandoned structures and foundations placed everywhere to keep players from building, finding a suitable building location will be frustrating to say the least. On some servers you even have trolls setting up spike walls around spawn points to troll re-spawns and new players. The developers discourage these practices but it dose happen and they are to busy with development to resolve most of the issues in a timely manner. Official PVP servers deal with some of these issues as well but not quite as bad as they have more entertaining ways to get there jolly's.
Your best bet is doing non-dedicated servers or rent a server to play with friends, it costs around $13 a month for a rental server with 10 slots and can be increased as needed. Basically this gives you control to what happens in your server and even if you do open it up to the public you can deal with the trolls immediately returning your playing experience and your guests to a enjoyable one.
You also can join other private servers and there are some good ones out there. (just be wary of Admin abuse) Even weeding through the admin abuse servers will be easier than playing on official servers in my opinion as all official servers are plagued with the above stated issues and more.
Conclusion / TLDR:
Ark is a great survival game that draws you in and can and will provide you with 1000's of hours of rewarding and fun game-play. I highly recommend this game as it is fun to play and is a fresh take and concept to the many other survival games out there. In my opinion Ark is a survival game being done right and I look forward to the finished release.
Disclaimer: A tolerable gaming experience is very subjective, what is not tolerable to me might be just fine to others, so if you disagree with my observations here that's fine and good gaming to all.

The game is user-hostile.  The interface is horrible with no in-game indications whatsoever of what's going on.  Don't go "fresh" into this game at all unless you gain satisfaction from an overwhelming system of punishment.
I can understand holding off on making your UI reasonable during early access.  But there's a limit to what's usable and what's just plain awful.  Sliders everywhere, as far as the eye can see.  And little to no guidance as to which slider does what or how it will effect gameplay.  Numbers everywhere with no context into the usefulness of what's going on.  Who cares?  I don't.  It doesn't look like the devs do either.  Maybe make a wizard out of the game setup so at the very least I can understand just what section of sliders makes a change to what aspects of the world.
Character customization?  No.  Don't pretend to have it.  There's one style of male body and one style of female body.Any change to the base values just makes the character look unnatural.  And no, there are no downloadable presets.  Or maybe the servers just weren't up.
The mechanics feel haphazardly tuned.  Every action requires you to invest hunger, thirst, or stamina.  But that doesn't mean you have a reliable source from which to draw on in the early game.  I've had spawns that were near somewhat tame creatures (dodos, fish) that turn into murder fests within the first 5 minutes.  The furthest I got was a little thatch hut--maybe that's the most fun I had in the game.  But it did't take long to get murdered by birds and piranha.
The heat/cold system makes no sense to me.  Suddenly, it's too hot when 10 minutes ago it was too cold.  Am I supposed to be naked? Or am I supposed to wear clothes?
The gathering system is atrocious.  It doesn't feel balanced at all.  Harvest what feels like a few acres of tatch, fiber, and berries to build a tiny hut and some basic clothing.  Get overencumbred very easily because you end up gathering dozens of material byproducts that you're not interested in whatsoever and then worry that you have to choose between spending your upgrade points on shelter or on storage.  No.  You can't have both at the same time.  It's either a house or a box.
50 animal hides for a BASIC bed?  C'mon!  And that's for the privelege of having a respawn point...
No, this isn't a fun game.  It's an endurance test.  And I had the wisdom to stay off of the multiplayer PVP servers.  I can only imagine based on the reviews below just how much of a cluster that is.

10/10 - Great game, better with friends near and far.
I have enjoyed playing this game and I highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys Halo, Tera, and Overwatch. You get the look and feel (as well as the game night fun with friends) of Halo with the community style of Tera (including a guild system), and the archetypal characters of Overwatch. Sure, paying in game for items and characters is fine for some but the game is built to allow nonpaying players to acquire everything available to purchase in game with enough progress and effort. Want a weapon you see on the in game market? Buy the blueprint for it with in game currency naturally earned by doing missions and looting (or find a drop, earn from a mission...), build it in the ship foundry once you've gathered materials from missions and looting, wait for it to be built in a timely manner and voila, no need to buy platinum with real money. Still playing one of the three warframes you choose to start with but want to play a different one without paying platinum? Easy, peasy, lemon squeezy. Just rank up to 2, 4, 6, etc to get another warframe slot, do missions, maybe farm a boss or two to get the warframe part blueprints, gather resources and credits to build said parts, get ahold of the main blueprint as a drop or by credits in the market, put it all together and bam. New warframe. There's so much more to this game than missions though. Space fights with archwing missions, quests of varying mission types, an expanding universe of possibilities, lovable cat and dog (even robot) pets to raise and train, challenging bosses and busy trading community, clans (guilds) to join to help you access research to acquire certain warframes and weapons or make new friends and such...4 man party system that is completely optional for missions you need help with...annoying Ordis. You can play it casual or really get into the game with a passion, It's perfect for so many play styles, for so many players and it just keeps getting better with every update, adding more warframes, content, pets...so promising.
If you try it out, I hope you enjoy it. I sure have.

TL;DR: I've quit playing Warframe and I strongly recommend you against playing this game as it is not actually fun and is run by developers and administrators who do not value their players.
...
It's been an interesting last couple months for me in my life, ironically also time that I spent away from Warframe. It started off at the start of May when I simultaneously got sent out of state on a work assignment and also got a 30-day ban from Warframe's forums thanks to its power-tripping, fascist and draconian moderators. While the temporary ban was a slap in the face, since it was over trivial crap such as posting a funny picture in response to a post or saying "git gud" every now and then (seriously, they don't allow you to say "git gud". WTF?), it didn't necessarily bother me as I was too preoccupied with work to even bother with the forums or the game itself.
The funny thing about being given that long away from the game, though, is that it gives you a chance to step back and evaluate your experience with the game overall and to consider how it's gone and what you think of it. But most importantly, it gave me time to think about the most crucial point overall: Is Warframe a fun game to play?
What I've come to realize is that the answer is No; Warframe is not a fun game. At best, it is a mediocre, boring game, where the overall objective seems to be to simply convince yourself that you're having fun so that you can obsessive-compulsively complete the tedious little goal-posts set up in front of you of "Get this achievement", "Master this weapon", "Complete this questline", "Max this Warframe", "Get this item drop", and so on. When it comes down to it, Warframe is a sparse, vapid, content-less game that relies upon time-gating and RNG to confuse you and keep you under the impression that what you're doing is fun and interesting as well as hide how dismally short and boring the game's quests actually are. If one were to utilize 'platinum rushing' (spending the game's premium currency to speed things up - a common free-to-play game gimmick) at every step of the way, it's likely that you could complete the entirety of Warframe's story content as well as acquire almost everything in the game in less than a day.
What's worse, the game's developers spend the majority of their time churning out cosmetics and other superfluous nonsense instead of addressing more pressing issues such as fixing game-breaking bugs that stick around for months/years or more at a time, balancing the game's content, and adding real (non-cosmetics) content to the game.
That attitude on their part is unsurprising, too, because it leads back to another realization I've had: The game's developers do not respect my time. After all, to them, I - and all of you - are simply piggy banks. Little human-shaped ATMs that are supposed to simply open their wallets and faithfully hand money over to them and then go away. If my time was respected, there would be more to the game than such insanely aggressive RNG that only exists to time-gate the game so that you remain on the developer-designated hamster wheel long enough for them to churn out more vapid cosmetics for you to buy. In-between working, I came back to check up on Warframe and saw that a new un-vaulting had occurred (an event where "prime" items that were removed from the loot tables were again made temporarily available, in order to encourage players to continue mindlessly grinding for rare item drops) and now a few shiny little primes were up for grabs. It's also the first time where I just stared at such information, felt absolutely nothing, and thought "Why even bother?" No, really, why bother? I've done just about everything that can even be done in the game - far more than I should've ever wasted the time even doing - chasing after a notion of fun-having that isn't even there. The prime un-vaulting has come and will go (or has gone? I don't even remember when it ends/ended), I'll have made no effort to take part in it, and don't even care. It's a complete waste of time with no real reward, much like the entire game itself.
So with that in mind, and neglecting to mention the rest of what's wrong with this game for time's sake, I've quit playing Warframe and I highly suggest the rest of you avoid it. I will not be wasting any more time or money on this game, and probably won't even bother with any of Digital Extremes' other games; I can't imagine they're any better than this, if this game is supposed to be representative of their craftsmanship.
Hopefully this review saves you from wasting time on this game. I wish I had known what I know now, so I could've spent all the hours I wasted on it doing something else instead.
P.s. git gud, Digital Extremes. GIT GUD.

People have to actually play the game, and not just grind every single Warframe and weapon to max level on one mission node.

- The market via the ship, at first it was a bit confusing, most people thought that DE did away with buying blueprints all together, however. All they did was make a single page for each item, yes, they have the Platinum purchace on top, but everything is still there, blueprints bought with Credits and all.
- The lootshare style Fissures that replaced Void missions. Granted, I loved Void missions, they were awesome. But, with the new Fissure/Relic system there is more reward in playing with people that solo. More people = more chances at getting the Prime item you were looking for.
There or a ton of other reasons this game is still amazing, most notably the fact that this past update has effectively "removed" all the people that complained about everything while everyone that still plays worked together to get everything figured out and streamlined.
