Anyone that is just now considering playing this game, and or, is glossing over reviews to see what people think about the latest update: Specters of the Rail.
Here's my take on it, it has effectively changed the game into something that is far more playable than it once was, IF YOUR NOT JUST SALTY THEY TOOK AWAY THE "EASY" BUTTON AND ACTUALLY TOOK THE TIME TO UNDERSTAND THE UPDATE for example.
Seriously, people literally rage quit a game they dropped potentially hundreds of dollars into because they didnt take the time to get familiarized with the update.
- First and formost, Draco, the most abused node in the entire game, and the single most thing that people complained about with the update because of this fact, was moved to a different planet, with a different map layout, that now isn't nearly as exploited for experience points. People have to actually play the game, and not just grind every single Warframe and weapon to max level on one mission node.
- The new starchart [Well, old starchart with a facelift] Nobody lost any progress with the update, I had every planet with every node unlocked and post update, everything but new content was intact and ready to go
- The market via the ship, at first it was a bit confusing, most people thought that DE did away with buying blueprints all together, however. All they did was make a single page for each item, yes, they have the Platinum purchace on top, but everything is still there, blueprints bought with Credits and all.
- The lootshare style Fissures that replaced Void missions. Granted, I loved Void missions, they were awesome. But, with the new Fissure/Relic system there is more reward in playing with people that solo. More people = more chances at getting the Prime item you were looking for.
There or a ton of other reasons this game is still amazing, most notably the fact that this past update has effectively "removed" all the people that complained about everything while everyone that still plays worked together to get everything figured out and streamlined.

This is pretty much my favorite game I've played here on steam. Multi player, pvp, pve, and solo play are all really amazing options. Content is updated fairly often (around once every 2-3 weeks), slowed down from when the game first released (which was once every 3 days). I bought this game a month after it launched on Steam and have never felt that I wasted money. The game has both free and purchasable DLC, The Center which is a new map and Scorched Earth which is a new map and adds additional creatures.
This game isn't easy. It is not like minecraft; wake up punch a tree, continue on. Each day you play has new challenges, and if you restart (though you learn spears and Bolas should be gold-plated for how amazing they are) you still have appropriate challenges.
PROS:
: The few public servers I played on had large communities and were pretty nice, despite usual PVP talk. Private Servers are available if you want to join other people's paid maps, which is usually a smaller community (5-30 people in comarison to 50-75 on public servers). Or play solo on your own computer until you feel confident enough to play with others.
: You start building right off the bat. You need to if your going to survive, though it doesn't have to be pretty for it to hold back a Raptor or a Carno. You can even build underwater with vacuum tanks now. (Its was late game. After Bosses late game.)
: Huge modding community. Public Servers won't have mods of course, but the majority of private ones do (Usually quality of life style, some with adding paid DLC in for free, some adding babies/eggs in the wild).  (Annunaki; Look it up!) If vanilla ever feels like it gets old, there are plenty of overhauls such as Primitive Plus game play, Annunaki, Bush People NPC Mod. Ark now has an 'official' mod group that gets paid for it; they put out quality work every update.
: So many creature. No some aren't true dinosaurs, and yes there are Wyverns and some 'fantasy' styled creatures. There are Dossiers (think like teasers) for some Dinos that are future released (I think only like 5 left?), and there are so many creatures available to tame. Som can't be, some can, and some just wreck your face in for even thinking about it. (Looking at you Allosauros. Worse than a freaking Giganotasaurus.) You can breed them, catch, tame, sacrifice them for more tames, loose them, kill them (Opps :/ )(Also build them a gravestone - its just common courtesy.) You can do anything on this island with Dinosaurs.
: Another game available is Ark SURVIVAL Evolved. Its all this on a Hunger Games styled Map. People win cash every month. Cool right?
CONS:
None!
Lol JK
: For me public servers always seemed a little....slower/laggier. I'm located on the East coast so after playing for a while I eventually switched to playing on privates. Privates however have other challenges. The game could be totally broken (1 tree hit = 10k wood + 3k Thatch), or it could be set up where admid roasts you every weekend on 'Purge' styled PVP. Or something that is trully sad, the server could be wipped. After hatching triplet quetz from eggs. Sniff. Eventually you find one you like/purchase one for your self.
: Build has improved (VASTLY), but sometimes you still get difficult moment placing items, finding level ground, etc. It makes you swear, but then you just keep going. Part of the game at this point.
: Sometimes on private servers, Mod's just break the whole game and you can't play until it has to be updated. You just come back in like 5 hours and the admin usually has done it by then.
: The game has so many Dinos. Starting over it makes it somewhat hard to choose what to tame/kill/run away from. Sometimes it feels like the devs are just adding dinos with unique properties every single new dino update. Or they break my pteranadons wings. Sniff.
: That game? Survival of the Fittest? So freaking hard. Never actually won one. Always keep coming back though!

Ark is an interesting game but I really can not recommend it.
The main reason is that at the current time there is no way to have a stable game.   Every game I have played has basically ended due to bugs from either Ark updates or mod updates.  The way the game is setup you HAVE to get the updates.   Even if you set Ark not to update in Steam and launch Ark from the executable avoiding the Steam launch, Steam will occasionally still update the game.  This will cause a version mismatch between the server (which you can control) and the client (which you can not).
The updates will often invalidate what you have been having fun with, breeding dinos for example, so 10’s or 100’s of your hours will be wasted.  The goal that you were going for will be removed.   This is why there are so many♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off posts.   Since this has happened many, many times over the last year and a half it appears that Wildcard does not care.
The straw that broke the camels back is the new, horrid UI.   This is a great example of form over function.  Things that were easy and efficient before are now annoying and cumbersome.   What was easily readable text is now hard to read.  Mouse movement between inventory which used to be adjacent is now across the screen.   Information that was easily available before is now hidden unless you use pop-up tool tips which hide adjacent items.
The game was more fun a year ago than it is now.

So after about 180 days of playing, getting a decent chunk of the equipment worth using, and over 800 hours, invested, I think I should probably give a more in-depth opinion about this game.
To start with, Warframe is a sci-fi-themed TPS/hack-and-slash game that uses a type of class-based player selection by having you control the titular "warframes", mysterious exosuits, each of which have a variety of different abilities for various situations. And with your guns and pointy stick of choice; you must carve a bloody path through the galaxy to maintain the balance of power in the system (and you know, get paid).
It also has a crafting system that takes a page out of mobile games, in which everything is locked behind a time wall (items can take anywhere from 1 minute, 12 hours, to 3 days to finish). Crafting has a lot of emphasis here as its largely required for you to get the best pieces of equipment in the game, and apart from cosmetic items like decorative armor parts and bobble heads; everything in the game can be crafted and obtained without using premium currency, so WF's F2P title is spot on.
For warframe's actual gameplay, its farming. That's all you really do here, farm resources, weapon and warframe components, mods and credits to create end-tier items. All this just to allow you to farm more items better.
Perhaps that's the most glaring problem of the game and why I can't recommend it after all this time; warframe is basically a blood-drenched version of farmville. There's no real challenging end-game to put all your hard-earned gear to the test, because the difficulty is so wonky that either everything is too easy that you get through places without any resistance, or so hard that you have to resort to cheesing through the game using specific builds, with the game never achiveing a middle-ground that makes for a challenging yet fair game (something a lot of online RPGs have already accomplished).
With that, that's why I can't recommend this game; the lack of meaningful difficulty. It'll sustain you for hours with at first when you're trying to get to the top, but when you get there; its kind of underwhelming and it just kinda makes you feel all your efforts went to waste. Don't get me wrong, the game is still fun. I wouldn't have spent all this time and money if it wasn't. Combat is solid and wrecking platoons of enemies feel murderously fulfilling. But overall, it just lacks that true bit that makes grind and farm-based games fun; a reward worth justifying the time and effort you've invested in your grinds.
P.S.: This is a post-Specters of the Rail addenum - end-game has become even more irrelevant with the introduction of void rifts. This game really is turning into farmville with ninjas.
P.S.S: This is a post-patched Specters of the Rail addenum - End game is still dead, but there's actual difficulty and variety now. Its kinda...sorta fun, but still not enough for me to reverse my opinion.

Ok first of all... the negative parts:
Ark is a really great game but everything takes sooooooo looooong to achieve... I mean it takes hours... even real life days, to build a simple house! I've been playing this game for about 2-3 days and i'm not even level 20 yet! And everything is so hard to get... and add menacing dinosaurs getting in your way while doing this... it just isn't too pleasant...
Another thing is the dinosaurs are insanely overpowered... I mean like... i was a level 10 to 15 and i took on a level one trike... and it owned my ###, I was so ticked off (to be fair there was a level 28 trike right next to it to assist it)... a raptor jumpscared me and i had some fairly good gear (it was hide lol)... it nearly killed me... i was able to collect a supply crate from a beacon and when I traveled home... another raptor attacked me and i was pretty low on health... I barely made it to the water in time (Knowing that raptors are faulty swimmers) to escape from the raptor. You gotta turn down their aggression developers! I mean C'MON MAN GEEZ!!!
Another thing is the lag... when you start up the game and join a world it lags insanely!!! And mind you i had an anti-lag code! and after it's finally loaded in all the graphics... even the small things, like turning your head = lag... stabbing a dodo with a spear = lag... walking = lag... etcetra... etcetra... etcetra! So thats a thing that they need to work on (P.S. imagine how laggy it would be in multiplayer!!!)
Positive things:
But just the element of it all is really good... i mean after you make a great accomplishment it feels so good... and the models... animations... textures... I mean when i looked at a trike... the eyes actually moved... that one bit just makes this game feel so much more realistic!
The adventuring aspect isn't bad either! there is so much to explore... and with challenges at the helm... it just makes you feel so much more alive... from simple beaches... to terrifying caves... this game is just so exciting and adrenaline inducing!
And finally... the content! There is so much to do! So many items to gather and it is so accurate! I mean the defecating addition could be taken out... but it's the simple things that make this game feel like you're actually there!
In my opinion... i'd say it is a very well rounded, accurate game that could use some tinkering, but other than that... it's not too bad! I'd definetly reccomend this game once its fully complete and finished with early access!

Without a doubt the BEST model of F2P I've ever seen! NOTHING in the game is locked behind paywalls aside from cosmetics that do nothing for gameplay AND the payed currency is tradeible in game, which is great because it means you can trade the high level dups you get to other players. Tenicaly, it's possible to own everything (aside from the User Uploaded stuff and the spec-editions that aren't avalible anymore) without paying a single thing!
I had to put that first because it's a big deal! This is one of the only F2P games I can think off that is totally 100% fair to all users. While the game does have a lot of down-time with item creation, taking hours at a time which can be sped up for real cash, I can understand that for the lack of anything completely overpowered only being avalible to paying members.
The gameplay itself is incredibly fun. I often call this game "Cyber Ninjas In Space" becaus that's pretty much what you are. A thrilling mix of gunplay and melee combined with a smooth-as-heck parkor engine keeps even people like me (who don't often play shooters) hooked to the end.
At the crux of it all, Warframe is a grind. You grind for the blueprints to build stuff, then you grind for the stuff to make it, then you wait for the hours to tick by, but the gameplay is so much fun (even more so with friends) it doesn't feel like a grind unless the RNG is being REALLY nasty and you're having to run the mission for the 50th time.
I can't praise this game enough! Hopefully more F2P games will adopt similar models from now on.

Looks familiar, no? Released in mid 2015 the game still suffers from countless Bugs, Performance problems and the usually biggest  issue: Players.
This game is not really more than any other "survival open world" game currently on steam, except for the fact that its setting uses technology and ancient dinosaurs.
How the game usually goes: Spawn without anything, buuld up a small hut, upgrade lvl and gear, upgrade your base, upgrade lvl and gear, upgrade base [...].
Unless you increase the exp and ressources gathered by a huge ammount it will take a lot of time and farming to be able to reach higher levels and thus higher tiers of equipement, bases and dinosaur taming. However, unless you are playing on a PvE server, this all doesnt matter. Why is that?
Because most of the playerbase enjoys just one thing: PvP. They find enjoyment only in getting max tier and lvl right away and doing PvP / base raiding instead of playing the acutall survival part.
This is just like any other EA Survival Game ever. Only difference: You can ride dinos into battle. Yay.
So much for the gameplay. If you want to play the initiall "survival" game, you have to play solo or look for a server with PvE only and Exp / resource gain set to normal.
The Visuals look stunning, right? Well, only in videos and screenshots. Despite having more than twice the required minimum hardware the game runs on a solid 20-25 fps only when set to minimum. It's like playing GTA V on an N64. The game can be great, but if it looks like you are playing in 1987 you just wont have much fun.
Overall: No, i cannot recommend this. Early access forever, perfomance is still♥♥♥♥♥♥and the playerbase consists mostly of PvP Maniacs who don't even know that this game is a "Survival" game - at least according to the store page.

So after about 180 days of playing, getting a decent chunk of the equipment worth using, and over 800 hours, invested, I think I should probably give a more in-depth opinion about this game.
To start with, Warframe is a sci-fi-themed TPS/hack-and-slash game that uses a type of class-based player selection by having you control the titular "warframes", mysterious exosuits, each of which have a variety of different abilities for various situations. And with your guns and pointy stick of choice; you must carve a bloody path through the galaxy to maintain the balance of power in the system (and you know, get paid).
It also has a crafting system that takes a page out of mobile games, in which everything is locked behind a time wall (items can take anywhere from 1 minute, 12 hours, to 3 days to finish). Crafting has a lot of emphasis here as its largely required for you to get the best pieces of equipment in the game, and apart from cosmetic items like decorative armor parts and bobble heads; everything in the game can be crafted and obtained without using premium currency, so WF's F2P title is spot on.
For warframe's actual gameplay, its farming. That's all you really do here, farm resources, weapon and warframe components, mods and credits to create end-tier items. All this just to allow you to farm more items better.
Perhaps that's the most glaring problem of the game and why I can't recommend it after all this time; warframe is basically a blood-drenched version of farmville. There's no real challenging end-game to put all your hard-earned gear to the test, because the difficulty is so wonky that either everything is too easy that you get through places without any resistance, or so hard that you have to resort to cheesing through the game using specific builds, with the game never achiveing a middle-ground that makes for a challenging yet fair game (something a lot of online RPGs have already accomplished).
With that, that's why I can't recommend this game; the lack of meaningful difficulty. It'll sustain you for hours with at first when you're trying to get to the top, but when you get there; its kind of underwhelming and it just kinda makes you feel all your efforts went to waste. Don't get me wrong, the game is still fun. I wouldn't have spent all this time and money if it wasn't. Combat is solid and wrecking platoons of enemies feel murderously fulfilling. But overall, it just lacks that true bit that makes grind and farm-based games fun; a reward worth justifying the time and effort you've invested in your grinds.
P.S.: This is a post-Specters of the Rail addenum - end-game has become even more irrelevant with the introduction of void rifts. This game really is turning into farmville with ninjas.
P.S.S: This is a post-patched Specters of the Rail addenum - End game is still dead, but there's actual difficulty and variety now. Its kinda...sorta fun, but still not enough for me to reverse my opinion.

Now, my experiences are *ALL* on a private server with just my husband and a few friends, so this is from a pure gameplay standpoint. From what I've heard, the public servers are just that much worse due to other players, so I can't imagine my score changing if I had played, except to even worse.
This game had, and possibly still has potential. The only way for it to reach it, however, in my opnion, would be for some other company more competent to take it away from the devs before they decide to play another round of "how can we ♥♥♥♥ this up for the players and still keep some going?"
When my husband and I first started playing, it was during the winter event (when Ark had a big sale, so there were a lot of new players joining) where everything was frozen over. Which was nifty... except for the fact we were very quickly freezing to death. We looked on the forums for a soultion, and the answer was basically to beg older players to give you some hide armor, which was the only one that could deal with the cold. Not really possibly on a new server. So after several attempts of us trying to keep warm with fires and what clothing we could make, and failing miserably, we upped the Fortitude stat (so you notice the temperature changes less) so one point would give you 40 Fortitude. 3 levels later, and we could actually play.
So that was the first round of "Wow, they didn't think that one through" and the forums talking about people quitting because of it.
The second one came fairly quickly after, with them deciding to 'balance the tamed dinosaurs' which basically meant nerfing the hell out of the stats. Personally, I think the damage they do is fairly insane, but when the attack damage is also tied to the GATHERING ability of the dinosaurs, there's not really much you can do there, is there? Oh wait, there is. They could have had a gathering stat, which would have solved a hell of a lot. Or had it so there was different sizes of dinos, and they did 2x or 1/2x versus smaller or larger sizes, respectively. Or a ton of other options they didn't bother with. But enough people complained about this that they put something in the .ini to 'set them back to normal'
So that hemmoraged a lot of players too.
Then there was the issue with BattleEye. Yes, cheat detectors are always invavsive and give off false positives, but BattleEye is KNOWN to be a really bad one. They could have chosen many others, but they decided to go with the one with the bad reputation. Thank goodness you can turn it off with servers.
There were several other minor updates too. And with the constant glitches that didn't get fixed (the devs seem much more interested in adding new crap versus fixing anything old), the lack of much to do after a certain point, and the general worry of 'what are they going to nerf/break/make me like the game less this time', we quit after about 5 months of playing. Yes, I got that many hours in 5 months.
And no, I wasn't playing during the idiotic DLC fiasco, but it's not suprising. The devs just seem to like playing the 'what can we do to♥♥♥♥♥♥off the player base' game. And I for one, don't play games that play that game.

TLDR: Game is still fun, people are throwing tamper tantrums over a patch instead of logically thinking about, would still say give it a go.
There is currently a lot of hate going around right now for this game do tot he last patch. And fair enough its impact was HUGE. At the same time people are also basing their entire perception of this game based on one aspect. So this review is going to cover the game in general, how it was prior to this patch, and after the patch.
Let me just start by saying the game itself is fun. The concept is unique in that it is your basic survior, but instead of zombies its dinos; dinos that you can tame and ride. If it was in the Jurassic Park movies, chances are you will see it in game. The devs went step further though. Yes they brought in the classics (Rexes, Brontos, Trikes, Stegos, etc.), but they also are continually introducing more creatures from various time periods that I am sure quite a few people were not aware of. Take this with a grain of salt too. The dinos portrayed in this game are more reminiscent of hollywoods style rather historical acccuracy. But who cares when you're on a rex running down the guy who just tried to rob you.
Some Aspects:
-Tame and ride dinos
--Build and defend your base while raiding others
Its online PVP. Wear your thick skin
-There is a PVE and solo play option as well.
-You can form tribes and tribe alliances
-Plethora of player hosted servers as well official servers to choose from
-You will die. If you are having really rotten luck, you may die several times right as you spawn. Luck of the draw on whats   around you at the time. If this happens just keep cycling through spawn points.
Game Pre-patch 256
For the purpose of this review I will be focusing mainly on non-scorched earth dinos and map (The Island and The Center).
Currently there are 55 non-flying dinos (land based and aquatic) in game that you can tame and ride. Comparatively there are only 5 flight based dinos in game that you can tame and ride. Of those 5 only 2 are considered essential. The pteradon and quetzal. Prior to the patch these two fliers dominated both the pvp and pve landscape of the game. The pteradon is the fastest flyer. It is suppose to have low health and low stam though to counter that. Its purpose is suppose to be an early game flyer for new players and fast scout in the end-game. What it became instead was the go to pvp dino. Between its broken stamina and speed, it could fly across an entire map without landing, fly fast enough to out pace a bases defenses (it would go right past before any guns could fire), and stay airborne for long periods of time. Basically exceeding its role as a fast light-scout. The quetzel literally could stay airborne indefinitely. High weight capacity, high health, and a broken stammina mechanic, this was the other go-to dino that was a must have for any player/tribe. If the quetz was running low on stam, all you would have to do it dismount. It's saddle is big enough to where you could do this airborne without falling off. So without having to land, and high in the sky out of reach, a player would wait 10-20 seconds for their quetz to rest up and then carry on with their taks. Also, the quetz is one of 5 dinos that can have a platform saddle. This means you could build a small base on its back. I will let your imagination fill in the blanks with that one. So between those two specific dinos, taming anything else is more out of want than need. All other dinos are just eye-candy at best as they are out-classed and out-performed by 2 flying based dinos. In short = gameplay broken
Post Patch 256
Here is where everyones anger begins. All flying dinos got a health and stammina reduction and their speed capped at a fixed amount. Now this was needed. Flyers were broken and the game meta was getting boring. With that said, the nerf that took place was beyond huge. We will use the pteradon for the explanation. This was the super fast dino that could out pace base defenses. Players over time had gotten used to flying it at 200%+ its base speed. After the patch, a perfect tamed ptera is capped at 135%. A big reduction and it is noticable. The devs have since come and said this is not the final number and they will continue to change till they a find a good medium. But lets face it, no one likes change. Well personally I say tough. I look at this as a good thing. The game meta has been changed up, people are now forced to re-think a strategy that used broken mechanics, and it forces players to look to other dinos as well. Could the devs have communicated this better, absolutley. But the players also need to remember, although we draw close to the official release date, this game is still technically in EA. That means any and everything is subject to change.
Conclusion: Now players can no longer travel across a map in 10 seconds without landing. Boo Hoo. The world just became bigger and more dangerous. Improvise, adapt, and overcome. Was this a needed change, yes. Could it have been implemented and communicated better, without a doubt. Am I going to stop playing? No. I would still reccommend this game. It is still fun. I will hold my final judment till its official release. Till then, take changes with a grain of salt.

However in this game the PvP isn't necessarily enjoyable, and feels slightly skewed in balance (Certain weapons are garbage and certain ones are too good)
The PvE eventually gets old, as the usual enemies and biomes are recycled over and over. The same bosses are encountered time and time again. Eventually the mastery levels and syndicate standings become meaningless, and become more of a tedious grind to get to the next one, only to be rewarded by more slots for weapons and such, which by the time you get to mastery rank 10 or so and enjoy the game, you've probably dropped about $200 on a prime access pack or some platinum, which you'll probably buy slots anyways then.
The market itself features items that are insanely overpriced, and although you can trade for platinum (paid currency) it's once again a chore to acquire such platinum.
In other words, play it to enjoy it for the few hundred hours you get on it, get something nice for yourself in the market if you feel like it, however once you get there, you're pretty much done as the updates are way too far apart to take any real interest in the game to keep it fresh. TLDR: Game is still fun, people are throwing tamper tantrums over a patch instead of logically thinking about, would still say give it a go.
There is currently a lot of hate going around right now for this game do tot he last patch. And fair enough its impact was HUGE. At the same time people are also basing their entire perception of this game based on one aspect. So this review is going to cover the game in general, how it was prior to this patch, and after the patch.
Let me just start by saying the game itself is fun. The concept is unique in that it is your basic survior, but instead of zombies its dinos; dinos that you can tame and ride. If it was in the Jurassic Park movies, chances are you will see it in game. The devs went step further though. Yes they brought in the classics (Rexes, Brontos, Trikes, Stegos, etc.), but they also are continually introducing more creatures from various time periods that I am sure quite a few people were not aware of. Take this with a grain of salt too. The dinos portrayed in this game are more reminiscent of hollywoods style rather historical acccuracy. But who cares when you're on a rex running down the guy who just tried to rob you.
Some Aspects:
-Tame and ride dinos
--Build and defend your base while raiding others
Its online PVP. Wear your thick skin
-There is a PVE and solo play option as well.
-You can form tribes and tribe alliances
-Plethora of player hosted servers as well official servers to choose from
-You will die. If you are having really rotten luck, you may die several times right as you spawn. Luck of the draw on whats   around you at the time. If this happens just keep cycling through spawn points.
Game Pre-patch 256
For the purpose of this review I will be focusing mainly on non-scorched earth dinos and map (The Island and The Center).
Currently there are 55 non-flying dinos (land based and aquatic) in game that you can tame and ride. Comparatively there are only 5 flight based dinos in game that you can tame and ride. Of those 5 only 2 are considered essential. The pteradon and quetzal. Prior to the patch these two fliers dominated both the pvp and pve landscape of the game. The pteradon is the fastest flyer. It is suppose to have low health and low stam though to counter that. Its purpose is suppose to be an early game flyer for new players and fast scout in the end-game. What it became instead was the go to pvp dino. Between its broken stamina and speed, it could fly across an entire map without landing, fly fast enough to out pace a bases defenses (it would go right past before any guns could fire), and stay airborne for long periods of time. Basically exceeding its role as a fast light-scout. The quetzel literally could stay airborne indefinitely. High weight capacity, high health, and a broken stammina mechanic, this was the other go-to dino that was a must have for any player/tribe. If the quetz was running low on stam, all you would have to do it dismount. It's saddle is big enough to where you could do this airborne without falling off. So without having to land, and high in the sky out of reach, a player would wait 10-20 seconds for their quetz to rest up and then carry on with their taks. Also, the quetz is one of 5 dinos that can have a platform saddle. This means you could build a small base on its back. I will let your imagination fill in the blanks with that one. So between those two specific dinos, taming anything else is more out of want than need. All other dinos are just eye-candy at best as they are out-classed and out-performed by 2 flying based dinos. In short = gameplay broken
Post Patch 256
Here is where everyones anger begins. All flying dinos got a health and stammina reduction and their speed capped at a fixed amount. Now this was needed. Flyers were broken and the game meta was getting boring. With that said, the nerf that took place was beyond huge. We will use the pteradon for the explanation. This was the super fast dino that could out pace base defenses. Players over time had gotten used to flying it at 200%+ its base speed. After the patch, a perfect tamed ptera is capped at 135%. A big reduction and it is noticable. The devs have since come and said this is not the final number and they will continue to change till they a find a good medium. But lets face it, no one likes change. Well personally I say tough. I look at this as a good thing. The game meta has been changed up, people are now forced to re-think a strategy that used broken mechanics, and it forces players to look to other dinos as well. Could the devs have communicated this better, absolutley. But the players also need to remember, although we draw close to the official release date, this game is still technically in EA. That means any and everything is subject to change.
Conclusion: Now players can no longer travel across a map in 10 seconds without landing. Boo Hoo. The world just became bigger and more dangerous. Improvise, adapt, and overcome. Was this a needed change, yes. Could it have been implemented and communicated better, without a doubt. Am I going to stop playing? No. I would still reccommend this game. It is still fun. I will hold my final judment till its official release. Till then, take changes with a grain of salt.

My favorite Free to Play game. Absolutely unique, fairly well polished, and with tons of content.
This game despite being a F2P that started years ago, is still getting tons of new content, events, free things along with the payed things, and it's pretty great.
Most of the game is PvE, with a smaller entirely optional PvP section. This lends to an on average better community with less jerks and more fun game playing. Not to mention the game is fine if you wish to play it completely singleplayer as well. You will have to log-in and be online, but playing everything singleplayer is perfectly fine (If understandably usually more challenging)
The combat is one of a kind, with there being long ranged shooting, close range melee, and many different weapons that mix up the two. You'd be hard pressed to find a game that had combat and movement like this. Every different weapon is just that, very different. While some are obviously better & more powerful than others, pretty much every one, melee and ranged, have a different style of play required to be able to use them. Combine this with the abilities that each Warframe (different character) has, and there are tons of ways for you to play in this game.
The freedom of movement in Warframe is awesome. You can pretty much get anywhere you want in this game (Though beware of invisible walls). The developers really made a movement system that *feels* like you are a ninja, or a space ninja. Like everything it isn't perfect, but overall you have speed and precision with your jumps and spins.
The biggest negative I can see with the game is the naturally grindy F2P-ness it has. To make that new weapon, you WILL have to play many different missions in order to get the materials and credits needed to make it. In order to make that new character, you WILL have to fight bosses over and over to get the parts required to assemble the character. And even when you do get the things needed to assemble your new item, you WILL still need to wait upwards of 24 hours to be able to use that character after it is assembled. Warframe is a game that will require you to be patient for your things, or to just have a lot of money to outright buy the item or rush the build time instantly.
Thankfully, there will be plenty of things to do while you have things being assembled. The game rewards you while you grind for stuff with XP & levels for all of your gear, lots of credits, and lots of resources. It rewards players who take their time and explore the level to find extra loot, and there is always some new alert mission or event mission to do while waiting for a thing to build or something. Along with the fun & satisfying gameplay, grinding usually isn't nearly as bad as it can be in other games.
Almost everything in this game is obtainable from a 100% free perspective. Though a lot of very less important things like cosmetics and such will only be obtained for free through trading in-game items for the paid currency with other players. To begin with, most things are already obtainable for free, but even the things that seemingly only cost paid currency are obtainable if you barter enough with other players. My experiences with trading in-game items I earned free for paid currency with other players have been 90% positive, and I have earned many of my cosmetic items this way.
If you are looking for a F2P game that has lots of content available from the start, if you're looking for the type of F2P game that makes you actually WANT to give money to the devs, then I recommend Warframe. A very fun & unique experience.

This game used to be fun, but the devs have focused not on adding progression to a challenge, but just screwing over everyone now.
Recent patches have added Dinos that instantly steal things from you, typically found in packs of 3 and they'll run in 3 different directions, so you're guaranteed to lose 2 items, and it's pot luck if the dino you chase down still has the item in its inventory when you kill it.

Birds, which when you kill that pego to get your item back, will agress you in the starting area knocking your weapons out of your hands. and killing you

A mob that destroys rafts in 3 hits, limiting your mobility around the island.
Add to this the issues with the server actually registering that you hit the mobs, that you're trying to save yourself from/retrieve your items from, and all of the fun has been kicked out of this game. It used to be about starting somewhere building momentum to push into the next more challenging area, with great opportunities for exploration. Now you spend your life chasing down your missing items, into a fight for your life when you kill the thing, which kills the exploration, and the abiliity to choose and take on your next challenge.
Taking down big mobs in this game involves, standing above it on a cliff where it can't hit you and just shooting it till it drops (Gee that sure is fun and engaging gameplay), because the AI is so bad, it either runs directly at you or directly away, it has no pathing capability. After nearly 1800 hours and roughly a year's worth of playing, I cannot recommend this today.  The devs keep adding new crap instead of working on issues that have been around for a long time.  Video driver crash comes to mind.  Performance optimization is sub par, but with the right tweaks, can be a consistently playable framerate.
New dinos added always obsolete older ones.  For example, the prime wood gathering dino was the Mammoth.  Beaver was added that is easier to bring home to tame and carries wood at 1/5 the normal weight.   Nearly a year later, Therizinosaurus was added which obsoleted just about every other gathering dino, including said Beaver.
There is the issue of dino nerfs.  Nerfing dinos on a case by case basis would make too much sense.  Instead, there are usually big blanket nerfs.  Dino HP and Melee damage a year ago nerfed ALL tames instead of nerfing a few overpowered ones.  Today, the blanket nerf is on flying dinos.  Blanket nerfs on Stamina and Speed.  Flying in general did need a nerf, but like the melee/hp nerf from the past, they took it too far.
PVP.  Simply put, if you are not in a decent sized tribe, good luck doing anything on official.  The servers are dominated by alpha tribes, with other alpha tribes from other servers coming to raid every so often.  Unofficial servers exist, so that is good for anybody wanting a more fair pvp experience, but those have their own issues.  Either neglect from admins, abuse from admins, or the different mods on the server.
On the subject of mods, they expand on the existing gameplay.  There are lots of them in the workshop that you or server owners can pick which ones they like.  In theory this sounds great, but in practice, you are stuck downloading GB upon GB of mods for each server you want to try.  There is no simple "click this to delete mod" button.  Unsubscribing doesn't delete the files from your computer, so you can be stuck with 30GB+ of wasted space if you don't take appropriate action.  Once you've finally downloaded the many mods required to play the server that caught your interest.  It is more than likely laggy beyond belief.
These and other various issues are why I cannot recommend you get this game anymore.  Ask me a year ago, and I would have.  If you like PVP, the gap between the haves and have nots increases each patch.  Dino balance is anything but, until they are blanket nerfed.  Mods add to teh game, in both content, and drive space usage.   Attempting to install the game now will just end up using way more drive space than advertised.  A recent attempt to install said it would use near 76GB, but with over 100GB free, it still ran out of space.  Save yourself the hassle and money.
TL;DR:  Updates just add more issues and headaches instead of fixing what's wrong.

Combination of last 2 patches just ripped all progression out of the game for PvE players.
This game used to be fun, but the devs have focused not on adding progression to a challenge, but just screwing over everyone now.
Recent patches have added Dinos that instantly steal things from you, typically found in packs of 3 and they'll run in 3 different directions, so you're guaranteed to lose 2 items, and it's pot luck if the dino you chase down still has the item in its inventory when you kill it.
Dinos that knock you unconcious easily in the starting areas, and kill you.
Birds, which when you kill that pego to get your item back, will agress you in the starting area knocking your weapons out of your hands. and killing you
A flyer nerf which pretty much limits your mobility around the island.
A mob that destroys rafts in 3 hits, limiting your mobility around the island.
Add to this the issues with the server actually registering that you hit the mobs, that you're trying to save yourself from/retrieve your items from, and all of the fun has been kicked out of this game. It used to be about starting somewhere building momentum to push into the next more challenging area, with great opportunities for exploration. Now you spend your life chasing down your missing items, into a fight for your life when you kill the thing, which kills the exploration, and the abiliity to choose and take on your next challenge.
Taking down big mobs in this game involves, standing above it on a cliff where it can't hit you and just shooting it till it drops (Gee that sure is fun and engaging gameplay), because the AI is so bad, it either runs directly at you or directly away, it has no pathing capability. Likewise want to tame something that just runs away constantly, stand so it's between you and a cliff, and it'll get stuck trying to run through the cliff wall.
In general I welcome adding oddball mechanics, but those mechanics should be now and again. When you're constantly hit with the same mechanic, faster than you can even respond to it with the tools you have at that point in the game.. Well I'd rather go play something different.

SINGLEPLAYER REVIEW
I do not reccomend this game for the singleplayer experience. Here are some reasons why
1,Grinding: there is too much grinding in the game. Getting any kind of base started is going to take alot of time and resources, especially since you have very limited carrying wheight.
2. spawning. The dinosaur spawning is not very great. In the swamps, for example, they will just spawn in clumps of random dinosaurs, whether they be hostile are not. Its just not realistic having a bunch of 5-8 or more dinosaurs spawning around eachother. It looks more like a chaotic warfield than anything. It is especially frustrating having brontosaurus spawn near your base, all it takes is one accidential hit or an attack by a carnivore and you can kiss your base (and most likely your dinosaurs) goodye.
3. brontosaurus and other large longneck dinosaurs. They are too glitchy. they can hit you from pretty far away with their tail that has a larger than fair hitrange. They can pretty much take anything down or destroy your base within seconds.
4.Exsploration and death. The game has a very large sized game map that is very beautiful, but traveling is not possible since the bad dinosaur spawning will make a barrier to keep you from exsploring. the only way to exsplore is with a flying creature. dying to is just a horrible system. when you die you lose all the items you had. theres no option to make it possible to retrieve them, which games like & days to die and Minecraft do have. There is also no way to locate your body easily. Back to grinding to get the items you once had so you can go lose them again. The death just takes away any reason or fun from exsploring.
5.Graphics. The graphics arent bad, its just your going to need a beefy computer to handle it. It might also be difficult to get things just right for people who arent tech savy, since the graphics menu has a ton of options to change ( which some may enjoy, but others not)
6. Some recipes in game just dont make much sense. Maybe its just me.
Now, to be fair, it does seem like a fun game. I just dont recommend playing it unless you play with friends and you are someone who can dedicate time to playing through the grinding, because this is definiately not an hour a day game. your not going to get anything done

First off, I came from Xbox which I had 315 hours on, so I'm not new to this game, just new on Steam. But for this game, this is an amazing survival game that they have slowly but surely began to ruin. It is supposed to be a prehistoric game where you can tame cool dinos and team up with friends, right? So they add jetpacks, teleporters, and robotic t-rex armor while doing nothing to prevent problems like friends who get together, play 5000 hours and just wipe every single tribe on every server for fun. This game isn't ark anymore, it's become black ops 3 type of game where you have no chance to get started because people teleport their robotic fish to your peaceful little  base to wipe you off the server. Along with that, every single server is filled with people that have more power than you can imagine, people who play the game purely to just assert their dominance over anybody, even a little level 10 minding his own business will have all his work destroyed. Rust does a server wipe once a month to prevent this from happening and that has had a very good response from the community. Ark devs just allow people to run rampant not allowing anybody to enjoy their "early access" game. And last I checked, early access games don't come out with DLC's worth 65% what the game costs. So my advice is absolutely do not buy this game because it is at the point where you have no chance of getting started and would only be fun if you had played this game since the day it came out. Please, just save your money and don't support devs that don't support you.
EDIT: Something I failed to mention is the spawning system on this game is horrible. I couldn't spawn by where I was building because it just throws you in wherever and half the time, you spawn being attacked by dinos with no chance of escape. Three times in a row I spawned in the middle of the same pack of six raptors and had to abandon where I was building. Ark has so many things to fix before this game becomes playable.

If I had to sum up Warframe in 1 sentence, 'confused space ninja game with lots of guns and visual customization'.
A lot of the content I would say is more accessible compared to the game's earlier years but unfortunately it lacks content to keep the end game players interested. By content i mean, its all about the loot grind where we'd spend days (yes days even if you don't have a job) massacring thousands of mobs to get the newest frames and weapons and after that it's about leveling up those weapons.
Of course, you can do other stuff like quests, arc wing (fly around strike witches style) and raid bosses but after being subjected to the endless grind mentioned prior I've become so desensitized to the game, I did it for loot so I can't really comment on the fun and lore aspects of these modes.
Lastly, the cash system in this game, platinum is pretty interesting. Platinum is used to buy almost everything from resources, skins, weapons, frames to random upgrades but none of the premium items are flat upgrades, they're all farmable things. But the spin is that you can trade platinum with other players for upgrades, parts for weapons/frames, etc which are farmable but hard to acquire. Thus creating a symbiotic relationship where F2P players can get skins by taking the time to trade whatever people want on the market at the time. However I find the new player experience questionable if you don't intend to spend money on the game.
Overall Warframe is a good game with interesting mobs, variety of characters and weapons that have hilarious results depending on how you customize them. But I don't really recommend it cause when you hit that end game ceiling, you'll just spend hours a day mowing down whatever gives you the best exp or clearing the quest in the quickest way possible to speed up the farming process. Most new content for the game doesn't really make me feel interested to come back to it as its typically new weapons, frames, one quest or a new way to grind.

Without a doubt the BEST model of F2P I've ever seen! NOTHING in the game is locked behind paywalls aside from cosmetics that do nothing for gameplay AND the payed currency is tradeible in game, which is great because it means you can trade the high level dups you get to other players. Tenicaly, it's possible to own everything (aside from the User Uploaded stuff and the spec-editions that aren't avalible anymore) without paying a single thing!
I had to put that first because it's a big deal! This is one of the only F2P games I can think off that is totally 100% fair to all users. While the game does have a lot of down-time with item creation, taking hours at a time which can be sped up for real cash, I can understand that for the lack of anything completely overpowered only being avalible to paying members.
The gameplay itself is incredibly fun. I often call this game "Cyber Ninjas In Space" becaus that's pretty much what you are. A thrilling mix of gunplay and melee combined with a smooth-as-heck parkor engine keeps even people like me (who don't often play shooters) hooked to the end.
At the crux of it all, Warframe is a grind. You grind for the blueprints to build stuff, then you grind for the stuff to make it, then you wait for the hours to tick by, but the gameplay is so much fun (even more so with friends) it doesn't feel like a grind unless the RNG is being REALLY nasty and you're having to run the mission for the 50th time.
I can't praise this game enough! Hopefully more F2P games will adopt similar models from now on.

My favorite Free to Play game. Absolutely unique, fairly well polished, and with tons of content.
This game despite being a F2P that started years ago, is still getting tons of new content, events, free things along with the payed things, and it's pretty great.
Most of the game is PvE, with a smaller entirely optional PvP section. This lends to an on average better community with less jerks and more fun game playing. Not to mention the game is fine if you wish to play it completely singleplayer as well. You will have to log-in and be online, but playing everything singleplayer is perfectly fine (If understandably usually more challenging)
The combat is one of a kind, with there being long ranged shooting, close range melee, and many different weapons that mix up the two. You'd be hard pressed to find a game that had combat and movement like this. Every different weapon is just that, very different. While some are obviously better & more powerful than others, pretty much every one, melee and ranged, have a different style of play required to be able to use them. Combine this with the abilities that each Warframe (different character) has, and there are tons of ways for you to play in this game.
The freedom of movement in Warframe is awesome. You can pretty much get anywhere you want in this game (Though beware of invisible walls). The developers really made a movement system that *feels* like you are a ninja, or a space ninja. Like everything it isn't perfect, but overall you have speed and precision with your jumps and spins.
The biggest negative I can see with the game is the naturally grindy F2P-ness it has. To make that new weapon, you WILL have to play many different missions in order to get the materials and credits needed to make it. In order to make that new character, you WILL have to fight bosses over and over to get the parts required to assemble the character. And even when you do get the things needed to assemble your new item, you WILL still need to wait upwards of 24 hours to be able to use that character after it is assembled. Warframe is a game that will require you to be patient for your things, or to just have a lot of money to outright buy the item or rush the build time instantly.
Thankfully, there will be plenty of things to do while you have things being assembled. The game rewards you while you grind for stuff with XP & levels for all of your gear, lots of credits, and lots of resources. It rewards players who take their time and explore the level to find extra loot, and there is always some new alert mission or event mission to do while waiting for a thing to build or something. Along with the fun & satisfying gameplay, grinding usually isn't nearly as bad as it can be in other games.
Almost everything in this game is obtainable from a 100% free perspective. Though a lot of very less important things like cosmetics and such will only be obtained for free through trading in-game items for the paid currency with other players. To begin with, most things are already obtainable for free, but even the things that seemingly only cost paid currency are obtainable if you barter enough with other players. My experiences with trading in-game items I earned free for paid currency with other players have been 90% positive, and I have earned many of my cosmetic items this way.
If you are looking for a F2P game that has lots of content available from the start, if you're looking for the type of F2P game that makes you actually WANT to give money to the devs, then I recommend Warframe. A very fun & unique experience.

There are a lot of reviews talking about the flyer nerf. I understand their concerns, but they may not have read what The Right Hand said on the Wildcard forums. The original nerf was quite heavy-handed; they acknowledge that. Their design philosophy is the opposite of Blizzard; they strike things down quickly like ripping off a bandaid, then buff up slowly from there. I don't necessarily agree or disagree with this philosophy. All update paths have their own issues.
That being said, Ark is one of the most interesting games I've seen on Early Access. For all the whining about flyers, you can tame pretty much anything on the map. The AI that runs the dinos isn't isn't Watson, but it isn't HAL either.  If you are a survival purist, there are official servers for you to get clubbed in. If you like to live dangerously there are hundreds of unofficial servers all with their own combinations of mods, stat changes, level numbers and skills. There are massive, well-made mods and setting up your own server is easy/inexpensive.
All in all, I'd say Ark is worth the money. The developers are actively working on it and really care about their community. You can tell the latter because they don't give us everything we ask for.

Operation Northwoods was a proposed false flag operation against the Cuban government, that originated within the Department of Defense (DoD) and the Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) of the United States government in 1962. The proposals called for the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) or other U.S. government operatives to commit acts of terrorism against American civilians and military targets, blaming it on the Cuban government, and using it to justify a war against Cuba. The proposals were rejected by the Kennedy administration.
At the time of the proposal, communists led by Fidel Castro had recently taken power in Cuba. The operation proposed creating public support for a war against Cuba by blaming it for terrorist acts that would actually be perpetrated by the US Government. To this end, Operation Northwoods proposals recommended hijackings and bombings followed by the introduction of phony evidence that would implicate the Cuban government. It stated:
The desired resultant from the execution of this plan would be to place the United States in the apparent position of suffering defensible grievances from a rash and irresponsible government of Cuba and to develop an international image of a Cuban threat to peace in the Western Hemisphere.
Several other proposals were included within Operation Northwoods, including real or simulated actions against various US military and civilian targets. The operation recommended developing a "Communist Cuban terror campaign in the Miami area, in other Florida cities and even in Washington".
The plan was drafted by the Joint Chiefs of Staff, signed by Chairman Lyman Lemnitzer and sent to the Secretary of Defense. Although part of the US government's anti-communist Cuban Project, Operation Northwoods was never officially accepted; it was authorized by the Joint Chiefs of Staff, but then rejected by President John F. Kennedy. According to currently released documentation, none of the operations became active under the auspices of the Operation Northwoods proposals.The main proposal was presented in a document titled "Justification for U.S. Military Intervention in Cuba (TS)," a top secret collection of draft memoranda written by the Department of Defense (DoD) and the Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS). The document was presented by the Joint Chiefs of Staff to Secretary of Defense Robert McNamara on 13 March 1962 as a preliminary submission for planning purposes. The Joint Chiefs of Staff recommended that both the covert and overt aspects of any such operation be assigned to them.
The previously secret document was originally made public on 18 November 1997, by the John F. Kennedy Assassination Records Review Board, a U.S. federal agency overseeing the release of government records related to John F. Kennedy's assassination. A total of 1,521 pages of once-secret military records covering 1962 to 1964 were concomitantly declassified by said Review Board.
"Appendix to Enclosure A" and "Annex to Appendix to Enclosure A" of the Northwoods document were first published online by the National Security Archive on 6 November 1998 in a joint venture with CNN as part of its 1998 Cold War television documentary series —specifically, as a documentation supplement to "Episode 10: Cuba," which aired on 29 November 1998. "Annex to Appendix to Enclosure A" is the section of the document which contains the proposals to stage terrorist attacks.
The Northwoods document was published online in a more complete form, including cover memoranda, by the National Security Archive on 30 April 2001. In response to a request for pretexts for military intervention by the Chief of Operations of the Cuba Project, Brig. Gen. Edward Lansdale, the document listed methods, and outlined plans, that the authors believed would garner public and international support for U.S. military intervention in Cuba. According to the documents, the plan called for the following:
Since it would seem desirable to use legitimate provocation as the basis for U.S. military intervention in Cuba, a cover and deception plan, to include requisite preliminary actions such as had been developed in response to Task 33 c, could be executed as an initial effort to provoke Cuban reactions. Harassment plus deceptive actions to convince the Cubans of imminent invasion would be emphasized. Our military posture throughout execution of the plan will allow a rapid change from exercise to intervention if Cuban response justifies.
A series of well coordinated incidents will be planned to take place in and around Guantanamo to give genuine appearance of being done by hostile Cuban forces.
United States would respond by executing offensive operations to secure water and power supplies, destroying artillery and mortar emplacements which threaten the base.
Commence large scale United States military operations.In addition to Operation Northwoods, under the Operation Mongoose program the U.S. Department of Defense had a number of similar proposals to be taken against the Cuban regime of Fidel Castro.

Ark, is an amazing game, period, and it honestly hurts me to no recommend it. But, to avoid echoing what everyone else has said, here are some of the pros of this game, that make it so amazing
New content:
There is always new content to explore, as new content is always being added. Rarely gets boring, even when you get to the end of one world, there are always new things to dive into, and starting a new world is always fun. Also, many many well-made mods to keep you busy for years.
-AMAZING graphics:
seriously, I can't stress this enough. The reason I don't play more dinosaur games is because all of the animations, movement, even basic environment, tend to be utter crap. In the sense of graphics and the feel of the game, Ark does everything right.
-Great Progression
I'll adress the flip side of this as well in my cons. But over all, the game is clear about how to to start and how to progress without actually having a tutorial (for everything else, pro-tip: the wiki is your friend) It's very hard to get tangled up in one thing if you do your research.
-Extensive mods
So good I had to mention this again, the mods for this game are absolutely amazing, there is some serious talent out there, and the game's sponsored mod program makes it even better. Don't like something in the game? 90% of the time you can find a mod to suit your needs.
-Made for Multiplayer
Seriously, who wouldn't like to play a game about dinos with your friends? I'll also be adressing this in my cons.
Now, onto the reason why me (and so many others) are not pleased with the game's developers at this point.
-Pvp is frustrating (x10)
I'm not going to try my hand here, since I (for good reason) do not play pvp. But long story short, alpha tribes will wipe you from existence, you get no chance to actually get started on a server. Pvp is extremely broken, the top of the tier and sheer size of some tribes makes some tribes so insanely overpowered that chances are, when you get good enough gear to defend yourself, it'll all be gone the next day.
-PvE gets utterly SCREWED (x100)
Here is where my rant begins, you thought pvp was bad? Well, even in pve, you still have another enemy to fight, the developers. In their efforts to try and fix Pvp, they have utterly BROKEN and DESTROYED all apects of Pve. Why? Well, because the develeopers somehow fail to make the connection that PVP and PVE are two entirely different things, and they do not differenciate between them. Thus, any change made to PVP in an attempt to fix it, breaks or removes any aspect of fun PvE may have had. The deveopers put absolutely ZERO focus towards trying to fix PvE or have different apects to PvE than Pvp.
-Singleplayer gets EVEN MORE SCREWED (x10^45x1.06)
Heed my words when i say THIS GAME IS NOT MADE FOR SINGLEPLAYER, thought you could be safe in your own little world? NOPE. The developers' utter refusal to separate aspects of PVP, PVE, and Singleplayer into their own categories, leaves new players or lone wolves fighting against the developers to not have this game taken from them. What do I mean? Well, EVERY SINGLE ASPECT of the game is designed to be done by more than one person, which is why taming rates are so slow, you get so little engram points, and you get so little resources. Fair enough, the game is fun with friends, but this reaches all the way to single player AND HAS NOT CHANGED SO FAR.
Taming, a long and extensive process designed to be a tribe effort to protect the dino from harm and watch over it while it tames up, in singleplayer is UNECESSARILY long, expecially with the significantly less amount of resources you have as only one person, you can't possibly watch over this process (especially early in the game) without starving, or having your tame killed regardless. (Granted, you can adjust this setting, but still, developers have not automatically changed this preset for singleplayer.
Speaking of resources, in multiplayer, one person gets the wood, 2 others get metal, ect, you see what I'm getting at here? It's real easy to get resources when you have more than one person working at it. As a singular person, this process becomes much harder, and given how many little resources you get. But of course, this has thus far, stayed the same as PVP rates , you have to modify it yourself to adjust it to something more reasonable for one person. Thus, a game that is already 80% grinding, goes to about 99.9% grinding for singleplayer.
Biggest thing, ENGRAMS, the fundemental part of the game is learning blueprints for the essential items you need to progress. The way this is done is via 'points'. You get a certain amount per level to spend to get blueprints. problem in singleplayer? THIS IS SUPPOSED TO BE A MULTIPLAYER EFFORT. No seriously, it is damn near impossible to craft everything you NEED to progress because you get the same amount of points that you'd get in multiplayer. This makes sense in multiplayer, because that way no one person knows ALL the recipes, it's a tribe effort where everyone spends points on different things in order to have all the recipes when together. In singleplayer, progression, as hard and grindy as it already was, becomes 10x more so because you'll sometimes need to grind up more than one level JUST TO GET SOMETHING YOU SHOULD'VE HAD AGES AGO.
+A ton of other assorted problems. A multiplayer game with a singleplayer option is supposed to be peaceful, fun, and mildly challenging, especially as many new players will start here, this games singleplayer is a hot mess that gets more ruined with each update.
-"Rebalencing" rebalences nothing/rebalences the wrong things
see the above. All game modes get worse.
-Anything after the end is boring
Remember when I said the game wasn't boring up until the end? Here's what happens after 'the end': You kill every dino with one shot, no worries unless you are on pvp, in which case, see 'pvp is frustrating'
-The game at it's core is flawed
No seriously, I love the fact that this game has so many mods and a sponsored mod program. it rocks, but it speaks MILES when you need modders to FIX THE GAME FOR YOU. If the developers got their♥♥♥♥♥♥together, they could eliminate the need for about70% of the mods in this game. Why? BECAUSE THE MAJORITY OF MODS ARE JUST FIXING/ADDING A CORE ELEMENT THAT THE DEVELOPERS COULDN'T BE BOTHERED TO FIX THEMSLEVES.
Final notes: Once again, I LOVE this game so much, I want to see it flourish into somethign beautiful, but I, as a mainly singleplayer user, cannot review this game in a positive light right now.

At first I didn't know much when I started the game. So many things are just thrown unto you when you start. The Wikia is essential for learning what you have to do for certian missions. The weapons you get in the market can be obtained for free. The one thing that can not be obtained for free are primed cosmetics, Which dont impact your gameplay. Warframe is the pure definition of a free to play game. The community is helpful and you barely meet toxic players. The platinum currency that you obtain with real money can also be aquired through trading with other players. Just be weary of those who try to scam you.
The game has a few bugs but that doesn't ruin the fun. There are some things you want to obtain that take time because of all the grinding missions, but doing those missions are fun too when you get other players on board. There are Player VS Player modes but those modes are heavily criticized since there aren't any dedicated servers for them yet, so the host has an advantage if their network is slow. The PvP is still fun though, but that's the players personal preference. Speaking of personal preference, all the weapons and Warframes you choose depend on what you like to play with/as.
The Developers are lively and also listen to their community and try to fix bugs and implement updates to keep the game alive, the Streams they do are entertaining as well. You wont regret trying this game, AND ITS FREE TO PLAY!! :D
Well there's still a lot of good content I haven't gone over like the Quests, Factions and Clans. Get Warframe if you dont have it already, its addictive.

Long story short, I definitely recommend this game. Don't let the Free-2-Play tag spook you, since Warframe is by no means a P2W game. It is a PvE-centered game with a model that revolves around Pay-4-Convenience. If you don't like grinding, either skip this game or keep your wallet close.
Now, Warframe has a common theme - Faction X fighting Faction Y to save the day - but it is fleshed out in a way that makes the story interesting. The earlier quests have at best average storytelling, but the latest one stepped up this aspect a lot, and the developers promise more quality content to come. Free of charge no less.
The gameplay itself is very addicting: you have a warframe, some weapons, and a companion with which you need to kill enemies, complete an objective, or both. Most of the fun in Warframe comes from discovering new equipment and coming up with fun builds to play around with. Don't expect to use a specific set of equipment and have fun with it for hours on end. Unfortunately, the variety in missions is lacking, even though new variations have been added. There is also not a lot of variety in environments at the moment (I refuse to call them maps).
However, like I said, the grind is real in this game. Depending on your mindset, you may feel the grind fatigue after a mere 100 hours, or at the 1K mark. I personally have noticed I'm getting burned out on this game. This is mainly due to the nature of Warframe's gameplay, which is not really fleshed out; you shoot an enemy and said enemy dies. There are (mini-) bosses which spice up the gameplay, but they're often held back by one or more issues. Think of invulnerability phases, insane damage reduction, and sometimes outright bugs.
Another point of criticism is the attitude of the developers. Overall, the people at Digital Extremes are incredibly talented and motivated, but I cannot follow their reasoning sometimes. They come up with 'solutions' for non-issues, push out new content with apparent flaws, and release new stuff while not fixing age-old problems. That said, DE have managed to positively surprise me on more than one occasion with their creativity in fixing certain problems, such as balancing.
Their coding department also deserves a round of applause - this game looks and runs great. I'm using a 2nd gen Intel i5 and a Radeon HD 5670 and I have little problem running this game. Obviously on a lower resolution due to the weak GPU, but the game still looks great regardless.
Warframe is an example of a F2P title done right. If sci-fi shooters are your thing and you don't mind sinking a large amount of time in this game, I cannot recommend it enough. You could realistically gain hundreds of hours of entertainment out of Warframe without paying a dime.

A crazy amount of warframes are available for you to unlock, either by purchasing or by crafting. Blueprints can be bought or earned through missions, resources are to be gathered, with each planet/moon having different resource drops. A crazy amount of primary, secondary and melee weapons are available, that can easily fix one up regardless of what play style they prefer. Parkour system is great (even epic), game is fast, looks amazing, game modes are plentiful, missions are repeatable, lots of quests and progression. Once your mastery rank goes up enough, you actually do a 'test', like a martial arts test, to rank up to the next level. You can join a clan, and enter a dojo that can be built by the players, which unlocks access to another huge amount of utilities and weapons. You can take to battle any weapons you like, and you level up these weapons to increase their power. Mods are dropped which boost the weapons/warframes like ammo size, damage, shield recharge rate, total health, shield, armour etc. Mods can be fused and levelled up too, increasing the stats. The actual combat itself is very fun, fast, and satisfying.
The more you play, the more of the game is revealed to you and it becomes more and more interesting, I am still constantly being impressed with this. Developers are always updating the game, for free also, and wiki's and forums mean you'll never really have trouble finding an answer to your questions. The game is free but admittedly there are slots to unlock requiring platinum and most likely a small amount of money will need to be given to grow. I gladly handed over my cash because the developers have pretty much made one of the best fighting/combat games I have ever seen, if not the best.
Well worth trying out as it is free. Grab the Excalibur frame when starting out and see this for yourself. Have fun.

Great game to play with friends. When you all have different characters and weapons that all do different things it's fun to chat and compare. However, friends are probably the only thing that will keep warframe fun long-term because there is just so much grind.

I found it too difficult to upgrade from the starting equipment, in terms of all the hoops you have to jump through to craft items, rather than buy them for real dollars. This is not a condemnation. Obviously, the game's got to make money somehow. In terms of the action gameplay, it was top-notch. Graphics were really sharp, controls were fairly intuitive and it's a lot of fun to run-n-gun or hack-n-slash, or both... as suits your taste. But, for me... the credits that cost real money were *way* overpriced. A hundred bucks will get you a cool new warframe (suit) and complement of weapons, but then you'll be out of credits again. I'd recommend that anyone interested give it a try and see if the game is enough for you, without spending an amount of money that could have bought you five or six other *complete* games, just to have a few options in play. I'd like to recommend the game, I really would, but it just comes down to a sudden flat stop in interesting content in a mix of not having anything worthwhile to do that keeps one's attention or makes you want to really get to it, or other players in the case of servers, who may have placed unbreakable pillars everywhere because they needed to level up, reached endgame and decided to set all of their high level invinci-dinos to patrol spawns, or just flat out started killing them by hand.
Things suddenly stop feeling impactful or interactive once you look at them for too long as well, which isn't fun in any game. The first time a raptor guts you suddenly and attacks around your corpse causing you to disappear it's mostly still with surprise that you sit there watching. The hundreth time you've seen a dino do it it starts to slowly grate. Being Early Access affords it some slack, but then they made a DLC, and have been adding content non-stop, with a distinct lack of improvement on current content.
The primitive mode was novel for a time, but you quickly grow tired of playing with the melee system being bash face harder than other man. Ghille and vegitation is awesome then you realize people just turn off foliage if they care about being competitive in PVP. Things are sudden and quick in their animations when you first take a look, but upon closer inspection, it's clearly like that to mask poor hitboxes, lackluster animations, and similar troubles common in Early Access.
I remember on several occasions watching fliers take their battles so high into the sky that they disappeared and essentially were vanished from the game until a corpse abruptly plummeted to the ground, mostly due to the fliers not being able to turn quickly enough to hit one another, and instead just circling with the occasional lucky blow.
The level system earns another gripe in that you are required to have other people work with you in order to access an even moderate level of efficacy.
