I have very mixed feelings about this game. On one hand, it's a well produced dino game, with a few pretty cool mechanics. On the other hand though are the downfalls.
-This game is 99% grind
-You must grind to gather materials
-You must grind to gather berrys
-You must grind to keep dinos knocked out while you feed them those berries, sometimes for several hours
-You must grind to get the matrials for your house
-You must grind to bring those materials back to your base
-You must grind to level up
-You cannot craft things until you spend points to learn them, and it's almost impossible to get enough points
-This game is plauged by griefers/mega tribes
-people get themselves sick and then run around infecting as many people as possible
-Mega tribes simply take over a server, and then gather the materials there to transfer them over to other servers
-these tribes are essentially a cancer on any server they infect, making the game borderline unplayable
-This game is full of bugs
-People disconnect frequently
-Framerates randomly tank
-Dinos occasionally don't have sounds
-This one isn't that bad unless its a T-Rex sneaking up on you
-The devs are too busy adding (pretty cool) content to fix the bugs that are ruining the game
-Underwater bases are cool, but can we fix the fact that my dinos randomly teleport on occasion?
-Ungodly load times
-16 GB ram
-4GHz Processor
-GeForce GTX 780 Graphics card (not top of the line, but works great generally)
-still have 15+ minute load times into single player games, and they're worse for multiplayer
Despite all of this, the game is pretty good at it's core. There are great dinos, good mechanics, and a general challenge to survive in the world. However, despite this it's still very hard to keep faith in a game when I've spent countless hours building up a base simply for a mega tribe to teleport C4 and assault rifles over and bulldoze everything. After I decided that the multiplayer was too toxic/cancerous I moved over to single player, however many of the core mechanics rely on teamwork to accomplish, which is of course impossible in single player. Most of the (large) dinos become impossible to beat without relying on pure cheese, and they are completely impossible to tame. I've had to turn up the taming time, because **** babysitting and waiting on a triceratops for 3+ hours, and I also turned up the xp multiplier and resource drops. Despite my best efforts though I still end up grinding for several hours to go take care of the T-Rexs that have completely overrun carno island. Even after I finished cheesing and killling them another T-Rex had glitched itself INTO A CAVE on the island, and they're impossible to kill then when you can't outrun them and you can't see/shoot them. This game has potential, but is unplayable unless you make yourself a slave to a mega tribe, or play on singleplayer, where most of the experience is lost. The only exception to this is private servers, and good private servers are hard to find. I love the concept of this game, but sadly it's poorly executed and too glitchy and frustrating to enjoy.

CONs:

There is a lot of fun FPS action for the casual gamer and good amount of min/max customization for the more experienced players. In my personal experience the Warframe community has been helpful and friendly.

They even have a live weekly community stream that covers things that are happening in game and the Warframe community and a live bimonthly developer stream to talk about content updates and system changes.
If nothing else, try it out because:

2. Robot Space Ninjas!

Space ninjas on a quest to obtain power and wealth through loot.
Warframe is a unique game. It's essentially a 3rd person shooter/MMO/action game. You are Tenno, an ancient warrior race that fights using advanced armor suits packed with powers and abilities. Equipped with a primary and secondary weapon, you have some very solid and fun gunplay. You are also surprisingly effective with your melee weapon. When specialized, you can play through the whole game with just your melee weapon. You are essentially a space ninja, using deadly weapons and powers to lay waste to armies. This amazing gameplay and setting.. Is it hampered by an MMO style loot system? Or does it actually reinforce it?
PROS:-
+Very good fast paced shooter/Melee combat
+Very addicting loot system
+Very good art style
+Very good customizability in your characters and weapons  visuals and performance as well
+Wide variety in Warframe abilities
+Wide variety in types of weapons as well
+Very active player trading market
+Large Scale events
+Overall good and helpful community
+Good lore
+Pets
+Good clan system
+Very active and dedicated developers, making the game better everyday.
CONS:-
-Story not fleshed out well enough
-Very grindy and repetitive
-Everyone on the trade channel will try to outright rip you off
-Everything in the game store is unreasonably expensive
-Farming for parts has no bad luck potential
-PvP is still heavily unbalanced
-Raids are dead and full of elitists
-Very overwhelming start for a new player without proper tutorials
-Heavily instanced, narrow corridor style level design
-Random generation adds little to the repetitive level design
I'm a picky guy. I only play a very few select games which I consider to be the best. I'm not the type of gamer who will play any game and have fun with it. I only play those which I consider to be works of art. Warframe.. isn't exactly a work of art kinda game. Pouring 800+ hours into something like that is quite unthinkable.
So why? Because Warframe knows, better than any MMO I've played, how to get you addicted to loot! Not just that, they do it with a very robust and fun combat system which you can enjoy while you're farming away for parts.
In fact, the thing holding this game together is the great 3rd person combat and it's customizability.
Visuals
The game recently got a graphics overhaul as if it wasn't already good before. The game is flashy, shiny and very good looking. Not only are the graphics great looking, the game has a very unique overall art style. The enemies look cool, the world looks cool and our own warframe and weapons look so very cool too.
Sound
The sounds are all on point. The original game soundtrack fits the theme pretty well and isn't hard to listen to at all. The gun shooting, sword slashing and abilities exploding are all on point. It adds to the combat experience. The voice acting of the characters and their repetitive speeches, however, might get on your nerves.
Gameplay
As mentioned earlier, the gameplay is very strong and carries the game forward. The loot system is addicted I've and good and all but I would never have stayed to play this long if the combat wasn't this fun. You are a ninja and you feel like one as you dash, slide, wall run all across the map with infinite freedom, switching between ranged and melee weapons to deadly effect. The animations, although not perfect, are very smooth, fluid and great to look at.
Highlights:-
Weapon variety is among the best I've ever seen.
Primary weapons include assault rifles, sniper rifles, twin smgs, bows, laser cannons, flame throwers, etc.
Secondary weapons include pistols, pistol grenade launchers, crossbows, shrunken, Kenai, etc
Melee weapons include longswords, greatswords, Katanas, staves, machetes, clubs, etc
The sheer variety along with the great combat does add a lot of replayability to the otherwise repetitive heavily instanced levels.
Loot system is fun as it has you do some specific levels for some specific parts. These parts eventually come together to let you craft a brand new Warframe or Weapon. The Prime variants are the most popular and are sold extensively in the active trading market. So whether you want shiny new armor, flashy new weapons or simply wanna make some premium currency, there's always reason to collect loot. There's a lot more to it but that's a long story.
Very active developers. They are constantly in communication with the community. They always consider community feedback. They host live streams often and are always improving the game. Content is constantly being added and the game won't be abandoned any time soon.
Customization is awesome. You can choose among a huge variety of warframes and weapon types, add accessories and then customize their colors down to the smallest details. Once you have the visuals down, you can add mods to your frame and weapons. These mods can be bought from other players or obtained as loot. They add modifiers like adding armor to your warframe, change its abilities effects, add speed, etc. For weapons, they add fire rate, reduce reload time, increase damage, etc. There are a LOT of options here too and this allows you to create 'builds' for specific purposes. This works surprisingly well and adds a lot to replayability.
Summary:-
All in all, it is a great and unique game, constantly improved by its dedicated developers. I am not ashamed to say that I had a lot of fun with it while I did play it. However, I feel like I've experienced everything there is in the game and had begun to finally get bored of all the glorious loot and combat and so I have stopped playing from a while now.
I can assure you that you can enjoy the game for a lot of hours like I did and is definitely worth a try. You can play it completely free, like I did and do not have to spend a single cent to have fun in it.
It is a completely free game and it's good. Pros heavily outweigh the cons and I can do nothing but recommend it.
Verdict:- Essential

With a heavy heart, I have to not reccomend this game at this time.
There have been a handful of games that have changed the gaming world for me (Mario 64, World of Warcraft, Minecraft) and this is one of them. Open world, great early/late game content, endless customization, beautiful enviroment, large variety of creatures, AIRSHIPS!, rideable dinos, and nearly any kind of player to player interactions you could imagine (guy was at my base and was robbing me at gunpoint and I was able to talk him out of doing it and even to the point he gave me free gear/resources). In no other game is such a thing possible and to me that is some next level gaming.
So why no reccomendation? This most recent patch to nerf flyers has made them almost worthless. This was done (to my knowledge) to make pvp more balanced as flyers are op, I completely understand the need for something to be done. But the changes made have been done on a broad base to pvp, pve, and private players. These changes (outside of pvp) have only negative effects. Its not more challenging, only adds more time to the things you where already doing (2 min flights are now 10 min flights). By locking the movement speed for flyers, you are removing a whole playstyle from the game, and decreasing the ability to customize your dinos.
I understand why dev's and players felt the need for a nerf on flyers, for pvp I even agreed something needed done. But this is the part that gets me, your attempt to satisfy one group of your community you have complete disregarded the rest. People have spent THOUSANDS of hours, taming, breeding, and fine tooning there flying dinos. Spending countless nights with sleeploss to raise them. In one patch you have destroyed all of there time and effort without so much as a heads up. Yeah I get its still EA but in the 2 years of Ark we should be at a point where game changers have been worked out. I just don't get how no one considered how this would hurt so many players, or even worse to not care that it would.
I still have hope that the Devs will come to their senses on this and roll back the changes, its not to late to right this wrong. This is my favorite game right now and i wanna be able to play it again, but i need to be reasurred that my time isn't going to be thrown away to appease minority of players desires. I have always recommended this game to everyone and have even purchased it as a gift for friends. I was even going to purchase extra keys to just have to giveaway for when i met someone i enjoyed enough to play with. But this patch has made me pass up this last sale.
I will glady change my review to recommend if this patch gets rolled back. Devs I hope you read this and take it to heart.
Thanks for reading and have a great day!

SUCH A GREAT GAME ... at first.  Now, the devs have managed to slowly kill it beyond any recognition.
The devs have really divorced themselves from the community.  To be clear, updates are plentiful.  Multiple times in a single day are not uncommon.  At first, these updates provided real new content that made the game far more manageable given that it's one of the grindiest games to exist.  Then it just seemed that it was all about pushing out content for the sake of content.  Even a PAID DLC *while* in EA(?!?!?!) ...
Today's game is nothing like it was.  As a new player, do not expect to survive for any longer than a day or two on official PVP servers - I do not care how good of a gamer you are.  Since the devs have opened up cross-server transfers, what used to be thousands of discrete "islands" are now interconnected with MASSIVE cross-server tribes taking over.  You think that's fun?  Think this:  you will be grinding for literally HUNDREDS of hours to make a FULLY DEFENDED base only to have it WIPED to the ground in a single night  - while you were asleep by a tribe from another server that you had never even heard of or even ever see again.  That's today's Ark.  It get's better though.  The devs are now SO DISCONNECTED from the community that they push extremely drastic nerfs on its players ... WITHOUT a corresponding buff.  How is that even "BALANCED"?!  Specific example:  until a recent classic, idiot Wildcard mega nerf, a certain flying dino was VERY commonly used to make life easier on the Ark from PVP fighting to grinding higher level materials.  The geniuses at Wildcard who clearly have not put in the literally thousands upon thousands of game hours that it's hardcore base has committed decided that this flying dino should be rendered about as useless as the most useless land dino.  No joke here - check the forums.  This is what the developers did.
If you are still curious, hey it's your money.  Just be sure you come to a final decision before your refund deadline comes up.

The gameplay is very dynamic, and there is a great amount of customisation. The game looks pretty great, and runs very smoothly; however, the interface is somewhat barebone, this becomes quite apparent in later missions, when more complex mechanics are introduced, leaving the players with little information about what's happening.
While the game is heavily "grindy", this is a matter of preferences, and I don't find this a problem. YMMV.

If solo/small group play are your primary interests, spend your money elsewhere.

Recently, an update was released that harshly decreased the stats of flying creatures. In the same breath, a new aquatic creature was introduced that demolishes rafts in two-to-three hits, and there is no adequate way to defend against it in the early game. This has rendered the two primary long-range methods of transportation effectively useless, utterly crippling my ability to play solo or with only one-to-two other people. If solo/small group play are your primary interests, spend your money elsewhere.

So, I've come back to Warframe and so much has changed. I can finally say I love this game in it's current state. Yes, there's a hell of a lot of stuff that requires some pocket money but there's also a lot of stuff that you can earn yourself and I feel like you won't be hampered too much unless you find cosmetic looks insulting to your character. This game has fantastic fluidity in it's movement and combat systems (with the right movement combo you can genuinely go 0-100mph real quick). The game is graphically awesome and is well optimised in various areas, all of these options are changeable to your own spec ofcourse.
Warframe is a very nice switch up from the regular fast paced action MMOShooter and I truly believe and stand by the fact that if you played this game before the huge update it has had and stopped playing since, give it another go now. Honestly, I'm thoroughly impressed with the direction this game is taking. Do not be turned away by the microtransactions as like I said, a lot of these items are available through Mastery Rank and using blueprints to collect the resources you need to make them.
Pros:
- Great storyline so far
- Character design and background is very interesting
- Feel like a total badass whilst wrecking everything in your path
- Large choice of weaponry and armour (anything to tailor your destructive needs)
- Online servers are very, very good. Hardly ever any drop in connection etc.
Cons:
- Lengthy wait on the foundry for a lot of weapons and items (patience is required for better gear but not complaining)
- There are A LOT of micro DLC options (again not complaining but they're everywhere in game)
- Sometimes struggle to find a team to match up with (not all the time)
That's really it. Like I said if you haven't already, pick this game back up, it has its own launcher/patcher now as an external output from Steam once you've downloaded it from the store to your library but yeah, truly loving this game at the moment and cannot wait to reach endgame content!

Appeareance is another feature that you can buy with platinum, which to me isnt a big deal.
TL:DR Amazing Gameplay, Awesome story!, and awesome customization

Review: 3/4/17
In short:
Despite all the bugs and glitches in the game, it is still very much enjoyable to play, and definitely worth the money if you can afford it. Even in early access, it's still very much a fun experience and well worth the price tag, so long as you have decent income. If you have pocket change, then perhaps not, since you can buy a much more developed game elsewhere. However, the developers for ARK are always updating the game, so if you do decide to buy, I'm sure you'll have a finished game by the end of the journey.
My opinion on the Patch 256:
The newest patch has made players angry about nerfing the flyers of the game. In my opinion, flyers were too over powered to have at the start of the game. As soon as you get one, you have the ability to pick up certain dinos. This can be used to tame dinos easily, which can be exploited in Multiplayer Servers to get a small horde of creatures.
Personally, nerfing the Movement Speed and Stamina isn't how I would have done it, I would have made it more difficult to actually get these dinosaurs, and made their torpor much higher than it currently is. So that rather than shooting them with a few Tranqs, you have to actually plan an attack and shoot them with accuracy to be able to make them unconscious.
As said, despite the bugs and the new flyer stats, the game is still very much enjoyable. If you haven't bought this game, and would like to play for the first time, I would definitely reccomend it. If you have previously played this game, and are coming back to it/buying again for reasons, I'd look at the stats of creatures and the new dinos introduced, to see if you would still find the game enjoyable. The new Leedsichthys is going to be a problem for those building on Rafts, since I've tested, and this thing can take out Metal.

My opinion on the Patch 256:
The newest patch has made players angry about nerfing the flyers of the game. In my opinion, flyers were too over powered to have at the start of the game. As soon as you get one, you have the ability to pick up certain dinos. This can be used to tame dinos easily, which can be exploited in Multiplayer Servers to get a small horde of creatures.
Personally, nerfing the Movement Speed and Stamina isn't how I would have done it, I would have made it more difficult to actually get these dinosaurs, and made their torpor much higher than it currently is. So that rather than shooting them with a few Tranqs, you have to actually plan an attack and shoot them with accuracy to be able to make them unconscious.
As said, despite the bugs and the new flyer stats, the game is still very much enjoyable. If you haven't bought this game, and would like to play for the first time, I would definitely reccomend it. If you have previously played this game, and are coming back to it/buying again for reasons, I'd look at the stats of creatures and the new dinos introduced, to see if you would still find the game enjoyable. The new Leedsichthys is going to be a problem for those building on Rafts, since I've tested, and this thing can take out Metal.

So, I've come back to Warframe and so much has changed. I can finally say I love this game in it's current state. Yes, there's a hell of a lot of stuff that requires some pocket money but there's also a lot of stuff that you can earn yourself and I feel like you won't be hampered too much unless you find cosmetic looks insulting to your character. This game has fantastic fluidity in it's movement and combat systems (with the right movement combo you can genuinely go 0-100mph real quick). The game is graphically awesome and is well optimised in various areas, all of these options are changeable to your own spec ofcourse.
Warframe is a very nice switch up from the regular fast paced action MMOShooter and I truly believe and stand by the fact that if you played this game before the huge update it has had and stopped playing since, give it another go now. Honestly, I'm thoroughly impressed with the direction this game is taking. Do not be turned away by the microtransactions as like I said, a lot of these items are available through Mastery Rank and using blueprints to collect the resources you need to make them.
Pros:
- Great storyline so far
- Character design and background is very interesting
- Feel like a total badass whilst wrecking everything in your path
- Large choice of weaponry and armour (anything to tailor your destructive needs)
- Online servers are very, very good. Hardly ever any drop in connection etc.
Cons:
- Lengthy wait on the foundry for a lot of weapons and items (patience is required for better gear but not complaining)
- There are A LOT of micro DLC options (again not complaining but they're everywhere in game)
- Sometimes struggle to find a team to match up with (not all the time)
That's really it. Like I said if you haven't already, pick this game back up, it has its own launcher/patcher now as an external output from Steam once you've downloaded it from the store to your library but yeah, truly loving this game at the moment and cannot wait to reach endgame content!

So even though I have nearly 500 hours into this game I would not currently recommend it.  The developers talk about listening to the community, but that is only lip service.  The building system has been broken since the beginning, and it will drive you insane as you waste valuable materials by having to place items down over and over and over again to get them to work correctly and look nice.  Everything in the game is GRIND GRIND GRIND, and when you think you have a handle on the grind, you find out there is even more grinding to do.  For example.  These are actual number from the game for a smallish 5x5 metal base.
25 foundations, 124 walls, 2 doorframes, 2 doors, and 77 various ceiling tiles. This is just over 7500 metal ingots and 2000 cementing paste.  7500 metal ingots requires 15000 ore and a forge to process it.  if you only have 1 forge, it will take 20 seconds per ingot.  So just to PROCESS the metal will take 41 hours and 40 minutes... You can cut down by building more forges, but they cost more resources to make as well (and you have to empty them and check them etc).  But this doesn't take in to consideration the fact that it takes 10 to 15 minutes just to get 500-600 metal.
After the most recent change to the flying dinosaurs in the game,  the 10 to 15 minutes to get metal jumped to 20-30 minutes, and is considerably more dangerous now.
There was no user input about the flyer changes, and it was sprung on the community just a day before it went into effect, and they didn't even tell the community what the changes were, until they had already put them in the game.
Also the game promises to be a sci fi dino taming fest.  Well get used to staring at a single number click down (torpidity) and then hitting the use button to feed the dino narcotics to keep it unconscious, the majority of fun dinos in the game take HOURS to tame if you want a decent level, or they take a very large investment in trying to become an egg farmer.  Not very sci fi there...if I wanted to be an egg farmer, I would have moved to Walla Walla Washington.

I think the number of reviews that don't recommend the game, despite thousands of hours played, says it all: this is a game you can simultaneously love and hate.
First, the good: the concept is brilliant (who wouldn't want to relive their childhood obsession with dinosaurs?) and the game is clearly a labor of love. The developers have created a beautiful, immersive world and populated it with a living, breathing, dynamic ecosystem of incredible beasts. A lot of care went in to making the dinosaurs not just look different from each other, but behave differently as well. It will suck you in- you'll feel your gut tighten the first time a tyrannasaurus charges you, and you'll feel awful when your first pet parasaur dies. Ark's crafting system is deep enough that you won't get easily bored, and if you're an explorer you'll find the world more than large enough to sate your wanderlust. I've never been much for PvP, but my wife and I have enjoyed playing cooperatively on a private server.
Now, the bad: balance and bug fixes have clearly taken a back seat. You'll spend a LOT of time playing a mini-game I like to call "where did my dinosaur go?". Maybe they glitched into a tree and got stuck. Maybe they teleported through a wall and wandered off and died. Maybe they just magically despawned again. Maybe they were killed by another dinosaur, and you couldn't do anything because one of the persistent graphics glitches had turned your entire screen black. It's hard to get excited about the newest beastie when the basic mechanics are broken.
My advice, to anyone thinking about the game who's read this far: put it on your wishlist for now. Don't spend your money on an Early Access title that's having a midlife crisis. The moment that the developers get serious about polishing Ark for release, though. buy it and cancel your plans for the weekend.

A very enjoyable and addicting game, but with a very annoying and endless grind.
The game itself is a very cool and original concept: a space and planet based third person shooter revolving around "Warframes" which are basically these cool looking suits which all focus on different themes or abilities (like fire or rocks or telepathy, etc.). It also manages to implement a parkour system that makes you really feel like a ninja. The game also does a great job of balancing melee weapons with guns and bows. Lot's of cool types of unique weapons too, as well as co-op and pvp.
But the grind kills you. This game makes it so you either pay to get stuff that you want, or you have to grind forever to get something pointless. You'll see a cool new weapons or new Warframe and be like "oh that looks neat, I'm gonna work to get that". Then you spend a mininum of 4 days to make a very easy-to-get new frame (weeks for something that's actually good and rare) or a few days to make a new basic weapon.
So if you want to play, go ahead, but if you want to have fun, don't focus or worry too much about getting new gear like everyone else, or just don't play. So I'll recomend this, but it's only recomended for cetain people.

It's free to play, so you gotta expect people focusing mainly on three core aspects: Grinding, in-game purchases, and content.
Yes, there's a LOT of grinding included in the game. But so what? You're a space ninja fighting other factions to basically make sure that your race doesn't get hunted and killed off.
Because of that grinding, they have shortcuts, the in-game purchases. Like I said, it's FTP, therefore they gotta make money somehow. When you read up that they have absurd farming requirements (The cryotic and the oxium) the guns usually suck. Go online and search for some top tier or god tier weapons and you'll find that the guns that were in the game for years are some of the best, no insane grinding hear ladies and gents.
Speaking of the guns, yes they keep adding more and more. They also constantly add new Warframes as well. Like I said before, look at the older ones and some are amazing without the need to grind much. I will admit Warframe are a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to farm because you need 3 different parts and mostly get 2 out of the 3 repeatedly, but at least you get 'em for free. Newer frames are OK, Inaros is cool, but "eh". My advice? Start with Excalibur, look up "Exalted Blade Build", boom, game changer right there.
Conclusion, it's a great game, but the only way to find out is to play it yourself. It won't be that regretful because it's free.

Take into consideration that at the time of purchase this game was, and still is, in alpha stage. (content not performance improvements)
The game has 3 play styles. (generalised) PVP,PVE and PVPVE.
First server i played on was a PVPVE server and it was a nice introduction to the game as well as the threat of pvp. A nice combination of both aspects to the game all rolled into one.
Initially i started playing this game as a survival game with the addition of Dinosaurs. Awesome
Then i moved into the breeding side of the game. Awesome
Took my time and energy to figure out all of the aspects of the game and the players/admin on the server. Awesome
Eventually i was asked to become an admin and have managed to become the main admin for the server. Awesome
Content was being added and some smaller bugs fixed on a regular basis. Awesome
Devs were listening to some of the comments being made. Awesome
Devs changed dino stats effectively turning in excess of 2,500 hours of breeding into dust. Painfull to the point of quitting the game entirely.
Devs have caused every PVE player and most if not all of the PVPVE players to either quit or to put the game on hold until the Devs decide to either undo the stat changes they made or balance them instead of making them useless
Now on the whole, the positive points may outweigh the negative ones but in terms of gameplay, it has reduced this survival/breeding game into a PVP game with land/sea dinosaurs. (flying dinosaurs spend more time on the floor than in the air now) All dinosaurs are pretty much disposable due to the new patch.
With the majority of players over 2/3 of the play styles leaving the game in favor of different games due to the Devs patches as well as the majority of issues relayed to the Devs not being acted upon. At least not openly.
In short, This is a good game concept with a lot of challenges and rewards depending on time spent in game and effort into the different aspects, especially the Breeding side of things. Review 2.0
Pros:
- Play to Win, not Pay to Win: 99.99% of the content can be acquired without investing any money, remaining 0.01% being Prime Access exclusive Glyphs (really tiny profile pictures) and Prime cosmetics.
- Loads of different weapons: Over 400 unique pieces to collect.
- Modding system: Mod your equipment the way you like, or min-max for maximum efficiency.
- Lore: Actively developing lore and questline, answering many questions while creating just as much. Great suspense throughout currently available quests.
- Amazing community: Objectively one of best communities in MMO world.
Cons:
- Repetitive: It's Play to Win so prepare for grinding and mild timewalls (big ones ranging from six hours to three days, you can still play and progress meanwhile though so there is always something to do), but you can "pay" using Platinum (premium currency) to speed up certain things, like purchasing equipment directly from Market or speeding up crafting process for various items.
- Trial and error: There are tutorials for basic things, but you get to learn the game by figuring it out yourself. Alternatively you can always direct your questions about anything to the amazing community sources such as other players you meet in game, Wikia, Reddit, YouTube and more.
- Addictive: You've been warned.
TL;DR: Worth every single minute I invested in it, averaging 50+ hours / week and still can't get enough.

A very enjoyable and addicting game, but with a very annoying and endless grind.
The game itself is a very cool and original concept: a space and planet based third person shooter revolving around "Warframes" which are basically these cool looking suits which all focus on different themes or abilities (like fire or rocks or telepathy, etc.). It also manages to implement a parkour system that makes you really feel like a ninja. The game also does a great job of balancing melee weapons with guns and bows. Lot's of cool types of unique weapons too, as well as co-op and pvp.
But the grind kills you. This game makes it so you either pay to get stuff that you want, or you have to grind forever to get something pointless. You'll see a cool new weapons or new Warframe and be like "oh that looks neat, I'm gonna work to get that". Then you spend a mininum of 4 days to make a very easy-to-get new frame (weeks for something that's actually good and rare) or a few days to make a new basic weapon.
So if you want to play, go ahead, but if you want to have fun, don't focus or worry too much about getting new gear like everyone else, or just don't play. So I'll recomend this, but it's only recomended for cetain people.

Warframe is basically a space themed mmo, but without the quests and massive array of NPC's and areas you'll find in other mmo's.
You're not likely to see a more beautifully rendered worldspace than the one in Warframe. The forests feel lush and aive (even with some wild animals that have a big impact on combat); the asteroid base is dark and eerie, with a strong industrial theme; you get the idea.  The movements are wonderfully fluid and natural as well. In the tutorial there's a line "A Tenno should flow like water across the battlefield", and that's no exaggeration: you can easily run across the field, leap to (and continue running along) a wall, then drop back to the ground without hitch or pause.
Sadly, the beauty is only skin deep. There's no rich story or questline propelling you through the worlds, just an endless grind for better gear (so you can kill tougher stuff and get even better gear), and prestige/ranking. There are several quests, but they're basically just bundles of missions to complete and don't really change the world (though some do grant you extra abilities or unlock certain areas).
Even the introduction is skimpy, covering just basic movement and the few different weapon types you can start off with. The optional in-game guides aren't much help either, focusing more on what you can do with a feature than on how to use it. There are even several topics that aren't covered in-game at all (e.g. damage types, weapon stats, defenses). It's definitely not for inexperienced players. Thankfully the wikia page for it is very thorough. Just plan on spending a few hours (at least) reading about the game before you stop constantly thinking "what the *@#$ is happening, now?"
Secondly, the multiplayer part is virtually inescapable. There are a few mission
that are virtually impossible without other players (or ridiculously overpowered single player). And these aren't like raid bosses where you face a big challenge for big rewards, no these are regular missions where you have to accomplish multiple goals simultaneously (e.g. capture and hold 4 separate points on a map, or defend one point while looting enemy drops for fuel; both against endless and large swarms of enemies) for slightly better-than-average rewards.
The worst part of all, though, is the way it's monetized. As a free-to-play game, you'd expect strong incentives to spend real money (special gear, bonuses, graphical goodies, etc.), but you can't get anything in warframe without either spending real money or grinding for hours and days (acceptable for extra-special stuff, not for basic upgrades). Even your inventory space is limited unless you spend $$$.
Overall, if you don't mind spending time studying and grinding so you can play as a space ninja, you might enjoy this game.

The game has enough various things to do that you won't get bored.  There are different mission types to suit how you want to play.  There are different classes with enough variance in how they work that it feels fresh but similar enough that you won't get lost swapping to a new one.  There are weapons, over 200 from what I last counted.  Each has a unique approach on combat and reason to have around.  You will find your favorites and be able to tune them to how you want to play.
Can you pay to win?  No.  Can you pay to get stuff faster?  Yes.  You can get everything with enough time and effort, no money required.  You can even get the real money currency by trading with other players.  The only thing money will get for you is time.  There are various appearance things you can only get with money, but that is all.
The game is a blast, I have enjoyed every moment.  Never a dull day with life as a space ninja!

It's free to play, so you gotta expect people focusing mainly on three core aspects: Grinding, in-game purchases, and content.
Yes, there's a LOT of grinding included in the game. But so what? You're a space ninja fighting other factions to basically make sure that your race doesn't get hunted and killed off.
Because of that grinding, they have shortcuts, the in-game purchases. Like I said, it's FTP, therefore they gotta make money somehow. When you read up that they have absurd farming requirements (The cryotic and the oxium) the guns usually suck. Go online and search for some top tier or god tier weapons and you'll find that the guns that were in the game for years are some of the best, no insane grinding hear ladies and gents.
Speaking of the guns, yes they keep adding more and more. They also constantly add new Warframes as well. Like I said before, look at the older ones and some are amazing without the need to grind much. I will admit Warframe are a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to farm because you need 3 different parts and mostly get 2 out of the 3 repeatedly, but at least you get 'em for free. Newer frames are OK, Inaros is cool, but "eh". My advice? Start with Excalibur, look up "Exalted Blade Build", boom, game changer right there.
Conclusion, it's a great game, but the only way to find out is to play it yourself. It won't be that regretful because it's free.

This WAS an awesome game.  I put 2000 hours into it and really enjoyed it, but...
This game has a very large following of casual players, who play PvE.  The Devs have twice now made very DRASTIC changes to the game based on PvP feedback, with little to no consideration to the PvE player base.  The final staw for me was the "flier nerf".  As a casual player, flying dinos were fast transport across the landscape.  They made those dinos completely useless, because people didn't like how they were used in PvP.
The nerf wasn't just a "knockback".  They reduced the stamina of my primary flier to 20% of what it was.   In other words, it was 2500 stamina, and now has about 500.  This was a non-trivial, heavy-handed reduction--nor was it the ONLY thing they did to nerf the dino.  They made other, eqully drastic changes.
It's one thing to "balance" content; it's another to completely remove functionality that was originally intended in the game, because of a few whiners.  Had this retained the creature's functionality, but just adjusted it, I wouldn't be doing this negative review.
Worse, they did this on April Fool's Day, so everyone thought it was some sort of April Fool's joke.  It's now April 2, and the problems are stil there.
I played this on a local/private server, and have since shut it down, and will not play, nor chance my review until this is fixed.

This WAS an awesome game.  I put 2000 hours into it and really enjoyed it, but...
This game has a very large following of casual players, who play PvE.  The Devs have twice now made very DRASTIC changes to the game based on PvP feedback, with little to no consideration to the PvE player base.  The final staw for me was the "flier nerf".  As a casual player, flying dinos were fast transport across the landscape.  They made those dinos completely useless, because people didn't like how they were used in PvP.
The nerf wasn't just a "knockback".  They reduced the stamina of my primary flier to 20% of what it was.   In other words, it was 2500 stamina, and now has about 500.  This was a non-trivial, heavy-handed reduction--nor was it the ONLY thing they did to nerf the dino.  They made other, eqully drastic changes.
It's one thing to "balance" content; it's another to completely remove functionality that was originally intended in the game, because of a few whiners.  Had this retained the creature's functionality, but just adjusted it, I wouldn't be doing this negative review.
Worse, they did this on April Fool's Day, so everyone thought it was some sort of April Fool's joke.  It's now April 2, and the problems are stil there.
I played this on a local/private server, and have since shut it down, and will not play, nor chance my review until this is fixed.

EDIT Plains Of Eidolon Update:
The Plains Of Eidlon update revived warframe and gave it a new look, something that was needed. However, it also revealed the huge amount of things that need to be addressed. The release of update patches in Cetus night time when everyone is hunting Eidolons is a good example. However, what it the most important for me is whether new events/quests should be easy to complete, making them friendly to new players (like Gara's quest) or challenging enough to make old players actually enjoy completing them for the gameplay, other than just for the lore and rewards. There are also some great issues regarding Archwing. Being unable to use Archweapons and to use melee strikes while in the Plains makes the game even more confusing, especially for new players. Combine that with the relatively high cost of Archwing launcher charges and the delay it takes for the wings to arrive and it basically ruins the hole concept that was spread about this mechanic before the update went live. It's sad to say, after more than an year that I've given this game a negative review, most of the things that made me give that review still haven't changed. Warframe is still only viable to be played with a couple of weapons/frames against high level enemies and a lot of the new mechanics that are added become irrelevant really fast. I still play this game, more hoping that these issues will get fixed one day, but I fear I may be wrong
OLD REVIEW
I'm sorry, but this is the reality today. Seeing a lot of people with 600+ hours on this game writing negative reviews, I felt the need of expressing my own opinion. I play this game before even the Liset was a thing, and really enjoyed my time with it. It used to be a really addicting game, with lots of possibilities to customize your loadout. Sadly, today this has changed. Now, to be able to complete hard missions, only a small set of weapons and warframe is usable, which make things boring. Everytime someone is inviting for a high level mission, there is a warframe requirement: mesa, mag, frost. Unless you have this specific warframes, it won't be easy to find a spot in the squad. More than that, the Developer's team release new mechanics, game modes and weapons that become useless after 2-3 months or even less; some of them are useless by the time they are released, since there are weapons that excel at everything. And then come the nerfs. Instead of making the weapons/frames equally strong, accordingly to the enemy's strenght, overpowered weapons are nerfed while underpowered ones aren't touched. This result in a really hard game that instead of relying on the ability of the player, it's just the enemies that don't take damage.
Don't get me wrong, I really enjoyed my time playing warframe, but now this game is flooded with bad updates and bad decisions from DE.  It's really hard to see something you love being teared apart, but we have to move on and accept the fact that the thing we once knew, does not exist anymore.
I'm sorry my friend, but I have to let you go. Goodbye Warframe, may the void help you.

Warframe is an amazing F2P game. You must try it. I was never a fan of futuristic shooters but then I came across Warframe. Not only is this masterpiece free, but it looks detailed and fun as well. This is not just a mission based shooter; you'll dive into a world of customization, coordination, and quality content. *DISCLAIMER* Some things might be left out probably because I'm writing this as a MR 8 player and havent fully experienced WF yet. In my defense, i've played enough to know this game is great.
- Overall gameplay is A+
(gunplay, movement, player community, and the customizations are worthwhile and endless)
- Business model is FAIR. (this is a big one for me)
*some items will take forever to farm for (Vauban Prime grrr) but you'll aquire the necessary parts for most items after a few days of playing
Why do I keep saying this game is "fun"? What makes this game so damn fun is that there are a bunch of things to do. One of the main goals in this game are to rank up your Mastery Rank, which is your player's overall level of experience. You do this by getting new items and ranking them up to level 30. You can do this by FARMING for items. This game is all about enjoying Warframe's farming-oriented gameplay with friends. If you don't like farming, this game might just convice you to have fun while doing so (if you hate farming this game maaay not be for you, but still TRY IT). But you farm a lot in WF. A lot. Most of the time, you get some decent items and you (more or less) feel rewarded from your farming sessions. To touch more on the variety of content, most of the time in the game you'll be killing AI and completing missions (farming). It doesn't end there. There is a Team Deathmatch, CTF, and FFA mode called "Conclave". Visit this area of the game once you've got some kickass gear. It still doesn't end there. You then have a soccer/handball like sports mode called Lunaro. Its FUN. This is all in addition to the main kill-everything portion of the game. A little more on gameplay. You, as a player, can control different warframes once you build them through gained parts and items. Each warframe is its own character and playing as these warframes is what makes this game stand out to me. Its freaking fun, man. Its not just an average go out and shoot things - its go out, use your abilities to kill, support, or make life easier, aaand shoot things. The ability mechanic in this game looks spectacular.
Honestly though, if I had to point out Warframe's biggest flaw (in my opinion), it would be the learning curve. A new player can't do much without help from Youtube, the awesome player community, or many of the great (currently recruiting clans). A possible solution would be is to let DE (the devs) know how little information the tutorial provides us in comparison to most of the games content. And for argument's sake, im not asking DE to jam up the tutorial with walls of text info people probably with skip, im only asking that DE make this game easier to "get into". My point is, the game isn't going to spoonfeed you its higher level content. You will be (sort-of) forced into talking to people and going on missions/quests with others. MAKE SURE YOU JOIN AN ACTIVE CLAN. Be social in WF, it helps a bunch. By being social, talk (literally type out your questions) to your squad/clan mates. I can't stress this enough.
Bottom Line: One of the best games I've ever played. 10x better with friends. I recommend this to anyone with a capable computer, just because its loads of fun.

ARK is my favorite game in a long time, and nothing else fills all the various niches of gameplay that ARK can offer.
Open world sandbox, PvP if you want it, PvE if you don't, exploring the world and finding collectible/explorer's notes, taming and collecting/breeding creatures and then fighting alongside them... no game has really given me that feel before. I raised this little guy from an egg, and now he's fighting and possibly dying for me.
A gorgeous environment (with a good enough PC, game does need more optimization, but it's honestly gotten better) and a harsh world to try surviving in. And it also has building, for the architect in all of us, stake your claim on the land. Progression exp/leveling with RPGesque stat allocation. A paint system that lets you dye your clothing, hair, items, buildings, dinosaur saddles, and even paint tattoos on yourself, your buddies, or your dinos. That level of fun detail customization usually isn't found in many other games, especially PvP sandboxes -- I don't believe Conan or Rust has anything like that.
Many have put thousands of hours into ARK... something's good about it, and that's not going away.

I'd been wanting to get into this for a while now, and now that it's on sale thought "hey, why not buy it."
Big mistake. Not only is it a buggy mess,  beginning is a nightmare. Spawn system seems to teleport you further and further away from where you die each time, and has no regard for if there's a building or /aggressive creatures/ right on top of you. Most of my deaths were followed by second and third deaths because of unlucky spawns next to direwolves and raptors.
Not only that, but for some reason temperatures will screw you over. Too hot? Shade won't help, unless it's a structure you've built. That includes four walls and a roof. Too cold? Torches and campfires are your friend, but /only if you're inside a building/. That's right, holding an actual flaming log two inches from your face doesn't count as "heat" unless you've got a bit of thatch over your head.
And the combat! Good god at the motion blur when firing a spear or slingshot. It's like a constant earthquake. And if anything's above level 5? Good luck. Troodons will take one bite out of you and knock you out within seconds. And they're /tiny/. Hell, three Compy'sll screw your day over. Y'know, those tiny, smaller than chickens dinos from jurrassic park? Three. Not the pack of ten or so taking on a little 9 year old girl. Three teeny tiny two-legged rats with a temper problem, vs an extreme bodybuilding, possibly genetically engineered human. Oh and punching them kills you. Because reasons.
TL:DR: Not worth it

EDIT Plains Of Eidolon Update:
The Plains Of Eidlon update revived warframe and gave it a new look, something that was needed. However, it also revealed the huge amount of things that need to be addressed. The release of update patches in Cetus night time when everyone is hunting Eidolons is a good example. However, what it the most important for me is whether new events/quests should be easy to complete, making them friendly to new players (like Gara's quest) or challenging enough to make old players actually enjoy completing them for the gameplay, other than just for the lore and rewards. There are also some great issues regarding Archwing. Being unable to use Archweapons and to use melee strikes while in the Plains makes the game even more confusing, especially for new players. Combine that with the relatively high cost of Archwing launcher charges and the delay it takes for the wings to arrive and it basically ruins the hole concept that was spread about this mechanic before the update went live. It's sad to say, after more than an year that I've given this game a negative review, most of the things that made me give that review still haven't changed. Warframe is still only viable to be played with a couple of weapons/frames against high level enemies and a lot of the new mechanics that are added become irrelevant really fast. I still play this game, more hoping that these issues will get fixed one day, but I fear I may be wrong
OLD REVIEW
I'm sorry, but this is the reality today. Seeing a lot of people with 600+ hours on this game writing negative reviews, I felt the need of expressing my own opinion. I play this game before even the Liset was a thing, and really enjoyed my time with it. It used to be a really addicting game, with lots of possibilities to customize your loadout. Sadly, today this has changed. Now, to be able to complete hard missions, only a small set of weapons and warframe is usable, which make things boring. Everytime someone is inviting for a high level mission, there is a warframe requirement: mesa, mag, frost. Unless you have this specific warframes, it won't be easy to find a spot in the squad. More than that, the Developer's team release new mechanics, game modes and weapons that become useless after 2-3 months or even less; some of them are useless by the time they are released, since there are weapons that excel at everything. And then come the nerfs. Instead of making the weapons/frames equally strong, accordingly to the enemy's strenght, overpowered weapons are nerfed while underpowered ones aren't touched. This result in a really hard game that instead of relying on the ability of the player, it's just the enemies that don't take damage.
Don't get me wrong, I really enjoyed my time playing warframe, but now this game is flooded with bad updates and bad decisions from DE.  It's really hard to see something you love being teared apart, but we have to move on and accept the fact that the thing we once knew, does not exist anymore.
I'm sorry my friend, but I have to let you go. Goodbye Warframe, may the void help you.

Actual hours played is closer to 3k at this point since I've played about 3 years off Steam.
Pros:
+ Base gameplay mechanics (shooting + hack.slash) have been refined and are easily the most attractive part of the experience.
+ Content updates and consistent hotfixes keep the game refreshing, even after breaks.  A game that you can take a break from for any amount of time and return to later.
+ All gameplay-impacting systems, gear, and other accessories are available free in game, although the game offers the option to pay to get it faster. With a heavy focus on Player VS. Environment, there is a surprisingly minimal, if any at all, feels of forced payment/Pay2Win. Relatively fair reward straucture that paces overall within reason.
+ Large selection of features. Every weapon feels unique and can be made viable for endgame content, although some weapons are easier to use than others. Clans exist with actual base-building and research. Customization and cosmetics are as complex and indepth as the player wants.
+ High levels of transparency from developer/publisher DE relative to the industry as a whole. Consistent updates and biweekly developer livestreams allow for accessibility in showcasing player-made content and interactions between both sides. The developers are open to discussion online on social media, although over the course of several years many on their team have notably become less visible after personal attacks.
+The community is friendly and welcoming to both new and old players.
Cons:
- Only specific players will enjoy this game - if you don't like the shooting and hack/slash gameplay after trying it out, that's preference and that's fine. The game isn't for everyone and that's okay.
- The grind is immensely heavy, like classic Diablo 2 heavy. The grind never ends and RNGesus may or may not bless your luck. Although the game never asks you to pay or shoves paywalls into view, the grind itself is clearly evident to any new player and should not be taken lightly.
- While an initial tutorial exists, it is incredibly subpar in knowledge provided - new players will potentially be overwhelmed by the content overload due to the lack of required tutorials and guides alongside heavy complexity and systems. Although some players may embrace the encouraged player-helping-player and mystery, the lack of any comprehensive in-game tutorial weakens the new-game experience immensely.
- After major updates, expect numerous bugs. The team at DE is still relatively medium-small in comparison to larger organizations, and they often attempt to experiment and take risks more often than not. Compounded with in-game systems and reworks that build upon years of development and a variety of problem arise. The first week after major content drops is typically terrifying to watch as balance changes to the economy and player feedback transistions into the game.
I would highly recommend this game to people who enjoy games like looter-shooters, Diablo 2, or otherwise enjoy action games. Sometimes I feel like I've ripped off the developers due to how accessible the content is at no cost.

Warframe is one of the best Free to Play games on the market and certainly one of the best if not the best 3rd Person PVE based shooters out there.  A Very healthy community with many players who's endgame is just to help out newcomers.
That being said it really is a sandbox endgame.  For some, its grinding the void to get all the prime weapons and frames.  Others want to set records and see how far they can go in a survival or defense mission.  And of course Fashionframe is the true endgame.
Every frame and weapons truly feels unique and you will have countless hours of fun trying out new builds to fit your playstyle.
On the topic of the in game market.  PLatinum is the premium paid for currency used to buy weapons and frames from the market. However, everything except cosmetic items can be obtained without spending any real cash.  Some games have this model as well but with an absolute ridiculous odds and actually being able to collect everything you want unless you pay for it. You will never feel that way in warframe. With relative ease and alot of fun doing it will collect blueprints and parts and build different frames and weapons in your foundry.  The best part about it all?  If you grind out the rare prime parts from the void, other players will be willing to buy them from you for platinum which in turn can be used to buy things from the market.  If anything, Warframe is pay to speed up and most certainly NOT pay to win.
The Developers (DE) give constant updates and balances, and are in frequent contact with us.  Between Dev Streams and ingame messages about hotfixes, I can easily say that DE are probably the best developers at listening to their fanbase and responding to them.
Give warframe a try, its free and a ton of fun.

EDIT Plains Of Eidolon Update:
The Plains Of Eidlon update revived warframe and gave it a new look, something that was needed. However, it also revealed the huge amount of things that need to be addressed. The release of update patches in Cetus night time when everyone is hunting Eidolons is a good example. However, what it the most important for me is whether new events/quests should be easy to complete, making them friendly to new players (like Gara's quest) or challenging enough to make old players actually enjoy completing them for the gameplay, other than just for the lore and rewards. There are also some great issues regarding Archwing. Being unable to use Archweapons and to use melee strikes while in the Plains makes the game even more confusing, especially for new players. Combine that with the relatively high cost of Archwing launcher charges and the delay it takes for the wings to arrive and it basically ruins the hole concept that was spread about this mechanic before the update went live. It's sad to say, after more than an year that I've given this game a negative review, most of the things that made me give that review still haven't changed. Warframe is still only viable to be played with a couple of weapons/frames against high level enemies and a lot of the new mechanics that are added become irrelevant really fast. I still play this game, more hoping that these issues will get fixed one day, but I fear I may be wrong

Sadly, today this has changed. Now, to be able to complete hard missions, only a small set of weapons and warframe is usable, which make things boring. Everytime someone is inviting for a high level mission, there is a warframe requirement: mesa, mag, frost. Unless you have this specific warframes, it won't be easy to find a spot in the squad. More than that, the Developer's team release new mechanics, game modes and weapons that become useless after 2-3 months or even less; some of them are useless by the time they are released, since there are weapons that excel at everything. And then come the nerfs. Instead of making the weapons/frames equally strong, accordingly to the enemy's strenght, overpowered weapons are nerfed while underpowered ones aren't touched. This result in a really hard game that instead of relying on the ability of the player, it's just the enemies that don't take damage.
Don't get me wrong, I really enjoyed my time playing warframe, but now this game is flooded with bad updates and bad decisions from DE.  It's really hard to see something you love being teared apart, but we have to move on and accept the fact that the thing we once knew, does not exist anymore.
I'm sorry my friend, but I have to let you go. Goodbye Warframe, may the void help you.

Loved playing this game. Got my newest PC basically just for this game. I would love to play this game more and have tried playing it in a few ways (PVP, PVE, single player, and I'm starting to play some modded) but there are a few issues that plague this game and are doing it in for me:
1. Inconsistencies in user experience across the different 'versions'. Single player behaves differently than playing on a server (internal times don't stop game pausing on local etc.) and is beyond challenging to do some more trivial tasks (eg. taming a quetzal). PVE and PVP are almost (or should be) entirely different games but get grouped into the same category. Typically this means PVE ends up with loads of useless items that have no effect on dinos and nerfs that make the grinding all that more grindy without adding a challenge. There seems to be some differences in the two styles of gameplay (eg. spiked walls behavior with wild dinos) but no critical elements of the game are differentiated across the two game types. The servers themselves are also woefully unequiped for handling lag and there are practically no policing measures in place to deal with cheaters or a**hole players who grief. If you can trust 20+ strangers on the internet to - on faith - not f*** everything you do up then by all means play on official servers.
2. Broken mechanics. Almost every update introduces as many bugs as it fixes and there are plenty of longstanding bugs that have yet to be fixed. The best example I can think of is the building system - constant glitching of dinos and players through structures and an infuriating placement system. Structures aren't solid? Seems like something to tackle but no, the devs add eels, microraptors, and a horse.
3. Optimization. Even on mid-tear settings with my high end PC this game hardly eeks out 45fps. On high settings if I'm near my base I get 15 regularly. The game requires you to "catch 'em all" for the kibble tree and breeding but having more than 40 or 50 dinos in an area effects performance immensely. Every update adds small fixes but I haven't seen my frame rate climb much at all. Out and about on the map I get a relatively consistant 30fps but I bought this behemoth to get crazy frames AND clarity, not to pick one.
4. Updates and Early Access. This game is constantly being developed, as an EA game should be, but the updates come weekly to hourly. And mostly for no reason. Some of these updates have wiped my items and nerfed my tames. I spend hours getting dinos that are good and then the devs retroactively screw them over. If I spend hours on something to use it, it's because I like it and want to use it. There are so many additions to the game that it seems like the devs don't want to fix the game they just want to build out more 'unique' dinos.
5. Sandbox? With the loads of config options, promoted mods, and a pretty deep community of people to help out with editting ini files it would seem like the devs would want you to be able to play the way you want. But there are sweeping updates that generalize the player base so much that it feels like a majority of people are being blatantly ignored. The game changes so much so often that I come back from dinner and feel like I'm playing a different game.
6. No 'easy mode' or 'hard mode'. There are ways to make the game more challenging but to make it more simple or easy is impossible. New players stand little to no chance on official servers with a♥♥♥♥♥♥alpha tribe and even on servers with a kinder alpha tribe they can't grow very large. Back to single player, there is practically no difference in single player difficulty despite having no tribe to help you. The game is incredibly unbalanced and the devs know this. They try to fix it by smashing huge elements of the game.
The list of minor bugs and odd mechanics goes on but to top off this list of just my most major and overarching complaints the latest patch has destroyed the game for me. I lost thousands of resources that were in my smithy, fab, chem bench etc and it only feels fair to spawn those resources back in with cheats. Which to me seems beyond not thought out. The flyers that I have spent at least 100 hrs taming, breeding, and leveling have been nerfed to s**t so I guess gg? The game has plenty of challenges, obstacles, and an incredible number of diverse mechanics to keep you on your feet. But the devs seem to think it isn't a big enough time hog and grind. After watching countless hours of others playing and putting in a good number myself I can't see how the devs are possibly listening to the community. The game - even still - has such potential but I am not a BETA tester and I don't want to keep wasting my time on such an ill-planned game. Thanks for taking my money on a noncompleted game. And further thanks for continuing to not complete it. I'm going to stay on the forums and keep my eyes out for news of fixes but this game is becoming more and more chaotic and I have better things to do with my time (like writing this review lol).

Ark is easily my favorite survival game and one of my favorite games as a whole.  Graphics are amazing and it gives a decent challenge even to experienced players of survival games.  It takes a few tries before you learn to fear just about everything when you start for the first time.
Playing online can be fun, but it's often alot of suffering. I lost everything while offline countless times. I decided to get a private server of my own to play with friends and everything has been great since then. I can't really blame Ark for the aggressive PvP players but an offline protection in offcial servers would be great.  Raids can be very exiting when people man up and fight instead of offline pirating.
Solo or private servers have a pretty good range of settings based on what players might want from their experience. A few people mention that Ark gets too easy in late game. Though true, there's a simple solution. Don't tame the strongest dinos. You do have full control over how overpowered you get. Challenging yourself to survive with no tames is pretty fun too.
Over all, I recommend this game to anyone who likes survival. There's a lot to learn, and almost every dinosaur has a unique behavior and ability set to use to your advantage. If you join and official server, I recommend trying to find a decent tribe to join because solo is rough out there.

Warframe is an amazing F2P game. You must try it. I was never a fan of futuristic shooters but then I came across Warframe. Not only is this masterpiece free, but it looks detailed and fun as well. This is not just a mission based shooter; you'll dive into a world of customization, coordination, and quality content. *DISCLAIMER* Some things might be left out probably because I'm writing this as a MR 8 player and havent fully experienced WF yet. In my defense, i've played enough to know this game is great.
- Overall gameplay is A+
(gunplay, movement, player community, and the customizations are worthwhile and endless)
- Business model is FAIR. (this is a big one for me)
*some items will take forever to farm for (Vauban Prime grrr) but you'll aquire the necessary parts for most items after a few days of playing
Why do I keep saying this game is "fun"? What makes this game so damn fun is that there are a bunch of things to do. One of the main goals in this game are to rank up your Mastery Rank, which is your player's overall level of experience. You do this by getting new items and ranking them up to level 30. You can do this by FARMING for items. This game is all about enjoying Warframe's farming-oriented gameplay with friends. If you don't like farming, this game might just convice you to have fun while doing so (if you hate farming this game maaay not be for you, but still TRY IT). But you farm a lot in WF. A lot. Most of the time, you get some decent items and you (more or less) feel rewarded from your farming sessions. To touch more on the variety of content, most of the time in the game you'll be killing AI and completing missions (farming). It doesn't end there. There is a Team Deathmatch, CTF, and FFA mode called "Conclave". Visit this area of the game once you've got some kickass gear. It still doesn't end there. You then have a soccer/handball like sports mode called Lunaro. Its FUN. This is all in addition to the main kill-everything portion of the game. A little more on gameplay. You, as a player, can control different warframes once you build them through gained parts and items. Each warframe is its own character and playing as these warframes is what makes this game stand out to me. Its freaking fun, man. Its not just an average go out and shoot things - its go out, use your abilities to kill, support, or make life easier, aaand shoot things. The ability mechanic in this game looks spectacular.
Honestly though, if I had to point out Warframe's biggest flaw (in my opinion), it would be the learning curve. A new player can't do much without help from Youtube, the awesome player community, or many of the great (currently recruiting clans). A possible solution would be is to let DE (the devs) know how little information the tutorial provides us in comparison to most of the games content. And for argument's sake, im not asking DE to jam up the tutorial with walls of text info people probably with skip, im only asking that DE make this game easier to "get into". My point is, the game isn't going to spoonfeed you its higher level content. You will be (sort-of) forced into talking to people and going on missions/quests with others. MAKE SURE YOU JOIN AN ACTIVE CLAN. Be social in WF, it helps a bunch. By being social, talk (literally type out your questions) to your squad/clan mates. I can't stress this enough.
Bottom Line: One of the best games I've ever played. 10x better with friends. I recommend this to anyone with a capable computer, just because its loads of fun.

Warframe is basically a space themed mmo, but without the quests and massive array of NPC's and areas you'll find in other mmo's.
You're not likely to see a more beautifully rendered worldspace than the one in Warframe. The forests feel lush and aive (even with some wild animals that have a big impact on combat); the asteroid base is dark and eerie, with a strong industrial theme; you get the idea.  The movements are wonderfully fluid and natural as well. In the tutorial there's a line "A Tenno should flow like water across the battlefield", and that's no exaggeration: you can easily run across the field, leap to (and continue running along) a wall, then drop back to the ground without hitch or pause.
Sadly, the beauty is only skin deep. There's no rich story or questline propelling you through the worlds, just an endless grind for better gear (so you can kill tougher stuff and get even better gear), and prestige/ranking. There are several quests, but they're basically just bundles of missions to complete and don't really change the world (though some do grant you extra abilities or unlock certain areas).
Even the introduction is skimpy, covering just basic movement and the few different weapon types you can start off with. The optional in-game guides aren't much help either, focusing more on what you can do with a feature than on how to use it. There are even several topics that aren't covered in-game at all (e.g. damage types, weapon stats, defenses). It's definitely not for inexperienced players. Thankfully the wikia page for it is very thorough. Just plan on spending a few hours (at least) reading about the game before you stop constantly thinking "what the *@#$ is happening, now?"
Secondly, the multiplayer part is virtually inescapable. There are a few mission
that are virtually impossible without other players (or ridiculously overpowered single player). And these aren't like raid bosses where you face a big challenge for big rewards, no these are regular missions where you have to accomplish multiple goals simultaneously (e.g. capture and hold 4 separate points on a map, or defend one point while looting enemy drops for fuel; both against endless and large swarms of enemies) for slightly better-than-average rewards.
The worst part of all, though, is the way it's monetized. As a free-to-play game, you'd expect strong incentives to spend real money (special gear, bonuses, graphical goodies, etc.), but you can't get anything in warframe without either spending real money or grinding for hours and days (acceptable for extra-special stuff, not for basic upgrades). Even your inventory space is limited unless you spend $$$.
Overall, if you don't mind spending time studying and grinding so you can play as a space ninja, you might enjoy this game.

I am a PvE player who runs two private servers from my home for a small group of friends.
The Good stuff:
The gameplay is, overall, fun and engaging. It's also very satisfying both from a taming/breeding standpoint and from a crafting/building standpoint. The game is also extremely modable. There is strong support in the community for further mods and even server administration and automation.
The bad stuff:
1. While the client has been reasonably stable overall, most patches are not thoroughly tested before being applied. It is normal for the game to be so broken after a monthly major patch as to be completely unplayable for two or more days while the devs sort out the mess they made. Then random little micro-patches come out at all kinds of random times and intervals through the month, and frequently break essential functionality because they weren't properly tested before being deployed.
2. Random buffs/nerfs happen all the time. Most are minor and not greatly noticeable, but the last flyer buff on April first was not very well thought out... once again breaking several aspects of the game, without even accomplishing the percieved goal of the nerf. Feedback has beed heard previously, and in some cases applied. But this nerf was bad enough that it, along with several major bugs in the new UI system, have caused my little group to vote to move on from the game at this point.
Summary:
The overll gameplay is great, but the constant unaddressed bugs and the introduction of new ones due to a lack of testing, combined with the lack of forethought from the dev team on recent nerfs (and MORE bugs) took the fun out of it. If you're OK dealing with all this and you like survival games, buy it when it's on sale. The DLC is also good, but also broken as a result of the recent patch. My whole group bought the DLC and loved it until a few days ago. My group has moved on and I've shut both servers down.
My advice: Wait until released. This is more than the usual pre-release roller-coaster.

I'm sorry.
I love Warframe, it's an amazing game, it's pretty much the only F2P title on which I've spent real money (thousands upon thousands of platinum, actually!), don't get me wrong. But I'm afraid I'll have to be truthful here.
Unless DE manage to introduce something really interesting, new in some way or another, and game-changing there is no point in this game whatsoever. It's an endless grind, and even I, a lover of grindy action-RPGs (think Torchlight, Diablo, Borderlands, etc) often can't stand it.
Let's face it, the game really has gotten a lot better, it got a way nicer UI, a few neat gamemodes (except for Archwing, ♥♥♥♥ that♥♥♥♥♥♥, but as time goes by it gets more and more obvious that it's all about pumping out another gun/melee or a few each month, another frame every 3-5 months, another gamemode every 6-8 months, same with sentinels, primes, etc...
This is not okay. This will continue, more people will get angry. See, there's already a lot of negativity 2 years later. I'm not the first ~700something hours (I actually have more from the early standalone launcher days) player who loves the game, but is going to write a negative review.
You've had a great foundation, but instead of actually building something cool and interesting over it you've decided to start hastily slapping random bits on top of it just to see what happens. And it doesn't seem like you're going to stop anytime soon. Almost the same thing with, say, PAYDAY 2 - an endless stream of shameless DLCs that barely add anything and not much else. No actual improvement, just adding random bits over and over.
Oh, and the story sucks. You could've improved that, you could've spent more time on awesome "cinematic" quests, but no, gotta mindlessly pump out those primes and shiny new stuff
More to come, probably.
