I would actually recommend this game, under a few conditions. First of all... DO NOT PLAY ON THE OFFICIAL SERVERS!!!! I am sorry but food and water simulator 500,000,000bc is not a good thing. You will constantly run out of both, before you can really get your foot in the door. The tame rate on official servers is far too high, and the breeding system would require you, and/or your tribe, to be no-lifers. My god, we tried to hatch a raptor with default settings... It hatched after 2 or 3 hours... then you have to sit there and constantly feed it meat (I mean every single second), for 3 hours and 43 minutes... And thats for one of the easiest things, in the game, to breed. 18 hours and 32 minutes of constant food feed, on the Quetzel... on an official server!!!!!! Insanity wouldnt come close to describing how screwed up that timer is.
As for the single player elements and the private/unofficial server settings, which is what im basing my reviews on, I have fully enjoyed it. I can turn down the water and food consumption to make it manageable. I can set it up so it can be any difficulty that I, or my friends need. I can increase the tame rate so its more casually oriented (e.g. I only have to constantly feed a baby raptor for about 10 min, instead of almost 4 freaking hours!!!!!)
Don't buy this game if you are in it for the PvP, you will not have fun. If you want a strong co-op experience with hours of gameplay, I would recommend it, only if you rent or run a server yourself! The major complaint about the local host is the tether distance thing. I wish it wasnt part of the local host at all, but what can you do. If you want to play with others, there are several low cost server hosting options that can give you a large level of customization. My friends and I are splitting the cost of server, each of us paying $5 a month (3 friends). So its entirely possible to get a low cost option.

This game is overall pretty good. Its free to play, which at least allows me to reccomend anyone to try it out, and pretty much everything can be acquired without spending actual money. While yes, the actual spending part is the more desired route, as its a hell of a lot easier than grinding through to get everything, the grinding through and the success you feel after gathering everything is also pretty great. One thing I did have a problem with, however, is the wait times for the items after you get all the parts. Its not too much of a big deal, but its slightly annoying. Another thing I have to say: This will be one of those games where you will binge play it a ton and then stop playing for a long time, only to go back to it later. Thats not to say that the game is bad, its really fun. Its just that at some point you may grow a bit bored of the game. It can get repetitive.
tl;dr
PROS
- Pretty damn fun and addictive
- Free (and not pay-to-win)
- Different frames, with different skills, are pretty fun as well.
- Gathering everything and gaining something you wanted is satisfying.
CONS
- Wait times after you gather the parts. Not too big of a deal.
- Can get boring after a while.

PRO: Survival Game, Dinosaurs, Crafting, Multiplayer, Teamplay, Soloplay
CON: Mega Tribes, Exploits, Aimbot, Cheap Servers, Mass Gameplay Changes at whim.
So decided to update this as Ive been playing CrossArk it removes most of the Megatribe issue on my previous review.  Though the latest still has the issue of Exploits, Aimbot, as well as adding in Cheap Servers, and Mass Gameplay Changes made by Wildcard.
The latest change limits turrets to 100 every 10k units *this is roughly 33 foundation radius in an area*.  Now lets get an idea here most good big base designs are over 1000 turrets in that space, seen by the patch where we look at a turret and it says oh your at 1092 of 100 allowed!  So lets just break it down.  1000 turrets = 250 turrets each side of the base, or maybe a little less and some internal turret defenses for those that manage to get in.  Sounds like a lot right?  Its not, a raider with a good bronto/stego can battle through that but it takes awhile.  So now lets reduce that number from 250 to 25. NEVER buy this game. If it is very cheap, possibly...but probably not.
Pros: fun, what's not to like about fighting with dinos?
Cons: glitchy, buggy, paid dlc released before game is out of "early access", devs make poor decisions, devs are distant or will ignore community (I admit that the community can make bad suggestions at times. However, there are good ones as well), giant tribes or alliances across servers (official servers only), everything in this game is INSANELY time consuming.
Welcome to Ark, another "early access" game that hides behind the "it's early access, so you can't be upset if things don't work" phrase.
The game is glitchy and buggy. Expect to die, lose items, or lose dinos for the weirdest reasons. Due to the buggy nature of the game, you can expect many people to exploit these issues for their own gain. Let's not forget memory leaks. I have a gaming rig, with 24GB of RAM. It plays current games on the highest settings with no fps drops or any issues. Yet, when it comes to Ark, I will crash, have issues getting into game (not network related), or the game will close due to memory leaks.
Now let's talk time. Plan to join a large tribe of 10+ people who are online 24/7. If you don't, don't expect to have fun in this game on official servers. Resource gathering is not so bad, but taming and raising dinos can get INSANE. Expect hours of your day gone just trying to tame dinos, and days gone to raise babies. Do not play on official servers if you have any sort of life. If you don't have a life, expect to not play or do anything but this game.
And don't get me started on the Chinese or other massive tribe/alliances. Due to the implementation of being able to transfer items, characters, and dinos to other servers, Huge cross server tribes and alliances have formed. These can be anywhere from 100s or 1000s of people. They will come in, sometimes announcing that they are here to gather resources from players, and then promptly destroy any resistance with superior numbers, levels, and equipment. There is very little one can do against them.
Lastly, they make rash decisions that sometimes make no sense, and are ultimately removed. With this recent update, flying dinos have been nerfed heavily. My hope is that this is an april fools joke, but a part of me believes it is not. Without much discussion or adjustment, all flyers were given a speed cap that is so low that they are no longer able to evade danger or be used as transportation reliably.

This game is a lot of fun, it really is, but there's problems at its core that keep me from enjoying the game. The grind and the abundance of features that are added, have some bugs fixed once, then ignored forever are the two biggest problems I have.
The grind isn't horrible when you start the game, or at least, it didn't feel that way to me, but once you start trying to reach mid/end-game, there's so much you have to do to be even remotely powerful. First things first, barring even getting your weapon/frame of choice in the first place (which is a grind for materials, then a wait for it to actually craft in real time), you have to get damage/health boosting mods that are basically required to not have your gun be a peashooter or your warframe have no health. Then if your weapon/frame needs some expensive mods to be good, you have to forma (reset the level of) it, usually multiple times over, before you can afford to have all the mods you want. All of this takes way too long to do in my opinion. However, even if you like or can bear the grind, there's still one more big problem that keeps me from wanting to play.
DE added a gamemode a while back called Archwing, where you'd get a cool little space jetpack flight device thingy you can use. The gamemode, like many other features DE has added over the course of time, is not much different now than it was when it was first released. Basically, no one plays any archwing missions, because there's no reason to besides to level up the archwings and archwing weapons. This happens to basically all but a few missions as well. There's no reason to play them other than to proceed through the starchart to unlock more planets. There's like, 6 missions that are good, and they're all there to level up stuff that you've already forma'd half a dozen times. DE wants to fix the mission problem, but there's all these other features they added too that no one uses because they're either broken, boring, useless, or some combination of the three.
The game is fun, and I know DE wants it to be good. Right now though, I think it's in a place where it's just not worth playing.

I really enjoyed this game and have for many years at this point. I have about 3500 hours logged and that should speak to how amazing it has been. All games have good and bad patches. Here recently they had a two day rollback that set so many people back and they did very little to make amends for it. Now they have launched a new patch that has nerfed all flyers. While they did need to be nerf, there is a difference between hitting it with a nerf hammer and a nerf nuke. Such a drastic change warrants refunding points to existing flyers because one has to adapt to this new patch. There is no leveling movement speed and stam has seen, on average, a 70% reduction meaning a lot less time in the air. So, points need to be allocated to stamina to adjust to this. How are already leveled dinos that had plenty of stamina to adjust? They can't which forces one to completely start over and retame/rebreed an entire lot. That wouldn't be so bad if there wasn't a 500 dino cap per tribe. Chances are, we're going to do this, make the changes and then wildcard is going to microtweak this nerf and once more make the adaptations people go through void. Another issue is the size of vaults. Yes, they were massive. That said, many people took that into account and designed their bases -around- this so no we're left with these ridiculous looking gaps that will require days if not weeks on larger bases to fix. There are better ways to have handled the issues than making an integral part of the game nearly useless. Wild dinos have infinite stamina. Making it infinitely more difficult to get wyvern eggs seeing as almost nothing can outrun them now.

Interesting premise but terrble execution. Maybe in a year or two when they fix all of the issues and release the game it will be worth playing, but steer clear right now. I have hundreds of hours on PC in a PvP server and hundreds more of a XBox PvE server. The game is extremely laggy, combat is a joke, caves are laughable, and building bases is frustrating. Instead of fixing these issues they just keep adding content and nerfing things into uselessness. I don't have any faith in this development team to correct even a fraction of their mistakes before official launch which will probably never happen.
My biggest problem with this game is it is so time intensive. You might spend hours taming a dinosuar only to lose it to another player or a game glitch. If you want to breed dinosaurs kiss an entire day of your life goodbye. Raising babies take between 2 hours for the weak dinos and 9 hours for some of the most powerful. The best take 18 or 28 hours. And you have to hand feed them. It takes a few hours to get the rex or giga to a point where you can walk away from them for more than a few minutes. And after you get through the baby phase you are only 10% done. You also have to log in every few days to feed the dinos, lest they starve to death. Not to mention they go missing all the time.
End game is a stupid grind to learn to make overpowered armor and weapons. Guess its still impossible to make an MMO without mindless grind at the endgame.
And, if official launch ever comes, you better hope they wipe the servers. Otherwise you won't have any place to build and will be contending wit people that have a year's worth of stuff over you.

Okay... Despite the huge wave of negativity surrounding the Ark right now, I for one am very happy with patch 256. Good for you Devs to do what you think is best for the game despite the protests of the whining public. Its about time something was done about some of the Flyer OP issues.
Now before anyone starts railing me for what I just said, do note that I have 2,100 hours on the game and have been playing since about a week after the game's initial release. I've seen the early game issues. I was there was trees would wave and rubberband. I witnessed the deaths of many tamed Megalodons that came near the surface. I was there when the all powerful Giganotosaurus was released and the nerf parties that came afterwards. I saw the waves of hate that came from Scorched Earth and you know what??? The games is still going strong and I will still stand behind the development team.
This is an amazing game and will always be one. It brought something fresh to the world of open world survival and despite the amount of time its been out, road bumps, and competition the game still contends to be one of the best of its kind out on Steam. Sure the flyer nerf was a little too harsh in my opinion, but at the same time it was kind of needed. Flyers are the bane of PvP. There is no reason that an Argentavis or Pterandon/Tapejara which may I remind you has hollow bones be able to pick me up even though its carrying a rider(s) and I am carrying 600 lbs in metal. Its insanity at its finest. Am I sad that they can't cross the water any more... yes. The devs should have nerfed the weight instead of the stam and speed, but thats my personal opinion.
I know it sucks that PvE players are especially hurt by this, but there is other ways to cross the islands effectively and transport goods without taking to the skies. Get a Horse, Kangaroo, Rhino, Bear etc. These are all very viable animals that are bound to the earth. I almost never fly and I do just fine... and I know for sure that Im not the only one who roles like that. Actually... PvE players have it even easier since they don't have to worry about getting waylaid by another player.
So in a nutshell I will stand by the Ark and its development team. Good job guys.

This game is overall pretty good. Its free to play, which at least allows me to reccomend anyone to try it out, and pretty much everything can be acquired without spending actual money. While yes, the actual spending part is the more desired route, as its a hell of a lot easier than grinding through to get everything, the grinding through and the success you feel after gathering everything is also pretty great. One thing I did have a problem with, however, is the wait times for the items after you get all the parts. Its not too much of a big deal, but its slightly annoying. Another thing I have to say: This will be one of those games where you will binge play it a ton and then stop playing for a long time, only to go back to it later. Thats not to say that the game is bad, its really fun. Its just that at some point you may grow a bit bored of the game. It can get repetitive.
tl;dr
PROS
- Pretty damn fun and addictive
- Free (and not pay-to-win)
- Different frames, with different skills, are pretty fun as well.
- Gathering everything and gaining something you wanted is satisfying.
CONS
- Wait times after you gather the parts. Not too big of a deal.
- Can get boring after a while.

I've played quite a bit of Warframe and I have to say I really enjoy it, the insane grind you end up with from the RnG system tends to get a bit ridiculous depending on what items you are going for and there are plenty of bugs, plot holes, things needing explained, and it can be a bit of a tough start if you don't have friends or any kind of help. Though in personal experience the game was very enjoyable and what story quests there are started to get really interesting and had me hooked. Its also a good game if you are stressed and just want to burn off some negative emotions, hop into a survival mission and go at it. Another good thing about this game is that, compared to other games, the community of this one is very nice, friendly, and helpful! Of course the community isn't perfect and we have our bad apples but most of almost everyone I meet on here is reasonable and just looking to have fun smashing up the grineer. My biggest complaint is probably how you start with so few slots for weapons and warframes, as well as that the slots need to be bought with platinum, but I also understand that the company needs to make money too. Besides you can always just farm a couple void missions to earn some prime gear and see if you can find a buyer, which is also something I enjoy about this game is the fact you can farm and sell for the special game currency instead of either having to spend real money or do a bunch of tedious surveys and offers. This game is just so addictive and there is plenty to do from crafting, collecting, stealth, spy, escort, capture, overall slaughter, and so on. Combat has a very nice feel to it and each weapon has a set of combos, as well as every warframe has its own strengths and weaknesses, abilities, and some warframes even have passive abilities.
Overall I'd have to say that I absolutely love this game and want everyone to play it. Its just an amazing game, but it does have its cons and its all about personal taste, you might also find it hard to get into this game if you dont have some friends around or you could just get bored and not feel the same about the game as I do but I'd honestly have to say that its definitely worth a try.(The graphics are also very pleasing!)

This game is a game where prety much EVERYTHING can be obtained through trade and patience.  I have reached the point of the game where all I have left to do is collect a few weapons and cosmetics, in which I have made the money (platinum) for on my own time.  As a high ranking player, I have seen many types of players and many changes throughout the game.  The gameplay and trading in Warframe are merciless to those who start out the game, but provides an interesting learning experience to read the minds of the person on the other side of the screen.  It took me a couple of hours to just figure out the parkour mechanics, and many more to be able to hold my ground against enemies that you may think are stupid at first, but then realize that they are stupid, but hit hard.  Even with the legendary grind this game has striked into players, I remain playing the game, seeing new content put out that never fails to impress.  If you are looking for a game where you can casually spend time with friends, be astounded by the copypasta maps that always hold great beauty, laugh at the funny bugs that can be found on rare occassions, fight for the "honor" of the merciless tenno, or find a challenge mastering the game's distinct mechanics and unmatched third-person combat, then I welcome you to join Warframe.

Think of this review as a beginner's view at the game
For a free to play game, it is very impressive.
Lots of free to play games have a reputation of shoving useless items to your face and tells you to buy this so you can be OP. Fortunately, Warframe isn't like that. YES it is very slow to get all good things without spending money. But, THAT is the point of the game, working hard to get that thing you wanted. so judging from this, free to play in Warframe is executed almost perfectly.
Lets now go to the bad parts of the game,
Early on in the game, you won't know what to do. After finishing the mission Once Awake, I was completely in the dark. You won't even know how to get the things you need to craft Warframes. Then after that, I was greeted with a "Rank Up" Button in my menu. WTF is this? I was not even introduced to Mastery Ranks at that time. So once you start the game, get ready to figure things out by yourself.
Next is how the market is portrayed. This is where you will think that the game is pay to win. why? When you first open up the market, the first thing you will think is "I need to buy everything with Platinum????" The answer is simply no, it's just that everything is so badly shown that we think it that way.
Here are its Pros and Cons
Pros
-Awesome Customization
-True Free to Play
-Impressive movement system
-Stylish
Cons
-Doesn't teach you everything you need to know in the game
-Repetitive maps
-Boss fights are boring
-Bad presentation of the market
Overall, Warframe is as good as they say. It's so good for everyone that people are saying that it's what Destiny should have been. I agree.
Go and play it, there is no reason not to considering it's free.

Wait for this game to exit Early Access.  There are MAJOR flaws and nobody is fixing them.  I have to admit, once you start playing, the game seems awesome.  I've spent 700+ hours getting frustrated to the point of no return.  Good graphics, play control, multiplayer, social aspects, BUT.....  There are basically 3 modes and each have major flaws:
1. Single Player Mode:  There is nobody to raid you and destroy all the hundreds if not thousands of hours you need to spend on building and taming.  However, the game is designed for multiplayer.  If you play in single player mode, make sure you understand how difficult it will be.  You will have nobody to help you double team capuring tames and exploring with.  This basically makes it quadruple times harder and limits your strategies to extreme means in just about all aspects.  Which means MORE time spent, MORE failed attempts, and MORE resources waisted due to lack of a team for support.  Bleh! :-/
2. Multiplayer PVE Mode:  Unless you are super lucky to find a brand new server, already have a friend that will invite you to their tribe, or are ok with never being able to build or tame anything, then this might be ok.  Once another player or tribe has built part of a structure, you are unable to build anywhere close to it.  So tribes run around the WHOLE server placing one piece of structure ALL OVER the map.  This in turn keeps new players for ever building ANYTHING ANYWHERE.  So players just run around looking for a place to build a base, only to die in the process a few hundred times before they realize the server is full.  After doing this a few times on different servers, you realize there is NO FREE SPACE ANYWHERE ON ANY SERVER.  Good luck finding anywhere to build anything.  This mode has now been nullified.  :-/
3. Multiplayer PVP Mode:  This mode has the biggest flaws of all.  If you're a fan of spending hundreds or thousands of hours building and taming and learning, only to have another tribe casually transport to your server, wipe out you and everyone else's hard earned bases, materials, and dinos out of existence in a matter of minutes, then you're love it.  :-D  This mode is fun when there are only a few friendly tribes scattered accross each server, but the massive tribes on other servers can and WILL eventually destroy everything you've ever worked for.  This, in turn, will cause you to basically quit or attempt to find another server to build, where you will then again just get completely wiped.  Most of the time you are logged out, come back the next day and see all of your dinos dead, your base in pieces, and all of your hard earned materials gone or destroyed.  When you look at the tribe log to see who destroyed you, you'll just see a bunch of squares for names.  You'll never even KNOW who did it.  This mode will suck your soul out, chew it up, spit it back into your face, and laugh about it.  :-/
So, to wrap it up.....
DO NOT BUY THIS GAME.......
(until it comes out of early access)  :-)

As you can see by the hours I've invested in this game (PVE), you can see that it has been fun over the past year, but this last update (April Fools Joke or not) has put this game into my do not play category.
1.) Quit calling this game early access.
* This game after a year of playing it is not early access any longer. This is the game. Anything else you do to it is called updates or bug fixes or expansions.
2.) The developers need to decide several things and then stick to it.
* They are trying to combine two games into one game. Is this going to be PVP or is it going to be PVE?
* If they are going to make it PVP, then what they are doing to the game is great and will force more combat and difficulty for the players. But they then need to kill PVE.
* If they insist on keeping this both PVP and PVE. ANY change to the game has to be thought through for both aspects and have options included for PVE to disable the changes or adjust the changes that they made for PVP. Not sometimes, not maybe, EVERY single change.
* Anything other than this will keep this game from being successful.
* Test your balancing on the official PVP servers but let the unofficial servers follow a different patch cycle once you figure your balancing out and have included options for adjusting that balancing for non-official and PVE.
3. ) Dinosaurs, currently 28+ dinos they have in the game but that isn't something that is that big of deal except that noone can learn any of the dinos before either the developers change something, introduce something, or nerf something so that people can't learn anything and quit out of frustration of trying to keep up with the all the fixes and rebalancing because the developers don't slow it down to think their changes through.
4. ) Optimization. This and the number of dinosaurs is probably why they keep insisting this is still early access, but honestly at this rate 10 years from now, it will never be out of early access as they very rarely optimize anything or they are hitting some undisclosed limit to the engine they are using.
* Realistically, you can only have a total of 40 people on a Xeon E5-2670 with 96GB of ram. Why? because the game need major overhauls in performance. When I say performance, this isn't how much data is moved, but rather more optimization in how many threads *aren't* being used. When the whole server pauses for 10 - 20 seconds because of a backup, that is ridiculous. Wait for this game to exit Early Access.  There are MAJOR flaws and nobody is fixing them.  I have to admit, once you start playing, the game seems awesome.  I've spent 700+ hours getting frustrated to the point of no return.  Good graphics, play control, multiplayer, social aspects, BUT.....  There are basically 3 modes and each have major flaws:
1. Single Player Mode:  There is nobody to raid you and destroy all the hundreds if not thousands of hours you need to spend on building and taming.  However, the game is designed for multiplayer.  If you play in single player mode, make sure you understand how difficult it will be.  You will have nobody to help you double team capuring tames and exploring with.  This basically makes it quadruple times harder and limits your strategies to extreme means in just about all aspects.  Which means MORE time spent, MORE failed attempts, and MORE resources waisted due to lack of a team for support.  Bleh! :-/
2. Multiplayer PVE Mode:  Unless you are super lucky to find a brand new server, already have a friend that will invite you to their tribe, or are ok with never being able to build or tame anything, then this might be ok.  Once another player or tribe has built part of a structure, you are unable to build anywhere close to it.  So tribes run around the WHOLE server placing one piece of structure ALL OVER the map.  This in turn keeps new players for ever building ANYTHING ANYWHERE.  So players just run around looking for a place to build a base, only to die in the process a few hundred times before they realize the server is full.  After doing this a few times on different servers, you realize there is NO FREE SPACE ANYWHERE ON ANY SERVER.  Good luck finding anywhere to build anything.  This mode has now been nullified.  :-/
3. Multiplayer PVP Mode:  This mode has the biggest flaws of all.  If you're a fan of spending hundreds or thousands of hours building and taming and learning, only to have another tribe casually transport to your server, wipe out you and everyone else's hard earned bases, materials, and dinos out of existence in a matter of minutes, then you're love it.  :-D  This mode is fun when there are only a few friendly tribes scattered accross each server, but the massive tribes on other servers can and WILL eventually destroy everything you've ever worked for.  This, in turn, will cause you to basically quit or attempt to find another server to build, where you will then again just get completely wiped.  Most of the time you are logged out, come back the next day and see all of your dinos dead, your base in pieces, and all of your hard earned materials gone or destroyed.  When you look at the tribe log to see who destroyed you, you'll just see a bunch of squares for names.  You'll never even KNOW who did it.  This mode will suck your soul out, chew it up, spit it back into your face, and laugh about it.  :-/
So, to wrap it up.....
DO NOT BUY THIS GAME.......
(until it comes out of early access)  :-)

Waste of money. At first, the game may seen slightly entertaining and fun until you realise how bad it actually is.
Here's the main problems with the game (I tried to make the list as small as possible, but I couldn't resist).
-Bases are easily raidable online and offline. It's stupidly easy to create explosives that do huge chunks of damage to bases. If you were to play efficiently, you could easily raid a large base from scratch after an hour or 2. Basically, you're going to be raided unless your base is well hidden (Which is pretty hard to do due to the terrrible snap and collision points).
-There are countless bugs that aren't fixed yet new content is added. I've had this game for a fair amount of time now, and bugs/glitches that were in the game when I first played it are still here, yet loads of new purchasable content has been added.
-There is literally no PvP aspect to the game. If you're the type of person that likes close and fair PvP, don't get Ark. Within the 200 or so hours I've played the game I've only ever engaged in one or two fair PvP fights with other players (Although they only lasted a few moments). Most of the time that you find other players (Which is rare), they'll either be a completely different level to you (Meaning one of you is much stronger than the other) or they'll have a tamed dino that they can 1 hit you with. If you wanted a good PvP aspect, go play Rust.
-The game is completely unbalanced for new players. When joining a new server, the hardest challenge is actually getting resources without being 1 hit from wild dinos that are everywhere. And if somehow, you get enough resources to build a base, you face the challenge of not getting raided by alpha players on the server, who could easily destroy your base with one or two explosives that take them no time to get.
-Like I mentioned in the first point, the building aspect of the game is terrible. If you can't find a flat piece of land, then building a base isn't going to be fun unless the server has a building mod, and if you're trying to build a hidden base by building by rocks or trees for cover, then good luck because the snap and collision points of building items are terrible, leaving you with the choice of building an open base that can be easily raided or finding another server with a building mod.
-The User Interface is confusing, hard to use and bad looking. After the recent update, a new UI was added to the game (Even though the previous UI was perfectly fine). Oh, and guess what. They didn't fix any bugs in this new update! Not only does it look horrible, it's way too confusing for what it needs to do. Even with experience it takes me a while to actally understand what I'm doing in the interface. It almost feels like they've put looks over efficiency (Which they've horribly failed at).
So, overall. If you want a laggy, badly optimised game that is completely unbalanced, filled with bugs and glitches that they just brush to the side as they add new content, insanely bad looking and confusing UIs and with no PvP aspect at all, then this is the perfact game. If not, then there's always Rust.

Tons of unique Warframes and weapons

Outstanding mod system

Factions

I had fun in this game, playing alone and together with friends. There are several options to choose from, when you create your character that will define your game experience. Moreover, the different maps have beautiful landscapes and overall nice graphics.
That being said, here is why I still don't recommend:
- After two years in Early Access the game has finally been released. And there are still the same old performance issues, game crashes, glitches and bugs. For example, if you open a trough inventory, you get a freeze screen that will last up to ten seconds. There are certain points on your map where the game will always freeze, no matter what your settings are and it will happen not only to you, but everyone who passes by that certain point. These are just some examples. Might not sound like much, but it adds up and when you've experienced this for many months and have read devs promising to get rid of all of this again and again, it just really starts to get disappointing. ESPECIALLY after such a long time of remaining in EA.
DUPING is still a thing!
- Some features of the game are simply too time consuming. Like hatching and raising a Giganotosaurus, for example. You will be sleep deprived and pretty much have to disengange in any kind of real life activity for the duration of almost two weeks, just to raise one of them. It's one of the more extreme examples, still I think there is no real sense to this, other than to force you to stay online.
Taming takes hours as well in many cases, even if you brought the best available food option.
If you plan on breeding aquatic dinos, know that none of them will lay eggs, so you have to plan like with mammals. Example: A Dunkleosteus is pregnant for almost eight hours. The baby phase lasts a bit more than nine hours. Babies need to be handfed, meaning you will have to plan a whole day just to get that baby to the juvenile phase. It can then eat from the trough, which will have to be re-filled every few hours to keep the juvenile & adolescent offspring from starving. They eat a LOT. Since this is time consuming it makes sense to raise more than just one baby at any time. It also means you will have to farm food. It makes sense to play in a tribe where people can share responsibilities, but not everyone wants to play in big tribes, because it also takes away a lot of fun, if you enjoy progressing through the different stages of the game. It's just not the same experience, if there is no real need to do that because there's heaps of everything already there anyway.
- Legacy Servers: Those were created from old official servers that won't be wiped due to release. Players on such servers have no customer support anymore. What's the point?
- Server transfers: Have caused nothing but problems, e. g. chinese raiding tribes that wipe whole servers, before moving on to the next. Duping became extremely useful because of server transfers as well and has been an issue and probably always will be. Your character can be deleted while transferring and won't be restored, due to a policy change at Wildcard. All they offer is boosting a new character to the same level the old one was. Imprinting bonuses you might have had on your dinos will be lost. If you get them back at all. Your base and all your stuff might get lost this way as well.
- Everything has a decay timer: structures, dinos...if you don't log into the game often enough and don't reset your timers, everything will be auto-demolished / deleted. That's not a big problem if you play on a daily basis. Just don't go on a vacation or take a break from the game lasting longer than a week or two (dinos will be auto deleted after one week, with structures you have different timers). Again this is no real issue, if you're in a big tribe with ppl you met online. If you prefer playing with your boyfriend, kids, wife, real life friends...those people you also like to go on vacations with...well, then be prepared to start over when you come back. You will probably reach a point where it feels like you only ever log on to feed your dinos and reset timers. At that point it will become a nuisance to even think about the game, although in the back of your mind you will still like it. But let's be real: start over after you lost a base and your dinos that took months to build, tame and breed? Just because you wanted to take a break and travel a bit? Sorry, but that's just far too extreme.
- Some stuff just doesn't make sense, like for example glass structures: Those are fairly expensive to produce and it breaks easily, which is ok. It IS special after all. Why then, does it need a five day decay timer on top of that? It should last as long as metal structures, imo (16 days).
- Flyers: After the nerf they are still slow...too slow, much too sloooooooooooow.

Note "flyer" refers only the mountable flyers and excludes creatures such as the Onyc, Dimorphodon and Vulture.

I've played this game for far too long—even sold my soul to DE to become a Guide of the Lotus—and y'know what? I still enjoy it!
Bar a few, as with any other game, the community is great; full of kind and caring people who just want to help out. The developers are great people too, and you really see that come out through Prime Time and the Devstreams.
The game itself is pretty fun, though there is a fair bit of a grind at times (welcome to Free2Play, mate), but it's still good, and definitely worthwhile—and when you're sick of the grind, you've got the Relays (recommended) or Region chat to go to chat with others about various things!
If you're on a low-end computer, though, be wary, because you may find yourself freezing a lot and possibly being kicked out of squads if you freeze for more than about three seconds, or it will kick those in your squad if you're the host; turning your graphics settings down often helps with this.
Storyline in Warframe is mainly contained in quest dialogue, so I suggest paying attention to that as you progress through it; some stuff you expect, but others you might not—oh, and then there's some long-existing jokes from the game that became canon!
Have fun and good luck, Tenno!

EDIT 11/4/17 everything below asterisks is old.  But I wanted to add this one thing.....
The Second Dream is quite possibly the greatest quest that any game has ever come out with.  And it speaks VOLUMES that to this day (the quest is quite old now), the community for the most part does it's best to NOT spoil it for newbies.  The way the game fundamentally shifts after that quest is huge - your perception of who the Tenno are just so fundamentally shifts - the quest always brings out an emotional response of some sort.  Usually shock, and amazement - but it also illicit's tears of joys from some of us.
You OWE IT TO YOURSELF AS A GAMER - if you love this medium, to put the hours in necessary to unlock and play this quest spoiler free.  This quest is a masterpiece.  Everybody should play through it once.
************************************************************************
There is a very good reason why this game is always one of the top 20 most played consistantly on Steam for as long as it has - it's good... it's damn good.  It scratches that action itch in a way that makes you feel like an absolute badass.  You're a flippin' space ninja for Sigmar's sake!
Don't get me wrong, you'll put it down after a bit.  But you 'll quickly find once you get past the initial levels that it will be the game you keep coming back to again and again to fill those gaps between the games you really want to play.  It's like that old familiar lover you can't put down and like to hook up with again between relationships.  Reliable and solid.
Let me point out a few of it's Pros and Cons
CONS
- I'm not sure why the hell they call it a Beta at this point.  Game has a huge amount of polish and they are raking in the dough in the cash shop.
- Can be very very grindy if you can't get into the core gameplay (and if you can't what the actual ♥♥♥♥ is wrong with you?)
- It's peer to peer so playing coop on laggy hosts can be a pain.
- Really rough starting out - the new player experience needs a LOT of work.
- I don't like how most of the color pallet for customizating your warframe is behind a paywall, but that's really a nitpick.  Game is so awesome I really don't care.  Honestly I'm just trying to find bad things to say at this point.
PROS
- Game is absolutely beautiful and runs very well on even lower end machines.
- Very easy to group with friends
- They understands how Free To Play is SUPPOSED to work.  There is absollutely NOTHING that affects gameplay in the cash shop that you can't farm yourself if you're patient.  Only cosmetics are cash only, and even then they will allow you to trade the game's cash currency with players for certain drops in the game.
- VERY responsive devs are in charge of this thing.  They really listen to the community.
- The customization options in this game are absolutely INSANE.  Just walk into a relay and look at the sheer variety of Warframes and their color schemes... And they all look BADASS
- New content comes in often, and they are not afraid to revamp something that is obsoleted by something else.
And finally - the greatest thing I can say about this game above all else - the Community is AWESOME.  Great bunch of folks.  They have a passion for the game and thus love to help people through those rough new levels.
Really, I can't recommend the game enough.  You really should see why this game is played so much.  It's a sleeper hit that isn't getting enough attention - but that's probably what's keeping it's community so awesome :)

I copied this review from another user because it reflects my feelings for the game.
I have over 200 hours into the game, compared to a lot of ARK players i'm still a noob so if you aren't ready to turn this into a full time job, don't even bother thinking about getting this game. I'll explain why this game is a full time job later on, but basically it punishes any player that can't or won't play it 24/7.
First I'll talk about the PvE. I started playing PvE on a private server with friends and had tons of fun discovering everything there is to enjoy. We started on The Center, the biggest and in my opinion the coolest of the three maps. The beginning is the hardest part for new players. Every dino you meet can easily kill a noob, even the spitter dinos. It can be annoying running around naked and getting killed by raptors, but stick with it and find your friends and build a safe place. Once you get the base built, the game gets so much more fun. Every new dino you find is cool, and it so fun the first time you get all your friends together and explore a cave. The most dangerous foes we encountered in PvE were the alpha predators. Our base got killed multiple times by alpha raptors, but it was fun because it showed us that even though we had a big base with spike walls and gaurd towers, there was still a threat out there that had to be beaten. Ofcourse once you build a metal base nothing can break it anymore and once you tame flying mounts you don't have to worry about dangerous expeditions so late game it got boring. We basically got to the point that nothing PvE had to throw at us outside of boss battles was a challenge, and even fighting bosses had no point because what would we use the tek gear to kill? Harder versions of that boss? That's why we decided to turn to PvP to see if that was better late game.
Pro tip, don't PvP. This game is designed in such a way that the big tribes that are on top stay on top. New tribes and new players just get pooped on in every single way unless they join an alpha and become a resource harvesting slave. Let's walk through all the reason PvP is horrible.
1.) Alpha tribes. They wipe the server once or twice a week and completly blow up any new players base and kill their dinos. They own the server, they won't let anyone else even enjoy the game.
2.) Unless you're alpha, you don't get a base, they might let you live in a thatch hut. Refer to reason 1.)
3.) Unless you're alpha, you don't get to tame dinos, they might let you tame dodos. Refer to reason 1.)
4.) Unless you're alpha, you don't get to upgrade any of your gear. Alphas block all loot drops (the good ones anyway) and fill all the caves with auto-turrets to gun down anyone that tries to explore them.
5.) Alpha tribes are literally impossible for smaller tribes to fight. They have huge metal bases with hundreds and hunderds of turrets and plants that will mow you down if you so much as look at it wrong. Rockets get shot down in mid air by these turrets, and you won't get close enough to plant c4. You won't be able to bring dinos to tank the turret either, refer to 1.)
6.) Offline-raiding. Just imagine working for 2-3 weeks building a pretty cool base completely surrounded by plant-x and taming about 20 dinos then logging on to see a smoking crater where you base was. You don't get to save any of your gear, you don't get to save any of your dinos, you don't even get to fight back, it's all just gone. This happens all the time, and honestly offline-raid protection should be baseline on all servers.
7.) Battlemetrics. Alpha tribes and griefers use this website to figure out if you are online or not. If you log off for some reason, sleep or work or whatever, then they will know and they will raid you. They can even get text alerts that tell them the second you have logged off or on, or if anything else unusual is going on on "their" server. Basically, this site and sites like it are cancer. Also, it doesn't tell them your in game name, but you steam name, that means even if you make another character they will know it's you. Also, if you♥♥♥♥♥♥them off and try to go to another server, they can just look up where you went using Battlemetrics and come find you. There is no hiding and no escape, so you have to be nice and can't even PvP or else some loser with no life is going to come and find you on every single server you go to.
8.) Breeding. Just another way to keep big tribes ontop. They have huge metal air-conditioned rooms where they hatch 20 eggs at once, each hatched dino gonna be 2x the level of anything a noob will have.
9.) Tek gear. If the fact that they have 2-3x better gear by monopolizing all loot crates wasn't a big enough edge, if the fact that they have 2-3x better dinos by building huge breeding rooms wasn't a big enough edge, now they get tek gear too. If they come at you with anything tek and you have baseline gear and baseline dinos, you are DEAD!
10.) Ark is a full-time job. You must log on every day to feed dinos or they will die. Breeding and imprinting are horrible and time consuming processes that I won't even touch. You must log on every day to make sure you haven't been raided, and you must grind harder than everyone else to make sure you have the defenses and dinos to stop raiders. Don't try, you won't.
Look, I'm tired of typing this review, just know that if you enjoy PvP because you enjoy winning through skill, then don't PvP. No Pvp skill required at this point, their gear will have much higher armor and damage, their dinos will have much higher hp and damage, just accept your death and wipe multiple times because you will lose everything and you won't even be online to defend it, not like you'd have a chance if you were.

Like many other online MMO games... The developers often make radical, sweeping changes to the game that are often negative (NERFS) and the players have no control over it. There's been a steady stream of nerfs over the past 6 months.. first they reduce the health and damage on all carnivores by -80%. On top of all of this, if you play on official servers with 1x rates.. it will literally take up to 5 to 7 hours real life time just to tame one dinosaur. Then it can be killed in 5 seconds on your way home. You have to sit there at the computer for 7 hours to tame the thing. I'm not kidding, go google for "ark taming calculator" and pick a dino and type in level 120 (max level) and look at the taming times. And all of that isn't to say a wild dino might come up and kill the one you knocked out at hour 6 and it dies.
This used to be a fun, awesome game back in 2015 and spring 2016. But Now, today, in March 2017.. its a watered-down version of it's former glory. You need at least a modern 2016 I7 and a GTX 1080 if you expect to play this game and actually have 60 FPS. It's extremely poorly optimized.
DO NOT SPEND ANY AMOUNT OF MONEY ON THIS GAME WHAT SO EVER!! Or if you do.. Remember, only play less than 2 hours of it so you can get a steam refund on it.

Most common one is if you leave your dinos at home on wander, then leave the area and come back, they run out of your walls because there's a 30-60 second delay for the walls of your base to "render in".
No Multi-GPU support what so ever. You need a very powerful -SINGLE- video card to play ark. No DirectX-12 support (This has been promised for over 2 years.. still not here).
The game randomnly will delete your favorite servers list when you start it. Leaving you unable to find where you've been playing if you forgot. Sorting servers by which ones you have played on "My survivor" doesn't work at all. If your favorites list gets deleted, good luck finding that server again.
Many "UnOffical" servers are rented and the owner stops paying the rental service the monthly fee? your 1 year of work deleted in an instant because the server disappears. Many private servers are shut off when the server owner goes to bed, etc.
Let's talk about the mods. You want to join a server? Okay! It has 15 mods that it uses? Okay! .. Download 1 mod, exit the game to desktop, restart game, connect to server again.. Oh there's another mod to download.. exit to desktop.. go back to server.. oh another mod.. have to do this repeatedly for 15 times. Then when you have them all.. you can play there.
But wait! Another server has 15 entirely different mods that the first one didn't use! 15 more game restarts!
.. Oh look, another server.. this one has 30 mods! .... you can see where this is going.
While I'm at it I should mention that all official servers, there are no admins to police any activity. It's all based on "observe and report." You see something? The game itself is pretty fun, though there is a fair bit of a grind at times (welcome to Free2Play, mate), but it's still good, and definitely worthwhile—and when you're sick of the grind, you've got the Relays (recommended) or Region chat to go to chat with others about various things!
If you're on a low-end computer, though, be wary, because you may find yourself freezing a lot and possibly being kicked out of squads if you freeze for more than about three seconds, or it will kick those in your squad if you're the host; turning your graphics settings down often helps with this.
Storyline in Warframe is mainly contained in quest dialogue, so I suggest paying attention to that as you progress through it; some stuff you expect, but others you might not—oh, and then there's some long-existing jokes from the game that became canon!
Have fun and good luck, Tenno!

Okay, so most people sum up this game in two words: "Space Ninjas". But there's so much more to this game! Even though space ninjas is a very accurate representation. So, lemme give you the rundown of what this game is about.
You play as a Tenno,  an ancient alien race that for some reason act pretty much like ninjas. There are bad dudes like the Grineer, Corpus, infested, etc., and they don't like you very much. Well, not that the infested really care about you specifically, but there's a mission where you have to defend a bomb to blow them up and stuff, so..........
Anywho, they try to kill you and things like that, so try not to die. And along the way you get new weapons (over 100 in the game) and level up your Warframe. Your warframe is well, think about it like Iron Man's suit. It gives you certain abilities, and you can upgrade and even craft brand new ones as you go along.(About 20 I think, probably more.) Overall, this game is good, and if you're still reading this, go download it! It's free, after all! And you can unlock everything (i think) by hard work in-game. No money needed! Except, it might take a while. So money would speed it up a bit. This game is worth your time, and should work on most medium-end PCs. A low-end PC may have a bit of lag and low FPS, but tweaking the settings might help. I'm about to go recommend this game on my Curator page, if ya wanna check it out!

Fun and unique gameplay in the f2p shooter market. A lot of vertical movement to be had in its pretty responsive parkour system. Possibly one of the most fair f2p models I've experienced in my opinion (only spent $10 in the years I've played. Premium can be traded for with items earned in game). Probably one of the most helpful communities out there, too.
The only cons I can fault this for is the balance is pretty off (note it's mainly PvE focused), the new player experience is absolutely horrible, and the developers have a history of pushing quantity over quality updates (and they're not very receptive to the community either, frustratingly enough). Honestly, as bad as these sound, it's still worth a try IMO.
The grind is also pretty tedius and progression is timegated (although it's a free2play, so to be expected perhaps).
Give it a try and you might like it, but you WILL need to refer to the wikia often when you're starting off.

Warframe if unique, to say the least. You're in the middle of a warzone from the very beginning, and on top of your powers and armor, you're a goddamn ninja. The third person shouldercam is a bit weird for me, as I'm used to FPS games, but still a nice change from not being able to see the lower right corner of my screen. The movement system is pretty cool, what with all the parkour, but if you're used to crouching on the fly, you can't do that. If you try, you'll initiate a slide, keeping forward momentum for a few seconds, allowing you to dodge bullets aimed at your Tenno's upper half. However, if you're on a computer with no high-end gaming thingamabobs, the game runs quite slow.
Overall, I give Warframe 7/10, because Windows 7 would probably handle it better than my Windows 10 s***box.
*EDIT*
So, I got a PS4 for christmas, and Warframe is free on PS4. Naturally, I downloaded it, and I've got about 10 hours on it there. I hereby update my rating to 10/10. With 2886 hours in game(not game open, but the hours spent in missions actually playing) I figured it was about time to jot down my thoughts about the game that shows the true power of young minds.
I don't need to tell you why you should or shouldn't be a space ninja. Just say it out loud: SPACE NINJA.
Now, onto the juicy part of this meandering review.
-Warfarm isn't for you if you don't like spending a couple hours to get a new gun. This is a pay-to-win-faster sorta game.
-You won't get discouraged very easily from dying. You learn and then ninja the enemies in the... space butt.
-The community is like no other. Ask for help and someone will help, make a joke about the MK-1 Braton being terrible and someone will forma it 5 times just to out damage you in Sechura... That someone is me....
-The balance of requirements and overkill are only what you decide them to be. 633k kills on Banshee is only excessive if you aren't a try-hard, which of course, I am.
-If you like a weapon or warframe, you can build it with the right mods to make it good. Don't let anyone tell you something sucks, they just haven't built a power strength Loki to dissembowel the infested with a single pirruette.
-There is no finish to this game. After completing all missions you can still forma your Braton Prime 15 times to...
just 'cause.
-If it seams like I am starting to brag about myself, it's because I am. But if I have kept your attention this long in this review, something tells me you have a bit of over-killing-'cause-I-can-best-of-the-best in your blood. Tenno, you are ready to play Warframe.

I used to love this game but it's progressively getting worse.  My character was deleted while transfering servers (which is part of the game), wasn't rewarded my imprints back which take SEVERAL real life days where you have to do something special for a dino every three to four hours.  I only got my levels back.
Flying dinos were nerfed to the point where you can no longer travel anywhere efficiently on them and their special abilities basically make them have an asthma attack and fall out of the sky.  3.5/10.  The only real reason for the nerf flying dinos is to force players to take abhorent amounts of time to do everything.
Raising wyverns is no longer possible as flying around is no longer really a possibility.  For those who have never played Ark, you have to go to a really dangerous ravine on Scorched Earth DLC (that you can't take land dinos into) where there's wild wyverns flying around trying to kill you.  You can no longer put points into movement speed on dinos to be able to outrun wild dinos that fly faster than you.  The stamina was nerfed so badly you can only fly a small distance and then are forced to land while wild dinos have infinite amounts of stamina.  This makes you a sitting duck, absolutely impossible to outrun anything as you cannot possibly have enough stamina to escape unless you made your dino purely stamina.
So to raise Wyverns first you must get an egg from the wild wyverns.  The ravine has nests along the walls that you can get eggs from.  The nests are not very large so bringing big dinos like a wyvern or quetz (which would be the only dinos with enough HP [possibly] to even attempt getting eggs as a fire wyverns over time damage would kill you in two hits) would be difficult because landing mechanics are terrible.  You get rubber banded all over and they don't always land where you hope they will.  They will fly somewhere else to try to land.
To get milk you must knock out wild female wyverns.  Before you could kite them into a cage with a pteranadon because you could make them fly faster than wild wyverns.  Now this is impossible.  You would have to try to kite using a tamed wyvern and possibly sacrifice it to the wild wyverns to ATTEMPT to get milk.  Alpha wyverns (which are souped up wild wyverns) fly faster than any dino.  You'd be dead in the air on ANY dino.  They drop 50 milk but there's no way to kill them unless you can somehow get it to turrets or maybe a land dino before it kills you.
Only reason to play Ark now? They added a peeing noise to dinos.

Warframe is not a game that feels like it's evolving. It's just continuing. It's expanding, but it's not growing. They prioritise quantity over quality, just piling more stuff on, so the game is essentially a trail of systems in varying stages of quality, stuff which rarely, if ever, gets brought up to date. The focus on quantity of new content instead of quality of new or old content is ultimately damaging for the game in the long term, when it just becomes bloated and full of half-baked ideas and archaic systems.
DE does not make the decisions of a developer that has been doing this for years. They make mistakes they have corrected before, and then they keep making them; lessons to learn that should have been learned years ago. Four years and they still can't make a satisfying grind; it's just inflation of numbers and zero variety. Four years and the new player experience is still a mess. Four years and they create a mediocre reputation system with no variety when they already made another reputation system previously with much more variety. Four years and their reaction to players being 'overly' efficient is a knee-jerk nerf or a poorly designed unit, fixing the symptoms instead of tackling the problem.
And through it all they have an absolutely rabid fanbase that will tear you apart for daring to criticise while assuring DE that they're doing God's work.
It's fun though. If you can ignore the frustrating development and baffling design choices, you will enjoy it. Steam still needs a middle option. I'm not sure I'd completely recommend against the game, but I certainly would not speak entirely in its favour.

This review will be more a response to recent negative output.
Alright, I'm writing this as a player of 2k hours and right on the heels of the flyer nerf that went out today.
I know people are ♥♥♥♥♥ing about it.
I know peopl have been ♥♥♥♥♥ing about the duping issue, but I also know that there have now been two hotfixes put through to address it. Most of the complaining about corrupt devs is blown out of proportion, the rest is mere gossip.
The game, it's been good so far. I'm loving Wildcard. I've looked into their development process, and I've never seen a dev team so dedicated to putting equal effort into pragmatic work and audience pandering. They're listening to the players, but only to the extent of balanced gameplay.
As far as the content versus bugs/optimization issue, I'll put it this way. When you're doing board cuts to build a shelf, do you vacuum all the sawdust up after every cut, or do you wait until your cuts are finished to clean up the mess?
From a programming standpoint (to all you entitled, whiny gamers out there) it's extremely inefficient to address optimization before content is fully released.
I love the style of the game, I love the dedication to recovering after the insane losses of that recent lawsuit. I love the balance between historical accuracy and creative license. If you're someone who enjoys playing a game for the sheer experience, taking in the sights and sounds, this is a good one. If you're someone who enjoys the min-maxing of mass PVP and domination, there is great potential and already a decent platform in place. Yes, there are balance issues, bugs, and other impedences to PVP, but this game is in ALPHA STAGE OF DEVELOPMENT. If you don't enjoy the process of being part of the growing pains of an awesome, you may find it frustrating. But hang in there.
Be a man (or woman, or attack helicopter, whatevs), pull up your sleeves, dig in with both hands to a brutal and increasingly realistic island where survival is etched out through a bloody and terrifying process of adaptation and teamwork.
P.S., Team Wildcard, DO NOT GIVE IN TO WHINY PLAYERS. This update is pulling the game in the right direction. This flyer nerf will force players to think outside the box and  be more resourceful. Travel and harvesting is a little more terrifying, and tribe warfare is a lot more interesting. STAY STRONG, GUYS.

Still, I can say without a doubt this game is amazing for being early access. I've purchased $60 finished games that had a fraction of the game play value compared to ARK.
In addition, this game has an amazing selection of mods that are well supported and updated frequently. As a long time Stargate fan, the Stargate Atlantis mod is among my favorite!

I have almost 450 hours but mostly as single player so this review is mostly about my single player experience.
I did play multiplayer and it was challenging and fun but the time required, at least for me was too much. Too many times I would log on and find nothing left after hours of collecting and building. Considering the amount of people that play multi player I have to assume my experience was probably not the norm.
As someone who does like survival, exploration and building I found the game quite a bit of fun and still do. When I played Rift I spent way too much time fiddling around in their dimensions system. Even with Fallout 4 and if you can call that building, I got into it.
Ark allows that as well although I know the game is pre-release I would like to see some improvements to the system. Too many items don't fit right or look amateurish when they snap together.  I have spent a lot of time just creating amazing bases and learning what you can and cannot do but it can be annoying to see gaps or items poking through other items. Doesn't really effect the game play, just an OCD thing I guess.
Taming dino's takes way too long unless you have hours to devote to the game each time you play.  I understand why as they are prized possessions so to speak so they shouldn't be easy. I used the command console cheats on a build long ago so I could get a better understanding of the game but I don't like the idea of "cheating".  Once I got the idea of the game I only play the intended way now. Scorched Earth was a brutal start compared to the other 3 islands. I think I died 37 times before I got to water and a safe spot. That was not fun.
Read up on the Tips and Tricks on the Wiki page. I just tamed my first T-Rex and the adrenaline and rush just to get him to my trap and knocked out was pretty intense.  Working on the Ichthyosaurus just so I can say, Rode hard, put away wet.

As a solo PvE player who has bases on each of the 4 maps, all of them require access with a flyer (island base, cave base, mountain base, etc). I can no longer get supplies to 2 of the bases due to the nerf. If they fix the flyer nerf I will change my recommendation as well as play again but for now, Ark is collecting dust.
Edit: I started playing the game again after the official release and once again I will be shelving it. The game crashes way too much. I have no problem playing Battlefield 1 or any other game so I have no issues with my system. The game pauses and crashes about 15 to 45 minutes into a session. This game was not ready for release.

Devs. I also work in games, and I 100% understand and appreciate your sincere enthusiasm for what you've done. You have a right to be proud of your work and I want to personally thank you for the time, effort, sweat and tears you've clearly poured into this project. I sincerely hope that you will read my review and take onboard what I have to say.
This is a fantastic game to look at and its concept is great. The assets are all well done and to a high standard. The problems lie with optimisation and there being so little recourse where it comes to install size.
At my final uninstall, ARK was well over 100GB. The filesize looked like it would only ever be on the rise. As I need to use my PC for literally anything else, I had to uninstall. There are no options to choose what content can be kept or prioritised, it's all or nothing.
I played this game only with a few friends on a local connection and so I cannot speak for the wider online aspect. I can however speak for the fact that this game runs relatively poorly on even decent machines built for gaming.
I know you have a lot of good ideas for expanding the game, but until you focus more on making the core accessible and optimised, I cannot recommend this game despite loving it. Please do not make the mistake of leaving optimisation until the "end" of your dev cycle. The task will be too daunting to take on. Best of luck, and I hope to revisit this in future.

Okay, so most people sum up this game in two words: "Space Ninjas". But there's so much more to this game! Even though space ninjas is a very accurate representation. So, lemme give you the rundown of what this game is about.
You play as a Tenno,  an ancient alien race that for some reason act pretty much like ninjas. There are bad dudes like the Grineer, Corpus, infested, etc., and they don't like you very much. Well, not that the infested really care about you specifically, but there's a mission where you have to defend a bomb to blow them up and stuff, so..........
Anywho, they try to kill you and things like that, so try not to die. And along the way you get new weapons (over 100 in the game) and level up your Warframe. Your warframe is well, think about it like Iron Man's suit. It gives you certain abilities, and you can upgrade and even craft brand new ones as you go along.(About 20 I think, probably more.) Overall, this game is good, and if you're still reading this, go download it! It's free, after all! And you can unlock everything (i think) by hard work in-game. No money needed! Except, it might take a while. So money would speed it up a bit. This game is worth your time, and should work on most medium-end PCs. A low-end PC may have a bit of lag and low FPS, but tweaking the settings might help. I'm about to go recommend this game on my Curator page, if ya wanna check it out!

With 2886 hours in game(not game open, but the hours spent in missions actually playing) I figured it was about time to jot down my thoughts about the game that shows the true power of young minds.
I don't need to tell you why you should or shouldn't be a space ninja. Just say it out loud: SPACE NINJA.
Now, onto the juicy part of this meandering review.
-Warfarm isn't for you if you don't like spending a couple hours to get a new gun. This is a pay-to-win-faster sorta game.

-The community is like no other. Ask for help and someone will help, make a joke about the MK-1 Braton being terrible and someone will forma it 5 times just to out damage you in Sechura... That someone is me....
-The balance of requirements and overkill are only what you decide them to be. 633k kills on Banshee is only excessive if you aren't a try-hard, which of course, I am.
-If you like a weapon or warframe, you can build it with the right mods to make it good. Don't let anyone tell you something sucks, they just haven't built a power strength Loki to dissembowel the infested with a single pirruette.
-There is no finish to this game. After completing all missions you can still forma your Braton Prime 15 times to...
just 'cause.
-If it seams like I am starting to brag about myself, it's because I am. But if I have kept your attention this long in this review, something tells me you have a bit of over-killing-'cause-I-can-best-of-the-best in your blood. Tenno, you are ready to play Warframe.

Warframe is a fast-paced third-person shooter with polished visuals and some impeccably satisfying gunplay only hindered by the constant need to grind for materials, experience points, and the like. Playing as one of the Tenno, a hyper-futuristic warrior society, you man one of the titular Warframes, one of an ever-expanding roster of cyber-fantasy supersuits, and battle the forces of the Grineer--the ruined, endlessly cloned army of humans from Earth--and the Corpus--a cargo cult who view business as religion--in an attempt to stop greater powers from falling into their hands.
At the time of writing, there are currently 29 unique warframes in the game and they do all feel distinct, both in their strengths and weaknesses and their kit of abilities. Unfortunately, there are frames that have long-standing viability issues (Mag, Nyx, and Ember to name some of the least viable), lending to a heavily skewed meta where a handful of the frames are demonstrably more usable in a wider range of situations than others. Nevertheless, the developers are constantly tweaking and updating their kits, so at least the viability of the frames tends to change every now and again. Despite this, there are very few frames that are not fun to play. Each lends itself to a distinct playstyle and learning their greatest strengths is one of the most satisfying parts of playing Warframe.
You're not only outfitted with the cybernetic suit of your choosing, but an absolutely staggering arsenal of weapons from all across the solar system. There's plenty of variety to be found amongst these weapons; you have your standard rifles, shotguns, pistols and such, but you also have melee weapons such as swords, axes, and staffs. Among all of those, you have unique variations on each theme; an automatic shotgun that fires more pellets the longer its fired, a pair of pistols that fire crossbow-like bolts made for puncturing armor, and a whip weapon tipped with wildly swirling blades! While several of these weapons in each category do wind up feeling very similar to one another, you really are spoiled for choice.
There is an extensive modification system for both weapons and warframes, not to mention the companion creatures and devices you can equip, as well as a crafting system for new gear and weapons. However, these lead into Warframe's greatest problem: Grinding. By this point, Warframe is infamous for the grindwall that it presents as you try to get into the later game content. Searching for rare resources and drops is both taxing and time consuming and all but encourages constant re-runs of the same missions in order to try and get less common drops to appear. Luckily, the gameplay tends to mitigate some of the fatigue that the grind brings on, but only for so long.
Digital Extremes has made a point consistently update Warframe with new weapons, warframes, and missions throughout the game's lifespan so far and they look to continue this trend. There are many valid points about some of the 'content' that they add just being fodder to try and keep players interested until the next major piece of content comes along, but most of that discussion tends to be subjective to each player. In addition, it needs to be mentioned that DE have included premium currency in Warframe; Platinum, as opposed to the standard Credits. Luckily, Warframe does dodge the 'pay2win' label by making all of the gameplay-affecting content (frames, weapons, etc.) available to standard players, albeit behind some fairly hefty grinding. However, some of the best weapons and frames--the 'Prime' variations--aren't available with premium currency, the only way to get 'em is to grind.
All in all, Warframe is a pretty, dynamic shooter that has kept my interest for a long, long time and I hope the developers continue their upward trend in overall quality. This game relies on the grind pretty heavily, so consider that before you decide to get in too deep and drop actual cash on Platinum. That said, DE is very good about keeping in touch with the community, if a little slow on the uptake when it comes to fixing long standing issues with frames and weapons. Still, I reccommend giving it a shot.

I absolutely loved this game when i began playing on October last year, I loved the ambient, The scenarios, The weapons, The variety of the available warframes and just the stunning amount of things to get, The characters, The factions and the interesting universe where it all happened, Iearning more and more from the lore and origins of all the things i came across.
I ended up having the game running constantly as i wanted to play all the time, Even when i was doing something else, I enjoyed spending time on it as it was truly a fun experience to learn how to use every weapon and warframe i could get my hands on, It was fun to create builds for each and every one of them and despite spending so much platinum and time leveling my stuff again, I enjoyed it.
But, Digital Extremes has been making a lot of bad decisions for the last few months and the most recent patch for the 27th of May has been the worst yet, A second nerf for Mirage, A second nerf for Excalibur, A nerf for Trinity (With another one planned for EV in the future), A "rework" for Mag which is essentially a nerf too and  a "Rework" for Volt which left him even weaker than he was already, All of that piles on the first nerf for Mirage a few months ago, Mesa's "Rework" which also left her pretty weak, Buffed on this patch to her old numbers but im 99% sure DE will nerf her again for that and i could keep going on and on but you get the idea, And ALL of those nerfs, And the ones to come, Without bothering to rebalance enemies.
After nearly 2700 hours im quitting the game, Because the essence of it is being lost, Most warframes are wimpy now, End game content is unbalanced and without Mirage's Blind build or Trinity's Blessing build raids will be absurdly and unreasonably "Difficult" Not because of complex mechanics which are challenging but fair like say, In Dark Souls, But because warframes and weapons are getting weaker and weaker with every "Rework" they get, Soon DE will come up with some other nerf for something like Vauban's Bastille so it only holds enemies once and for 5 seconds at a time or making Frost's globe have a small health cap and have a timer on top of it and im simply not going to take all my builds getting broken every couple of patches just because DE doesn't know how to balance a game properly, You know, Buffing weak warframes to the level of the strong ones and tuning enemies accordingly, But im not here to tell them how to run their company, If DE wants to shoot itself in the foot and then shoot itself in the head i don't care, Not anymore.
I only want to keep good memories of this game and seeing it get worse and worse will kill those memories, I rather just move on, spending my time and money on some other game instead.
Goodbye Warframe, It was good while it lasted.

I always write a review when I decide to stop playing, so I'm probably writing this in a negative frame of mind.
First, the good.  The game has a huge amount of potential and is very pleasing to the eye.  Exploring is an adventure every time.  You don't know what is going to happen but it probably isn't good.  Definately a good start for a game.  The vast amount of dinos is impressive and building is both fun and necessary.  Leveling up unlocks all kinds of tools, weapons, armor, structures and items such as saddles.  It's a fun game to play...for a while.
Now the bad.  Dino pathing is just terrible.  Yes you can take advantage of that flaw to tame a dino that otherwise would have been very difficult, but you will pull your hair out trying to get any group of tames to follow you and not end up missing one or more of them, then having to backtrack to find them stuck on a 2" diameter tree.  Controlling your tames seems to be well thought out, but mechanically it just doesn't work very well...yet.
Getting stuck is way too common.  As your "active group" follows you, you frequently get stuck with your own tames and have to figure out ways to command them to move here or there or just jump off your mount and try to order your tame to move. (at which time you will inevitably get attacked by something)  If one of your members of the "active group" is a flyer and you are attacked by a flyer, say goodbye to your tamed flyer.  They will circle up and up into the sky, out of whistle range and just hover there for eternity unless you can get another flying mount to fly up there and whistle it to follow.  These are just some examples, but there are many more.
And of course the ponderous task of taming.  The amount of time it takes to tame a dino on an official server is just not possible for anyone with any type of life.  Like a job, school, marriage, kids, anything.  I had to play on an unofficial server with faster taming rates.
Overall, you have to try this game if you have the cash to toss at it.  It is worth the money but you will reach a point where you feel there's really no point to continuing on, it becomes work and not even enjoyable.
