So Warframe is a game where you play as a ♥♥♥♥ing H.R. Giger space ninja with a machine gun. The gameplay is downright incredible, and gets even better when you begin to use different Warframes (essentially this game's version of classes), weapons, and mods (Which add different stat bonuses and special effects to said Warframes and weapons). This and the premise alone would already make the game fantastic, but there's even more. The community is wonderful and pretty helpful overrall (Although there's the inevitable ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ here and there). The story and lore is really interesting as well, especially for a free-to-play game. On top of all of this, the game is constanty being updated, making it so you'll rarely run out of content as a new player.
Unfortunately, there are still definitely some problems with the game. There is certainly power creep, leaving a lot of older weapons completely useless. And if you aren't into heavy grinding/farming games, I can't really recommend it. That said though, the microtransactions are pretty damn fair, almost always either cosmetics, or weapons/Warframes you can simply obtain by playing the game.
So yeah, overall I'd say it's a great game, with tons of potential.

Lot of grinding at times but there's always new gear to get even if it's not the stuff you wanted so it's worth it because it might just fit better your playstyle or some missions or get you some in game currency (or look good).
The game is extremely beautiful with a -light but- good lore, nice animations and voice acting and LOTS of areas/game modes/characters and equipment. It's also actively maintained with regular updates on both the new and old content and new content is added quite often since launch several years ago. Impressive.
It's the kind of game you can spend hours on or just a quick 15min break. It can be higly dynamic or slow and painful depending on the mission, your character and the people you play with but still fun. The community is really helpful and friendly.
Keep one thing in mind:this game has a sandbox element in terms of customizing the experience. It's absolutely not clear by the way the devs explain the mechanics in game but simply put, the fact that you have so many weapons and characters and that you can have multiple instances of the same equipment and equip various boosts allows you to go hard ("easy mode") or be more subtle and tactical or even severely underpowered ("hard" and "legendary" modes).
The game tends to push you to get strong fast so you don't get frustrated in the advanced game content but if you take the time to play with those many variables, you'll make the game more enjoyable on the long run and it will make you explore all its content and grind all you need without even feeling forced to.
It's a pay-to-look-good and not a pay-to-win and it's free so give it a try!

This is a game which has made STELLAR strides since its initial release.
I have played ARK : Survival Evolved on both Xbox One and PC now ; Xbox since 2015, PC just recently. While this game was extremely buggy and lacked content when it first came out, the developers have taken STRIDES to fix their game while adding improvements along the way. The product I play now is light years further than the one I first bought, and had no idea how to play.
For those considering Early Access ; Updates are released on a consistent schedule, and the Wiki is very good at having that information be accurate for those of us who don't want to stalk the creators forum/twitter. While there are many performance miniupdates (which I never notice taking time to install on PC or Xbox), the major ones always have between 2-5 new creatures added in, sometimes new weapons, engrams, etc.
My advice for those who have never played; Play singleplayer to learn the mechanics. Start by making your own game, and raising the Experience Multiplier to something akin to 2-5; that way, you are not bound by what are otherwise extremely slow levelups (I find progression past level 35 difficult on vanilla). Also, raise the Taming Multiplier so you aren't spending potentially 3 hours by a knocked out creature- but you still get the experience of hunting it down, and knocking it out/feeding it.
Overall, I ABSOLUTELY reccomend this game. Just do not feel pressures to keep all the world states at their initial settings; customize it! Have fun! And make sure you catch something fun to ride!

By far this is my favorite game. Unfortunately it is buggy, does lagg from time to time and is not much fun on the official servers for someone trying to start out. I purchased this game with the DLC as a package deal at Christmas time for what i felt was a reasonable price. In fact my roommate and I purchased it at the same time so we could work together. We started on a low number of players server thinking we would have a chance at building ourselves up to decent levels. Well, we were wrong. We lasted about a week (real time) before everything we built (out of stone no less) on one of the tip islands off Herbivore Island was wiped clean. Figuring we had just run into a poor community I tried several other servers, some of which i couldn't even spawn on the map without being instantly assaulted by some form of defence weaponry. At that point I was totally disgusted and quit playing ark all together. I wanted a game that i could play with my friends and just have fun. The idea and actual game play is great except for the bugs, some work to your advantage at times some do not. For someone wanting an endless amount of things to do and a game that will last a very long time before you beat it, this is it. I liked the game enough to build my own server tower to just host a game for me and my friends. Unfortunately whoever is in control of the official servers can keep them, I had an absolutely rotten experience with them. I must say once i setup my server the game play is great, we do as we please and the game runs well. It still has its glitches where dino's are just stuck, fish are above water hovering, etc. It's on the developers to fix these issues. I am nearing lvl 70 now and things are coming together nicely. I have a stone raft mini base and a large ground base established. Several tamed farming dino's, couple of birds and the experience for us is much better. It won't be long before we're headed into the caves to acquire the artifacts. I really love this game. I have been gaming for way to many years to admit to and in my opinion this is the best game out there for several people to play together and work toward  mutual goals. If you intend to play this game with your friends I recommend building your own server or renting one, however it has to be. Don't bother trying the official servers if you're starting out, it's just not fun. Just for those of you willing to build a server, mine is nothing special. 2nd gen i5, 12gb ram, onboard video, 500 gb hard drive. I can't say it runs flawless at 60 frames per second, but then again most of the community with top of the line systems say they can't run 60 Fps on any server. My system is a i7 6700k, 32gb ddr4, gtx 770 with an SSD. Unfortunately I spent the money I was going to spend on a new video card on my server tower but I still average about 40 Fps on mostly medium settings when playing on my server. My roommate has nearly the amd equivalent system and we are on most of the time together so it is what it is. Until the point in time comes where there are servers that are friendly for new players I'll be right here playing on my own and having fun while i'm at it. I wouldn't be opposed to letting a few more players in provided they were willing to work as a group and play the game through. In my opinion this game has bosses to fight with. Until that whole scenario is played out I don't want to have to deal with PVP that's not why I purchased this game. I just want to enjoy the game with my friends as we play it through.

Long story short, this used to be an amazing game.  It still probably is.  But it is in a pretty severe decline.  The devs have shown a complete lack of awareness about the state of their own game and an unwillingness to listen to dedicated players.  Instead, they have begun trying to balance the game around mid-game content (T3/T4-ish) more more accurately around the skewed conceptions of casual players.  The recent nerfs to many top tier frames are a perfect example of this.  Casual players and players in mid-game content thought that Excalibur was overpowered, so the devs smacked him hard with the nerf bat, but the truth of the matter is that Excalibur wasn't even capable of doing most of the high-tier content in the game (sorties/raids).  He's now completely useless at end-game and middling at best in mid-game.  Simulatenously, they have gutted many of the frames that experienced players DO rely on, making high-level content difficult or generally just tedious.  The nerfs to Trinity and Valkyr have made it so that the only way to do a Sortie 3 Survival with a bad modifier is just to camp in a corner with a Frost/Vauban, which leads to undynamic, stale, boring gameplay.  They reworked Mag because they felt she wasn't played enough and all it did was completely gut her kit to a degree that she is now useless in end-game, while giving the illusion of greater complexity in the mid-game.
In a PvE game,  the correct way to effect game balance is to buff weaker characters/weapons/etc. to bring them up to the level of the stronger options in order to create a large diversity of EFFECTIVE playstyles.  Warframe's approach has instead been to brutally nerf all of the stronger options (except the ACTUALLY ridiculous things, because it's not like Ash needs some work or anything... >_>), removing diversity from end-game play, making everything feel far more tedious, making you feel generally underpowered (when the devs have explicitly stated that in Warframe "you should feel overpowered" because that's what warframes are in lore), and basically forcing high-tier content to be cheese in stupid, boring ways.  Since I don't look forwards to endless camping of a corner just to get through Sortie 3's, I'm not going to be playing this game much anymore, unless the devs pull a 180.  Which is a shame since I have over a thousand hours and hundreds of dollars sunk into it (by my own volition, because I believed in supporting the devs for their work).
Long story short, the devs are unwilling to address tediousness/grind in a frequently tedious/grindy game, and their attempts to do so have only exacerbated the problem by leading to LESS dynamic gameplay being the only viable option at high levels.  Give this one a pass unless the devs pull their collective heads out.

Warframe is a Third Person Sci-fi PVE RPG.
The lore states that there are 3 main factions, The Tenno, the controllers of the Warframes (Who you play). The Grineer, who cloned themselves to survive. And the Corpus, Who work with Tech. The Grineer and The Corpus are fighting to control the Solar System. The Lotus, a mysterious figure who claims to be the "Mother of all Tenno" wake up your Warframe, and that is where your story begins.
The game is interesting, it has fun gameplay due to a variety of mission types on various planets, you do a mission to gain resources and access other areas of the planet, then you can reach the Boss of the planet, who you defeat to access new planets. The game is mostly free, you can use money to buy "Platinum", which lets you buy weapons, Warframes and accessories, however. All weapons and Warframes can be obtained without platinum, and some accessories can be obtained through Alert Missions.
The only thing about Warframe I least like is the Foundry. The Foundry plays one of the biggest roles of the game, it is where you craft Warframes, Weapons etc. But they take real life time, a Warframe takes 72 hours, excluding the 12 hour time to craft one to three components, and weapons can take either 12 hours or 24. This would be okay for patient people but it can get annoying knowing you have to wait a full three day and nights to get a new character to mess with. Platinum can be used to rush these however if you're that impatient.
Overall, I love Warframe, one of the best Free-to-plays out there and has kept me playing for hours at a time. I recommend getting this game, and if you dislike it, at least you didn't pay money to play it.

Buy this game is you like creating things, playing socially and taming Dinosaurs.
However, if you like reaping the rewards from hours of grinding (and i'm talking up to 3000 hours, given some of the reviews i've read), then never buy this game. Of course I cannot speak properly on behalf of those who have accumilated roughly 3k hourse, but as far as the comments go, the pattern seems to be consistent. I speak here from my experiences.
In a nutshell, the alpha tribes coupled with the transfer system has completely ruined the game. With bugs and unbalanced Dinos, it is still very playable.
I have 200 hours on ARK: Survival evolved, and I have almost nothing to show for it. My first run in a tribe of three was very enjoyable. I played on a low traffic PvP server, played roughly 80 hours, training Dinos and getting a stone base, only to be whiped out by alledged "russians and Chineses" from other servers. I knew immediately that I wasn't for loot, as they left most the valuable stock I had. Thinking this was just a typical part of the game, I shrugged it off, built from the bottom in a more hidden area, only to experience the same thing, once again losing all the pride and fun I gained through amalgamating a miny city of buildings and Dinos of my own.
The real mick-take incident that got me peeved enough to submit this review happened today. After having lost all progress with my lvl 85 survivor, I bought the game for my brother as a gift and we started from scratch on a very low traffic EU server. I played an hour with him last night and already our tiny thatch base, along with an hours worth of gathered materials, has been incinerated; Killed by lvl214 Lightning Wyvern, by the same tribe that flattened my lvl 85 account.
Why. Can. You. Transfer. On. This. Game!?!?!? Why should you be allowed to take all your OP tames onto any server, and needlessly kill freshspawns? I was no threat. It was killing for no gain at all and for what momentary fun he had on his dragon, I cannot physically play as a result. Even after I changed server. There's no escaping it. If this game wants any form of future, it needs get rid of it, PLEASE!!
I loved playing this game a lot, so it's a genuine shame that it facilitates such over-powered crap. Hopefully when the game comes out in full release, this element of the game will have been fixed or removed.
Major rant aside, some other annoying things you want to keep and eye out for are:

ARK survival evolved is a brilliant concept which was not so brilliantly executed. A survival game where dinosaurs can be fought and tamed all while exploring a vast island sectioned off into unique regions including snow, swamp, redwood, and jungle just to name a few. ARKs launch was poorly optimized with even the best computers struggling to render the in-game world meaning players would just have to accept running from a dilo at 13 frames per second or the long taming times for dinos. These are only two problems out of a pool of glitches and bugs that were slow to be fixed or havent been fixed, luckily this game is in early access meaning it could turn into something great if the community and developers work hard enough. To save time on my part and yours Im going to list out some pros and cons.
Pros:
-Massive world blooming with caves, ruins, and creatures
-Active Devs
-Replayability
-Workshop content
-Amazing community
-Cinematic views
-Easy to learn gameplay
-Painting
-Being able to capture prisoners and make traps like IEDs, bear traps, and sleep/noise traps
-Editable rafts
-Battle brontos
Cons
-Official servers
-Snapshot_16 glitch
-Slow progression
-Slow taming speed
-Good community servers are few and far between
-Alpha tribes
-Jellyfish and eels (Hold you still as well as your dino in an electric field until you die)
-Building can be a struggle sometimes
-Trodons
-You need to eat every 3 seconds
-Mini sarcos jumping out of thin air to grab you off your mount (They dont let go)
-Bugs
-Compys
-Battle brontos
-Turret platfroms left in random places waiting to shoot the s*** out of you and your mount
Even though the dinos can be unbalanced and alpha tribes can wipe you with ease the game is still a hell of alot of fun to play with friends. The minute you spawn into a world so many options open up for the player and from start to finish its a grind with the game becoming easier and harder at the same time.
Its worth a buy

Right, i really wanted to write something for this game as it is becoming one of the main games i play really quick wich surprises me since i like to "stick" to games.
This game is just awesome, and especially for a free one. So if you're doubting to try it, its free & certainly worth your time.
Pro's :
-Runs really smooth, no strange fps drops, minor glitches, so far didnt crash a single time.
-Nice graphics
-Feels the devs are actually constantly doing their work wich can't be said about all games especially free ones
-A nice community
-Controls are easy to master, no need to faceroll your keyboard and hope you're hitting the right skill to make your char do what you want.
-Once you figure out the mod and crafting system its really nice to work out a decent build for the warframe you like.
-Wide range of weapons and skills to try out and level up, switch them around to your liking.
-Not too much "premium only content" meaning most of what is on the marketplace that you purchase with real money is also obtainable ingame with a bit of work. + real money credit (platinum) is also tradable ingame.
-Personal  pro : its nice to see old weaponry aka bows, crossbows, throwing knives .. are sometimes better than the spray and pray machine guns, it doesnt feel you're "weaker" when playing with less firepower, on the contrary, its even extremely satisfying to mow trough a mob with nunchucks.
Cons:
-People calling it grindfest and p2w ... well ... yes you have to put some effort in stuff gathering recourses and blueprints for the stuff you want and just buying things and canceling the waittime with platinum is real. BUT its a free game, don't expect to download it and get everything thrown in your lap.They need money , and you need something to work for and have a goal.
-Unlocking quests & certain features and items arnt really pointed out well, so if you dont know someone who's already playing the game for hours and hours, make google your best friend.Altho its really easy to find stuff on google and once you read the guidelines you're like "aahhh yeah" and not "?????" even more.
-Waittimes. As stated above, yes you need a goal etc but some waittimes are kinda rediculous ... 3days for a warframe to complete ... after waiting 12h for the seperate parts to finish, is imo a bit long altho theres enough stuff to do in the meantime.
So in short, if you're still doubting , its free and not a waste of your time to at least try it out its a well maintained and fun game.

I absolutely loved this game when i began playing on October last year, I loved the ambient, The scenarios, The weapons, The variety of the available warframes and just the stunning amount of things to get, The characters, The factions and the interesting universe where it all happened, Iearning more and more from the lore and origins of all the things i came across.
I ended up having the game running constantly as i wanted to play all the time, Even when i was doing something else, I enjoyed spending time on it as it was truly a fun experience to learn how to use every weapon and warframe i could get my hands on, It was fun to create builds for each and every one of them and despite spending so much platinum and time leveling my stuff again, I enjoyed it.
But, Digital Extremes has been making a lot of bad decisions for the last few months and the most recent patch for the 27th of May has been the worst yet, A second nerf for Mirage, A second nerf for Excalibur, A nerf for Trinity (With another one planned for EV in the future), A "rework" for Mag which is essentially a nerf too and  a "Rework" for Volt which left him even weaker than he was already, All of that piles on the first nerf for Mirage a few months ago, Mesa's "Rework" which also left her pretty weak, Buffed on this patch to her old numbers but im 99% sure DE will nerf her again for that and i could keep going on and on but you get the idea, And ALL of those nerfs, And the ones to come, Without bothering to rebalance enemies.
After nearly 2700 hours im quitting the game, Because the essence of it is being lost, Most warframes are wimpy now, End game content is unbalanced and without Mirage's Blind build or Trinity's Blessing build raids will be absurdly and unreasonably "Difficult" Not because of complex mechanics which are challenging but fair like say, In Dark Souls, But because warframes and weapons are getting weaker and weaker with every "Rework" they get, Soon DE will come up with some other nerf for something like Vauban's Bastille so it only holds enemies once and for 5 seconds at a time or making Frost's globe have a small health cap and have a timer on top of it and im simply not going to take all my builds getting broken every couple of patches just because DE doesn't know how to balance a game properly, You know, Buffing weak warframes to the level of the strong ones and tuning enemies accordingly, But im not here to tell them how to run their company, If DE wants to shoot itself in the foot and then shoot itself in the head i don't care, Not anymore.
I only want to keep good memories of this game and seeing it get worse and worse will kill those memories, I rather just move on, spending my time and money on some other game instead.
Goodbye Warframe, It was good while it lasted.

So Warframe is a game where you play as a ♥♥♥♥ing H.R. Giger space ninja with a machine gun. The gameplay is downright incredible, and gets even better when you begin to use different Warframes (essentially this game's version of classes), weapons, and mods (Which add different stat bonuses and special effects to said Warframes and weapons). This and the premise alone would already make the game fantastic, but there's even more. The community is wonderful and pretty helpful overrall (Although there's the inevitable ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ here and there). The story and lore is really interesting as well, especially for a free-to-play game. On top of all of this, the game is constanty being updated, making it so you'll rarely run out of content as a new player.
Unfortunately, there are still definitely some problems with the game. There is certainly power creep, leaving a lot of older weapons completely useless. And if you aren't into heavy grinding/farming games, I can't really recommend it. That said though, the microtransactions are pretty damn fair, almost always either cosmetics, or weapons/Warframes you can simply obtain by playing the game.
So yeah, overall I'd say it's a great game, with tons of potential.

I would like to start out by stating that I have many hours on this game and I have played it since it was initially made accessible. Given that, I have seen how this game has changed and how the developers have been to the community. But before I talk about the negatives, I would like to talk about some positives. First off, I love this game. It is by far the best early access survival game/simulator out there. I love the game's concept, gameplay, collectible artifacts, and setting as well as the immersive thrill it provides. The visuals are spectacular and the models for the dinosaurs and animals alike were carefully constructed and idnividually detailed, making them more believable and thus adding to the immersion.

Now for the negatives, which sadly otuweigh the postivies.This game has been accessible since June 2, 2015 and yet it is still in early access. There is much to say about early access games, however, that's irrelevant because the developers of this game clearly know what they're doing and know how to make a good game. I can also say that for an early access game, it is quite far along in terms development, though not in areas where it truly counts. In the two years it has been accessible the developers have made very few strides in making it optimized, which is most essential in making a game enjoyable. Even if you have the power of two GTX 1080s the game will still have lag spikes, microstutter and constantly be at a jumping framerate. The game is also subject to crashing randomly. This is a huge distraction and ultimatey takes away those positive elements I mentioned before. In simpler terms: the constant lag/stutter engulfs the joy of playing the game.

No matter how you tweak the graphics settings, this issue will remain. I know alot of people are going to tell me to set the very preeminent launch options that make the game more optimized. My response to that is this: Why do we have to go out of the way to make the game more optimized? Why do we, the consumer, have to set launch options that make the game look like an xbox game just so we can play it at a consistent framerate? That is solely the job of the developers. This leads to another negative. The developers have not only the audacity, but the time and resources to make a paid expansion pack with an entirely new setting and entirely new creatures and other assets. Why would they not take that time and those resources to make the game more playable?

It seems at times the developers are ripping us off by prolonging the completion of the game so they may make more money via expansion packs and other paid items. What I want to see, what the people who bought this game deserve is an optimized game. We do not deserve to be bombarded by paid DLC or micotransactions in the future. This is such a great game and has so much potential and it deserves to be 100% playable. That's all I have to say.

Like DayZ and H1Z1, ARK: Survival Evolved is another Early-Access survival game that has received an explosive amount of attention. But does it provide something different enough to warrant all the publicity? In short, no. You can collect materials, craft items, and tame dinosaurs, but many of those features are not exclusive to ARK, nor are they any better here. Serious functionality problems and lag exist, sapping enjoyment and crippling immersion. Still, it’s not completely awful. Given the chance, you can have a lot of fun, even if there are not many fresh ideas at this stage of development. The game can be entertaining at times and frustrating on occasion, but the evolution of survival it is not--at least not yet.

EDIT:
This review is a bit outdated, but the situation is pretty much the same, if not worse.
Game might seem fun in the beginning, but I would not recommend trying it as it quickly turns into horrible grind where you have to pay if you don't want to play hundreds of hours of the same missions to see if you are lucky, and if you are - go grind for resources now (which also in many cases takes quite a bit of time) and after that wait several days until the item is built.
But then at some point you are either burnt or unlucky and you just pay, as you get what you are looking for instantly and already built. With each update devs look for new ways to make you do that, while saying 'yeah, we want to decrease the grind, sure'.
Original review here:
I guess it was fun while it lasted. It's hard for me to write this after so long.
To begin with, the game has great community and still has a lot of potential if many core issues are fixed.
We started playing Warframe with my friends when it was not on Steam yet, like almost 4 years ago. None of them play it anymore just because of glaring issues that you begin to see after some time.
Developers are focusing mostly on new content no matter what. Game design issues that were in the game from the beginning are simply ignored or a band-aid fix is released which doesn't adress the issue itself. Broken enemy armor and health scaling, useless weapons and Warframes aka mastery fodder, energy management is non existant, most warframe abilities either useless and nobody ever uses them or OP due to superb CC capability or straight invulnerability etc. and at some point get nerfed without buffing other abilities to compensate and so on.
Every once in a while devs introduce a new system just to forget it for next year or two. Two-three weeks after it's been released and almost nobody uses it, and there's a plenty of such cases (Archwing, Dark Sectors, Conclave, Kubrows, Syndicates, Maroo's Bazaar, Focus... seems like similar destiny awaits recently introduced Lunaro)
Grind, oh god, grind increases exponentially with each new update. I feel really bad for newer players. Devs tell they want to change the situation where old-time players have tons of resources and nothing to spend them on. And how they fix it - they release a weapon with crafting requirement of 30000 for a not so common resource called Cryotic. To explain, you can get like 100 Cryotic in 2-3 minutes maximum if you're good at only type of missions where you can get it - excavation. There you have to defend excavator for 2 min which can be simply one-shot by high level enemy (there's enemy damage scaling issues too, yup). Not to say the weapon itself is again a useless one.
After community uproar passed and people seemingly forgot about this issue, devs release new Primed Warframe with requirements for similar kind of resource (Oxium) of 14000 (by similar I mean the way to obtain it - you have to play specific missions to get it and amount is like 10 per specific enemy at best, and there are not too many of those enemies).
After another community uproar it was changed to 7000, which is still a huge amount for many people, and more so for newer players.
Also Void, a place where Primed ("glorified") versions of Warframes and weapons drop. There were already many Prime Warframes released, and some of them have already been "vaulted" (taken out of drop tables). The official reason for that is there isn't too much space in Void mission for many Primed Warframes and weapons, and not to create dilution in drop tables some Primes were vaulted. But from dev-team's actions you can guess the real reason is different. There are several mission types in the Void that have little to no Prime part rewards and devs keep adding useless resources to the drop tables where they simply were not present several updates ago, thus intentionally diluting Void mission rewards.
Also devs tend to put most desirable Primed parts into most boring and long (20 min) missions in the Void. And the chance for this part is like 5% or so, and guess what? It's 5% for one of 5 different parts, making it 1% (if you're lucky) for the exact part you want.
I guess it's okay that people don't want to waste 2000 minutes of their time to have a chance to get the part they need. Not to go too much into details, I'd say Void missions are not the only missions that have this problem.
Recently there was an update addressing most of OP Warframe abilities, and that seems to be causing another community uproar now, as broken enemy mechanics are not fixed and most of the time those OP abilities were used to work around those broken enemy mechanics. I'm not sure how high level missions (Sorties) or raids (aka Trials) will look like after this update as in some cases there will be no counteraction to nearly instakill damage any more, especially when you barely scratch the enemy's health (lvl 100+ enemies).
Endgame here is like it's either you relying on those OP abilities to keep you alive or you get one-two shot the moment you fail to do so.
TL;DR
- Devs produce more and more content (and bugs and broken mechanics too) and seems like they forget of even 2-3 month old content
- Ever incresing grind, with latest updates - exponentially
- Warframe abilities nerfs without fixing core enemy problems that were causing players to rely on these "OP" abilities
- Many initial game design flaws that most likely never will be adressed

So now that I have an idea of how to play this game I can say I reccomend it but with caveats:
First its opaque, when you go into the equip screen the game looks pay 2 win or like a demo because pretty much everything costs premium currency. HOWEVER what the game doesn't tell you is that you can buy blueprints of everything on there and craft it yourself. HOWEVER HOWEVER that requires grinding ingame money and materials in order to make those weapons.
The intial offering of planets looks small but you need to unlock more by killing bosses and getting specific planet nav coordinates.
Now this is the most important thing I'm going to mention here, because its practically omni important: if you don't enjoy the moment to moment gameplay inside of missions you will not enjoy Warframe. If you aren't willing to spend real money to get things faster the game is grindy requiring you to grind for both money and materials to craft everything. However everything that effects gameplay(aka eveerything but cosmetics) is craftable without paying a cent. HOWEVER 2.0 it requires a lot of grinding to craft everything. So if you don't enjoy the basics of gameplay this game isn't for you.
The one thing I do like about the grinding is that there are a lot of smaller goals in upgrading your weapons and warframe to keep you going. Lots of percentage upgrades you can slot into and upgrade on your gear as you level it up.
So basically:
play through the tutorial and see if the gameplay appeals to you
be prepared to look up a guide on stuff if you don't have massive amounts of money to spend
The game IS free to play, truly free to play the main way they get money out of you is through cosmetics and avoiding grinding
Look into blueprints on the market, not just the equip screen, the equip screen makes the game look like a paid for demo(its not)
Level ranges for missions do not refer to your mastery level, they refer only to the level of enemies you will be facing there nothing more
Leveling your items on their own does not increase their stats at all, they increase the number of upgrades you can equip on them
completing a mission unlocks adjacent missions, somewhere on newly unlocked planets are the nav coordinates for the next planet in the progression

First things first; My Steam time is a total lie. I have spent 200+ hours on this game, just not on the PC version.
TL;DR I love Warframe, it is simply an amazing game.
Now for the actual review:
Warframe is a game where you are something by the name of a Tenno, and ancient race that fought in a war a very long time ago. You awake from your cryostasis chamber at the call of a person named Lotus. Get used to her because you're with her the entire game.
You are told by Lotus that you were awoken because the Grineer (An ingame enemy race) has begun to spread across the solar system with a vast army, and you are needed once again.
Que Tutorial, and basic class selection.
In the beginning missions, you must re-claim stolen parts of your ship (Which are basically the things that you use to build stuff, fuse and sell mods, etc.. Whatever.
After that, you can go to the market to buy blueprints for guns, melee weapons, other warframes (basically classes)
and some other, less important stuff.
Or, go to other planets, raise your level, try out the really cool movement system (which is part of the tutorial,) grind (if you really want to,) and more.
At the time of me writing this review, I'm half asleep, it's like 12:50 AM where I live, and I can't remember everything, so sorry about that.
Honestly though, Warframe is a really good game. I can say that this game is optimised amazingly well too, because I can get 60FPS solid, and my PC is not the strongest thing you'll ever see.
Warframe is cool (and i've said it like, 4 or 5 times now) but best of all, it's free to play, and the pay part is basically all optional, because you can get almost anything in game without spending money (If I rememebr correcty)
So try it, it's definitely worth a shot, because the only thing you have to lose is what, 22 GBs of computer storage, and you can delete it anyways.
Just try it, trust me, it's good.

EDIT:
This review is a bit outdated, but the situation is pretty much the same, if not worse.
Game might seem fun in the beginning, but I would not recommend trying it as it quickly turns into horrible grind where you have to pay if you don't want to play hundreds of hours of the same missions to see if you are lucky, and if you are - go grind for resources now (which also in many cases takes quite a bit of time) and after that wait several days until the item is built.
But then at some point you are either burnt or unlucky and you just pay, as you get what you are looking for instantly and already built. With each update devs look for new ways to make you do that, while saying 'yeah, we want to decrease the grind, sure'.
Original review here:
I guess it was fun while it lasted. It's hard for me to write this after so long.
To begin with, the game has great community and still has a lot of potential if many core issues are fixed.
We started playing Warframe with my friends when it was not on Steam yet, like almost 4 years ago. None of them play it anymore just because of glaring issues that you begin to see after some time.
Developers are focusing mostly on new content no matter what. Game design issues that were in the game from the beginning are simply ignored or a band-aid fix is released which doesn't adress the issue itself. Broken enemy armor and health scaling, useless weapons and Warframes aka mastery fodder, energy management is non existant, most warframe abilities either useless and nobody ever uses them or OP due to superb CC capability or straight invulnerability etc. and at some point get nerfed without buffing other abilities to compensate and so on.
Every once in a while devs introduce a new system just to forget it for next year or two. Two-three weeks after it's been released and almost nobody uses it, and there's a plenty of such cases (Archwing, Dark Sectors, Conclave, Kubrows, Syndicates, Maroo's Bazaar, Focus... seems like similar destiny awaits recently introduced Lunaro)
Grind, oh god, grind increases exponentially with each new update. I feel really bad for newer players. Devs tell they want to change the situation where old-time players have tons of resources and nothing to spend them on. And how they fix it - they release a weapon with crafting requirement of 30000 for a not so common resource called Cryotic. To explain, you can get like 100 Cryotic in 2-3 minutes maximum if you're good at only type of missions where you can get it - excavation. There you have to defend excavator for 2 min which can be simply one-shot by high level enemy (there's enemy damage scaling issues too, yup). Not to say the weapon itself is again a useless one.
After community uproar passed and people seemingly forgot about this issue, devs release new Primed Warframe with requirements for similar kind of resource (Oxium) of 14000 (by similar I mean the way to obtain it - you have to play specific missions to get it and amount is like 10 per specific enemy at best, and there are not too many of those enemies).
After another community uproar it was changed to 7000, which is still a huge amount for many people, and more so for newer players.
Also Void, a place where Primed ("glorified") versions of Warframes and weapons drop. There were already many Prime Warframes released, and some of them have already been "vaulted" (taken out of drop tables). The official reason for that is there isn't too much space in Void mission for many Primed Warframes and weapons, and not to create dilution in drop tables some Primes were vaulted. But from dev-team's actions you can guess the real reason is different. There are several mission types in the Void that have little to no Prime part rewards and devs keep adding useless resources to the drop tables where they simply were not present several updates ago, thus intentionally diluting Void mission rewards.
Also devs tend to put most desirable Primed parts into most boring and long (20 min) missions in the Void. And the chance for this part is like 5% or so, and guess what? It's 5% for one of 5 different parts, making it 1% (if you're lucky) for the exact part you want.
I guess it's okay that people don't want to waste 2000 minutes of their time to have a chance to get the part they need. Not to go too much into details, I'd say Void missions are not the only missions that have this problem.
Recently there was an update addressing most of OP Warframe abilities, and that seems to be causing another community uproar now, as broken enemy mechanics are not fixed and most of the time those OP abilities were used to work around those broken enemy mechanics. I'm not sure how high level missions (Sorties) or raids (aka Trials) will look like after this update as in some cases there will be no counteraction to nearly instakill damage any more, especially when you barely scratch the enemy's health (lvl 100+ enemies).
Endgame here is like it's either you relying on those OP abilities to keep you alive or you get one-two shot the moment you fail to do so.
TL;DR
- Devs produce more and more content (and bugs and broken mechanics too) and seems like they forget of even 2-3 month old content
- Ever incresing grind, with latest updates - exponentially
- Warframe abilities nerfs without fixing core enemy problems that were causing players to rely on these "OP" abilities
- Many initial game design flaws that most likely never will be adressed

This game is one of those games that I have a lot of memories with. However, Ark is indeed a game for a certain type of player. It can be long, grindy, and very competitive. Yet, it can be a damn amazing time with others. I bought this game fairly early in its lifecylce, about a month and a half after it released for Early Access. So I can tell you that from the beginning, it had some issue as any game might. Although, it managed to come around very nicely in the time since. The game allows for great creativity in base building.The developers fixed a lot of the early issues with frequent patches, the playerbase and servers have variation for whatever your playstyle may be, and the dinosaurs are more epic with every patch. Which brings me to the next item, the dinosaurs. At this point being nearly a full game, there are a ton of dinosaurs. Every dinosaur is well modeled, have their own distinct movements, have their own temperments, and are just all around great. I personally feel Ark does an amazing job with their creatures, enviroments, and overall look of the game. Character creation isn't the tier of Mass Effect or games of that accord, but it is still extensive for what is given, to say the least. Leveling up feels rewarding as you gain engrams points to spend on engrams (knowledge to build weapons, buildings, saddles for dinos, etcetera). However, it is indeed a grindy game. This game can and will take a lot of time off your hands. It will keep you busy, and even punish you if you aren't careful. Just about everything on the map wants to kill you; other players included. Not to mention, playing alone can be boring for some while welcoming to others. However, it puts you at a huge disadvantage. One character will not recieve enough engram points to learn everything, even at max level. Thus, you miss out on lots of things. To add, strength lies in numbers at times. It was quite common for smaller tribes to be harassed by larger tribes on official servers. Stating such, Ark's pvp isn't the greatest system, but it gets the job done and allows for massive strategizing. You have a plethora of weapons, dinos, and other players to have massive battles with. Now, there are still quite some issues with this game. As said before, the pvp isn't ideal as well as griefing being a common thing on official servers. The game is very, very long towards the mid and end game. It is very easy to lose what you have worked hours on. Whether it be from other tribes, griefing, or the unlucky chance a giant dino swings by. Despite what I've stated and the numerous other flaws that some people have stated in reviews, there is a work around. Ark has a major amount of unofficial servers. Typically in games, this isn't a big deal as people prefer official servers. However, player run servers add a lot for this game. It allows you to play on servers specially designed for your play style. It allows you to play on servers with faster leveling, faster resource gathering, faster taming of dinos, etcetera, reduce the grind, etcetera. You can find servers with players who are heavy into roleplaying. You can find servers that have very strict rules against griefing and offline raiding. You can find servers with their own lore and gods. You can find servers with active Admins who keep the peace and hold events. Admins who can solve disputes and rule violations. Unofficial servers allow for mods to be used, which alone can add hundreds of hours of great content. There's all kinds of player run servers with only PvE elements, and then some servers who are huge into PvP. There are massive amounts of variety that allow a player to fix the problems they see with the default game. The only major issue with unoffical servers is the latency can be worse depending on the server host. The latency and lag can be bad in offficial servers already, but there is indeed a difference. In my experience though, it isn't a huge deal as some unofficial servers are smoother than official. At the end of the day though, this game was a joy to play for me. I got to play with amazing people and start a family of dinos that my group grew to truly care for.

, powered by Unreal Engine 4, is a sandbox survival/MMORPG game.
You'll arrive to island called
with nothing and must learn to survive but also discover that the landmass is full of dinosaurs and other primeval creatures.
In
you need to survive by scavenging resources to craft tools and build a home to withstand the elements. Pick seeds and plant them, collecting dinosaur excrement to fertilize your farm. Or build improvised weapons to hunt prehistoric beasts for their hides and meat.
The world is dangerous and violence is necessary to survive, so players will need to kill animals before they kill you with fists, stone weapons, or firearms. There's minor blood splatter when fighting, and bodies that are slain remain until they're harvested.
Surviving on the island rewards you with experience points and more crafting options. As you level up, you can boost one of many attributes, ranging from health to stamina. You've to reach level 15 just to unlock a bow and arrows.
The game offers to you over 25 different kinds of dinosaurs to befriend and ride, with more being added regularly.
You can play solo or on multiplayer servers, as player-vs.-environment and player-vs.-player (PvP). Working with other players will speed up progress, allowing for development of larger compounds and earlier levels.

This game is one of those games that I have a lot of memories with. However, Ark is indeed a game for a certain type of player. It can be long, grindy, and very competitive. Yet, it can be a damn amazing time with others. I bought this game fairly early in its lifecylce, about a month and a half after it released for Early Access. So I can tell you that from the beginning, it had some issue as any game might. Although, it managed to come around very nicely in the time since. The game allows for great creativity in base building.The developers fixed a lot of the early issues with frequent patches, the playerbase and servers have variation for whatever your playstyle may be, and the dinosaurs are more epic with every patch. Which brings me to the next item, the dinosaurs. At this point being nearly a full game, there are a ton of dinosaurs. Every dinosaur is well modeled, have their own distinct movements, have their own temperments, and are just all around great. I personally feel Ark does an amazing job with their creatures, enviroments, and overall look of the game. Character creation isn't the tier of Mass Effect or games of that accord, but it is still extensive for what is given, to say the least. Leveling up feels rewarding as you gain engrams points to spend on engrams (knowledge to build weapons, buildings, saddles for dinos, etcetera). However, it is indeed a grindy game. This game can and will take a lot of time off your hands. It will keep you busy, and even punish you if you aren't careful. Just about everything on the map wants to kill you; other players included. Not to mention, playing alone can be boring for some while welcoming to others. However, it puts you at a huge disadvantage. One character will not recieve enough engram points to learn everything, even at max level. Thus, you miss out on lots of things. To add, strength lies in numbers at times. It was quite common for smaller tribes to be harassed by larger tribes on official servers. Stating such, Ark's pvp isn't the greatest system, but it gets the job done and allows for massive strategizing. You have a plethora of weapons, dinos, and other players to have massive battles with. Now, there are still quite some issues with this game. As said before, the pvp isn't ideal as well as griefing being a common thing on official servers. The game is very, very long towards the mid and end game. It is very easy to lose what you have worked hours on. Whether it be from other tribes, griefing, or the unlucky chance a giant dino swings by. Despite what I've stated and the numerous other flaws that some people have stated in reviews, there is a work around. Ark has a major amount of unofficial servers. Typically in games, this isn't a big deal as people prefer official servers. However, player run servers add a lot for this game. It allows you to play on servers specially designed for your play style. It allows you to play on servers with faster leveling, faster resource gathering, faster taming of dinos, etcetera, reduce the grind, etcetera. You can find servers with players who are heavy into roleplaying. You can find servers that have very strict rules against griefing and offline raiding. You can find servers with their own lore and gods. You can find servers with active Admins who keep the peace and hold events. Admins who can solve disputes and rule violations. Unofficial servers allow for mods to be used, which alone can add hundreds of hours of great content. There's all kinds of player run servers with only PvE elements, and then some servers who are huge into PvP. There are massive amounts of variety that allow a player to fix the problems they see with the default game. The only major issue with unoffical servers is the latency can be worse depending on the server host. The latency and lag can be bad in offficial servers already, but there is indeed a difference. In my experience though, it isn't a huge deal as some unofficial servers are smoother than official. At the end of the day though, this game was a joy to play for me. I got to play with amazing people and start a family of dinos that my group grew to truly care for.

, powered by Unreal Engine 4, is a sandbox survival/MMORPG game.
You'll arrive to island called
with nothing and must learn to survive but also discover that the landmass is full of dinosaurs and other primeval creatures.
In
you need to survive by scavenging resources to craft tools and build a home to withstand the elements. Pick seeds and plant them, collecting dinosaur excrement to fertilize your farm. Or build improvised weapons to hunt prehistoric beasts for their hides and meat.
The world is dangerous and violence is necessary to survive, so players will need to kill animals before they kill you with fists, stone weapons, or firearms. There's minor blood splatter when fighting, and bodies that are slain remain until they're harvested.
Surviving on the island rewards you with experience points and more crafting options. As you level up, you can boost one of many attributes, ranging from health to stamina. You've to reach level 15 just to unlock a bow and arrows.
The game offers to you over 25 different kinds of dinosaurs to befriend and ride, with more being added regularly.
You can play solo or on multiplayer servers, as player-vs.-environment and player-vs.-player (PvP). Working with other players will speed up progress, allowing for development of larger compounds and earlier levels.

So now that I have an idea of how to play this game I can say I reccomend it but with caveats:
First its opaque, when you go into the equip screen the game looks pay 2 win or like a demo because pretty much everything costs premium currency. HOWEVER what the game doesn't tell you is that you can buy blueprints of everything on there and craft it yourself. HOWEVER HOWEVER that requires grinding ingame money and materials in order to make those weapons.
The intial offering of planets looks small but you need to unlock more by killing bosses and getting specific planet nav coordinates.
Now this is the most important thing I'm going to mention here, because its practically omni important: if you don't enjoy the moment to moment gameplay inside of missions you will not enjoy Warframe. If you aren't willing to spend real money to get things faster the game is grindy requiring you to grind for both money and materials to craft everything. However everything that effects gameplay(aka eveerything but cosmetics) is craftable without paying a cent. HOWEVER 2.0 it requires a lot of grinding to craft everything. So if you don't enjoy the basics of gameplay this game isn't for you.
The one thing I do like about the grinding is that there are a lot of smaller goals in upgrading your weapons and warframe to keep you going. Lots of percentage upgrades you can slot into and upgrade on your gear as you level it up.
So basically:
play through the tutorial and see if the gameplay appeals to you
be prepared to look up a guide on stuff if you don't have massive amounts of money to spend
The game IS free to play, truly free to play the main way they get money out of you is through cosmetics and avoiding grinding
Look into blueprints on the market, not just the equip screen, the equip screen makes the game look like a paid for demo(its not)
Level ranges for missions do not refer to your mastery level, they refer only to the level of enemies you will be facing there nothing more
Leveling your items on their own does not increase their stats at all, they increase the number of upgrades you can equip on them
completing a mission unlocks adjacent missions, somewhere on newly unlocked planets are the nav coordinates for the next planet in the progression

I was gifted this game from one of my friends to play on their private server, which was set to 5x taming speed, XP gain, and resource gathering, with around 4 other friends. From this perspective, the game is GREAT!
However, I had to be cajoled into even trying the game due to all the negative Steam reviews. After a short bit of analysis and after consulting with my friends who have played the game for close to a year, I can say the following:
ONLY GET THIS GAME IF YOU PLAN TO PLAY ON A PRIVATE SERVER WITH FRIENDS!
Progression on official servers is horrifically slow, and the community is often compared to DotA 2's in terms of hostility and toxicity (sorry, I know that latter term is overused by oversensitive crybabies, but it definitely applies here). Only play on official servers if you know someone on a large, established tribe or if you masochistically like losing your progress over and over and over (and with it taking anywhere from 2-20 HOURS to tame ONE dinosaur, we're talking A LOT of progress lost).
That said, I'm still having lots of fun on a private server with few bugs (I have ragequit a few times since several creatures are annoying to encounter, to say the least), so I will recommend this game overall.
I'll update this review if/when I try to play on official servers myself, which will probably be contingent on some kind of massive overhaul of game mechanics when it comes to community interaction and progression. I'll also update this review when (if?) this game leaves Early Access (lol).

This game is, by far, my favorite game.  Over 2100 hours and still have zero intention of playing anything else tonight.  It has its ups and downs.  It does need a lot from your computer.  It may require you to free space or drop your graphics down to play.  Bug fixes and opt fixes are needed here, but for a game not yet released, it is a massive and amazing experience.  I'd recommend that new players start in single player or on a PvE server until you learn the ropes.  Trolling PvPers can suck your early game joy.  Don't let them kill this title for you, give the game itself an honest chance.  The mods available here make this game insanely fun and wildly more creative.  I don't just recommend this game to people, I insist.  If your PC can handle it, it is the best experience in town.  It can be any style of gameplay you like from friendly crafting, massive building, hard-core danger, PvP action, or any mix of all of the above.  If you don't like the game, change the mods up, try another server, and mold it to a style you prefer to play.  Joy is here to be had by all.
Side note, most of the salt and upset in the negative comments here are about 1 of 2 things -
1. A game not being finished yet so bugs/optimizations needed are not in place. Valid gripe, about a game that is still in Dev.  Coding takes time and is done by different groups at different levels. Fixes will come before release.
2. PvP salt.  If you don't like the gameplay, you got trolled, you got wiped... Try PvE, or better yet, rent your own freaking server and make the rules and people in it who and what YOU want.  Don't go on to the official testing servers and complain about fair, in PvP.

I love ARK, there are so many reasons why this game is great.
Here is a list of some PROS and CONS:
Pros:
- Dinosaurs are cool
- Graphics look really good
- All playstyles are fun (singleplayer, PvP, PvE)
- Riding dinosaurs is a lot of fun
- The general gameplay is fun and exciting
- The PvE community is great
Cons:
- Bugs, while sometimes these are funny, a lot of them could end up ruining the experience
- Very hard to run, most computers can't play this game at a reasonable frame rate
- The game seems empty and most of your friends probably can't run the game and play it with you
OVERALL:
This game takes a lot of grinding. If you want to get a base up, you will need to spend hours of your time farming, building and taming. If you have school or work, it might be hard to maintain a base and keep your dinos alive. However, if you put the time in and look past the cons, the game is very fun and enjoyable the play.

TL:DR
Great game, Horrible paywall.
Pros:
- Losts of customization.
- Fun gameplay.
- Active community.
- Can be enjoyed single player*
- Masterfully optimized engine (runs on medium specs gaming PCs).
Cons.
- An awful lot of grinding
- New equipment takes from 12 hrs. to 3 days to materialize in your inventory.
- New/better content constricted by necessary game currency.
- You play under the common consent that anything you have done so far without paying a dime, might be ERASED, DESTROYED and/or OBLITERATED in the future.
I have 90+ hours into this game ATM.
I won't lie. This have been fun.
The engine runs flawlessly even on medium/low specs gaming PCs and you can even multitask! (low RAM usage) and still looks pretty!
It is a multiplatform game (A thing I respect A LOT and a reason for which I gave it a chance.).
I've traded, chated, helped other players, GRINDED A LOT, procrastinated far more important matters, played a lot of missions; unlocked locations, armors, weapons, etc. But... After reaching a certain point... I was unable to do anyting more without spending money.
You can unlock warframes(characters/armors) by playing the game. But! If you want to have them in your inventory YOU HAVE TO SPEND (after the 2nd one FYI).
You can unlock weapons by playing the game. But, after a certain ammount, if you want to have them in your inventory YOU HAVE TO SPEND.
Wanna customize EVEN COLORS? YOU HAVE TO SPEND.
OH! Want a new, awesome ship that matches your gameplay? HAVE TO SPEND.
Did I mention the first weapon I ever got when starting to play is almost as good as what I have now? That makes no sense, even from a PvP balance perspective!
Yes, I know you can buy better things/get more game currency(platinum)/Speed things up by trading, but you have to put a ton of hours into it... Or... You can always SPEND.
*IMPORTANT!*
THE GRAPHICS, AS THEY ARE NOW, HURT MY EYES.
I can only play for a limited time until my eyes feel sore and are bloodshot. This is something only happened to me before when I was a kid. I've tried many configs, but nothing seems to help much (other than deactivating DoF and/or Blur)
None other game have this effect on me (even with longer play sessions).
I most probably will keep on playing, yes, but I will surely end up dismissing my experience with this game after I grow too much frustrated with the ammount of time I have to put into doing anything,
A man can have only so much time, or money, if his wallet allows him to.
*Oh! That single player thing?
- Only after reaching certain point,
Afternote:
If this game was $10 dollars after a 75% discount with all content unlockable (no need to pay for anything else up to now, just play for an acceptable ammount of time) I WOULD BUY THE HELL OUT OF IT. Now? I will wait for a random 75% discount on platinum(game currency) to show up, to buy what I need to keep playing,
BTW. Those discounts appear randonmly every day when you log in, or you can get any other sh*tty booster that gets you almost no help whatsoever instead. So... Good luck with that.

TL;DR - the developers are making an absurd mockery of both this game and the entire Early Access program
First a couple of (in)sanity checks: this game was released almost two years ago. Then a little over half a year ago an expansion DLC was released, with a price tag roughly 60% of what the base game is selling for. That expansion consisted of an entirely NEW world to explore, with new dinosaurs, new technologies...basically a whole new game that just had the same engine and mostly the same rules and mechanics. And still they hide behind the Early Access program instead of admitting this game stopped being "Early" a long, long time ago. OK, end of rant about the absurdity of calling this an Early Access title.
Now to cases. Here is what the game does well (evaluating only the base game, not the paid DLC):
1. Great concept, survival plus team play plus dinosaurs. A wonderful way to start.
2. Excellent world design, in graphics, diversity, and habitability.
3. Very fun dinosaur taming mechanics (for the most part).
4. Solid building mechanics, enabling everything from rude huts to massive cliffside fortresses.
All in all a nearly perfect start on creating a Game of the Century quality release. Now here is where it goes off the rails and dashes any such hopes:
1. A thoroughly toxic community, with absolutely no built in measures to stop the trolls and other toxic player types from actively ruining the gaming experience for virtually everyone else, even on PVE servers. Even on servers with mostly good players, and there certainly are some of those, only a few trolls and malicious players can quickly ruin things for everyone except the long-term, well established teams that have been on the server for ages, who only hold their own by measures almost as toxic to the server at large as the creeps they are defending themselves from. New players don't have a prayer, of course. Example, all efforts to stop established players from gobbling up all the buildable land in sight have been utter failures, and one or two attempts actively made the problem much worse, so that new players can scarcely find a place to even build a campfire, let alone a shelfter from the beasties and then eventually a home.
2. An update system that has an annoyingly prevalent tendency to break things, e.g. by ejecting your tamed dinos from their pens, by teleporting killer dinos inside your premises, etc. And they run updates far too often and for far too little reason. Apparently it never occurred to the devs to save up and alpha test new changes until they are both a) known to be at least as sound as the code currently running, and b) there are enough of them to bother doing an update at all. And of course premature updates then result in multiple hotfix updates to fix the problems introduced in previous updates. It is almost as bad as Microsoft Windows, where most of the bug fixes in each new update are there to fix bugs introduced in previous updates. And yet all those updates consistently FAIL to fix any of the serious bugs, some of which have been in the game since the very beginning.
3. After probably hundreds of incremental updates, the devs still haven't figured out how to make solid objects....solid. Dinos get stuck inside walls. Objects and players sink through floors and often the ground beneath them, becoming stuck and/or irretrievable. Tamed dinos blink out of existence entirely, only to appear minutes to hours later in places they cannot survive more than moments, like in the middle of a swamp full of hungry wild dinos...or hundreds of feet up in midair. Ravenous wild dinosaurs pass right through even giant steel walls to feast on your tamed dinos inside. Players fall out of the sky when their flying mounts suddenly become momentarily insubstantial or when the game knocks them offline because of even the briefest interruption of one's connection to the game server, which is often the result of....
4. ....crappy and highly inconsistent server performance, with very poor optimization and almost no safeguards against lag and other connection issues.
Put all that together and the real problem becomes blindingly obvious: the devs are too caught up adding new content, e.g. a progression of more and more dangerous dinos, new items, harder survival modes, etc. and totally failing to finish fixing the massive flaws in the existing content to bring this game up to anything even approaching the quality level of a final release. That is why it is perpetually stuck in "Early Access".
Edited to add one final note: I neglected to mention that the single-player of this game is actually decent, though it is still pretty gimped due to much of the content being dependent on team play to either be possible or to be enjoyable. I wouldn't recommend buying the game just for the single player mode, but thought it fair to point out that a few of the worst problems, like the toxic communities, bad server performance, and poor PvE implementation are not present in SP mode, and some others are mititaged.

Only 1000 hours of gameplay?  Huh, thought I had more...
Warframe was good when I first downloaded it years ago and has remained good all the way to the present.  I still play it in phases, and probably will continue to do so (will play for a few months, then get tired for a few months, then come back and check out all the new stuff).
One reason the game has remained good is that they have never needed subscription fees or a pay-to-win cash shop.  Sure, you can buy most equipment in the game with cash if you want, but you certainly don't need to.  Everything can not only be obtained though normal gameplay, but you can do so through reasonable means! (Usually!)  If you want something that requires platinum, trade other players for their platinum!  I played for a very long time without paying anything, and was still the top player in most public games I played.  I eventually bought their max price platinum package (while I had a 75% off discount...) just to support the devs who gave me hundreds of hours of entertainment at no cost to me.
Lack of need to spend money aside, I would never have played over 1000 hours if the game itself was no good.  You'll be at a handicap compared to other players when you start out, but after you get some good equipment together and start developing your playstyle...that's when the game starts to shine.  This is a long-term progression game, but that long-term progression has satisfying results.
Personally, I suggest playing this game by yourself (solo mode) or with friends (friends/invite only) who are also starting to play at the same time at first, as it will allow you to experiment and master the movement and combat.  When you feel comfortable doing all the mission types on your own, you'll be less likely to feel like you're dragging down the team in a cooperative game.  At that point, start trying some missions in public mode and try to learn from watching the other players.  When you find out / think of something new you want to experiment with / master, go back to solo and try it out.  I

Warframe is the ultimate life simulator. You have to work fckin hard to get enough materials to build the things you most desire. Only difference between this game and life is that after you get your weapon and new frame you go shitcrazy with them and eliminate EVERY.FCKIN.THING.
Now to be serious:
This game is one of the greatest f2p games I have ever seen. Yes, you may grind for things, it takes time to get started, but once you did, it's awesome. Especially when you play it with at least one friend. If you can't wait for the latest gears you can buy it for platinums, but you can also gather and sell rare stuff for platinums. The game's mechanics are incredible, however, sometimes you can run into some bugs (don't get scared if people call the game "Grindframe" or "Bugframe". Yes, these names are partially appropriate, but which game doesn't have some bugs?). You can run and jump on walls, shoot while doing so, you can use different types of ranged and melee weapons, skills, you also can have a dog or a companion robotish thingy (they can be very helpful). The maps are enjoyable, well-designed, the are different types of missions on planets, bosses, special missions, in-game events and a lot of other stuff.
I recommend this game for everybody who's into fast-paced action games, devastating weapons and epic skills.
TL;DR edition:
Pros:
- F2P
- Can get stuff which can be sold for ingame currency
- Tons of different and epic weapons, skills, frames
- Awesome mechanics (wall running, jumping, shooting, blasting through enemies)
- Good community(as far as I got with people while trading and squad making)
Cons:
- Sometimes too much grinding for stuff (totally worth it)
- Squad(party) making issues (My antivirus software caused it)

The best free to play game out there right now and better than most payed ones. Sure its grindy but the style of the combat and the variety of weapons and warframes makes it so you never get bored of it. On top of the amazing combat gameplay there is a very good overarching storyline that is weaved perfectly into the game in a way that all other developers should take note. You can pay to get things done faster if you want to skip a bit of grind but there is no point because somehow this game has managed to make grinding fun and ultimately that is the aim of the game. To get better weapons to fight higher lvl mobs. The developers did a great job with optimizing the game too. No matter how much is going on in the screen your fps will not change. Im using a 2 year old HP pavilion laptop and i keep a steady 40-50 fps no matter how much is happening (and my laptop has a lot of problems xD)
The only real negative thing I have to say about the game is the very relevant issue of power creep (older weapons being overshadowed by the newer ones). This is not to say that all older weapons are not viable no but there are simply too many weapons that cannot be used in high level play because of the much better alternatives out there which is a real shame because some of the older weapons are also in my opinion the coolest (a flaming sword and shield come on :D). The PvP is also terrible but that is not really what the game is about and the rewards for winning in PvP that can be used in the main game modes are nothing but some average cosmetics.
Above all this is a game that the developers have put a lot of time into, updating it every week with new and interesting content and I would recommend it to anyone that has ever wanted to play as a space ninja.

TL;DR version
Pros:-
1)You get to play as a badass space ninja
2) Tonnes of equipment to give you hours of entertainment
3)Satisfactory hack and shoot game, perfect to relieve stress/ kill time
4) Almost everything can be gotten for FREE, paying money only speeds up the process of getting stuff
Cons:-

3) Due to small dev team, sometimes problems take quite a while to be adressed (be patient guys!)
Long version:-
If you like shooting things and looking like a total badass doing it, this is the game for you. It's not pay to win at all, considering that this game is mainly PvE focused, and everything except for cosmetics can be earned without spending a dime. Even if you wanted to buy cosmetics, you could always trade for platinum (buyable in-game currency), as long as you're hardworking enough. It's not perfect, there are some balancing issues that could be addressed, but the devs are very supporting and trying their best to polish this game up to be in Prime condition (pun that you'll get once you start playing). Pumped almost 500 hours into the game(most of it before I connected to Steam, through it's independent launcher), and quite a fair bit of money as well, to show my support to the devs.
In conclusion, great game for the patient and hardworking, but if you're looking for something less time consuming, and won't consume your life into the endless Void, then this isn't the game for you.

This review has nothing to do with the questionable DLC deal or any of their business decisions.
I actually really enjoy playing ARK when I have friends to play with on a private or low population server.  It's really exciting getting to tame dinos and build up a base. You really feel accomplished afterwards and are proud of your work and pets.  Getting the higher level dinos is a blast since you can just roll through the jungles and forests, gathering or killing everything along the way. It's hard to find a good game with dinosaurs in it, and ever since I was small I always wanted to play games with dinos. ESPECIALLY being able to control them myself. This game does give you a sense of power from that. But there's a few reasons why I can't personally recommend ARK...
First off, it's ridiculously buggy. I've lost dinos that I've had and trained for weeks just because of getting stuck in foliage or on a wild dino that's inside me. I've lost count of how many bugs I've encountered in ARK. It's very poorly optimized, with my overpriced PC with a Titan X that can maybe run it on low-medium settings at around 40fps, and frequent drops down to 10.
The persistent world sounds neat at first but it starts to feel like a hassle.  If you're on a pvp server, you have to have someone guarding your things all the time. Dinos can guard for you but the AI is easy to lure and exploit. Platform saddles, which let you build structures and such on the dinos back, just seem to make every dino that doesn't have one feel obsolete, especially the flying one.  It's really hard to get anything done without a large tribe with at least a few people on at a time to guard and take care of things. I thought raiding on WoW made a game feel more like a job than a game, but ARK has it beat.
In my opinion, only get ARK if it's on sale and play it with friends. It can be really fun, but to me personally, it starts to feel really stressful if I'm not online making sure things are ok. That's not something I look for in a game.

By far the best FTP game I've played...  GFX and game play are outstanding, lots of frames / weapons to choose from so there's  plenty of options to suit anyones play style.  Their mod system even takes takes it one step further.  The customization of your warframe has endless possabilities.
For a small team they really do a nice job and rival any other game I've played (AAA or Indie) for quality and support.  If there's a glitch they come out with a fix quickly (like minutes to a few hours).  They constantly come out with new weapons and warframes or prime warframes and have slowly been creating new story quests and some of the latest ones are really fun.
My only gripe is they need new world content...  If you play for a long time it gets borring because the constant grind in the same areas for prime parts (in a area called the void).  My friends and I probably have done all the void missions 100s of times (we have all the primes) and it's chore after 20 runs on either mission.  You're sent there for every prime part and you must do them over and over in hopes that the end reward is the part you need.  Some maps can take upwards of 50+ tries to get and each attempt can take anywhere from 20 to 40+ mins depending if you want to save your keys and go for the seccond round rotation.  It would be more fun if there was new content when new primes come out for instance.  Or even if you could get them on the planet maps because once you play through them you rarely go back to them other than when events or alerts pop up.  There's so many cool maps that they could use instead of going to just the void.
Bottom line it's worth the DL and playthrough.  New players will have a blast and it will keep you interested for a long time.  Just be prepaired for a grind when you start maxing your frames.

A very beautifully crafted game. I expected this game to follow a trend, i.e all those Clash of Clans rip-offs- I expected it to be a bad Halo rip-off, but it is none of those- it is an original, beautiful game, and I can't believe it was free.
Never does the game show pop-ups telling you to buy platinum- ever. You can farm everything for free. You can earn platinum by selling items you farmed for free, and can skip some time by using platinum, while you can receive everything by playing without platinum. Point is, I am very pleased with the integration of the microtransactions- it is miraculous and I've never seen it integrated so wisely.
Gameplay rarely gets boring- with a good weapon, you can gib enemies tons of times, which is fun, as you get to see beautifully-crafted animations at work along with should-be-award-winning HD graphics, with extremely good optimization. Never have a dropped a significant number of frames, except for the loading screen, which is because of hard drive stutter.
The modding and crafting part of this game makes it playable, again and again. You can make your weapons do different things, hatch dogs (kubrows), have little guys follow you around and shoot the enemy or do something else (sentinels), and more.
This game was created very well and I commend the developers. Thank you for this. I can't believe that I hadn't experienced this until now. 5/5 stars.
