Even the most civil of discussion on the topic is being deleted on Warframe's official forum, and when asked to speak privately with Void_Glitch, DE's community manager told him to speak with their lawyer. I won't abide that kind of behavior and neither should you.
Day 3 edit: DE have released another statement. They've chosen to dig their heels in and condescendingly refuse to apologize or retract. My once fervant faith in this company has been sorely misplaced and I won't make that mistake ever again.

This is an incrediblly fun worthwile game, and one of the best f2ps on steam.
It's a ninja cyborg game with fun, fast based combat, and extremley worth it.
Pros:
+Incrediblly fun combat system
+Fun design
+Entartaining story
+Good enemies
+Feels free, and extremley non-linear
+Again, the combat system is extremley fun
+Non p2p, even though it may seem as so at first glance
+Good community
Cons:
-Grind
-Sometimes confusing story
Warframe is an incrediblly entartaining game, and the playtime has been going up extremley fast recentley. The most important thing about this game, (in my opinion), is the combat system. It is, (I can not stress this enough), one of the best combat systems in any game, and the controls are extremley fluid and responsive. Making you feel, very much in control of the character. There is a fun parkour/freerunning system that is extremley fun to explore. The weapons are also fun, and imagantive. The stealth system is fun, and the fact that you are not limited to certain weapoons, (and do not feel limited by certain weapons), is extremley refreshing, and something you do not see in many games like this nowadays. You will just have a general great time playing this game, and because the gameplay is much fun you will bareley feel the grind. The story, while confsuing at times, is generally extremley entartaining, and it's fun to see the story unfold. Also if you are into story heavy games this may not be one for you. You also feel extremley free in this game. Once on a quest you are not restricted to only do that quest. Anytime you want you can go to any of the planets, and you just feel a sense of freedom in the game. The community, (as far as I can tell), seems to be very nice, and the higher level players will nearly always help the low levels with whaterver they want, and are generally nice people. So the community is nice. I just wanted to also note that there is LOTS of grind in this game. I once did a mission 52 times to get a rare item. (Tbh was ready to kms after it) But as I said earlier the combat is so much fun that you, (on the most part), do not notice the grind. I also wanted to say that the premise ie extremley fun, and imaginatve. As you'll see when you get this game.
IMPORTANT THINGS!!!
BUY BLUEPRINTS FROM THE MARKET, (they help A LOT)
IF YOU DON'T HAVE FRIENDS TO PLAY THIS GAME WITH JOIN CLANS, AND GET FRIENDS IN THE GAME. (it is much more fun with a friend)

I've played this game since its open beta in 2013. Took some time off and on between each updates and somehow ended up with 900 hours of gameplay. There's a couple of things I want to talk about it.
Pros:
- The game is F2P. Aside from the Founder's package which contain the Founder exclusives, everything else is available for crafting and collecting if you spend enough of time grinding.
- Fun and challenging game modes that can keep players entertained for a long time.
-  Massive modding system, allowing you to freely customize your warframes and weapons the way you want. Feel like the gun's too slow? Slap that fire rate mod on. Need extra magazine? You can mod it no problem.
- Consistent lore. Not a lot of people talk about this, but Warframe have some good backstory. The characters are memorable and consistenly appearing in events or missions. Bosses are constantly fleshed out as year go by to add more into their personality which is fantastic.
- Developers respond to the player base fast
That said, some of its positive point is its downfall. After spending so much time in this game, i'd say I'm not recommending it to someone who's not a hardcore grinder or a completionist.
Cons:
- The game is F2P. Yes, that's the negative thing about Warframe. Because everything is free, the developer have to somehow entice people into microtransaction. So? they make the game as grindy as they can. Players either have to spend a huge amount of time grinding to progress or throw some cash to bypass the grindwall. And believe me, eventhough you technically don't have to, you'll be REALLY tempted to spend money on this game.
- The RNG is bad along with super diluted drop-table. The drop table in this game is getting more and more diluted after each new content. Instead of spreading the loots evenly across the game. They just scram all the new stuffs into one already packed mission to increase the RNG (and frustration). There's one piece of part that you need to complete your set? Good look pulling it out from the mission with 7 other parts mixed in.
- The game is time-gated. It's not for impatient player. There are resources which decays over time and resource that only appears at a specific time everyday day so you can't stockpile. If you're a busy worker or a student, you might only get 1 each day if you're lucky. The game is increasingly demanding for those resources to craft new stuffs, so it could take months to craft a specific gear you want.
- The Developer have a backward mentality. While overall, they're quick to respond to the community, Digital Extreme somehow have a one step forward two steps back tendency. Sometimes when they say they'll do or fix something, they'll do the complete opposite, much to the player's dismays. Recently the player base has been complaining about the grind fatigue and DE responds by saying they're aware of it and is looking to fix the issue. Only to further increase the grind right after by adding new contents into aforementioned diluted drop-tables together with inflated crafting cost. Their respond? Recommending you to some loot-cave spots to grind the mats and politely tell you to deal with it. Yes, that is their official respond
Overall, Warframe is a fantastic game. If not, I wouldn't have played it this long. Just be aware that the grind is real and you'll most likely burned out really quick. Just take a long hard break and comeback a few updates later like me. If you're someone who don't mind grinding or with any issues I've mentioned then do give this game a try.

TL:DR
Great game, Horrible paywall.
Pros:
- Losts of customization.
- Fun gameplay.
- Active community.
- Can be enjoyed single player*
- Masterfully optimized engine (runs on medium specs gaming PCs).
Cons.
- An awful lot of grinding
- New equipment takes from 12 hrs. to 3 days to materialize in your inventory.
- New/better content constricted by necessary game currency.
- You play under the common consent that anything you have done so far without paying a dime, might be ERASED, DESTROYED and/or OBLITERATED in the future.
I have 90+ hours into this game ATM.
I won't lie. This have been fun.
The engine runs flawlessly even on medium/low specs gaming PCs and you can even multitask! (low RAM usage) and still looks pretty!
It is a multiplatform game (A thing I respect A LOT and a reason for which I gave it a chance.).
I've traded, chated, helped other players, GRINDED A LOT, procrastinated far more important matters, played a lot of missions; unlocked locations, armors, weapons, etc. But... After reaching a certain point... I was unable to do anyting more without spending money.
You can unlock warframes(characters/armors) by playing the game. But! If you want to have them in your inventory YOU HAVE TO SPEND (after the 2nd one FYI).
You can unlock weapons by playing the game. But, after a certain ammount, if you want to have them in your inventory YOU HAVE TO SPEND.
Wanna customize EVEN COLORS? YOU HAVE TO SPEND.
OH! Want a new, awesome ship that matches your gameplay? HAVE TO SPEND.
Did I mention the first weapon I ever got when starting to play is almost as good as what I have now? That makes no sense, even from a PvP balance perspective!
Yes, I know you can buy better things/get more game currency(platinum)/Speed things up by trading, but you have to put a ton of hours into it... Or... You can always SPEND.
*IMPORTANT!*
THE GRAPHICS, AS THEY ARE NOW, HURT MY EYES.
I can only play for a limited time until my eyes feel sore and are bloodshot. This is something only happened to me before when I was a kid. I've tried many configs, but nothing seems to help much (other than deactivating DoF and/or Blur)
None other game have this effect on me (even with longer play sessions).
I most probably will keep on playing, yes, but I will surely end up dismissing my experience with this game after I grow too much frustrated with the ammount of time I have to put into doing anything,
A man can have only so much time, or money, if his wallet allows him to.
*Oh! That single player thing?
- Only after reaching certain point,
Afternote:
If this game was $10 dollars after a 75% discount with all content unlockable (no need to pay for anything else up to now, just play for an acceptable ammount of time) I WOULD BUY THE HELL OUT OF IT. Now? I will wait for a random 75% discount on platinum(game currency) to show up, to buy what I need to keep playing,
BTW. Those discounts appear randonmly every day when you log in, or you can get any other sh*tty booster that gets you almost no help whatsoever instead. So... Good luck with that.

Unless you have massive amounts of free time, official servers are a huge grind that is not worth the effort for solo/duo players. However, private servers alleviate this issue, buffing rates, adding mods, and generally hosting friendlier players. I Personally play on a 15x everything PvE server where i play very casually, taming whatever catches my fancy, and I'm still exploring things 700 hours in. But then there are others with multiple thousands of hours who play official PvP, participate in massive tribe wars, and play almost a completely different game than I do. But this only goes to show the diversity and staying power of ARK. Is PvP balance a mess? Hell yeah. Is the game unoptimized and buggy? HELL YEAH. But despite its various controversies and issues, ARK can suck you in for hours at a time, where you can spend a whole day playing without even noticing because you are so engrossed in your own adventures. And for those that can afford the machinery to run it, this game is absolutely gorgeous.

To be honest, I've been playing Ark less and less ever since the Thylacoleo's started headcrabbing out of nowhere like invisible twomp traps with teeth.
The majesty and wonder of a virtual Jurassic Park full of beauty to explore and marvel at, has progressively lost all joy for me as more and more has been added to the game to eviscerate any attempt at relaxing flights, exploratory rides with friends, and peaceful walks along cliffs and beaches to admire the view. Where I started in a serene work of digital art, I am now hunted and pestered almost non-stop, no matter where I go, with any attempt to stop and marvel at the surroundings, invariably devolving into a litany of pointless jumpscares and abrupt death.
I not only don't design or paint anymore, I don't even put armour on anymore; I just can't be bothered. I literally only log once every few days in to say hi to my dino herd, feed them, and prevent my creations from simply disappearing.
The exact same thing happened with SubNautica, which is why it is so disheartening to witness again, as if the horrors of the real world are determined to poison EVERYTHING, even virtual worlds, with their vile constant competition and endless strife. This was not what I signed on for and not why I bought all my friends a copy of the game. I get enough stress, conflict and sensory bombardment in daily life, without having to endure it in my off hours as well.
TL;DR
Mr. Hammond, after careful consideration, I've decided NOT to endorse your park. 😒

• Nice, quick and fluid combat mechanics
• Challenging crafting system

Cons:
• The game is literally a grindfest. If you can overlook the fact that 99% of the goals you can set for yourself in the game are achievable through hardcore grinding.. go for it.
• Lack of diversity in mission objectives. Protect that refinery, steal the codex, protect the bomb or kill everyone on the map that is 'infested'.. either way it all comes down to.. guess what? GRINDING!
• Character customization isn't so vast, just a few armor sets here and there and you needing to pay to buy a color palette.
• AI is weak. Aside from being overwhelmed by OP droves of idiots they're really not that intelligent. They just storm in on your location and try to overpower you.. some have abilities. That's about it.

Most reviews on this have at least 1,000+ hours put into their playtime. I only have 100+ so far, and I'm already reviewing it. Strange, right? That's because I love this game.
While I have not tested out multiplayer yet (my time spent in the game is 100% singleplayer), the game is very good so far, despite being in early access. Bugs I've experienced all over, but they don't make me hate the game. You can't blame anyone for the glitches. Unlike many other reviews, I am actually reviewing the game itself, and not what happened to me and judging the game off of that.
It's hard to start out; you have to get wood and thatch, get food and water, and struggle with trying to prevent dangerous carnivores trying to kill you. You will likely die a few times, but you'll just come back for more. Eventually luck takes over and you actually begin to advance. You cook food, make a thatch house, create tools, and more.
Eventually, you get to taming your first dinosaur. For me, it was a Dilophosaurus. But it could be a different dino for others. You tame more dinosaurs and advance more. You gain access to wooden structures, and begin to explore the ARK. From exploring, you level up. From exploring, you also find new things and get resources.
Then you make a sword and a crossbow. That's when you feel powerful. But eventually, you'll think these items are rather weak as you advance. You now have a flock of Dodo Birds for a food source, an army of dinosaurs with Trikes, Dilos, Raptors, and more, and you have a large stone house. But there's still more to accomplish.
The game is great in singleplayer. If you feel lonely or need help, you can invite your friends. I feel as if the negative reviews on this game are unfair, simply because all they're focusing on is how this one tribe consisting of Chinese people destroyed your tribe and how PvP is unfair. There is more to the game than just that. At least try singleplayer for once and invite your friends.
Even if you die, you'll eventually come back for more.

I have played this game for years. I've played since the first version of the star map, since before the landing craft was a tangible thing. Back then, there just wasn't enough to keep me interested in the game, and I would play it for short periods, months apart from one another.
Nowadays, I feel like there is too much. Not too many items, but too much to do to get them. As others have noted in the community, there is a very definite "resource creep" - that is, a slow and methodical increase of crafting costs - that has been overtaking the game slowly. First it started with increasing the prices of existing materials with each new item. Next was adding things like Oxium, Tellurium, Cryotic, and now Nitain, new resources that are required in new items, introduced solely to add a level of difficulty to crafting. I can't blame them for this, they are trying to create a desire in the playerbase to use the premium currency, Platinum, which can be used to buy resources (as well as ways to craft them) as well as to trade other players for items (namely Prime parts) which are typically difficult to attain.
However, with the most recent few updates, the resource creep has become a resource sprint. I spent part of my last week collecting enough Oxium (a fairly uncommon resource that drops in small quantities from a very specific and uncommon enemy type) to build a particular weapon. The gun required 3,500 oxium, which drops in quantities of 7-11 per unit. While this was ridiculous to me, I had heard the gun was one of the best ways to kill a particularly annoying boss, and so I buckled down and did my farming to get it.
Unfortunately, the gun was a bit of a disappointment, but I feel that is in part due to the hours (literal) I spent trying to get it. If the cost wasn't so high, I would enjoy this gun way more, but because I spent so much time working up to it, the end result ended up being lackluster.
There is another weapon which has a similar spike in required resources, the Sibear, which requires 30,000 Cryotic to build - a resource that drops in quantities of 100 from extractors that take a full minute to complete, and which can be damaged and destroyed by enemies if not guarded carefully.
I thought this was bad, but with the most recent update to the game, they introduced Vauban Prime. Vauban, for those who know, is a Warframe whose parts do not drop from bosses, but from (rather rare) in-game Alerts. As such, he is a rather uncommon frame, as most people have not put in the time to get him, or have just been unlucky about the alerts. I understand, then, that they want to make Vauban Prime difficult to attain as well. However, they did not accomplish this by restricting drops (which are pitifully low anyway, with the rarest parts dropping at an ~5% rate in some of the games most difficult missions) but rather by ramping up the resources required to craft him, severely. Initially, it required 14,000 Oxium and 9,000 Cryotic to craft all his parts, as well as 20 Nitain (a resource that only drops from in-game alerts and specific Sabotage missions). DE "fixed" this in the next patch by reducing the amount to 7,000 Oxium, though Cryotic and Nitain stayed the same. However, as someone who just very recently spent hours getting even half that amount of Oxium, and who has spent hours in the past trying to get Prime parts with pitifully low drop rates, I am not at all thrilled by this prospect.
So, naturally I'm just going to spend money to get that stuff instantly instead of spending hours (possibly even full days worth of time) trying to get what I want.
Well....no. It's actually pushed me in the other direction. I'm not going to quit just because there are a small handful of items with ridiculous crafting requirements. I can live without Vauban Prime and without the Sibear (and I unfortunately already have the Grattler). What I am afraid of is that this game's crafting requirements will keep increasing at this ridiculous rate, and I can guarantee you, if it does, I will stop playing this game. I have already vowed to myself that I will not be buying an Platinum with the game in it's current state.
A side note, more to DE than the players, I am actually okay with Vauban Prime requiring so much Nitain, as Nitain is tied to alerts, and Vauban's non-prime variant is also tied heavily to alerts. It makes sense, and ties that alert-exclusivity back into the frame. The Nitain in conjunction with the other unreasonably high requirements, however, is too much, and almost appears player - or at least new player - hostile.
For new players interested in starting Warframe: only do so if you are either willing to spend hours upon hours doing the same mission over and over again to collect resources for crafting, are prepared to spend tens and possibly even hundreds of dollars on in-game content, or expect not to get new content for the game until long after it comes out. (Which, admittedly, isnt' a terrible option, there are still a good number of good weapons that don't have ridiculous requirements...yet. But several of the game's 'best' weapons have already been committed to the Prime Vault, which means you will have to spend either platinum trading for them, or money buying them direct from DE.)

When I first downloaded this game, I thought it would be another free-to-play garbage game and I would uninstall it after playing for a couple of minutes.
I didn't even know how wrong I would be.
The game has a very good community, graphics that could compete with AAA titles, addictive gameplay, and frequent updates.
It's "free-to-play" status may scare off a couple of people, making them think it's a pay to win kinda f2p game, but trust me, it's not. Everything in this game can be acquired through effort and sometimes luck (well except for excalibur prime. *crying*).
There are micro-transactions in-game but the only thing they're good for is supporting the creators and reducing your grinding time from 1 hour to 1 minute. Most of them are overpriced too.
The PvP might not be super popular, but it's fun if you can get some friends to play it with you.
At the beginning, you might think that Warframe has no story at all. Since you just go through missions like The Archwing or Howl of the Kubrow, but everything changes when you get to the cinematic quests. The Second Dream and The War Within. Their amazing soundtracks and even more amazing advancements in Warframe's story will be sure to make you want even more of this game.
The game also has a sort of "collect them all" kind of mechanic, if you're into that.
The devs are awesome, too. They listen to the community.
The only thing that I've found with this game which might be a con to a lot of people is that it needs a lot of grinding.
Overall, this game is fantastic. It sets an example of how good f2p games can be. Go try it.

For all of its flaws I still really like Ark.  This is coming from the mind of someone who spent extreme amounts of time playing Minecraft starting in Alpha all the way through official release.
I have played Ark since a couple months after its early access release.
Likes:
Like Minecraft, I like building stuff.  Ark gives a variety of things to do and a variety of ways for folks to play.  You can go solo building up your own base, when you get bored building, you can branch out to the other game opportunities like taming, breeding, boss battles, or go meet your death by going in the water or deep desert.  there are cooperative playing options via alliances with other tribes, that way you can still be in your own tribe, but still do things like boss battles with others.
Dislikes:
Game still has bugs that it has had since early on set.  Random glitches that causes bad things to happen, such as you get killed and your death cache (bag that holds everything you had on you for 15 minutes) falls through the ground or the dinos getting stuck in/falling through solid object.
Other than those Game related dislikes my only other dislikes are with how support of the game and its various issues are handled, but I don't do a deep dive into that.
Oh and people who join PvE servers and try to do PvP griefing on people (and then support doesn't do anything about it).
I digress...
Words for new/potential players:
THIS GAME IS STILL IN EARLY ACCESS.
Don't join the game and then rant and rave when something crappy happens because of a glitch.  We have all been there.
You WILL die... and you will die a lot.  It is just a fact of the game.
This is a SURVIVAL game, not a "Hey I am new help me out by giving me a bunch of good stuff" game... or "Hey I'm new let me into your tribe so I can mooch off of your progress and hard work at the game".
Think of someones tribe as their home... you wouldn't give some random person who just showed up in the neighborhood and knocked on your door nearly unrestricted access to everything in your house and the opportunity to kill all your pets and burn your house down, would you?
Most servers have pretty simple 'rules', don't be a jerk, don't beg for stuff, learn the game prove you are going to stick around and know what you are doing, then people may think about bringing you into the fold.

This is one of the greatest games I've ever played, although it's not for everyone. It's incredible in terms of exploration, survival, and team building (DINO PETS!). It also involves base building, farming, boss battles, and multiplayer servers. As you progress through the game, there's a great feeling of accomplishment, surprise, curiosity, and even fear.
The game is filled with amazing moments, which great games should have. The first time you delve into the depths of the ocean. The first time you are finally able to go on a murderous rampage down the beach with a massive carnivore. The first time you finally get the courage to explore a cave (far more dangerous than it sounds). Even the first time you can use a dung beetle to make poop into fertilizer (poop is quite a big deal in this game, haha).
The reason I say this game isn't for everyone, is because it can be tedious. Some people say it's too grindy, or has too many chores in it. Personally I love farming, taming creatures, gathering resources, crafting, and building my base. However, some people just want to run in, guns blazing, and watch things die, and this game isn't really made for those types of people. That being said, the gathering/xp/taming and what not can all be boosted to your heart's desire, but I imagine playing like that would ruin a lot of the game.
Also, the game is quite frustratingly hard. Like, you can spawn, and there will be a dino close by that can kill you, so it does, and you're dead. You can build a whole house, then a dino kills you, and you can't find your house again, because you didn't build a bed yet. If a dino is sitting on your bed, it will spawn kill you. Every. Single. Time. You can spend hours to get an awesome dino of your own, only to watch it die in a horrible accident. It's a hard game (unless you turn the difficulty way down, but like above, this likely ruins a big part of the game).
Overall, the game is absolutely amazing, with vast amounts of content, and is worth hundreds of hours of gameplay. Personally, the sense of exploration, and the ability to have a team of dino pets are my favorite things about this game.
Games kind of like this include Space Engineers, Savage Lands, and Minecraft.
EDIT: Now that they've released, and added more content, and I've gotten further, I thought I'd make an additional comment.
This game is designed to be a multiplayer experience. You CAN play singleplayer, but it's really not meant to be played that way. Basically the way the game works is this:
1. Create a base, tame dinos, create awesome gear.
2. Delve into all the caves to get artifacts.
3. Get the best rexs (stats), and breed them excessively, until you get an army of super rexs.
4. Use the artifacts and your super rexs to defeat the three bosses.
5. Use the trophies from the bosses to enter the Tek cave, and defeat the Overseer. This is end game.
There are three difficulties you can do bosses/tek cave on (Gamma/Easy, Beta/Medium, Alpha/Hard).
Here's the thing; gamma is entirely possible in single player, maybe even beta (with literally hundreds of hours invested in your one single player world), but alpha is absolutely ridiculous, and if you wanted to do it single player, it would take many hundreds of hours to do it. Why? Because you need rexs with totally perfect stats. You need to tame dozens (if not hundreds) of very high level rexs, until you get HP of attack super high on it. To do this, it's really meant to have a tribe of a dozen people or more, so that the workload is way less.
To add on to this, when you do the battles, you REALLY need more people helping. Someone riding a rex does twice as much as a rex without a rider. More people with guns always helps.
So basically, if you're looking for a single player game, you're either going to be unable to complete the game, or you'll have to drastically cheat in order to make it doable.

Hey!  Release day finally came!  I don't have a bajillion hours in the game, but I've played most of the content over the course of a couple of years, so I feel like I have some perspective.
Ark is pretty good.  Ark also has a lot of negative reviews.  It's not hard to understand why.  Ark has had a long early access, so it's changed a lot and gone through some resets, and a lot of people lost hundreds-to-thousands of hours of "work" in the process.  As far as I can tell, it's still far from optimized.  You need a crazy powerful PC to run it well.  PvP servers suck if you're not going to be playing 8+ hours/day (and hand off your base to the night shift of your tribe), because other players will kill you and destroy your bases relentlessly.  It seems like the release of DLC while still in early release was a cash grab - but then, I didn't buy the DLC, so I'm not out anything on that one.  It's also just a gaming style that most people aren't into - you really need to work to survive.  If painstakingly sneaking your way around yet another hill to avoid a predator while you struggle to eat enough berries to stay alive isn't your thing, you won't be into this.  If pausing what you're doing to go hunting, and then to find enough stuff to build an icebox so that the meat you harvested won't go bad, and then realizing that a raptor has followed you home and having to relocate your whole base because the damn thing won't leave doesn't sound like fun to you, you won't like this game.
That said, I'm into that stuff, so I love this thing.  It's still surprisingly rough around the edges (and my feeling is that the devs are done doing core engine updates), but it's beautiful and fun and unforgiving.  Be ready to make your own server if you don't want people messing with you.  Get ready to die in new and unexpected ways.  And have fun.

Played for a week, uninstalled it (about 15 hours of gameplay).
Pros:
• Awesome warframe design
• fluid combat, excellent mobility
• visually engaging game
• intresting modding system for frames.
Cons:
• Paid content makes getting through the game naturally a struggle
• Crafting (even for required questlines) takes hours OR can be rushed for real $ (as with everything)
• levels feel redundant to the point where you constantly ask 'Haven't I played this mission?'
• Lotus transmissions have no dialog variance, repeats incessantly,
• Incredibly ugly enemy design, Very little diversity in universe's characters.
• Story SUCKS.
• Garbage AI (sometimes requiring me to out-of-bounds switch teleport with my hologram (using a Loki frame) to get to an enemy who had been stuck behind a wall in the enemy spawning room in defense missions.
• Quests are incredibly repetitive and often suffer from poor mission design, making them infuriating rather than fun.
Game goes between feeling fun and feeling horribly balanced and P2W.  Game also attempts you sucker you into buying Platinum (the real world currency) with daily discounts.  Note: none of these purchases feel good.  ALL aesthetic items are paywalled, Playing daily becomes an internal argument of 'this sucks maybe I'll just buy it' and honestly that's a horrible way to design a game, where the core game is so grindy and monotonous that the person would just rather throw money at the issue in frustration.
If you think it looks interesting, check it out, but stay away from the transaction system.  However you'll probably find it to get tedious within the first few hours of play.  Honestly, your time is better suited to other games that give you a sense of progress and accomplishment in a way where you feel good about it.

One day, I was bored and looked for a new game to play. I decided to look through the top free-to-play games on Steam and noticed that Warframe was always at least in the top 5. Warframe is easily one of the best looking Free2Play games out there right now, and it has remained that way for a few years now.  You select a "Warframe" which is basically just your character, each one has their own abilities so making a team of 4 warframes with balanced abilities that help each other out is great.  In order to get new warframes and weapons you need to grind thorugh levels getting blueprints and the ingredients necesarry to make them, then when you construct them you must wait a period of generally 24 Hours (for weapons, 72 for warframes). The game is definitely worth a try, however, if you find grinding to be a bore then it's best you stay away from the game.

Hmm, where shall i start?
Many people say this is a grindy game but after 1000 hours in the game there are 3 types of "grinds" i could mention.
1: The prime grind (Prime weapons are empowered, stronger versions of normal weapons that drop in towers as mission rewards)
This grind is generally the one you will suffer the most with, its all up to RNG and in the end we all know RNG hates you. Sometimes you get what you want when you are not even particularly trying, sometimes it takes 50 missions and still nothing but more often than not you will be able to get any 1 specific part in about 5-10 missions which depending on the mission type can be very short or slightly long (not that you will ever have enough keys muahahaha). My response to this would be that there is always a better way. Suppose you really need that Nikana Prime blade but drops only at the 20,40,60 etc min mark and you already did 5x 40 mins and still nothing, you could always just do something in the game to earn Platinum (premium currency) and buy the part itself. It would generally take less time to get 60 Platinum worth of, say, corrupted mods than the part itself except if you are lucky, I do this if something takes too long and im broke at that moment.
2:Resource Grind
To be honest this isnt even a thing, after 1000 hours I was almost never short of anything in the game apart from the rarer resources (argon crystal,neural sensors,orokin cells) but if you get that 2x resource or rare resource login booster than you can stock up on these very easily. As for normal resources, unless you just started the game and want to build the most resource demanding item in the game you wont be short on them. Rarely, if you build a lot of consumables or just in general like 10 weapons at once, you may run out of one but getting enough resources to build a single item is generally very quick. My recommendation is that you just play the game at the beginning and only worry about getting a new weapon when your current one is level 30 or is about to be level 30.
3:The XP farm
This is a fairly tricky one and usually only concerns higher tier players. Getting mastery XP (account level) can be tricky if you dont have much platinum, which you probably wont when you start, but you can also just carefully select what weapon(s) you wont use anytime soon or have already decided to drop them. Levelling a weapon by affinity (xp for the equipment itself) is usually easy in normal missions and if you want to make this process the fastest possible, just look up "how to draco" and you will find yourself pleased, though, depending on your level it may not be the best option and finding a team that will voluntarily carry you can also take some time.
As for weapon build times i just look at it as start it and dont worry about it, just get it the next day i start playing, its not like you cant play when you build :D
tl:dr: Best F2P out there, if this wasnt F2P it would probably be one of those $80 games lol, you can get ANYTHING without paying a single cent aswell, you can get platinum through trading and through that even cosmetics that are platinum only... not that you wont buy any plat... ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)

Developers should be ashamed both of their poor craftsmanship in regards to optimziation and of their decision to unehtically charge money for a game they clearly have no intention of ever actually finishing. I would quit my job if it meant putting my name on a project like this.
If you play single player, you will invest literally hundreds of hours only for a bug to completey ruin the world you've built. The dinosuars you spend 3+ hours to tame will simply disappear when they were previously sitting safely in base...you WILL run into something that turns all of your hard work into dust. It's happened to me 3 separate times now...it wont happen again.

I recommend this game, with a few caveats:
First up, it's still glitchy as all hell and poorly optimized. That's pretty frustrating for a game that's been playable for a year already, even though they're calling it "early access".
Secondly: MOTHER OF GOD setting up a dedicated server is a pain. It took fully a day of screwing around with it to iron out all the problems.
Third: it's not particularly intuitive how a lot of stuff works, and failure tends to pile up pretty quickly. It can be very frustrating.
Lastly: DLC in an early access title is pretty shady. That alone almost made me skip the game altogether. Literally the only reason I didn't do so is that a few of my friends have it and said good things about the gameplay.
That said, it's still quite well done overall, so I'll go ahead and give it a thumbs up.

When I first downloaded this game, I thought it would be another free-to-play garbage game and I would uninstall it after playing for a couple of minutes.
I didn't even know how wrong I would be.
The game has a very good community, graphics that could compete with AAA titles, addictive gameplay, and frequent updates.
It's "free-to-play" status may scare off a couple of people, making them think it's a pay to win kinda f2p game, but trust me, it's not. Everything in this game can be acquired through effort and sometimes luck (well except for excalibur prime. *crying*).
There are micro-transactions in-game but the only thing they're good for is supporting the creators and reducing your grinding time from 1 hour to 1 minute. Most of them are overpriced too.
The PvP might not be super popular, but it's fun if you can get some friends to play it with you.
At the beginning, you might think that Warframe has no story at all. Since you just go through missions like The Archwing or Howl of the Kubrow, but everything changes when you get to the cinematic quests. The Second Dream and The War Within. Their amazing soundtracks and even more amazing advancements in Warframe's story will be sure to make you want even more of this game.
The game also has a sort of "collect them all" kind of mechanic, if you're into that.
The devs are awesome, too. They listen to the community.
The only thing that I've found with this game which might be a con to a lot of people is that it needs a lot of grinding.
Overall, this game is fantastic. It sets an example of how good f2p games can be. Go try it.
Nominated for "Free to Play but Triple A" Award.

The heck with this game, thats for sure. After 21 hours, any player should at least have a grasp on what the hell they are doing. Not here. The learning curve is impossible, the land is extremely unforgiving and over-powered, and there is so much crap in this game that ruins the fun aspect of it.
Let's start with the learning curve. As a new character, you expect at least a tutorial or some written stuff on how to help you begin. Not here, you join any game whatsoever, and you just spawn. Punch a tree, make a pickaxe, and get killed by an agressor that by the way, you weren't even bothering. You walk around blind and not sure what you are doing for hours before coming to any idea on what you should do.
Next is the overpowered land and animals. I talked about it a bit above, and yes, it is bad. Whether it be a dilo (spits poison), raptor, or God-Forbid, a Tickle Chicken (Therizinosaurus). Even at low, low levels, these monsters can kill you. I had about 20 hours of work and 4 high-level dinos (1 Terror Bird, 1 Parasaur, 1 Trike, and 1 Pteradon all above 150) be absolutely obliterated in seconds, and the Therizinosaurus was only level 16. Don't even consider taming one, thats impossible unless you have high-level T-rexes or Gigas. The dilos and raptors are easy enough to kill once you get a spear, but for a fresh spawn, you will be killed instantly. There are many more dinos that are overpowered (Sarcos which are crocodiles, Titanboas which are boas, and Gigas like I said above) that spawn all the time and end your game easily.
Finally, we get to the little amount of fun it has. All of above combined just makes it impossible and rage-inducing for anyone, experienced or unexperienced, to start out. Serious cheats are required, which luckily are easy to get, to start out well as a freshly spawned new guy.
By the way, the cake metaphor is great, and also check the "approximately how long will this game be in early access?" note. June 2016? Not a chance in hell with this overpowered mess of a terrible game.
I would not wish this game upon my worst enemy.

Once you reach level 30 with one of your warframes, the game itself becomes very very repetitive, it's all about grinding either reputation with Syndicates or matchmaking with people who usually AFK out so you're left alone.

I'll say that for a free game, it's not bad, however, the complete deal braker is that all the aesthetic goodies you can get are only available through microtransactions and you can't obtain them othwerise. There are certain giveaways, but the games main selling point (Looking Cool) is shadowed by the "Pay to look Cool" marketing scheme.
It was fun for a couple of hours, but I wouldn't recommend investing too much time in it since basically, all you do at endgame is grind new frames and max out mods with no real other gameplay than grinding.

I had about 20 hours of work and 4 high-level dinos (1 Terror Bird, 1 Parasaur, 1 Trike, and 1 Pteradon all above 150) be absolutely obliterated in seconds, and the Therizinosaurus was only level 16. Don't even consider taming one, thats impossible unless you have high-level T-rexes or Gigas. The dilos and raptors are easy enough to kill once you get a spear, but for a fresh spawn, you will be killed instantly. There are many more dinos that are overpowered (Sarcos which are crocodiles, Titanboas which are boas, and Gigas like I said above) that spawn all the time and end your game easily.
Finally, we get to the little amount of fun it has. All of above combined just makes it impossible and rage-inducing for anyone, experienced or unexperienced, to start out. Serious cheats are required, which luckily are easy to get, to start out well as a freshly spawned new guy.
By the way, the cake metaphor is great, and also check the "approximately how long will this game be in early access?" note. June 2016? Not a chance in hell with this overpowered mess of a terrible game.

I've been playing this game for... quite a long while, as you can see up there. Maybe more than I should have, but that's definitely not the game's fault.
So, where to begin. Here you have a solid game with a similarly solid core of features: it has an extremely good (yet surprisingly scaleable, and I've been able to play with good framerates even on older hardware) graphic compartment, excellent animations, a very interesting setting and great art design. The sound compartment is quite good as well, the music is not particularly evocative (although it does have its moments), with the sounds being quite diverse and interesting from firearm to firearm, from power to power and from tileset to tileset.
The gameplay itself is where the game truly shines: it can be described as a third person action title with a strong shooter and melee component, a good if not great parkour system and a vast wealth of different Warframes (your RPG class, if you'd like), each one of them carrying different powers in battle. And let's not forget the large amount of different weaponry you'll be able to wield, from rocket and grenade launchers to Dead Space-esque cutting lasers and incredibly diverse melee weapons. There is no shortage of content here, especially if you tend to be a completionist.
Now, don't misunderstand me. It's not all roses and flowers. this IS with no doubt a "typical" free to play game. If you have too much time on your hands, like I do (insert sad face here) then you might want to stop a while and play with this one. You will have many items to grind for, many events in which to partake, interesting and sometimes even challenging missions to try. The fairly recent Sortie addition was quite pleasant as well, especially when you realize that Warframe doesn't really have any "end game content".
Yes, that's right... you might consider your end game a solo Survival mission when you get past the 120 minutes barrier, but... let's be honest here. Not many will be willing to do such a thing, considering it's easier and more time efficient to just do 40 minutes runs. If you're one of those players who enjoy finding their own challenges and beating the odds they had chosen themselves, then you should consider this content enough for you. If not, well... there's still a great game here to be played- even considering how repetitive it can become after a month or so.
All that considered, I can definitely recommend Warframe to anyone who might be looking for a fast paced, intense and rewarding (yet sometimes very frustrating... but most of the good thing in life are) third person shooter that is being steadily developed, with more items, warframes and quests being added in the foreseeable future. Just... try to take a break every hour or so. Even the game tells you that!

On console, I played Ark for upwards of 1000 hours, and even though it was slightly buggy, grew to love it.
The same is true on PC - It may not be my most played game, but it is among my favorites. I find the gameplay to be 'complete', and am not sure how else to describe it... When playing a game like rust, I feel like it's just a grind, with little else, but Ark isn't, it feels like there's objectives - but perhaps that's because I like it more.
The aspect of taming dinosaurs is both incredibly fun and incredibly rewarding. Be warned however: while this is the main pull of the game, and what distinguishes it from similar games, like the aformentioned Rust, it is not a game for those who want to hop on for an hour, then do something else. Ark is soul consuming, and unless you find a server with ridiculous rates (which isn't hard at all), and don't mind the lack of a challenge these severely increase rates bring, then I wouldn't recommend it.
But if you don't mind putting in the hours, and dealing with the grind that comes with survival games - which I find easier in Ark, perhaps it's the wildlife - then I would totally recommend this game. The only downside is losing a dinosaur which you become attacthed to: too many times ahve I lost a tame that served me well. Oh, and I suppose you have some toxic players, but I've never met any that I couldn't deal with. Supposedly there's a giant Brazilian (perhaps Chinese) megatribe, which goes server to server wiping everyone, but I have't met anyone like that.
So in short: I totally recommend this game. And for those who complain about the Tek Tier ruinign it because everyone becomes Iron Man: have you seen the materials you need to craft one of those things!? And you have the beat the boss multiple times, which I imagine most players won't do. If the futuristic, or even modern aspect, of the game is too much, there are always servers with it disabled.

Many F2P games are criticized for avoiding the 'Free To Play' model, in favor of the more immediate, and destructive, "Forced To Pay" style of game.  Warframe is one of the few F2P games on the market that does right by the F2P model - You spend money if, and only if, you want to, and the game does a decent job of selling itself as a product.
At its' heart, Warframe is exactly what it says on the box - A third-person Co-op 'horde' shooter, pitting you and a small group against hundreds of foes per mission, almost Gauntlet-style.  While somewhat mechanically plain, the mission objective types fit well into the game's lore - you are Tenno, a force of balance in a system of chaos.  Cull the ever-growing clone armies of the Grineer, foil the devious machinations of the Corpus, and hold back the tide of a biological infestation that seeks only to devour all life.  With an ever-growing list of Warframes and weapons, you will have any number of ways to decimate your enemy.
All of the gameplay content is entirely free of real-world monetary cost.  There is no 'pay-to-win' content in this game, and only a fraction of it (1 frame, 2 weapons) is exclusive to those who supported the game in its' early stage.  In addition, monthly events provide free weapons and weapon mods that are usually hard to get by other means.  The real-world game currency - Platinum - is also TRADEABLE, which means you can trade some of the more sought-for 'Prime' equipment for the Platinum you need for aesthetic customization.
As anyone who has played an F2P game for long enough knows, these games are never truly free.  As the saying goes, "Time Is Money" - and in Warframe, you pay with your time.  Collecting the materials you need to build equipment can be arduous, and then you'll have to wait for their construction (for frames, this can take over a week in total time spent).  Nevertheless, it is a cost you pay in other games anyway.
While Warframe is not the most incredible game out there, it certainly stands out.  This is a game you can't lose by trying, so I suggest you do.  Also:  You're a space ninja.  Who doesn't want to be a space ninja?

First of all, although it says I've played 20 hours, I had another steam account before this, and my profile in-game says I've played for 80 hours.
The only reason I actually downloaded the game in the first place was because of all the hype around Destiny and I heard a comment somewhere that said how there was this f2p game on steam called Warframe that was similar to it. Since I wasn't able to buy Destiny, I decided to download this... And I sure as hell don't regret it.
The whole concept of the game was pretty new to me when I started and that is that you're some machine/human thing that goes around and does missions to stop the evil people from doing what they are doing. When they added the infected (another type of enemy), it added even more depth to the game as each faction has their own strength and weakness.
After playing the game for a while, there was a feeling of boredom and I felt like everything was super grindy to get, which to a certain extent is true because this game is f2p and the micro transactions help keep the game running (I assume), but to no certainty is this the type of game where you need to pay money to get items, it just speeds along the process.
Since i got bored of the grind that I had been doing being a solo player and all, I gave the game a few months to rest and sit while I played other games. Recently when I got back into it after finding out a friend of mine plays it a lot, I decided to keep playing with him and everything still felt slightly grindy, but it was more about having fun and playing with other players and friends.
To be completely honest, I wouldn't say this game is for everybody due to the kinda boring/grindy solo play, but in a group, this game doesn't get old.
I definitely recommend checking it out, (what do you have to lose, its freeee), and I would give it a solid 8/10

You can trade for it with mods, prime parts, etc.  Then use it to buy weapon slots and frame slots to diversify your collection.  This is, by far, the best use for platinum in the game when you're new.  Also, keep an eye out for certain alerts (special missions), as some of them will have items you need for higher level play.
It's free to play, not pay to win, and a lot of fun.  Try it out, if you haven't already.

Here you have a solid game with a similarly solid core of features: it has an extremely good (yet surprisingly scaleable, and I've been able to play with good framerates even on older hardware) graphic compartment, excellent animations, a very interesting setting and great art design. The sound compartment is quite good as well, the music is not particularly evocative (although it does have its moments), with the sounds being quite diverse and interesting from firearm to firearm, from power to power and from tileset to tileset.
The gameplay itself is where the game truly shines: it can be described as a third person action title with a strong shooter and melee component, a good if not great parkour system and a vast wealth of different Warframes (your RPG class, if you'd like), each one of them carrying different powers in battle. And let's not forget the large amount of different weaponry you'll be able to wield, from rocket and grenade launchers to Dead Space-esque cutting lasers and incredibly diverse melee weapons. There is no shortage of content here, especially if you tend to be a completionist.
Now, don't misunderstand me. It's not all roses and flowers. this IS with no doubt a "typical" free to play game. If you have too much time on your hands, like I do (insert sad face here) then you might want to stop a while and play with this one. You will have many items to grind for, many events in which to partake, interesting and sometimes even challenging missions to try. The fairly recent Sortie addition was quite pleasant as well, especially when you realize that Warframe doesn't really have any "end game content".
Yes, that's right... you might consider your end game a solo Survival mission when you get past the 120 minutes barrier, but... let's be honest here. Not many will be willing to do such a thing, considering it's easier and more time efficient to just do 40 minutes runs. If you're one of those players who enjoy finding their own challenges and beating the odds they had chosen themselves, then you should consider this content enough for you. If not, well... there's still a great game here to be played- even considering how repetitive it can become after a month or so.
All that considered, I can definitely recommend Warframe to anyone who might be looking for a fast paced, intense and rewarding (yet sometimes very frustrating... but most of the good thing in life are) third person shooter that is being steadily developed, with more items, warframes and quests being added in the foreseeable future. Just... try to take a break every hour or so. Even the game tells you that!

They do work hard on the game and it's constantly updated, though. I don't recommend this game to others, but to me, the uniqueness and fun outweigh the problems. Maybe in the future, the team will improve, and I'll update this review.

After logging more than 80 hours on Ark I feel like I can write a fair review for the game. Mind you my review is all based upon my experience playing on a PvP server. If you play on a PvE server you may have a wildly different experience.
To start, you're dropped in the middle of nowhere, with a loincloth and nothing else. No instruction. No direction. Just you and your nearly-naked self. Luckily I hopped into a server where two of my buddies had started a day or two before me so they had some helpful starting tips.
You'll probably start in an environment that is either too hot or too cold, and soon you'll be starving and dehydrated, and if you don't do something about it, you'll be dead before long. A shelter is important, but won't guarantee your survival. Me and my two pals, built our base, collected resources and avoided contact with everyone else on the server.
Heres why we avoided contact:
If you're new, you will be destroyed, wether you deserved it or not. You are weak, and there WILL be people on your server that will want to destroy you, simply because you are new, weak, and killable. Unless you are willing to join an exisintg tribe and play by some other person's rules, you will be wiped. Wholly, continuously, and without provocation.  After somewhere around 150 man hours our (we thought nearly indestuctable) base was destroyed. No explanation. We moved and built another base on the opposite side of the map, as far away from everyone as we could go and that base too was destroyed within hours.
I asked myself a few times during my 80 hours why I continued playing. The servers are terribly laggy, there is no goal other than to survive, and battling glitches is nearly as common as battling the environment.
Ark is pretty, but compared to so many other survival games out there, that may be all it has going for it. I'll admit, it was mildly enjoyable up until we got destroyed. Although, I spent the majority of my 80 hours mining thousands of pounds of metal to make a metal house.
Taming animals is a chore, and it often takes HOURS to successfully tame an animal, during which time you have to completely focus on feeding it and protecting it from any predators in the vicinity. So be ready to dedicate an entire playing session to taming an animal if thats what you want to do. And even after you have tamed an animal, it could easily be killed by something while you are off the server not playing, so just be grateful if it's not dead every time you sign on.
I paid thirty dollars for the game, got 80+ hours out of it so it wasnt a complete wash, but unless you are ready to dedicate yourself COMPLETELY to this game and are okay with being frequently frustrated, I suggest looking elsewhere.

So. Wanted to take the moment to put out a short review about my experience with the game.
You'll note that there's a lot of negative feedback about it releasing DLC while it's still in alpha, that the multiplayer servers are rife with PVP juggernauts that squash new players trying to solo (similar to just about any other server based pvp / survival game ala Rust/7 Days to Die/etc..) and specific complaints about balance and pandering to veterans.
These are all genuine complaints, but in absolute truth... This game is amazing.
Would I recommend this game? Absolutely- Hell play it solo for a while. Playing with a tribe definitely increases what you're capable of but the sheer scope and vistas of even the regular game without Scorched Earth (I personally got both on a Steam sale, but rarely use SE content) is epic.
The Island map genuinely feels like something out of Jurrassic Park. I find myself comparing the taming part of the game to something like... Pokemon Primal... you suddenly discover that you want to catch them all! This game is VERY time intensive on live multiplayer servers. Taming and breeding can eat up literal hours of your life at a time, but I personally don't mind this. It gives me "projects" to work on during a weekend.
This game is not perfect, but really for what they're asking me to pay for I've already logged about 300 hours so far and I don't mind that. One sage piece of advice, be sure to check 3rd Party internet resources to assist with taming and breeding. There's a handful of very useful sites and apps that can get you rolling quite quickly if you don't mind doing a little research.
Visual: 8/10 We're not talking jaw dropping CPU melting graphics here. There's clipping issues, some of the textures are less than optimized and there's not a lot of difference in flora.  That said, it's a genuinely pretty game at some points. The Lighting Effects work very well, and the dino's themselves are rendered well. The genetic based coloring of each dino lends some real interesting artistry to breeding for specific color traits.
Audio: 8/10 The sounds of the game work very well, my one complaint so far being the inability to sound proof buildings aside from using distance. Once you find yourself in a barn environment you can sometimes find yourself overwhelmed by repetative creature sounds, but fortunately the game staggers them a bit. The music is... well its acceptable but I often turn it off completely and either go with the natural sound effects of the world or maybe play the Jurrassic Park theme, because... why not?
Setting: 9/10 The Maps the provide are vast, intriguing, and well designed. Hidden inlets, protected valleys, steep mountain tops and grassy plains greet your every moment. Going under water opens up an alien and harsh world to you. The dossier system seems at the cusp of offering a legitimate story to the game... which fromt he moment you see one of the obelisks in the distance, makes you immediately wonder more about. That's really the only issue I have with the setting really, that there's little to no actual story. But then again what the game does offer in the form of its Dossiers and survivor notes is far more than I've experienced in other survival games.
Gameplay: 7.5/10 The game itself is good. Combat is fluid and dangerous, and pack mechanics of your tamed dinos works great. That said, the game does suffer from bugs. Many of them, the dev team does appear to occasionally go back to revisit bugs, however they are notoriously  bad for working on "the next new thing" rather than fixing what's already broke. For what it's worth though, I don't find it unplayable at all. It's difficult at times, but I don't think it detracts from the game. Building structures is a little more nuanced than I think it needs to be, Articulating snap points for your home can often be more art than science.

The best F2P game I've ever come across. A fair bit buggy, but that's to be expected. The amount of content/updates that are constantly added to the game are insane. To give an example: If you were to compare what Warframe is now to what it was back in 2013, you'd be playing a completely different standalone game in a technical sense. There's so much to cover that I cannot fit it all into one review, but let's start with the fundamentals. The only other shooter I've played with mechanical depth that can hold a candle to what Warframe allows would be Resident Evil 6. This game's combat system is that deep. I'm not talking about things like Mods or attribute values, I'm talking about the sheer number of movement and attack options you have.
In default mode, the shooting mechanics are pretty straight-forward. But the moment you hit the key to switch to a dedicated melee mode, the game reveals its mechanical complexity. With melee now your primary means of attack, you're able to empower attacks, block/parry, do combos through the use of Stance mods. The game now resembles something closer to a simplified version of Devil May Cry than an traditional shooter. Delaying your melee attacks at key points in animations will allow you to do a comboed move rather than a generic slash. And with most Stance mods having at least 5 combo chains, (in addition to some weapons having multiple dedicated Stance mods) the skill ceiling is significantly increased.
Beyond that are your movement options. You can do a sliding slash both on the ground and mid-air. You can run on and scale/hang from walls, dodge in any direction, and can even divekick enemies to knock them down or springboard off of friends and foes alike to complement your standard double jump.
The basic aspects of combat are further supported via the use of Mods. Mods are items that fit into weapons and Warframes alike to help improve and tailor the player's chosen combat style. Every item has 10 Mod slots and 1 Stance or Aura slot. Each Mod has a number value that deducts from a point pool on a chosen item. Mods can also be fused with other mods to improve their effects. Weapons are also able to be fitted with different combinations of elemental mods to produce a new effect. It it through this system that allows Warframe to appeal to virtually any type of player's preferred approach to combat.
Customization is a large part of Warframe, whether aesthetic or stat-wise. You're even able to choose your own ship (though such a choice is purely for show), customize the interior of it along with your frames, weapons etc. Better yet, most Warframes and even certain cosmetic items can be aquired simply through grinding.
This, however, brings us to some of the cons that Warframe can rely on a bit too much at times. The game is very grind-heavy and can eventually wear an individual down as you run the same missions over and over to acquire a certain blue-print, To its benefit, there are a variety of mission types and enviornmental tile sets to go along with them. Furthermore, the game is exceptionally optimized; and is able to keep literally dozens of enemies on screen with respective particle and weapons effects without dropping below 45-50 on a mid-range computer (I had an GTX 660 as reference).
Another problem the game has is its inclination towards being buggy. One of the worst I've heard of so far is the inital Archwing mission causing the game to outright lock up when the game is in Directx 11 mode. There are also numerous other bugs that will crop up as a player puts more and more time into the game.
Certain cosmetic items (and even Warframes) are sometimes only purchasable with Platinum, which requires that players spend real money or trade/sell in-game items to other players for Platinum (if one does not wish to spend real money).
Story-wise, the game explains very little to the player up front and uses Codexs to allow the player to piece the lore together ala. Dark Souls. With multiple factions each having their own agendas in addition to the Tenno themselves, there is a lot of world building content for players to go through.
Overall though, it's an amazing and unique F2P game that will likely not be outdone by its competitors anytime soon. If ever.

First of all, this review is from a singleplayer standpoint and directed towards newcomers to this game. I tried playing in a server once last year, and absolutely hated the experience. The PVP element seems to be mainly why this game has gotten so many negative reviews. But instead of getting stomped all over in the servers by the trolls & alpha tribes, if any of you are interested in playing by yourself or on LAN, read on!
All I heard about this game when it first came out was that it was really poorly optimised and in early access. So I avoided it like the plague. Until last year, when I started watching Let's Plays on Youtube, and I fell in love. It still is the game I play the most out of all my games. Last week I tamed a T-rex for the first time. It felt awesome. Yes there is so much grind, and yes I do have all the XP/taming rates turned up, and it still is a grind. But damn, it's a fun grind. And I learned so much about dinosaurs in the process! It makes the inner dino-obsessed little girl in me so happy :)
You start out naked and alone, and with tools you craft yourself you slowly build up a base. Location is everything. In the north, the cold and large carnivores will defeat you very quickly. But in the south, the weather is milder and the dinos are not so big and scary. Taming dinos is fun and frightening, and often frustrating but it makes the grind a lot easier as different dinos help you to gather different materials with ease and of course help protect you. I used to wonder what the point of this game is; you grind to get better gear, and then you grind some more. But if you enjoy the grind and being scared out of your wits most of the time, then you will love this game and get a very rewarding experience out of it.
But it still is very brutal. Sometimes you spend so long taming something, or building a base, only to die and lose it all in an instant. Be prepared to be very very frustrated, it definitely is one of the most challenging games I have ever played. The original Island map is fun and massive to explore, but the free Center expansion map is even bigger and much more beautiful and varied.
There are caves you can explore underwater and the devs are adding more and more aggressive water dinos that make it very challenging and rewarding to explore the seas. If you make it to end game, there are several artifacts you can loot in dangerous caves you have to fight your way out of, and there are bosses you can summon & take on for very big rewards. You can take your time, and gather & build, or you can take out the big guns, level up, tame high tier dinos, expand and technologically improve your base. There is an insane amount you can do, and you can play it your way without being restricted by a linear storyline.
Now on to some cons, it is super glitchy sometimes. The worst one is when you get stuck on knocked out dinos, or rocks, or in doors, or.. really anything. It is frustrating and sometimes all you can really do to fix it is to wait it out, break the rock you are stuck in (if you're lucky), or log out & log back in again (which takes forever for me). This doesn't happen often but when it does, it is very irritating. It is also a common sight to see wild dinos stuck in trees, which makes taming them easy & cheat-y. Though some of the weird graphic glitches can actually be quite funny :) Another thing I dislike about this game is the building mechanics. It is not intuitive at all, and sometimes you can't build or place certain items "because Ark". This means that you frequently have to tear down what you have built, which ends up costing you half the materials you used to make it.
And the other thing I really dislike about this is the fact that the game is STILL in early access. I was very disappointed when the devs made the Scorched Earth map a paid DLC. Not that it isn't fun to play, it really is - but I felt like they really should have finished the main game first before making DLCs. There is a new minor update almost every time I play this game, which is a bit annoying as you have to download it every time - but all that they seem to be doing recently are adding more and more interesting & slightly OP dinos, which is great, but makes some of the older dino models now obsolete. I really wish they would focus more on ironing out all the little problems with the base game rather than adding more and more new dinos. I would love to also see some new and varied character designs & more in depth customisation on the way your character looks & sounds (the devs are now sponsoring mod makers to develop their mods, which I think is great news for Ark).
Even after all these flaws, I still keep coming back for more. If you love survival games, exploring, crafting, building, gardening, breeding (!), fighting, and let's not forget - if you have any sort of interest in dinosaurs, you will love this game. Make sure you have a good PC to run this and start taming! Prepare to throw away a whole lot of hours on this as it is damn addictive :)

I love this game. I've spent way too much time on it. I'm not much for the PvP aspect of the game, but even so, I still find lots of other activities to enjoy. [Such as: Breeding, building, gardening, taming, exploring, egg stealing, and generally being able to have fun with my friends.] I've been playing the game since the early beginning and I've watched the progress and enjoyed all the new creatures and tweaks that have been implemented. I'm looking forward to the randomized maps and underwater bases. I can't wait for aquatic based breeding as well, I heard that's up and coming.
I even have the expansion Scorched Earth. It's like ark, but more difficult and everything is trying ot kill you twice as fast. It's fantastically terrifying, and hey, did I mention dragons?
There are also a lot of wonderful mods to pair with your gaming experience out there. Don't be shy about adding a few on to enhance the experience.
There are a few drawbacks here and there, but again. I can't comment much on PvP. Public PvE is okay, but sometimes you run into unpleasant players that think it's fun to harass others, but there's nothing you can really do about it because it's a "npk" server. Survival in a world with much larger, faster carnivores should be hard.
Staying sane in world with infinite lives, where you die to anything smaller than you because they are impossible to aim at, is harder but other games do the "die, rinse and repeat" model justice.
Resource gathering in a world whose physics actively aids the environment is ARK: Survival Evolved.
Physics should be a given, it should be the dinosaurs' behavior, the taming, the crafting that you have to figure out.
Finding a safe place to sleep (aka log out) should be the hard part, not standing in the exact correct place on the solid-looking floor to avoid falling through it when you log back in. And logging back in to find yourself embedded in a wall.
The AI can always path to you if its aggro, your loyal ones won't be able to return to you 45% of the time, even in line-of-sight.
You can build fantastic structures:
- tree houses to sleep in, then log in, fall to your death,
- houses on the backs of giant herbavores to sleep in, then log in, fall to your death
- boats to sleep in, safe from nearly anything except... logging in, where you find yourself in the water, pulled apart by sharks.... having fallen through 2-3 solid floors to your death
The same game premise, controls, taming method, combat, art, but on a real, robust physics engine - would be bigger than Minecraft, which pales compared to this. But I always know why I've died in Minecraft.
Several years of public beta, paid expansions, new features, still no solid floors.

This game's not bad, and I DON'T hate it. That said let's move to cons and pros
CONS:
It's free so they make up for this by demanding either the player grinds like a MF to unlock new gear (armor, weps, etc), or of course pay up real money for such assets. What killed this game for me was this point, because I personally got bored with grinding with the same gear in a game which has such a plethora of interesting gear (so alluring from the marketplace!). Now if you don't/can't pay then grinding with a team or clan can definitely speed up the process and is almost required if you want to get gear in a timely manner - relatively speaking, it's still not super fast or anything. However if you're like me and just want to play this game casually with a friend or two then this means essentially never getting any new gear.
PROS:
I liked this game for the time I played it, I really did. the mechanics of it are smooth and fluid, you feel like a total badass space-ninja, I mean that in itself is a great start. The combat is fun, which for how much grinding the game demands of you it NEEDS TO BE. And the gear in the game like I said is very unique and there's a lot of it. And of course it's multiplayer which is almost always a plus.
CONCLUSION:
In the end I can't recommend it because I feel like I can't fully (hell not even close to fully) enjoy the game and have to miss out on experiencing much of what the game has to offer because my play style isn't compatible with this game. That lays out the biggest pros and cons I experienced, your experience will probably be a little different, but if you can't see your play style (or wallet) fitting into the mold this game has, then it might not be for you.

Let's get the free to play aspect out of the way first. I've spent only $15 on this game so far, and I didn't have to. I just wanted to buy cosmetics and support the developers. With a couple of exceptions of content reserved to Founders (people who funded the game's initial development), there is no gear that is locked behind a paywall (and their exclusive gear isn't even good). Only some cosmetics are locked behind a pay wall, and most other cosmetics can still be bought with platinum. Platinum being the game's premium currency, which can be traded between players for rare gear that drops in missions you can play for free. This game has the best free to play model of any I've played. One of my favorite aspects being, there are no premium or non-premium accounts. Every player is equal.
What about gameplay? Well the amount of playstyles and weapons offered to the player will keep you trying new things for a very long time. As of writing this there are 29 unique classes (refered to as Warframes, roll credits) in the game, with a 30th to be added in the coming months. There are hundreds of weapons to choose from, and almost half of them are actually good. Movement is fluid and satisfying, with momentum giving weight to the player's actions.
Story in Warframe didn't really used to matter. But over time, lore was built into a world that is really shaping up. Through quests outright telling you things, to passing comments from NPCs, and codex entires gained by scanning an enemy enough times, a universe is crafted that will keep you interested and wanting to know more. There's more to this story and the answers are waiting.
Endgame is not very well defined at the moment, but hopefully that will change sometime this year. Fashionframe is the true endgame anyway.

Great graphic, nearly no story (even less than MMORPGs).
Still fun to play but keep in mind that at some point it's basically only farming for parts and stuff (after you've completed all "story" missions which are also repetitions of 7 different mission types).
Also note that Warframe is NOT free to play in the true definition of the term.
It's a function-based, time unlimited trial.
Without spending platinum - which you can only buy for real world money or get in trades from players who bought it - you cannot own more than 2 warframes and 4 weapons.
(Out of 50+ or so warframes and 150+ or so weapons in existence, numbers always growing).
How to play warframe free - fastest and easiest way for new players without rare-mods and items to sell:
Join a syndicate as soon as possible (check warframe wiki for more info) and farm syndicate standing as much as possible by always completing all daily syndicate missions.
Then sell the syndicate mods (for 10 platinum per mod) and weapons which go for about 20-35 platinum in the trade chat.
Use the platinum to buy the warframe, weapon and equipment slots (12p for 2 weapon slots, 20p for 1 warframe slot).
Note that there are prerequisites for joining a syndicate, it will still only take you a few days playing warframe to do so.
Note that to increase your MR (mastery rank) - which is basically the player level which mostly determines which weapons you can use - you have to rank an equipment or warframe from 0 to 30.
The affinity (XP) you get from ranking an item from 0 to 30 is only awarded once (even if you forma it or buy a second one). Therefore you have to keep getting different weapons and warframes to increase in MR.
