First of all, although it says I've played 20 hours, I had another steam account before this, and my profile in-game says I've played for 80 hours.
The only reason I actually downloaded the game in the first place was because of all the hype around Destiny and I heard a comment somewhere that said how there was this f2p game on steam called Warframe that was similar to it. Since I wasn't able to buy Destiny, I decided to download this... And I sure as hell don't regret it.
The whole concept of the game was pretty new to me when I started and that is that you're some machine/human thing that goes around and does missions to stop the evil people from doing what they are doing. When they added the infected (another type of enemy), it added even more depth to the game as each faction has their own strength and weakness.
After playing the game for a while, there was a feeling of boredom and I felt like everything was super grindy to get, which to a certain extent is true because this game is f2p and the micro transactions help keep the game running (I assume), but to no certainty is this the type of game where you need to pay money to get items, it just speeds along the process.
Since i got bored of the grind that I had been doing being a solo player and all, I gave the game a few months to rest and sit while I played other games. The best F2P game I've ever come across. A fair bit buggy, but that's to be expected. The amount of content/updates that are constantly added to the game are insane. To give an example: If you were to compare what Warframe is now to what it was back in 2013, you'd be playing a completely different standalone game in a technical sense. There's so much to cover that I cannot fit it all into one review, but let's start with the fundamentals. The only other shooter I've played with mechanical depth that can hold a candle to what Warframe allows would be Resident Evil 6. This game's combat system is that deep. I'm not talking about things like Mods or attribute values, I'm talking about the sheer number of movement and attack options you have.
In default mode, the shooting mechanics are pretty straight-forward. But the moment you hit the key to switch to a dedicated melee mode, the game reveals its mechanical complexity. With melee now your primary means of attack, you're able to empower attacks, block/parry, do combos through the use of Stance mods. The game now resembles something closer to a simplified version of Devil May Cry than an traditional shooter. Delaying your melee attacks at key points in animations will allow you to do a comboed move rather than a generic slash. And with most Stance mods having at least 5 combo chains, (in addition to some weapons having multiple dedicated Stance mods) the skill ceiling is significantly increased.
Beyond that are your movement options. You can do a sliding slash both on the ground and mid-air. You can run on and scale/hang from walls, dodge in any direction, and can even divekick enemies to knock them down or springboard off of friends and foes alike to complement your standard double jump.
The basic aspects of combat are further supported via the use of Mods. Mods are items that fit into weapons and Warframes alike to help improve and tailor the player's chosen combat style. Every item has 10 Mod slots and 1 Stance or Aura slot. Each Mod has a number value that deducts from a point pool on a chosen item. Mods can also be fused with other mods to improve their effects. Weapons are also able to be fitted with different combinations of elemental mods to produce a new effect. It it through this system that allows Warframe to appeal to virtually any type of player's preferred approach to combat.
Customization is a large part of Warframe, whether aesthetic or stat-wise. You're even able to choose your own ship (though such a choice is purely for show), customize the interior of it along with your frames, weapons etc. Better yet, most Warframes and even certain cosmetic items can be aquired simply through grinding.
This, however, brings us to some of the cons that Warframe can rely on a bit too much at times. The game is very grind-heavy and can eventually wear an individual down as you run the same missions over and over to acquire a certain blue-print, To its benefit, there are a variety of mission types and enviornmental tile sets to go along with them. Furthermore, the game is exceptionally optimized; and is able to keep literally dozens of enemies on screen with respective particle and weapons effects without dropping below 45-50 on a mid-range computer (I had an GTX 660 as reference).
Another problem the game has is its inclination towards being buggy. One of the worst I've heard of so far is the inital Archwing mission causing the game to outright lock up when the game is in Directx 11 mode. There are also numerous other bugs that will crop up as a player puts more and more time into the game.
Certain cosmetic items (and even Warframes) are sometimes only purchasable with Platinum, which requires that players spend real money or trade/sell in-game items to other players for Platinum (if one does not wish to spend real money).
Story-wise, the game explains very little to the player up front and uses Codexs to allow the player to piece the lore together ala. Dark Souls. With multiple factions each having their own agendas in addition to the Tenno themselves, there is a lot of world building content for players to go through.
Overall though, it's an amazing and unique F2P game that will likely not be outdone by its competitors anytime soon. If ever.
8.2 out of 10.

I love this game. There's a good reason for that: I don't play it online.
One of the biggest, reddest flags for me before buying this game was the awful, AWFUL online community this game is so infamous for. And it should be for you, too. If you play online, you will be miserable, because the community is completely unbalanced and unfair. It rewards trollish, childish behavior, and punishes anyone for being new. I don't know if this was intentional on the devs part, but either way, they've established a narcissist breeding ground.
But that's not to say the game itself is terrible. On the contrary... it's great. As long as you don't rely on any other humans within it (unless they're a couch co-op companion).
1. The survival aspect of the game is pretty decent. Hunger, warmth, health and other conditions are pretty well-balanced, even in a single-player experience. Even thinking about the torch I'll be carrying with me at night when it gets insanely dark is fun to me.
2. Taming and riding dinosaurs alone makes the game worth it to me. I'm a total dino nut, and thinking about owning my own rideable velociraptor was one of the things that made me want this game so badly. I already tamed one dinosaur and built a base for myself, and I'd say I'm still pretty noobish.
3. Exploration is incredible. The map is so vast and so immense. I feel like I could spend weeks on it and still never fully see everything.
4. Crafting and leveling up is a bit addictive. I've spent a great deal of time searching through my ranks and skills to see what I should buy next, and to see what I should risk getting, since I play alone and don't have others buying other skills opposite of me. It poses a bit more of a challenge.
5. I love the environmental threats that I'm always cautious of. If one raptor sniffs me out, I'm done for. I have to make sure my base is secure and my bedroll is placed so I can respawn. I love taking that cautionary approach.
6. The immersion level in a single-player environment is much higher. You feel like you're struggling to live, and being on your own makes you feel more vulnerable.
7. I still laugh every time my character just randomly craps on the ground while jogging through the terrain.
1. As noted before... the online community. It's the gaming equivalent of cancer. If you really want to play with your friend, this game can be played co-op, and I recommend you do so far away from anyone else. If you have a group of friends you want to play with, host your own server, or play with them on a server they host. Unless you have a masochistic streak and like being harassed, don't play on one of the common servers. Because you will be-- constantly. Sometimes you'll be murdered the instant you spawn on a server. There's literally no point whatsoever to playing on a large server. It's a waste of time, and nothing but an aggravation. The only ones still having any fun on those servers are those that have been there since launch and spend all their time griefing people like you. It's ironic that the game is unplayable online, since that was the main selling point for it on release. It was all about tribe-building. It's not really. It's just about PvP bullying. A PvE server isn't even an option because they're over-crowded.
2. Performance. Unless you have an amazing PC, it seems the game runs at half the power. The graphics are noticeably cheapened by a less powerful machine. I can run more advanced games on medium range graphics, but this game takes a serious hit. Even with lower settings, I still get insane amounts of lag. This might be due to hosting my own sole server locally, but I can't be certain.
3. It can start to feel repetitive, online or offline.
online.
4. I said before that there wasn't a map. Come to find out, there really
an in-game map. But it doesn't act anything like a map in other games. It acts like maps in real life, complete with longitude and latitude. This is cool, I suppose, and feels realistic, but it also takes extra time to mark and check your map constantly. You'll eventually get to know your surroundings, but you have to play a while to get that feeling.
5. In single-player, I feel a lot weaker. Not sure if this is intentional, but I feel like I could die at any moment. Good for survival and immersion, but not good for frustration levles.
6. There doesn't seem to be any area that has level-progressed enemies. You can start out in an area surrounded by enemies many levels higher than you. This can make progress feel incredibly slow when playing alone, because you're gated behind difficulty. There doesn't seem to be any "difficulty" setting that I'm aware of, so you could be running for your life away from raptors before you even get what's happening.
The game is indeed worth it, but play online at your own risk. If you do want to play with friends, play on your own server or co-op. If you like survival and dinosaurs, it's a good buy.

This game is a lot like JJ Abram's Lost. At first it really pulls you in, and it seems like there is some epic story unfolding. For the first two seasons, you are thinking Abrams is the master, and you can't wait to see how it will turn out. Then you start to realize none of the loose ends are ever tied up, nothing ever concluded. Nothing ever actually turns out at all. Things just keep turning up though. You realize they keep opening up new plot points and nothing is ever coming to a beautiful close. Then you realize JJ Abrams has been pulling stuff out of his♥♥♥♥♥and you were being fooled the whole time, tricked into thinking there would be some rewarding conclusion, some masterful plan the whole time. But, no, that would take an actual master.
In Ark, the gameplay is terribly balanced for tedious boredom, getting worse every day as they add more crap. Basic dinosaur management is still completely broken, to where you still cannot run across the land with a dino following you without losing it. Inventory user interface and crafting system are one of the most frustrating ever conceived, with ludicrous limitations, half implemented controls, and once again balanced around tedious boredom. Everything in this game will ultimately lead to disappointment, and it is usually because of some BS that is unfinished, unbalanced, broken, and not your own fault.
The worst part is that it is very obvious that they have no intent on fixing the bugs and interface issues anymore, or crafting the overall experience. They did it for the first month the game was out, and then after that they handed the project off to their goombas to add new dinos and engrams. There are fundamental flaws with the interface that have gone unchanged for years. Just basic stuff like putting items into a box, which is done better in almost every single survival game out there, is unfinished. It's not like it is broken and cannot be fixed, it was just left as it was on early access launch. Good 'nuff.
This game gave the same illusion as Lost did. That this was going to be a mastered experience, THE dino game. Then instead of taking what was there and wrapping it up nicely into a perfect package, they just kept adding and adding, because that is all they knew how to do. This is because their plan all along was to keep adding crap, just like JJ Abrams. It wasn't that they had some master plan, and then it fell apart. It was that the plan all along was to constantly create crap and feed it to the dumb audience under the guise of a master plan as long as they could get away with it.
To this day, I have not seen past the 2nd season of Lost, and I cannot recommend it to anyone without warning them of the shameless shafting they will be receiving.

The best F2P game I've ever come across. A fair bit buggy, but that's to be expected. The amount of content/updates that are constantly added to the game are insane. To give an example: If you were to compare what Warframe is now to what it was back in 2013, you'd be playing a completely different standalone game in a technical sense. There's so much to cover that I cannot fit it all into one review, but let's start with the fundamentals. The only other shooter I've played with mechanical depth that can hold a candle to what Warframe allows would be Resident Evil 6. This game's combat system is that deep. I'm not talking about things like Mods or attribute values, I'm talking about the sheer number of movement and attack options you have.
In default mode, the shooting mechanics are pretty straight-forward. But the moment you hit the key to switch to a dedicated melee mode, the game reveals its mechanical complexity. With melee now your primary means of attack, you're able to empower attacks, block/parry, do combos through the use of Stance mods. The game now resembles something closer to a simplified version of Devil May Cry than an traditional shooter. Delaying your melee attacks at key points in animations will allow you to do a comboed move rather than a generic slash. And with most Stance mods having at least 5 combo chains, (in addition to some weapons having multiple dedicated Stance mods) the skill ceiling is significantly increased.
Beyond that are your movement options. You can do a sliding slash both on the ground and mid-air. You can run on and scale/hang from walls, dodge in any direction, and can even divekick enemies to knock them down or springboard off of friends and foes alike to complement your standard double jump.
The basic aspects of combat are further supported via the use of Mods. Mods are items that fit into weapons and Warframes alike to help improve and tailor the player's chosen combat style. Every item has 10 Mod slots and 1 Stance or Aura slot. Each Mod has a number value that deducts from a point pool on a chosen item. Mods can also be fused with other mods to improve their effects. Weapons are also able to be fitted with different combinations of elemental mods to produce a new effect. It it through this system that allows Warframe to appeal to virtually any type of player's preferred approach to combat.
Customization is a large part of Warframe, whether aesthetic or stat-wise. You're even able to choose your own ship (though such a choice is purely for show), customize the interior of it along with your frames, weapons etc. Better yet, most Warframes and even certain cosmetic items can be aquired simply through grinding.
This, however, brings us to some of the cons that Warframe can rely on a bit too much at times. The game is very grind-heavy and can eventually wear an individual down as you run the same missions over and over to acquire a certain blue-print, To its benefit, there are a variety of mission types and enviornmental tile sets to go along with them. Furthermore, the game is exceptionally optimized; and is able to keep literally dozens of enemies on screen with respective particle and weapons effects without dropping below 45-50 on a mid-range computer (I had an GTX 660 as reference).
Another problem the game has is its inclination towards being buggy. One of the worst I've heard of so far is the inital Archwing mission causing the game to outright lock up when the game is in Directx 11 mode. There are also numerous other bugs that will crop up as a player puts more and more time into the game.
Certain cosmetic items (and even Warframes) are sometimes only purchasable with Platinum, which requires that players spend real money or trade/sell in-game items to other players for Platinum (if one does not wish to spend real money).
Story-wise, the game explains very little to the player up front and uses Codexs to allow the player to piece the lore together ala. Dark Souls. With multiple factions each having their own agendas in addition to the Tenno themselves, there is a lot of world building content for players to go through.
Overall though, it's an amazing and unique F2P game that will likely not be outdone by its competitors anytime soon. If ever.

The day the developers finally balance the game will be a great day.  As is they made it way to easy to aquire technology, way too easy to tame the dinos and have left it a crushing resource hog if played with decent graphics.
I recommend playing in Primitive+ and using the Survival Plus Alpha mod.  Seriously, where's the challenge once you have rocket launchers, or even machine guns?
At its base, this game is about constant resource farming.  Wood, fiber, stone, metal, oil, crystal, etc.  Food too.  First it's a struggle to stay alive, then a struggle to make survival easier, then you finally feel secure enough to do some real exploring.  Rinse and repeat each time you set up a new base.
Edit:  With the game about a month from release they have made some serious improvements, but there's also some setbacks.  For instance:  The game is reasonably optimized now, but also crashes every 2-3 hours.
I still consider dino taming too easy and access to OP tech too fast.  Still recommend the Primitive+ DLC, or the Survival+ mod (they don't seem to work together), over the base game - there just isn't much of a challenge in vanilla.  It's been a while since I played on a server, so not sure if the anti-cheat works.

If you do decide to get this game either play on your own server or play on a non-pvp server, and I would also recommend playing on a boosted server to reduce the grind.

Firstly lets talk about the basics, Warframe is a third-person over the shoulder Shooter, in it you control your character and complete missions and quests taking place on the different planets in the solar system, and if that sounds pretty generic thats because it probably is, however you are not some generic soldier, you take control of the Tenno, a race of basically humans designed as living weapons by a long dead ancient race, who are lead by The Lotus (space mum) to keep the peace in the solar system.
Lets talk about the gameplay, The controls are pretty standard (WASD to move, Space to jump etc.), but theres actually a bit more to it than running around and shooting, some missions require you to be stealthy instead of aggressive, and since the Tenno are basically space ninjas you'd expect them to be able to pull of some acrobatics, and youd be right, its almost impossible to go anywhere without pulling off a little parkour in some of the missions. Now we come to the characters themselves, the Warframes, these are robotic suits-ish that the Tenno control and complete missions with, now theres actually a large amount of these ranging from healing ones, to defensive ones, stealthy ones, and aggressive one, each one coming with its own unique set of abilities, stats and look. There are no real "Good" Warframes as they are all good in there own way and who am i to tell you how to play your game. So just go out, find one that you like, and have fun.
So the fact that Warframe is a free game might put you off, and yes even though warframe has a currency that is obtained by paying real money, but that does not mean this game is Pay To Win, this is because you are allowed to freely trade said currency with other players for their items, so if you dont want to use real money but you want an item that you can only get with the currency, then all you need to do is farm for a little bit, and sell of the items you got to players that want them, meaning that every single item can be obtained without having to pay any real money.
All in all I highly reccomend you at least give Warframe a try, I mean, what harm can it do.
tl:dr
Good game, basic controls, basically 100% free to play, space mums included, check it out

This game is just so much fun. As third-person shooters go, this has to be the best by far. I, and some of my friends, just love grinding up materials and crafting some more items, from ciphers to health packs to warframes and weapons. This game is especially fun with a full squad.
The whole idea of the foundry, and crafting weapons and gear needed for the next Void mission, is such a good one. You buy the blueprint off the market and then you can re-build the item over and
again, and then trade the duplicates for Fusion Cores (more on that later).
The modding was a creative idea, which can completely change the type of weapon that you're using. For example, on my pistol I have a mod which decreases the reload speed and now it's turned into an unlimited-clip machine gun. You can even fuse mods together, which increases their stats and is so awesome. Fusion Cores, which you use to fuse mods, are incredibly common, so you have no problem if you want to get a huge range melee. (yes, thats a thing.)
If you've ever played TF2, you'll know of Mann Up mode. Void missions are basically that
you don't even need to pay for the keys! All you need to do to play Void missions, is just to play other missions. Survival, defense and excavator missions all drop Void Keys, and more difficult the mission the more Void Keys you recieve and the higher the tier of key, from Tier I to Tier IV.
Obviously, there are some negative aspects of this game. The only one I've managed to find was that there are some parts which are pay to win, but all of the parts which are, you can do without buying Platinum. For instance, you need to wait until some of the things crafted in the foundry are completed but you can skip it with Platinum.
tl;dr
Warframe is an amazing game and you should get it.

With 2.5k hours, I think I can write a proper review now.
Warframe is a rather...unique game. To say I love it to death would be an understatement, but I will try to keep it objective.
What I like:
-The gameplay. You are a space ninja armed to the teeth with guns, blades, and space magic. Very free movement, highly customizable weapons and abilities with large focus on team composition.
-There are 160+ guns to pick from. The guns aren't just stats, all (excluding the varients of certain guns) of these feel different in how they fire. Some of them are quite unique (black hole gun, saw blade gun, exploding laser cubes, ect). Now not all of these are endgame viable, but if one puts time into it, I would say a good third of them are usable endgame.
-43 melee weapon "stances."  Stances are basically animation sets for specific melee weapon types.  Each of these stances is unique and has a different feel or even use.
-30 playable classes.  Yes, 30.
-God knows how many "mods."  Mods are what progress you through the game.  I currently own ~1500 unique mods.  You can make your gear work the way you want it to with these mods.
-The game just looks nice.  FashionFrame (player customization) is also a big deal.
-Premium currency is tradable and earnable. I have a very large amount of player customization items only available through premium currency and I only ever spent $5 on the game to buy someone at DE lunch. If you know what to grind for, earning premium currency is very reasonable.
-Grindy, but not too bad. I love games where I can work towards progress in a game.  Warframe provides that but not behind a huge time wall. One can reach total endgame within 100 hours of gameplay.  Unlocking a new class ranges from taking 20 mintues to (if RNG really hates you) about 30 hours.  Compared to some other RPG games out there, thats not too bad.
-The community can be very helpful and kind. If you ask for help, someone will likely help you, as long as you aren't being annoying about it.
-The developers really love and care for their game. With all of the hate DE recieves for their bad calls, they deserve just as much love for bringing us such a great game that is free. New content comes out every week to two weeks.
What I don't like:
-The developers are sometimes blind to what the community wants and sometimes (sorry DE) plain old stupid. I know its impossible to meet the demands of everyone in the community, but DE listens to the vocal minority on the forums far too often.  Also, some of the balancing in the PvP portion of the game is just wrong.
-RNG is your lord and destroyer in this game. I have farmed for 30 hours before for a single piece of something I wanted to just end up buying it from another player. Farming is part of the fun for me, but sometimes my poor luck makes it too much.
-The community also has its negative side. Most players are simply interested in grinding out their "Mastery Rank" (which doesn't do much for you past a pretty early point) and play the same mission 200+ times in a row to grind out the exp. Also, many players are just...BAD at the game and refuse to listen to advice or help.  This can lead to some rather sketchy situations for the others on the team.
-The game is repetative in nature. DE has done a lot to try and prevent this by having the huge variety in gear and many gamemodes. But there are only so many missions. Now, I think its safe to say most if not all games are repetative, so not a huge minus.
-You can write the game's story on a paper napkin. It doesn't exist. You have some lore that needs some digging to uncover, but no real story. (Update) Now needs 2 paper napkins!
Advice for new players:
There is a rather steep learning curve at first, but that can be part of the fun. Find people to play with, talk in game, ask for help. If you just go off solo, the game will get boring rather quickly, especially early game.
Final thoughts:
All in all, I love Warframe. There is a reason I sunk 2.5k hours into the game, its hands down my favorite game. If you like progression and shooting things while doing a mid-air backflip, THIS is your game. If you like grinding and huge variety, THIS is your game.
Its free for crying out loud, just try it!

Ark Survival Evolved has a lot to offer. Here are my pro's and con's with the game:
1:Beautiful Graphics, but it demands to much which results in a low frame rate
2:Mods-There are plenty of mods for the user to utilise, espically with thier new mods which changes the game completely such as the space survival mod.
3:The biggest problem I had is that certain areas which are high level allow you to enter them which ultimately results in you dying and losing all your equipment.
4:Great upgrades table, the game offers a wide variety and fortunately does not allow you to learn all skills unless a cheat/command is used to unlock all.
5:New content, every couple of days or weeks there's new creatures,tools,etc.
6:The game may update a lot, but there still seem to be a lot of glitches, so dont expect the game to be perfect.
7:NPC's & AI:The creatures are usually stable but sometimes they do the wierdest and most unexpected things.
8:Ark Scorched Earth Expansion, It does'nt make sense to me that you charge a full amount for Ark Survival evolved and another full price for an expansion, If you find the expansion worthy of the money then go for it, I understand it renovates the whole game with a new map,dinos,etc, but for all that it is'nt a whole game.
If you dont mind glitches and low frame rates for high graphics and loads of content then this is a good game and has alot of work , But doesnt dissapoint you if you want new content. Just make sure you consider more space for your machine for the massive updates.

(Long review)
This is my overall view of the game so far.
Since I started this game 2-3 weeks ago I have logged almost 100 hours when writing this review. The game itself has so many things to do it's unbelievable, but that is if you are willing to spend the time to play it. This game is not for “Casual” players who want a facebook based game where you log on for 5-10 minutes click a few buttons and hop off. After reading a lot of the negative reviews I have figured out some of the major “Issues” people claim the game has.
(To grindy)
(Not enough things to do)
(Game is to hard)
(Pay to win)
After playing the game for almost 100 hours I do have to partially agree when people say that there is too much grinding, I wouldn't say there is too much grinding other than the grinding and missions are to spread apart I.E it takes time to reach the next main story quest. This is not really a problem considering plenty of people complain about other games having to short of a story. Like I said before this game is not for the faint of heart in order to play this game you are going to need these three things,
(Time, and effort)
(Non lazy personality)
(Dedication)
If you have these traits in your personality then this game is for you. Now a bit more into the gameplay for the game. The gameplay in Warframe is very ninja like jumping, swinging, slashing, fast paced combat. The default controls for the game are very odd but you can rebind them to what makes you feel comfortable. There is missions that you can complete to progress your weapons and warframes, these missions are on planets that you unlock by killing bosses. Each planet has their own individual boss that you kill in order to unlock the next planet. One of the major mission areas that you will spend time in is called the void, this is where the majority of the grinding in the game is. In the game you can buy with real money ingame money called Platinum, this is used for trading with other players to get prime blueprints which are farmed in the void. Something that should be noted you need void keys in order to unlock missions these are farmed in normal missions on planets. If you are taking the free to play approach to the game then you will be doing a lot of farming to sell these prime blueprints for platinum. This is the end of my long review so far of the game, give it a try if you don’t like it then you don’t but do not make up false negative reports just because you’re lazy and you give up too easily.

With 2.5k hours, I think I can write a proper review now.
Warframe is a rather...unique game. To say I love it to death would be an understatement, but I will try to keep it objective.
What I like:
-The gameplay. You are a space ninja armed to the teeth with guns, blades, and space magic. Very free movement, highly customizable weapons and abilities with large focus on team composition.
-There are 160+ guns to pick from. The guns aren't just stats, all (excluding the varients of certain guns) of these feel different in how they fire. Some of them are quite unique (black hole gun, saw blade gun, exploding laser cubes, ect). Now not all of these are endgame viable, but if one puts time into it, I would say a good third of them are usable endgame.
-43 melee weapon "stances."  Stances are basically animation sets for specific melee weapon types.  Each of these stances is unique and has a different feel or even use.
-30 playable classes.  Yes, 30.
-God knows how many "mods."  Mods are what progress you through the game.  I currently own ~1500 unique mods.  You can make your gear work the way you want it to with these mods.
-The game just looks nice.  FashionFrame (player customization) is also a big deal.
-Premium currency is tradable and earnable. I have a very large amount of player customization items only available through premium currency and I only ever spent $5 on the game to buy someone at DE lunch. If you know what to grind for, earning premium currency is very reasonable.
-Grindy, but not too bad. I love games where I can work towards progress in a game.  Warframe provides that but not behind a huge time wall. One can reach total endgame within 100 hours of gameplay.  Unlocking a new class ranges from taking 20 mintues to (if RNG really hates you) about 30 hours.  Compared to some other RPG games out there, thats not too bad.
-The community can be very helpful and kind. If you ask for help, someone will likely help you, as long as you aren't being annoying about it.
-The developers really love and care for their game. With all of the hate DE recieves for their bad calls, they deserve just as much love for bringing us such a great game that is free. New content comes out every week to two weeks.
What I don't like:
-The developers are sometimes blind to what the community wants and sometimes (sorry DE) plain old stupid. I know its impossible to meet the demands of everyone in the community, but DE listens to the vocal minority on the forums far too often.  Also, some of the balancing in the PvP portion of the game is just wrong.
-RNG is your lord and destroyer in this game. I have farmed for 30 hours before for a single piece of something I wanted to just end up buying it from another player. Farming is part of the fun for me, but sometimes my poor luck makes it too much.
-The community also has its negative side. Most players are simply interested in grinding out their "Mastery Rank" (which doesn't do much for you past a pretty early point) and play the same mission 200+ times in a row to grind out the exp. Also, many players are just...BAD at the game and refuse to listen to advice or help.  This can lead to some rather sketchy situations for the others on the team.
-The game is repetative in nature. DE has done a lot to try and prevent this by having the huge variety in gear and many gamemodes. But there are only so many missions. Now, I think its safe to say most if not all games are repetative, so not a huge minus.
-You can write the game's story on a paper napkin. It doesn't exist. You have some lore that needs some digging to uncover, but no real story. (Update) Now needs 2 paper napkins!
Advice for new players:
There is a rather steep learning curve at first, but that can be part of the fun. Find people to play with, talk in game, ask for help. If you just go off solo, the game will get boring rather quickly, especially early game.
Final thoughts:
All in all, I love Warframe. There is a reason I sunk 2.5k hours into the game, its hands down my favorite game. If you like progression and shooting things while doing a mid-air backflip, THIS is your game. If you like grinding and huge variety, THIS is your game.
Its free for crying out loud, just try it!

Warframe is one of those games that has a development team that actually listens to the player base, is ACTUALLY FREE, and contains endless parkour. The design of the maps and characters are works of art that are stunning. This 4 player co-op game carries the definition of creativity and an actual free game. Meaning that you are NOT required to pay a single penny to be good at the game! Of course if you want to make your look flashy then you're going to have to spend a couple of bucks, but if you want that sweet new frame or weapon that just came out, then you can put yourself on the field and earn it's components that are required to build it without paying a single penny.
Warframe was also made to be played on lower quality computers, but people have to change the graphics settings first and have the ability to make a perfect balance between looks and performance. The gameplay is smooth and very fast paced, and before you begin complaining that this game is in third-person let me explain to you why: Warframe is a very fast paced game that has you jumping on every wall there is and executing attacks at high speeds. Would you be able to execute hundreds of flips, rolls, twirls, spinning attacks, and endless jumping within 2 minutes in first person? No! It would just be confusing and frustrating! Which is why it is in third person!
For my conclusion, Warframe is truly a wonderful masterpiece that deserves every buck I put into it. From it's artistic landscapes and maps to its stunning gameplay and mechanics, Warframe was made to be a game that will be remembered for a long, long time, and it will be.

I will only comment on what I have seen in 2100 hours of game time.
From a monetary standpoint this game is well worth it, as you can see from my hours played and almost every other ark players. You will definitely get the hours out of the money you put in. The world is on a much grander scale than any of the other games in the genre. There are hundreds and thousands of things to do, see, and explore. You'll tame things that only you have on your server, colors that only you found, stats that only you got the luck of the roll to get.  You'll build a base in your own spot, with your own view.  You'll get attached to those tames, and that base.  This, however, is where I run out of positive things to say and these positives start to bleed in with the negatives to leave you with a truly bitter game experience.
I play only on a pvp server. Anything you build and tame can be attacked and wiped by any other player or tribe that is stronger than you.  Your first couple of hundred hours might be spent building multiple bases just to have them wiped by other tribes. However you get better, and smarter, and eventually you build bases that are hard to raid if not a total waste of time and resources for the enemy. This is where I found myself.
My tribemate and I built up an entire base of quad thick walls, quad thick ceilings, tamed hundreds of creatures, placed our turrets without blind spots. All of the things you do once you realize how to defend your base. We are socially competent, making good relationships with the tribes tougher than us, and we are pretty safe from raids and wipes. This being said you can be wiped at any time. Its a resource game and if they really want inside they will get in.
We, however, and many others in this game fear Wildcard Studios and the in game Ark bugs much more than other players. We spend more time, lose more tames and buildings to bugs than anything else in the game by far.
The game constantly pushes your tames through the ground, causing you to lose them forever. This has happened to multiple tames of mine that were completely safe otherwise. You get disconnected randomly. Randomly can't get on the game due to timeouts and the dreaded "snapshot 16".
Just this week they caused the final straw. Rolling back all of the Offical servers by 30 hours because of a duping glitch that they had caused themselves.  They deleted all crossark inventories, destroying peoples tames and items.
We lost tames, buildings, and time.   I will not be coming back to this game and I advise anybody who owns the game to give an honest review.
In conclusion, at this point I would say the game is not worth the money. At the beginning I said you would definitely get the hours out from the money you put in, and you will.  However you will constantly question the value of these hours. I know Wildcard does not value these hours otherwise bugs that have happened to me a year ago such as trees and rocks poofing tames would no longer exist.
Do not buy.

Everything good there is to say about this game has already been said by other reviewers, way better than I ever could. Get the game. No two ways about it.
However, I want to take this opportunity to further elaborate on Warframe's trading system:
Warframe has its own trading system and economy. As a newer player, this system may seem a bit overwhelming at first, and many long-time players may attempt to fool/scam you out of your Platinum (the real-money currency you can buy at the store) at first, by trying to sell you items at 5-10 times their actual worth. So in order to get an idea of the general prices of different items/mods, you can go to the warframe.market site and type in whatever item(s) or mod(s) you are interested in in the search bar, and see a list of people who are selling, and at what price.
The prices on the site are almost always fair, as it is mostly used by long-time players to buy and sell to each other, so everyone has to list items at decent prices, or they won't ever sell them. I've included the link below, in hopes that it helps some of the newer players to not waste their platinum on things that are pretty much trash.

Welcome to the furture, space ninja.
Warframe is a simple concept that has some fantastic results for the right consumer. They took the mmorpg formula and upscaled it so that grinding was fun. This game is made for you if you love looking cool, but if you can't stand doing anything repetitivly, do not get Warframe (it is not for you). If you want a more detailed guide, expand the full review.
This is the thing everyone is initailly concerned about when they start playing - what do i do? Well, Warframe is a game about grinding. That's it. No more, no less. It is all about the grinding for more gear, better upgrades, and more challenges. Your goal is to progress and completely have, use, and upgrade everything that the game cna and will offer. While it seems idiotic to play a game that is just there for the grinding of materials, but actually provides a great experience once you truly start playing the game.
Upon initial download, the tutorial is a little lackluster, lacking true help and instruction on the vast array of unique mechanics that Warframe offers to a new player. Other than this, Warframe offers a great plethora of weapons, armors, abilities, and enemies to keep anyone hooked. The combat is extremely well-made and fluid, which makes the grind worth the time. Players do not look at the game as a grind, but rather as a way to look cool while grinding. The same principle lies behind the grind; however, Warframe makes the grind fun through solid combat, eccentric enemies, and gorgeous setpieces.
This game is pretty. That's is it. While their isn't much music, the sound design is all around very solid and gives a sense of power when you pull the trigger. The visual designs are magnificent, and my hat goes off to the artists at DE for the amazing models that appear in the game. The warframe's armor and different weapons all seem unique and very interesting in each one's individual sense. Not only is the player looking superb, but also the ambient enviornment and the enemies all have visual beauty as well as a distinctiveness that greatly helps the game seem imersive. The one complaint I have is that the setpieces and rooms often get repeated, in a copy and paste fashion, to maker the levels. I guess DE wanted to make sure that their designs got looked at.
Warframe is an addictive third-person grind-fest that combines excellent gunplay and comabt and mixes it with aethetic beauty to create a great game. If you get bored really easily, do not attempt this game - it is a time sync. If you have the time and are ready for the challenge, then jump in and help save the solar system - we need you. I give Warframe a 9/10 for the reasons stated previously in the review.

I will start by saying that this is possibly the only game that I can put unlimited hours into and still enjoy. With that out of the way, I will get into the objective pros and cons before heading onto a bit of my subjective opinion.
Pros:
Interesting, in-depth, useful, and some what optional parkour system. (Despite the system being required in some situations, these are limited; It is good that this system is its own playstyle rather than a requirement to play)\
Dozens of weapons to collect, level, and customize.
Most weapons are side grades, with some exceptions, meaning that if you prefer one playstyle to another, you are not punished for this.
A deep mod system used to customize exactly what your weapon does, its power, and how it plays that includes hundreds of mods. Depending on how you mod a weapon, it could feel like an entirely different item.
Several dozen classes (or warframes) that are each unique in playstyle, appearance, and attributes.
A compelling story that has left me breathless at times.
Level design is beyond beautiful, and each level is procedurally generated to keep things fresh.
Plenty of things to do all the way from start to end game. There is always something to occupy oneself with.
A skill based combat system that rewards player progression as well as character progression.
A wonderful clan system that encourages player socializing.
A clan "dojo" that utilizes a construction system so that you can make your own home for yourself and your friends.
A research system using the dojo to incentivize clans and give access to weapons and warframes that would have been otherwise barred to you.
An overall supportive and friendly community.
A mission matchmaker that allows you find a party at a moment's notice.
Very, very active developers who are constantly adding new content and keep in contact with the community.
A vivid character customization system that allows you to tailor your warframe to your own, personal style.
Constantly evolving lore that affects missions, gameplay, and the world around you.
A crafting system to create weapons and warframes that makes each addition to your collection feel like an accomplishment.
Every expansion comes for free.
Combat becomes a power fantasy at higher levels, giving a feeling similar to what you might see in anime.
A faction system in which each faction gives its own rewards that another faction might not. These do not get in the way of gameplay, allowing you the freedom to continue without being pulled away.
Cons:
Rather high system requirements and bandwidth consumption.
Rather prevelent lag in public matchmaking that can sometimes render a mission almost unplayable.
Widely present monetization; Color packs for customization must be bought, warframes and weapons can be bought outright instead of crafted, slots for warframes and weapons are limited unless more are bought, most cosmetics must be bought, and so on and so on.
Crafting system can sometimes feel unfair, requiring you to gain the materials and then wait another period of time as it is crafted via automation onboard your ship. This period of time can range from 8 hour to as long as 3 days. This, of course, can be rushed with premium currency.
Some weapons are objectively more powerful than others. For instance, the Nikana Prime (an advanced form of katana) is currently the single most powerful melee weapon in the game. It does the most damage of any one-handed weapon with a rapid swing speed, area of swings that rival most two-handed weapons, high crit chance, high status chance, and so on. This can sometimes feel daunting as the game offers no excuse to any other weapon aside from these upper tier weapons at higher levels.
The community is almost painfully competitive. Sometimes as a player is being friendly to you, they are leaving you in the dust and completing the mission objective before you can even get your bearings on your surroundings. Most will just let you die if they do not think that you are pulling your weight in a mission. Then there are the trolls that are present in any gaming community. This is to be expected, though.
Story can sometimes feel absent as main story elements are single quests once every long while. You complete this quest and wait for the next event or expansion.
The grind is real. If you are not okay with grinding toward something based on your own motivations, then this game probably isn't for you.
Maps are procedurally generated from a fixed number of map tiles. You will find yourself running, sprinting, flying, gliding, wall jumping, and sliding through the same rooms and areas over and over. While this does lend itself toward learning the areas and using them to your advantage, they can get quite repetetive.
Some items are openly barred from you if you are not willing to join a clan or create your own and pump resources into the research items.
There is a very active player trading system that can often leave you asking why you put hours of work into getting this item when this other person just bought it.
Parkour system can be somewhat difficult to learn at first. While rewarding once learnt, you will find yourself stuck on bits of scenery time and time again until you get the hang of it.
Faction system can sometimes seem nonexistent until your opposing factions send an ambush of relatively high-level mini-bosses that will wipe you out if you are not prepared or if you are just trying to level items up.
Once you have maximized your warframe and at least one weapon, the game can feel somewhat overly easy until you do some end game raids in which enemies become almost unfair bullet sponges and smack you about like a schmuck.
Side-Note: I have not played the PVP portions at all, so I incapable of commenting on PVP. All that I can say is that it does exist, and it is very intense due to the parkour system.
As for my personal opinion, the flaws do not bother me too much. The monetization is mostly paying for cosmetics or convenience. The problems of the community are inevitable for any gaming community and this sort of game. I find more pleasant members of the Warframe community than not. I enjoy pretty much every part of it, and after spending 465 hours as of this review, I am still not bored. I just completed the newest story mission, and it touched me in such a way that most entertainment and media has not. It continues to surprise me, and the development team feels close to the player base. If I want to take things slow and relax, I can switch to a solo session and gain the ability to actually pause. If I want to socialize, I can hop into a lower level mission and heal for them so that I am not carrying. If I want a challenge, I can either solo a higher level mission or group up for end game content. I love it, and I hope that others can enjoy it as much.

Regardless of what anyone says this is a fun game. I can say I got my moneys worth. Its creative, entertaining, fun, challenging, and huge. The world is massive and full of dangerous and or useful creatures. You can make any building you want, anywhere you want. Get creative with it! Make a castle / cottage / small city / barn / skyscraper / ship / ANYTHING. The building process can be frustrating, but there are many little tips and tricks that will make your structures much more durable, and realistic looking.
The dinosaurs offer great advantages, and have specialized rolls. Get a Direwolf to gather meat, a Deod to help you crush stone and build your structures, an Argy to fly around the map, scouting for building locations, carry goods or dinos or people around the map. You can build a mobile base on top of a Brontosaurus! Seriously a walking functional base on the back of a dino. Every dinosaur has a use even the Dodo that lays valuable eggs at the rapid rate.

The environment is ♥♥♥♥ing gorgeous. Like serious eye candy if your computer can handle it. Coupled with the huge maps you are able to settle in many different beautiful areas that will immerse you in the game that much more. Dangerous swamps, freezing cold snowy mountains, massive redwood forests, lush tropical jungles, and sandy beaches. If your computer can handle the graphics I would venture to say it would almost be worth buying the game just to build a little warm and cozy cottage next to a nice waterfall or cliffside escape in the redwood forest.
This game will drain time without you knowing it. Things take a long time to accomplish. Buildings take a long time to gather materials for dpending on how big you go. Dinos take  long time to tame. Places take a long time to get to. The crappy part is all that can be gone very fast. In-fact you will lose everything and want to quit over one night. For some reason though i got over this, and actually almost looked forward to starting a new. Guess it depends on the player.
There are bugs that need to be worked out, but i would love to see this game polished and finished. I think it is actualy relativly close.

This game is not for the light hearted and heavy walleted. Every single thing you want to build in this game takes a MINIMUM of 12 hours to craft. This means that if you want to craft a weapon that requires several parts you will need to find the resources, then the BP, then get credits to craft it if you don't have enough, then craft it, then wait 12 hours, then you have a nice weapon. Same thing to craft new warframes (aka new characters) but after you craft a all the parts that take 12 hours you must then put them all together which takes THREE WHOLE DAYS.

(Long review)
This is my overall view of the game so far.
Since I started this game 2-3 weeks ago I have logged almost 100 hours when writing this review. The game itself has so many things to do it's unbelievable, but that is if you are willing to spend the time to play it. This game is not for “Casual” players who want a facebook based game where you log on for 5-10 minutes click a few buttons and hop off. After reading a lot of the negative reviews I have figured out some of the major “Issues” people claim the game has.
(To grindy)
(Not enough things to do)
(Game is to hard)
(Pay to win)
After playing the game for almost 100 hours I do have to partially agree when people say that there is too much grinding, I wouldn't say there is too much grinding other than the grinding and missions are to spread apart I.E it takes time to reach the next main story quest. This is not really a problem considering plenty of people complain about other games having to short of a story. Like I said before this game is not for the faint of heart in order to play this game you are going to need these three things,
(Time, and effort)
(Non lazy personality)
(Dedication)
If you have these traits in your personality then this game is for you. Now a bit more into the gameplay for the game. The gameplay in Warframe is very ninja like jumping, swinging, slashing, fast paced combat. The default controls for the game are very odd but you can rebind them to what makes you feel comfortable. There is missions that you can complete to progress your weapons and warframes, these missions are on planets that you unlock by killing bosses. Each planet has their own individual boss that you kill in order to unlock the next planet. One of the major mission areas that you will spend time in is called the void, this is where the majority of the grinding in the game is. In the game you can buy with real money ingame money called Platinum, this is used for trading with other players to get prime blueprints which are farmed in the void. Something that should be noted you need void keys in order to unlock missions these are farmed in normal missions on planets. If you are taking the free to play approach to the game then you will be doing a lot of farming to sell these prime blueprints for platinum. This is the end of my long review so far of the game, give it a try if you don’t like it then you don’t but do not make up false negative reports just because you’re lazy and you give up too easily.

Started off in the Northeast part of the Island.  Mulled around gathering berries, wood, and other assorted items to build a shack on the beach to acclimate myself to the area.  Doing great, have a few tamed critters including a scorpion, a raptor, a triceratops, and a couple of little mammals with clubs on their tails.  Get the shack built out of thatch and all is well except all the sudden my screen rumbles from heavy footfalls coming my way.  I open the door to see what kind of critter could make such a ruckus and what do I find?  A T-rex, standing nose to nose with me right outside of my door!  Well obviously I proceed to back into the hut and go prone hoping he didn't see me, but I was too late.  I was greeted by chomping  on my roof until he busted a few sections then it appeared he grew bored and started walking off north after eating all of my critters except for my club-tailed mammals who fortunately can roll up into balls to protect themselves.
So I spend the next bit of time scrounging up the resources to build walls around my little hut and convert it all to wood.  Wood is some heavy stuff!  Multiple trips with the mammals helping me bring in the haul, all the while looking over my shoulder to the north knowing that the T-rex was still stalking out there and could come back to terrorize me at any moment.  After the walls were built, and no sign of the T-rex in a while, I decide to try my luck and go up on the mountain ridge to the north.  Not far from the base I notice down on the beach the T-rex is still stalking prey.  He sees me and immediately charges but thankfully I am high up on a hill and he can't get to me.  I pull out my trusty bow and sink no less than 30 arrows into it's hide before it goes down, but was ecstatic about it.  Donning my new T-rex helm skin I trod off proudly with packs full of meat back to my growing little base.
...........

SINGLEPLAYER REVIEW
I previously played ark before in 2015 sadly the perfomance was awfull. But a few months a ago I decided to re-purchase it and that was a great decision.
Pros:
Ark is the dinosaur survival game dino/jp fans have wanted for a long time.
It captures the ambience better than any game released in many years. The sounds , the weather and the dinos and terrain all blend amazingly.
The items unlocked through engrams are well desinged and chosen well for the setting from starting from a thatch hut with a spear to a stone outpost style base with a crossbow and a trusty raptor pack to the awesome treetop metal baseses with rifles and rexes you do feel the progession and how the gameplay changes depending on what stage you're on.
Dinosaur variety is awesome from dodo's to rex's to dragon's ark has all the prehistoric and mythical creatures you need and there always adding more.
Cons:
Still unopmtimized even though I've gotten only one issue so far it's common for others though force most of my friends to avoid the game just for that reason.
Multiplayer is meh if you're playing with just friends then on a private server I can see it being fun, but public servers are to be avoided I've only spent about 10 hours on them not fun within an hour the tribe I joined got threatend by and unopposible force unless you've got a large group of freinds that can help and play 5 or more hours a day it's a struggle.
Glitches though not major problems glitches do get a bit annoying especially early game I'm talking about dinosaur getting stuck on or in trees/rocks wich is a bit supid from a gameplay and realism pov ,the only other minor "glitch" i've seen is dinos not being occupied by a player and wild dinos take no fall damage which is annoying from a realism pov since they can fall from the tallest mountain and take no damage?
Mixed:
The grind is good and bad it adds plenty of depth but can be fustrating depending on what you're grinding for I don't mind if it's to make an even better base then fine but spend double the time grinding for a base just for a few bulllets is daft.
Overall
Ark is great singleplayer or private servers I'm always happy to come back and see what adventures (sorry I know adventures is chliche) I'll get up to next
I give ark a rating of
7/10 solo game
8/10 private game
5/10 public game

Okay, so ... this only gives me two options...I would recommend the game and I have but not for the MMORPG. I don't like MMORPG's I like multi-players where I can play with people I know, trust and want to socialize with. My family is going in on a private server so that is all we have to deal with (They don't play MMORPG's either) we like Single Player and Private Server Style.
As a single player game it kicks your♥♥♥♥♥over and over again, I've had glitches where I've lost Dino's, Building, whole built up territories and a 65 Level Character because of how they do their map saves. (The Island and The Central Map use the same character just a warning, if you start a character on one of those maps, and try to start a character on the other map it will delete your first one). That I don't agree with, they should fix that infact for single player games they should allow you to have as many characters as you want, it shouldn't matter and you should be able to delete them as you see fit. It's taking me a lot of learning to figure out how to play the game itself and a few character restarts. Restarting your map isn't easy, cleaning up the clutter is a ♥♥♥♥♥ but that's alright these are things I can live with because the game is still Early Access and I hope they frankly fix it down the road.
Eventually I found my stride, it was some where between level 10 and 20 where it wasn't so hard to survive as long as I lived by the Croods motto everything will try to kill you and everything is bad. Swamps Bad, Jungles Bad, Forests Bad, Snow Covered Mountains EXTRA BAD. I wish I could put on the red hand prints.  There was a while I was collecting ways to die, drownding, burnt alive, Eaten by Alpha Compys  it started being a badge of honor I swear... Oh I had a Bronto Push me off a cliff into shark infested waters add it to the list. Giant Beautiful Bird Like Dinos that are aggressive herbavors ambushed me and my high level trike while we were exploring a trail in the woods... you get used to the masocism and it starts becoming weirdly fun.
I purchased Scorched Earth, which was a whole new level of Masocism, the poundings just kept coming and coming with no real light at the end of the tunnel until about level 60 when I kept a Dino for more then ten minutes, was able to carefully clear out a water source with weird gorilla tactics in the heat of the day, and spent three days slowly building up an Adobe House to protect me from the elements (except th scorching red heat) and I still can't find a source of crystal but again I am surving with Crood Tactics.
After all this single player punishment I am still having fun, My house is only one story with the second story being built and it tells me during those sweltering hot heat storms that I need to get underground (I have no idea where a cave is to be honest, or if you can build into the ground that would be nice if you can) but I do have the desert armor so it's made life more bearable (By the way you have to have a smelter and work bench to even make that, and an F*Ton of Silk... you get from flowers.. maybe) and I have a few dinos (Though occasionally something will take out a dino or two.... I have no real way of fencing it off, but it's beautiful.
If you enjoy the struggle, the survival, the constant scraping by then sure this is a game for you. I love the Dinos, I love the scenery and I love sharing this game with my family and friends.
Now I hear that public servers are not the way to go, but to me they are like every other MMORPG out there the strong being bullies to the weak, and people otherwise ruining a good game for the masses. So, I don't play the MMORPG game.

Graphics 8/10
The Graphics in this game are just great. Everything is pretty to look at, the coloring is nice, and all the models look how they should. You really feel like the space ninja when everything is visually designed so well.
Story 2/10
This is an mmo there isn’t much of a story to follow. I never felt like it was progressing and that the game was focusing on plot points well. Although it is a lot better this way without a story to follow i can focus on the other parts of the game without much tension. Basically what I’m saying is that there isn’t much of a story and it’s better that way.
Music 6/10
This game makes you really feel like the ninja of space. The music focuses on the stealthy music thing. Though if you choose to go guns blazing the music amps up. Its very basic music but that doesn’t stop it from having impact.
Gameplay 9.999999999999999999999999999999999/10
The gameplay is the game is so close to being absolutely perfect. In the game you go on planets and complete missions by yourself, with friends, or strangers. You can use a bunch of weapons and you can carry 3 weapons into missions in 3 categories. You can carry a Primary, Secondary, and a melee weapon into battle. The best part is to craft better weapons you must go to different planets to gather materials to make them. You can also make different warframes in which you must find the warframe part blueprints, craft them, and them craft the warframe together. There are several different mission types there is the spy, extermination, sabotage, defence, mobile defence, escort, capture, excavation, survival, arena, invasion, assassination missions, ect.
Overall 9/10 with the rating of play it

The game's quests are very well thought out and the most impactful one is the Natah/Second Dream quest chain. It is at this point in the game you realize that the game is about energetic balance and harmony, not about all the killing.
Depending on what you like, this game can be very addictive. I wish I joined the game back when I saw it a year ago on Steam, but it's better late than never. Some tips for the starting player is to either buy 2 Warframe inventory slots or 2 Forma from the market with your starter 50 platinum.

This is my overall view of the game so far.
Since I started this game 2-3 weeks ago I have logged almost 100 hours when writing this review. The game itself has so many things to do it's unbelievable, but that is if you are willing to spend the time to play it. This game is not for “Casual” players who want a facebook based game where you log on for 5-10 minutes click a few buttons and hop off. After reading a lot of the negative reviews I have figured out some of the major “Issues” people claim the game has.
(To grindy)
(Not enough things to do)
(Game is to hard)
(Pay to win)
After playing the game for almost 100 hours I do have to partially agree when people say that there is too much grinding, I wouldn't say there is too much grinding other than the grinding and missions are to spread apart I.E it takes time to reach the next main story quest. This is not really a problem considering plenty of people complain about other games having to short of a story. Like I said before this game is not for the faint of heart in order to play this game you are going to need these three things,
(Time, and effort)
(Non lazy personality)
(Dedication)
If you have these traits in your personality then this game is for you. Now a bit more into the gameplay for the game. The gameplay in Warframe is very ninja like jumping, swinging, slashing, fast paced combat. The default controls for the game are very odd but you can rebind them to what makes you feel comfortable. There is missions that you can complete to progress your weapons and warframes, these missions are on planets that you unlock by killing bosses. Each planet has their own individual boss that you kill in order to unlock the next planet. One of the major mission areas that you will spend time in is called the void, this is where the majority of the grinding in the game is. In the game you can buy with real money ingame money called Platinum, this is used for trading with other players to get prime blueprints which are farmed in the void. Something that should be noted you need void keys in order to unlock missions these are farmed in normal missions on planets. If you are taking the free to play approach to the game then you will be doing a lot of farming to sell these prime blueprints for platinum. This is the end of my long review so far of the game, give it a try if you don’t like it then you don’t but do not make up false negative reports just because you’re lazy and you give up too easily.

Welcome to the furture, space ninja.
Warframe is a simple concept that has some fantastic results for the right consumer. They took the mmorpg formula and upscaled it so that grinding was fun. This game is made for you if you love looking cool, but if you can't stand doing anything repetitivly, do not get Warframe (it is not for you). If you want a more detailed guide, expand the full review.
This is the thing everyone is initailly concerned about when they start playing - what do i do? Well, Warframe is a game about grinding. That's it. No more, no less. It is all about the grinding for more gear, better upgrades, and more challenges. Your goal is to progress and completely have, use, and upgrade everything that the game cna and will offer. While it seems idiotic to play a game that is just there for the grinding of materials, but actually provides a great experience once you truly start playing the game.
Upon initial download, the tutorial is a little lackluster, lacking true help and instruction on the vast array of unique mechanics that Warframe offers to a new player. Other than this, Warframe offers a great plethora of weapons, armors, abilities, and enemies to keep anyone hooked. The combat is extremely well-made and fluid, which makes the grind worth the time. Players do not look at the game as a grind, but rather as a way to look cool while grinding. The same principle lies behind the grind; however, Warframe makes the grind fun through solid combat, eccentric enemies, and gorgeous setpieces.
This game is pretty. That's is it. While their isn't much music, the sound design is all around very solid and gives a sense of power when you pull the trigger. The visual designs are magnificent, and my hat goes off to the artists at DE for the amazing models that appear in the game. The warframe's armor and different weapons all seem unique and very interesting in each one's individual sense. Not only is the player looking superb, but also the ambient enviornment and the enemies all have visual beauty as well as a distinctiveness that greatly helps the game seem imersive. The one complaint I have is that the setpieces and rooms often get repeated, in a copy and paste fashion, to maker the levels. I guess DE wanted to make sure that their designs got looked at.
Warframe is an addictive third-person grind-fest that combines excellent gunplay and comabt and mixes it with aethetic beauty to create a great game. If you get bored really easily, do not attempt this game - it is a time sync. If you have the time and are ready for the challenge, then jump in and help save the solar system - we need you. I give Warframe a 9/10 for the reasons stated previously in the review.

I will start by saying that this is possibly the only game that I can put unlimited hours into and still enjoy. With that out of the way, I will get into the objective pros and cons before heading onto a bit of my subjective opinion.
Pros:
Interesting, in-depth, useful, and some what optional parkour system. (Despite the system being required in some situations, these are limited; It is good that this system is its own playstyle rather than a requirement to play)\
Dozens of weapons to collect, level, and customize.
Most weapons are side grades, with some exceptions, meaning that if you prefer one playstyle to another, you are not punished for this.
A deep mod system used to customize exactly what your weapon does, its power, and how it plays that includes hundreds of mods. Depending on how you mod a weapon, it could feel like an entirely different item.
Several dozen classes (or warframes) that are each unique in playstyle, appearance, and attributes.
A compelling story that has left me breathless at times.
Level design is beyond beautiful, and each level is procedurally generated to keep things fresh.
Plenty of things to do all the way from start to end game. There is always something to occupy oneself with.
A skill based combat system that rewards player progression as well as character progression.
A wonderful clan system that encourages player socializing.
A clan "dojo" that utilizes a construction system so that you can make your own home for yourself and your friends.
A research system using the dojo to incentivize clans and give access to weapons and warframes that would have been otherwise barred to you.
An overall supportive and friendly community.
A mission matchmaker that allows you find a party at a moment's notice.
Very, very active developers who are constantly adding new content and keep in contact with the community.
A vivid character customization system that allows you to tailor your warframe to your own, personal style.
Constantly evolving lore that affects missions, gameplay, and the world around you.
A crafting system to create weapons and warframes that makes each addition to your collection feel like an accomplishment.
Every expansion comes for free.
Combat becomes a power fantasy at higher levels, giving a feeling similar to what you might see in anime.
A faction system in which each faction gives its own rewards that another faction might not. These do not get in the way of gameplay, allowing you the freedom to continue without being pulled away.
Cons:
Rather high system requirements and bandwidth consumption.
Rather prevelent lag in public matchmaking that can sometimes render a mission almost unplayable.
Widely present monetization; Color packs for customization must be bought, warframes and weapons can be bought outright instead of crafted, slots for warframes and weapons are limited unless more are bought, most cosmetics must be bought, and so on and so on.
Crafting system can sometimes feel unfair, requiring you to gain the materials and then wait another period of time as it is crafted via automation onboard your ship. This period of time can range from 8 hour to as long as 3 days. This, of course, can be rushed with premium currency.
Some weapons are objectively more powerful than others. For instance, the Nikana Prime (an advanced form of katana) is currently the single most powerful melee weapon in the game. It does the most damage of any one-handed weapon with a rapid swing speed, area of swings that rival most two-handed weapons, high crit chance, high status chance, and so on. This can sometimes feel daunting as the game offers no excuse to any other weapon aside from these upper tier weapons at higher levels.
The community is almost painfully competitive. Sometimes as a player is being friendly to you, they are leaving you in the dust and completing the mission objective before you can even get your bearings on your surroundings. Most will just let you die if they do not think that you are pulling your weight in a mission. Then there are the trolls that are present in any gaming community. This is to be expected, though.
Story can sometimes feel absent as main story elements are single quests once every long while. You complete this quest and wait for the next event or expansion.
The grind is real. If you are not okay with grinding toward something based on your own motivations, then this game probably isn't for you.
Maps are procedurally generated from a fixed number of map tiles. You will find yourself running, sprinting, flying, gliding, wall jumping, and sliding through the same rooms and areas over and over. While this does lend itself toward learning the areas and using them to your advantage, they can get quite repetetive.
Some items are openly barred from you if you are not willing to join a clan or create your own and pump resources into the research items.
There is a very active player trading system that can often leave you asking why you put hours of work into getting this item when this other person just bought it.
Parkour system can be somewhat difficult to learn at first. While rewarding once learnt, you will find yourself stuck on bits of scenery time and time again until you get the hang of it.
Faction system can sometimes seem nonexistent until your opposing factions send an ambush of relatively high-level mini-bosses that will wipe you out if you are not prepared or if you are just trying to level items up.
Once you have maximized your warframe and at least one weapon, the game can feel somewhat overly easy until you do some end game raids in which enemies become almost unfair bullet sponges and smack you about like a schmuck.
Side-Note: I have not played the PVP portions at all, so I incapable of commenting on PVP. All that I can say is that it does exist, and it is very intense due to the parkour system.
As for my personal opinion, the flaws do not bother me too much. The monetization is mostly paying for cosmetics or convenience. The problems of the community are inevitable for any gaming community and this sort of game. I find more pleasant members of the Warframe community than not. I enjoy pretty much every part of it, and after spending 465 hours as of this review, I am still not bored. I just completed the newest story mission, and it touched me in such a way that most entertainment and media has not. It continues to surprise me, and the development team feels close to the player base. If I want to take things slow and relax, I can switch to a solo session and gain the ability to actually pause. If I want to socialize, I can hop into a lower level mission and heal for them so that I am not carrying. If I want a challenge, I can either solo a higher level mission or group up for end game content. I love it, and I hope that others can enjoy it as much.

Summary: It's good. try it out. refund it if it's not for you. Simple.
