Yes to offline play. No to online play.
This game will literally demand that you log on every single day, or it will destroy your hard earned work. (if playing online)
Pros-
- It is the most rewarding game I've ever played. You work to tame dinos by building up certain ingredients for them to eat, you hunt them down, you breed them to make super strong pokemon. No game has ever felt this rewarding for the amount of work I've put into it.
- The smooth gameplay is really nice. Dinos are fun to drive around, combat is fast and intense, etc.
- It's extremely deep and content filled with whole different worlds to learn.
Cons-
-It will take back everything you worked for faster than you got it.
-If you disconnect? Fall off flyer, die, lose dino and inventory.
-If you dont log in for 8 days? Every dino you own decays, along with your buildings. Which is ♥♥♥♥ing disgusting. We put insane amounts of work into this game and in return, it actively seeks to destroy our empires.  The decay timer and offline damage is too far.   Every time i disconnected while playing this game, I would go insane, frantically trying to get back online in time to save myself from the dangerous dinosaurs that could be nearby, eating my afk body and dinosaurs.
- Territory wars
- Massive clans claim 80% of the map, leaving new players with little room to build, and once you do build, you too have to place pillars up to protect your land, and if you don't? Those 40 new neighbors that bought the game on a steam sale will now be placing houses alll over your base, which prevents you from editing anything if they live too close. Break one of your own walls? Cant replace it cause someone placed a foundation too close.
- A dino that requires being trapped? Dont even think about it, because you CANNOT build a trap anywhere due to there being too many foundations from other players nearby, no matter where you go. Get use to chasing dinos across the map, shooting them with tranqs as they aggro every predator in the game and probably get killed by one before you tame it.
- It creates hate for new players.
Older players are extremely hateful towards new players, and if they're not, the new players thrive and build empires of their own, encroaching on everyone else, making the game even more cramped.
- PVE is not actually PVE. It is still PVP in this game. Everything is competitive. Instead of directly ♥♥♥♥ing your neighbor, you passively aggressively ♥♥♥♥ your neighbor. If you don't, they will ♥♥♥♥ you instead.
- Other players can drag your offline body into danger if you dont log off in a secret location
- Other players can steal your eggs, which are farmed to produce kibble to tame dinos
- Other players can leave their dinos in your base, preventing you from building there
- Tribes allow every player to steal everything, ruining the whole tribe, nobody can be trusted.
- Allying allows any ally to build on your land and you cannot demolish their buildings , which could ruin your whole base if they wanted to.
- IF you don't have one of your clan members or allies fly around to everything you've build at least every few days, they will decay. YES THATS RIGHT, you have to visit every single structure you own or it will decay, EVEN THOUGH YOU'RE STILL ACTIVELY PLAYING.
- There is no "Unstuck" feature. If you get stuck in a hole, you hve to die and lose your inventory.
- Dinos that have been downed after tranqilizing, often disappear, making your effort futile.
-Breeding takes  WAY too long. I tried to breed some sabers and some sloths. The saber needed to gestate (pregnancy) for 4 hours, then once the baby was born, I had to feed it constantly until it was 10% done, which took like 4 more hours, I forget. But i had to stay up all night or it would have died. Then I was going to attempt to breed a sloth, but it had an EIGHT hour gestation period and then even more time of feeding it as a baby or it will die. You have to plan everything for the days you're not at work, and even then, there are dinos that take DAYS to breed....  Oh, and then when you log off for  a week, they'll die. They can die faster than it took them to be born. OK ark, forgot you don't like people with a real life.
Ontop of that, the game is insanely difficult to get started in. I'm not even complaining about that part. The challenge is the fun. But when you combine that with all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t rules and glitches i just mentioned, it's too much. I played for almost 500 hours before writing this review, online, and I thoroughly enjoyed the good aspects of the game, but the negatives out weight it by a ton. It's too much stress. We should not have to treat ark as if it were real life, living onit 24-7 to maintain our progress.
Online play is everything. We get to interact with other players and thats a huge part of the game's appeal. So I am sad to be forced to play offline only, in order to relieve myself of the " DUTIES" that ark demands I regularly fulfill online.

This game has quite a bit of potential and looks really good if your computer can handle it. But it's also riddled with serious bugs. I'm playing this game on about the most powerful Mac you can have for games ( GTX 980, 32 GB RAM, 4-core Xeon, HyperX Predator SSD) and it is struggling to get 20 fps.
Parts of the game are unplayable due to serious bugs and I see no effort from the developers to solve them.
The game is as much a Player vs Bugs as it is Player vs Player or Player vs Environment.
I've played many Early Access games, but this is the most buggy so far. Others were incomplete, but not this buggy.
I've played about 350 hours now, so I do have an idea of what the game can do. When the game works properly it is very nice.
The game also seems to have some serious performance issues on Mac. Much more than comparable games I have. For example, I get about 15-25 fps, independent of any graphics settings. Something else is holding the game back, I suspect the way network traffic is handled, as I can get up to 180 fps in the server browser, if I cancel the list update/scan. There is also a long standing issue with the rendering of crops, that makes my fps drop to 3 or less whenever I'm near any farm.
There are also issues with players, and dino's and other objects glitching through walls, weird effects with the order in which things are rendered/loaded from disk some of which can cause serious in game problems.
If not for the bugs, this would be a really nice Mac game, if your computer can handle it.
(Apple seems to have lost it since 2013 and their more recent hardware is very weak for gaming. Get yourself an old Mac Pro and put a GTX 980 in it like I did).
EDIT: I stopped playing for a couple of months and just came back to see if things were better now that official release is imminent. It certainly is NOT. The game has gotten worse. The sea now renders as an opaque blob, which makes large parts of the game unusable. This game is nowhere near release in its current state.
SECOND EDIT: The game is even more broken now. The mouse is no longer working properly. The game is totally unplayable on Mac. Don't buy it !

I have pumped thousands of hours into this game and plan on pumping thousands more. That being said, like most people who have played as long as I have... we are a bit biased.
I avoid Official Servers entirely. My experience has been entirely corrupted due to this. If you are looking for someone's opinion who plays on an Official Server, look elsewhere. That being said, I strongly encourage people to stop playing on Official Servers and start playing on Private ones becuase most of their "issues" with the game can be solved in this way.
ARK is an INSANELY grindy game. You have to be dedicated and willing to pump hours into this game at it's core. This game is not easy or fun if you are playing alone unless you join a private server with everything bumped up. ARK is insanely fun to play with friends, or as a group. There are many shennanigans to be had and minor bugs that are funny (rag dolling bodies, for example). At it's core, ARK isn't very fun if you're alone, but with friends it is great.
The game is in EA. We all know this. Yet because it is so far along in development, people expect it to be a completed game. Let me stress this: ARK is NOT a completed game. It is NOT optimized and it is NOT ready for the average gamer. This game is buying a "fixer upper" and realizing it only needs some paint, some new appliances, and a new roof; this game is not buying a "fixer upper" and getting a mansion that doesn't need any work what-so-ever. Many people expect that from this game and it simply will not be that.
There is a huge community rift in understanding on content creation vs bug fixing. Most people expect bugs to be fixed as soon as they occur and no more content to be added, without realizing that it is different teams. Consider your daily work place, it takes many different teams to make your entire company run smoothly, from the grunt laborers to the management, each are a piece of the full scale image, but each run separately with their own goals in mind. ARK is like this, as is every other major company.
Would I suggest ARK? It depends on what you want to do. If you're looking for a fun game you can put an hour or two in a day one Official servers... absolutely not. This game will never be hat. If you're looking for a fun game you can mod, explore, enjoy, and aren't afraid to break from the "norm" and play on private servers that speed things up to fit your job schedule: absolutely!

It kind of hurts to not be able to recommend this game. But in it's current state, it's my honest answer.
When I first play this game, it was honestly a magical experience. I don't think I've ever had so much fun and the hugest "The sky is the limit" feeling while playing a game. One important thing to mention that if you really want to have a good experience you'll want to either play on a nice PvE server or on singleplayer. PvP is no fun unless you want to integrate into a large aggressive tribe and crush other people.
But for the people that just want to tame and ride dinos, explore, build, socialize, and have an experience that isn't entirely dependent on competition, Pve is the way to go. When I first started playing, in server 335 (What used to be an extremely welcoming server filled with tons of nice people that wanted nothing more than to help others) I said, like ost others, "I'm new, what should I expect?" Seconds later a leader of the largest tribe appeared from nowhere on a huge beautiful flying beast, what i later learned was a Wyvern. He offered me a tour of the map. As I crouched on the back of the dragon scared out of my wits that I would slip off, miles above the ground, a feeling of wonder that I hadn't experienced in years washed over me. It was amazing. I looked across the map, saw all the different areas, saw scattered settlements, saw a huge♥♥♥♥♥bronto-looking creature that was so large I could see it even from all the way across the map. Everything was so damn big and it seemed like there was endless possibilities.
Eventually this same man led me to a nice clearing where not a lot of people had built, a rare sight. He helped me by gathering wood, giving me an extremely useful Stegosaurus, and providing a few spiked walls to protect it while I was offline. From that point on I was logging in every day, having an amazing experience socializing and sharing stories and having amazing amounts of fun. Everything I did was a new, magical experience. My first dodo, my first dilo, my first raptor, my first trike, my first bary--and oh lord, my first Ptera, Jasper. Grinding until I was high enough to make her a saddle, then flying straight up and watching my tiny little house disappear beneath me. The whole world was available to me, It honestly made the game. Everyone in the chat was congratulating me, it was one of the best feelings I've ever had in an online game in my life.
Then, I logged in one day, and every dino I owned was dead. My securely walled off pen was now empty, sides for a single  armadillo that was covered head to toe in blood. I checked my logs, and a carnotaurus and theri had somehow glitched through the walls of my pen and killed everything. Some other players suspected someone was after me.
Shortly after I had regained all of my lost dinosaurs, I logged in to a Titan (The largest and most dangerous dinosaur in the game) in my pen. My dinosaurs were all on passive, so it hadn't killed any of them. The man with the wyvern came and, over the course of 15 minutes, lead it away from the settlements and killed it. Tomorrow, it happened again. Titan in my pen. The next day, again. It was soon discovered that someone was after me. I logged in one day to all of my dinosaurs dead once again, despite my secure pen, and that's when I gave in and quit the game. You win, Wise.
This game broke my heart. I considered coming back, only to find that the recent updates were planning on screwing over PvE servers. The devs began cutting the game out so that only large competitive, pre-existing and long-lasted tribes can have fun. Extremely nerfing the speed of flyers, one of my favorite features of the game, so using them to travel is now near-impossible. And Wyverns, one of the most difficult things to get in the game? Their most useful aspects were nerfed. Now they're obsolete. Hundreds of hours of work and sleepless nights gone to waste.
When I came back, the kind people were gone. The server was filling up with competitive ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s who were bent on capitalizing the server and blocking off resources. I can't find it in me to come back. The title music causes me emotional pain now.
So my final verdict, do not buy this game in it's current state. Maybe someday the devs will realize that a huge portion of their playerbase is PvE, that the actual point of the game is being ruined by the idea of mass producing dinosaurs. Things that were once rare and wonderous are now in huge supply. The value of dinosaurs is dropping. There is no longer any reward for doing anything in this game.
It honestly hurts so much to look back on all the good memories i had in this game. It seems like that's how most early access games go. It's good until it's not. It's fun until the devs decide to change it. The game they are going for is no longer what is advertised. You will be spending more time fighting with other people, fruitlessly trying to make your base less vulnerable to trolls, trying to make any sort of progress only to have it stomped out by people who dedicate literally their entire lives to maintaining power. The game is not about fun anymore. It's about power. Everything is about power.
This game will hurt you. Do yourself a favor and avoid it at all costs, unless you're one of those people that only want to play it to crush other people and make them regret buying the game, like Wise and the devs have done to me.

Ok, I rarely do reviews for games, but I want to comment on some of the issues people have been posting. Cause i honestly enjoy this game a lot.
TL;DR: A fun game that admittedly might feel grindy at times; but feels much more complete than many other early access games out there. Though do be prepared to die a LOT the first few times (from dinos), its part of the experience.

1. Poor performance: while i do agree that this game could be a lag central for low end PCs, me and my family play ark all the time, and i have a mid range PC and most of my family have lower end of mid range and we can all run it with very little problems, the game has many options to cut out some stuff that might be causing lag.
.: to be honest none of us have run into many (if any) bugs or problems. The only thing i had happen is once i thought i the server had deleted two of my dinos but after checking the logs (yes the game keeps a log of things that happen pertaining to you that you can check) i found out they were killed by a rampaging rex (which the rest of my dinos killed [yes rexes are not invincible killing machines]).
3. Server antics: this is one where you kinda hve the hit or miss experience. We were on a fairly chill pvp server (yes those exist). Even when i died and spawned inside someones base and couldnt get out, someone from the tribe came and opened the doors for me. I understand not every server is like this, but the understood rule on that server was "dont be a jerk to us, and we wont be a jerk to you" (this was also an official server). Now that is probably not the majority of pvp servers out there (cause lets face it, for some reson most people like to be jerks online). Which brings me to my next point: there is a single player survival mode. Dont like dealing with people, play single player.
4. Paid DLC: yeah i kinda gotta agree with this one i guess, a game should not be releasing paid dlc while still in alpha phase, but to be fair, the dlc is right on par with the other map the game has (The Island) and is made to be much tougher (it IS a desert). I cant comment much more on that as i do not own SE (but my brother who has it says its awesome)
Now there are a couple things that may deter some people:
1. Resource gathering can be a hassle and feel a little grindy. Especially on the official servers, I was always lacking stone. Now in single player and unoffical servers all these things can be tweaked to fix that. Me and my family wanted to try The Center map (FREE dlc btw) so we started a private server just for us and tweaked the resource gathering values and the dino taming rates (which is my next point).
2. Taming dinos can be a long, annoying process: On the official servers some dinos (especially the larger ones) take a LOOOONG time to tame, even with a dinos "favorite food". So do be prepared to defend the area around your tame if you arent playing with increased rates. That being said, everything that may take a while or feel grindy and be tweaked and modified for single player and unofficial servers. On our server I have not fel like I have needed to grind for much of anything, resource collection is a part of any survival game and its hard to make it not feel grindy.
Overall I have enjoyed this game and recommend it to my friends to try, if playing online you do have to understand humanity just tends to be jerks a lot of times (even with these reviews). If you are worried about not being worth the price, wait for it to go on sale as it usually is fairly often from what ive seen. You'll appreciate it when you are standing with your held held high next to your favorite dino overlooking the island you have overcome.

I kind of wish there was an "eeeeh?" button rather than a simple yes or no for recommendation. My husband and I have literally hundreds of hours each playing this since day one, and initially, it was loads of fun playing on a private server I ran for the two of us. The problem is that this game is clearly not intended to be played on such a small scale.
With each new patch, the difficulty gets ramped up in ridiculous ways. The amount of resources you're required to gather to make even mid-tier items, without altering the game files to mess with multipliers, is insane. Nothing scales, so whether you're playing solo or with another person, the item costs are still treated as if you have a large tribe to help farm for them. It never used to be this way, and unless you want to edit the game, which I don't feel is something I should have to do in order to achieve balance, you're talking about many, many, MANY hours of grinding in order to progress.
It's not about "it's too hard". It's about a lack of scaling difficulty and an apparent expectation that you're either going to play with tons of people to share the load, or manipulate your game's files to account for it, which is something you'll wind up doing with every patch as things are added, nerfed, and tweaked. My husband and I are both adults with jobs... we don't need a game to be a job as well. Considering that when we bought this game it was perfectly playable on our smaller scope, I think it's a valid complaint that the game has altered so drastically over time. I can't even imagine what it must be like trying to play on a large multiplayer server where it would be impossible to compete against big tribes with time on their hands and the muscle to take what they want.
Ark is ultimately a very ambitious game with a lot going for it, but sadly after almost two years, it's asking for a lot more than I can give it.

The goal of this ticket is to bring WildCard's attention into "Lost Character" issue and to warn other players about the issue.
There's still a bug that may completely delete your character during a cross-ark travel from one official server to another.
This is a very critical bug, during last Amazon AWS outage many players suffered from this problem. While Amazon fixed all the problems, WildCard did not and there are still many such cases occuring on a daily basis.
Considering that this game is still in EarlyAccess the bug itslef is understandable.
However, this entire game is built around your character. Following things are bound to your character:
- Imprints
- TekGrams
- Experience
- Hair / Beard Styles
- Tribe participations
- Personal buildings
- Personal dinos
And when you lose your survivor you also lose everything mentioned above.
There is no in-game option or anything depending from player to fight this. When this issue happens you're helpless and the only thing you can do is to write a Support Ticket seeking for help.
Since the amount of tickets is huge compared to the amount of Game Moderators your ticket will take at least few days until you get a response.
Currently the only support GMs offer is to add some experience to a new survivor. You will get back your level (Experience) but everything else from the above list will be gone. If you're lucky enough to be in a tribe you may also keep Personal buildings/dinos but all your imprints will stop working since they're associated to a different survivor (the one you lost).
Such a "support" could be helpful for some cases. If your survivor didn't progress much then the added experience will most likely return you to the point you were.
However when it comes to survivors with many in-game hours this does NOT help at all and it does NOT provide any support.
First of all, if you spent many hours (4000 hours in my case) in this game then you are familiar with all the mechanics and gaining experience is not a problem. We had a friend joining us on Scorched Earth (DLC map), he leveled from lvl 1 to lvl 72 in one day. You can level to lvl 100 in a week, or maybe even in less time.
The most important thing is the Sample # (Charated ID), it's the only identity you have. It's a number indicating your ID, it is visible in your inventory when you move mouse over your implant.
This number defines which dinos are associated to your character. And for someone who achieved 100% imprinting on such dinos as:
- Giganotosaurus (11 days without proper sleep)
- Quetzal (7 days without proper sleep)
- Rex / Wyvern / etc (4 days without proper sleep)
These dinos are the most valuable thing in the game. Something which current WC Support will not return to you.
Restoring such dinos (i.e. growing and imprinting new dinos from zero) will take huge amount of time (maybe months).
On long-term this bug needs to be fixed, let's hope that at the game release it will be.
On short-term they can at least return player's Sample # (Characted ID). It's just a number and editting this number should not be that hard.
If this is because GMs do not have corresponding console command available then it needs to be implemented.
In my case the character had highest possible level for the moment, all current TekGrams unlocked, had custom hairstyle from St. Valentine's event and many 100% imprinted dinos.

After few days my ticket got a response with a template text. It was pretty much suggesting to create a new survivor and GM will add experience to it.
After few attempts to explain to the GM that I don't need any experience, all I want is my ID got this answer:
This doesn't really make sense, if I have to create a new survivor with new ID what GM means by "your survivor"? It's gone, isn't it?

My feelings towards Ark are mixed, but overall I like this game and it's going to be one I play for years to come. Which is great for people like me who can't afford many games. It's certainly engaging enough to play for that long, but there are some problems.
There are some things that need to be fixed here, but the devs update the game frequently, and they do try and fix the problems. If you play, you'll have a bit of an irritating time getting the game to run smoothly. This is definitely a game for people who like gameplay over graphics because in its current state playing with higher graphical settings turns it into a major resource hog. I've had the game crash due to filling up all 16 GB of available ram when running the game and a private server. That shouldn't happen, but hey, the game’s not finished yet and tonight's patch says it's a performance fix, maybe it will fix it. The last one fixed the server’s memory leak issue.
Stick things on the medium settings and even my old 750 Ti can get the job done. The game looks good even without everything set to ultra.
Now, as for Official Servers... HA! Yeah, no, don't. At all. Not for one second. PvE sucks because everyone is an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and will build spawn traps to lock you inside the areas you spawn in, preventing anyone from getting to play on that server. PvP sucks because at the moment, all official servers allow for character, dino, and item transfers so dudes from other official servers can and do pop in on the back of a dragon just to hunt down noobs, which forces everyone on a server to kill newcomers on sight.
All that said...
This game is fun as hell when you have a friend to play it with. It's a true community based survival game. You NEED others help to be more than a naked hobo punching trees. On a private server, or an unofficial server with a community who has disabled player transfers, you'll find a really cool and fun game you could sink years into if you liked. THere's no possibility for casual gamers to play this, which is great! It's designed for people like me who liked actually hard games you have to sink weeks into. Ark is to gaming what a steak dinner is to food.
Get some friends, get the Ark Server Manager program, set up a private server on your rig, customize it so the dinos do a bit less damage than the vanilla settings, disable Troodons from spawning because my god are those things broken and in need of a major nerfing, up the harvest values just a little, and then have fun building a village and surviving together. It beats the hell out of just sitting around watching youtube.
This games takes a lot of time to do anything. Which is great! That ♥♥♥♥♥♥ little thatch hut you make becomes something you appreciate, and the game will make you actually FEEL emotion when a dino decides to wreck your house because you didn’t know how to defend it yet.
Name one other game which can go from stone age tools to having a laser fight with cybernetically augmented T-Rexes. You can’t? Damn right you can’t! Now go buy Ark.

I think this is probably one of the best games I have ever played!  It has updates that add new content almost every time, or every other time.  I started playing this game around the middle of 2014 and then got off for a while, and a ton has changed!  The only thing that annoys me is when they release a new primed version of a Warframe (primed Warframe is an improved version of the original), they tend to... well... Make it a bit too hard to obtain (Saryn Prime).  Other than that I have nothing but good things to say about this game.  The trading system is, for the most part reasonable, and if it does not seem reasonable that's where Warframe Wiki comes in handy, and the trade channel is used to obtain strictly prime Warframe parts (head, systems, and chassis) and when I say "strictly" I mean no Volt parts, Excalibur parts, or Mag parts, (those Waframe names I just listed are the ones you can choose to start out with) only primed versions.  As I was saying... you can also trade for primed companion parts, and prime parts for Platinum.  Another fun aspect of this game is the weapon mods.  They can give a whole new vibe to your once bland weapon.  For example, I have a bow... its name is Dread.  He was very OP, and its owner did not think it could get any better till he equipped the Thunderbolt mod to it (Thunderbolt is a mod that if maxed has a 30% chance to explode on impact).  Ok, that's where I'm going to wrap up this review, if this review helped... well I'm glad!  Lol, well go ahead and send me a friend request if you get the game, and I'll be happy to help you if you've got any questions or need help with anything.

I originally posted a review for this game at 170 hours of playtime. Since then, I've hit 290 and I intend to go on and on and on.
This game is honestly incredible. Everytime I worry I might get bored, brand new content is thrown in, including amazing dinosaurs, helpful items, and brand new dangers and goals. Yes, it is early access, but that is the beauty of having it now. I have so much time to explore and learn this game inside out. And at 290 hours I STILL haven't learned everything there is. Heck, I JUST started breeding and understanding that system!
At 170 hours my largest complaint was bugs. At 290 hours I have seen so many things fixed and improved that I absolutely retract that. Yes, there are still bugs. It's not completed, there WILL be, but the fact that they have fixed so many things really says something for the dedication to the early access mode. They aren't just finishing the game, they're making sure it's completely playable to their community NOW, even for small things.
The best thing I can say for a new ARK player is to give it time. You're GOING to die when you first start. You're gonna walk up to a dinosaur, not realizing that it's aggressive, and get your face mauled. It's just the way of ARK life. I can't tell you how many times I died at first, but as I learned more and more about the environment and the game I became a true in-game survivor. It's a learning curve, and you just need to realize that instead of throwing your keyboard the first time you or one of your dinosaurs die.
There's so much that this game offers. The combat for aggressive players, the building for creative players, and the hunting and gathering for the players who are quest and purpose driven. There are BOSS DINOSAURS LIKE. Wow. That's a good time. I haven't even FOUGHT one yet.
Don't worry though, the allosaurus army is coming along.

So after playing this game, uh, a few times I can definitely say that that this is worth playing.  This game is a fresh and fun take on the many survival games out there.  Only it does it with one very cool and unique twist: MOTHATRUCKIN' DINOS (and other prehistoric creatures just as terrifying)!! :-D
From a gameplay standpoint, the game can be--and IS--fun and challenging.  It puts you as a hapless survivor into the wild somewhere on either the default Island map, the amazing The Center map, or (if you begrudgingly bought the expansion pack of much controversy) the Scorched Earth desert map.  From here, your job is to survive, gaining experience through battling the many wild creatures cohabiting this hostile map with you and through crafting various items.  You can build, craft, hunt, gather, tame, and even go on a little adventure here and there for those REALLY precious resources.  Playing with friends doubles the enjoyment (unless your friends are just a bag of♥♥♥♥♥♥♥  If so, I recommend a nice bola of betrayal to the back, a jab with an electric prod, and then stealing their blood for helpful bloodpacks).
It's a nice balance for both PVP and PVE lovers.  The official servers are pretty well maintained, but for those not really looking to get their♥♥♥♥♥♥stomped in every few days and/or restarting from scratch often, you will find several great unofficial servers with a less competitive player base.  If you are the stomp-er, you can also find several nice PVP servers that will cater to your sadistic needs as well.  The mod community is where this game really comes to life.  The support for the mods is really impressive and the sheer variety available can really shake the game up if you grow bored of the vanilla game.
For an EA game, I am really impressed by the amount of content that you get for $30.  It can be buggy at times and in some more infuriating instances, you end up losing precious resources to stupid things like faulty dino AI or poor map generation (or, my personal favorite, falling through the ground).  The optimization still needs some work, but the team appears to be improving it with each update.  It doesn't deserve the hate it drew after releasing Scorched Earth (which to me was kind of a 'meh' expansion pack, but it did add some cool little things.  JERBOAS <3 ).
Don't let the Mixed rating deter you.  This game is worth trying.  Just be prepared for falling for that first precious dino you tamed...only for it to die in the worst, most violent way protecting you. (RIP Polly the Parasaur.  Know that the raptor ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is now a glove, my friend.  The bloodiest of gloves. T-T)

1) Ark can take up alot of time but it doesn't have too
If you are a actual person and have you know one of those things called a life well then you will probably not be playing the for 16 hours a day. Out of the reviews I have seen they say that you need to spend your entire life on the game. While this can be true if you decide to play on official servers where the gathering rate is rediculous and you need to play all the time to actually protect the cheap base you built. But if you don't have that amount of time well then there are a few options. You can simply play on a PvE server where no one can raid you (even though they might bring a wild dino and your defenses agro it but this is easily avoidable by not putting up defenses on the outside). The other option is playing on a unofficial pvp server that has a increased gathering rate. Even though you can still get raided the gathering rates are increased so that you can easily get defense up and have some kind of chance.
2) Ark is not full of bugs...
Ark is not full of alot of bugs. It is a alpha game so yes it has some flaws but it is not game breaking and can be easily avoidable along with easily being fixed. Also these bugs don't last long since the devs put out updates all the time fixing stuff and adding stuff like new dinos and items. This means that a majority of the time (if playing on a modded server this doesn't count since the mods are at fault but as long as they are popular mod like structures + then it will be fixed fast) all bugs are not noticed and will be fixed faster then you even realize they are there
3) The game eats pc power...
I will be honest this game will take that computer that you spent 1000$ and it will give it a run for it's money... But their are different launch settings that will help with that. I am using a gtx 960 4 gb ssc, 16gb of ram, and AMD A8-7650k Radeon R7 and I have to run the game in low settings for a 60 fps gameplay. Had to redo my earlier review due to it no longer being true.
The game is still good for the casual player that wants ot play with a few buddies but any competetive, end-game seeking player is SOL.
End-game PVP is non-existant. PVP gear doesn't exist, none of your mods/weapons can be taken into pvp at all. So with PVP no longer an option we're left with end-game PVE. Let's talk about that.
First of all, with PVP so♥♥♥♥♥♥ we know PVE is all the game has going for it. But is their enough unique satisfying content at the highest level to hold a competetive PVMer? Not even close.
Most if not all bosses are extremely easy after you're geared out with all primes and good mods. And the ones that require a team to fight, only do so because of some gimmicky game mechanic.

Really it can be summed up in one question. Have you played the game for a few hours?  Well then you're pretty much already out of unique content.
Of course there is unique content, just not nearly enough of it. It's all, go here kill these, go here survive for x amount of rounds, go here and capture this guy.
Over and over and over again the same♥♥♥♥♥♥different day gameplay. It's fun for awhile until you see behind the veil. That in reality you're just grinding for nothing.
In other MMo's you're grinding for a goal, not JUST to get another prime part. There's more than the grind, when the grind ends you move to the next thing. Whether you like PVP or PVM is your thing, just know you'll find neither with this game that will satisfy none but the casual saturday with friends.

Where do I even begin? This game is quite honestly one of the best games ever made and the fact that it's free to play blows me away. So first up the selection of warframes is quite astounding, since there is pretty much something for everyone near guanteed. You have 4 elemental warframes where one Zephr can do air attacks, while another: Atlas uses the very earth to tear the opponents to shreads, then there's Amber which can set the entire place on fire which is incredible. Lastly there is Hydroid which can summon a kraken to eat your opponents and drown your enemies.
There are mods which are a basic must, as once your Warframe reachs the level cap you then need good quality mods to really let loose that hidden power of the Tenno. Mods for health, energy, stance mods for weapons, aura mods for your warframe and the list go's on.
You have different missions such as Interception, (wait till you do Ceres Draco oh ho ho you'll wish you hadn't young Tenno) as well as Capture missions where you simply find the target and take them down. Then we have a couple of typical favourites Survival and Defense which are always popular for xp leveling.
We then have the superb stuff: The Orocin VOID & Orocin Derelict which is where you can get some very good quality mods as well as get the fantastic Golden Gods (my wording there actually just slightly better warframes and they look cooler :/), these are called intake breath: THE Prime Warframes OOOhhhh. What they do is have slightly better stats as well as better matched polarity's and they look Boss. As well as the mods and warframe prime parts you can get in the void you can also get some prime weapons which may well deal better damage not huge but decent.
I would then say all up game replay abilty is quite high as you always find new things to do and if you somehow stuggle to find things, there are always the story mode quests which are quite neat and interesting as well as this the game developers always add new content. There are also 8 person missions that can be unlocked as long as you meet the requirements, resource wise and such. That brings me to the next things you have resources of course where as you complete missions you will get rewards such as mods and these resources to craft new weapons and things such as gear as such. Each planet is unique as some planets might have completely different resources as well as drops.
I guess I would finish by saying this is a truly superb game and in today's market that means a lot, as some game developers forget the point of what it means to work in a area such as gaming. That is the fact that if your loving your job in that company and the fans/customers are loving what you do then I'd say that's a win, it by all means is never easy but if you care have that patience and time to learn what needs to be done then you will make a great employee that I am sure of.
It's free to play, the developers always add new content, there are main quest missions, there are plenty of things to work for such as: mods, Prime Warframes, Prime weapons, companions that help kill, customisation is very sweet as well for that true artist. It by all means is definately not pay to win as everything can be earned with actual hard work as well as team work. If your lazy or cheat then don't bother playing games. As these Developers Digital Extremes actually care and I know from where I have grown up that is a rare thing in today's society.

I think this is probably one of the best games I have ever played!  It has updates that add new content almost every time, or every other time.  I started playing this game around the middle of 2014 and then got off for a while, and a ton has changed!  The only thing that annoys me is when they release a new primed version of a Warframe (primed Warframe is an improved version of the original), they tend to... well... Make it a bit too hard to obtain (Saryn Prime).  Other than that I have nothing but good things to say about this game.  The trading system is, for the most part reasonable, and if it does not seem reasonable that's where Warframe Wiki comes in handy, and the trade channel is used to obtain strictly prime Warframe parts (head, systems, and chassis) and when I say "strictly" I mean no Volt parts, Excalibur parts, or Mag parts, (those Waframe names I just listed are the ones you can choose to start out with) only primed versions.  As I was saying... you can also trade for primed companion parts, and prime parts for Platinum.  Another fun aspect of this game is the weapon mods.  They can give a whole new vibe to your once bland weapon.  For example, I have a bow... its name is Dread.  He was very OP, and its owner did not think it could get any better till he equipped the Thunderbolt mod to it (Thunderbolt is a mod that if maxed has a 30% chance to explode on impact).  Ok, that's where I'm going to wrap up this review, if this review helped... well I'm glad!  Lol, well go ahead and send me a friend request if you get the game, and I'll be happy to help you if you've got any questions or need help with anything.
Thanks!

I have been playing Ark for quite some time now and there is no doubt this game is addictive. The multiplayer experience with tribes is especially fun. However, this does not excuse the glaring issues that have been in the game since the beginning. Firstly, the glitches in the game are incredibly frustrating at times. For example, I have gotten stuck in a tree numerous times while trying to evade Troodons (one of the most annoying dinos in the game atm) and have to die numerous times trying to recover my gear. Though this may not be an issue for a high level player, noobs to the game may find this incredibly frustrating as I did. Another glitch is when your body falls through the map, potentially leading to all your rare ascendant gear to be lost forever. These are only a few of the glitches that exist in Ark. Another grievance is the issue of player transfers across official servers which allow mega tribes to move from server to server wiping everyone out. This is particularly infuriating as more often than not it is almost impossible to communicate with these tribes as they speak a different language and their messages appear as unintelligible boxes in the chat box. This makes negotiating peace impossible. Furthermore, on most official servers there is an omnipotent fear of being wiped at moment by an alpha due to crossing the line between being a noob tribe and a tribe worthy of being raided for resources. I could go on and on about the issues; the building mechanics are clunky (thought mods like s+ make it significantly better), dino AI is basic and stupid, disappearing  tamed dinos (which takes ages) etc etc. yet somehow the game still seems to be addictive. This is most likely due to the experience you get playing with your friends, building a base together, taming dinos and riding them, meeting other friendly people from the community, but the cruel unforgiving nature of Ark is what can make you throw your mouse at the monitor and take a break for a few days. There is nothing worse than having your super dinos that you careful bred suddenly disappear or your quetz (which takes forever to tame, I’m talking hours and hours) get stuck in a rock or another wild dino and get shredded into bits while you sit there helplessly mashing your keyboard and frantically throwing your mouse around trying to get it unstuck to no prevail.  I haven’t even mentioned the absolutely atrocious optimisation the game has at the moment which I hope Wildcard addresses soon (though with the launch of their new game Conan Exiles I feel like it might be a while before they make some serious improvements). Yet somehow, despite all this, the game still seems to suck you in with its beautiful scenery, detailed dinos, and the enjoyment you get from exploring the map with your friends. As to whether you should buy this game right now? I’d probably wait a bit until it is fully released.  By then…hopefully… many of these issues will be fixed. :)

Warframe: An Average Joe's Tale
Warframe is a different breed of game. It's genre and characteristics are difficult to define, it's hardly a bad game and nearly a great game.
First off, Warframe is not bad in the sense you might think of at the sight of a "not recommended" review. It's time. The game demands time from you. You can do everything without paying for the game. But you will spend hours and hours of your life working towards a digital item.  That you could've bought for 20 bucks. And if grinding is the only time grabber, then let me introduce the Kubrow. It's a kanine inspired creature. It's aggressive look but friendly temperament is the wonderful detail that makes you want one. But if you don't play at least every week it will die. You will mourn it for hours, thinking "what did I do wrong". And then you'll realize, that owning a pet in Warframe is like owning a tamagatchi, if you don't cater to the videogame, you're going to lose it. If you like being able to come back to a game at anytime and still feel satisfied with it, then you won't like Warframe.
Now, I love Warframe. It's got a beautiful art style. It has the fast pace that a lot of people enjoy in games, it is detailed in every way. It compares in greatness to The Elder Scrolls series, the Fallout Series, even to the greatness of an entire console like the Nintendo 64. All powerful and memorable experiences. I would love to recommend this game but the pure obsession and time you have to pour into this game entirely negates the entertainment value.
And sure I'm just some random steam user who dislikes a single aspect of this game, but I've easily spent $200 in game on inventory spaces and character props and the like.  And I regret every dollar spent.

2nd March 2017
Due to a duplication glitch and lack of fail-safe on the official servers transfer facility (Amazon was down), all official servers were rolled back two days. This isn't the first time this has happened in the last 6 months. What do the developers do to compensate? The standard evolution weekend rates and then complete silence with all the hatred and rage they're getting on the forum and Twitter. This is unacceptable for such a situation that has happened more than once now. Many players have lost their base or some of it, high quality items or blueprints, important tames or breeds (breeds take ages and are a real time sink on official servers even with 1.5x rates temporarily) and last of all their sanity and patience with this game.
Last month the developers also nerfed (item stat clamped) high quality saddles and blueprints relating to a fishing rod exploit that was fixed many months ago while leaving the blueprints and items already gained from that exploit around official servers for many months after. They nerfed them to the point that those legitimate ones were badly affected too, from raptor claus, caves and legitimate fishing. Not too long afterwards they increase the clamp but they don't fix the blueprints and items already wrongly affected and worst of all cost just as much!
Due to this I'm revising the developer communication rating to 1/10 now, some friends and many people appear to be quitting the game now due to all of this.
I hate to leave a negative review but sadly it's justified, I was planning to leave a review after the game was finished (if that happens). I'll start with the negative points first and then move on to the positive points. If things change then I'll change my review accordingly.
Official server guidelines, other than cheating and exploiting, seem to mean nothing. GM's just say they're going to investigate a reported problem, in my case my tribe has reported a Chinese tribe on an official SE PvE server as pillaring our base in, luring rock elementals to our base which has been destroyed twice so far, and pillaring most of the map as well as doing the same to other bases. The GM tells my tribe member it will be investigated but nothing happens, and due to 'player privacy' they can't say anything about the progress of the investigation. Sounds like an excuse if you ask me. Other people on the forum have had similar experiences. My advice is to find a good unofficial server, one with admin command logging enabled especially. If you do go on official PvE then try to avoid setting up permanently on Scorched Earth as that's where the griefing commonly occurs thanks to rock elementals.
Updates are usually late, communication is sometimes non-existent or last minute, or some content is often removed from a planned update just when it's about to be released. It would be better to surprise the community in my opinion rather than provide a patch note with an exact date, albeit ETA. A classic one that has been in the further out section for a long time has been dynamic length bridges, a workshop mod however has achieved this a long time ago.
The latest issue that's stirred up a lot of complaints on the forum at the time of writing this review is with a tribe tamed animal limit being applied to official servers (PC), with no consideration about other methods previously suggested by the community and the fact that this tribe limit is easy to workaround. I'd hope some day this is improved upon however.
The only reason I'm rating it 3 out of 10 is because there have been a few occasions where they've had better communication and interaction with the community, such as when they fixed the lack of wildlife spawns not too long ago, and some stress testing for performance data from the experimental no tame servers.
Plenty to do! Plenty of wildlife, structures, and content to explore as a whole. Enough said. I would however like to see structures improved a little bit, and by that I mean having 2x2 or even 4x4 tiles, such as a 2x2 wall, or a 4x4 floor. This would greatly help reduce the number of structures on the server and help improve server performance as a result.
It used to be a time sink but the official default rates were doubled in December 2016 which has helped a lot. However, this is only for XP, taming animals and harvesting resources. I would like to see improvements to the breeding rates eventually as well.
Griefing on some official servers can be quite an issue due to the lack of moderation assistance from official support. Events thus far haven't been great on PvE. Halloween on 'the center' map was unsupported in 2016 even though it's an official DLC map (only maintained by one person). The Christmas event in 2016 wasn't festive or fun with the constant competition, bickering and fighting between players to who got to the raptor claus drop first. Valentines event in 2017 was a bit of a flop too with the recent timer optimisations presumably causing a bug when animals should eat, therefore some babies died. Easter is next but last year PvE players couldn't carry bunnydodos to a cage to get special Easter eggs (where PvP could), so I'm expecting the event this year to equally be a disappointment.
Workshop mods add to the game, which allows for new ideas, I haven't explored this much yet though.
Bear in mind it's early access and we're slowly getting to the phase where optimisations are beginning to be done now. The performance of the game is slowly improving over time, but at the moment you will still need a fairly good PC to be able to use the 'high' settings. If you're playing online on a busy server then expect a lag spike every so often when the server does a save.
I'd like to recommend the game but unless official support actually means something to those who bought the game then I can't say I recommend it. If you don't need official support and just plan on going unofficial or single player then by all means try ARK, it has plenty to offer.

Hey Steam brothers and sisters!  I am writing this review with over 1700 hours in playing PVE on servers 327 (island) and 760 (scorched earth).   I started playing this 5 months ago with a friend, and man do I have some epic stories.  The game was a wonder to figure out and learn.  Yes it has bugs even still and there are many quality of life fixes that are being completely ignored in favor of new dinos and features being rolled out.  But, we still soldiered on.  This game takes a TON of work to get anywhere near the "end content"  and anywhere along the way you can be griefed by not only the game mechanics but by other players.  Just a few days before the Valentines event started, we hatched 20 wyvern eggs on server 760.  Three of us took shifts raising these 20.  Why 20 you ask?  Well, it's just as easy to raise 20 over four days as it is to raise 1.  And having had wyverns dissapear, getting dc'd mid fight and losing them, you start to go for overkill when you raise so that you are not as devestated when you get "ark'ed".
Well boys and girls, there is another enemy you have to worry about now on PVE.  Griefers.  While raising an army of Rex's on 327 (island) server, someone on 760 (could have been from another server, don't know really)  drug a rock golem from somewhere around the Scar (wyvern trench)  all the way to the map barrier where our raising building stood.  They then used a high health wyvern or golem to tank this wild golem to break down our behemouth door (per the tribe log) and then kited a fire and poison wyvern inside to kill 17 wyverns we had just raised.  Three of them had been taken over to the island server just a day or two before.  These same people also attacked at least two other bases neaer us, and they also attacked four bases in the middle of the map (one was ours as well).  If it were not for the two Gigas with 260+ melee we had parked at the base in the middle of the map, im sure we would have lost everything there as well.  Wild Card's official response to this PVE griefing is "It is working as intended".
We chose to play PVE in this game for many reasons.  We normally play PVP on most every game, but in Ark we just wanted to focus on gameplay and the experience/breeding aspect without the worry of raiders and offline raiders.  I'm sure there are some snarky comments that people could make about our situation, but at the end of the day some jerks decided to erase hours and days of work while we were not there to defend said work.
My advice to those who are thinking of playing this game is this.  Decide what you want out of it before you start.  If you just want to mess around, then I suggest you play un-official servers that have an acutal admin.  I've heard that un-official servers had experienced admin abuse on PVP servers, so I would stick to PVE.  Second, if you aspire to reach end game content you either need to be unemployed or you need at least 4-6 tribe members who are able to be online everyday.  Third, do not expect Wild Card to do anything.  About 3 months ago they changed all their reponses to trouble tickects to an automated script that basically tells you to they aren't doing anything about it.
It is a shame that this game is going on it's third year in early access and that they have been allowed to push out a DLC for more money, push out new content that is broken without fixing core mechanics that are still broken.  And that leads this review to the lag and disconnnects.  The lag on island servers and constant disconnects when more than 10 people are online has gotten out of control since early December of last year.  Filing a trouble ticket does nothing.  Losing things you are taming, babies you just hatched and mounts you were on when you get lagged out or dc'd erases hours of work put into the game.
Well I hope this gives some insight as to my experience with this game.  I have no intention to stop playing it, but I will not be pouring as much time into it as I have already.  It is a highly time consuming game and it will raw dog you every chance it gets.

My review of ARK:
As far as games go an early access game such a ARK: Survival Evolved it is a decent game, as it is updated I am finding more and more features that I absolutely love about it so here are my Pros list for this game.
Pros; Decent Character customization, not into its full potential I would say but on the more positive side. Leveling up and Engrams seem to becoming more balanced and as the game Evolves it seems that something new is added every so often including saddles for certain Dinos which I am sure many love this fact as much as I do. During Solo plays of the game it is quite the challenge and something that many gamers adore, other gamers find it not as rewarding. The tribe aspect is amazing and the things you can achieve seem to be endless.
Cons; um like I said this is still early access, so I find myself attempting to keep dinos pinned up and out of the way and they tend to GLITCH into the foundation, or inside of a wall, so rebuilding the structure that took so much in the way of time and supplies is a must if it is a Dino, that was hard to Level, Tame or even hatch. Another con I have found is sometimes Dinos have unrealistic Reach when you are on a Flyer more than twenty or so feet off the ground, unless the thing chasing you can jump or is huge, how can it hit you? Now onto a specific Dino type con The kitties throughout ARK seem to be under powered, and sometimes out right stupid yet easy to be killed once tamed. (This may or may not be something I am doing wrong after taming but I thought I should say it either way.)
SYSTEM ISSUES: I have yet to have issues with running ARK, thought unlike many users I do have a Self-built PC  with a Processor over 3.4, Ram of 8, Not only do I run three screens while playing, My BIOS are divided to run certain things off my Motherboard Video Graphics and other things off of my High end Video card. Though I have had a tribe mate who had to turn of certain things because either his Video card or his sound card at times could not handle all the game had to offer. On one occasion the Video card itself crashed. So it is a bit more demanding than other games I have come to enjoy but I love it non the less.
I am sure with more updates soon to be released I will find more things that I love or Hate about ARK but for now I will just Enjoy the work and time I have put into the game and understand that it is Early Access.

TL;DR at the bottom.
Main features at the bottom before TL;DR
Cons:
1. Pretty bad tutorial.
The tutorial simply guides you through basic combat, and nothing more. The more complicated mechanics such as mods and damage types are barely touched on. These two main mechanics are crucial in-game, and due to the lack of a tutorial for it, I've encountered far too many new players who are clueless. You will have to google for a crap ton of information. (Bless the wiki page)
2. Pay-4-Convenience.
If you're rich, you get through majority of the game faster. But it is NOT Pay-2-Win. Everything is obtainable, and the grind isn't insane unless RNGesus hates you. A person who paid money and a free-to-play player will end up with the exact same gear. Essentially, you buy time in this game, and nothing more.
3. Limited areas to play in.
It's not open-world. Instances have a certain tileset for each planet. It randomizes, but generally remains the same. There are, of course, new tilesets added in certain updates.
4. It's easy to get burnt out.
By burnt out, I mean that you'll probably play the game on and off when you first start. This is due to the long waiting times for crafting new items, which are the only way you can get new items on your own. That tied with the daily trade limit makes it difficult to play for several hours straight. But once you've attained a fair amount of items, getting burnt out becomes few and far between.
5. You're free to do what you want.
This can't be a bad thing, right?  But it is for those who want some form of direction in a game.  I initially found it really hard to stick to playing this game. I love every aspect of it, but having no actual goal is painful. This game is recommended for those who like loot-based games like Diablo 3.
Pros:
1. Everything is obtainable if you play the game. (With the exception of the Founders Pack)
Yeah, play the game and get everything. Simple as that. Wanna get something that is no longer available? Trade.
2. Fantastic Graphics on low-end PCs
I'm able to run this on a PC with only 2GB of RAM and an Intel Graphics card. I've upgraded since then, but it runs at a smooth 30 FPS on that disgusting old rig.
3. Gameplay.
Gameplay doesn't get dull, unless you're one of those cancerous people who plays Ash-hole. Fast paced, and both melee-only and ranged-only builds are viable.
4. The Dev team.
It's clear that the Warframe dev team cares about the game and does not try to turn it into a cash-grab. New expansion? Free. New item being released? Don't need to fork up any money. New mission? Do the pre-reqs and gain access to it. Entirely new mechanic that could possibly act as DLC? FREEEEE.
5. Community.
You will rarely ever encounter any cancer players. Why? Because Warframe heavily relies on working with others. If you're a horrible person to group with, you'll build up a bad rep and eventually no one will group with you. The downsides of being an♥♥♥♥♥are so huge, that if Kanye played this game, you'd think he's Oprah or Ellen or one of those nice people that everyone likes.
Features
+ A lot of 'Warframes' which act as classes (extremely flexible)
+ Detailed mechanics (modding, damage 2.0)
+ Large amount of viable weapons (majority are extremely different from each, all are able to be molded to endgame)
+ Fantastic graphics (recently got a revamp with better smoke and fire physics)
+ Incredibly optimized (expect smooth framerates throughout)
+ Plenty of customization and cosmetics (you will rarely find another person that looks exactly like you)
- Dull movement system (despite having a parkour system, you'll be rolling/bullet jumping everywhere. This is starting to change with the added Orokin Moon Tileset)
- Limited areas to play in
- Repetitive (very limited number of mission types)
- PvP is pointless (you don't get much other than cosmetics)
- Ridiculously grindy
- A lot of flukes (there are certain builds that do all the work by pressing A SINGLE BUTTON. I kid you not. Check out 'Warframe draco runs' on youtube.)
- Limited trades each day (tallies with your Mastery Rank, which you can increase by leveling items)
- Limited inventory (appears as a cash grab quite early on, but you can earn Platinum through trading)
- Certain items are obtainable at certain times (2 main items; orokin catalyst and orokin reactor. They are untradable, and I've personally wasted over 400 Platinum on the market buying them because I missed an alert that was only available for 1 HOUR. The recipe that can be bought on the market is stupid)
TLDR;
It's free, but can appear as P2W.
You can obtain everything if you spend time and effort.
Play if you like loot-based games.
Expect to wait. A lot.
Community is awesome.
Devs are awesome with constant updates and hotfixes.

Free to play games are usually shunned among alot of gamers, often written off as nothing but a trap hoping to make the player pay even more than they normally would. And it's undeniable, there are some really big names out there which give this particular part of the industry a pretty bad name. When done right though, it can be the poor mans way to gaming.
Warframe is a game that does this better than many others. First off, Platinum(the games special currency) can be used for these following purpouses:
-Speed up crafting
-Buying weapons and warframes instantly withough having to get the materials
-Buying cosmetics
-Trading with other players
-Buying slots for warframes and weapons
None of these provide an unfair advantage in the end. Players have the same potential for being good at the game no matter how much or little they pay. They simply cut down on grinding and waiting. Also the only purchase you'll ever need to make is more slots which are super cheap anyway. Note the fact that you can trade it with other players. This of course means you can earn Platinum without paying a cent as long as you know what to do.
But what about the game itself then? Well...
Warframe is an action-RPG shooter hybrid where you play as magical space ninjas with sparkly superpowers. The sole purpouse of the game is to shoot stuff so that you can get resources and blueprints so you can shoot stuff harder and get more resources and blueprints. You also have a quite robust parkour system at your disposal. It's not quite Mirrors Edge but it works and it brings alot more style and excitement to battles.
The game revolves around crafting and buying new warframes and weapons. Weapons can be all different kinds of rifles, launchers, laser miniguns etc. while melee weapons range from dinky knives to greatswords bigger than its user. Warframes on the other hand are basically different characters. Each warframe has a set of stats and four abilities.
Pros:
-Parkour system is fun and makes the game feel uique from other shooters
-Lots of lore to explore for those who are interested
-Always satisfying to try out a new frame or weapon
-Good f2p model
-Tons of gameplay hours to be lost here
-Generally polite and helpful community. Of course a-holes are to be expected here and there
Cons:
-Grinding can sometimes get tedious if RNGsus is not on your side

Warframe: An Average Joe's Tale
Warframe is a different breed of game. It's genre and characteristics are difficult to define, it's hardly a bad game and nearly a great game.
First off, Warframe is not bad in the sense you might think of at the sight of a "not recommended" review. It's time. The game demands time from you. You can do everything without paying for the game. But you will spend hours and hours of your life working towards a digital item.  That you could've bought for 20 bucks. And if grinding is the only time grabber, then let me introduce the Kubrow. It's a kanine inspired creature. It's aggressive look but friendly temperament is the wonderful detail that makes you want one. But if you don't play at least every week it will die. You will mourn it for hours, thinking "what did I do wrong". And then you'll realize, that owning a pet in Warframe is like owning a tamagatchi, if you don't cater to the videogame, you're going to lose it. If you like being able to come back to a game at anytime and still feel satisfied with it, then you won't like Warframe.
Now, I love Warframe. It's got a beautiful art style. It has the fast pace that a lot of people enjoy in games, it is detailed in every way. It compares in greatness to The Elder Scrolls series, the Fallout Series, even to the greatness of an entire console like the Nintendo 64. All powerful and memorable experiences. I would love to recommend this game but the pure obsession and time you have to pour into this game entirely negates the entertainment value.
And sure I'm just some random steam user who dislikes a single aspect of this game, but I've easily spent $200 in game on inventory spaces and character props and the like.  And I regret every dollar spent.

I think i've played ARK a little bit. At the very least enough to tell you that this is a great sandbox game and you could easily have hours and hours of fun in singleplayer or multiplayer.
Most of the negative reviews you'll see are people complaining about how the game is not longer for casuals or complaining about "alpha tribes" and honestly, those problems are very easily avoidable and they just put themselves through that. A bit of a info on what they mean:
~Alpha tribes are massive 20+ member tribes on PvP servers who, as anyone would expect a large tribe to do on a PvP server, take it over and give new players/smaller tribes no chance to do anything.
~If you plan on joining an offical PvP server alone or with very few friends, you can expect to basically get S**t on, as you would in any PvP game where you can have large groups.
Again, both of these are EASILY avoidable if you go to a non-offical server, run by other people JUST LIKE YOU, who will set rules to prevent such things. Bam, the biggest complaint about this game from players gone. Just like that.
I run a PvE server, but i've played many an hour on these non-offical PvP servers and had a lot of fun and even made some friends. ARK is a great game for both PvP and PvE players. The only downfall currently I can note is that the devs seem to prioritize adding new dinos and features over fixing bugs that can be annoying. That said, they are extremely active, very friendly, and do fix bugs. I've had to update my server about 14 times this month alone from all hotfixes.
it's a great game and the negative reviews are extremely silly for the most part. If they talk about the game not being for casuals, alpha tribes, or the new tek system being game-breaking, just ignore it comepletely as they aren't game issues, but rather those people having issues they put on themselves.

You can either go in blind and try to stumble your way through or you can do a little research on the basics and spend more time actually enjoying the game.

It's finally time to write an ARK review.
I played the absolute♥♥♥♥♥♥out of ark, and loved it initially, but the big two things that have ruined it is its community and a lack of region locking.
There's a lot of content, gameplay is pretty good (for what the game is), and there really is a ton of things to do as far as time sinks.
But this really is the game: Time sinks. If you do not play singleplayer, you are required to log in at minimum daily, to perform upkeep on your base, turrets, feed your dinos, restock generators, etc etc. The list of daily tasks you have to complete to maintain a base is astonishing, which is fine in a clan; not fine as a solo player.
It requires a massive dedication of time.
But here comes the chinese:
LIke a disgusting plague of one-child law terror, the chinese have destroyed this game, on the official server side, and made it unplayable. Officials are no longer options for anyone not preestablished in a large clan. server hopping being added has destroyed server communities, and blocked off important resources for progression.
Unofficials are the way to go, but with so many children or NEETS playing the game, you're better off just hosting your own.
Lastly; the content is pretty good, but the game is not early access. It charges 30 dollars for base game, 20 dollars for DLC. Once you charge full price for your game, it's not early access; so the big flaws of terrible combat and awful animations, combined with nearly endless bugs is still there.

First off: This review is not for people who play official servers. I have next to no experience with official servers. However, you can run a dedicated server from a spare laptop with this game, and tweak all the settings to your liking. So, my friends and I had a lot of fun playing cooperatively on a private server with vastly sped up mechanics. We are more causal than people who play on dedicated servers by my understanding.
We each had our own personal base, and we could help each other out with resources, blueprints, crafting, hunting, and taming. We went into caves together, hunted alphas together, tamed things together, and then retreated to our own personal homes for the night. No penalty for not logging in for a few days, just "hey can you feed my dinos?" rather than risking being wiped out by an opposing tribe.
The customization available for dedicated servers is what made this game great for us. So take that for what it is.

One of a kind MMO. Recommended to anyone, from casual to hardcore players who like sci-fi setting with Space Ninjas.
But let's see what's the pros and cons.
Pro:
- Wide variety of Frames (like classes, or alt characters in other MMOs) within one account, and within one character.
- Wide variety of weapons, from a stealthy kill daggers, samurai swords to rocket launchers, laser rifles, vortex guns.
- Wide variety of missions, from covert ones (spy, rescue) throu exterminate, deception, sabotage to defense type (defense, mobile defense, interception, excavation) and a few more, each one with more than one possibility to complete them.
- You have the control how much time you want to spend in each type of mission. You can just blaze throu them within 2-3 minute, or spend a hour for extra rewards. That's why it's good for casuals, if you have only 10 minutes to play, that's more than enough. Nut hardcore players can push their skills to the max, survive and complete for example a hours long survivals/defense/etc. where high level enemies swarming at you, and each shot can be lethal to you.
- Unique server system. It means, that in a team, one of the player are the host, the others are the clients, thus the game servers are not that burdened, resulting in no lagg at all (sidenote: I have a good internet connection, so usually I'm the host, and random peoples who join me, even with poor net, they can play w/o lagging)
- You can play either in a team, or totally solo, like a single player game. Team finder is automatic, just choose the mission, and set it to public, and the game assembles a team in matter of seconds.
- Friendly and helpful community. If you need help, you will get it most of the time. Trolls, and toxic players are rarely found. Region, LFG (or recruit in this game) and Trade chat always lively and flooding. No hackers or bots at all. (DE bans them immediately)
- Totally free to play and no Pay to Win. You can earn everything what's in the market by playing the game, except cosmetics (skins, colors, extra decoration).
- You can be a Space Ninja. With unique abilities. Srsly, a 4 man ninja "cell" power is equivalent of an army, loaded full with guns.
Cons:
- RNG (random loot is random) can be mean sometimes, resulting in a lot of grinding to get what you want.
- The game is quite aggressive and fast paced, no time to dawdlng around in missions (except if you already killed all of the enemies).
- If a poor net player is the host, everyone will lag. But you can just leave, and try with another party / host.
- The game is addictive. If you don't have the will to say no to another mission, when you don't have time for that, then be careful.
