TL;DR at the bottom.
Main features at the bottom before TL;DR
Cons:
1. Pretty bad tutorial.
The tutorial simply guides you through basic combat, and nothing more. The more complicated mechanics such as mods and damage types are barely touched on. These two main mechanics are crucial in-game, and due to the lack of a tutorial for it, I've encountered far too many new players who are clueless. You will have to google for a crap ton of information. (Bless the wiki page)
2. Pay-4-Convenience.
If you're rich, you get through majority of the game faster. But it is NOT Pay-2-Win. Everything is obtainable, and the grind isn't insane unless RNGesus hates you. A person who paid money and a free-to-play player will end up with the exact same gear. Essentially, you buy time in this game, and nothing more.
3. Limited areas to play in.
It's not open-world. Instances have a certain tileset for each planet. It randomizes, but generally remains the same. There are, of course, new tilesets added in certain updates.
4. It's easy to get burnt out.
By burnt out, I mean that you'll probably play the game on and off when you first start. This is due to the long waiting times for crafting new items, which are the only way you can get new items on your own. That tied with the daily trade limit makes it difficult to play for several hours straight. But once you've attained a fair amount of items, getting burnt out becomes few and far between.
5. You're free to do what you want.
This can't be a bad thing, right?  But it is for those who want some form of direction in a game.  I initially found it really hard to stick to playing this game. I love every aspect of it, but having no actual goal is painful. This game is recommended for those who like loot-based games like Diablo 3.
Pros:
1. Everything is obtainable if you play the game. (With the exception of the Founders Pack)
Yeah, play the game and get everything. Simple as that. Wanna get something that is no longer available? Trade.
2. Fantastic Graphics on low-end PCs
I'm able to run this on a PC with only 2GB of RAM and an Intel Graphics card. I've upgraded since then, but it runs at a smooth 30 FPS on that disgusting old rig.
3. Gameplay.
Gameplay doesn't get dull, unless you're one of those cancerous people who plays Ash-hole. Fast paced, and both melee-only and ranged-only builds are viable.
4. The Dev team.
It's clear that the Warframe dev team cares about the game and does not try to turn it into a cash-grab. New expansion? Free. New item being released? Don't need to fork up any money. New mission? Do the pre-reqs and gain access to it. Entirely new mechanic that could possibly act as DLC? FREEEEE.
5. Community.
You will rarely ever encounter any cancer players. Why? Because Warframe heavily relies on working with others. If you're a horrible person to group with, you'll build up a bad rep and eventually no one will group with you. The downsides of being an♥♥♥♥♥are so huge, that if Kanye played this game, you'd think he's Oprah or Ellen or one of those nice people that everyone likes.
Features
+ A lot of 'Warframes' which act as classes (extremely flexible)
+ Detailed mechanics (modding, damage 2.0)
+ Large amount of viable weapons (majority are extremely different from each, all are able to be molded to endgame)
+ Fantastic graphics (recently got a revamp with better smoke and fire physics)
+ Incredibly optimized (expect smooth framerates throughout)
+ Plenty of customization and cosmetics (you will rarely find another person that looks exactly like you)
- Dull movement system (despite having a parkour system, you'll be rolling/bullet jumping everywhere. This is starting to change with the added Orokin Moon Tileset)
- Limited areas to play in
- Repetitive (very limited number of mission types)
- PvP is pointless (you don't get much other than cosmetics)
- Ridiculously grindy
- A lot of flukes (there are certain builds that do all the work by pressing A SINGLE BUTTON. I kid you not. Check out 'Warframe draco runs' on youtube.)
- Limited trades each day (tallies with your Mastery Rank, which you can increase by leveling items)
- Limited inventory (appears as a cash grab quite early on, but you can earn Platinum through trading)
- Certain items are obtainable at certain times (2 main items; orokin catalyst and orokin reactor. They are untradable, and I've personally wasted over 400 Platinum on the market buying them because I missed an alert that was only available for 1 HOUR. The recipe that can be bought on the market is stupid)
TLDR;
It's free, but can appear as P2W.
You can obtain everything if you spend time and effort.
Play if you like loot-based games.
Expect to wait. A lot.
Community is awesome.
Devs are awesome with constant updates and hotfixes.
Being a Helicopter with dual axes is fun (yes you can do that in this game)

TL;DR: You will be screwed over and over by cross server raiding. Read rockybattlenet's review as his is the most accurate I have ever read.
I would have recommended this game prior to the launch of cross server featuers, but that is no longer the case. Ark is an amazingly fun game that requires a lot of hard work and dedication to do well it. None of that matters though when you have offline base raiding from another server.
Losing everything in a blaze of glory can have its merits but there is no fun in waking up one morning and the past 3 weeks worth of work from your tribe is partially destroyed in the very wee hours of the morning by a tribe from another server. It sucks and it's out of your control. Rebuild you might say and I would agree, only the degree of loss takes many many more hours of taming to get your production back up to where it was at to repair it all. Just when you think you have things mostly retamed and rebuilt you wake up again 3 days later and you loss even more than you did the 1st time. That cycle can and will repeat itself. One might think that any tribe on your server can do that, and of course you would be right, however that gives you a target a goal for revenge, reason to work even harder. I have experienced taking revenge on the server bully after coming back from nothing and it was one of the most satisfying things I have ever had in Ark. Cross server eliminates that aspect. You are left with a sense of loss, hoplessness and nothing to direct your anger to. Why farm every hour after work if it's just going to be wiped again while you are offline?
One of the funnist aspects of ark is the PvP element, that unkown player threat or trying to handle server politics. Without the PvP element in Ark you can still have a lot of fun on PvE side but it runs out at a very fast pace. You have minmal to no loss, no competition for resources, no fights for land. You get a pretty base set up and your dinos set up for what? Danger is what keeps it interesting and the greatest since of danger is from players.

First impressions:
This game is gorgeous, and it's very optimized as well.  I didn't get the actual FPS count but gameplay was smooth and graphics were beautiful, this is with 4gb RAM and a GTX 750 graphics card, 1080p resolution.  I've seen games with worse graphics and more lag.  Plus one point.
You can't start with a shotgun.  Minus one point.
The sword is faster than the staff.  This is not true in real life, a staff can kick (most) swords' butts in speed.  Neutral.
The bow can stick people to the walls.  Plus one point.
Parkour system.  It's not as smooth as, say, Mirror's Edge or Celaria, but it's there.  Plus one point.
The coop is a bit confusing at first, I wound up in a game with a random stranger I don't recall asking for.  Fortunately he was helpful and we cleared the maps with little snags.  Also on this note there wasn't much network lag.  Neutral.
Overall, I haven't played enough to give a solid recommendation or not, but things are looking bright.  The melee combat feels simple to learn, hard to master, I'm hoping that proves to be the case.  At the moment it feels in the vein of Jedi Academy.  Make of that what you will, I like it.  Definitely worth a look and ten gigs on your hard drive.

TL;DR: Do not buy for official server play or do not buy dlc. Play on unofficial servers, singleplayer, or make your own server, enjoy lots of game enhancing mods.
Being honest, I would have to say this game is not fun for official server surviving, whether you're in a tribe or not. However, in singleplayer you can adjust many settings to make the game easier and more fun, along with plenty of workshop mods to enhance your experience so much more than it already is. I recommend either singleplayer where you can set all the settings yourself, adjust many game.ini settings, have any and all mods you want to play with (Annunaki Genesis or Extinction Core are both great core mods) OR if you prefer multiplayer/tribe play I recommend either playing unofficial servers other players have set up either their levels/mods, or having a private server set up (like SL1PG8r or KingDaddyDMac have) and playing that way, I DO NOT recommend buying the DLC, as the Extinction Core mod adds those dinos to all maps, and is not worth the $20 for something a few mods can do much better, and for free.

Been playing ARK for quite a bit now. I still haven't finished the game or even seen everything but I've had a base built, a lot of dinosaurs tamed and some boats. I've seen a lot of the main map and have explored quite a bit.
The game looks great, plays quite nicely but it has a lot of unfinished or just plain annoying mechanics (for example taming on a regular server takes way too freaking long, come on), the UI is quite clunky, I wish it was smaller and sleeker in general.
While playing multiplayer you have a choice of playing on PVP or PVE servers. PVP is a gankfest, if you are not willing to play 24/7 to keep an eye on your stuff on a random server then forget about it. PVE works fine if you just want to enjoy the game and not be concerned about other people runing your stuff "for fun".
I'm playing on a private server and it has been a blast with some mods. We're building, taming dinos, exploring and just having fun.
Performance is quite terrible, really. I hope that in the future they will optimize the game some because right now it's pretty much a slideshow if you are playing on the highest settings with anything less than a beast PC from the dark side of the moon.
Overall if you like survival with a nice theme and a lot of updates, creatures and stuff to do then I'd recommend ARK. Oh and there's a few DLC available that add creatures, maps, items, cosmetics etc so it's not that bad.
Overall I'd recommend the game, preferably if you want to play something cool with friends/SO :)

PLEASE READ, CAN BE HELPFUL FOR NEW PLAYERS!
My favorite steam game so far (from all the ones i've played and seen). Definitely the most interesting and most intriguing game i've seen in a while as it presents so many different aspects new to survival games, such as giant maps, daily updates that include new animal species, new planst, new crafting items and new settings. This game is actually pretty hard to play but not impossible, i highly recommend playing with your friends and progress as a tribe while collecting, looting, killing, harvesting, exploring and cooperating against nature. The best thing is that it takes so long to level up so the game is not as easy as minecraft let's say. It actually took me like 52h in real life playing with my cousin and we both reached level 16 only, but managed to tame a low level Parasaur, build a big wooden hut on a mountain near the waters and trees, kill carnivors, build 2 rafts, 3 different camp-sites, leather clothes and we explored all the coasts of the map. This game was worth every penny and every minute spent on it, do buy and enjoy.
Tip: If you wanna play with a bunch of your friends without always getting raided create an online private non dedicated server for you and your friends only, that way you can really take your time to explore and play and the game will bug way less because no hackers and there's not an immense amount of players in the same server, and you can voice chat inside the game with B (press/hold, depending on the button layout).
A few down sides for this game: it does use a lot of internet and sometimes slows the usage for everyone using that same router, so be careful (unless you have a very high wifi speed). Also, no matter how strong your pc/laptop is, it's impossible to play the game on full graphics so set everything on low or medium to enjoy maximum fps. Also, if you die, you lose all equipement unless you go recover it where you died, and you need to really know the map for that to happen so my advice is: try not to die! Avoid sticky situations, lay low around carnivores and don't hang too much inside the waters. Keep player hydrated, fed and heated.
I hope i helped someone, please do listen to my tips, AND happy exploring everyone!

This game is getting bashed by players for not doing what they specificlly want while the developer team already has a set plan for how they will develop the game. The devs get punished for adding new content to the game and not optimizing even though it is incredibly difficult to optimize a game that is consistenly updated. The developers have said that they will focus entirely on optimization and bug fixes once all the content is added. One example of added content that caused issues was the addition of the Tek Tier which supposedly takes away from the primitive setting of the game. Incase you haven't noticed, the game is science fiction with obelisks in the sky, a barrier around the island, and the implants in every player's arm, along with tha fact that Tek Tier was planned from day one. Tek Tier gamplay is even optional with servers having the ability to disable it.
The last reason is the inaccuracy of the creatures. People complain that the animals don't look or act like their real life counterparts, but all the creatures in the game are fictional species based on real life animals that have evolved to live on the island among dozens of other creatures from different time periods. They are supposed to be inaccurate and far different from real life animals.
It's just sad to see so many people uninformed on the game's plan and direction. All my hours of gameplay were spent in either single player or with friends on a private server with friends, and I still continue to enjoy the game and support the devs.
Edit: Although, the devs should have waited to release Abberation in December in the first place to cash in on Christmas sales instead of delaying it for two months.

TL;DR at the bottom.
Main features at the bottom before TL;DR
Cons:
1. Pretty bad tutorial.
The tutorial simply guides you through basic combat, and nothing more. The more complicated mechanics such as mods and damage types are barely touched on. These two main mechanics are crucial in-game, and due to the lack of a tutorial for it, I've encountered far too many new players who are clueless. You will have to google for a crap ton of information. (Bless the wiki page)
2. Pay-4-Convenience.
If you're rich, you get through majority of the game faster. But it is NOT Pay-2-Win. Everything is obtainable, and the grind isn't insane unless RNGesus hates you. A person who paid money and a free-to-play player will end up with the exact same gear. Essentially, you buy time in this game, and nothing more.
3. Limited areas to play in.
It's not open-world. Instances have a certain tileset for each planet. It randomizes, but generally remains the same. There are, of course, new tilesets added in certain updates.
4. It's easy to get burnt out.
By burnt out, I mean that you'll probably play the game on and off when you first start. This is due to the long waiting times for crafting new items, which are the only way you can get new items on your own. That tied with the daily trade limit makes it difficult to play for several hours straight. But once you've attained a fair amount of items, getting burnt out becomes few and far between.
5. You're free to do what you want.
This can't be a bad thing, right?  But it is for those who want some form of direction in a game.  I initially found it really hard to stick to playing this game. I love every aspect of it, but having no actual goal is painful. This game is recommended for those who like loot-based games like Diablo 3.
Pros:
1. Everything is obtainable if you play the game. (With the exception of the Founders Pack)
Yeah, play the game and get everything. Simple as that. Wanna get something that is no longer available? Trade.
2. Fantastic Graphics on low-end PCs
I'm able to run this on a PC with only 2GB of RAM and an Intel Graphics card. I've upgraded since then, but it runs at a smooth 30 FPS on that disgusting old rig.
3. Gameplay.
Gameplay doesn't get dull, unless you're one of those cancerous people who plays Ash-hole. Fast paced, and both melee-only and ranged-only builds are viable.
4. The Dev team.
It's clear that the Warframe dev team cares about the game and does not try to turn it into a cash-grab. New expansion? Free. New item being released? Don't need to fork up any money. New mission? Do the pre-reqs and gain access to it. Entirely new mechanic that could possibly act as DLC? FREEEEE.
5. Community.
You will rarely ever encounter any cancer players. Why? Because Warframe heavily relies on working with others. If you're a horrible person to group with, you'll build up a bad rep and eventually no one will group with you. The downsides of being an♥♥♥♥♥are so huge, that if Kanye played this game, you'd think he's Oprah or Ellen or one of those nice people that everyone likes.
Features
+ A lot of 'Warframes' which act as classes (extremely flexible)
+ Detailed mechanics (modding, damage 2.0)
+ Large amount of viable weapons (majority are extremely different from each, all are able to be molded to endgame)
+ Fantastic graphics (recently got a revamp with better smoke and fire physics)
+ Incredibly optimized (expect smooth framerates throughout)
+ Plenty of customization and cosmetics (you will rarely find another person that looks exactly like you)
- Dull movement system (despite having a parkour system, you'll be rolling/bullet jumping everywhere. This is starting to change with the added Orokin Moon Tileset)
- Limited areas to play in
- Repetitive (very limited number of mission types)
- PvP is pointless (you don't get much other than cosmetics)
- Ridiculously grindy
- A lot of flukes (there are certain builds that do all the work by pressing A SINGLE BUTTON. I kid you not. Check out 'Warframe draco runs' on youtube.)
- Limited trades each day (tallies with your Mastery Rank, which you can increase by leveling items)
- Limited inventory (appears as a cash grab quite early on, but you can earn Platinum through trading)
- Certain items are obtainable at certain times (2 main items; orokin catalyst and orokin reactor. They are untradable, and I've personally wasted over 400 Platinum on the market buying them because I missed an alert that was only available for 1 HOUR. The recipe that can be bought on the market is stupid)
TLDR;
It's free, but can appear as P2W.
You can obtain everything if you spend time and effort.
Play if you like loot-based games.
Expect to wait. A lot.
Community is awesome.
Devs are awesome with constant updates and hotfixes.
Being a Helicopter with dual axes is fun (yes you can do that in this game)

Warframe has, even in comparison to paid MMOs, utterly changed my standards for MMOs. It is a third person, free-to-play, RPG, shooter.
And it does it perfectly.
Pro:
+Tons of weapons, powers, Warframes.
+Customizable weaponry, powers. Each weapon can be have it's stats and damage can be changed through "mods".
+Tons of different gamemodes: from run and gun "exterminate",  to the hiest-like "spy", there are tons of different mission types. Not to mention: raids, PvP, "sorties", and event missions.
+In-game trading: Trade with other players for premium currency. At later levels, it's extremely easy to earn enough platinum for anything you want in the currency shop.
+Parkour system: You're a space ninja, and you can move like one.
+Amazing level design: Some of the levels are just plain beautiful. I'm looking at you, Void towers.
+Lore: This game doesn't divulge it's secrets right away. There are plenty of secrets hiding in plain sight, and many more hidden off the beaten path.
+Gameplay: Warframe is very much a play-it-your-way game. Whether you're stealthy, love gunplay, or want to go in swinging with a battleaxe. There's a frame and weapon for you, and they all work.
Cons:
- Intimidating at first: It's, admitidly, overwhelming at first. There are so many missions, frames, and weapons.
- Guidance-needed: It may be hard to find that weapon you really want without consulting a wiki.
- Grind-walls: Everything is a grind. Perhaps not a long one, but there will always be a wait time, or a grind.
It's a game about being a space ninja: play it.

Warframe is truly a gem, something you only encounter once in a lifetime. You'll find Warframe in the Free to Play section in the Steam Store, and that's the first reason you should play it, it's free! The second reason is that the game doesn't ever force micro transactions on the player (there is still some really cool♥♥♥♥♥♥you can get with real money). As far as I can tell, most of the things that can be bought with real money can also be obtained by just playing the game.
Aside from that, Warframe boasts a colorful combat system where the player uses a set of abilities exclusive to their "Warframe" (the suit that the player wears), as well as Primary, Secondary, and Melee weapons. The combat plays out like any third person fighting game, you run around doing cool♥♥♥♥♥♥while your enemies cower in fear and fire randomly at you. But there is just something that sets Warframe apart from those other games...it's that Warframe just does that better than any other game, and for that, I can't recommend it more!

I've already made a review, but came back to read what other reviewers were saying about ARK, and let me tell you... Nothing I read was objectivelty true about ARK.  I have over 1,500 hours playing ARK Survival Evolved.
ARK is one of the most content filled, well designed, beautifully crafted Multiplayer survival games ever made.  Some reviewers complain about low FPS, because ARK isn't fully optimized yet.  True.  But that's because the developer's focus is on content and finished the game design before going back and optimizing graphics.  If you have a good system, ARK will play fine on High settings.  Even an average gaming system will run ARK on medium.  Just turn down ground clutter (or off) and you'll gain a huge boost in FPS and performance.
Some reviewers complain it's too hard.  You're surviving against the elements as well as multi-ton carnivores, so what do you expect?  ARK isn't really hard.  It just requires forethought.  Those guys want to run naked through the forest with a wooden spear, and then they complain they were killed by raptors or a T Rex.  Real Life is too hard for such people.
Some reviewers complain about lack of options.  That's because they're only playing on Official Servers with low settings and strict rules.  There are THOUSANDS of Unofficial Servers hosted by other players, each with different settings and mods, all available through in game's unofficial server search.  Find something that suits you, and play your way.
ARK may not be for every gamer or every taste, but nothing about ARK being a "Bad game" is true.  You just have to be smart, which unfortunately is just too much to ask for some gamers.  Coming straight to ARK from Minecraft... yea, ARK may be a little difficult.  Sorry people, but not all PC games are going to be designed for Leap Frog players.

The community is kinda chill, welcoming and high lvl players helping new players to get the real taste of the game. The thing i like in this game is making your own items. You dont need to farm up in game currency to buy items/weapons/warframes. You have to set out and find items and components to get your desired things. And the squad system makes the game less lonely and team up with other players to have fun. And the developers keep adding new contents. They also make streams known as Devstreams to let players know how things are changing and so on. If you are looking for a MMO with a big community i suggest to try this game.
For the best experience, try avoiding being carried and spoiled by the others. Enjoy it at your own pace. Take your time to explore the game by yourself, try out different things and learn from your experience. Warframe is a game where you decides whatever the hell you want to do. The game wont tell you to go do this, go do that.
Note that you will have to grind alot and it can be fun when you do it effficiently.  Otherwise you will get bored and get tired at the end of the day.
NOT A PAY-TO-WIN
Some will say this game is a Pay2Win as soon as they see the market. Dont panic cuz there are ways of getting everything in game without spending your own money.
Even if you pay money to obtain all types of weapons and end game stuffs wont make you good at the game as the knowledge comes from your gameplay experience. You can get everything in with just spending rediculous amount of money but you'll end up with zero understanding of the game mechanics. No matter how good stuffs you have, you are nothing if you dont even know how to mod a weapon. The point is, money wont buy you the advantage in this game. You are nothing if you have 0 experience.

Except these balancing issues, the occasional bugs and the sometimes random enemy AI, ARK is a very enjoyable game, but almost exclusively in Multiplayer. Don't go in expecting a fun and immersive singleplayer.

First I'd like to adress something other reviews often don't make clear - YOU choose how you want to play this game- You can play on your own, you can choose to let other people into your world, or you can jump on one of the dedicated servers(Official or Unofficial) and create and play characters on any one of those.
My point: You can play on a server where everything you've built can't be raided, you can play on a server that is actively moderated and will kick toxic players, you can play on a server where you won't be muscled out of resources
You can play how you want to play.
Especially if you just wanna tame dinosaurs and rampage around  - This game is absolutely great

--------
The specifics
For the most part this game works exactly how you'd want it to - you start out in your undies, your only concern with surviving, and as you gather resources and learn about the world, you start getting more established, making more things, making better things, and eventually its you chasing down the dinosaurs instead of the other way around. You level up by getting experience, which you gain from doing mostly things you have to do anyways to survive, and that unlocks engrams, which are recipes for crafting things - from clothes, to tools, to buildings(including plumbing :p) there's all kinds of engrams. So if you want to be a crazed dino-tamer hobo, surviving off berries and raw meat, you can do that, if you want to build a 40 floor spire consisting of nothing but single 10'x10' rooms one on top of another, all made of thatch and inhabited by your friends....you can do that too.
Now, there are two primary issues with the game right now -
1) The hit boxes for the dinosaurs are pretty screwy, so you'll likely periodically find a dinos sitting still directly next to a tree or a rock, having gotten themselves stuck. However, I've so far only noticed this issue with objects which are destroyable (by harvesting) so you can usually pop out your axe or pick and free up a dino if you need/want to.
2) The error everyone mentions - on the OFFICIAL servers (this is an important distinction) people are able to transfer pre-existing characters and their dinos to other servers, so mega tribes are able to rove about like locusts and raze and pillage like Genghis Khan's mongol horde. HOWEVER this can be avoided by running on most of the unofficial dedicated servers, which have disabled or strictly controlled transfers, and as of this writing there's about 1000 unofficial servers running, so you should be able to find a world to your liking. If you want, you can make your own server, either by running a non-dedicated server (basically your single player instance of a map which you can password protect and allow other people to join) which only runs when you're online in Ark, or host a dedicated server (you don't even have to rent space from Wildcard, there's ways of setting things up on a machine you don't mind leaving running.
So yeah, don't let yourself be scared away by the hysteria over what are primarily community issues if you just want a dinosaur survival game. The game's not perfect, but I defy you to not feel a little wonder at all the cool places and things to do you'll find in this game.
Just remember - Troodons are ♥♥♥♥ing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s :P

Ive played this game for more than 1.5k hours (63~ days) and i can tell you this is by far the best Steam, free-to-play game ive ever played, ive played video games all my life and this is the only game that i have put this much effort into and i dont regret any of it. Im MR12 (out of 21) and barely cratched the surface.

This will be a long review, split into sections with a TL;DR for most.
Warframe's new player experience is disappointing. The game's tutorials don't teach important concepts such as fusing cores to level mods, what all of the mission types are, and how to complete them and the list goes on. The game fails to even mention some of the key features of the game and just hopes that the player will stumble into them and figure out what they do. This needs serious work, needing to look up a tutorial on how to perform basic actions is unacceptable.
- The NPE is awful and needs a lot of work from the devs to become acceptable as a tutorial.
Warframe has some of the best combat I've found in a game recently. The 'Movement 2.0' system is similarly amazing, making being a space pirate spy ninja possible. The combat and movement is responsive and clean, allowing for some truly amazing stunts both in and out of combat. And who doesn't love doing bullet jumps through a sub-marine base?
- The combat and general movement systems are amazingly well put together, responsive and allow for all of the in game stunts to occur.
Warframe's progression system comes mostly in the form of 'Mastery Rank' or MR. This is basically your account level, and things such as weapons and quests will unlock at a certain MR.
Mastery Rank is earned by leveling weapons and Warframes to their maximum level of 30. Weapons and Warframes have to be crafted in your ship's foundry. This is where the game begins to show it's F2P payment model, as almost every craftable item has a building time between 1 minute (for ciphers and restore pads) and 72 hours (for a new Warframe). This can often lead to frustration after grinding out the last part for a new Warframe and having to wait for three days before being able to use it.
- Progression in the game happens through Mastery Rank. This is earned by leveling weapons and Warframes. Item building times can be frustrating after the elusive grind for that final part of a weapon/frame.
Warframe's social aspects are very central to the overall game's feel. Often people will be running missions and alerts in groups of up to four. Clans are present in the game and unlock clan-exclusive weapons through various weapon labs located in the clan dojo. I recommend finding a small group of people to play with consistently as certain mission types are very difficult to complete a a one man army (these inclue Defense and Mobile Defense missions).
- Warframes social aspects are very powerful and important to move into the late game content such as daily sortie missions and 8 player raids.
Warframe's business model is fair, but can be irritating. Buying the premium currency of Platinum is not required in any way and it can be earned through trading 'Prime' parts in the game's trading chat. However, obtaining key items such as Warframe/Weapon slots are only purchasable with Platinum. This is a frustrating limitation as having to sell a Warframe to make room for your newest one is often undesirable and a purely arbitrary limitation to the game. Platinum can be used to purchase 'Prime' weapons and Warframes from other players in the 'trading' chat, these Primed items often have a small stat boost and a different look over the basic version.
- Warframe sells 'Platinum' as it's monetization system. Platinum can be used to purchase 'Prime' items and slots for weapons and Warframes. It is a convenience item and is not necessary to enjoy the game.
I did not find Warframe's story content interesting or captivating. A lot of the quests felt contrived and like a normal mission with some custom voice acting. Now for The Second Dream (
).
Warframe's endgame content is very strong and compelling. Running the daily Sortie missions are a great way to unlock new frames/weapons and play collaboratively with others. Ability to complete the higher teirs of the Orokin Void allows for the player to farm for their own Prime parts either by themselves or in a group. Warframe currently has two 8 player supporting raids to earn some of the final pieces of equipment required to have a fully meta-built Warframe and weapons.
- Warframe's endgame content is very strong and keeps a good variety of missions, from the daily Sortie missions to raiding with up to 8 players.
Warframe is a very solid offering in today's F2P game market. It has amazing combat and movement systems to back up it's integral social elements. It has many hours of play within so long as you are wlling to repeat missions a few times to get all of the shiny loot out of it. And as a free to play game, all you have to lose is your time. Unfortunately it lacks in it's new player experience and will require the

I've had ARK for quite some time, and it's a game that my wife and I always come back to. There are plenty of ways to play, either hunting dinos, base building, both in PvE and PvP.
ARK at launch was a bit janky, it was slow at times, framerate drops and crashed often, but now it is a very stable, smooth game.
PvP servers are not easy, don't expect to go on and dominate out of the gate, you won't survive long. Either the Island will kill you, or players will. Sometimes, though, you can join a tribe and it can make your life significantly better.
Don't like PvP? No problem, the PvE mode is fantastic, and you don't lose too much for it. You can be creative with your base, and even though players don't prove to be dangerous, the Island is plenty killifying if you're not careful.
It's a genuinely fun game, and if you do run solo or small party, don't be afraid to tweak the settings to your liking. Don't like the slow XP gain? Bump it to 2.5 or higher. Don't like the low amount of resources? Bump it up.
It's very easy to adjust to your tastes, and in worse case, there are hundreds of fantastic mods that tweak the game in ways that'll certainly be your thing.
ARK is an ambitious game, but it's far more stablethan it's early access might indicate. It's a brilliant game, frustraiting at times, but any game like this is. That's the nature of survival games. It just so happens that you have to Survive T-Rexes.

Definately would be far more enjoyable if the flaws weren't so glaring.
The first is the over-the-shoulder gameplay, without a target snap option, you either spin wildly when moving or have decent unaimed target placement; never both.
A second is that because of the low capacity of powers (Until you're a higher level) that you need item drops to replentish, the majority of fights/missions are mashing A or B (Jump and melee respectively).
After you get through the first Tutorial story missions, all the missions blatently state that they fit a specific mission archetype in the description, telling you exactly what to expect, leaving no room for investment in whatever story it adds.
On that note, There is only one tutorial that points out how to use the modification crafting menu- there really ought to be a better explaination in the other 8 hub menus when you first unlock them.  (Not really a complaint about not being able to apply reasoning, and more of a time reduction in the learning to play aspect)
And the biggest issue is that of the free-to-play nature, advertising all of the interesting-looking warframes, items, powerups, weapons, equipment in the store from level 1, unlockable from the beginning with premium currency.  Even worse, the abilitycustomize is completely limited to that same currency, in the form of unlocking more than a single row of the basic, bland, everyday common colors (You have to unlock black and white But can pick from two shades of grey, a brown or a medium roygbiv).  Not to mention about 7 other pallet types like gloss, metalic, and Flame.  All costing premium currency.
If you're not intuitive enough to figure out complicated crafting menus, I would not reccomend this game until they put up some better menu tutorials.  If you don't like repetitive gameplay or cut-and-paste level generators, I don't reccomend this game.  If you dislike Free-to-play economics, You might be able to play if you enjoy the mechanics, but I wouldn't advocate it personally.

I have played over 1000 hours in ark by now, and still going through it all, that been said even after i played so long i have yet to find everything, there is just so much to do, and the game is still getting updates to keep people busy and playing.
I go over some of the Pro's and  Con's in the game as all games have them.
Pro's
Good leveling system (it gets harder as you progress in the game)
Vast amount of Dino's to find and tame (still more been added, and there some ingame i haven't even found yet)
great map size (the map is large but not to massive to make it a challenge to explore, dont forget to explore caves and ocean aswell!)
PvP  ( it great to be in a tribe, and defending your stuff from raiders and catching people by surprise)
Challenge (if your easy going that is fine you can take it easy but as you go deeper inland get ready for lots of bigger dinos and obstacles to tackle)
Player Stats and dinos (you can be anything from a Fighter to an explorer or builder and so on, stats customize your experience in the game in many ways so try everything)
steady progression ( this is to Emgrams, when you level up you get emgram points to spend, they are used to unlock new things to make and use to make surviving a lot more easy)
Now for the Con's
Taming (This will be one of the annoying things to do is taming, taming can be easy or extremely hard, to give a hint Dilo to tame will maybe take 2 minutes to 5 minutes, but something like a Rex might take 2 hours to even 6 hours and still some even higher then a day! you will need a active Tribe always for some dino's)
Grinding ( Yes there is lots of grinding in this game, alot of it, be ready for hours of gathering and harvesting in this game)
Egg hatching (while eggs and baby are cute *mostly the baby's* it a living Nightmare sometimes, the dino may hatch and die right afterwards due to no food been eaten, you got to watch the dino's and Eggs at all time's intill they grow up to a point they can look after themselfs, and this itself can take hours or even days)
Bugs (there is going to be Bugs here and there,so be expecting them, dont worrie about it to much, once found the devs bring out a hotfix's as fast as they can)
Hard start for new players (there is no tutorial, no guide to follow it just you and your wits unless you look it up, and even then it dont make life easy for starter's cause most things like dilos can kill you without effort)
Beefy computer ( now i use to play this on a laptop it was not as great, having the lowest settings can still lag like hell your going to need a good to great computer for this game to get it's full experience, graphics, FPS, performance and all that)
PvP again (it not so fun getting raided when your away on a active server im afarid)
Expect to die, alot ( about everything can kill you, falling, starving, freezing, get eaten, Midget Tribe member with a shotgun...)
Other then all those the game is still Great, if it is for those who love dino's, challenges and survival this is a great game to have.

Warframe has, even in comparison to paid MMOs, utterly changed my standards for MMOs. It is a third person, free-to-play, RPG, shooter.
And it does it perfectly.
Pro:
+Tons of weapons, powers, Warframes.
+Customizable weaponry, powers. Each weapon can be have it's stats and damage can be changed through "mods".
+Tons of different gamemodes: from run and gun "exterminate",  to the hiest-like "spy", there are tons of different mission types. Not to mention: raids, PvP, "sorties", and event missions.
+In-game trading: Trade with other players for premium currency. At later levels, it's extremely easy to earn enough platinum for anything you want in the currency shop.
+Parkour system: You're a space ninja, and you can move like one.
+Amazing level design: Some of the levels are just plain beautiful. I'm looking at you, Void towers.
+Lore: This game doesn't divulge it's secrets right away. There are plenty of secrets hiding in plain sight, and many more hidden off the beaten path.
+Gameplay: Warframe is very much a play-it-your-way game. Whether you're stealthy, love gunplay, or want to go in swinging with a battleaxe. There's a frame and weapon for you, and they all work.
Cons:
- Intimidating at first: It's, admitidly, overwhelming at first. There are so many missions, frames, and weapons.
- Guidance-needed: It may be hard to find that weapon you really want without consulting a wiki.
- Grind-walls: Everything is a grind. Perhaps not a long one, but there will always be a wait time, or a grind.
It's a game about being a space ninja: play it.

This game, with all its drawbacks of people raiding your bases, bugs, and devs not doing such a hot job with fixing much of it (adding a DLC on an early access??), this game I still think is worth a buy simply because it is a well designed game for being in early access. here's why:
Pros:
First, lets talk about how dynamic this game is. Its by far the most beautiful open world game, in terms of graphics, that I have seen yet. These guys did a phenominal job with how their maps look, and it shows. On the flipside, this game can reduce graphics levels to an astounding level. It has MANY options on the start screen that you can choose to reduce these levels on your machine. As long as you're not running this on a toaster or potato, this game is still great. (its not a pretty picture if you lower things this much but I'm a guy who prefers performance over graphics anyways) there are some balancing issues with some dinos, and its a bit frustrating to have to constantly be researching dinos on the web to know what food they want or how much narcs (keeps them knocked out) they'll need in the taming process) but you begin to catch on pretty quick. Base building is well tuned in my experience. Lots of different ways to build bases, decent physics mechanics (you cant just put 1 foundation on the side of a cliff and build the rest of your base in midair), there are a couple of annoying tweaks you have to work around but steam has made the modding community really easy to add mods into the game. You don't need mods to build bases, but they have their advantages in some aspects. The communities BnL are friendly. Depends on the server you play on, but generally, especially if you're new, they're helpful and sometimes lend a hand. (there are some servers that don't have very friendly people in which I just recommend you move to a different server.
This game was designed to be played with friends. It has MANY benefits to playing together and makes the game more enjoyable and less of a grind at the beginning. I will admit, the start of your characters is a bit of a grind (not starving/freezing/being eaten/etc) and getting resources yourself is kind of a chore, but the grind is greatly alleviated with multiple people.
Cons:
This game is STILL in early access, with a DLC that costs almost as much as the game itself. In my book, that's ridiculous. They have an "unfinished" game and all they do is add more content to it. With that said, they are continually adding more content, so its always changing, and shows that the devs are still working, and not sitting on their hands as the cash flows in. IMO, they should focus more on the core game and fixing some internal issues that have been present since day one (like AIs and various glitches).
The combat is dynamic, but fairly basic. Most dinos have one attack, bite, and pretty much have the same animation with variations. There are a handful of weapons you can use which are pretty cool (like guns, grenades, swords, and RPGs) but most of the time you'll be on a dino in combat, most of the time.
Taming is great, but with some higher end dinos, it will take (I kid you not) HOURS, which is bittersweet. Its a lot of dedication, but its rewarding at the same time. ex: "You just tamed your first T-Rex after 5-6 hours of watching it slowly eat meat while periodically keeping it under. You're so excited, and you crafted its very costly saddle, and now you're ready to take on the world, you set out to go test it's skills and accidentally walk into the swamp with your level 30 T-Rex. within 5 minutes, maybe, your hours of dedication crumples to the floor, dead as dead can be, with the rest of the other creatures that killed it chasing you." This is a story that is not uncommon in this game. Your hours of dedication can all be wasted by a very very small percentage of that time, and only gets worse in PVP servers where some people find it a pure joy to kill penned up dinos with RPGs, grenades, or rifles while you're offline. (remember that time still moves on even when youre at school or work.)
It is not at all uncommon to be robbed while you're offline, which only adds to the frustration and grind of this game. And because of this, its a game that is hard to put down, especially if you have invested a decent amount of time in your world. There is a REMEDY from this problem, however. There are PVE servers, but are often heavily crowded with player bases, OR you can create your own server (or singleplayer world), that is private (or not), and only comes online when you come online. DISCLAIMER: it limits the people that enter that world to a relatively small proximity around you (meaning they cant be across the map, they must be nearby you). Its not a great alternative, but it keeps your stuff safe and "pauses" when you leave for work. (I HIGHLY recommend this to anyone who plans to play this game without any friends. This game IS NOT worth the grind to do it alone in a PVP server) Again, this game was designed to be team-based, and IMO, (In My Opinion, for those of you who dont know what that means) the game is already out to kill you anyways, so the fact that you remove the enemy players isnt such a great loss anyways. You also have the ability to alter the settings of your world to recieve more XP, increase dino taming speed, etc, and allows you to place any mods in the game you like. its a great sandbox that is always trying to kill everything you love! :) awesome!!
OVERALL:
This is a fantastic game, I HIGHLY recommend it if you and your buddies want a survival game that has the graphics and the content. (this game is LOADED with content) The maps are gorgeous, and it is VERY rare that you will ever have NOTHING to do. There is always SOMETHING that needs to be done. Singleplayer? I dont recommend unless you play offline or on your own hosted server. (if you have a dedicated server, then you wont have the limitations i stated above. "dedicated" is different than "hosted server") PVE servers also are a good playingground if you still want to play online as a single player. there are some bugs to AI (flying dinos) and periodic glitches, but REALLY it is honestly an excellent game that always challenges you.

Ive played this game for more than 1.5k hours (63~ days) and i can tell you this is by far the best Steam, free-to-play game ive ever played, ive played video games all my life and this is the only game that i have put this much effort into and i dont regret any of it. Im MR12 (out of 21) and barely cratched the surface.

This will be a long review, split into sections with a TL;DR for most.
Warframe's new player experience is disappointing. The game's tutorials don't teach important concepts such as fusing cores to level mods, what all of the mission types are, and how to complete them and the list goes on. The game fails to even mention some of the key features of the game and just hopes that the player will stumble into them and figure out what they do. This needs serious work, needing to look up a tutorial on how to perform basic actions is unacceptable.
- The NPE is awful and needs a lot of work from the devs to become acceptable as a tutorial.
Warframe has some of the best combat I've found in a game recently. The 'Movement 2.0' system is similarly amazing, making being a space pirate spy ninja possible. The combat and movement is responsive and clean, allowing for some truly amazing stunts both in and out of combat. And who doesn't love doing bullet jumps through a sub-marine base?
- The combat and general movement systems are amazingly well put together, responsive and allow for all of the in game stunts to occur.
Warframe's progression system comes mostly in the form of 'Mastery Rank' or MR. This is basically your account level, and things such as weapons and quests will unlock at a certain MR.
Mastery Rank is earned by leveling weapons and Warframes to their maximum level of 30. Weapons and Warframes have to be crafted in your ship's foundry. This is where the game begins to show it's F2P payment model, as almost every craftable item has a building time between 1 minute (for ciphers and restore pads) and 72 hours (for a new Warframe). This can often lead to frustration after grinding out the last part for a new Warframe and having to wait for three days before being able to use it.
- Progression in the game happens through Mastery Rank. This is earned by leveling weapons and Warframes. Item building times can be frustrating after the elusive grind for that final part of a weapon/frame.
Warframe's social aspects are very central to the overall game's feel. Often people will be running missions and alerts in groups of up to four. Clans are present in the game and unlock clan-exclusive weapons through various weapon labs located in the clan dojo. I recommend finding a small group of people to play with consistently as certain mission types are very difficult to complete a a one man army (these inclue Defense and Mobile Defense missions).
- Warframes social aspects are very powerful and important to move into the late game content such as daily sortie missions and 8 player raids.
Warframe's business model is fair, but can be irritating. Buying the premium currency of Platinum is not required in any way and it can be earned through trading 'Prime' parts in the game's trading chat. However, obtaining key items such as Warframe/Weapon slots are only purchasable with Platinum. This is a frustrating limitation as having to sell a Warframe to make room for your newest one is often undesirable and a purely arbitrary limitation to the game. Platinum can be used to purchase 'Prime' weapons and Warframes from other players in the 'trading' chat, these Primed items often have a small stat boost and a different look over the basic version.
- Warframe sells 'Platinum' as it's monetization system. Platinum can be used to purchase 'Prime' items and slots for weapons and Warframes. It is a convenience item and is not necessary to enjoy the game.
I did not find Warframe's story content interesting or captivating. A lot of the quests felt contrived and like a normal mission with some custom voice acting. Now for The Second Dream (
).
Warframe's endgame content is very strong and compelling. Running the daily Sortie missions are a great way to unlock new frames/weapons and play collaboratively with others. Ability to complete the higher teirs of the Orokin Void allows for the player to farm for their own Prime parts either by themselves or in a group. Warframe currently has two 8 player supporting raids to earn some of the final pieces of equipment required to have a fully meta-built Warframe and weapons.
- Warframe's endgame content is very strong and keeps a good variety of missions, from the daily Sortie missions to raiding with up to 8 players.
Warframe is a very solid offering in today's F2P game market. It has amazing combat and movement systems to back up it's integral social elements. It has many hours of play within so long as you are wlling to repeat missions a few times to get all of the shiny loot out of it. And as a free to play game, all you have to lose is your time. Unfortunately it lacks in it's new player experience and will require the

I give a thumbs down because of the developer issues. This is a fun game that I enjoyed up to a point when I decided to quit. If you want to keep playing and spend additional time breeding and building by all means feel free. Where I really take issue is with developers putting out paid expansions on an unfinished game that I paid to back. Also lag is completely game breaking if there are more than 15-20 people on a server. Updates are never on time and bugs don’t seem to ever get addressed. Hackers are not banned or penalized when caught. You can’t turn off chat and there are trolls constantly baiting people.
I really liked the beginning of this game. When you start off it is fun to explore and build up your base/character. My brother and I were relatively successful with just two people on a PVE server. As you progress it becomes exceedingly difficult to level up without spending literally hundreds of hours trudging through and near impossible to gather enough resources to do any of the cool stuff without working with a few other players.
There’s two ways to play
PVP involves joining the biggest gang on the server so as not to get slaughtered every 10 seconds by jerks. Basically it sucks, read the other hundreds of reviews about it.
PVE
No one can hurt you so you can build up a nice creative base and tame a bunch of dinos. This is what I did. I played for 450 hours total and basically stopped because to go any further in the game would require me to dedicate my life to it.
Beginning Game (0-200 hours)
A lot of fun, you spend time building small bases, exploring, getting eaten, hunting, etc.
Middle Game (200-500 hours)
Takes a lot of time to gather materials to do anything cool like building giant castles or taming bigger better dinos. You need help to do this. You cannot leave the game for more than 2 to 3 days because your dinos will starve to death while you live your real life.
Middle Game (500-1000 hours)
There were people on my server putting in 60+ hours a week to raise and breed dinos. Seriously life sucking game at this point and there’s no way around it. Breeding literally takes days with more supervision than a real life human baby, I’m not exaggerating.
End Game (1000+ hours)
It really isn’t until this point that you can even start to get those cool laser beams they advertise. You need help, period. Getting the high tech stuff requires multiple boss killings which flat out can’t be done without a team of high level players and high level dinos. But if you made it that far hat’s off to you.

Warframe. This game is amazing, to say the least. The AI was actually smart, and ran away to get off a good shot when I rushed up with my amazing Excalibur warframe with a huge sword out. The characters are very cool, and I found infinite pleasure in watching a surprised enemy slowly stumble back after I chopped the top half of his body off, watching in gruesome detail, thanks to the incredible graphics, that would put most $60 games to shame. Now, moving on to the bad things. The other characters were in fact locked behing the disgusting, overpriced paywall, angering me incredibly. I'm about 9 hours into this game, and I have still noticed little to no variety about the enemy characters. Every few missions, you find one new enemy character, but that usually only shows up for one or two missions, isn't exciting, and they are few and far between.
In conclusion, I shall quickly recap on what I think about Warframe. Graphics: 9/10.  Variety:6/10.  Sound: 7.5/10. Characters: 8/10. AI: 8.5/10.      Overall rating: 8.3916.        Warframe, recommended to any fan of RPG's or TPS's.

Ark Review: Primite Plus
Initially I started playing this game about a month ago now, and today I still play almost religiously everyday. I love the design, I love dinosaurs, and as well I love the experience of an open world building survival.
Primitve plus is the lack of advanced tech that is the soul of the base game. Its basicly iron tools and early muskets as the most advanced ingrams. Early into the game everything was working perfect, except rubber banding, and I barely noticed things were not included yet such as therizenosaur saddles or even a bit later recurve bows. The more I got intune with how to play the game, the more I started to notice a lack of contant that was already in the game. Feathers are now missing, prime ribs don't even exist, and most importantly the scissors to cut my gross looking hair (recent).
Ark has a lot of replayability but its full of jerks and land grabbing hippies. The people who pillar their land and remove all the trees with foundations destroys a lot of content on the maps and severly lags the game. Its a mechanic in the game that should be refined and not abused so obsurdly. noobs need places to live near others to gain knowledge and learn to play. As to conlcude my semi bad review, and its not all bad; The game has a lot of things going for it like flying a bird and taking on a trex with a bear, but im still addicted its just the game has to have updates to primitive plus and the broken content.
In short;
Pros: replay content is here, free roam construction, dinosaurs, tough luck, and good times if youre playing with friends.
Cons: Players can be jerks (its the internet dont expect much), broken content is in the game and not even temporarily removed till fixed, and so many people pillar and foundation everything that it destroys the map and the mineable resources.

Fun gameplay, but a MAJOR grind.
Graphics:
The locations, character models, everything is VERY beautiful, even on low settings.  The weapons have great effects, the card mods look like those nice holograohic trading cards.  This game is just nice too look at.  I can get lost in the areas just looking at stuff.  I have died a few times in the Void simply because of this, ha ha.
Sound:
Everything in this game sounds just plain nice.  The voicework is top notch and great.  The music is very nice to listen to at all times (my favs are the Orokin themes) and the ambiance just works so well for each area.  I get a chuckle at the grineer voices when I sneak up on them (it sounds like they say "OH NO" when they find me there).  The soundwork just helps this game.
Controls:
I use a controller to play this and aside form the tutorial still telling me the keyboard buttons, I have no complaints with the controls, and am happy that the game recognizes the xbox 360 controller.  The controls workl quite well and I find myself being able to jump around, slide, dodge and run like a ninja.  It feels good being able to slide into a sneak and stealtkill an enemy.  More action games should look at this game's controls for inspiration.
Gameplay:
Oh dear...  This is where the issue comes.  It's been all glowing so far, but here is where I hit the snag.
You see, the main issue of this game is there is no real goal, other than to grind.  No story for WHY you're doing what you do, other than to make money.  You start as a tenno that just awakened, just as Captain Vor plants the ascaris on you.  The first set of story missions is you trying to get it off.  Once you complete that set missions, you are given a few new quests to run, but those require grinding in order to finish.  And if you finish them, and want more, you must GRIND for the parts to make the keys to acess the quests.  That's right.  You don't talk to someone and get it.  You have to grind for it.  You literally grind for EVERYTHING in this game.  Weapons, frames, everything requires a grind.  Which wouldn't be so bad if it weren't for that in order to rank up, you have to keep leveing things up.  So you have to keep getting new stuff and leveing it up, which means more grinding to make the stuff, then waiting the parts to craft to so you can craft the main thing, all of which takes btween 12-72 hours!
OR, you can just buy it with platinum (real money).  You can buy the missions, the weapons, the frames, and the skins.  And if a new frame comes out, you can pay for Prime Access and avoid the massive grind to get it.  Now, I like that players can trade the primes parts for platinum, which means there's no auction house for the R.M.T.s and general asshats can go to inflate the game's economy like in most mmos.  It also helps the grind a bit for some players who wants the primes, but don't have enough platinum to buy it outright.
But this game's business is simply grind or pay.  Grinding is usually only for just gaining a new levels for the next quest or to get endgame gear.  Grinding shouldn't be happening to just to UNLOCK a key for a new set of missions or just to get a new rank.
I WANTED to like this game, and I played for a decent amount of time.  But the grind to do anything and the general lack of an overall story just grinded my ability to enjoy this game.  If you enjoy the type of gameplay this game offers, but all means, try it!  But if you can't stand having to grind for EVERYTHING, skip it, or be prepared to pay.

Honestly, I thought this game was amazing.
The mods for it are awesome, the people that make them are even moreso. The graphics are stunning, yet still need optimization, but that all comes in time. It slowly improves.
The devs stick to the game well enough, but the recent price hike just absolutely insults the community and everyone who bought the game, creating a vast, barren ravine between the devs and the people. Wildcard did the right move at the worst possible time imaginable, but that doesn't remove the now-blaring fact that this game is a money-grab and a pilot for further infestations of Studio Wildcard's "games". You can't be an indie and expect people to pay AAA prices for an indie game. That is not how this works and (I hope to Lord Gaben) will never work like that. You ♥♥♥♥ed up, Wildcard.
But at first, it truly was paradise: I felt like I was walking in John Hammond's Jurassic Park.
Other than that, the game is just another grind-to-the-top-and-do-it-all-again deal, with no reward other than the work you've done and the time you've wasted. The game becomes linear, you figure out how to do things and how to get them done quicker each time, eventually draining the fun. The grinds become mindless timewarps for resources and dinos, eventually being without feeling or ambition. The community, especially from across the ponds, is cancer and poisonous, and won't bat an eye to destroy all you own and kill every companion you've made, all for the effort of their own progress. The only solace, fun, and saving grace you can have are on the unofficial PVE servers, where the real community exists for Ark. They are few, but they are free. You can actually go over to your neighbors for a kibble and not get shot in the a** by an autoturret or a Plant X. But, other than those few goldmines, the game becomes empty and punishing.
I find that the DLC is worthless since the newest Tek additions are broken in and unable to obtain in said DLC's. Primitive is a joke, might work for singleplayer & multiplayer but non-dedicated co-op is a bust. Not sure what Wildcard has in store for us with this game or any other they come up with.
They made Troodons the most pathetic dino in the game since people complained about them too much, so now we have those that only attack at night and won't come near you if you have a torch out. I honestly just respected them and stayed clear unless I was certain I could take them on, so they didn't bother me all that much.
7/7/17 EDIT: With the recent price increase, it is officially overpriced in comparison to the headache-to-fun ratio. If you like grinds and having to redo everything every time a dino gets killed or you get raided, go right ahead and pay $60 for this game. But if you're looking for a fun time, I would suggest a game with actual human beings as devs. However, you can actually see accomplishments in PVE better than the official servers. It
be worth it to play PVP if there was a ranking system to show how you stand in comparison to other survivors (like PUBG), but that's not a thing and will never be a thing in this game. Survival of the Fittest, however, might be worth a look if that's your kind of thing. 2/10 would tame a dodo again.

I would like to start out this review by placing an *. The * being that my experiences may be different simply due to the way and whom I play the game with. My friend owns a private server, and myself as well as five other people play on it. This is going to be MUCH different than the playstyle of going into official servers and dealing with "alpha" tribes and trolls. That being said, I still feel like I should place this review as I don't have to feel like I need to give the game a "Bad review" because of bad players. Bad players do NOT make a game good or bad, the game itself does and this review is based on that.
So, I've played the game quite a bit. I really do enjoy the music, the graphics are simply amazing, the different animals each hold a function and/or use and with the RPG elements you are able to create the character you want to be. Want to be melee? Go for it. Want to be a cook? Upgrade crafting speed and watch everyone love your custom food. Build a big castle, or fancy boat, go cave exploring or just deal with survival on a day to day. This includes bosses as well.
I guess a good way of putting this review is what my group and I are currently doing. I'm breeding t-rexs to perfection whilst another friend works on raptors (for caves), another friend is working on metal and crystal gathering with another one working on building a wall around a very dangerous part of our base. It's okay, we have Donald Trump (The Jerboa) on top of the wall guiding us, so it will be fine. This is all going to get us set up for going for Tek-tier equipment as well as getting the gear necessary to go into a particular cave without dying horribly to poisoned gas. Each one of us is "doing their own thang" but all toward an end goal which will be glorious.
The game also lends itself to some pretty sureal moments. The server owner and I were off trying to get leech blood to go fishing. It was night, and all we had was each other and a standing torch in the middle of nowhere near a thicket of trees. We're talking and all of a sudden, my friend says: ".... Run.... RUN!!!" and I was wondering what was going on, but when he says run it's generally a good idea to do so. So we run, in the pitch darkness, away from our safe light and warmth. Three allosaurus's come into view near the torch we were just at; he saw the sillouettes of them coming through the trees toward us - shades in the night. It was glorious.
There are some bad things with the game, not counting official server alpha tribe stuff, but they're mostly insignificant compared to the actual game. One of which, is you need a pretty good computer to run this well. The developers are focusing more on actually getting the game fleshed out before focusing on optimizations. If you ask the owner of the server I play on, he'll say: "They're not game developers, they're f'n artists making a game!" It looks really, really nice.
Other things include some bugs such as in one particular cave there is a place where it teleports you randomly back to the surface. It's annoying, but not game breaking. The times for things such as breeding dinos are EXTREMELY long, as they intend you to have a tribe to help take care of animals (or fight bosses... they can be quite hard) but there are server options you can utilize to make it more bareable. For example, we have 8x growth, so dinos will grow up 8x faster. Instead of taking literally 4 days of RL time to grow a rex, it only takes 12 hours and 12 minutes. (As long as you have one friend, it's not that bad and you can customize it so it could take like 45 minutes if you're that strapped for time.)
The last thing I want to state could be considered a pro or con. There are 4 different difficulties for the game, with higher difficulties not only raising the dino levels (30 on easy, 60 on normal, 90 on hard, 120 on very hard; also means your tames will be better) but increasing quality of loot found in things such as beacons. That same server owning friend also states pretty regularly: "Ark is the kind of game that likes to f*** you  at the worst possible times." This came from when he was taming a level 120 anky (ankylosaurus) and when it was about 5 minutes being done, a random Carno (Carnotaurus) ran up and bit it once, lowering the taming effectiveness from about 97% to 30%, losing out on about 30 levels and making it worthless. Another friend, the metal gathering one, was constantly beset by troodons and Therizinosaurus and ended up needing to get a pair of mated carnos as bodyguards. Once he got those, it was much easier.
All in all, a great game. I greatly look forward to see it progress, and the mod scene is pretty amazing. From new dinos to better ways of building (Seriously, get S+ building if you get the game. It's a godsend), you'll be good.
(Again, I do not play on official servers. In my opinon, editing the server files slightly and playing with a group of friends is the best way to do it. You don't have to deal with the whole "Highest level and best geared possible people entering newbie areas and torching all your stuff and killing your dinos just for a laugh" going on. Seriously, you do not need to bring a tek-rifle to kill my dodo, you sons of....)

This review is for ONE aspect of the game:
with my girlfriend.
I don't like teh hardc0rez PvP survival, so I don't play it. I like the game less punishing, so I configured a server to be the way I wanted it.
As such, my girlfriend and I are having great fun with this game. It's a game where we can explore, build camps, hunt, tame (and ride) dinosaurs together in a gorgeous environment. As a single player game locally, or in small groups of good friends, this game fits my taste well. Most aspects are configurable, and even more are modable, so you can make the game as easy or hard as you want.
... just be prepared to lose any and all dinos you tame. It is more likely than not to happen, but the good news is you can always tame more.
It has its (incredibly) frustrating points, particularly when you and your dinos die "unfairly" because of glitches, bugs, crashes and poor AI, but overall I feel the game makes up for it.
It was not effortless to set up a dedicated server. Even as a tech-savvy gamer working in IT, and following the many online guides, it was not straight forward. Often the server would not be in the list, with no clue as to why. Sometimes Steam would show it in the servers list, but the game would not. Sometimes you could connect through Steam, other times not. Be prepared to do some leg work, read many posts on the topic, and for lots of trial and error (which can take a while since it can easily take 5-15 mins every time you want to boot the server again to try a new ini tweak).
Local multiplayer with a non-dedicated server is possible, but the thether distance made it too frustrating in the long run. The tether means that the person joining the host of the game can never move further than a certain distance from the host. Sometimes you simply get yanked to the host, which is unfortunate when the host is flying over the deep sea, with sharks. Big sharks. Really big sharks.

Fun gameplay, but a MAJOR grind.
Graphics:
The locations, character models, everything is VERY beautiful, even on low settings.  The weapons have great effects, the card mods look like those nice holograohic trading cards.  This game is just nice too look at.  I can get lost in the areas just looking at stuff.  I have died a few times in the Void simply because of this, ha ha.
Sound:
Everything in this game sounds just plain nice.  The voicework is top notch and great.  The music is very nice to listen to at all times (my favs are the Orokin themes) and the ambiance just works so well for each area.  I get a chuckle at the grineer voices when I sneak up on them (it sounds like they say "OH NO" when they find me there).  The soundwork just helps this game.
Controls:
I use a controller to play this and aside form the tutorial still telling me the keyboard buttons, I have no complaints with the controls, and am happy that the game recognizes the xbox 360 controller.  The controls workl quite well and I find myself being able to jump around, slide, dodge and run like a ninja.  It feels good being able to slide into a sneak and stealtkill an enemy.  More action games should look at this game's controls for inspiration.
Gameplay:
Oh dear...  This is where the issue comes.  It's been all glowing so far, but here is where I hit the snag.
You see, the main issue of this game is there is no real goal, other than to grind.  No story for WHY you're doing what you do, other than to make money.  You start as a tenno that just awakened, just as Captain Vor plants the ascaris on you.  The first set of story missions is you trying to get it off.  Once you complete that set missions, you are given a few new quests to run, but those require grinding in order to finish.  And if you finish them, and want more, you must GRIND for the parts to make the keys to acess the quests.  That's right.  You don't talk to someone and get it.  You have to grind for it.  You literally grind for EVERYTHING in this game.  Weapons, frames, everything requires a grind.  Which wouldn't be so bad if it weren't for that in order to rank up, you have to keep leveing things up.  So you have to keep getting new stuff and leveing it up, which means more grinding to make the stuff, then waiting the parts to craft to so you can craft the main thing, all of which takes btween 12-72 hours!
OR, you can just buy it with platinum (real money).  You can buy the missions, the weapons, the frames, and the skins.  And if a new frame comes out, you can pay for Prime Access and avoid the massive grind to get it.  Now, I like that players can trade the primes parts for platinum, which means there's no auction house for the R.M.T.s and general asshats can go to inflate the game's economy like in most mmos.  It also helps the grind a bit for some players who wants the primes, but don't have enough platinum to buy it outright.
But this game's business is simply grind or pay.  Grinding is usually only for just gaining a new levels for the next quest or to get endgame gear.  Grinding shouldn't be happening to just to UNLOCK a key for a new set of missions or just to get a new rank.
I WANTED to like this game, and I played for a decent amount of time.  But the grind to do anything and the general lack of an overall story just grinded my ability to enjoy this game.  If you enjoy the type of gameplay this game offers, but all means, try it!  But if you can't stand having to grind for EVERYTHING, skip it, or be prepared to pay.
