ARK: Survival Evolved is in itself an interesting concept but because of its multiple flaws it's a game that I have quickly abandonned and do not plan to get back to. My personal experience of "ARK" has been running -and playing- a private server.
First of all, why did I decide to create a private server? So that I don't get my stuff stolen, because I've read countless reviews of frustrated people losing all their♥♥♥♥♥♥to other players, often completely unknown to them, stabbing them in the back.
Running a server:
Running a server is very unintuitive. The documentation is very vague and unneccessarily complex. The server command box doesn't offer important stats, such as performance drops and user commands. There is litterally NOTHING you can do from the server window once it's started, except closing it (with the "X" button). Each time Ark gets an update, you need to manually close the server, update it, and relaunch it. Since it happens often and virtually at ANY time, you'll soon be looking into shady .bat files that check for updates at specific intervals, close the ARK process, and install the updates. More often than not, the server will run in issues resulting in you, the admin, having to manually restart the server.
Summary of running a server: It's very cumbersome, unintuitive and difficult to automate/self-sustain without requiring user intervention. The opposite of what running a server should be.
Playing the game:
-Ridiculous efforts for little rewards
The game is far from balanced. Grinding takes hours, as does taming dinos and doing virtually anything. Any kind of food does NOT last forever so if you don't play, you'll see a lot of your resources vanishing into thin air. For someone like me with a busy lifestyle, playing this game made me felt like I had to play it all the time or I'd just lose all the effort I put into it. This was the biggest turnoff for me.
-Punishing the player
Being killed in the game heavily punishes the player. It doesn't stop at your death. It is virtually impossible to get your stuff back since the dino that killed you is most likely sitting on top of your bag of goodies. Naked and vulnerable, you'll just get killed trying to get your stuff back... IF you can even manage to find it. Which brings me to the next point:
-The UI is T.E.R.R.I.B.L.E
The game's UI is a complete disorganized mess. It is not intuitive, doesn't always work as you think it should and is overly complicated. There's too many options and sliders in virtually every menu. It could be organized a lot better. When you die (see point above), it's very difficult to find back your stuff since you don't have a point telling you where you died, especially if it's night.
-Night is D.A.R.K.
If you have a remotely good monitor with good contrast ratio, you can't see anything at night. This is the game I have played in which the night is the darkest. There is no option in the video settings to adjust gamma/brightness. The only way is to write it in the command line.
-Performance is abysmal
This is the videogame that takes the most computer power in the world. I have a GTX 970 and I have to play on the lowest settings to retain a good framerate. But I can play remotely any other game on Ultra settings.
Overwall, I do not enjoy this game and would not recommend it. There are a lot of other games on the market which are a lot better in term of experience and are way more polished. I do understand that a lot of people have found genuine appeal in this game, but its flaws throw me off.

I expected space ninjas, instead I got
kids controlling space marine armor. The gameplay boils down to a third-person shooter with some fancy additions.
You have the melee combat(the one thing that I thought would be good) which is♥♥♥♥♥and even with the stances(that you have to grind for to drop) don't add any variety since melee in this game is pretty useless. Not to mention guns do the same job better and faster.
There's the parkour which is a nice idea, if it was actually part of the core gameplay. Its only ever used in between shooting at things to get from point A to B while mashing sprint and jump and holding forward. Shame because I liked the environments and the level design but the combat breaks both of those and makes them inconsequential.
The shooty parts aren't that bad, pretty regular for a third-person shooter. See, I switched from Payday 2 after the Safes update and I can say that I still prefer Payday 2's shooting over Warframe's. The shooting clashes with the space ninja theme and as mentioned, stops the flow of the parkour system.
Weapons and the warframes themselves do not have much variety, either. Only a select few are ever useful and the rest are just trash for Mastery Level points. Warframes may differ in stats and skills but in the end those skills(the useful ones) are just there to make shooting things easier and faster, all to grind faster to get something that you need to drop, after which you do the whole process over and over again. Its a gear threadmill where you keep grinding to get the shiniest weapon and to get the best stats so you can... parade it around town, I guess? Except the game doesn't really let you do that. Once you max out whatever weapons and frame you prefer, there is nothing left to do except to grind missions and wait for new content to grind for again. It links in with their weapons customization where you grind even more by resetting your weapon level back to one so you can fit in more mods.
Instead of the usual RPG character level progression for games like these, you get mods that let you customize weapons and frames to your liking, which is a good idea, if the system was actually handled for uniqueness between each player. Instead you get strict mod requirements set by the community to make your weapon or frame effective. Then again, this is just the difficulty in balancing the game, its not something that's easily resolved. There will always be a most effective and efficient build. The main problem is that you have to grind for the mods to drop, then grind again to level the mods. Then grind your weapons/frames to be able to put the mods in. This goes on and on and on. Removing the usual level progression, only to replace it with the same concept with even more grinding isn't exactly innovative. Its just busywork.
Then you have the missions, where you do mission nodes once and forget them forever except when alerts come out or when its one of those nodes that you can grind materials for. You get the defense missions where you defend something or somethings(Defense, Mobile defense, interception, hijack) for an amount of time. You have variations of kill everyone missions(exterminate, survival, crossfire) and kill one-guy types of missions(assassinate, capture). You also get missions where you follow objective markers, do something then escape(spy, rescue, deception) Not much of a difference between them, although the popular ones are obviously survival, defense and assassination which are perfect for grinding, until you realize that drops are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t.
There are bosses in this game too, which are the targets for assassination missions. They just end up being boring fights against some guy with tons of HP and probably have some gimmick to beating them. Still, nothing beats shoot-them-till-they-die tactics. Bosses in this game just end up being tedious bullet sponges that drop♥♥♥♥♥♥you want. One example of these bosses is Lephantis, which the community hyped to be a pretty good boss fight. Except its not. Its a boring♥♥♥♥♥fight where you wait for the head(s) to pop out after 5 years, shoot them until they hide again, rinse and repeat 3 times until they all die and phase 2 happens where you fight all 3 heads at the same time. Again, shoot them until they die. How the ♥♥♥♥ is this good boss design? My expectations instantly went down the drain. It wasn't even a challenge. It was a tedious fight where you wait for it to show its red glowy weak spots so you can shoot them. Pretty generic boss design and they somehow made it very disappointing. The fight just abruptly ends, you collect your loot then escape just so you can do it again so it drops the blueprints you need.
Stealth missions are also present in Spy missions and to a certain extent, Rescue. Spy missions are the only fun missions where you get to explore the level. The game makes good use of its level design and allows you to use the parkour system to its fullest. Too bad it gets boring pretty quick. Actually, if they just took the idea of the security puzzles and implement it to other missions, the game wouldn't be repetitive and the grind wouldn't be just as bad with interesting missions.
A shame, really. If they focused on making the melee combat good and have it flow with the parkour system, combine it with the good level design and put them in interesting missions, this would have been a pretty enjoyable and good game.
The whole identity of this game is grinding. Lots and lots of grinding. If that's your cup of tea, then good for you, you'll probably enjoy this game more than I did.

Do you enjoy spending hours waiting to connect to a server? Hours downloading mods? Hours taming dinosaurs?
Then this is the game for you. Once you get it working, this game is unsurpassed in terms of dinosaurs survival games. Trust me, I go out of my way to buy all the dinosaur games I can find.
If you play on an Offical (non-modded) server, be ready to spend hours (I'm not kidding, taming a high level bronto can take upwards of 7 hours and you need to be watching it to make sure it doesn't wake up the WHOLE TIME) and hours of your life taming critters only to have them get rekt in a moment by an alpha rex.
If you play on Unofficial (modded) servers, then you can actually have fun in short stretches. That is, if you can download all the mods required before their creators update them. But the mods make the game playable, and it's fantastically fun and so so so addicting once you get into it.
You NEED to have someone show you how to play, however. I had this game for six months before I played it because it's so confusing and there's really no tutorial. But if you can find a friend who's been playing this game for a while, or get on a server with a friendly community, then it doesn't take too long to learn the ropes. And the wiki is pretty decent too.
All in all, I'd recommend this game to anyone who loves dinosaurs. If you don't love dinosaurs, well that's basically the entire appeal of the game. I'm personally a PvE player so I can't speak to any PvP experiences, but they look pretty cool.

Prepare to journey to the magical land of Space-Japan, where you will fight an inbred clone army, a conglomerate of corporations that construct mecha from the remains of your fallen allies, and hentai monsters that will make even the most abstinate boy or girl cream their pantsu.
You are a space ninja, or a "Tenno" as the game calls you, but everyone knows that space ninja sounds better, and that ten is a terrible number, hence "ten" and "no." Anyways, there are lots of weapons and different kinds of space ninjas, each with differing appearances, stats, and abilities that make them unique. You have primary weapons (can be anything from a bow and arrow to the mighty "straight outta World War II" soma), you have secondary weapons (sidearms) and you have melee weapons. Melee is really fun. You have staffs, whips, brass knuckles for your hands AND feet (giggity) and the mighty Nikana, which is glorious moon-bathed Space Nippon steel. Melee is visceral, despite there being little to no bloodspray; you quite literally rend enemies limb from limb, and can cut them in half with your glorious space katana! Combat is great, and there is parkour! What great ninja game would be complete without parkour?! Also, microtransactions. They aren't required, but if you haven't the patience to farm for materials to upgrade your weapons (forma and "potatoes"), they are there. You can purchase weapons, skins, paints, and the upgrade materials with platinum, the microtransaction currency that you purchase. It all comes down to time vs convenience.
Anyways, venture to space Japan today, and receive a body pillow of the oh-so-cute hentai faction, the infested.

Today, as of late 2017, I have to say that this game has gone down a very continual negative spiral.  It has gotten more than frustrating, more than time wasting, it has become mysoginistic to play this game.  The primary reason is instability.  The developers need to establish more organization to when they update their game and when their paid modders update as well.  I can't play multiplayer thanks to the incredibly poor quality experience that is.  South Koreans by teams of 40 are wiping servers meanwhile average joes erect towers of irrigation reaching the highest point on the map, not only removing immersion, but removing the indivual's chance of success or progress.  Single player or small team coop are ruined by the fact that every single FU**ING day one mod or another which by any right minded developer should have already been integrated into the core game is updated separately and all progress in said game involving said updated mod is mysteriously wiped.  Not to mention how unreliable every update and patch seems to be.  Where this game used to be fun and playable in its early access it has actually grown to contain innumerable glitches, bugs, and problems.  The developers who once had a passion for creating fun diverse gameplay are either gone, dead or dead inside, because clearly gameplay is the last of their priorities today.  If they paid even a quarter of the attention to their playerbase as they used to, all these problems would be gone.  As a sad representation of how far this game has turned around, I will leave my previous review from a year and a half ago.  The game was fun, once.  May the developers find it in their hearts to focus on the right things again, I will erase this top paragraph and leave the bottom once again.
Old Review from before 2017:
First I would like to say that this is one of the greatest games I have ever played.  I have been involved in this game for years now and have sunk far more hours into this game than Steam has on record due to the fact that I have experience playing online and offline.  It has incredible graphics, diverse, rewarding yet unforgiving gameplay, and hundreds upon hundreds of hours worth of content.  There is an active modding community and the game lays out a great foundation for a multitude of multiplayer experiences.  If you are torn about purchasing this game, or unsure of its worth, read on.  The remaining review is my response to the negative reviews plaguing the reputation of this deservedly illustrious game.
People have found complaint in the fact that official servers are being crowded with griefers or OP tribes, and accuse the developers of conspiring this plot in order to remove their maintenance of the official servers from their budget.  Well I say to that, "SO WHAT!"  If the developers did somehow come up with a genius plot to manage you sheople to stop using official servers.... JUST GO TO AN UNOFFICIAL SERVER!  The developers HAVE to manage the finances to some extent.  The player base is extremely unappreciative of the quality of service they are receiving from these developers.  For the price, this game provides more content than that of any other big name game and the players writing these negative reviews are unwilling to pay a 15 dollar toll to gain access to a small portion of the wealth of added content these kind and hard working developers bring in ALMOST EVERY MONTH.
Secondly I just want to say that it is clear that the developers are not just creating a wishing well of an early access for players to throw money into.  In spite of the recent trend and following hype centered around early access, this game stands as a testament to the potentially positive outcome of an early access game.  Nothing in life is perfect, not this game, not its developers, and certainly not its player base.  The vast majority of the negative reviewers to this game appear to me as unintelligent and entitled followers of the anti-early-access trend.  Sadly, developers have to concern themselves with the semantics of "This game is early-access!" versus "This game is two years old!" in order to sell.

At the end of the day, people forget two major things which I will list here.  One, regardless of the semantics, (release date, early access, paid DLC) this game has some of the best graphics, most diverse gameplay, and wide range of content on the gaming market.  Two, the developers have to make a profit, and in spite of their ability to provide millions of people with more enjoyment than most other game developers on the market even care to imagine, the player base WHINES when they have to pay for DLC.  Players whine and complain because, "OH, they released a paid DLC before the game was finished, and with all the bugs it already has!"  Rather, they should be thanking the developers and eager to provide such a minimal and trivial financial compensation for their hard, ground-breaking work in developing a game with such beautiful graphics and diverse playstyles.  This game is more bang for your buck than the other reviews will ever let on.
Due to the fact that this game is starting to receive mixed reviews, I have a legitimate concern.  My concern is that the entertainment industry, specifically involved in gaming is going to suffer from these reviews.  Similarly to how the news and media have suffered from ratings.  People don't know what's good for them.  When an accurate news report is released, allowing the public a glimpse of reality, people are bored.  So the news becomes the destructive, misinforming hype-monster that it is today.  When a good game comes out, people really enjoy it, you still have an audience of idiots who blame the developers for the players' actions.  You still have players who don't want to pay a dime to the company that makes a living providing them with this game.  My concern, or fear... Maybe even a prediction, is that good games like this will fall under the radar as they are washed out like combat veterans get washed out by stolen valor or real news stories are washed out by dramatic, exaggerated, subjective news.
TL;DR:  BUY IT

My basic guideline for if a game is worth it is if I get an hour of play per dollar spent on it. In the last two weeks alone I have 82 hours and 341 hours on record. So I've already passed that mark, and I have thoroughly enjoyed the game.
First off, with the other reviews mentioning that people from other servers can come and wreck your♥♥♥♥♥♥while you are sleeping, they are 100% correct. They added that late december I believe and that update has been widely regarded as pants-on-head ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. However for the most part that is limited to Official servers only. If you run your own server you have the option to disable that. Or if you play single player, you don't have to worry about it.
Graphics. Looks great, but has some beefy requirements if you want to turn all the sliders to the max. Some practical issues with hitboxes and clipping but nothing that will seriously detract from the immersion any more than any other game.
Sound. Awesome, make sure you have some good headphones because they paid attention to the little details and sound can be a very important aspect of the game. The music is all right, but sounds kind of bland like most video game music. I generally turn that off after the first few hours.
Gameplay. Wake up naked on a beach. Punch trees, get wood. Craft♥♥♥♥♥♥ rule the world (server). Sounds simple but it isn't. Almost 80 creatures in the game to interact with each with their own abilities and personalities (admittedly there are like 5 behaviour types so not so much in actuality), and you can tame the majority of them. Lots of items to craft and each has their own use. I would prefer more aesthetic items in terms of base building but thats personal preference, and there is always mods. I find combat a little limiting, there is a large focus on ranged combat (because most sane people wouldn't want to go hitting a trex with a sword), and your options are either a bow, crossbow, or longneck rifle (elephant gun) for ranged, and pike or sword for melee. There are higher tier guns but I find they just don't get used that often, if at all.
Dev support. Yeah they are constant with the updates, not involved in the community outside my own server so I'm not qualified to say anything more.
Overall if you want a good survival game, this is one. You have the options of selecting from vanilla Official servers or UnOfficial servers which can be vanilla or modified to suit their owners tastes. Most (All) Official PvP servers are ruled by hostile Alpha tribes, that will always tell you:
"You are not welcome on this server, go away or get wiped"
"This server is overpopulated, we do not allow new players to join. You are not welcome here."
"This server is chinese only, if you don't have an invitation leave our server now."
Please note these are all official servers, this is the game you bought.

No matter what you build and where you hide, they will eventually find and wipe you with no effort whatsoever. As you have nothing to defend yourself with against alpha tribes. Even if you build auto turrets and a 4 wall layered base, they simply come with a quetzal and a turtle to take aggro and soak up the bullets and destroy it in matter of seconds. Where you can only stand there and watch them do it.
The game is greatly imbalanced towards new players. And alpha tribes gain more and more strength with each patch, and new players have nothing to defend themselves with. Now Tek tier came, and who do you think is going to profit from it, new players or alpha tribes?
Its a shame that you will pay money for a game, where other people won't even let you play. Its just like throwing money out of a window as even though you buy the game you wont be able to play it.
Now we come to PvE servers. If you try to avoid being wiped by playing in a PvE server, you will be dissapointed again. The PvE servers are filled with trash and ruins. No matter where you go its just filled with debris. But not only that, in PvE players intentionally block spawns of various resources where due to being unable to destroy those structures, you won't be able to do anything against it, as there are no admins to clear those places up.
Overall I give 10/10 for the base gameplay itself. And 0/10 for playability.
Maybe if you can buy your own server or enjoy playing single player then this game might be for you.
But otherwise I do not recommend buying it untill wildcard decides to balance the game, and make new players able to defend themselves somehow.

Alright, so I'll keep this as short as I can. I have played both the PC and PS4 versions of this game, and the jury is out. For one thing, the graphics are AMAZING no matter what system you play it on. However, If you expect to run it on pc and enjoy the wonderful graphics, you WILL have to sink money into an excellent graphics card. I use the Geforce GTX 960 graphics card and this game runs supremely well on it. But it cost me a significant some of money to get the darn thing, so for arguments sake the PS4 is more cost effective with a *slight* graphics downgrade. As for the gameplay, I use the same controller for both (using DS4 to mod the controller) and got the same result. If you have friends that also want to play the game, or if you want to play with randoms, the PC is the way to go.  There is a SIGNIFICANTLY bigger community on PC that will be able to support you as the missions get tougher. Through and through, I'd qualify the argument like this: The more people you want involved, stick with PC. However, if you prefer solo grinding then go with the PS4.
As per the Gameplay: It's definilty a "freemium" game. You will crunch through the first few planets on you're own and feel like you're a BOSS. Then you will eventually get to a point (depending on how good you are at third person shooters) where the difficulty spikes up and you'll start considering getting better weapons. Oh! You wanted weapons/new warframes? I'm sorry, you'll either have to grind for rare resources for hours on end in easier planets getting little to no XP only to have wait an additional day or three to get it, or by it using platinum. Using the cost of the frost warframe as our example of platinum expenses, it would cost me about 25$ to buy him lock, stock and barrel. Yes, you can get him for free. But you'll have to wait till you're on Ceres to farm the final boss there (which is difficult) to get the one, random part per boss fight, buy the 25,000 credit blueprint, get the resources for him, and assemble it all in the foundry for 3 REAL TIME days. Now it my sound like I'm hacked off about it, but truth betold i'm not. It's merely a tedium you have to get through, and if that's you're thing then EXCELLENT!! You have found your game.
Alright, so that's all I got. Hope this review clarfied a few things for you. Enjoy the Game!

I personally really enjoy this game, though I haven't dedicated as many hours as some others have. While I think it's fun, there are some aspects of it which I think leave much to be desired. I want to try and give a helpful and fair review based on my own experience playing the game.
Pros:
- As a lover of dinosaurs and prehistoric/extinct creatures this is what initially drew me to the game. It is a unique experience in which you must survive a harsh environment where you will be hunted by these animals and other players. It is unique in that you are given the ability to tame these creatures and use them as mounts, which is really badass and cool af in my opinion.
- The game frequently updates and is always adding new content to the game like new creatures and objects, and there are really fun events as well. Sometimes if I burn myself out on playing this game, I will leave it alone for a while and come back later to find that it has updated with a lot more content.
- Graphically the game is gorgeous [if you have your settings on high] and I have a lot of fun just exploring the different maps for an hour or two, finding secret hidden gems and exploring caves and neat places to make a base at.
- There is so much content and so many things to do with how many items there are in game. It is really fun to build and challenge your creativity with making a really awesome base if you have the time and patience for it.
Cons:
- PvP. I'm not normally fond of pvp games to begin with, but with this game it kinda takes my dislike for them to a whole new level. I normally play by myself or with friends on a non-dedicated server, because the people playing this game take it waaaay too seriously, and actually ruin the game for new players by being excessivly hostile and toxic. I've had it to where I just spawned in and was immediatly killed by another much higher level player. What's worse is now players are able to transfer over (I think) bases and dinosaurs with the warping mechanism to an official server and therefore they can completely wipe out anyone they see as a threat.
I would honestly recommend just playing on a PvE server or playing with your buddies on a non-dedicated/private server. It's much more enjoyable that way...
- Tbh, without the console and being able to spawn in items and give my self experience and speeding up taming/breeding/hatching I would probably tire of this game very quickly... all of these things take a very long time and if you don't have the patience for it you might not even bother getting this game, imo. It would be nice if things went a little bit quicker (like for example it takes actual irl hours to tame certain dinosaurs and it hoestly sucks)
These are the pros and cons I can think of off the top of my head- I know there are more, just take a look at the other reviews. This is just my input as another player of this game. o: I still find it enjoyable but yeeea, I can totally understand other people's distaste for it.

Ark survival evolved is an impressive, early access title that when I first saw gameplay futage of it, I could not believe it was still in development.
Ark is a survival sand box game, with dinosaurs as your main adversary, obstacle and friends. yes, I said friend because there is a taming mechanic, so that rex that is constantly chasing you and chomping you, if you use your head you can turn around, trank that sucker, tame it and be riding around on its back, letting it chomp anything that you desire or perceive as a threat. That plus the fact that nearly every dino has their own unique skill means there are many was that you could go about surviving.
This impressive first impression aside, there is also murmurings of other "Arks" as you see with the introduction of the Scorched Earth DLC, mythical creatures came to ark and not as bosses for the summoning. Wyvern, Rock golem and Deathworm all make an appearance in Scorched Earth, leaving many to wonder what this still developing game has instore for us in the future, as between the gigantic obelisks that make the dinos look like modern reptiles due to their sheer size, to what appears to be alien tech in the loot drops and said obelisks, as well as a tiny chip on your characters arm, you get a sense that there’s something going on here, and that this is not just about riding dinos.
The game can be... to put it simply, brutal, from the poisonous Titanoboa, to the ravenous insects and Rexs, I am not exaggerating when I say, that every carnivore on this island, want to see you dead so they can eat you. Even the adorable Compy, who follows you around seeming as benign as can be... will turn on you with a piranha like frenzy, if there are enough of them around, and that’s not even mentioning the actual Piranha.
However, many gamers today actually enjoy a game that doesn’t hold your hand and puts you through a challenge, myself being one of them, so that's not the reason for the mixed reviews.
The reason why this game is getting this negativity, are varied, however one of the main issues being players seeing an early access DLC as a money grab and questioning the reasoning for it. Personally, I do not think this to be a problem. If the developer decides they want to release a DLC then who am I to judge. I don't know why they did it.  So long as they finish the game I’m fine with it. I don't have to buy it.
However, what does seem like a legitimate problem, is the Issue that I like to call the Server wars...
If you read some of the negative reviews, then you likely already know something about this.
After Ark implemented a transfer system, Players were capable of moving from one server to another, now ordinarily this would not be a problem ... however there is curently no check, restraints or limits to this system, which means a powerful tribe can send their entire army of dinos to your server and wipe you out, not even caring and moving on to the next like a swarm of locusts... now this is a problem, as it takes a long time to make any progress in ark, between grinding for materials to hour to hours long taming sessions... there’s just no time to build up any means to retaliate when one of these tribes blows in, and everything you worked so hard for, hours of work and perseverance, gone in one night.
Because of this, the lead tribe on different servers, often called the Alpha tribes, have gone on the alert, Blocking off transfer points, fortifying defenses, and (and this it the big one) Wiping out any tribe that is a threat to them, or new players to their server because they could be a spy for the mega tribes. I personally felt some of the sting from this back lash. This causes the server to stagnate and pretty much be under the rule of this alpha tribe who if they decide to let you stay, will expect you to follow their rules, or else. And no more getting those loot drops i mentioned, because people can transfer through those, so they are blocked off too, meaning you can’t even leave if you want to, you have to start all over on another server if you want to get away from them. It's ironic because the mechanic that was supposed to allow free passage between any server actually made the game much more restrictive, and the devs don't seem to be doing anything about it...
Now I know that seems pretty bad... but there is a silver lining.
Ark has a growing and healthy modding community as well as unofficial servers and this particular problem, from what I can tell, seems to stay to the official servers, meaning you can get away from that nonsense and actually get to enjoy some cool mods in the prosses. Also, there are various tools that can be used, such as offline raid protection, that a server owner can set up to protect the people playing on his server, all you have to do is find one. Also, there is a single player offline mode, for those who want to get used to the game before having to deal with the human element.
So... in conclusion, Ark has its flaws and difficulties. It's still early access so expect some lag or glitches, but overall is an enjoyable game for players who want a game that forces them to play smart, and deal with challenges. It will throw you on your butt at times, costing you a favorite dino or some other painful backlash, however that's part of a survival game, and should be taken in stride, but the game itself is well worth a try. If you don't like it, you can refund it.

In terms of 'bang for your buck', I don't think there's any other game on Steam that provides as much value as Ark does.  The game itself is incredibly fun, especially the beginning.  Sure, you will die a lot at first and there will be some frustration at times, but you will be proud once you get that first hut built and tame up a few dino's (I recommend a trike!).
Controls, graphics, options, hundreds of servers, infinite replayability, active dev's/modders/playerbase.... what's not to like.
My only negative is the community.  There are a lot of very vocal nay-sayers (many who also have 100's of hours in the game) who are constantly negative and unsupportive of dev's who created a game they clearly love.  People were upset when Scorched Earth came out and review bombed the game, most of those negative reviews are unwarranted and have nothing to do with the game itself.
How can you not recommend a game that costs $30 full price and offers more than virtually every AAA title released in the last few years?
You can't!  So I highly recommend Ark to anyone who has even the slightest curiousity in it.

Warframe is a game that surpasses a lot of expectations for a F2P game, with it's stunning graphics to fluid combat system and creative mods, it's hard to frame this game as anything worse at all. Let's get to it then.
Pros:
*Combat is fun and always satisfying, from slicing a Grineer footsoldier in half with a katana to blowing up an osprey shield drone with a rifle, anything that moves save your teammates is something that can be sliced up.
*All Weapons designs look amazing with different categories of them including (machetes, swords, hammers, gauntlets, whips, daggers for melee and many more)
*You can choose lots of different warframes with different abilities, from the standard Excalibur, the sly Loki to the rampaging Rhino, there's always a warframe for you.
Cons:
*Some content in the game requires you to be premium (buying credit off the game's market to do this).
*Combat can get very repetitive very quickly, with little change to it except for the different maps.
*Creating different items in the foundry can be a long, slow process, taking up between 2-4 days depending on the type of item being forged.

Gameplay:
Warframe is a 4-player co-op PVE(with smaller PVP) Online third person shooter with fast paced movement and run and gun play in mind. The heart of the game is to build up your arsenal of Warframes and guns to be as versitile as possible. The gunplay and parkour, which makes up most of the game, is done extremely well and it flows together well. Another aspect of Warframe is its crafting and farming. While it does take an overly long time to craft (Minimum is around 6hrs for a weapon) and farming is a PAIN, it had to be done since this is a F2P(More on that in Marketing) game. The crafting and farming is still very rewarding while letting you experience the gunplay and parkour to let you craft. Last of all, the free constant updates to this already free game extend the life of this game. Overall, while the gameplay does have flaws, it does extremely well especially for a F2P game.
Score: 1.5/2
Story:
The Tenno, a warrior race of long ago, have begun to awake because of the turmoil and apocalyptic state of the galaxy. You must awaken and begin taking down alien baddies while building up your arsenal of weapons and Warframes. While the story is convoluted in multiple layers of gameplay and codex entries, the lore is crafted AMAZINGLY. The atmosphere and lore is interesting yet does not show much in most missions. Overall the story is hidden which hurts it very much.
Score: 1.5/2
Graphics:
*See screenshots for more* The graphics of Warframe have been updated since initial release and will keep being improved upon in the fututre. By no means does this game have the absolute best graphics. I would say these graphics are mediocre. Overall they are okay and can't compete wth most modern games but are by no means an eye sore.
Score: 1/2
Community:
Having a great community to a F2P MMO is key to gameplay. With the community DE has created, new players are welcomed and there are many places to trade, socialize, team up, and play. The chat has multiple tabs and is constantly under watch by a bot and a mod. The matchmaking is somewhat hard to find depeneding on where you live but that is not DE's fault. The trading and chat systems are mostly basic and have some flaws but are very good overall.
Score: 1.75/2
Replayability/Marketing:
The replayability of this game ties in to the marketing strategy of it. The F2P model does not hinder the ability for players as most of the game is PVE and only a small portion is PVP. The crafting and farming can be bought as the developers must make money. While having an understanding of this the replayabilty can go down or up depending on how much you like the gameplay. You must also take into affect how your attention span deals with this game. In my opinon it is done very well and I will personally always come back to this game.

Private Servers or don't bother. I played about 20 hours on public servers, and never got a single thing done without being murdered for fun by some schmuck on a flying dino sniping me from a mile away. Either that, or the two guys who ran around naked all the time with primitive weapons just killing everything for no apparent reason. I think they got me five or six times, never looted anything or destroyed anything, just killed me and continued aimlessly running around to spawn zones to kill new players.
So, I made my own server and played my own game for the rest of my 80 hours in Ark. It was glorious until I got lonely. I also messed heavily with settings. I made my settings what I would call "realistic". I wish I could have tweaked the settings to completely stop resource respawning, but it wasn't an option. Both I and the dinos hit harder, died faster, and lived more dangerous lives.
One thing I hated about the public servers was how long everything took, so I increased the speed of everything I could. It didn't take me 45 hours to tame a dino, nor did it take me 700 arrows to kill a T-Rex. Similarly, I died just as easily, so the game was much more tense overall and, for me, much more fun.
I'm considering jumping back in and making a private server for people who want play that way. People who want to thrive and work together, not just destroy and grief. I think Ark would be the best survival game out there if it didn't have the same pitfalls as all the rest--namely, players who make it their quest to make sure no one else has any fun.

Warframe is normally the type of game I avoid like a plague. I am not a fan of FPS and games with "space theme", Warframe didn't seem diferent to me soo I didn't play it until recently. Overall It is a great F2P game.
Story:
You are a Tenno a surviver of the old war you were put into a chamber in a deep slumber, one day Lotus rescued you from your cryostasis chamber, It seems a threat is rising.....The Grineer, with Lotus guidance you must find and destroy the Grineer.
Well this sums up what you know on the beggining of the game of course the story evolves but anything more than this would be spoiler.
Warframe:
Once in the game you can choose your warframe....what is a warframe? Well a warframe is (trying not to spoil anything soo this definition is going to pretty vague) an "Armor" or a "Weapon" you use to fight the grinner. You have a LOT of warframes to choose from (20+ if I am not wrong) each with 3 different abilities and a backstory soo diversity is pretty big. Of course to get these Warframes you have to craft them, but Its easy to get the materials you need to make them.
Combat:
The combat in warframe is something that amazed me, in the beggining you will have a bit of trouble getting used to the controlers but once you get the hang of It you will have a blast. You posses a primary weapon (a gun, bow, etc), a secondary weapon (throwing daggers, pistols, etc) and your melee weapon (a spear, sword, daggers, and soo much more).
Levels:
We currently have the Player Mastery Rank, Weapons/Archwing Rank and Warframe Rank.
Weapon/Archwing/Warframe Rank- When you use weapon/archings/warframes in a mission you get affinity (experience points), with enought affinity gained the weapon/archwings/warframe can rank up (max beying rank 30) the higher level more mods you can put one the weapon/archwings/warframe making It stronger.
Player Mastery Level-is a method of tracking a player's relative skill level and how much of the game's content they have experienced. Mastery is earned by leveling up companions/weapons, and Archwings/Warframes. When you have enought experience to level up you are required to do a test if you fail you will have to wait 24h to repeat it.
Mods:
Modules (Mods) are essentially the upgrade system in warframe in the form of special cards that can be equipped to Warframes, weapons, sentinels, Kubrows, and Archwings to enhance damage, power, survivability, speed, precepts, and utility.
Archwings:
The Archwing is a set of mechanical wings of Orokin design used by a Tenno to fly and engage in combat in space, offering a potent mix of firepower and mobility to engage spaceborn enemies.
Map:
The game is instance based you have your spaceship and then you have the planets (mars, jupiter, you get the point) each planet has around 20 missions to complete from Exterminate missions to Survivel ones, Sabotage, Expionage, etc
Crafting:
To make weapons and warframes you need to craft them (or if you buy platinum with irl money you can just buy them already crafted from the market and use them right away) to do that you go to the in-game shop choose a weapon/warframe you wanna make and buy the blueprint, after that get the materials needed to make the blueprint and leave It crafting (you need to wait at least 12h or more for the carfting to finish or you can simply rush It with platinum)
Pets:
You have 2 types of pets, Kubrows (dog like pets) and Sentinels (hovering companions), Kubrows have to be hatched from an egg ans you have to constantly mantain them or they will die, sentinels are robot like companions you only need to carft them.
Pros:
-Great combat mechanics;
-Art Style and Music is really good;
-F2P It isn't P2W If you know what you are doing you can easily get platinum in-game;
-Great Variety of weapons and wraframes;
-Great Playerbase.
Cons:
-Can get repetitive really fast;
-The story was OK but the latest story adition didn't make the playerbase that happy (At least in the foruns It seems the playerbase was divided by the ones that liked and the ones that didn't like It)
-Some bugs here and there.
TLDR: Great Game, playerbase is really friendly and helpfull, F2P.

There are two ways to play Ark. You can play cautiously by looking over your shoulder for raiders, or you can play on a calmer server that allows you to build a massive base with very little worry from other players. You can’t have both as an adult. My first time through I would rate Ark a negative, because of how toxic the community was. People don’t want you to have fun, and the second you begin building anything remotely close to a fortress, people will offline raid you. When you finally realize what has happened you will wake up in an empty base and all your dinos will be dead.
That is the Ark I was introduced to and would have left my original review as just that. A negative experience filled with an abundance of A-holes. Fast forward to today and my experience and perception of the game has drastically changed. Me and some friends joined a server called Champion Ark and we couldn’t be happier. The PVP element is still there, but you must now declare war with another tribe, which happens rarely. Instead you get to enjoy Ark and what it really is.
Everyone thinks it’s all about PVP, but once you remove that layer you get to see how beautiful and thriving the world really is. I’m not only able to build a fortress worthy of a king, but I get to do it without looking over my shoulder. Instead of killing people we help each other. We trade, we have laughs; we are just a fun community that says hello and goodnight. Sure, it can get a little stale without the hardcore PVP element, but I stand by first sentence. You can’t have both.

After nearly 400 hours in the game i think i have a good enough feel to leave a review.
Those negative reviews are not lying, the game really is that difficult to enjoy. Notice I said difficult and not impossible.
The issues i have with ARK are as follows
1. extremely time consuming
2. Alpha tribes
3. WildCard seems to push content THEY want, not what the community wants
4. extremely poor balance
5. still buggy after years of development
Ill start with the first, ARK is time consuming, painfully so. It takes HOURS to tame a good dino and even longer to build enough defences to keep it alive from other tribes. Eventually you will realize that low level tames arent worth it, and will find yourself dumping hour after hour into this game to tame dinos and buff defences. When you finally log off you will be left without the feeling that you made much progress, because in reality you didnt, and often you will experience a glitch that will cost you LOTS of hours. For example, i was attempting to raise a baby rex to adulthood, and after nearly spending an entire real life day at my computer the baby got stuck and starved to death when i couldnt access its inventory. Essentially wasting nearly 24 hours of my life.
Point 2, now this is the one that has actually forced me to leave the game. I have gone to nearly every official server available and found nothing but toxic communities. There isnt enough balance to allow other tribes to grow without getting destroyed by established alpha tribes. You can build defences and spend hours mining and building and taming but it will all be destroyed while you sleep. You can try to be allies with the Alpha but they will almost always enforce ridiculous rules like "no Quetzals or Gigas" essentially barring you from any of the end-game content. Hoping that Scorched Earth would be an escape from this kind of play, i foolishly purchased the expansion. After only 2-3 hours i knew that it was even worse than the Island map. Thanks to the new transfer system the majority of these servers are owned by Mega tribes, which keep other players from even starting there. They openly say the server is "closed" and use it exclusively to tame and transfer high level golems and wyverns etc. to strengthen their other servers. Now, i understand it is possible to join these tribes, but they are normally DIFFICULT to join and if you are an independant player like i am and would prefer to play alone or with friends, you will not be succesful. And dont even think about playing single player, as time doesnt pass when you are gone, making farming, hatching babies, and any other time dependent task nearly impossible. There are MANY more issues with the plague of alphas on official servers but for now /rantover
Wildcard....Wildcard seems to push content they WANT to develop, not what we as players want. Many players would like a way to play on official servers without constantly getting shredded by alpha or mega tribes, but instead they release things like server transfer, paid expansions, and TEK tier. This brings me to another important point. I have invested almost 400 hours of my time in ARK, and havent been able to reach end game content at all. I havent participated in a boss fight, havent tamed a giga, ive never had a quetz. literally all because alphas squashed me and my friends before i could reach that point, and trust me when i say we tried and often got close. Now with TEK tier, which you can only get from boss fights, the ALPHAS will become unreasonably strong. The technology looks fun to use, but only a tiny percentage will ever access it, while the overwhelming majority will get trampled. This is a fast and efficient way to lose a fan base.
balance...I have already largely covered this point, but will reiterate. Alphas using transfer and TEK tier are unreasonably strong and cannot be touched. I know people may read this and say that if alphas have invested so much time they should have the power to own the server, and i agree. However, to make it impossible for small tribes to survive because of balance issues seems ridiculous. They need to find a solution that will balance the game in a way that small tribes can atleast fend off alphas, and enjoy the game as it was meant to be played.
this point doesnt need much explanation, the game has been playable for years but devs continue to add content instead of fixing the bugs. Wildcard seems much more fixated on quantity over quality, and it can be extremely frustrating when your tame falls through the floor, or your character randomly gets deleted. These need to be fixed, as hundred of hours can disappear in an instant..
Overall, i do not recommend this game to players that are looking for a fun crafting/survival game. If you are a fan of sucking up to those stronger than you, or rebuilding over and over because you got raided, then go for it.

I've been playing Ark for about a year now, and I can honestly say its one of my favorite games of all time. I ended up becoming an admin on a private server I liked the game so much. 90% of the negative reviews you see can be avoided by playing on a private PvE server with active admins.
- Hate working for dozens of hours and then someone else coming and smashing your stuff? PvE fixes that by not allowing people to smash your stuff.
- Hate not being able to log off and go about your real life because you're always living in fear that someone will attack you while you're offline? PvE fixes that too. I play 1-3 times a week for a few hours apiece. Sometimes I'll skip a week or two without playing at all.
- Afraid that the game will suck you in and you'll never be able to escape? Lots of servers allow you to save your dinosaurs and your character so you can stop playing for a while and pick it up again at a later date.
- Hate that the official servers offer zero support when it comes to bugs and issues? A private server with decent admins can fix lots of issues you encounter with a couple lines of code.
- Hate losing a special dinosaur because your game locked up while you were in a dangerous spot, and it got eaten before you could log back in? A server with an active admin might just respawn your dino for you if you explain what happened.
- Hate people trolling and griefing you and claiming space on PvE servers? An active admin can prevent these things from happening by banning the perps and destroying their stuff.
- Still interested in combat? Some PvE servers allow you to declare war against another tribe, but both sides have to agree to the war in order to fight each other. Other servers will have PvP weekends once a month or optional wars or things like that.
There are a lot of ways to play Ark. For me, PvE has all the upsides with none of the downsides. Don't let the whiners cause you to miss out on something good. (^_^)

I've been playing Ark for about a year now, and I can honestly say its one of my favorite games of all time. I ended up becoming an admin on a private server I liked the game so much. 90% of the negative reviews you see can be avoided by playing on a private PvE server with active admins.
- Hate working for dozens of hours and then someone else coming and smashing your stuff? PvE fixes that by not allowing people to smash your stuff.
- Hate not being able to log off and go about your real life because you're always living in fear that someone will attack you while you're offline? PvE fixes that too. I play 1-3 times a week for a few hours apiece. Sometimes I'll skip a week or two without playing at all.
- Afraid that the game will suck you in and you'll never be able to escape? Lots of servers allow you to save your dinosaurs and your character so you can stop playing for a while and pick it up again at a later date.
- Hate that the official servers offer zero support when it comes to bugs and issues? A private server with decent admins can fix lots of issues you encounter with a couple lines of code.
- Hate losing a special dinosaur because your game locked up while you were in a dangerous spot, and it got eaten before you could log back in? A server with an active admin might just respawn your dino for you if you explain what happened.
- Hate people trolling and griefing you and claiming space on PvE servers? An active admin can prevent these things from happening by banning the perps and destroying their stuff.
- Still interested in combat? Some PvE servers allow you to declare war against another tribe, but both sides have to agree to the war in order to fight each other. Other servers will have PvP weekends once a month or optional wars or things like that.
There are a lot of ways to play Ark. For me, PvE has all the upsides with none of the downsides. Don't let the whiners cause you to miss out on something good. (^_^)

tl;dr: I'm not saying anything that hasn't been said 1000 times in the reviews. Wildcard s(h)its out content into the game. 3 months later, nothing has really changed, you're hardly using the content theyve been adding. Consistent Server Lag, learn to accept it. This is probably the only game where there isn't a noticable difference between dial-up and high speed. It's odd how many people I've talked to that have explained to me that they just deal with all the problems with this game.
1. The menu's are atrocious. There's hundreds of survival crafting games out there that all follow a very similar formula when it comes to inventory and menus. Ark chooses to throw all conventions out the window, in favor of buttons to perform any inventory action. It feels very counterintuitive to what almost all other open world survival games have laid the groundwork on.
2. You literally jump as high as your characters ankles. You'll get stuck in doors/walls hoping off a mount. You'll hop off cliffs if you make the mistake of getting off near an edge.
3. I solo and get several dino's as well as a medium sized base together, i have friend hop on to join for a few hours. Need to make tribe so they can use the base. Afterwards, I wan't to disband the tribe as it wasn't a serious name, so i leave the clan. Now I don't have any access to my dino's or base, despite it having my name as the creator. I now need my friend to get on to get me back in. Why in the hell do I not still have a priority being that I am the Owner? This should never be something that is missing in a game.
4. There is little to no Dino A.I. Yeah there's many dino's, but no encounter is really all that different.
5. Official Servers LAG. Completely takes away the enjoyment of dinosaur battles. Makes flying mounts frustrating to land. Enjoy using a pike to poke the air 3 times before landing a hit according to the server.
6. Hey there's a ton of content here. Always something to do. The only problem, literally everything in the game lacks any polish. Why doesn't my cooking pot cook meat?
7. I'm just going to say bugs.
With all that said, i'm still playing it, but its not something I really am investing anything important into.
EDIT: Bought the newest Expansion with the Season Pass on sale. I've tried to play for about 20 minutes, and I've had two crashes. WIldcard...What the ♥♥♥♥ is your issue. You're constantly such a let down. I'm so glad this hit several months late like this, and in this state. Shame.

tl;dr: I'm not saying anything that hasn't been said 1000 times in the reviews. Wildcard s(h)its out content into the game. 3 months later, nothing has really changed, you're hardly using the content theyve been adding. Consistent Server Lag, learn to accept it. This is probably the only game where there isn't a noticable difference between dial-up and high speed. It's odd how many people I've talked to that have explained to me that they just deal with all the problems with this game.
1. The menu's are atrocious. There's hundreds of survival crafting games out there that all follow a very similar formula when it comes to inventory and menus. Ark chooses to throw all conventions out the window, in favor of buttons to perform any inventory action. It feels very counterintuitive to what almost all other open world survival games have laid the groundwork on.
2. You literally jump as high as your characters ankles. You'll get stuck in doors/walls hoping off a mount. You'll hop off cliffs if you make the mistake of getting off near an edge.
3. I solo and get several dino's as well as a medium sized base together, i have friend hop on to join for a few hours. Need to make tribe so they can use the base. Afterwards, I wan't to disband the tribe as it wasn't a serious name, so i leave the clan. Now I don't have any access to my dino's or base, despite it having my name as the creator. I now need my friend to get on to get me back in. Why in the hell do I not still have a priority being that I am the Owner? This should never be something that is missing in a game.
4. There is little to no Dino A.I. Yeah there's many dino's, but no encounter is really all that different.
5. Official Servers LAG. Completely takes away the enjoyment of dinosaur battles. Makes flying mounts frustrating to land. Enjoy using a pike to poke the air 3 times before landing a hit according to the server.
6. Hey there's a ton of content here. Always something to do. The only problem, literally everything in the game lacks any polish. Why doesn't my cooking pot cook meat?
7. I'm just going to say bugs.
With all that said, i'm still playing it, but its not something I really am investing anything important into.
EDIT: Bought the newest Expansion with the Season Pass on sale. I've tried to play for about 20 minutes, and I've had two crashes. WIldcard...What the ♥♥♥♥ is your issue. You're constantly such a let down. I'm so glad this hit several months late like this, and in this state. Shame.

This is a review for Loading Screen Simulator 2017. The loading screens are, just, the best. There is a list of servers, depending on how long you want your loading screen to take. Then the game takes you to a premium loading screen with a simulated mist effect along with a stylized "A" that appears to be there as an artistic flourish. A loading bar is seen in the bottom left corner of the screen and has text that changes simulating actual game files to add to the total immersion. After several minutes of awesome, pulse-pumping simulated loading, there is a few seconds where the screen goes black, which is most likely a glitch on my end. But, the loading screen quickly resumes and simulates even more loading before gently laying me to rest at the title screen. I have never, in my life, felt so satisfied. If you have British ancestry, or wish that you had British ancestry, and queueing is your thing, then Loading Screen Simulator 2017 is the game for you.

First I will say that this game isn't necessarily 'Free to Play', you will at some point need to buy some of the premium currency (Platinum) in order to progress (namely buying slots for items). I should say however, that one of the login rewards for this game is a discount to buying the premium currency (Platinum) and it is also possible to earn it from trading with other players. So technically it is a 'Free to Play' game but it is a lot of grief if you don't buy at least a little bit to get you going. Secondly this game has a steep learning curve for new players and the in-game tutorials are quite frankly completely pants. If you are new to this game then I would recommend looking up some videos on YouTube about how to play the game, such as MCgamerCZ, Tactical Potato, Mogamu and Rob from AGGP. Thirdly is 'The Grind'. This game brings a whole new meaning to the grind in games. If you are looking for a part or resource in the game expect to have to play a particular mission over and over and over again trying to find it.
However I don't think I would have lasted over 1500 hours of gameplay if there wasn't some good points about the game. The game is visually stunning. It is quite possible to play Solo, even though it is slightly more difficult than Coop play. The game has it's own Lore and Story to follow, which is pretty awesome. You can spec or mod your equipment in 1000s of different ways to suit your play style, and there are many different play styles to explore. Once you find the equipment that suits you there is so much fun to be had in this game. The gameplay flows extremely well and is very satisfying, you do after all get to be a Space Ninja!
Overall this game is a lot of fun; even better if you have friends to play it with and the time to play it. Well worth a go.

In it's current state, the game is an unbalanced, buggy mess.
The building mechanics are very clunky and unintuitive.
The AI is absolutely horrible.  Occasionally you will run into a large pack of hostile dinos, get surrounded, and die without any chance of fighting back or running away, but most fights can be won fairly easily with ranged weapons.
Performance is abysmal.  You will have to lower the graphics setings and endure low framerates regardless of how powerful your machine is.
Gathering resources is tiresome and dull, which is unfortunate because a huge portion of your play-time will be devoted to gathering basic building materials like stone, metal, and wood.
The developers seem disinterested in fixing the game's many issues.  Instead they continue adding more and more content to the game, compounding the problem.
This is an early access game and the game will constantly remind you of that fact.
I think this has the potential to be a great game, but  I recomend waiting until the final release version before you consider playing it. Hopefully the devs stop spamming content and focus their efforts on making a playable final product.

This game has been great since i've been around and it's been a couple years. It's kinda repetitive at some point and that's why i have few hours on it (as i have long periods where i do other things).
Still, devs are doing a great job. They keep adding new stuff, interesting events and they keep expanding the lore. THIS is the reason i still love playing Warframe: the Lore. With every update you discover something about past events and main NPCs and it's lovely (especially after two years wondering who the fu** they are and why they are there).
Also, graphics are very good and they get updated every now and then (just saying: last big patch, albeit exceptional, was almost 7GB, most of which texture updates and other visual stuff), weapons come in every form and measure and there are TONS of options to upgrade them: most regular stuff can be dealt with by any weapon with the right build. More powerful weapons give broader options as they aren't required to stack damage mods to work as efficiently.
Still, there are weapons ranging from daggers to heavy twin-bladed axes to polearms to handheld motorized saws for melee. Oh and let's not forget boomerangs and similar weapons (did someone say chakram?). Ranged weapons are even more varied, from regular pistols to C4 thrower (look up for the Stug) to assault rifles to LMGs to rocket and grenade launchers to lascannons and almost every kind of ray weapon you can desire. There are some 200 different weapons (some are just variations of the same weapon -Prime weapons for example- but there is a lot of room to experiment and find the one just for you.
And Warframes are possibly cooler than that. I'll leave them up to you to discover (but you HAVE to know there is a freaking DRAGON frame).
There is one thing breaking the mood tho.
If you start playing alone, do NOT team up with someone with brains (and avoid going public unless you need it). While MP is recommended -and in fact mandatory for quite some stuff- i unfortunately find there is a huge weakpoint:
- if you play with friends or with someone with some brain you can't go back to solo play, it's too boring
- if you play in PUGs expert people will just run, wreck the place before you can aim your weapons and you won't get what happened or XP either. When you get to their level it's like going solo but with someone else on the map (since everyone minds his own affair defeating the whole purpose of going MP) and it's SUPER boring.
But if you can gather a regular group or you can keep your enthusiasm for discovery and a fast paced combat bolstered by explosions, great looking powers and incredible carnage then this is the game for you.

I bought this game a while back but never got around to installing it.  When Conan Exiles went into early access I thought I'd give Ark a shot.  I wish I hadn't.  This game, in comparison to Conan Exiles which isn't even out yet, is garbage.  You have to unequip your weapon just to pick up a rock off the ground, you can't have a torch in one hand and a weapon in the other, and you are going to die A LOT before you even finish making a pair of pants.  After spending 20 minutes getting the stupid free DLC to work because of this weird issue it has of not downloading properly I finally got into the game.  When I first spawn I go about collecting the resources I'll need to survive without ever going more than a few feet from my spawn point.  I get attack by a level 90 raptor and die.  I respawn and repeat the process, get attacked by a level 90 giant fly and die.  Repeat the process, get attacked by a giant horse cow dino thing of level 40 and die.  Repeat the process, get attack by a swarm of level 20 chompers and die.  This goes on and on and on...  At least in Conan Exiles you are given a fighting chance to survive.  In Conan Exiles you start off surrounded by creatures roughly your level that you could kill with a pickaxe and then as you work your way deeper into the map you face stronger enemies.  In Ark there are level 100 predators in areas where you spawn so you insta die over and over again.  Also in Ark you are CONSTANTLY running back to water and struggling to keep your food meter topped off.  This game is absolute garbage and I would not recommend anyone play this game.  If you want a good and fun survival game then go get Conan Exiles, even in early access it is leaps and bounds better than this garbage game.
Adding an Edit down here to revise my review.  Friend of mine started playing Ark and we got a private server to play on and it is much better to play.  So I thought I would come on here to edit this to let people know that the game is enjoyable if you are playing with multiple people / or are the owner of a private server where you can level the playing field a bit.  If you are playing by yourself, especially on official servers, the game is cancer.  Official servers established Tribes and players fly around on eagles looking for new player to pick up and drop to their deaths for absolutely no reason other than to troll you.  They will destroy your thatch homes and wooden rafts.  They will kill you and drop all your items out of your inventory so they spoil faster than you can reach your corpse.  Even if you do reach your corpse they will wait and kill you again.  They will destroy your containers in your base just to destroy items you own, they don't even want it.  They will kill your Dino's even if it's just a level 1 compy.  DO NOT PLAY ON OFFICIAL SERVERS!  Official servers are straight up cancerous and will make you quit the game faster than single player ever could.  If you plan on playing find a good private server with a good community or buy your own server.  I got mine for around 12$ for 20 players from

I find this game very frustrating. My experience with it was jarring. First off, most of the official servers are ruined. They're littered with pillars spammed all over the maps so that you can't build in most areas. The ones you can build in aren't going to save you from being destroyed by higher level players. There is really no protection against being raided while you're offline, either, except for a mod that most servers don't even use. So, you work really hard to accumulate resources, dinosaurs and a base only to have some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ take all of it from you the second you log off... Or a tribe of high level players steamroll you while you're online. If you don't mind being♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off and having your hard work wiped by trolls, you might enjoy this game.
The performance issues are really bad here. All of the official servers suffer from rubberbanding, which is when you get jerked backward because your packets are being dropped. The framerate is awful but you can use a launch command through steam to play the game in directx10. This, however, causes GPU driver crashes. The lighting is bad as well, and you'll see it go through walls. I had a torch outside my house and every area inside it was lit. Just now, I was riding a flying dinosaur and my game crashed. When I logged back in (because your character persists when you log out for some stupid ♥♥♥♥ing reason) I was drowning, being attacked by fish and my dinosaur was hovering probably a hundred ft in the air where I was unable to get to him and my whistle commands didn't have any affect, so I lost that dinosaur and had to walk back to my base which took 10 minutes of sprinting and dodging carnivores.
There are WAY too many dinosaurs spawned at the same time. You can't look in any direction and not see mobs. It makes no sense and if they're that easy to find, there's no sense of a hunt to be found. You can just walk 20 steps and there's a dino. Real immersive. To make matters worse on that end, some of them STEAL FROM YOU. That means you're regularly going to have to chase down smaller dinosaurs and kill them to get your stuff back. If they're part of a group, that means others will be performing this behavior.
There are sliders to change the decay rate on things like hunger and the gain rate on stuff like XP. However... most servers have the XP and gather rates cranked up to 10 times the normal rate so it feels like you're cheating. Others have it lowered to almost nothing. Nobody chooses the sensible middle ground. Normally, I'd be eating 5-10 pieces of meat just to survive only to watch the hunger meter deplete anyway. It's a nuisance and only serves to detract from the gameplay, it should NOT decay as fast as it does by default. I'm not sure what developers are thinking when they put this hunger mechanic in the game and turn it up to these insane degrees.
"Hey guys, you know what sounds fun? Having to stop and eat every 2 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes. The sense of being yanked out of whatever the hell you were doing to mash the key you have food bound to repeatedly so you don't starve to death strikes me as super immersive!"
There are a variety of weapons and they handle well. The problem is, the higher you go in tiers, the more cumbersome maintaining these weapons becomes. I have a rifle. That means I have to make bullets. To do this I need several ingredients and they take a long time to smelt. Then I turn those into bullets. 10 minutes of labor yielded me 30 bullets. I used those up killing ONE dinosaur and all I got out of that was some meat and hide. It was not rewarding and none of that ordeal made me want to make more ammo and shoot anything else.
The CONCEPT of surviving, taming and fighting dinosaurs and raiding might sound like fun but it is not executed well in this game. Before a few days ago, people were suffering from a bug in the game that crashed peoples' GPU drivers regularly, even preventing them from playing. It was introduced when Sorched Earth was released and reports date back to 2015. It was fixed a few days ago... Like 90% of Early Access games, this one is probably never going to reach a 1.0 state and the performance bugs (audio crackling, framerate stutter, crashing) are unlikely to ever be fixed.
I want to recommend this game, but it wouldn't make sense to. Stay away until the negative reports dwindle or buy at your own risk. 4/10

This is a single player review.
For those of you who are curious about single player mode, I hope this review helps.
After playing Ark solo for 11 hours straight, I can say that the single player mode is solid.
(I haven't tried Scorched Earth or multiplayer, so I have no comment on that.)
First, my PC spec: i7-6700 (4.0GHz), GTX1060 (6GB), 32GB RAM, SSD (R550MB/W500MB)
My old LCD monitor can only go up to 1680x1050 (60Hz).
- This game is very taxing on your machine. I first started the game on medium settings, got around 60 fps and it looked like a PS3 game (which isn't so bad in my opinion). Then I tried Epic settings, the game looked absolutely stunning but I got around 30 fps or lower and it felt stuttery. After tweaking some options (e.g. Epic textures, medium quality shadow, distant ambient occlusion off, etc.), now I get around 40-50 fps and it's good enough for me.
- Basically, it's the same game as multiplayer but you do everything alone. If you have played other survival games, you know the drill. Punch trees, craft, kill monsters, get loots, craft better gears, kill tougher monsters, craft, so on.
- Ark allows you to set the parameters for your session (similar to Don't Starve). I set my game to give more XP, faster resource respawn rate, more harvest amount, slower food & water drain and left other options to their default values. This makes solo mode a lot less grindy but not too easy. You can still get your♥♥♥♥♥kicked by dinosaurs.
If you're not entirely happy with your settings (too easy or too hard), just quit to the main menu, re-adjust your game, and continue.

- The default map is huge and there are tons of stuff to do, plenty of skills (engrams) to upgrade and lots of things to craft.
- The crafting system is convenient. You can craft basic equipment and items right from the menu.
- If you prefer controller, the game works fine with a wired 360 controller. You can also use keyboard and mouse for the menu and inventory, and controller for movement and action.

If you're interested in Ark for single player experience and you have a decent computer, go for it.
The game + DLC is about $10 on sale. Good deal for a fun survival game.

Approaching my 400th mark in hours. I'll be as candid as I can be.
ARK is still in early access. If you haven't figured this out yet, slap yourself first and read it again....STILL IN EARLY ACCESS.
You aren't going to run ARK on a toaster (aka laptop) unless said toaster is high-end, you know, for actual gaming...not checking email and playing browser based games on Facebook. A bunch of people, myself included, have answered questions on the ARK forums about this issue. The devs were kind enough to put up a FAQ about what you should have to run ARK...READ IT, then if you still can't figure it out...don't buy ARK until it is a finished product.
Now the skivvy:
ARK can be a quite enjoyable game. Yes it is ever evolving as the game progresses forward. Yes the devs patch the game like 50 times a week, but that's okay when they're fixing stuff, but not great when they break more than they fix. Trial and error I suppose. If you want to learn ARK, all the ins and outs, the quirks, taming, and so on, I suggest starting either in Single Player mode or playing on one of the many Unofficial servers that don't allow griefing. If you like long walks on short piers, being dropped from excessive heights, being sniped for no reason, and/or dying just because you are a "noob"...then go play on any populated Official Server.
This game has been rated "B" for Brutal by pretty much every player that has more than 300 hours invested, some maybe less. Even withstanding not playing on official servers, the dino's will make a meal out of you more often than not, and fairly often at your "random" spawn points. I've literally seen people "quit" this game just from being killed repeatedly by dino's and get a refund for it or attempt to. If you've played other "survival" games and thought this one would be similar, /sigh. ARK is definitely a "one of a kind" brutal adventure.
The optomization sucks still, but hey, they'll get to it eventually. If you have a little faith behind the devs and you read the positive reviews by players that have invested time, then you should be able to make a proper decision on whether or not to pick the game up. There are some butthurt longtimer's (1k+ hours played) and they've been putting up crappy reviews, but those are few and far between. They don't like the fact that the game is still in an Alpha state and the fact that they sold an alpha released DLC (I think many are miffed by this, but whatever). You'll see negative reviews from people on "high-end" PC's ♥♥♥♥♥ing about how their 3k+ PC can't run the game over 30FPS. Let me be the first to tell you, the thinker of possibly getting this game, that nobody's PC's can really handle ARK, high-end or low-end or anything in between. It just is what it is.
Food for thought. ARK supposedly is going into beta in April, so if you want to get this game cheap or for likely to be less than what it'll be after it is a finished game, get in on it now and catch one of those EPIC sales they have from time to time. Even if you don't actually play the game, you'll have it for when you want to check it out. You'll either like ARK or you won't.
