Ark: Survival Evolved is a sandbox survival game developed and published by Studio Wildcard. Players are stranded on a lush tropical island inhabited by mammoth dinosaurs. Survive by scavenging resources to craft tools and build a home to withstand the elements. Pick seeds and plant them, collecting dinosaur excrement to fertilize your farm. Or build improvised weapons to hunt prehistoric beasts for their hides and meat. As you play you level up in RPG-fashion, earning points to increase your stats and unlocking new craftable items. Tame ancient reptiles with food to assist you as pack mules, or ride them to fly, swim, and run faster across the sprawling landscape. Every animal in Ark obeys a predatorial hierarchy and wanders a specific ecosystem; tamed Dodo birds won’t do much good against a pack of velociraptors. While dinosaurs pose a threat, it’s humans who will kill you without mercy or provocation. Join a tribe with other players and create a thriving community, sharing resources and working together to survive. Or, raid other tribes for loot, in fast-paced and brutal PvP.

Hands down the best survival game on Steam. Tons of content and a lot of different things to do... variety of animals is great, and now you can grow a beard and wear a mowhawk :D
Map design is great and because of that, the world (on both The ARK and The Center) is beautiful and fun to play in. The game features Caves which are kind of like a mix of dungeons + 3D platformers, where you have to hop from rock to rock as you go down the cave, fighting giant spiders, scorpions, millipede, snakes, and bats.
Crafting is also very good, loads of tools, weapons, and structures to craft and build. The actual building mechanics of houses could do with some more attention, though. You can find blueprints of different qualities which allow you to build more advanced/deadly versions of the basic tool or weapon you can find in your engram list. Of course, for the better versions of these items, you will need more supplies than normal to craft.
Tools and weapons are varied, for actual weapons, you can craft a Bow, Crossbow, Pistol, Automatic Rifle (with different attachments such as a light, laser sight, and holo sight), Sniper Rifle, and (only on Scorched Earth DLC) a Flamethrower. If you defeat the bosses (giant Spider, Gorilla, and Dragon), you can unlock the Tek tier which currently (more stuff is going to be added) features things like Iron-man like suits, a helmet for the Rex that has LASERS on it, and also laser guns for you to use ;D

Ark: Survival Evolved is a sandbox survival game developed and published by Studio Wildcard. Players are stranded on a lush tropical island inhabited by mammoth dinosaurs. Survive by scavenging resources to craft tools and build a home to withstand the elements. Pick seeds and plant them, collecting dinosaur excrement to fertilize your farm. Tame ancient reptiles with food to assist you as pack mules, or ride them to fly, swim, and run faster across the sprawling landscape. Every animal in Ark obeys a predatorial hierarchy and wanders a specific ecosystem; tamed Dodo birds won’t do much good against a pack of velociraptors. While dinosaurs pose a threat, it’s humans who will kill you without mercy or provocation. Join a tribe with other players and create a thriving community, sharing resources and working together to survive. Or, raid other tribes for loot, in fast-paced and brutal PvP.

The developers hate the players and vice versa. This is the first game I've ever played where people love the game and hate the devs. The recent addition of Tech Tier is a good example of how the devs handle the game. Leading up to its release the devs explained how to get tech gear, which revolved around accumulating artifacts to summon the boss, and when the patch went live all artifacts were deleted from the game forcing any players who stocked up to go get more. Getting an artifact is easy, that’s not the point, the point is that deleting them is a♥♥♥♥♥♥move and it represents a lot of the BS the devs do for 'reasons'. They also did not design the game for human consumption as the most optimal methods of taming will take several hours and the least optimal can take over a day depending on the dino, breeding  can take a player a week where they have to log in every 3-4 hrs for optimal results, not accounting for keeping the baby alive.
The game is balanced for large tribes, making a few aspects of the game (tech tier as an example) impossible to do solo, and other aspects nearly impossible (taming first quetzel as an example) to do solo.
Whenever players use their heads and find clever ways to accomplish a task, the devs will♥♥♥♥♥♥block it. A good example is not allowing players to use grappling hooks in boss battles, or when people used pillars to block golems movement while making them easier to hit the devs let golems walk through pillars as though they weren't there.
The game is ultimately better than traditional MMO's, which isn't saying much, and it does just enough right to keep people playing. Do not pick up unless you can spend 4+ hrs in a single play session at the absolute minimum.

I wanted to love ark, I really did. Taming and breeding your own dinos, exploring and creating, all of this was 100% up my lane. But unfortunately, there are many issues that ultimately tarnished my enjoyment of the game. I can accept that I die or lose some of my hard earned dinos if I make a bad choice or play to aggressively. But if I lose valuable equipment and hard earned creatures to bugs, clipping errors and a embarrasingly horrendous wayfinding system again and again and again it sucks the fun out of the game. This, combined with some questionable design decisions (Pegomastax = tiny herbivore of doom. They are aggressive as hell and for some inexplicable reason they target tamed Paracers and other creatures they completely ignore in the wild. More than once I almost lost a valued beast because I left it in a Area devoid of carnivores on passive only to come back and see a Pegomastax brutally savaging its hitpoints).
I would like to come back to Ark but until the team put at least some work on playability instead of (seemingly) focusing entirely on new animals and gadgets I'm going to stay away for now. If these issues are addressed I'll gladly change my review to positive, since I still believe that Ark has a lot of potential. But currently, it's become primarily frustrating and that's what RL is for.
Edit: I'm well aware, that ARK is still in development. However, after consulting several forums and my own experience it seems that the developing is currently more focused on adding late game content instead of fixing the issues in gameplay. However, it is hard to evaluate and enjoy the new content if you run into the same old issues over and over again.
Edit (18.02.2017): Recently I wanted to give Ark another try and look at the other map they are offering "The Centre". First: The map is gorgeous and feels organic. It constantly crashes, sometimes after less then 15 minutes playtime and if freezes up every other minute which makes playing more akin to watching a powerpoint presentation than an enjoyable gaming experience. This is completely unacceptable. If there was an option to, I would switch my review to "REALLY! do no reccommend this game".
Sorry guys, fending of hordes of killer lizards and taming the survivors sounds like lot of fun, but if all I can do is watch my character die one frame at a time, like some masochistic strobe light show, something is seriously wrong with your game. And before anybody asks whether my PC is a relic from the stoneages, I bought it as a gaming PC in January 2017. And unless Wildcard produces games for the same community that buys gold plated AKs this PC should be good enough to run Ark at least at low to medium preferences (which it doesn't).

Warframe is fantastic game! there is at least one Frame that suits the playstyle of any player, and the developers did a great job in giving each frame unique movesets. They also went far enough to make each weapon look unique! You don't have to pay for anything if you don't want to which is a nice touch, yes there is a bit of real time waiting for when constructing something (12 hours for a weapon, 72 hours for a Frame) but its worth the wait. there are only a few things here and there which you would have to dig into your wallet to buy, but those things are justified, otherwise they are really hard to find/farm for. Speaking of which, the Farming/Grinding for specific blueprints or materials is way more fun then in other games as you'll more likely than not come up with other intriguing rewards, they may not be what you're looking for, but almost everything that you can find has a use.
The one teeny tiny problem I have is with a little bit of the voice acting. mainly with Lotus. Now don't get me wrong She's beautifully designed, the one thing she's lacking in my opinion is any real emotion, but I guess that is kinda explained in one of the stories (Second Dream). Second Dream was  a great story speaking of which, however (without any spoilers) I can honestly say that I was mind blown, but after a while in the end a little dissapointed but thinking back on it I still like the ending because it still leaves some questions/secrets which I hope will be answered soon. I can't say what specifically disappointed me about it without spoiling a huge lore secret so I'll just leave it at that. However, that out of the way, Second Dream was all in all pretty damn epic.
OH MAN!!! I almost forgot something else that's really well thought out about this game. The extra (DLC like) stories (or episodes) are completely free! you just have to rank up, buy the blueprint for the specific episode and craft it.
I can't wait to see what else is to be done with this game, and believe me if I could make 3D models I would be designing helmets for a lot of the Frames (IVARA IS LACKING A LOT OF HELMETS!!!)

It is incredible how much a good (and i mean really good) survival game can suffer from bad decissions made by the developer/marketing strategist.
I played this game over 400 hours since early 2016 and it evolved itself so much in so many good ways. More creatures, better AI, better look, better handling - and even with some bugs and glitches it works really nicely and is an awesome timesink for those who want a multiplayer/coop survival experience.
And here comes the but, and it's a big BUT, indeed:
1. ARK Survival evolved comes with free official multiplayer servers - usually for up to 70 people. But the servers actually can not handle half of the max population without lag spikes from here to Mars. With the mediocre shardware server structure a ARK game can quickly become an issue - because it feels like you are playing with an ancient 56k modem.
Even with a pretty modern PC and a extremly fast internet there are losts of issues causing lag - so there are quite a few construction sites in this game, that need to be fixed. Sadly, although this game is looking quite nice, those problems make the game experience quite gruffy!
2. Since Scorched Earth is online, people are transporting items and/or creatures from one game mode to another. That quickly evolved to a overly large problem, because big tribes and grievers are using this to their advantage, occupying one or several servers, killing off new gamers, destroying others structures and generally harassing people.
The possibility of traveling between servers and bringing over ressources and OP creatures killed a lot of the unique envirioment qualities the maps had - and enabled grieving even more.
3. Which leads to another problem: the developer "Studio Wildcard" is in general looking after the servers - like server structure - but there are no admins (available). People can do whatever they feel like, which gives grievers and big tribes easy access to rule their server - or even plural -servers. There are a few servers, where a few people are in control of the maps, with walls, spring guns and tamed agressiv dino armies on each spawn point, walled off and spring gunned ressource plots and so called "task forces" on wyverns killing each new player they can get.
There are even "events" by some big tribes, where they do head hunts in groups up to 20 people - camping spawn positions, killing people and using pvp equipment like shakles and cages, so people can't play later on on those servers.
All in all - the game itself is really awesome - but I STRONGLY recommand, that you set up your own private(!) server, if you want to play with others, or you play solo on your own comp.
The way Studio Wildcard's policy is set up for public servers and the community on those is FUBAR at the moment, so there is almost no way, one can play this game alone or with friends on public servers atm.
Around 28 Euros are way too much for getting constantly griefed + harassed by other players and not supported by the game developer AND the constant problems causing lag spikes.
Unless the policy turns around, or you have access to a private server,
I CANNOT RECOMMEND this game to new gamers AT ALL!
